review_text: If you visit Orlando, you have to take two days out to go to the Universal parks. We had so much fun. The two best rides were Spider-man at Islands of Adventure and Shrek at Universal Studios!!!

I think these parks (Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure) are the best in Orlando. There's so many thrills and chills there. USF is so brash and exciting. They're not afraid to set everything around you on fire or blast you 0 to 40 in two seconds. I think that this is why it appeals to the teenage crowd. However, these aren't the same parks. One is based entirely on the movies, and one is based on a fictional world with several different themed lands. So, because it's two parks, I'll review both of them.  Universal Studios This was the original park, but it's grown a lot since its shaky opening over a decade ago. The park now includes amazing attractions. As soon as you walk in, you're met with several different things to do. Everything seems so realistic. In the New York area, there are buildings everywhere and it appears as if you're walking on a street. In the Amity area, it seems as if you will be eaten by the big shark himself-Jaws. Here are some of the highlighted attractions: Men In Black: Alien Attack: This is an interactive ride in which people of all ages can team up in their own spinning cars and careen through New York streets. Your job is to shoot all the aliens that you can find. Kids will like it too--the aliens aren't scary (sort of cartoon-looking), and the spins aren't bad. Revenge of the Mummy: This is the new attraction, so the lines are a bit long. You board a mine cart which travels through different scenes before racing through a high-speed indoor rollercoaster. Included among the madness is a launch uphill, a ceiling bursting into flames and plenty of thrilling drops. Some say that this is a good enough reason to travel to Universal. The only thing that I can say is this: ignore the hype. Whatever you do, ignore the hype. If you do, you'll be pleasantly surprised. Jaws: The ride starts out as a nice tour through the Amity lagoon. Your skipper happily points out the landmarks and everything is going as planned. Soon, a frightened call of a fellow skipper signals something much worse. The infamous shark has returned. You and your fellow boatriders are trapped in the murky depths as the animatronic bursts out of the water. The skipper tries desperately to kill it, using his grenade launcher. After a scary boat house and a wall of flames, the final showdown comes. With a blast of fog and noise, Jaws attacks for its last time, just happening to eat an electrical line instead. Anyone want fried shark? There are many, many other attractions here including the E.T. Adventure, Shrek 4-D, Twister, Earthquake, Back to the Future, T2-3D and a whole section for kids. Like I mentioned earlier, Universal has more in-your-face action but it also provides calmer things for the young ones. For example, there's Jimmy Neutron's Nicktoon Blast, which is still fun even if you're older then the targeted crowd. There's also a kid's play area and kiddie coaster. Shrek 4-D is stunning. The effects are so crisp. You see Donky flailing his hooves at you as an evil dragon bellows fire in cool 3-D. I think it's worth the visit. However, if you're traveling from afar, go to AAA travel agency and book a room at one of their hotels. It's definitely worth it. People complain of long lines, but if you stay on-site you get an Express Pass which allows you to bypass all those lines. Plus, you can walk to the parks or ride a river ferry.  Islands of Adventure The adventure begins as soon as you walk under the infamous bridge and enter the Port of Entry. This is only the first of the islands, and though it boasts no attractions, there are many secrets to be uncovered. The island is themed to be a bustling sea-side village where the adventurers gather before beginning their quest to all of the other lands. Next up is Marvel SuperHero Island. As soon as you walk in, you're greeted with adrenaline-pumping comic book style music. Everything is themed to be in a city, where Marvel superheroes (Spiderman, Hulk, Wolverine, Storm, the Fantastic Four, Captain America etc) battle it out with the ultimate villains (Magneto, Dr. Doom). There are large cut-outs of the characters in action, and they're extremely detailed and colorful. This island is home to the Incredible Hulk Rollercoaster. Instead of being a simple chainlift standup rollercoaster, you're blasted from 0 to 40 (I think) in two seconds uphill in an enclosed chainlift. Once you exit the Gamma Radiation tomb you do a complete inversion a 100 feet in the air. After this you plunge back to the earth before completing the rest of the twisted track. The beginning is worth the whole ride, in my opinion. Next to the Hulk is Spiderman. This is a must-see ride. It's a 3-D adventure in which your vehicle actually moves through sets, some of which are real and some of which are 3-D. For example, you see the shadow of Spiderman before he leaps onto your car. When he does, the vehicle shakes slightly due to his weight. Sometimes you won't know if it's real or projected imagery. At one point, there's a simulated 400 ft drop, where you almost crash into the cement before Spiderman spins a web to save you. There are other attractions, but I'll skip over them for now. The next stop is at Toon Lagoon. Several cartoons call this their home. You can join Dudley Do-Right as he sends you on the ultimate logride. There are several small drops, but they're nothing compared to the huge one at the end. Some say its the steepest and fastest one around. In your puny log, you plunge down what seems like an infinite slope before crashing through a cartoon shack, through a bunny hill, and finally to a splash down. After you've gotten soaked, you can get soaked once again on Popeye and Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges. I'll skip the details on that, there is more to explore. The next island is Jurassic Park. If you've never heard of this phoenomanal movie, I don't know what you're doing reading this. This island is surrounded with vegetation, electric fences (for the dinosaurs), and small JP style huts. With a Discovery Center (where you can watch a baby raptor hatch or participate in some small interactive games), a raft ride, and a play area complete with cool caves, Jurassic Park is definitely worth walking through. The Jurassic Park River Adventure is the most talked-about attraction of the area. You're raft drifts through a peaceful lagoon where you're welcomed to Jurassic Park. You float by a towering Ultrasaur (like a Brontosaurus), which cranes its neck above you're head. The narrator gives you a little information about the peaceful dinosaurs, but something has to go wrong...right? Yep, this is Universal, and they're not going to leave it as a gentle drift with animatronic dinosaurs. Your raft is knocked off course and is accidentally sent to the raptor containment area. You enter the lift where raptors attack from all sides, including some spitter dinosaurs, before you face the ultimate carnivore. The raft with its survivors is put face-to-face with a T-Rex. The dinosaur pops out of the mist and roars (it looks exactly like the one in the movie). It leans its head down, poised to eat every person on board. The raft has a different idea...before you know it, you're plunging 84 ft to the bottom in an awesome splash-down. Now, that's not all the islands...there are still two awesome dueling coasters and a fantastic world of Seussian creatures. What I explained was about half of the park. Until next time...the adventure lives on!
3 hours to get on a ride, $5 icees and $7 for a cold pizza?? After the initial park entrance fee I expected a bit more.

We really had a great time at this park. My 7 year old was a little frightened at some of the rides but my 9 year old went on everything. Children under 7 probably would not do well on most of the rides. We stayed on property so we got the use our room key to go to just about the front of every ride. This made the cost of the room well worth it! We loved every ride except Back to the Future. Like a previous post mentioned it was so jerky I hit my head on the back seat several times. I felt like I had whiplash and I'm only 29 years old. Both of my daughters really liked Men In Black and the Animal Planet Live show.

After spending time in the Keys, we decided to leave a day early and spend our last day at Universal Studios which is close to the airport. We bought the cheaper tickets which allowed us to visit 1 side of the park (there are 2 sides). At first we thought our 4 teens (plus 11 yr old) wouldn't be entertained... we were expecting a lot more rides. However, some of the few rides they have are awesome!! The 3-D Spiderman ride was amazing, along with Duling Dragons and The Hulk. Mom and daughter loved Jurasic Park, a jungle in the middle of the city. Our 16 yr old took crazy photos with every super hero. The park is very clean, and easy to navigate. We stayed at a LaQuinta 5 minutes from the park. On Jan 4, it was 70 degrees and not very crowded. Everyone loved it. We suggest two days total at Universal (assuming the other side is just as entertaining).

I'm not sure what park the people were at that are complaining about universal studios. But I have gone there every year for 10 years. Speaking of drunk people tripping over their kids, It's called CityWalk, an ADULT part of the park. Who takes their kids to a back to back night club?Anyway, If you don't want to wait in line, order your tickets online like most people do. If you don't want to wait in line at the park, stay at one of the onsite resorts. Do your research before you go and your stay will be wonderful. And park food? Oh my you can get all you can eat for 20.00 bucks. It's good food too. If you have never been to Universal, You must go!! It's the best park in the world!!

We visited the both parks at the end of Jan. I bought 7 day passes on the Universal website. I paid $85 per person for unlimited use of both parks. I thought that was a great deal. The lines were very short for the most part. We did visit the parks on a Sunday and the crowds were much larger then. My 4 year old went on or watched (Barney show-Animal actors)10 attractions at the park so I don't think Universal is only for adults. The Mummy is great-go as a single rider. You save so much time. The Jaws boat ride was a little scary for my little guy although he loved the Woody Woodpecker rollercoaster. I think he went on it 7 times in a row! Shrek was fun and my son really liked Jimmy Neutron. There were characters roaming around and in easy to find areas. We found all the staff member to be friendly and helpful. I would visit Universal studios again.

There are so many reasons to hate this park. The "rides" were very short and the lines very long. (We got there very early on a Friday in April.) Paying $70 per person to get into the park, makes you a second class citizen waiting in line. You can buy an "express pass" which allows you to jump in line. After waiting 10-20 minutes in line, we watched as "express pass" holders walked up and walked in ahead of us. This of course made our wait longer. We started off with the Men in Black ride, which involved using play laser guns to shoot "rubber aliens" sitting in garbage cans and around corners. The car you ride in spins a few times which is the really big excitement. Then the ride broke leaving us locked into our seats for about 30 minutes until the staff finally shut off the ride then came and led us out of the ride. Twister was realistic but again, very short. For each ride we went on, the exit forced you through a gift shop, which was irritating. If I want to go into the gift shop, I will. This park seems to be geared toward children but the rides are based on movies primarily from the 1970s to the early 1990s. In fairness, we were not able to get into the Terminator, Earthquake or Mummy rides/shows. I had heard those were quite good. For those, the lines were so long (35+ minutes) we did not wait. I am used to waited for rides but these were oh so not worth the effort. You will be acosted by people taking surveys for tv shows. We were stopped six times. This park promotes itself as taking people behind the scenes of movies/tv shows. In reality, it is little more than a bunch of concocted, poorly designed, cheaply conceived ride/show experiences. Why create a park like this? Universal Studios is a cynical money grab by Universal/NBC to try to wring a few more bucks out of its tired media properties. Stick with the mouse.

We have gone to Florida many times and had not gone to Universal Studios, so we thought that we would try it this time. Big waste of time and money.  The system they use to enter the park is slow and unorganized (it took well over an hour to actually get in the park) There were not that many rides, and of them they were lame and outdated.(the best one for me was the Jaws boat ride, and that was due to the girl that was driving the boat she put alot of effort into her job) Rides were short, lines were long. Food is a bit pricey (to be expected though), Gyros (chicken) were unexpectedly good. Liked that they had fans in some of the lines to cool you down. What they did not lack was gift shops(rides exit into them), and someone trying to sell you something by saying "would you like to see a magic show". They are most certainly magicians, my money disapeared and I have no idea where it is. I would not recommend this place to anyone I know (that includes my enemies), I can't believe they stay in business. I will not be back........total waste.

I was looking forward to my day there and I took the day off and was so excited as I was taking my friend who had driven here from Georgia to spend Martin Luther King day, as that is a holiday for my friend. Arrived and after going tru the line , we rented a locker to keep our warm up suits and jackets in case the weather was colder toward the evening. TO my dismay , there were rides that were not working and shows that were close down and not working. such as back to the future--no excitement in park--no one making our day exciting---paid for something that we did not get. You should have all rides and shows up and running or let the customer know befor entering park,  Very dispointed with the day , we so looked forward to and spent only a few hours instead of the full day I had planned,  Scott Mitchell

I went with my friend to Universal and Islands of Adventure for 1 day. We bought an express pass since we knew we only had 1 day to do it all. The "express" lines seemed longer then the normal lines. I'm not sure the park keeps track of how many they sell. I wouldn't invest the extra money again. The mummy ride and MIB ride are both great.

We had two children with us when we visited Universal. I can say that had it been just adults it would have been a decent time but this park is just not very geared towards children. Yes, there are areas within the park that cater to little ones (though not too little, children under 5 years old would be hard pressed to find many rides they can go on) but overall having children with you won't work at this park. You are going to walk about a mile to get from the parking structures to the actual park entrance. They advertise motorized walkways but many were not on during the 3 days we went there. Then you are going to stand in ride for about an hour to go one a 90 second ride (hope the kids are patient to stand outside waiting for the adults since they cannot go on most of the rides). Also, DO NOT FALL FOR THE MEAL PASS. You pay $20.00 for an all you can eat for one day pass but there is only 4 places in the place that accept the pass and it takes about 40 minutes to get through the line to get food. Then the people that work at the places where you eat are nasty about portions and won't let you have enough to feed yourself and insist that you go through the 40 minute line again to get a (free) dessert to go with your dinner. All in all, you may have time and get a chance to eat about $10 worth of food and that is if you are willing to spend 90 minutes in a restaurant for each meal -which cuts time out of the day for standing in line at rides. You have to go through the 40 minute line just to get a free refill on your soda! NOT WORTH IT! If you are a family with kids go to Disney's Magic Kingdom. We were there for a 4 hour evening event (Pirate and Princess Party) and went on the same number of rides that we go to go on during 3 days at Universal. Plus, Disney had rides that little ones could go on. Skip Universal unless it is a really slow time of year. The staff is rude and can't muster a smile to save their lives and the lines are long. The food pass is a rip off.

We just got back from USO and IOA and it was great. (12/13-12/15) It was a ghost town! Most lines were only a 5 min wait, with the more popular rides (the Mummy, Shrek, The Simpsons) getting to be 30 mins or so. Stayed onsite so express pass :) With it we walked, and mean just walked onto all the attractions expect the simposons. We even rode the mummy a few times in a row by cutting through the child swap and flashing the hotel key.  I need to comment on the previous post however. The Meal Deal clearly states that it is for Burgers, Pizza, Drinks, ect. If you didnt read the pamphlet dont take it out on the park.  They had the Macys THanksgiving Parade there as well. It wasnt worth the hype, a few ballons and ballon floats but most of them were from parades in the past (like in the 80's) other then that the park used their own floats (the Mystery Machine) to fill in the parade.  All in all the park was great and Ill keep going back. Remember its not Disney so stop trying to compare them they are totaly different parks with different goals. So if your a disney person go there dont knock Universal for being different!

We took our grand kids (teenagers) to Universal Studios as a side trip to the Magic Kingdom. Our grandkids both agreed that Universal was far better than Disney. Attraction wait lines were minimal and covered (no waiting in the sun). They fell in love with the Mummy and rode it several times. Disaster was amazing (great special effects), and all the shows were great! Universal has surpassed Disney as far as we're concerned. Not only in entertainment but also in cleanliness and food quality. We come to Orlando 3-4 times a year and Universal will be at the top of 'to do' list.

We visited with a 3-day combination pass for Universal and Islands of Adventure, with EXPRESS PASS, AND the MEAL DEAL included . All FREE for a bonus trip through my husbands company. YES...a great experience but I have a few things to point out. You MUST get the EXPRESS PASS if you are going to truly enjoy this park! I actually felt GUILTY walking to the head of the lines at times, and getting right on the rides! But if you DON'T have the pass, you waste SO much time waiting...up to 90 minutes waiting in line for a 3 minute long ride!! Life is TOO short! The MEAL DEAL is a good value...but the choices that they give are ALL JUNK FOOD!!! We had been doing the South Beach diet prior to our visit and it was simply IMPOSSIBLE to eat within the rules!! Pizza, nuggets, burgers, fries, desserts..and NO drinks included. We will SURVIVE three days of junk, but I am NOT looking forward to getting on the scales tomorrow after all of my hard work over the previous 3 weeks!!  Rides to NOT miss: Woody Woodpecker's Nuthouse Coaster....the BEST for the kids AND Parents!! Simpsons...Jimmy Neutron... E.T. . .(DEFINITE MUST!!!)... The Animal Actors on Location....it's a live animal show...they loved it! JAWS....LOUD, SMELLY, HOT, and somewhat scarey for a 5 and 7 year old. Somewhat entertaining for us adults that grew up watching the JAWS movies!!  Didn't get the chance to do Twister and Disaster...too intense for the kids...would liked to have done Shrek 4 D....no help on these.  Bottom line...get Express Pass, (it is included with some of the nearby hotels like Hard Rock Hotel)....GO EARLY, buy it with the combo pass to Islands of Adventure which is more catered to young children! Take a lanyard (strap around your neck with a clear see through pouch) for the Express passes...you need to show them again and again. Wear cool clothes and comfortable sneakers with socks!! Have fun!!!!
park is no good for for small kids, very long walk from car, ET broke down so to did jaws, only good thing there was shrek 4d, food was poor, disney studios is much better, dont waste your money

What a waste of time and money. For the fortune it cost to get in and the WAY TOO HIGH cost of a Fast Pass, that isn't fast at all, you would be better off going somewhere else. In fact anywhere else. The rides are all outdated (the one new ride didn't even except the fast pass and there was a TWO HOUR WAIT. I was with adults, children and teens and not one of us had a good time. So don't waste yours. We were at the park on Friday, August 21, 2009.

After taking 2 trips to WDW, we decided to hit Universal (both parks) and Seaworld. Islands of Adventure, was a bit boring to us. The Spiderman ride was fun. We went on the Dueling Dragons "Fire". It was okay, but Kracken at Seaworld is better. None of the shows where playing so we headed over to the main park, Universal. We enjoyed most of the rides, but find the people to be unfriendly at both parks. Our favorite part was the Scary Movie Make-up Show. We may take another 1 day visit after the new Harry Potter area opens... maybe. Everyone should visit, even if just 1 time.

Some of these rides are really feeling their age, they are based on films that I would think most visitors under 20 wouldn't have heard of. My overiding feeling was of being underwhelmed and saying 'was that it??' The newest ride, the RockIt coaster which lets you choose your own soundtrack was a HUGE disappointment! I would definitely not recommend queuing for it. Didn't have time to select a song before it started so got some rubbish techno, the ride was dull and banged my head around a lot. And to top if off the cameras were broken so couldn't see the video of us riding. I'd say skip this park altogether and just go to Islands - the rides there are a million times better! Hulk is my favourite coaster ever.

I have been to Disney World many times so I thought I would give this park a try, just to see if I may also enjoy it. Our day started out bad and didn’t get much better. We went the Friday after Thanksgiving and found it to be not all that busy. Because of this, they had only ONE ticket stand open for those who wanted to purchase tickets there before park opened. Only five ticket purchases where in front of us. A half hour wait and the park was opening but we still did not make it to the ticket window. They finally did open a second window but the people all behind us in line moved over to that window.  Once in, the first ride we went to had an announcement saying because they were running ride at lesser capacity, the wait will be longer than usual. Park opened at 9am but some things inside did not open until after 10am. The Mummy ride was not open yet at 10:30 and the worker next to it said they do not have an estimated time of when ride will start. At one of the restaurants, they had only one person taking orders. Only until the line began to grow way beyond her ability, did they open two more stations. At night, place is poorly lit. POOR, POOR, POOR customer service at this park which is why I will not return here.  Not impressed with the rides in comparison to Disney. At least 5 rides we went on were mainly watching a movie and the seat moved or wet stuff hit you to make you feel you were there. That is ok for one or two rides but not be the majority. The best of these was the Simpsons because the visuals surrounded you. The Mummy ride was impressive but way too short. Glad the most we waited was 45min for this. Even that was too long for the seconds the ride lasted. In all, I would say the rides are OK. Some things are kind of cool but you get much more bang for you buck at WDW.

We are annual pass holders and I am amazed at some of the negative comments on here. Our kids are older (teens), so we really enjoy Universal and it runs circles around Disney. We have thought so for years - even when our kids were younger. The price for regular admission is such a bargain compared to WDW and their FastPass system is just a joke. I recommend either staying on the Universal property so the Express Pass is included in your stay (your room key becomes your Express Pass and is good for unlimited trips through each ride) or buying the Express Pass. I do recommend Spring or Fall to avoid the crowds, but we just spent NYE there and it was crowded, but wonderful.  Only negative regarding the park is that the new Rip Ride Rocket line is ridiculously long, even for single riders. There is no Express Pass option for this ride, so if you want to do it, you have quite a time commitment involved. I saw many improvements that could be made to that particular ride's operation (more cars, quicker turn around between cars, Express Pass option, etc), but that is my only negative comment on either park.  It is an incredible value for the entire family and we prefer it hands down to WDW!

Right off the bat, you get squeezed 12.00 for parking. Tickets into the park(s) were grossly overpriced.  Many of the workers could use some type of training in customer service. We didn't see very many of them smiling, either. A few of them were helpful but the majority seemed unhappy.  Their system of scanning fingerprints and ticket barcodes to enter the park was terribly inefficient.  It rained the day we were there and the leaks were unbelievable. I mean, there were leaks INSIDE several buildings. My kid was next in line to have his picture taken with Sponge Bob in the gift shop - which, of course, was strategically placed at the end of a ride (Jimmy Neutron, I think) - when one of the workers started yelling about a leak. The leak formed a large pool of water on the floor, ending the photo op. There were also leaks - I mean, really big leaks - from overhead coverings when standing in line at several rides. How could that be? It certainly wasn't the first time it ever rained in Florida. Shouldn't Universal have addressed those issues?  The lines weren't long but this was more than likely due to the weather.  The food at Mel's Diner was overpriced. The shakes weren't bad but our burgers were very dry. There were barely enough tables in there to seat all of the people who were eating.  The management of the Men In Black Alien Encounter (or whatever) was extremely poor. As we were getting in line, we were told that all bags had to be stored in small lockers off to the side. This meant getting out of line and walking over to the lockers which didn't have a direct route and was a total mob scene with everyone and their proverbial brother trying to get a locker and narrow walkways. The hold-up was that you are assigned a locker by entering information onto a touch screen. There were two screens that I saw and a mob of people trying to get at them. No workers were around to help or control the scene. No lines. Just a mass of people trying to get to the screens. Plus, part of the deal was that you hadda get your finger scanned. After the ride, it was much of the same. You hadda go to one of the screens and press some buttons to access your locker. To give you a better idea of what a mess this was, after punching in the requested information, a light on your locker goes on which, I guess, helps you locate it quickly. My locker was more than a few feet away from the screen. After I entered my information, the light went on and before I could get to it, some kid saw the light and opened my locker. Now, once the locker is shut you can't get it open. The system "thinks" you removed your belongings. So the girl saw something in the locker and started to shut it and I hadda yell for her to stop before the door closed. What a mess. Oh, and if you don't retrieve your belongings within 45 minutes or so, you have to pay to get your belongings back!  I will say that many of the rides we went on were clever and interesting. This includes Jimmy Neutron, Shrek, Men in Black, Simpsons (which was in the old Back to the Future building, I think), Terminator and Spiderman. ET was so boring that it was painful. And so was the Storm Accelertron (sp?). While on the subject, we thought that many of the Universal rides were blatant knock-offs of Disney rides. ET was like a cross between Peter Pan and Small World; Storm was pretty much the same as the Mad Tea Cup; and Men in Black was like Buzz Lightyear.  I can't imagine us going back again. In fact, the only reason why we went was because my wife got a free ticket as a promotion by Universal during this year's Super Bowl. (Remember the Denny's free breakfast promo?)

Years ago, I visited Univesal Studios with my husband and although the day was enjoyable, I mostly remember the line-ups. So many line-ups.  Today, with our three year-old daughter in tow, I can honestly say it was well worth the money. The Woody Woodpecker Kidzone was fabulous. She sang and danced at A Day in the Park with Barney, we spent an hour in both Curious George Goes to Town and Fievel's Playland, the line-up for Woody Woodpecker's Nuthouse Coaster was relatively quick (even on President's Day), and she enjoyed the Animal Actors show so much that we attended it twice! We also took in Shrek 4-D, and although I enjoyed it, I think it was a bit too scary for young children. All in all, a great day.

We loved Universal! I admit the lines are long, but aren't they always? My family liked it better than Disney and Sea World. Do you think Disney is going to have shorter lines? We could barely see the parade there!

There are some really great and innovative attractions here such as the recently opened Rip Ride and Rockit and also Shrek 4D and the Simpsons ride. There is plenty of film memorabillia around the park such as the Delorian from Back to the Future. There are aslo some good classic rides such as Jaws and ET. This was really quite when we visisted in November and with minimal queues you can do this in about half a day and even when it is busy I think you can probably do everything you want to do in a day. This is a really fun place and is mainly geared to older children and adults.

Granted, I am a bit biased- this was my sixth vacation to Orlando to visit Walt Disney World. Once before I went to Universal Studios, but it was a fairly uneventful trip and, at the time, I was disappointed to not visit the Islands of Adventure theme park. This time, however, we decided to take the extra trip away from Disney and go to Universal's Islands of Adventure with the main purpose of seeing the new Wizarding World of Harry Potter attractions. Boy, was this excursion a complete waste of money. I spent $174 for two tickets into this terrible park and, in the course of five hours, rode only two rides. The Harry Potter world was small, ridiculously crowded with no guest control and no directions. There were a hundred signs between Minnesota and Florida advertising this new attraction, but once you get into the park there is NOT ONE SIGN to lead you through their confusing paths to get to the Harry Potter section. Once we find our way, we wait in line at the Hogwarts Castle attraction for an hour- people crowded and bottlenecked into a shrinking room with no arranged line- walked through the bottom level of the castle, saw some stupid "sculpture" and a fake prop or two, and exited the line due to its lack of movement. Apparently, the ride had been broken all day. The other rides had terrible signage- you never really know which ride you are on line for. To make the experience worse, there were 30-minute-PLUS lines TO GET INTO THE SHOPS! Absolutely ridiculous. Universal obviously has no idea how to plan a park or have any type of crown control. Their ticket prices are also ridiculous- they do not offer nearly as many parks or amenities as Disney, yet they charge the same as Disney with the exception of their Express option. This is like Disney's "FastPass" with some differences: first- Universal CHARGES EXTRA ($55) for this option unlike Disney, which is free; second- there is no crowd control on their Express- hundreds of people can purchase this option and all rush to the Express lines, making the wait for an Express longer than stand-by... AND THEY CHARGE EXTRA FOR THIS! Needless to say, I felt that I wasted enough money on Universal to not spend anything else there. The only reason to put up with all of Universal's shortcomings is for the few thrill-rides they have- but those few are not really worth the disappointment (and I'm a roller coaster fanatic!). So, if you're trying to decided where to go for your Orlando vacation, I can say with complete confidence that Walt Disney World will never disappoint. With a Park Hopper +Water Park ticket, you get unlimited access to four theme parks, two water parks, DisneyQuest, transportation, and so much more! There is definitely something for everyone, and everything is easy to find, each and every thing is themed perfectly to the finest detail, and everyone there- including the staff- are all happy to be there. Trust me... you won't regret going to Disney.

I have mixed feelings about this section of Universal/Islands of Adventure. In some ways, they did a really good job with the design. Hogwarts looks really great but at the same time disappointing because of the significantly smaller scale they built it on. They situated it so you are looking up at it and this makes it look larger, and I am sure space was a factor, but still it is a bit disappointing on size. You don't actually go inside the castle for the ride, but it does make it appear that you are. The immediate outside waiting area is set up to resemble the greenhouses. When you go inside, you get the feeling of being in the castle and there are a lot of nice effects. They have the hour glasses counting the house points, but again to me they were on the small size and not very impressive. It includes a view into Dumbledore's office and a classroom. The ride loading area looks like the great hall complete with floating candles. There are some nice effects where you seem to actually see Dumbledore, Harry, Hermione, and Ron. The best effect imo are the paintings. They are cool, look like paintings with brushstrokes, etc. but move and talk. The ride itself is good, lots of thrills. We tried to time our two rides at about 9:30 p.m. before closing. This worked one time on Sunday night with a wait of about 30 minutes, but did not work the second time on Thursday night with about a 90 minute wait plus a ride malfunction which stopped the line two different times. The lockers are a bit of a pain as someone else commented, and I saw one woman who could not get her locker open after the ride because it did not seem to recognize her fingerprint.  The gift shop was not conveniently located and they should have made it much larger with much more merchandise to chose from. Hogsmeade is nice to look at, with snow on the rooftops, but again it is on a much too-small scale imo. The shops of Ollivander's and Honeyduke's were wayyyy too small, they would let in a certain number at a time and the lines to get in were horrendous. After our second ride on Thursday night, the park workers had made everyone who was not waiting for the ride leave the area because it was so late, and we were able to walk right into Honeyduke's and look around. Chocolate frogs are over $10 for one. We got into the Owl Post for a quick look - again, not well set up and much too small imo. A few stuffed owls sitting up high, a shelf or two with packages piled up, but the shelves below appeared to be filled with wand boxes. The singing frogs from one of the movies were cute, but they should have them stand on a raised platform. They stand on the ground inside a little fence and the only people who can see at all are the ones right at the front by the fence - no one else has a chance. Butterbeer can be purchased in a regular cup for $3.99 or a souvenir cup for over $10. My 2 cents on the taste is that it is like a butterscotch cream soda with a foam on top. So overall, I did like it and enjoy Harry Potter World, but at the same time it did not measure up to what I was hoping it would be like.

My family stopped en route back from a powerlifting tournament in West Palm Beach. Now, I'll admit that our entire family is larger than normal, but NONE of us has had a problem getting on rides at Disneyworld, Six Flags (Batman ride was close because of my height), or any fairs or festivals.  Because we only had one day, and have never been to Universal, we decided to spend our money there instead of Disney for a change. $345 for a family of four for a one park, one day pass (highway robbery, but Disney was the same price!!).  The kids selected Islands of Adventure because they like the rough rides. Line for Harry Potter was 2-hours as expected in July, but it seemed well organized with a park employee holding a sign to mark the end of the line. The employee also suggested getting in line after 3pm because it is much shorter. They even give you tickets half-way along to indicate any line jumpers.  Our first ride we tried to get on was the River Adventure in Jurassic Park...after 30 minutes of waiting, the ride broke. Nobody could give us an idea of how much longer it would be. Being we were towards the front of the line, we waited another 20 minutes. We asked again how much longer...5 minutes? 30 minutes? 3 hours? Nobody knew. There were no misters to keep everyone cool, so we decided to get out of line. As we were walking out the exit, the ride started back-up (grrrrrrr).  After getting drinks, Harry Potter line was much shorter. Got in line and was in Harry Potter area within 30 minutes. The line is not for a ride per se...it's just to get into the area!! Once you are in, it's a free for all! Lines abounded to poorly labeled rides/shops/etc. First ride we tried to get on was the Dragon Challenge roller coaster. Employee at the entrance said we had to sit in the test seats. Test seats?? Sure enough there were test seats for "Guests with certain body types". NONE of us fit in them...including my 13 year old daughter. Flight of the Griffendorf ride is LAME! The Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey ride had test seats too (no dice). WARNING...there are NO indications on the Universal park maps or on their web site WHICH rides have the test seats. Had we known THIS many rides had them, we could have made a more informed decision about where to spend our money (which is prompting a nasty letter from me to Universal).  Went back to River Adventure in Jurassic Park and it was working (ride #1).  Next tried to ride the Ripsaw Falls water ride in Toon Town. Guess what??? Test seat!! We could get in but you had to put your feet so close to your body that your knees were in your chest!! We decided to wait in line anyway. After an hour of waiting in the extreme heat (misters were not working and line area before going to inside qeue had NO misters and was enclosed so there was no breeze)...guess what BROKEN!!! The employees in the ride were making announcements, but they never turned the music down in the ride...so all you heard was mumbled jibberish. It was only after the third announcement could we make out the phrase "technical problems".  Went to Spider Man ride in the the Super Hero area. Got on the ride, but guess what??? It malfunctioned!! They let us jump back on again and it worked the second time around (ride #2 and 3?)  Test seats on Hulk coaster and Dr Doom Drop (no dice). The kids did get to ride Storm Force Accelatron (wife and I were so mad at this point we didn't want to ride) (ride #4). Both claimed it was lame (Tilt a Whirl at a fair was more exciting).  We had planned to leave at 6:00 anyway due to dinner reservations...so $345 and 8 hours later...we rode 3-4 rides due to time wasted to malfunctioning rides and size limitations.  I will NEVER go to this park again...even at my optimum weight because I would STILL not be able to fit on these rides.

We had a great time at Universal Studios and IOA! The rides at IOA were a blast, lots of coasters and speedy thrills. US was also really fun for its nostalgic rides/attractons and overall vibe.  WWHP was really a site to behold! After reading all of the books and watching all of the movies it was really quite cool to be walking through Hogsmeade and Hogwarts drinking a Hogs Head Ale or frosty Butterbeer.  BUT, they have a lot of work to do with WWHP. It is way too small for the amount of demand there is now and in my opinion will be for a long time. It is crammed at ALL times and feels pretty claustrophobic after an hour or so. I really wouldve liked for them to include some additional streets, like maybe a Diagon Alley area within. Also, There are only 2 rides (one of which is really for young children:flight of the Hippogriff) and theres the Forbidden Journey which is a simulator (beware for those that get nauseous on this type) and not even a ride. THEY NEED MORE RIDES! Great Idea but a lot more needs to be done before the idea becomes a true realization.  Also, City Walk was great times, nightime entertainment was top notch and we generally enjoyed the heck out of what it had to offer.  All in all a great park, but...Cant Be Comapred To The Park That Need Not Be Named!

It may have been a bad day when we were there but a lot of the rides had problems. The Rip Ride Rockit was not working properly and so you could not choose your own music and I see others have said there have been problems with this ride. There were also problems with Men In Black and I am sure The Mummy was slower than normal. I do love all the classic rides here though like Jaws. The Simpsons ride is great. Assuming it is not peak season you can do this park in half a day although if you have the time you may as well take it slowly as it will be hot. Universal staff are not particuarly friendly and unfortunately I am used to the friendliness of Disney so find this quite disappointing. This park is beginning to look a bit dated in places (I have been 4 times in the last 8 years) but I am not sure what they need to do. Although there were hardly any queues here when you do queue it is quite often out in the heat of the sun so a hat is a good idea.  Any questions just ask

Those visiting for HHN, be warned. They have teams of security looking for under age drinking and parents who may pass a drink to their kids to hold. Even if your kid is holding the drink for a second, they'll take you to a large processing area, take away your tickets, and ban you for a year. If you argue, you'll be arrested. Many people have been arrested for arguments with security. Do yourself a favor and stay away. The new HP shopping mall has long lines. The new roller coaster is always broke, because it's a carnival coaster.

End of September is a great time to visit Universal. If you start off early when the gates open you can avoid long lines and get a lot more done! I had a great time. The rides were fun and it wasn't too hot to walk around!

Had a fabulous time in Orlando in October, when the weather is cooler and the crowds are down. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is AMAZING! The Forbiden Journey ride is soooo cool - very high tech and realistic. Lunch at the Three Broomsticks, complete with butter beer, was great! For Harry Potter fans this place is Mecca, Graceland, and Neverland. Can't wait to go back! We all want to live at Hogwarts!

For those who want either a change of pace from Disney World or are looking for less kid-oriented rides/rollercoasters, Universal is the place to be. If you're like me and my boyfriend (we're 27), you won't need to a lot a ton of time there, unless you go during the busy season. We went in late January and were able to see everything and ride most of the best rides twice in only 1 day. This was before the addition of the Harry Potter area and the Simpsons ride, so this may have changed a little. All in all, I would definitely recommend Universal - if only for The Mummy, The Hulk, and Dueling Dragons alone.

Visited for first time. Looks just like you stepped into the movie. Butterbeer tastes like a creamy root beer with whipped cream on top. Stores are super small and you have wait on line to get in. 1 1/2 hrs to get into Olivanders, 20 min for Dervish and Banges. 40 min wait for 3 bromsticks which is a cafeteria type line. Dont forget to order somehing or you'll have to wait on line again. Food was good and atmosphere was great. Look for Dobby's shadow in the rafters. If you just want to buy a wand without the experience, they sell them at stores at front of park. Castle ride is great but has funky seats n people we saw who were not even big people had to request modified seats. They did a good job but have some things that need fixing.
organised, fun, and everything was in working order

We visited Universal for the first time on January 18th and 29th, 2011. My family thoroughly enjoyed both the "Islands of Adventure", and the "Universal" parks. We spent one day at each park so we could take our time to fully explore what each "side" had to offer. My best advice here is to avoid weekends and holidays if possible. The "Wizarding World" is a huge draw and the crowds reflect the curiosity of Harry Potter fans. Having said that, we loved the Wizarding World. It is so authentic. If you're not a Harry Potter fan you wouldn't understand. We had Butterbeer, bought a wand, ate at the Hogsmeade restaurant, and rode the 3 major rides. This area of the park just gets busier and busier as the day goes on. Go there first when the lines are the shortest. The shops get very crowded, but my family agreed it was worth it! As for the rest of "Islands of Adventure" and "Universal"; lots of fun for everyone. The parks are very clean. Rides and attactions terrific. The prices are not too bad. The Universal side has some really nice restaurants. If you are a theme park buff you will enjoy Universal immensly!!

I'll try to be brief. I feel robbed or at least cheated with our recent visit. It cost over 500.00 and received almost nothing but aggravation. Parking was slow and took at least 20 minutes. Attendants were yelling at guests. We were yelled at to get our stroller off a walk way. We were solicited to buy a credit card. After a long walk we were confronted with another long wait to buy tickets (45 minutes) and more sales attempts (this same process took about 5 minutes at Disney at half the cost). After the hike to Harry Potter we were turned away to go wait in another long line for a timed entrance pass in a very crowed area, also getting yelled at because the whole family was in line not just a representative. (Why this couldn’t be addressed at ticketing or at least the info for the need to get another ticket!) During the day I was only able to go on 3 rides, my family 4. At Disney the hours were always extended due to crowds, at Universal it was the opposite. An employee told us closing was at 8:00 but after assuming there was time to eat (at the worst food in the world, Burger Digs.. We left finding the park closed at 7:00 and unable to do ANYTHING else. At Disney parks we could see characters, shop and linger, nothing at Universal. Harry Potter was somewhat well done but not made for crowds at all, again yelled at for going the wrong way or wrong door. Then the family was subjected to walking thru all the bars and party atmosphere on leaving, not meant for a family. I will never return, I truly feel foolish for throwing away hard earned money to be miserable and feel like I was an inconvience not a guest. If there were a money back guarantee I would be asking for my money back, what a rip off. We left Disney feeling happy with a wonderful experience we left Universal feeling like the only interest was to make money, which of course it is.

we expected it to be expensiveand it is, but the quality of the food there is dreadful - mostly 'fast food' rubbish, including cold, slimey fries, dry sandwiches,and very very few choices. We recommend taking 'good food' with you and water as well. Our biggest disappointment was with the Harry Potter ride. It was difficult to judge what it was like from the outside as all rides seem to have the same 'warnings' on them. I would suggest a rating of say 1 to 5 based on motion, scaryness, or some other variable to give people more information about rides before they go on them. Neither of us are particularly squeamish but this ride is a violent and vomit-inducing experience that I wouldn't recommend to anyone. We felt we had somehow 'survived' the experience, rather than enjoyed it.

My daughter was looking forward to going to the Harry Potter attractions at Universal. Yet when we arrived we found the park to be misleading and unorganized. We were shuffled through numerous lines in order to even enter Harry Potter World, and once we arrived at the final stand-by line we had to stand in the unbearable heat for over an hour. To top it off, while we were in line the one drink stand ran out of water! When we finally got into the park all of the rides were over an hour wait and the heat was so excruciating that it was impossible to wait, can't they install some fans for those waiting? Overall, my daughter only got to go on one ride at the entire park of Universal because the line waits were ridiculous. We would have bought the express package if the prices weren't already so absurd. This park is NOTHING compared to Disney. Universal should take a training course from Disney so they can learn how to run a park.

I found Disney to be too spread out and a lot of the rides that werent aimed at kids were old and tired looking. Universal on the other hand was as handy as it could be with both parks right beside eachother and within walking distance from I Drive. Most days I went to the park mid afternoon to avoid most of the queues (and the heat) and was rewarded with shorter lines and a much more pleasant experience. The rides here are way better than anything I experienced at Disney (with the exception of the tower of terror) the mummy ride, hulk, jurassic park, dr doom, harry potter, simpsons and rip ride rockit rides were all first class. Don't shy away from the cartoon area in IOA like I nearly did, it has some pretty good rides like rip saw falls and the bilge rat barge, however expect to get wet, no matter where on the ride you sit expect to get soaked! The eateries in the two parks are average, with all seemingly serving the exact same choices of food. A better bet would be to venture out unto city walk and give the hard rock cafe or nascar a try! Overall these two parks are well worth a visit, even more so with a fast pass to beat the long queues in that heat!

I went to Universal a few weeks ago and they had some great rides. I loved the Mummy ride, Simpson ride and Spiderman was awesome! We went to Universal Studio's the 2nd day of our trip after Harry Potter. It was nice because it wasnt crowded and the most wait time was15 minutes. I liked the way the rides were set up because as hot as it was outside we stayed cool with most of them being inside or under cover. Even know i liked the Unversal Islands better this was a nice park and i will be back next year!

My wife and I visited on a Thursday at the end of June. I was coming back after 10 years and remembered some of the attractions, which were getting dated, such as Twister, Jaws, Terminator, ET. The newer stuff (Shrek 4-D), Rip Ride Rocket (excellent), and Simpsons were serviceable but with the exception of the roller coaster, were much more pointed towards children. As adults without children, I would suggest Islands of Adventure if you had to make a choice. With kids, Universal would have been good for them.

My family has been to most of them and we all agree that Islands of Adventure rated the worst. We opted for the lower level fast-pass to shorten our wait times, but approx 600 hundred dollars for just the tickets for a family of four - I got ripped off. Most hi-end parks we end up closing the place because there's so much to see & do but here we were done by 4pm.  My teens love fast roller coasters, so deuling dragons and the HULK were fun! But most of the other rides felt outdated. Poseidon looked so cool on the outside! But it comes across as silly inside. Jurassic Park - yawn. Dr. Seuss land was visually stunning, but nothing for teens there. Superhero section was also weak - but we rode HULK multiple times and that was great.  Half my family are Harry Potter fans - so we waited 45 minutes in line JUST TO GET A TICKET TO ENTER Harry Potter village later in the day. When it was our time it was so crowded you could barely get through it - constantly squeezing your way through the crowds. There were 30 minute waiting lines to get into any of the shops. Probably about 15 minute wait for a mug of butter beer. We threw away a couple of hours there and saw next to nothing. The HP ride was ok. I find rides that rely on you watching video screens tend to make me nauseous.  Lunch was another disaster. We waited in a line for over a half hour in the hot sun and only two people walked away with food. Haven't they been doing this a while? Haven't they figured out how to sell product to the masses day in and out? Apparently not. We bailed out of line and grabbed a water and a pretzel at a cart. TIP for those still willing to waste their hard earned money and go: for lunch go back to the entrance because there are more dining options.  Save some money, increase your fun, and go to a Six-Flags - most that I've been to were a lot more fun than this. Disney & Sea World also kick butt on this place.

I was extremely impressed! I am so glad we did 2 days here. 1 at each park. From the covered parking garage to the rides, it was all such high quality. I felt like we were being pampered! The park was clean, food was great, rides were fun. We went with a 12 and 15 year old. My 15 year old and myself had more fun here than the other well known place in Orlando. We could all ride everything together. There are so many simulator rides here and those are so cool! Harry Potter land was packed but so worth the wait on the main ride there. It was amazing! It feels like you're right in the movie. I suggest hit this part first thing, early a.m. It gets really packed later. I wish we wouldhave stayed at one of the universal resort hotels because with some of them you get a "Fast Pass" which isn't free otherwise. Something to definitely look into! The stores there were great too. We even stopped at the "dinner reservation" cart in the park and asked about the Hard Rock. They told us they don't take reservations but they gave us a preferred seating ticket with a $5 coupon and we got right in. It's so convenient to have all that right there. We spent about 8 hours in each park and did almost every ride there. They even have free lockers up to a certain amount of time. I never paid for 1 and used one several times. Also the moving "flat escalators" were very nice for my son who was recovering from a fractured ankle. We had a blast!

We visited the parks mid-July and did both in 1 1/2 days not feeling like we missed out on much. The most helpful tip I had received before leaving proved true: we got there early on both days (8:30am) and the longest line we did was for The Forbidden Journey (about 50min).  Universal Studios: we did this park at the end of the 1st day (got there around 4pm and it wasn't that crowded) and on the 2nd day (we left around 2:30pm). We really liked how it has older and newer attractions and our favorites were the Rip Ride Rockit, Spiderman and The Mummy. The park was very clean, and the longest we waited there was probably for the Terminator because it's a show. There is plenty of shade (more than in IoA) and I feel the park is more family oriented than IoA. Because the lines weren't too long we could use the lockers for free, which allowed us to always have our water and food with us. I found the staff to be friendly and helpful. My main critic is that you have to pay for the express pass, but there are also single riders line on some attractions that are as fast as the express line. ->Tips<- - get there early morning or late afternoon - have a good breakfast, pack snacks and drinks - bring flipflops for water rides, sneakers for the rest - bring a rain jacket (so you don't buy junk rain ponchos) - eat outside of the park if you can (had lunch at the Hard Rock, was very filling, we got free refills and the price was reasonable: $35 for 2) - bring a backpack - use single riders line when available (cuts wait time and it doesn't make a big difference who you're sitting next to anyway) - take plenty of pictures and enjoy!  Islands of Adventure: see review on the specific page

is a great park, but the should have more different restaurant that were you can do the meal deal , not just 3 places or at least let you get more soda in different location so you can refill anywhere, but over all is a decent price for the the meal deals and will probably get it again, park was slow so we were able to go in the attraction much quicker but it better to plan the whole day before heading to the parks and if its slow not to get the express pass, i cant wait to go back down for hallowing horror nights.

this was our first visit and we did not realise that universal is split into 2 parks until it was too late. we bought tickets and entered one side of the park when we wanted to see the other, but didnt realise what had happened for a couple of hours. we really wanted to see harry potter, and the dr suess attraction. we accepted it was our mistake and asked if we could pay the difference and upgrade to the2 park ticket for the final 2 hours, and were told no we would have to purchase a full new ticket, which we could not afford. very poor customer service for niave first time middle aged visitors.

I went here with my family 10 years ago and thought it might be an entertaining vacation again....WRONG. The rides are old...the food is dreadful...the shows are also outdated and hokey. Roughly $1000 for two days-parking, lunch,stupid chahka...What was I thinking!!!!?? Spend your dough on a beach vacation in Naples. Orlando is really a boring place

I spent a perfect day here! I loved Terminator 2 3D, Shrek 4D and The Simpsons Ride. It was very funny! E.T. Adventure was really cute. Whole park had a great movie atmosphere. At the evening there was an amazing Mardi Gras Parade and Ne-Yo sang there.

Universal Studios offers fun for family members of all ages. All attractions are accessible by wheelchairs.. etc. Express pass is a must. This comes when staying at an onsite hotel. Jaws, The Mummy, Men in Black, and ET were really fun. The October month is great because Halloween night time events are incredible. There are complimentary lockers available at most rides. Food is not priced too bad-no worse than other parks. Food plans and refillable cups are available-may be good option.

So I came back to Orlando after 12 years and we visited Universal studios and Islands of Adventures. The first park is a rip-off. So aparently there was only one park, 10 years ago, and they added some attractions and divided them into 2 parks, to charge more money. They should be one park, because Universal studios has ery few attractions, most of which are really old. Jaws and ET, for instance, are unimpressing, considering today's technological standards. They have a few shows, and 4D attractions like Shrek and the Simpsons. The Simpsons is great, but it doesn't justify the 90 USD that you pay to get in. Twister, even it it is old, is still very nice, but again, 2 cool attractions do not justify the 90 USD. Nor does the rollercoaster. In Islands of adventures, there are better rollercoasters. If I had to go back again, I wouldn't waste my time going to Universal Studios, I'd just go to Islands of Adventures. Now, that park isn't great either. There are some cool attractions, several actually, but the only one that is really well done is the Harry Potter land. They have not paid attention to detail, like Disney does, at the other attractions. There is no "concept" behind the rollercoasters, for instance the Hulk rollercoaster has nothing to do with the Incredible Hulk really. Disney parks are so much better at creating an atmosphere and telling a story as you ride. My advice: go to Islands of Adventures and skip Universal studios, it's just not worth it. And if you have small children, you might as well skip Islands of Adventures, since most of the rides have height requirements that would leave your kids out.
Lots of options for kids of all ages! Great rollercoasters and shows!
Our 11 year old loved the thrill rides. Our 4 year old loved the little kids area. Rides seem to break down often, though. Some really long lines.

Took the kids to Universal and Islands of Adventure. They had a blast. Kids really liked the new Rip Rocket coaster and everything in Islands of Adventure was liked. Staying at the Universal Hotels for the free Express Pass is HUGE!!

We don't have kids and we've found that Disney doesn't offer us much. We took this trip to spend time at the Universal Parks. It was great fun. Harry Potter Ride is amazing and SCARY! We love Revenge of the Mummy. It is probably our all time favorite ride. Halloween Horror nights was like a dream (or nightmare) come true! So much fun being scared and the production values of the 8 houses was fantastic. We spent 4 days at both parks and didn't get bored at all.

Over the years we have found early November to be the perfect time to visit WDW. The weather, though not great for swimming, is warmer than the Northeast and there are very few crowds to contend with. Last week was our first visit to Universal and we found the same held true. My adult daughter and I purchased the 2 day park to park pass which we took advantage of. Our first day was spent at Universal Studios, but at 5pm we went over to Islands of Adventure for 2 more hours. Then the next day we started at Islands, but jumped back to the Studios to re-ride the Mummy. We did not purchase the Express pass at $20/day and did not regret that decision. Our longest wait was 10-15 minutes for the Mummy ride and some group-type shows, but basically, we walked onto every other ride without a wait. Our greatest surprise was in the Harry Potter area. We had to slow ourselves to see everything on the long walks to the rides in the castle and the coasters so we wouldn't miss what people there on high traffic days would be entertained by during their long wait. With the lack of crowds we were able to see everything we wanted and several rides we did twice.
Unless you want to pay through the nose of all the hard earned money you made last month, go. This place is nothing but a shopping mall that charges admission.

We went to Islands of Adventure on our first day. I thought Universal Studios Orlando Resort was much small and less to do, but it really isnt. You will do more casual walking around and not as much stress and as crowded as Islands of Adventure, but still lots to do. The Simpsons Ride (replaced the older back to the future ride) is a must. Only drawback is, if you get there when they open, which I highly recommend, you can literally do all the rides you want and see what you want to see in less than 4 hours. Pretty expensive for 4 hours. If you show up later in the day, on busy days expect 30 to 60 minutes per ride and it take a lot longer to see everything. No problem though, just head out to City Walk, eat at Hard Rock Cafe, Jimmy Buffets, Pat O'Briens, or catch a movie at the huge theater, then head back in.

We went between Christmas and New Years. Biggest crowd the park has ever experienced. Regular Lines were over an hour long, made even longer by those using express pass. Resort was really neat, just too crowded on this trip.

The Universal Orlando - Islands of Adventure was a fun park to visit. There were fun rides and the Wizarding World of Harry Potter entertained us. The butter beer, wand shop, Hogwarts, etc.... had our 15 year old in awe. OK I loved the way they created a world so identical to the the movie world. it was more fun than I expected.

The whole experience was overwhelming and as an oldie I did not think that I would enjoy it however I could not have been more wrong. I wished I could have stayed in the park for a week because there was so much to see and do. Harry Potter was exceptional and I will return for a longer period very soon.

I have visited Universal's Islands of Adventure before and love it. I was equally impressed with Universal itself. I do think the rides on this side are more fun. HOWEVER, there is a lot of construction going on so it seemed like a lot of the park was closed or inaccessible. I am looking forward to attending when it is completed.

My family and I went to Universal Studios Orlando on the weekend of Feb 17 and 18. Kelly Clarkston had a concert scheduled in the part at 8 pm on the 18th. That is the exact time the park closes. The crowds quickly formed at the site of the concert. The geniuses at Universal were forcing everyone to go throught the concert site even if all you wanted to do was leave the park. That is all we wanted to do. There was no way that we could make it thru the crowd to leave. We tried to back track to try to go around but the Universal emplyees stopped us and sent us back. I tried to explain that we just wanted to leave and had no desire to see the concert. My young children were overwhelmed by the crowds but the emplyees didn't care. It took us about forty five minutes to get to a restaurant that happened to have two doors. I thought we could cut thru but the crowds jammed the door ways and no one was going anywhere. If there had been a fire or an emergency, there would have been many many people hurt or killed. I even asked one of the emplyees if there was anyone we could call to let us out of the park and she said that I would have to wait until the concert was over. We kept trying and finally back tracked around the entire event not paying attention to anyone that tried to stop us and after an hour and a half finally made it out. I I was planning on getting my kids some souverneirs but by that time the store where we wanted to get them was closed. It was 10:30 pm before we had dinner. Their lack of planning ruined an otherwise good day. It will be a very very long time before I ever return there. This would have never happened at Disney.

We were somewhat disappointed with Universal Orlando Resort. The place really starting to show it's age. Jaws, King Kong, Back To The Future & Earthquake ALL GONE...I really enjoy the NYC area and the Blues Brothers, but overall this park is a let down. I guess it must be tough to keep up with the mouse, but Disney parks and attractions easily trump Universal's meager offerings.
Stay on site for early access and line jumping privileges.
Harry Potter was great. Food prices are really high but it was fun.

It's not good to have the feeling you're ripped off right from the start of the day. When we first purchased tickets, we were told that if you want to skip the long lines, fork over $40 more. That's on top of the $120 per ticket (we got the two park pass). I had already visit Disney where tickets were $90 each and they offer the short line option called fastpass for free to everyone. So right off Universal left a bad taste in my mouth. The rides are more geared for adults and teenagers. The grandparents and my kids (younger than 5) didn't enjoy most of the rides with the exception of Spiderman and Cat in the Hat in Island of Adventure. I was excited to ride Harry Potter but the anticipation was better than the actual ride. The wait can be really long unless you go into the single rider line or paid the extra $40 to skip the regular line. The roller coasters were okay. We couldn't do a lot of the rides (height limit as well as not age appropriate) as a family so that took away the experience. They have a parent swap where one parent can ride while the other stays with the kids then they switch but this is not as fun as riding together. Overall I will not visit this place again.
very dated with movie themes that I saw but my kids did not such as terminator, men in black and storm chaser. Not very much to do, not great rides and kids wanted to leave by lunch.

Took the kids there for Spring Break and it was great. I think I had more fun than they did. Going later in the day was definitely a good idea as the lines were shorter and we only had 15 to 20 minute waits for rides. Even enjoyed "Fear Factor", realized that the "Simpsons" ride is where "Back to the Future" used to be. Our two day pass was more than enough, actually got to see most of the parks this time. Universal and Island of Adventure are great parks and really fun filled for the whole family, we had a great time.

We had a fabulous time at Universal! The longest we waited in line for a ride was 15 minutes for the Spiderman attraction. Most of the time we could walk right up and get on the ride.  Absolutely loved our time at Universal!

Finally was able to afford to go to Universal Studios in Orlando, Florida. Haven’t been there in a very long time. Also, been to your park when it first opened. Made 2 reservations for the park tickets and hotel directly through the Universal Orlando Web Site for 6 of us in total. My wife, 2 nephews, and my in laws. After making the long drive arrived on Monday April 23 until Friday April 27, 2012. Went to Harry Potter World/Islands of Adventures on Tuesday and to Universal Studios on Wednesday. Been wanting to go to your Harry Potter World since it first opened but hasn’t been able to go until now.  To summarize the whole thing, let’s just say that it was a very bad experience and at the end a waste of money. To make things worst, my father in law was on a wheelchair and did not found out until leaving the park on the last day that you offer an “express” pass for people in wheelchairs to make things easier and with assistance. No one said anything about that when we got to the park the first day. Also on your ride at Universal Studios – The Simpsons – had us standing up waiting in the room that you go in before getting on the actual ride for a long time when found out afterwards that could have go in there with the wheelchair and sit and wait.  We also purchased on the first day your meal pass with the drink cups. The food was terrible, cold, and not really worth the money. Was told that the next day will get free drinks since already got the cups and to bring them back. The next day when went to get drinks was told that there was not free and will cost $.80 cents per refill. This shows that was lied about it. Since on the first day the food was horrible and not good, did not purchased the food meal deal the next day.  Also was told that when buying the rides pictures, each picture after the first purchase will be $10.00 each with the photo connect card. That seemed not to be the case when went to get a picture at the Men in Black ride (this wasn’t the first time buying a picture) and was charged the full regular price.  At the end of the second day at Universal Studios went by your guest services department to talk to someone about the entire 2 days bad experience and was told by the guest service representative that was there that had to call a supervisor to talk about of what happened and such. After waiting for 45 minutes no supervisor showed up at all which shows very well that they don’t care at all. Ended up leaving the park.  Also most of the rides that your parks offer now are roller coasters and not meant for the whole family. This makes it not a park for the whole family.  You got rid of the Back to the Future ride and replaced it with The Simpsons. Same type of ride but different “theme”. That does not makes it new, and by the way the Back to the Future ride was much better. You also get rid of Jaws and is closed and nothing there, also seems to be in the process of building a ride for Dispicable Me and Sponge Bob. Your Terminator 3D you seemed to have cut the “show” in half and got rid of a lot of it. We are all very unhappy and dissatisfied with our visit. What it was supposed to be a fun vacation it wasn’t.  For what it cost in total going to your theme parks would have gone to somewhere else like Disney and I bet it would have been much better.  I will tell everyone I know about my terrible experience with you and to beware and consider not going and go somewhere else.  The only reason ended up going to Island of Adventures is because that is where Harry Potter World is and no other way of going to it without going to Island of Adventures.  Universal it is NOT what it used to be when started, that is for sure. Going down the drain !

Universal Studios, as in the park has became very poor. Most of the rides are alright ( The Mummy is probably my favorite of them all ) this park is just a collection of rides, no real theme or connection between them. The parks one real bit of theming which is the Streets, has been ruined by the building of the Rockit rollercoaster ( see picture ). If you want just rides then it wouldn't be an issue, but if you had to chose between here and Islands of Adventure then its no contest in both theme and rides.
Amazing park. Time spent in Univeral Orlando Resort we will remember for a long time. We were in the park in February and there was not a lot of people. I recommend this park to everyone.

Our flight was in by 830 am and we were at Universal Studios by 10 am....after renting a car! Celebrating Mardi Gras......easy parking,.....long walk in tho...but we were so excited it didnt matter.....Was an excellent day....visited just about all the attractions we wanted to.....just one complaint.....we were there from the airport and I had my handbag and wasnt admitted to an attraction...had to put it in a locker that was outside the attraction.....I was not comfortable with leaving my bag with all my credit cards and cash out there so we did not go on the ride. We stayed all day and nite for the parade and concert with Cyndi Lauper! Perfect first day in Orlando with my teenager son! We will be coming back in July with both my sons!

Went on May with 4 teenagers -- had a blast. our time was limited so we scheduled well the rides to hit 2 parks ( Islands of Adventure and the regular Universal) in one day. It was doable bec the place is compact (unlike Disney). Saved money and time. Most favorite ride is The Harry Potter one and all the wet rides... There are free lockers to store belongings -- leave huge bags home/hotel bec they will not fit. When hungry and tired after the whole day of gallivanting? No worries -- a lot of restaurants to choose from in the Universal City walk. Parking is covered building -- NICE !!!

I had high expectations, me, my husband and 10 yr old son. There wasn't much to do in there. The day we went, we walked on to everything, no lines, and we even had fast passes and didn't need them. I thought it was old, and outdated. The ET ride is OLD! The Jaws ride is gone, and that whole area is under construction. The MIB ride....kinda lame....Disaster...ugh, kind of a disaster. Twister....o.k. kind of lame. Shrek was fun, and that was about it. We got pix with the characters there, that was okay. We saw everything and left the park at 3:00pm. I won't go back there, I would rather go to something else. Local news reported 2 price hikes in a month on tickets and people were screaming about it. The bathrooms were shut down twice for flooding...This place in't worth the money.
the cleanliness, the rooms, and the closeness to all Disney places.
Great day. Loved the characters around the park. New Spongebob shop opened a week before with everything you could ask for and Shrek 4d and Terminator 3d shows were brilliant.

We took the kids for spring break to go and see Harry Potter. That was the main attraction. It was ok. It was so crowded. I guess that goes with the was it is. Everything was an upgrade. not too cheap. The food was not good. Especially for the price. But all in all it was a fun day and the kids had a good time. It is a good one time place to go. Next time we will go to Cedar Key instead.
a must visit for adults and children alike. with live shows and movie themed rides. had a wonderful day there and will definatley be going again

Wonderful park! Great attractions for the kids, teenagers and adults. We even had fun in the rain. There were lots of rides open and activities to do in the rain with ponchos. Everyone enjoyed themselves!

Although I'm not an avid film goer, I had read about the attractions here, and as a bit of a ride junkie, universal was on my bucket list. We arrived early, and turned right towards the ET ride - this meant we missed a lot of the queues, and managed 3 rides in the first hour. The great thing about Universal Studios in the summer is that most of the attractions and queues were inside in air conditioning, and were largely unaffected by the frequent storms. As long as you get your head around the fact that Universal Studios is a park to showcase film effects, and not a theme park based around rides, you will not be disappointed. My own personal disappointment is that we are Brits in America on the 4th July. We wanted to see a July 4th Firework display and Universals website said that there would be an addition to their normal evening spectacular. Unfortunately, this was not the case, and we had to make do watching other fireworks in the distance. Had we not been mislead, we would have chosen Seaworld for the 4th of July, as their display was apparently themed for Independence Day.

We visited Universal on the last day of our holiday and were sorely diappointed. Universal Studios was the only one we visited where we found dirty disgusting toilets. The queues were horrendous with well over an hour for most of the popular attractions. Yes, you can buy an express pass but it costs $70 per person where Disney has the fastpass system which is free. This almost doubles the cost of your day. Also some of the attractions are dated and have not been changed for many years, Twister and Disaster being the more noteable of these.

We went to Universal Studios Islands of Adventure last week (07/27/12) because our children (ages 11, 20, and 22) really wanted to go to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Our master plan was to ride the Dragon Challenge (both the Chinese Fireball and the Hungarian Horntail), the Flight of the Hippogriff, and the Hogwarts Castle Tour Ride (aka Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey).  However, we were immediately drawn into Hogsmeade village as soon as we walked in. We had our photos taken on Platform 9 3/4, alongside the conductor for the Hogwarts train. Then, we walked into various shops - Dervish & Bangs, Honeydukes, Zonko's, and of course, Ollivander's Wand Shop. All of the shops were mobbed. For those of you who MUST purchase a wand, it should be mentioned that you can obtain 'popular' wands (such as the Harry Potter wand) at ANY of the Universal Studios shops on site.
