However, if you want one of the other more obscure character wands, you need to go to Ollivander's.  Back to the rides - we enjoyed all the rides in Harry Potter World. IMHO, the Hungarian Horntail was the best ride, but many preferred the Hogwarts Castle Tour ride. We loved the village of Hogsmeade and enjoyed the Three Broomsticks restaurant. It was nice and cool and not crowded at all when we were there. Out of the five of us, only two of us enjoyed Butterbear. Be advised - it is very sweet and tastes like butterscotch. I enjoyed it very much, but my daughter became a little queasy after drinking it, then walking around in the heat and riding the rides.  Because we were @ Universal Studios from a cruise ship, we were on a very limited time schedule, and just planned to spend our entire time @ Harry Potter World, and did not ride any of the other rides except for Poseidon's Fury which we all enjoyed. I had wanted to ride the Incredible Hulk ride, but couldn't guilt any of my family members to ride it with me.  All in all, the Islands of Adventure Theme Park was tremendous fun, and we would have enjoyed spending more time there.

The organization of this attraction is dangerous. To start, there are three exits to this ride, one of which is before the waiting area for parents so your kids can exit without you seeing them. There are height limitations so parents cannot enter, you send your kids off for 45- 60 mins unsupervised. My wife and I split up to ensure our kids couldnt exit without out finding them, no seating area at one of the exits. Upon questioning a worker about the set up he also said it was not good. This is an attraction that is poorly arranged, limits supervision for parents, and is a lawsuit waiting to happen. Dont send you on this ride, its not work worrying for an hour, which is what all parents were doing--No FUN.

I must say Islands of Adventure is by far the most fun park I have had the opportunity to visit. After a week at the Disney parks I wasn't sure what to expect. The rides were fantastic. I have never screamed or laughed more. My grandson became ill on the Harry Potter ride and he was treated with great compassion. The staff came over and talked with him and ask about clothing size. They promptly returned with a new t-shirt and apologized for not having shorts in his size. We were instructed to go to a close by shop and get him a pair of shorts to change into and called ahead for a fast pass on any ride of our choice. We had an awesome day. I personally loved the Harry Potter ride and rode multiple times but avoid if you experience motion sickness. The Hulk, Dr. Doom, Spider-Man were also great thrill rides. The water rides are fabulous. You will get wet!

These are always a good parks but I would say they are not tailored so much for the younger children. Some great rides here at both parks I am not going to name them as I would list most of the rides here. The Halloween horror nights are great this year was not as good as previous years but still worth going to. My only slight moan is the shows at both park leave a bit to be desired I would say they are ok but would not want to see them too often. But don’t let this put you off seeing them for the first time.

Great: Harry Potter area, Forbidden Journey, Dueling Dragons coaster (only in the front row of seats), stores and Three Broomsticks restaurant. Hulk roller coaster is still terrific. Noticed this time that head snapping is accentuated in the seats closer to the back.  Good: Spiderman, Minion Mayhem, Simpsons, Storm Force (very short, so only good if no line), Hippogriff (for kids or weenies), Rip Ride Rocket (no Express Pass, not worth a long wait), Camp Jurassic (for kids who like to climb and explore).  So/so: Mummy, Pteranodon Flyers (good for kids, but wait can be ridiculous -- we walked on during early admission), Jurassic Park River Adventure.  Terrible: ET, Poseidon's Fury, Suess Landing (whole thing, except for smallest kids, and if your kids are this small, you have no business paying big money for you all to come to this park), Twister, Men in Black.  So many areas are crying out for demolition/staring over. I think they would have been better off keeping Jaws (had kitsch appeal, like Disney Jungle Cruise) and wiping out Lost Continent, Suess Landing, and other areas which are really pathetic and have become places to walk through on your way to other areas.

A lot of the 3D experiences are old and tired and really not up to today's technology savvy guests. I wouldn't bother waiting for E.T, Terminator and especially or Shrek or Twister.  Also, after we had waited for ages for the Dispicable Me parade, it finally arrived and some of the dancers that got off it, just stood around having a conversation. First of all with each other, then walked over to a cafe and a cafe worked walked out and then all 3 of them stood there having a gossip. Please see photos. I couldnt help but think, 'this would never have happened at Disney'  One of the few good things about Universal is the child swap option which allows some people in your party to queue and the others to go into a holding room with the pushchairs and then when the first group finishes, you are walked straight to the front of the queue.  To be honest, everyone in our party said that we wished we had never bothered going to Universal at all. Especially when we had Disney tickets, which far surpasses this resort. We only went because it is so legendary but I doubt this will be the case for much longer....  Please note, this does not stand for Islands of Adventure, which was brilliant. An added entry cost though.

My wife and I have been to this park so many times and its worth it. The rides are exhilarating! The staff was always around to answer questions. Although the food is just ok. I wouldn't recommend it for young children. More for the adults to do than the kiddies.

We love Universal Studios! There is literally nothing about Universal that we didn't like - even the food was great! The park is very well laid out and as we visited the week before Thanksgiving the christmas decorations were out in full force and looked wonderful. And as for the rides and shows - brilliant! The two Universal parks are streets ahead of the Disney parks in my opinion - we had a great time in both, can't fault them!

We took our 5 year old twin boys to Universal Studios along with 4 adults the week after Thanksgiving. It was a great time to go because all rides were walk on which was nice. There is not a whole lot there for younger kids to do especially during Winter/Fall when the water attractions are too cold to do. My kids did love the balladium area in the Curious George playground. They played there for a solid hour and would have gone longer! They also enjoyed the Men In Black ride. They rode that 7 total times! Adults loved that ride too. The Mummy coaster was very fun. I was not a huge fan of the Rip Ride Rockit coaster.  We watched the nighttime movie tribute show and it was okay but I was not super impressed. Same for their parade. Just not up to Disney quality. But maybe they are okay with that. The employees were friendly and efficient. Not great for food allergies at counter service restaurants because all their pizza dough is processed in a factory with peanuts so our go to peanut free food (pizza) was not even safe. So we had to eat at Finnegans where they made him a grilled cheese by special request that was safe.  I think this is more for older kids or adults and teens because of the thrill rides but they do have enough so that there is something for the whole family. They were building a huge new ride while we were there. The worst ride is the Shrek 4 D. It was just terrible. No other way to describe it. Despicable Me was the better 4 D show so I say just do that one and skip Shrek.

Universal did not meet our expectations at all. The employees did not seem happy.  Harry Potter was amazing the whole area was done very well. However it was very crowded. This is not a place for toddlers and grandmas. I really wish we would have known this before we went. My baby ended up spending all day in the stroller and my mom was bored. We liked the rides but I don't think I would spend the money to go back.

We paid $850 for the family. Took us an hour to get in. Then proceed to wait in lines that were as long as 3 1/2 hr long. All the big rides were 2 hrs +. We road only 3 rides. We could not even get into Harry Potter area. They had it closed off so only people holding a pass could get in. They ran out off passes. They could have said something about this before we bought our tickets. There is no doubt they were way over capacity and very surprised a fire marshal would not have seen a safety hazard. Not exaggerating the place was packed. It was no fun for our kids. One of the little ones only went on one ride. It was a was of money and you could clearly see it was only about the money for Universal Studios. Fast passes were a $109.00 for each. We will never go again. Stay away for the holiday.

We were there Jan. 9th and again on the 13th, 2013 and had a fabulous time. The longest wait time for any ride was 40 min. and most were only 5 to 15 min. so no fast pass was needed anyway. Everything was very clean and it wasn't overly crowded. We were very luck to have great weather. When I am back in the area I would definitely go back.

We actually had more fun here than at Islands of Adventure which seems different from most reviews. There were a ton of shows and we loved them all. There were also great rides and fun coasters. I would suggest getting an express pass. We didn't get one the day before at Islands and had plenty of time to get everything in. It was still a fairly slow day when we went here, but because there were more shows we wanted to see, it did take longer to see everything. Also, there is no early entry to Universal like there is at Islands, so even if you have a one hour early admission pass, it will not work here. This seemed to be a surprise to everyone standing in line. Definitely see the Beetlejuice show if you like music shows and the Fear Factor show was great too.

We had not been here for about 12 years. In 2001 we only went to the Universal Studios movie theme park. Not a lot had changed there since 2001. They still had the "Twister" attraction (which is pretty lame). Who in the younger generation remembers the movie, "Twister"? I consider this park mildly entertaining. Perhaps my favorite attraction is "Terminator 3D". One other thing that turned me off about this park was the people at the "Shrek 4D" attraction. When we paid for our admission, we were told that there was a special customer lounge for those who paid with an American Express card at the Shrek 4D attraction. When I asked someone at the Shrek 4D attraction about this supposed customer lounge, the person went "into his character" and played the part of a smarmy resident of the kingdom of Duloc. I never did get a straight answer, and was too tired (nearing the end of our day) to dig any deeper. Great help, Universal; that kind of B.S. should be saved for those 15 years old or younger.  The Islands of Adventure park was far more entertaining. Perhaps out favorite was the Spiderman 3D ride. Unbelievable technology. It really feels like you are immersed in the action, with characters jumping on your car as you ride through. The Harry Potter ride was good, although not 3D. I went on the Hulk roller coaster, and felt weak in the knees for a while after getting off! That is one wicked roller coaster. I do not recommend the Jurassic Park River Ride, unless you like getting soaking wet. Personally, I thought that sucked.  Regarding the part about your wallet... admission cost to this place is really ridiculous. I think mentioning prices in these reviews is frowned upon, so I'll just say that you should look for discounts. Also, unless you purchase an express pass for another exorbitant fee, expect to wait in long lines to get on rides.

Once the sticker-shock wears off a bit, you can appreciate the more adult rides/attractions than those found at Disney (not as clean, though). I enjoyed the rollercoaster, and the Mummy ride.. But that was about it.. I was a bit dissapointed by the Terminator 2 show. I'd forgotten how annoying Ed Furlong was (at least his voice had changed by the time they got around to doing this show), and it was pretty corny.. (SUPER annoying pre-show Cyberdyne spokesperson (how do they DO that 6 times a day?? They must have to switch them out often to avoid suicides). We got chased out at 6pm (even though the stated closing time was 7) because there was some big shots having an event by the Men in Black section.. Big gaping nothing where the Jaws ride used to be.. The food was alright.. I had a good cappucino and danish in a cafe near the enterance. Thw Twister show was terrible.. Waste of time..

We had family visiting from Chicago and decided to take them to Universal Studios. We had the perfect day. The crowds were minimal. The most we had to wait in line for any ride was 30 minutes. The nice thing about Universal Studios is that most of the lines are in covered areas or inside so you are protected from the sun. It's not your typical amusement park with lots of fast rides. All the rides or shows are themed around Universal Movies or TV shows. There are lots of 3-D and special effects. There was just enough to see and do to fill the day.

This park is probably great for teenagers. Not so great for younger children. There are shows and rides for everyone except the young. There are probably only two or three rides/shows geared towards younger children. There are several "playground" areas with water features geared towards the young. The water features are probably great in the dead of summer but not so much in January. There are also misting machines all over the park that you can't avoid. Not necessary in January. There were a lot of eateries and features that were closed. No signage displayed. You only knew when you walk up to the building and it was completely dark and barren. This is a small park by most large amusement park standards. The sister park (Islands of Adventure) is much better for all.

I visited Islands of Adventure. The rides looked like fun, but I could not tell you for sure. After spending almost $200.00 to get in the door, there was a 2 hr wait for any ride. 30 mins if you spend an extra $55.00 per person. Universal has no crowd control and they expect you to pay extra for their lack of planning. I went back a couple months later and tried Universal studios. Wow what a let down. I took my girlfriend and my 5 year old son. My 5 year old was bored on the rides. I don't know how to explain that any better. Once again there is no crowd control, the food was inedible(My son wouldn't eat pizza!!!) I could put cheese on cardboard and he would eat it, but not pizza from universal. The people were rude, the rides were boring, and the food bad. Cost $400.00 for 2hrs of misery. Universal is really good at getting you in the door and taking your money, but thats where thier service ends. There are a lot of great theme parks, but this is not one of them. Go to Busch Gardens or Disney. You and your kids will have a much better time for less money.

Visited Universal Studios in October 2012, we had a great day & visited several times in our trip with the flex ticket.  There was quite a lot building work going on when we visited but am looking forward to end result it looks good!  We found the Rockit quite rough & jerky so avoid if you are sensitive to those kind of rides. The Mummy is one of the best dark rides I have been on. The new Dispicable Me attraction is very well done & there are "real" minions to dance with at the end :)  We found the food prices to be quite resonable, counter service offerings being around the $8 mark which isnt that bad to be honest!  All in all an excellent day out, cant wait to go back when all the new stuff opens!

I read some of the bad reviews but to me they are all pointless. Universal studios and Islands of adventure should not be compared to Disney and if people read up on the park before they went they would know its not really suitable for young kids.  For both parks if your from the uk the best time to go if you can is before the kids summer holidays start (hard to do). June and September aren't as busy as July and August and the queues are smaller.  Universal studios: More suitable for people who don't like big roller coasters as there's only really 2 (mummy returns & rock n rolla) but the rides aren't really for young kids. I go with my family every year and my mum Hates roller coasters, she did the mummy returns once but never again but she loves universal there's loads she can do. Her favourite is shrek. A family favourite is men in black and we always enjoy jaws. ET is a must for the whole family it's fantastic and beetle juice has something for everyone. Food isn't sprawled out across the park there's specific food courts/areas across the park which I think is better but it's personal preference.  Islands of adventure: Not for people who don't like roller coasters really. However! My mum hates them but there's still things for her to do like spider man, the log fumes, Harry potter etc. and she enjoys having the chance to sunbathe while the rest of us go on the bigger rides.  If you like roller coasters this is the park for you with the hulk, doom (wouldn't q for this ride) and Harry potter triwizard. There's still other things to do and walking around Harry potter land is great!  These parks aren't as decorated as Disney which is a shame but that's not what these parks are about.  Citywalk is great at night bubba gumps is a must if you like shrimp and the cinema is nice to fill some time. Hard Rock Cafe is what you expect and u shud book in advance.
2 days at Universal is plenty. Perfect for bigger kids. Lots of fun. Great rides. Good food. Fun to be had by all.
In my opinion this is the best of all the parks in Orlando absolutely fantastic, everyone is so friendly and helpful and the attractions are first class

Universal and Islands of Adventure certainly know how to do it. Staff are funny and attentive. The attractions definitely suit older kids and adults more than Disney. The pre build up to rides and shows is entertaining and well done. We returned after a break of 12 years and it's definitely advanced since then. A couple of attractions are the same but with added extras to modernise and appeal to today's visitors. Great day out and longest queue was 30 mins and that was rare. Can't wait to return in the future to experience Transformers, which is a huge construction in progress for this Summer

I don't even know where to begin. We started at Universal Studios on our holiday, they have a wide selection of rides for all ages, and are constructing new ones at the moment. The Simpsons Ride is a fantastic family ride, along with Men In Black: Alien Attack and Despicable Me: Minion Mayhem, however my favorite ride in the parks (and all of Florida) is the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit, it looks a lot worse than it actually is and you shouldn't miss it out. it's a rollercoaster where you choose a song to listen to, which is synced perfectly to the ride, and I find it fantastic. We also went for the Mardi Gras parade which was a great event, and watched the "Universal Nighttime Spectacular" in the lagoon afterwards.  Next Up, Islands of Adventure, this park is generally busier than Universal Studios due to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, however shouldn't be missed. My advice is leave Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey right until the end of the day, when I went the wait time was 125 minutes in the morning, and went down to 20 around 9pm. I usually start the day by heading over to Superhero Island, which features the Incredible Hulk Coaster, another fantastic ride, one of my favorites, there's also other attractions and "The Amazing Adventures of Spiderman" which was recently refurbished into HD 3D, and is a half virtual half track ride, in which you follow Spiderman around the streets of Manhattan. As you continue, you'll enter Toon Lagoon, the 2 main rides are Dudley Do Right's Ripsaw Falls and Popeye and Bluto's Bilgerat Barges, Log Flume and Rapids rides. Nothing Special. Through the Jurassic Park area, you'll come into The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The Butterbeer always has long lines, but is worth it, it's also nice to look around the shops as well. The Dragon Challenge coaster (Formerley Dueling Dragons) Usually has a wait of <20 minutes, as most of the crowd goes to Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey.  Universal Orlando resort host's my favorite parks in Florida, and my favorite coaster in the world. If you have teenagers, this is a MUST SEE. Do not miss out!

I would suggest buying the meal plan. Its good value if you are going to spend the whole day there. We drank water so it was just the food. Pop is ok if you buy the cup they refill it for a lower cost. Theres 2 parks. The original was MGM studios years ago. It hasn't changed much since then. The other park has Harry Potter and Spider Man attractions in it. We didn't go to that one. So the original one, is the only rating we can give. My kids are teens so we had no problems with anything. And having the meal deal with teens is great.

My husband, my 11yr old son, and I visited Universal for 2 days last week. The park was clean and the lines weren't too long. We really enjoyed the new Despicable Me Minion Mayhem ride and the 3D spiderman ride. The Twister was a little disappointing, I thought there'd be more wind and less water (I got a bucket load dumped on the back of my head). My son loved The Simpsons ride. The Beetlejuice's Graveyard Revue was surprisingly great. The Superstar Parade was awesome with characters from Despicable Me, SpongeBob, Hop & Dora. Catch the Character Party Zone where the characters come off their floats and get pictures. VERY disappointed that the minions weren't in the parade or available for pictures in the park. You can only get a picture if you catch them immediately after the Despicable Me ride at the exit to the ride. It's a very short period of time to catch a picture then they leave.

The good: -The Simpsons. -Strolling on streets. -Shoping. - Minions new atration but thera are better on other parks. The bad: - Men in black.  Adbventure island: -The best: Spider man, good technology. -Harry potter castle simulator best technoilogy ever ( don´t remmenber the name). -Hulk coaster. -Jurasik park boat coater ride (youll get really wet, be prepared).

Universal is more for kids 8-16 years of age. It is a down-sized Disney. Most of the rides were simulated and involved 3D Glasses. Each park had one coaster. Universal Studio was better than islands of Adventure. We purchased the food ticket and drink ticket. We had no trouble finding the restaurants and drinking refills at Universal but Islands was hard to find and scarce drinking refills. The Maps for each park are really crummy - they definetely need more details to help you find places or find yourself! Signage is not helpful. Going into Islands - the music is way too loud; hasn't the Park realized we are teaching our kids to turn down the volume to save their hearing. Most of the attractions were a lesser copy of a Disney Ride. Not enough attractions. Shops were a bit high priced. Food was good at the Universal Restaurants on the Meal ticket.

Amazing rides, we went in May so the queues weren't too bad. We had a great time. It's loads better than Disney and so much cheaper 2! Only negatives are the fast pass is super expensive and unlimited food you can buy is a total rip off. You can only use it at 3 food places and they are super picky about what you can have and it isn't detailed clearly. Loads of people were getting their food, then getting to the till and have to pay as they picked the wrong thing

First day here and it was a freaking blast! I got a chance to ride my first roller coaster(The Hulk) and after that I was hooked. BY far the highlight of the trip was the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. As an avid Potter fan, I felt like I had died and gone to heaven. One tip though, the crowds are pretty bad in certain areas, so if you can, go ahead and spring for the early park entrance tickets. Bit pricier, but well worth it.

Gutted! Out of all the parks we had done as a family we were looking forward to this park. We paid for the tickets beforehand luckily as queues were long. Entered the park early (0830). We were at the Island Adventures side. Baring in mind tickets are expensive we were shocked at the queues already in place, especially for Harry Potter 'rides' location. If you choose to fast pass this park it is called 'express pass'. A further $96 per ticket.(Disney Fast Pass included in price) Although we done most the rides the park is not as enjoyable as Disney attractions and we believe unless a mass Harry Potter fan it can be avoided.
The rides were interactive and fun. I recommend getting the express pass to bypass the long lines. Wear comfortable shoes! We had a great time - even my teenager!

My party and I went to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure and bought a 3 day park-to-park pass. Although we missed the "US & Canadian Residents Buy 2 Days Get the 3rd Free" deal going on, the money was well worth it! There were so many memorable attractions and with the help of the Universal & Undercover Tourist apps, we were able to ride each attraction with minimal wait times. Even the brand new Transformers ride (which I recommend to hit RIGHT when the park opens) was only a 60 minute wait compared to the average 140+. Every ride there is enjoyable and fun, the parade was adorable and I even got a few autographs from Betty Boop, Bart Simpson, Captain America, and Woody the Woodpecker! Along with the rides there were very cool things to see such as Fear Factor Live and displays of the cars featured in the famous movie franchise "Fast and Furious". Even though we stayed for three days, there was something new and memorable each day. Can't wait to come back.

the thing about universal studios that is better than disney is the lines are not that long and the attractions are much closer together than at disney. you could see everything in one day if weather permits, where as disney is so spread out you could spend days and never see everything. my teen actually prefers universal over disney

Our family of 4 visited Universal in August 2012 as a side trip for few days from our Gulf coast vacation. The kids were 15 and 11 so they were ready for the rides! This place is a full on assault on your senses and your bank account. We chose to stay off-site in Orlando and drive into the park for three days. I was trying to save some money over staying in the park hotels, but after the first day at the park, I realized that the long lines are meant to demoralize cheap/poor people. The line skipping feature called Universal Express lets people skip to the front of the line. To buy this upgrade in the park is ridiculously expensive BUT if you stay in their hotels you get this feature for free. The Express upgrade would have cost $150 per day for my family on top of the park ticket prices. If you don't want to feel abused by line skippers, stay at their onsite hotels. Both parks were exciting, but Islands of Adventure (IA) had newer, more exciting rides than Universal Studios (US).  Here are our hits and misses for IA: Hits: Spiderman, Hulk, all Harry Potter village rides, Ripsaw Falls, Popeye River Raft, Jurassic Park River; Misses: None!  Here are our hits and misses for US: Hits: Despicable Me, Hollywood rocket, Simpsons, Shrek, Revenge of Mummy; Misses: Men in Black=Waste of time!, ET & Twister=Time to retire these!  Eating: We had a big breaksfast before going to the park and brought lots of water and some fruits and buns we "borrowed" from the hotel. Food at the parks is expensive and fatty and the cleanliness in the eating areas is terrible. Would it kill them to change that grey stinky rag once a day? Food service staff are apathetic! Apparently having a job is a waste of time!  We were gouged $40 for hotdog meals! The only place where there was some sanity and value was the Confisco Grille just inside Islands of Adventure gates.  We had a great time but I had to put aside my sensibilites and accept that I will stand in line for an hour, I will pay $10 for a hotdog and flat pop and staff will glare at me even though I'm blowing $400 per day to be there. These theme parks are a right of passge for parents I suppose, if you go, pack your patience and a sack of money ... good luck!
Likes the Mummy ride and the Simpsons ride. Fear Factor Live was very neat to see but I wasn't blown away by the park. Some lines were over an hour late, we went on a somewhat rainy day.

Recently went to Orlando Studios, Adventure Land, Orlando, Florida & had a very good time. Liked the rides, shops, magic show, etc there. Didn't even have enough time to take it all in on one day so plan to return there in the future! Offered a variety of different rides for all family members & loved the Harry Potter castle & ride!

Universal studios is mainly show type rides but they are out of this world. T2 is an old favourite, its fun to see the actors mimmick arnie, furlong and Linda Hamilton. 3d effects r very good. There r a lot f characters to meet and take photos with. Scooby doo, despicable me characters, spongebob, Dora, Simpsons. Transformers is absolutely amazing, kids rode this 4 times. You can also take pics with bumble bee, optimus and Megatron. Men in black is alot of fun and rip ride rock it is an intense rollercoaster. There is also a superstar parade at 5pm. With so many awesome attractions, you need at least 2 days here. We had a 14 day multipark ticket so ended up coming here 6 times. Our favourite park of the holiday. BTW, the 100yr celebration show with fireworks is also amazing. Check it out.

Make sure you buy the Express Pass or book a hotel room on Universal property for unlimited pass uses or you'll waste your days waiting in line. It pays for itself if time matters to you. Arrive BEFORE the park opens for fastest ride access. Rides are faster, thrilling, more outrageous, and slightly more irreverent than at Disney parks. Simulators like Transformers, The Simpsons, Despicable Me, and Shrek 4-D will excite and nauseate large crowds at once. Thrill seekers with flexible necks and backs will love Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit Rollercoaster and The Mummy coaster. The park is best enjoyed by people who don't mind lots of walking and standing, large crowds, Florida heat and humidty, and loud music. Tweens and teens abound. Bring a small backpack filled with water and Gatorade.

Had a brilliant day there Transformer ride is the best simulator ride you will go on ,queueing times were not bad at all just a shame the jaws ride isn't there any-more and spider-man ride wasn't working .Extremely hot but didn't put as off and had the odd welcomed shower would go back again .Although they need to have free wi-fi like Disney resorts so you can download app for ride queueing times and restaurant reservations.

The Despicable me and Transformer rides are incredible. The rest of the rides are OK. Neat layout to the park and easy to get around. We have a special needs child and the staff was very inconsistent in how they managed the special needs pass. They are not clear on the 30 minute rule and were told conflicting things from the staff at each ride.

Oh wow! The best in Orlando......we did them all, Disney, Universal, Sea World and Busch Gardens and Universal Islands of Adventure were by far the best.  Harry Potter is the big draw and it was well worth it. The place is fantastic from Hogwarts Castle to Hogsmead, the rides, the shops and scenery and the finishing touches like the Butterbeer on sale in the street.  We all had a fantastic day and I would go again and again if I could.

It is true to say I think Universal have lost the plot! I agree with other contributors - 2+ hours queuing for a 4 minute ride! The lines for getting into attractions are just way to long to make the experience enjoyable; especially with a six year old!! To buy a fast pass is just unbelievably expensive and cannot be afforded by the average family! $100 + each unbelievable and outrageous! As a Family we managed 2 main attractions yesterday because of the times spent in lines! Personally I will not be going back; much preferring the Disney Parks and SeaWorld!

after visiting all the major parks with just me and the wife we decided to review them all. Universal's content put it joint top in what it had to offer.  IMO it has the 2 best rides in Orlando, Being the Rock roller coaster and The Mummy ride. Being chosen due to its amount of "crap your pants excitement" without the wanting to throw up afterwards effect.  The Beetlejuice show is awesome so don't miss it.  The rest of the shows and rides are a nice mix and made the whole day and enjoyable mix.  Now to the bad points.  The cost- Breaking down what we paid for the tickets and Fast Passes (and unfortunately you need these which i hated. que times for the top rides were between 60-120 mins, with a fast past this was between 10-15mins) came to $115 a day per person compared to Disney $50 a day.  Without the fast past we would have had no chance of seeing all the rides but $59 per person is a bit extortionate.  The character organistation. Disney park has organized lines, a helper for the characters and a professional photographer who is happy to take a picture with your own camera. Universal had non of these.  On the food a drink front they do offer $9 special drinks container where you can refill for $1 all day long (and just by chance if you are there for more than one day take it back with you and keep saving on your second day). Food was overpriced like everywhere $10 for a krusty burger!!!!!!! we stuck with sandwiches and saved $30 a day roughly.  so to sumarise if your coming to Orlando to do the fast rides and your willing to fork out $115 a person do it. I think if your here with a family stick with Disney.

The only way to get on some of the more publicised attractions is to buy an Express pass, over and above the entrance fee; this costs $69.99 per person + tax and there is no discount for seniors or children. During July, when the American schools are also on holiday, it's probably the only way to guarantee that you actually get on a ride. Without the Express pass, you have to queue and the advertised wait times are less than the actual wait times. Our visits to these parks were also spoiled by large tour groups, mainly consisting of teenage girls, chanting and marching 10-15 abreast, expecting everyone in their path, young or old, able bodied or disabled to move for them. They also don't want to queue and try to push their way in front of everyone else. Whilst Disney also suffers from these groups, it's fair to say that their parks are better organised and their queuing system is fairer.

Been visiting the park for years and it gets better every time we return - they are always changing, improving and adding to their attractions and you are never stuck for things to do. Highly recommend paying out the extra for the express tickets to jump the queue, it allows you to do more in a single visit as you aren't standing around in a queue for hours on end.

I have been visiting Orlando since I was 4 now I'm 22 and I get mega excited especially for Universal Studios! The plastic are fantastic, nothing is a problem always outgoing and happy to help! Queue time differ on the time of year, the past 2 years I have been in April and May and found it to be full of I'm guessing schools? Loads of groups of kids walking around which tends to annoy people! I think the company souls organise specific days and allow a certain number in the parks as it can be annoying hearing hundreds off hyper kids when your trying to queue! All the attractions are brilliant, Deffo recommend despicable me, the mummy and rip ride rockitt.. Fab experiences and deffffs the Beetlejuice show it's amazing! I am hoping to return this September for Halloween horror nights! I've never experience it but hope people can give me some advice :)

Me and my fiancé visited universal last week and had a great time. We visited both islands of adventure and universal studios in one day but we prefer universal studios. Prior to visiting we decided to get express passes, these are expensive and annoying to buy as it is free at disney. But as we are from the UK and we needed express passes to get on everything. It was well worth the expense as we got on all the rides and some twice. The new transformers ride is great, it's one of my favourites from all of the orlando parks. The mummy was also great and quite scary. Shrek, the Simpsons, rip rocket and MIB were also top rides there. Even the older rides such as disaster, ET and twister were good fun and rides I member when I visited 20 years ago when I was five. I found the staff to be friendly and the park was clean and ran well. I would say this park has the best ride selection out of all parks in orlando
The studios are fantastic glad we stayed so close so that we could come and go as much as we wanted. The Express passes are essential as there are long queues for the most popular rides.

Ah, I do love Universal studios and it had been a long time since we last went. A lot has changed since our last visit six years ago, but nonetheless it's still a brilliant park. The variety of rides is great, and everyone has something that they'll like, and if they don't then they're not looking hard enough, honest.  It's easy to get around, and everything is has a natural flow about it making for easy navigation around the various parts. Rides can also be spotted from a distance considering their distinct architecture on the outside, each contributing to the feel of the park. Which is great.  The only gropes I'll have about this park is the amount of time it takes to go through security at times, the lack of support for certain cards in their cash machines and the locker situation. I'll start with the locker situation, as it's the more alarming.  1:: When I went six years ago, they didn't mind you taking your bags on with you, or leaving them at the platform so that you can collect them on the way out. This has since stopped, and forces you to use one of their so called "Free" lockers, which aren't. They're free for the first hour, but past that they make you pay X amount for every X minutes over you've had it, but a lot of people hold the line up when it comes to that because they've trapped their money inside these lockers, unable to pay. They then need to grab a security guy, to then grab an attendant, and so on. So, if you're going I wouldn't recommend taking a bag with you, of any size, because they'll force you to use their lockers.  2:: We were in utter disbelief as our card, a money passport (since we were merely tourists), wasn't accepted by any of the cash machines within the park. It did work over some shops within the park, but not all. When we went to the 'Guest Relations', they merely told us 'tough luck' and made us go on our way. This was appalling in my eyes. They're happy to screw money out of you, for lockers (for the smallest of bags, no exaggeration), but when you require help around these, they really couldn't care less.  3:: Whilst this isn't mentioned on my initial list, I'll warn you now. Do not go if you believe it will thunder. As soon as we got to the park, and went on one ride a single bolt of lightening was seen and every ride in both parks were shutdown and subsequently closed. Even the rides which were inside were closed, leaving many in lines, hoping they'll open again. After this it started to rain for at least an hour and a half, everything seemed as if it was about to open again, when another bolt was noticed. Everything closed again. After this we left, as we had no interest in waiting six hours for the rides to open again.

Universal Studios was an awesome experience. While some rides are more modern than others the overall experience was great despite the heat and crowds. I noticed that things were less crowded in the late afternoon. The fast pass option really helped the day go smoother. I highly recommend the extra expense.

I thought of this part mostly boring, but what can I say, I have been to universal studios in Los Angeles . What I would recommend to go there if you arrive early is go to the transformer, but if you want fun I would recommend Rock It; it's very creative. Island of Adventure is really fun, and has a lot of fun rides like Harry Potter, Hulk, Spider Man, and etc.. If you arrive to Island early I would recommend you to go to the Harry Potter ride first because it takes about a hour to wait if you go about at 1:00 PM.

Not as fun as Universal Islands of Adventure for a family with high school kids but had some good points. Lombard's Seafood restaurant was really good. I don't care for the Simpsons so there was ALOT too much of that for me. Also the only employees on the entire Universal vacation we encountered who were bad were at Ben & Jerrys in the Park. 3-4 people working and only one of them trying. The rest trying to close the place at 5:40 and didn't care about the line backing up out the door  Everything else was really good but not as good as Islands of Adventure.

This theme park is perfect for teens, pre-teens and their parents, The roller coasters were phenomenal and the restaurant selections were amazing. Much like Disney World, there are different "themes" within the park that cater to all ages.  The only complaint is the cost for a fast-pass or express pass. While expensive for these "add-ons" I would highly suggest getting them. With them, my wife, two kids and myself were able to go to a ride and be done within 15 minutes while those individuals without passes were often waiting up to 1 1/2 hrs. The other comment is that you should try to arrive at the park as close to opening as possible because it get's quite busy by lunchtime.
The greatest ingredient is the AE lounge which gives free water, granola bars n chip, it has AC, good place to rest

We were pleasantly surprised with how professional the entire experience was at Universal Studios in Orlando, It is like they took the "Disney" Model and stepped it up a notch. I must admit, we thought it would be an overflow attraction, but it was better in most areas. Other than the old school attraction of rides and familiar Disney brand, Universal is more updated, current and fresh. Down to the waiting lines being more interesting and fun and the associates' uniforms having more details, etc. The associates themselves seemed to be "in-character" to a higher degree added to the enjoyment. Minor perks like free lockers next to each ride was a great convenience. Our on-site hotel, the Royal Pacific was also top-flight and detail oriented also.

This is a great park. We and our older kids (10 yo) had a wonderful time. Each and every attraction was interesting.  There were hardly any queues, so we managed to do both thus park and the Adventure Island within a day.( using the park to park option). There was no need for an express ticket.  Nevertheless, this park is not suitable for kids younger than 8. Although they can ride according to their height, the overall experience can be quite scary.
Despicable Me ride, such fun. As was the Transformers ride, excellent. Great time of year to attend as the time to get on the rides was averaging about 20mins if you attend early in the morning.

I loved the rides that me and my partner went on, transformers was my favorite and the mummy was his. We were planning to go to the Horror night at Universal Studios, we were told by a member of staff that it was best to come on a Wednesday (which we did). We got to park and we were going to ask if you need to pay for your ticket as the theme park ticket as I had been told that it would not cover it, only to find out that it was not on that night and on top of that you needed to pay an extra $40 to see it. I was not happy that I paid for a ticket which would not cover it, it just goes to that universal love to make money off people. We weren't really bothered that we were missing out, we decided to go on more rides and enjoy our day. The next problem I had was on the Men In Black ride, which I had been on before (about 11 years ago). I got through no problem waited in line for 10 minutes, only to get told as I got to the very front that my bag was unsuitable for the ride. I knew the ride was a rollercoaster so it should of been alright, plus I was wondering why the member of staff did not stop me from the beginning. So annoyed I walked through the exit, went straight up to the member of staff who was letting people in what had happened. To be fair he did calm me down and told me that there was a free locker I could use while on the ride, he then told me to go back up the exit to get on the ride. When finally on the ride me and my partner sat down and enjoyed it, but one thing I did notice that it was clearly alright to have my bag on that ride.

We did both parks in one day.  We bought the express passes but if you get there for opening at one park I wouldn't buy an express pass for that park but for the other park that you plan on visiting later in the day as at opening it's very slow.  Bring a change of clothes for island of adventures water rides. You will get soaked.  It's a great time.

I will agree that many of the rides here are similar and not much fun. However, the Mummy is awesome. This is also a great place for concerts throughout the year. And the annual pass is cheap compared to Disney. One tip I can offer, you can use those lockers next to the Mummy and Men in Black for a little longer than just the ride.

I am a year long passholder and I always love going to this park. Worth the money spent on going. My sister attended the Halloween night there and she loved the Walking Dead zombies walking in the streets at night. And because everyone was at the haunted houses the lines for the rides was even shorter than normal. The rides never get old for me but all I can say is that I wish this park had faster roller coasters. Other than that make sure your kids are not too young because there is not a lot for them to do.

I've been in more than 5 times and I am not tired of it. It's adsoluted must visit to see the new Transformer. Best of all, when I visit I could see that in the next year will have provably other attractions. I never tire of seeing a twister or the mummy and if you want the trill you have to hop to the rock and roll roller coaster If you're an adult with a few days but want to have fun I recommend a day at Universal, one day at Islands of Adventure, one at Sea World. If you enjoy swimming pool access (I do not) then extend your stay and visit Aquatica or Wet and Wild.
Amazing day spent here. Will visit again and again. A must do while in Orlando. Loved the rides, the staff were friendly and helpful and the food was great.

We were in America for one month and started our journey in Miami, we drove up to Orlando and started from there. Universal was awesome, great souvenirs, awesome rides, yum food. Such a rad day!! MAKE sure you wear sunscreen!! :)

This park lacks the magic of disney or the character of the other parks. Easily completed the park in a day and felt the rides were lacking in comparison to other parks. The disaster experience was the most entertaining. I see there is construction underway so hopefully this will replace the atmosphere of a few years ago. Wouldn't rush back.

So the whole park was great, and nicely theamed... but I went on Transformers 6 times within 2 days! Best ride they have in my oppinion hands down! Enjoyed MIB, Simpsons, Twister and Despicable Me as well!

From all the parks available, this one was the most disappointing. A bit of a weird lay out and just lacking the atmosphere and detail find in the other parks.  it really isa shame they don't have a fast pass system, only the pay through the nose to jump the queue option as after a few rides, the queues just build up. At one point the Minions ride was almost 2 hours long. We had to skip some of the rides we were looking forward to doing because of the queues.

I have been to universal studios the past three years and I just can't get enough of it! It is a wonderful holiday experience with lots to do. All the rides are based on movies which is great because it makes you feel like you are in the movie. Both parks are really clean and the staff are really friendly. The restaurants are nice and the food is delicious! I would highly recommend the Hard Rock Cafe and the three broomsticks at the wizarding world. I would recommend not going in the summer season because it can get really busy and the queues get really long. So going out of season would be more beneficial. Although the parking is expensive at $16, it's still good as it's all uncover and is linked to the parks with walkways so you don't have to walk far. The parks are well sign posted and maps are provided in order to get around easily. I love this place and I'm going again next year!!!!

Vegans please be aware that Universal Studios lies about food to get you to go there. 4 times Bob Burdick, chef at Universal Studios, Orlando told me that all the cheese on pizzas is vegan. On my 5th message to him I checked if he knew what a vegan was and explained it to him, highlighting that I believe the cheese had cows milk in it. Bob Burdick then admitted that the cheese was not vegan at all and blamed it on his suppliers giving him the wrong information I complained about Bob to customer services and several days later I received a phone message from customer services stating that they had spoken with Bob Burdick and all the cheese is vegan. Doh!!! It clearly is not. Why is he lying about this to people? He has admitted to me it is not vegan but is continuing to tell people that it is vegan. I wouldn't not expect all the cheese to be vegan and that is not what I am asking - Just be honest, as you could make people with milk allergies really ill....

We had a great time at the horror nights, will definitely be back next year. The zombies walking around are awesome and really get you jumping when you're walking through the park. I highly recommend it as a group activity, get a hotel for the night, drink, and make sure you get the express passes. If you don't get the express passes you will definitely regret it as the wait can be VERY long for the houses/rides (~2 hours). With the passes we were able to go to all the houses and do the roller coaster twice, and a couple of the other universal rides that were open. The Cabin in the Woods was just amazing, so true to the movie, and really scary. Again, we loved it, and it will probably become a tradition to go every year from now on!

We went the first week in November and crowds were light. We walked right up to the Rock It- the only real roller coaster on the property. Our 7 and 8 year old boys were terrified walking up to the Mummy ride and kept their eyes closed for the entire ride. At this point my husband couldn't do any more simulated roller coasters because they made him nauseous and gave him a headache. The boys and I did the Simpson's Ride and even that seemed to be over the top in effects. We really enjoyed the Animal Actor's show. The host was very entertaining and the kids loved seeing the animals do tricks. Our last ride was Despicable Me. We did have to wait 35 minutes but in my opinion that was the best virtual roller coaster. The story was entertaining. There was motion but it didn't make you sick. The 3D effects were wonderful. This was our first day using our meal deal plan and were surprised to learn that we could get Ben and Jerry's as our snack. Yum!!

Loved to be there. Was one of the best places i recon, the best to me was the back to the future. It was incredible. If your going there, prepare for adventure, and has alot to pick from! Regards, Pet-r-us

Really good and loads to do. The "Despicable Me" ride is spectacular!! New things being built, like the train station from Harry Potter in Islands of Adventure to Universal itself, Always something new to see.

There are some amazing rides here. The Despicable Me attraction is a "virtual roller coaster" which feels just like a real one. The seats move and tilt like you are going up and down and around the curves. The Shrek attraction is more stationary but has other "special effects that make you feel like you are in the story. There are a variety of dining choices and of course shopping opportunities. Kids, both big and small will enjoy these 2 parks.
Most kids don't know what ET is....needs to be removed and another ride put in it's place. It is slow loading and just not worth the wait.

We had a lot of fun on our recent trip to Universal. They have so many different and unique rides here. There is something for everyone. They have a variety of shows to see, including the Beetlejuice show which was really cute. The Minions 3-d ride was so fun, as was the Shrek ride. It takes longer to go through this park than the island of adventure as there is more to do here.

But it was worth every penny! Definitely get the frozen butterbeer and make sure to visit the ladies room! We had lunch at The Three Broomsticks. It was ok. Loved the character actors and Ollivanders!

The lines are extremely long. The lines in both parks for pretty much everything were at least 90 mins. They let the people with express passes pile in, increasing your wait time exponentially. Why did we even buy tickets then? Seems like a waste of money unless your willing to pay even more for an express pass. They really could take a lesson from disney and offer shorter lines to all. The parks have some cool rides, but whats the point if you can't get on them. We will probably just stick with disney in the future.

If you are in Orlando to visit theme parks, do not overlook Universal Studios. It is a must-see for those over the age of seven. If you have younger children, then you may want to stick with Disney World or try Islands of Adventure, which has a section for children.

Harry potter world is worth the trip. My twenty something kids loved it! Day after Christmad so it was insane, but we tougher it out, got there really early and had no problems! You HAVE to stop ai Ollivanders and get a wand!

What a great park! So much to see and do! But plan on arriving early or go latter in the day as some of the lines were long - Harry Potter ride was 150 min wait time! But overall my teens were happier here than other parks like Disney and Sea World. Also, even though we were there during a very busy season we found this park's design could better accommodate the crowds.

I'm not sure how I feel about The Universal Studios park, even though I had a fast pass we still had to wait quite a while to get on the Despicable Me ride, which broke halfway through and we had to experience it all over again, Shrek 4D is a waste of time, it takes about 15 minutes until you can go in to the theatre and then when you are in the show isn't all that great, the chairs are meant to move but ours (in the back row) barely even moved, which we weren't told about. The Hollywood rollercoaster was great, probably the best ride there. The Transformers ride was very good, but like the Despicable Me one, broke halfway through and lost it's sound, which was disappointing. The rest of the park I can't really comment on as it was way too packed to walk and very tiring, the Macys christmas parade was a little overrated and not very good, just blow up animal shapes and a few naff characters, the park is a lot less christmassy than Islands of Adventure and has less food and drink options, slight disappointment and wouldn't really go back again.

The Universal Studio theme parks are definitely something to visit at least once in a lifetime if you are a movie buff!! The Harry Potter section is extremely well done and the major ride (in the castle) is totalling amazing!! We did it 4 times!!! Not for people with 3D "motion-sickness" though!! LOVED our 3-day stay there!!

We went to Islands of Adventure on Dec 28th, 2013. We have never felt so ripped off in our lives from start to finish. First off, we had to wait in line for 40 mins to park. We were then charged $16 to park. We paid almost $100 each for 5 entry tickets. Upon entering the park, it started to rain, which granted, we were not prepared for. We duly had to pay $8 each for plastic bags to cover ourselves, $40 total. Universal is likely buying these bags for about 2 cents each. They could easily make them complimentary to their patrons. The average wait time for the majority of the major rides was an hour and a half, and 2 hours for Harry Potter. We felt compelled to purchase 2 express passes at a mind boggling cost of $139 each!!!! Even with these passes, we found we could not use them for the Harry Potter Forbidden Journey. When we got wet on some of the water rides, we decided to use the drying facility at a cost of $5 per use! Again, this could easily be complimentary or at worst $1. It just seemed that they shamelessly wanted to screw customers out of every last dime. Toon land is a complete joke. Incredible Hulk, Jurassic park and Spider-Man are good rides. Seuss land is great for smaller kids. We left the park at 9pm after having spent close to $1,000 and we brought our own food!!! We will not be back and we will be recommending that none of our friends go there. Disney is so much more customer friendly and organized, with knowledgeable staff. It is altogether much more worthwhile with a speed pass system that is fair to all, not just the few who can afford to fork out exorbitant fees for express passes.
Harry Potter world is being extrended to include the Hogwarts Express and Digone Alley. Loads of rides and attractions for all ages.
This theme park is one of the best in Orlando it has rides for youngsters and older visitors and the entrance fee is very reasonable.

We went to Universal for the first time at the end of December 2013 and beginning of January 2014. All of the Christmas decorations were still in place and I must admit they do a lovely job of decorating. That being said - THE WAIT TIMES FOR RIDES ARE HORRENDOUS!! Over 2 hours for Despicable Me/Minions and Harry Potter! Why does Universal NOT GET A CLUE?? When you trap people in lines for rides, they are NOT SPENDING $$ ON THEIR OVER PRICED FOOD AND SOUVENIERS!! Charging people for an "Express pass" isn't going to work - people will almost always choose to wait over shelling out more money to ride an attraction. Be smart Universal and copy the FREE Disney fast pass system so you can squeeze more $$ out of the guests!!

My wife insisted we visit Harry Potter world at Islands of Adventure while we were in Florida, so we opted for the two day ticket to take in Universal Studios as well. It was great, and although they may not appreciate the reference, their attention to detail and creating atmosphere was very Disney-esque. My favorite "land" was the Simpsons and Krustyland. I had no idea how much of Springfield they had recreated, and of course my favorite was Moe's Tavern. The Simpsons ride was one of the best in the park. The Transformers Ride was good too, but the wait was tremendous. It stated 90 minutes at the door, but we waited over 2.5 hrs. The rock n roll roller-coaster was memorable as well. Overall, we were very impressed and look forward to going back to Universal Studios if we are ever back in Florida.
Fantastic theme park. Would highly recommend buying the fast pass as it saves so much time,yes it is very pricey but so worth it! A lovely place to go in the evening as well as during the day.

We hadn't been here in a few years. Jaws is gone, Back to the Future is now the Simpson's ride, Mummy is still pretty cool. Some other rides need to go...Twister is boring and half of the special effects aren't working. It would be great if they would change the show for Disaster. It's still the same from 5 or 6 years ago. The Simpson's Springfield area is awesome. My kids loved seeing the restaurants and shops from the show. The Barney area is outdated. Who watches Barney anymore? I would love Universal to replace that area with a Spongebob bikini bottom themed area and rides. Now that would be awesome! Food is expensive as theme parks usually are. We took advantage of the refillable popcorn bucket. $5.99 first, then 99 cents a refill...good for the rest of your life! So I have that saved with our vacation stuff if we ever go back. Ice water is free. The night show was a great tribute to movie history. I think seeing it once was enough. I would probably skip it next time and ride rides.

I don't get it. too expensive, too busy and no value for dollar. went day before Christmas - added express passes to our tickets to the tune of $400.00 more dollars to our already too expensive tickets and blue man show which ended up being cancelled - still have to get money back for that. Kids stood in line for hulk - express line - ride failed and they waited an hour+ had one ride and the youngest felt too sick to go on too many more. Went on several walk through adventures which were a joke. Not interested in Harry Potter where t was even crazy busier. Stayed for fake Santa Claus parade...all in all not a really fun and very expensive day.

I had heard so much about this event that my boyfriend and I decided to go to it instead of Howl O Scream ( won't make that mistake again). The line for every house was no less than 100 mins and that was with the fast pass. We only got to 4 of the 8 houses. There were more booze stands than anything else and the place was full of drunk people that at one stage you could not tell the difference between them and the staff dressed as zombies. The only saving grace was the Rocky Horror Tribute which was FANTASTIC. I love Universal Studios but this is one event I won't be returning for.

I love Universal. There is so much to do and see, and the rides are incredible. I think the parking is a big high, and the waits for the attractions are the only downers. You can get the express pass, but it is very expensive for a family of four. If you go during a busy time period, the express pass can cost you almost as much as the ticket itself. So it's a very expensive day ...... but it's a blast!

We just came back from a quick trip to Orlando. We went to Islands of Adventure first to experience all that is Harry Potter, and my kids decided to check out Universal Studios on day two because of the Minions ride. We got into the park around 11:30 or so and by 3:00 we were headed out the door with a quick stop at the store to get a few last minute souvenirs (merchandise from Islands of Adventure is also available in Universal Studios). The place just seems randomly organized and quite run down. The rides seems to be either thrill ride roller coasters or 3D adventures that rely on similar tricks (spritzing water). We happened to be there during a parade and let's just say that the good folks at Disney have NOTHING to worry about. It was fairly lackluster and underwhelming - even the performers looked bored or embarrassed. Later, we were sitting on a bench having a snack (they DO have turkey legs) and a woman dressed as Betty Boop along with a handler came down the street. She had difficulty attracting any interest. One family insisted their children pose and it was the most uncomfortable scene I've witnessed. Betty tried gamely to get them to smile and pose and the kids just had no clue who this strange woman in red was. I imagine if you lived locally and loved roller coasters or were interested in the musical acts that perform (it was Mardi Gras and Daughtry and Robin Thicke were among the featured performers) it would be worth a visit, but otherwise you can easily skip this park and do something else in Orlando. All of this could change with the addition of the Harry Potter attractions slated for this summer (including transport via Hogwarts Express to Islands of Adventure). I suspect that the reason for bringing Harry into this park is to try to spread out the crowds and reinvigorate Universal Studios. For what it's worth, the Mummy ride was fun and the Rock Roller Coaster has a fun feature that allows you to select a song from about 20 options to play while you are having your neck and spine re-aligned on the ride. To be fair, we didn't experience some of the big attractions (Transformers, Fear Factor) as we just had become bored.

There are two parks here... The rides are very good with both actual rides (roller coasters and kids' rides) and 3D rides. There is literally something for everyone. Good food choices as well. Wait times were minimal. We did not enjoy Disaster (the ride was good, the intro was LONG and not enjoyable); same went for Terminator (not worth the wait - which is intro time not considered wait time). We went as a party of 4 with two adults, one 18 year old and one 15 year old. We all had our favourites. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was phenomenal but a smaller area than expected. The teens loved the Butter Beer (not the Pumpkin Juice). We ate at The Three Broomsticks Restaurant. Good value for the money and wonderful atmosphere. This park is much more relaxed than Disney. If you want a beer, shop around...prices vary significantly. They have 'free' lockers requiring a finger print to acquire and release the lock. They are free for different periods of time depending upon the attraction. We did have a problem and we were charged $9 for a few minutes longer than the time allowed, even though we do not believe we were longer. The ride line was 5 minutes in length, our party went on twice and returned to find we were fined. A credit card is then required to release your lock.

If you are travelling with kids, this park is not worth it. I am here with a 6yr oldsnd a 10 yr old my parents in their 60s. So we wait online for 1.5hrs to ride the last transformes. We did not mind since we only had that and dispicable me to ride. Well the transformer ride broke down in the middle of the ride. We waited ten munutes to walk down three flights of steps and then were given an express ticket to cone back or use in another ride. So we went to dispicable me. Still not bothered just disappointed. But then were tdld wecould not use it on that ride. So we wd hv to wait another hour! No consideration that we had just waited an hour half for ride that dodnt work. Also kids were bored of all the same type rides. Staff not as well trained as Disney's. Not worth the 98 pp admission. At all.

Universal Studios Florida is not as fun as Universal Islands of Adventure, but still a great day out. My family with a 16 year old, 14 year old, and 12 year old spent five hours there. However, we did get the Express Passes, which were awesome. Our favorite rides were the Hollywood Rip Ride Rock It, the Revenge of the Mummy, and the Despicable Me Minion Mayhem. We also enjoyed the Shrek 4-D show, the Transformers 3-D ride, the Men In Black Alien Attack, and the Simpsons Ride. I also loved the atmosphere in the New York section of the park. We ate at Mel's Drive In, which was standard park food. It was a fun day, but I wish there were more rides. Something we all agreed on: Universal DOES NOT need another simulation ride. They're okay, but not as good as the real roller coaster experience.
It Is so cool they have done a wonderful job bring the Harry potter movies to life. I can't wait until it is completely finished. Which will be July of 2014.
Loved the Blues Brothers show. Beelejuice is great too. I loved ET, but I guess I'm a big softy! Great for families, something for every age.

I have visited all of the Orlando theme parks multiple times since I was a kid. Never have I been so disappointed with Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. First, we got there and were required to take a "3 question survey" that actually turned out to be around 30 questions. I have no problem with surveys when the time is appropriate. My family spent PLENTY of money to spend the day at these parks so the last thing I want to do is take time to fill out a survey. Although that was annoying, that wasn't what ruined our trip. As we continue to walk through the parks we were asked to take several more surveys. We decided to visit Harry Potter attraction. My advice - DON'T GO. I am a Harry Potter fan and found it be completely overrated. There was a winding line to just to get into the candy shop or to get a "Butter Beer" aka overpriced cream soda. You can hardly walk through "Diagon Alley" without rude people constantly bumping into you or stepping on your feet. Still, that's not the thing that made me lose my cool. We waited in extremely long lines for them to tell my father he was too big to ride certain rides. My father is a tall man who is a bit larger, but not obese. His knees were crammed into the roller coasters that seemed to be made for 5' 5" tall people that weigh less than 200 lbs. Just know that these rides are not created for all body types. We also waited in line to ride "Revenge of the Mummy" in Universal Studios. They stopped the normal line for more than 10 minutes to let all of the "Fast Pass" users to go before everyone else. I understand that they paid extra to cut the lines, but you should not stop an entire line for over 10 minutes to let every single one of them go. The line shouldn't have gotten that long in the first place. The thing that irritates me the most about this experience is that they don't tell you this kind of stuff beforehand. They take your money and don't care whether you can enjoy their attractions or not. I am someone that cares about the ethics of businesses and I believe that Universal Studios strictly cares about making money and will do whatever it takes to do so.

Its been awhile since we've been to Universal, and after our visit to Epcot I have to admit I was a little apprehensive that we'd find that it hasn't aged well either. I was very thrilled to find that while there are still some remnants from the past Twister and Terminator that should arguably retired, they are more than balanced out by newer additions such as the The Simpsons, The Transformers, and Dispicable Me. Rounding the whole thing out are classics such as The Mummy- my wife made us ride that one twice- and E.T. The Simpsons ride is very cool, and the Springfield area of the part is awesome- make sure to visit Moe's Tavern for a Flaming Moe and a Duff beer and Lard Lads for a giant donut. Oh, and how can I forget the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket? Just hang on and enjoy the ride of your life while listening to some great tunes; be careful though if you are a big guy like me as the seats are a little tight and you have to be a little careful of the leg restaints. I've never even seen the movie Dispicable Me but I really enjoyed the ride. Rain was eminent all afternoon, but held off until the day was almost over for us- then the monsoon came. We waited it out and ended our day with E.T. which somehow managed to be nostalgic and almost quaint for me. Two final words for you: Fast Pass.

Liked all rides etc, but felt tickets are expensive, especially for one day, also considering not cheap felt that universal should spend some money and update certain old rides/shows ie terminator etc plus certain things like wand and extras were overpriced
great park, its fun for all ages, I highly recommend getting the express pass, well worth the cost of it.

I coudnt wait until my kids were old enough to go to Disney. Would have been my first time too. Boy was i disappointed! The sun was hot, the lines long and everything ridiculously expensive! I spent so long waiting in lines but the end of the day we had only gone on two! The show was great though! The kids enjoyed only that! Dont think I will be going back

This is one of my favourite parks, I must say.... If you buy the express plus pass, you don't have to get in line at all (in Disney parks, you're granted with three fast passes, and that's all), so you can easily make through all attractions before the sun goes down. And you can buy beer almost everywhere, which is also pretty nice! :)

The Fireworks show at Universal Orlando resort:    Let me begin by saying that i love both Disney parks and the Universal parks. We are spoiled with the highly creative shows en excellent quality at Disney. But please keep in mind that at Universal all fireworks are at close proximity to the audience, and there is no space for shooting high aerial fireworks as seen at the Magic Kingdom or Epcot. The fireworks products being used at Universal can be compared ( are the same) with the Fantasmic show over at Disney Hollywood studio’s. Those products are very expensive and of the highest quality. And is also the only product that can be used at that distance to the audience.  I think that the concept of the Cinematic spectaculair at Universal is briilliant. The music, narration, the movie-clips en how its blend into each other It has enough potential to give the audience goose-bums and take them on a journey into the Universal films. Overall i think its very entertaining and worth waiting for.  Perhaps a new pyrotechnic designer and show designer can do a better job and give the park and spectators a fireworks show that it deserves.

We had a great time. There is a little something for every age. Lines were somewhat long and it's annoying that you wait 45 minutes to an hour in line while express pass people keep flying by. Now I know they paid for that right but other parks, like Disney, seem to alternate pass riders and line waiters in a more efficient and equitable manner. Universal needs to work on that! The staff members were generally friendly even though many of them were quite young. This park needs more covered areas throughout the park where visitors can get out of the rain when needed.  On a side note, mainly for anyone from the park who reads this, when exiting the park in the evening we were approached by a young woman about taking a survey about our experience. We were moving quickly to try to make our shuttle bus on time so we wouldn't have to wait another hour for the next one. She asked nicely if she could ask us some questions and I very politely said, "No thank you ... we're in a terrible rush for the shuttle." She responded as we walked past with an extremely snide comment that I won't repeat here. This annoyed me because I was very polite to her and didn't just ignore her, but it really bothered me because I later had to take time to explain away her rudeness to my 7 year-old daughter who was also bothered by the incident. I try to find a silver lining by looking at it as a teachable moment for my daughter but it never should have happened.
Very long lines n to hot we paid to much money to be waiting so long! Fast pass that is only good after 4 is crazy! My kids can't be up so late!

What can you say about a Adventure that can take many tangents and lift the spirits in so many ways. Thankyou Universal for not just having a great place to escape and enjoy, but continuously upgrading your facilities and attractions, as I have visited your Studio's now 8 different times on my 21 visits to USA. My wife and I are heading back to Florida on May 07, for a Convention and hopefully we will get to revisit for the 9th time and see the improvements since our last visit in 2012.

We visited the Universal Studios side of the two parks the day after we did Islands of Adventures. We enjoyed this side more as it seemed to have something for everyone (there was a 12 year old, 35 year old, 39 year old, and a 70 year old in our group). There were less people around which made moving throughout the park easier. Favorites of my family were the Simpsons area, Transformers area and ride, and the I love Lucy Tribute.

Enjoyed universal but sad to see jaws gone. Being replaced by another Harry potter venue that will connect both sides with Islands of adventure ( which I do not like). Too bad because jaws was a classic. Had fun on the old faithfuls such as ET, Disaster and twister. The shows are always good and loved Fear Factor live which I saw for the first time.

Islands of adventure is better, but only because of the Harry Potter stuff. The Minions ride (Despicable Me) is a ridiculous wait for a ride that's absolutely not worth it. But it must be the newest ride there, because it's always an hour+ wait. We got there early one day and got on in about 30 minutes. Wouldn't do it again unless it was about a 10 minute wait. Transformers ride and revenge of the mummy are way better. Overall very good, although it seems all the ride technology is essentially the same (motion simulators).

I have been going to Universal regularly for several years and one thing I can count on is that there will always be some sort of construction going on at the park. I really enjoy the park overall and love the Springfield area but only appreciate coming here because I have an annual pass that makes it a good value.  I don't think it's worth the price of a 1 day ticket. Many rides like Simpsons and Transformers are great. I just watched the Beetlejuice show for the first time and was actually impressed at how good it was but they lack the attention to detail that Disney gives to the appearance of their parks. The streets just look dirty and old. A lot of the buildings have giant printed tarp coverings on them, I don't know why.  The quality of the staff has been declining over the years also, I guess that they don't emphasized friendliness in training and evaluations anymore.  Overall I still enjoy going and liked that the lines were reasonable when I went without needing an Express Pass but I hope that management takes a break from building new things after the Harry Potter section opens to improve the visual appearance of the rest of the park.

What can I say; had higher expectations. Been about 20 yrs since last visit and the place looks like it had not been updated nor maintained since then. Tried to have my kids ages 5&9 meet a fee characters and they would close the line when we arrived. Tried to use my dining plan at an indoor place and the crowds and lines were unmanageable. Then when I did redeem at a pizza place the service was awful and took forever to figure out what the deal was with the plan.  Employees are in faded and worn out attire. No one seemed pleasant and happy to serve.  Ended with a stop for a slice of cake and coffee at the cafe near exit and both cakes tried were awful; worse than the cheapest blandest piece of cake ever tried. Waste of $10+.  Terribly missed the Disney experience. Never again.
Brought my 8 year old & we all loved it. I've been to Disney World & I enjoyed it more! We are planning a trip back to Florida in December & I hope to have time to go back.

Fun is available for people of all ages at this attraction. Tons of rides and things to see and do. Food is pricey as can be expected at a theme park. Be prepared to do lots of walking and standing in line.

Went last October and had a great time! Thought it was good value for money, for the ticket, food and drink. All rides were really good, loved the 3d/4d Harry Potter and Spiderman rides!
