The staff were all very friendly and helpful, plenty of bathrooms around the parks and places to get snacks and drinks. Maybe not much in it for very young kids but plenty in it! Found it much better than Disney's Magic Kingdom! Would love to go back

October 2013. We went to universal studios the Harry potter ride was my favorite. I am so glad they added this ride. We also went to the haunted houses and we had so much fun the only issues is the long lines. If I had to do it again. I would buy the upgrade to pass the lines

We enjoyed the new rides but were also happy to see some of our old favorites still in place like Men in Black. Enjoyed the character dances and easy engagements. Like the multiple selections of food options.

They mange the front gate very well. They had extra personal to get people in. The lines moved very smoothly. All the staff we encountered were friendly and very helpful. I have to give cudos to the child swap experience. This is the first time we used this because we now travel with small children. I am a grandmother of 59 and I still ride everything. We did not have to go back into line when it was my turn or my daughter's turn,they have a room for you to wait in. I thought that was awesome. Another thing with water costing $2.75 a bottle the cups of ice were free. I was able to share one bottle at a time between three grand children (that was awesome). At the end of most rides they had the characters there for picture taking, again that was a great idea. My favorite rides were Harry Potter &Transformers. Still love Despicable me, Mummy , Spiderman, Simpsons, Jurassic Park and Men in Black. Shrek in 4d was Awesome. It did not scare the grand kids. One more thing fresh fruit was a good idea. This was a good source of hydration in the heat. For the 100 years of Movies Light Show that night we had cupcakes as we watched the show. One day we stopped into Ben & Jerry's for ice cream, and we visited the old time soda fountain. Drug Store style on another day. one of our favorites is Mel's Drive In, we eat here every visit. I do not remember the name on the Isles of Adventure's side, we stopped into a bakery, My grand daughter had a funnel cake and I got the cheese cake. I was so glad I did not have to carry cash. I was able to use my debit card everywhere. And the Triple A card saved us a lot of money as well. We did not go to disney this visit to Orlando, but we do not feel like we missed out on anything. Thanks Universal for an Awesome vacation experience.
Me and my family had a great time there. I really enjoyed the 3d rides. It was adventurous. Will differently visit again!

Bought a 3 day ticket with express pass. The express pass was worth it for us, but we really only needed two days to ride/see everything. If you have the stamina to stay all day, you could buy the 2 park pass with express and see it all (both parks) in one day! The rides are amazing, my favorites are Potter and Simpsons, because you don't need to wear 3D glasses. My only complaint is about the lockers next to each ride. Several times they would not re-open for us and we had to go find an attendant. The water rides are great. Jurassic Park and the flume one get you perfectly wet to tackle the hot weather. But if you go on the Barge ride, bring a change of clothes!!

Mixed feelings about US overall. Too many 3D ones for my liking though. I had express pass which is a must have. A few great rides: Dragon Challenge, The Mummy, Rip Ride Rockit (i LOVE this ride, it was the best one in the parks), Jurassic Park Biggest let downs were: Hulk, Spiderman, Dr Dooms Fear Fall, Ripsaw Falls  Frozen Butterbeer is delicious, though it could be shared as it's pretty sweet and rich. Lunch at Three Broomsticks was a good hearty meal

Arrived before it opened so assumed we would beat the queues. Spent the first 30mins waiting to get on despicable me ride. Good ride. We then managed to get on the mummy twice without queuing - awesome ride! Thereafter the day became much slower. Twister a waste of 30 mins. Was looking forward to beetle juice however was pretty poor - Dracula needs to find a career that doesn't involve singing. Shame was much better 20 years ago. Simpsons ride was good - no actual Simpson characters to be found? Great Duff beers and Krusty burgers. Mixed bag really.

Went here for Star Wars weekend whilst in Florida on holiday was good but wasn't as impressed as the other parks not that much to do the rides it does have are good and the Star Wars ride is awesome but in general I wouldn't visit again

This is my favourite theme park. The Simpsons, the Mummy, T2 3D, ET and Transformers are all excellent and well worth the price of admission. The new Springfield area is also brilliant - try a Duff beer (alcoholoc) and Flaming Moe (non-alcoholic) at Moe's!

We did this as our yearly summer vacation and had an absolute blast! We loved the rides and managed our time well amongst the lines! The food was a little expensive but the park was a great adventure! Harry Potter land was by far the fave!

The main reason was to visit both parts of the Harry Potter world and ride the train. The staff was excellent, and the two day park hopper with fast pass ticket was expensive, but unlike Disney the fast pass can be used over and over not just 3 rides like Disney. The staff played their parts well, and were helpful and fun even during the brutal Florida July sun and heat. A lot of walking, and some of the rides cannot handle fat people like me. I am not HUGE, and can fit any Disney ride, but they do have seats outside rides that you can try before going to the line. The fast pass was worth the price if you only have a day or two, food good for a theme park, but like Disney expensive. The people the employees make the park and experience, hopeful upper boss will learn these.

We travelled from park to park on the Hogwarts Express which wasn't as popular as we'd expected. Most people were there for the Harry Potter Diagon Alley opening. We got a return ticket so we trawled the rear of the park and returned only to find that it was another four hour wait for the Gringotts ride. Life's too short!

Universal studios is a nice place to visit. We enjoyed all the movie attractions. Getting into Harry potter was nearly impossible, because they just opened it to the public last week. If you are able to go to universal studios you will have a great time.

This was our first time and it was amazing! We were lucky enough to go to the new area of Diagon Alley and it is breath taking! The new ride in that area is fantastic and defiantly worth the wait. The transformers simulator is really good as well as the mummy ride and disaster! Would defiantly recommend buying the freestyle unlimited drink as it is definitely worth the money and would defiantly recommend having an express pass as it makes your experience 10 times better!
This is a must see if you go to Orlando. Our day in Universal was much better than the day we spent in Disney World. Perfect!

This is the 3rd time I have been to Universal Studio's and I cant fault it.  Two parks to this location, Universal Studios & Islands of Adventure.  The rides you must go on are as follows:-  Islands Of Adventure The Hulk, Spiderman, Transformers .  Universal Studios Hollywood Rip (Rollercoaster), Simpsons, Mummy (it's not bad).  The park also shows TNA Wrestling shows which are filmed for TV. You can get free tickets to be in the audience on the day if you go to the Audience Ticket Centre at the front of the park as you go in. If you have never been, worth going to see just for fun.  A must is the Blue Man Group. This show you will have to pay to go into, its about £55/60 a ticket but well worth it.  Advise on park drinks & food (like all the parks) the stuff is over priced (compared to outside in Orlando). Take frozen drinks in with you and let them defrost during the day otherwise you will be spending £'s on drinks due to the hot climate.  Get your pictures with the characters, the kids love this ( I loved it)  You can purchase Fast Pass Tickets for around £55ish (I think). These are useful if the lines are really long, but I think that the cost is alittle cheeky as you have already paid to get in.

Great park, lots of fun rides, down side, is the very very long queues , some over 2 hours, so you are forced to buy fast pass , which for a family of 4 will cost you £ 240 for one day only and does not included harry potter rides, feels like a ripe off. They also charge $5 for use of lockers to go on some rides. A great day out and some of the best rides but very very expensive.

After visiting Universal Studios Fla, my immediate impression was that there was no need for Guantanamo Bay because there's Universal Studios.  The good: The rides are fun, especially for older kids. I really liked the Simpsons area because I'm a huge fan. The Harry Potter area was entertaining as well, but again you'd have to be a fan. The Transformers that they bring out for pictures were very realistic.  The bad: The lines were terribly long when we visited. The wait was more than an hour at every ride. The "fast pass" should be renamed "slightly less slow pass". A lot of people upgraded to the pricy fast pass (about $90), so you'll still be in line for a while. Long lines and malfunctions are a common complaint with the reviewers, but they still give the place 4-stars, which makes me wonder if people had overheated during their visit to the park.  The ugly: What would happen if every airline scheduled a 9 am departure at an airport? Come to Universal Studios and find out. The crowd to get into the park in the morning is crazy (see attached photo), all because of a small bag-check area. I'm surprised that no one has been trampled to death.  For me, the pain wasn't worth the fun, and Universal is worst in managing crowds compared to the other theme parks. The wait time is so long that it's simply not a good value. But, there must be something there, because everyone keeps going back.

My first time checking out Universal Studio and it was great! Had a lot of fun with much to check out! I don't have an amazing enough adjective to describe the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Spent our entire day here checking out both sides of the park. Friendly staff as well.

The Rides in this park are phenomenal, especially the " Harry Potter Ride " the simulator's used in the park are exceptional, unbelievable infrastructure. The Roller coaster rides are Jaw dropping. I recommend everyone to get an express pass, if you don't wanna wait long(1-1'1/2 Hrs) for every ride in the park and its better to get the express pass along with the Park tickets online, rather then getting it there in the park as the express passes are little bit expensive when you want to purchase them in the park. Me and friend covered the 2 parks in one day, with express pass.  I love this place, I would definitely recommend this, and of course TRIPADVISOR is the best \m/

This is a great park, plenty to do. Buy your tickets online to get the best deals. The fast pass is arou d 50 dollars per person which in my opinion is overrated as the cues were long everywhere. There is a massive fuss over Harry Potter there which means if you want to go on these rides be prepared to cue for 3-4 hours. Good park, a must if staying in Orlando.

It's been 5 years since we last visited Universal and it the interim Universal has stepped up their game. Not only have they add great new attractions but more importantly I felt there was a real up-grade in the level of service. Disney has always been the benchmark, but Universal has matched them. The cast members are friendly, courteous and extermly helpful. I am handicapped and everyone went above and beyond to make my visit pleasurable. One area Universal now has it over Disney is parking especially for handicapped. Two times on my visit to Disney I wasn't able to use the handicap lot and instead had to use a overflow lot. One time I almost didn't make it back to my van because my batteries were low and I was parked so far away. Universal on the other hand has more spaces available in covered garage.  The new attractions are now on a par with the best of Disney World. The Harry Potter areas are like stepping into the movies. The attention to detail is unbelievable. There are costumed cast members interacting with the guests. And there are spots around Diagon Alley where purchasers of magic wands can do magic. The crowds were huge though so if your are bothered by that you need to wait awhile for the novelty to wear off. We ate at the Leaky Cauldron and the food was excellant. My only complaint with food at Universal is that there are no full service resturaunts. Make sure you try the butter-beer.  Also new to me this time is Springfield, home to the Simpsons. This was a real fun area. With Moes Tavern serving Duff's beer, the Quicky-mart, Duff Brewry Beer Garden. You find yourself right in with the characters. My wife raved about Krash thru Krustyland that replaced Back to the Future. ( I got a call from work and didn't get a chance to ride).

We could not understand how people could spend a full day here unless they stood in a long queue for every ride. Mostly just shops and overcrowded places to eat which we thought were overpriced. Certainly not worth the entrance fee.
Spent a few days here, lots to do, queues not too bad outside of school holidays, prices for food not too bad (considering it is a park!) great restaurants at city walk on the way out too.

The new Diagon Alley attraction is awesome, and is actually much better than Hogsmeade. The lines are long to get in the stores and ride, but well worth it. I'd highly recommend getting a hotel room on site, because you get 1 hour early admission into Diagon Alley. (Also, you get free Express passes for everyone but they aren't accepted at Diagon Alley; they'll help a lot in the rest of the parks though.) Get to the line for Escape from Gringotts as soon as you can, because even with a 1 hour advantage you will easily have a 1-2 hour wait! If you don't have that advantage you will have a 4 hour wait, easily. The ride itself is only ~2 minutes, though it is exciting and moderately fast.  The other rides are good too. I couldn't ride Rip Ride Rocket because there was lightning. I loved Mummy; it was indoors so weather doesn't affect it and it was quite thrilling, more thrilling and high-speed than Gringotts.  They have a lot of 3D rides/attractions, such as Shrek, Simpsons, Transformers and Despicable and the like. If you do these all in a row your senses will feel over-stimulated at the end. Most of these are suitable for small children too.

Firstly rides were amazing my favourite was despicable me minion mayhem there were plenty of restaurants and the food was great park was clean and tidy and staff were extremely kind only thing I didn't like was one of the rides which was twister as I felt it was dated but apart from that amazing.

I went to Florida 3 times in the last 20 years, going to all the parks. I found it really clean and great value (pound was strong against the dollar, first time 1998). Everyone could not do enough for you, so happy and friendly! The food was excellent, anything you wanted and at any time. You need to have your I.D with you all the time for drinks, as they need to see your age (the server is responsible legally if you get drunk in their bar). Would go back, this time I will take my daughter, but children need to be older to experience it fully (12 and over should get a lot out of it).

We visited this park yesterday and got there early to avoid the queues. Obviously alot of people had the same view but that was ok. i didnt expect it to be empty due to being such a popular park. We paid 17 dollars for parking which i find high but can understand as they need to maintain the park and pay for the staff etc, i used the tactic off turning right as soon as we entered as most people head for the first ride which is the Despicable Me ride. Within the first hour we managed to complete three rides including the Simpsons ride which was brilliant and MiB. The disaster ride was broken at first but by the time we went back it had finished. The average wait time for us was about 30 minutes. Dragons Alley was too long 150 minutes so we didnt bother. Despicable Me was the longest wait 60 minutes but was well worth it as it is the best ride in the park. We even managed to watch the Beetlejuice show. All in all we had a fantastic day and thought it was far better than next doors Islands of Adventures.

We queued for far too long! It broke down 5 times while we were queuing. The ride it self was a very poor relation to the ride in the other park. It last 3 minutes and didn't thrill or excite, so when asked if we wanted to queue again on the fast track our group voted with its feet and went back to the other Harry Potter ride in the other park!

Surprised our kids (girls: 19, 15, 11) with a four day trip to Universal. This was our first time here and we had a great time.  Wizarding World of Harry Potter: Diagon Alley reviewed separately. All food is also reviewed separately.  Get there at early open (we went to Islands of Adventure and took the Hogwarts Express over). Head straight to Diagon Alley.  Despicable Me was such a cute ride; 3D animation was awesome. Took a lot of bumps but I laughed a lot.  E.T. Adventure you can tell has seen better days, but who doesn't love the little alien? If anything, take some time to cool down.  I can't do roller coasters: so no reviews on those for me. Sorry!  Shrek was not all that cool, but I was never a fan of the movie.  Twister Ride-it-Out was disappointing. Stood in the back row and was wondering when the show was going to actually start. Thought it would have been a lot more than it was.  Transforners ride was loud and bumpy, and thankfully a tall person was in front of me, so the full effect of 3D was lessened.  I thought the Horror Make-up Show would have been more interactive instead of a little skit, but the audience participant made it worth the time.  Now, The Simpsons ride was (outside of Harry Potter) was the ride of the park. I haven't watched The Simpsons in a long time and my kids have never watched them, but the wait was 10 minutes so we went on it. I laughed my BUTT off the entire time. I had no idea the ride was going to be what it was, which made it ironic and funny, since I'm not a coaster fan. Best ride, IMO.

Visited Universal Park on a park hopper pass and had a fantastic time. The Harry Potter Diagone Alley was the most amazing rendition of the shops and the in and out streets off the alley gave you the feeling of being on the movie set. The park has some incredible rides like the Transformer and the Dispicable Me, the Men in Black, ET and Gringots Bank. I loved the Dragon atop Gringots Bank that spews fire balls. The park is very friendly and very clean for as many people as visit daily. I liked that they post waiting times for the lines so you knew how long you would be waiting. The Islands of Adventure side is as much fun and with Hogsmeade and the Castle and Lost Continent and Jurrasic park are amazing. Prices are comparable to other theme parks.

More roller coasters, love it, enjoyed all of them even though some were a bit dated, the characters wandering around were really good, again yes it was busy & yes you had to queue, but didn't bother me!

We went to Florida to take my 9 year old daughter to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter The week after Diagon Alley opened. We expected long lines and alot of people but we still had a great time!  The interactive wands made the trip worth while and I love that everyone stays in Character in whichever part of the park you are in. Frozen butter beer, Fish and chips, earwax flavored jelly beans and all of the Harry Potter clothing you want. Both side of the park were great the rides on the Hogwarts Castle side we awesome, The coolest thing we were able to do was go into Diagon Alley at night. Dragons breathing fire, lanterns lighting up with a flick of the wand, the creepy knockturn ally and Borgan and Burkes. If you are a Potterhead this is the place for you.

My family and I attend universal 2 to 3 times a year because of all of the special programs offered day and night for every person in the family. With its close proximity to several dining and extended activity options...it is the perfect vacation for everyone! What we do is stay always within a 2 mile radius of the park (most close hotels have free shuttles) to save us on parking fees or cab rides. We pack light lunches as most of the hotels have small kitchenettes... This helps to cut the cost of food as there's no use going to the parks without the vip pass..... and this can be pricey...it's what you need though to get the absolute most out of your vacation. Short wait times on rides, exibits, and your made to feel as though your attention span is consistently entertained! For the pass, our family also carries lanyards to hold onto our passes, this promises that they won't fall out of your pockets on the coveted loop De loop!! Good luck! Have fun!! (:
We came here Feb 2014. No queues, not too crowded. Had a whale of a time. Ticked off the bucket list :)

Universal studios has something for all ages. This is my family's favorite theme park. The new rides like Tansformers,The minion ride and the Simpsons ride were awesome. The workers there are so wonderful. My daughter's asthma got really bad due to the heat and we took her to the first aid office to check her vitals. They checked her out and got us a special pass so that she could skip,the lines.we were just going to leave because we were concerned about her being out in that heat and humidity. The heat was agrivating her asthma. I was very happy that they have such a kind staff.

But I was pleasantly surprised by Universal Studios Florida! The feel of the place was very nice, not too crowded (although the crowd levels were higher) and not as hot (if that is even possible). We rode more rides here than at IOA and loved nearly every one. Transformers was first and it was a thrill ride and a half! Loved the theming in the queue and the ride experience was fantastic. We rode ET, very tame, but cute. It needs to be updated, I think, to make it relevant to the generations who may never have seen the movie. Twister, well, we were very disappointed by this experience. We expected something more than what was delivered. The Mummy was absolutely fantastic! Great Coaster! MIB was fun (even though I didn't win). Daughter and her boyfriend rode The Simpson Ride and said it was a blast. The longest wait we had all day was for the Hogswart Express train ride from Diagon Alley to Hogsmeade. The wait time was posted as 10 minutes, but we were in line for fully 45 minutes and it was not worth it. Also, the posted wait time for Escape from Gringotts was over 2 hours, so we opted to not even try it. But the Dragon was spectacular! All in all, I would recommend The Studios over IOA any day.

Great as ever, had to queue for 3 hours for Gringotts bank.... only worth it if you are an ardent HP fan as other ride in Islands of adventure is better. Hogwarts express very good. Visiting end of Aug great as parks not so busy as US children back in school. Single rider option great if not desperate to stay as family unit; you can pretty much get on all rides without a wait. Park well maintained and restroom clean.
Again like islands of adventure highly recommend fast @ $88 each. Would have only done 3 rides if no passes as the queues were quite long.

We spent a few days at Universal and still didn't get on everything! The rides are something else, minions, shrek, transformers. simpsons etc, all fab and very well thought out. The queues are something else too (90mins+) so if you can buy a fast track ticket for the day as it will allow you to get around more rides. Great mix of rides for all ages and attractions, Harry Potter train a must!
Had the most fun at: 1. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter 2. Revenge of the Mummy 3. Despicable Me Minion Mayhem 4. Transformers  Try Express lane or Single Rider lane to avoid the long wait.

Awesome theme park. We spent 3 days there including the islands of adventure. If you're visiting around Halloween I would highly recommend going to the haunted houses. The experience just walking along the streets is unbelievable.

Amazing time had by us all at Universal Studios. I have a broken leg so we took our rented wheelchair along as we weren't sure if there would be an EVC available. Looking at the advice onine, we had read that we should go straight to 'Guest Services' (which is on the right at the park entrance) . We qued for about 20 mins to ask and found out they are $70 to hire. Didn't fancy paying $50-70 each visit, so my partner and son took turns to push. The entire park is wheelchair friendly and some rides we had to que with everyone in the normal manner but some took us from the que to a different entrance for easy access to attraction. I unfortunately couldn't ride most things but what I did manage to do was great. Transformers, Spiderman and Harry Potter (The Forbidden Journey) were my favourites. A TIP is on the Harry Potter ride, you ask a staff member to show you the lift and there is a special, separate ride entrance with a non-moving floor allowing you to access the ride :) The overall experience was great even though I have a broken leg!

This is one of my favorite parks in Orlando. There have been two new additions since my last visit, Transformers which I highly recommend if you like the Spiderman ride in Islands of Adventure and the newest part of the Harry Potter areas Diagon Alley. The themeing throughout the park is outstanding but once you step foot in Diagon Alley you will be amazed at the attention to detail. Looking forward to seeing what Universal has in store for the future. One tip I can offer is to head into the park and check out the wait times before investing in the express passes. We 2 days after labor day and we didn't wait for any of the rides so paying $70 per person for the express pass would have been a total waste. They sell them all throughout the park so if you start making your way through and the lines become long you can always purchase then. Also the express passes do not work for the Harry Potter attractions.

The new addition to Universal is a must see. Butter Beer and the Ice cream of the same is a definite try. Enjoy the ride at Gringot's. Most rides at Universal require you to store your loose articles in a locker, but no worries it is free for an hour. Our wait was longer and was not charged though. The train ride to and from Islands of adventure is different each way, so take both trips. Hogwarts and Hogsmeade in Islands of adveture are a must see, but the ride in Hogwarts can cause motion sickness. It is a warning, but it was at Gringot's as well which we found much less intense and more enjoyable.

Having stayed at Hard Rock Universal, we were within 5 minutes walk, and have got to say that the rides are a lot better in Universal Studios. Harry Potter is such a large sector of the theme park and is truly amazing. We were allowed extra hours of a morning, including Harry Potter, which made the day so much easier to fit everything in. The staff are extremely friendly and know how to make you have a better day. So many amazing souvenirs to buy as well so leave luggage space

I visited the park with my family and i was amazed, it was so well done, the saff was expelent and helpful, i was on a trip down my memory lane ! many cool rides and cool attractions. will visit again when i return to the US !

We got to the Universal Studios when it opened and that's the way to do it. Having arthritis we had to take it slow and just go in order of appearance. I started off at the roller coaster which had no line, it was great. I'll give highs and lows: when we arrived at the Harry Potter area we couldn't find it, all we saw was a double decker bus and then we went right past it. It wasn't until I reviewed the map again and said we passed it that I realized its like a secret entrance, still there should be signs. So it was the most crowded part of the park. We went right to the only ride they have there, had to put our things in a locker and got in line. The line didn't move much, then we found out the ride was having issues. Ugh. Luckily it didn't have issues for long because once it starts moving the line goes quickly. The issue is the seats, they are new and unforgiving. Don't be overweight or you will not fit, It's not a normal ride seat it also lifts up your legs a bit, hard to describe but it's definitely made for a certain body type. The ride itself it great and a lot of fun, I really enjoyed it. My most favorite ride, in which I clapped when it was finished was Transformer. Wow that's a great ride!! How do they do it?? The worst ride was the Mummy. The seats were the same as Harry Potter but the ride jerks you around so much I had the Heimlich maneuver once, elbowed the guy next to me a couple times and just hated every minute of it, all dark and jerky movements. What's fun about that? A couple rides we wanted to go on were closed, one had the smoke alarm start when we had just started in and the other was closed for a bit so we missed a few on our list. Twister had no wind, I guess it was broke? Time to get rid of Twister and do something new. By late in the day the evening people were arriving and it was getting crowded, so we got some Bubba Gump shrimp and called it a day.

We bought tickets from Orange Lake at the hotel and were not told that we required identification. Luckily the lady accepted a driving licence and credit card with my bus pass. We wasted 45 minutes lining up to obtain the proper tickets.  We then went to the old part of Harry Potter to see Hogwart. We enjoyed the atmosphere of this and all the extras in the castle, where all the pictures talk. We liked the magic set up for the children to follow. Several children were in front of the shop windows trying to find out how to magic items. They have brass plates which you stand on to operate the mechanisms. Children were enjoying this activity.  We bought tickets for both parks so we could ride on the train in both directions. The organisation was excellent and different scenes were seen on both journeys. When we arrived at the station it took us a while to find Diablo Alley, which was atmospheric and creepy. The dragon blowing fire from the roof was very realistic. It was fantastic. Apart from this and Sinbad's voyage we felt some of the rides were tacky and entrance to both parks were overpriced.  Without Harry Potter this would not be somewhere I would want to visit. Harry Potter made the visit worthwhile.  Debbie Quinn

Well they did it again this year and it was awesome again. This is truly the best Halloween attraction in the world. All 8 hours were great. All four scare zones we're cool. I will definitely be there again next year.

I was disappointed with Universal Studio's Florida we were there this Sept 27-14 . We got there early as the Park closed early at 1700 and we didn't want pay extra for the Harry Potter Halloween night thing as it was an extra 40$ per person. Didn't get our value for the money we paid. The Best Ride was the Simpson Family ride the biggest disappointment was the Harry Potter Ride HARRY POTTER AND THE ESCAPE FROM GRINGOTTS™ that had broken down and we had lost some valuable time. I found that the rides were short in duration but what really bothered me was leaving the park early and wasted time at the broken rides. Would I go back NO!

We are hard core Disney fans and this was our first time to Universal. We brought our 2 special needs boys ages 11 and 12. We had a great time! We loved the Despicable me ride and the Transformers ride. Harry potter was amazing! Universals special pass for our kids worked much better than Disney's. At Universal they only give you a return time if the line is more than 30 minutes long. We only had a return time once. At Disney it's 10 minutes, so we got to do a lot more rides at Universal. Although don't expect them to celebrate your anniversary or birthday. My husband and I were celebrating our wedding anniversary and had dinner at Mythos. When I asked if they do anything special so I could surprise my husband our server looked at me like I had grown antennas and gave me a grouchy "no". We would still return to Universal just not for anything special.

We had a two park pass to ride the Hogwarts train between the two parks. Diagon Alley was nice, we rode Gringotts several times. The ice cream shop there was good, with some unique flavors like orange marmalade. t2 3d was a nice show, and Twister was also a show type of attraction. We rode the Mummy(that was pretty wild). We rode most of the rides there several times. ET is still around, it is a easy going ride, and nice and cool inside.  Special thanks to All of the staff at both parks!

We went last Friday and even though it rained all night, we had a fantastic time. Showed up before the scheduled opening time, and they actually opened the park at 6 PM instead of 6:30 PM. It was busy and most likely if we go back next year we will purchase the Express Pass in the future. They start the street off with The Purge:Anarchy when the open the gates. It was pretty cool the way they did it, and The Purge street was awesome.  As far as the houses go, the best without a doubt was The Walking Dead and it was a very big house and walking through it took some time. The worst house was the Dracula house and unless there is no line no waiting, do not waste your time on it. From Dust till Dawn was the second best house, Halloween was good, Giggles & Gore was freaky with the clowns, Alien vs. Predator was cool, the Dollhouse was okay and I really liked the ending and Roanoke was nothing special and would not wait more than 10 minutes for it.  The Face Off street was good, Bayou of Blood was okay, did not see the other street. We saw all eight houses, and it took about five hours. The longest line was Halloween and it was a solid hour wait. If you hate clowns or are scared of them you have to do Giggles & Gore. I hate clowns but I really enjoyed the house, and would have liked to seen it a second time. I would also have like to seen the Walking Dead, Alien and Dust to Dawn again.  The women in the Dust to Dawn house are amazing, the bar scenes were created very well, and it was a very cool house. But you cannot leave the park without seeing the Walking Dead House, in the 20 some odd years we have gone to HHN, this without a doubt is the best house they have ever done.  There is plenty of security and Orlando Police at each house, and if anyone got out of line they were dealt with accordingly. I cannot recommend HHN 2014 enough, it is far better than last years event. If it was not so costly, I would go back again preferably on Halloween Night.

I went to Harry Potter World (which was far better than my expectations) as part of a work event and lost my phone (actually thought that it fell out of my pocket on a roller coaster). A few days later, I got a call from the lost & found saying that they had found the phone and had gotten my number from the "Lost My Iphone" message on the screen. When I returned their call the customer service person was fantastic; she was patient, professional, asked questions to be sure it was my phone, went out of her way to tell me the condition of the phone, and best of all, they shipped it back for free.

The rides are intense and fun! But I only found it fun to ride the rides. Didn't do any shopping. Disney has much to offer. I'd only suggest getting a 2 park pass for a day going to US and IoA and city walk after. Rides you must ride: Mummy, transformers, dueling dragons, Harry potter
Love the new Harry Potter section. The theming is even better than in Hogwarts. Gringotts has been closed both times we tried to go to it though. Do not miss the Simpsons Krustyland ride.

Thank you Universal, for bringing the magical Diagon Alley to this park. We knew it would be special as we walked up to Grimmauld Place, and waited to see Kreacher peek out of the window in Sirius' house. The Knight Bus across the street with Stan and the talking shrunken head were awesome. Gringott's is amazing- I love everything about the bank you go through as you wait in line. September was a good time to go, with max wait time for this new ride at 45 minutes. If you get a chance to participate, the Wand Chooses the Wizard demonstration next to Ollivander's (which is a much larger store than the one in Hogsmeade) is super and the wizard made it very realistic for us. There were 4 adults on our trip, but everything about this part of the park made us feel like young wizards. We ate lunch at the Leaky Cauldron- good food and a great atmosphere! The rest of the park is enjoyable as well- Seussland, Twister, Despicable Me, Mel's Diner, ET, Men in Black & the parade were some of our other favorites. We spent 4 days touring both parks, staying about 1/2 of the hours they were open each day. The multi-park ticket allows you to ride Hogwarts Express, which has different scenes and actions when you go in the opposite direction, so take it both ways if time allows.

The lines were WAY to long - even watching those with express pass - seems most everyone waited. Some of the rides were NOT worth the long wait. The Harry Potter section of the part was awesome. The lines there were extremely long. Save yourself the time and trouble of the train ride (Hogwart's Express) - it was short and LAME - and that was the longest line that we waited in - VERY disappointing. Diagon Alley was very cool to walk around in. The Forbidden Journey Ride was excellent! Too many ticket prices and options Universal - get your act together.

This is a must, but be advised you will need the fast track tickets to get around. Some of the queues were over 2 hours without the tickets so getting round in one night is almost impossible without them.  The houses were all good apart from Alien v Predator which was pretty poor. The Walking Dead house was awesome, my wife was scared out of her skin and had her eyes closed clinging on for dear life at the end.  Some of the streets are also themed and my wife thoroughly enjoyed these. I would not advise taking under 15s as I think it would be too much for the majority of them.  It was expensive with the fast track, but you're in Orlando so it's to be expected and as a one off is worth it.

Went on a Sunday night with wife and another couple, visited 4 houses and spent over four hours in lines waiting. Will not go again, but will return to the Park. If any one does want to go, buy the Fast Pass.

This was our first visit to Universal Studios, we went October 11th. We had fun but it was a little busier but not too bad considering it was a Saturday. I refused to pay more money for the express pass, talk about nickel and diming you and it is expensive!!!! I am glad that we experienced it but it doesn't beat Disney World in my opinion.

This is our 3rd trip in the past 10 years. Each time, its better and better. In my opinion it is more teen to any age adult, especially with Harry Potter in both parks. Yes there is some areas for little kids, but those places are about things that were on tv 10 years ago.. I see there is a listing for City walk, but since we only go to Jimmy Buffett Margaritaville Restaurant we skip the rest, and so will I skip City walk except to say it cuts down on getting to one of the two parks. I do like the new security implemented for the parks, with so many people the terrorist factor is down. However I am trying to get a response as to how long the keep the fingerprints as I do believe in personal freedom.
Make sure you get a fast pass! Did all 8 houses and 6 rides in one night. Michael Meyers house was the BEST! Definitely doing it next year.

We went to Universal Studios as soon as we could after the opening of the new Harry Potter portion. We walked past it and had to ask a staff member where it was. It is actually hidden behind a wall almost. I am sure later in the day with everyone going in there it is a bit more obvious. You walk through and it is amazing because it shows the brick wall looking like it just opened for you. It was awesome! The new ride is great! Not as long or motion crazy as the other ones. The shops are all extremely small though. I thought they would make them bigger but they didn't. Still great. The amount of work and detail that went into the entire expansion was breathtaking. Everywhere I looked was something new and amazing. It was great! The signs on the buildings were fun. Painted on. Old school looking. I basically loved everything.  I think last time we went to Universal we gave most of it a skip. This time we had more time and actually had a lot of fun on the Universal side. The Simpsons Ride was cute and fun. It was a bit of a stomach turner if you are motion sensitive like me (Had my Dramamine luckily!) but not terrible. The Transformers ride was also a lot of fun. Not sure why we didn't go on it last time but it was a blast. Plus we ran into Optimus outside and got a picture with him.  The entire day was a blast and I can't wait to go back. Need to convince my husband this should be a yearly trip.

Thought I would try HHN this year and wasnt to bad starting out. Went into the line for the 3rd house and asked what the wait time was and they said it was 45 minutes just like the sign said. We have now been in line over an hour and a half and still not near the front of the line. They keep letting all the Express Pass people in and very little people in the stand by line in. Last time I come to this event!!! Unless you buy the Express pass would not recommend coming to this event!!! I will not be back!
even weather was horrible we love this place. great attractions and you need more than 1 day to spent there time.

U will love it here! Rides for young and older. The rockit roller coaster is amazing! Harry potter part on both sides awesome. U have to use the train between both parks if u go. The ride is magical Harry potter. Love it here so much. Will really miss it.

According to policy all items must be removed from pockets and loose items must be stowed before riding which is completely understandable. We were asked to get off the ride and go to the lockers because a staff person, Nicholas, noticed a phone in my husband's pocket. Although we were disappointed, we went to the lockers and stowed all items. After waiting in line again, we got back on the ride and this time they harassed us again saying there was stuff in our pockets although there was literally nothing. Staff refused to let me off the ride when I said I didn't want to go. Nicholas along with another unknown staff person have some sort of power struggle and use their authority as universal studios staff persons in an abusive way to bully people. If we saw this person outside the park I really doubt he would act that way. Who do you think you are? This ride pretty munched ruined the day. Thanks Nicholas! Thanks rip ride rockit. Worst roller coaster ever.
Amazing attraction and worth the money anyone who loves Halloween will love this. Worth the money and worth the wait in line for each haunted house. Street performers were a,axing as well.

Visited here with my hubby and 2 young children. The Harry potter part of the park is just fantastic and was loved my all of us. My 4 yr old was unable to do alot of rides here but she still loved it. The Curious George part of the park which is full of water kept them amused for literally 2 hours. Take a change of clothes though because they get soaked. Really great clean park that we visited a few times on this holiday.

The ever upgrading and new rides makes this the best theme park going .With harry potter gringotts ride the best I,ve been on ,others to check out are minon myhem ,transformers,Simpsons,men in blk and disaster movie plus beatle juice .Great rides ,great entertainment, great time.

We absolutely loved universal we bought a 2 day pass. My daughter & husband are a Harry Potter fan, they couldn't wait till we got in to go to Daigon Alley. Yes we got in at 8 am so we could miss the massive que's. We found that whole place exciting. The Gringotts ride was excellent so was the other Harry Potter ride it felt like you were flying on broomsticks and part of the action. Oh yeah, don't forget to try the Butter Beer it was to die for. You won't be disappointed make sure Universal studios Florida is on your to do List. Definitely we will be back.

I went for harry potter. But left having experienced so much more. What can i say went on all the rides loved them all. Have to say transformers was absolutely amazing. I never rated these kinds of rides until universal. They are amazing so well done. My 5 year old loved the minions and et. Great experience. But please car park charges are a rip off

What a wonderful family trip to Universal Studios Florida. It took us two 9 hour days to see and do everything in the park, 4 days total with Islands of Adventure, and frankly, it wasn't that crowded. We rode every single ride and saw every single show, and loved it all. The few coasters they have are TERRIFIC. My kids LOVED all the motion simulator rides (minions and simpsons were their top picks) and of course the Harry Potter themed rides, attractions and shops were AMAZING! I hated having to pay extra for park hopper tickets to ride the Hogwarts Express. It is a fantastic, not to be missed attraction, but I had no other reason for the park hopper pass. We bought interactive magic wands for each child. They will likely never use them again, but they had a BLAST making magic during our visit to the park. I'm not sure if it was $50 worth of magic, but very magical, none the less. If you can, let a wand choose you in Olivanders shop rather than purchase at the push cart. My hubby loved the butterbeer. We also had ice cream from the shop in London. Long line and expensive. I picked chocolate chili, which the clerk seemed to be trying to talk me out of (too spicy, he warned) but it just tasted like chocolate. I would have ordered the lavender instead, but no taste tests allowed. We had lunch at Moe's on day and the Irish pub one day. Moe's was good, except weird holding pen area before they would let you approach the food counters. Lunch the other day at the Irish pub across from the Mummy. Took forever and just OK food. The evening water and light show when the park closes was great. worth staying around for. The worst ride was probably Twister. I miss JAWS! But overall, GREAT TIME!

If you are into Harry Potter, this is YOUR park! They have a great amount of space dedicated to just this group of movies. I enjoyed most of the rest of the park and would have liked to see some of the older materials incorporated into it. They have a great deal on drinks, buy the souvenir soda cup and get refills for 99 cents for the day. It is worth it. We really enjoyed the Spiderman ride and I did like this park more overall than Magic Kingdom.
Probably the best park in Orlando. A lot of Fun and very nice staff overall. Great rides and food. Highly recommend.

My family of four, two kids 9 and 10, spent two days at Universal Studios Orlando. We bought the express line pass which we felt was worth it. We loved LOTS of the rides. The Harry Potter parts in both parks were amazing! They have truly created exactly what you'd imagine. You definitely need two full days - we still missed some rides. We also has a lovely lunch at 'Fisherman's Wharf'.

If I had to measure Islands Of Adventure against this park, I'd have to give it to Islands of Adventure. However, I will say that I definitely think this park is better than the Universal in Southern California. It's almost impossible to get bored here. We rode a couple of attractions here, but spent the majority of our time at Islands of Adventure since we had the hopper option. It did drizzle on us, but I'm one of those that actually appreciates the rain when it comes because what happens when it rains? People go home. What happens when people go home? The park gets empty and when the park gets empty your wait times are next to nothing. See what I did there? I took something that could have been a downer an made it something positive! It's what you do when you're on vacation. Why? Because we can't control mother nature so might as well make the best of it. What I thought was pretty cool was when we got off of the Rock It coaster that not only can you buy your photo but, you can get the DVD of your on ride experience as well. Did I buy it? Yes. Was it expensive? Yes. It's a theme park. You have to expect that souvenirs and food are not going to be the prices we'd like them to be. I think the one attraction that I felt was a little bit of a waste of time was the Disaster! ride. We waited what was quoted at 20 minutes and ended up being longer than that. You wait in the queue, then you go into a room where a gentleman introduces himself and asks for volunteers to star in a "movie" directed by a Christopher Walken (he uses another name of sorts). You then go into another room where you sit and watch these actors act out what they are asked to do. When you're done there then you load into another room and board a "subway" and are asked to look scared when the props "explode" and water "floods". When you're done there is a video made that you view on the "subway" of the actors and yourselves. It's amusing don't get me wrong but, had I known it was going to cost me an hour of my time I wouldn't have done it. After that we made our way back to Diagon Alley. I did a separate review of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and let's just say I'm really, really impressed with all of it. I do want to point out that I had a blast riding the Mummy roller coaster. It's not a very long ride, but it is pretty theatrical and fun for being an indoor coaster. I can also appreciate that those operating that particular ride made me laugh by keeping in character as you leave the station. I know I'll be back eventually. I love these two parks!

We started at Gringotts to avoid lengthy queues. Loads to take in for Potter fans. Make sure you see the dragon at night for the flames and try the ice cream shop. Amazing. I had apple pie and chocolate. Nice. Went on a tour after this, Men in Black (v good), Simpsons (amazing ride), ET (don't bother) The Mummy (A must do), Transformers (brilliant), Twister (worth it), Despicable Me (Oh yes), Terminator (Fantastic). Stop to admire it all. Great fun and a great day out. Make sure you do the Blues Brothers & Beetleguise review..Excellent entertainment. Enjoy...

I would actually say that this is better than Disney. The park does not take its self as serious as Disney and seems less focussed on seperating visitors from their money. Good gluten free food available in most restaurants. One tip is DO NOT buy snack food a hot dog costs $9.99 without a drink, while for £13 we sat down in Finnagans restaurant had a full meal and drink with waitress service. Best bits Harry Potter rides and Hogwarts, Dispicable Me and The Simpsons. Plenty of Rollercoasters too at Islands of Adventure. One of the other plusses is that there are regular character appearances and plenty of chances for photos with the characters, unlike in Disney where I saw The Chipmonks and Mickey Mouse each for less than 10 seconds as they walked through a wired off section of restaurant. The entire park is geared for everyone old and young. I absolutely loved it.

the rides were great. Transformers as really good. Harry potter same. Twister was ok at best. The Mummy was great. Buy the express line to bypass some of the lines (except Harry potter). Very expensive day. Over 200 a person before food and souvenirs. Lots of fun.. but not sure it's worth it.
Had a great time, will be back next year. Disliked the long lines. We ended up getting special tickets to skip the lines. Expensive but worth it :)

Need I say anymore! The Harry Potter section of Universal is absolutely brilliant, fantastic. The Simpsons ride is great, really makes you think you're with them. The Rockit ride was great. In fact everything about Universal Studios was brilliant. Spiderman, Transformers, Minions, Terminator, Men in Black, all amazing! It's definitely not Disney and is more for the older children who are adventurous. The shows were good too!

Lots of different rides and things to do for all ages and interests. They have various options for food from fast food to healthier at a reasonable cost for a theme park. May I suggest booking your passes in advance on the internet to save money. Bring your print out like we did and you will save a little money. They use finger print identification to get into the park. USE CAUTION when you buy your passes if you are wanting to also go to Island's of Adventure next door also. If you buy the wrong type of ticket you will not be able to the second park without buying another ticket. The big attraction between Universal Studios and Island of Adventure is "Harry Potter" with a train ride going to and from the two parks. I suggest if you are interested in "Harry Potter" head there first as it is very popular and crowded. A little less crowd when the park opens. Fun day to just have fun and enjoy the surrounding

Make sure you make the trip to Universal Halloween horror nights. Always fun and lots to see. Can get expensive since it's a separately ticketed event and express pass is a must; otherwise you will be waiting for 1-2 hrs per haunted house and there are 8 of them! As for regular visits; always awesome as well. The wait for Harry Potter is absurd and we could never get on the roller coaster; either 90 min wait or broken!!!!

I was worried that Universal Studios Florida was going to have outlived it's fun. I was wrong, we had a great visit with the new attractions and rides they've added in the recent years. We came to visit the new Harry Potter Diagon Ally, which was truly awesome for my kids who love Harry Potter. We also had a great time exploring the world built around the Simpsons characters (Krusy, Moe, Lard Lad, etc). We loved the Transformers ride and the Despicable Me ride, also new to us. And the fun rides I recall being there before were still fun - ET, Rip-Ride-Rocket. We spend three days at both parks and I was surprised how much fun we had at Universal Studios Florida.

I highly recommend searching for deals for your tickets. We were able to purchase three days for the price of two, and it was really the perfect amount of time to spend in the two parks. We spend one day at Island of Adventure and two at Universal. The kids bought wands at Universal and we spent about five hours just in the Harry Potter area so they could perform their magic.  While I liked the 4D rides, there are so many of them they got a little predictable after about the third one. The shows were entertaining, but not thrilling. I do wish there were more roller coasters.  What I really appreciated was that my four-year old (who is 41" tall) could ride a majority of the rides and those that he couldn't allowed a parent swap so that we could all wait in line as a family and both my husband and I could ride... and my teen loved it because that meant she got to ride twice.  We went in the middle of November and the lines were so short many were walk-on. The longest wait was 30-minutes for the Gringotts ride. We were glad we didn't spend the extra for the fast pass.  We did stay late one night to watch the parade and light show. It was worth the wait. Very creative and engaging. The kids also enjoyed it.

This was my family's favorite place to visit in the Orlando area, followed by LEGOLAND Florida and then the Magic Kingdom. I don't even think I can do it justice. If you do Universal, make sure you get the park to park so that you can enjoy the Hogwarts train ride between here and Islands of Adventure so that you get the full experience. Also, the extra wand purchase is entirely worth it to enhance your Harry Potter adventure to try out spells throughout the area. Besides going on about the Harry Potter experience, I have to say, we also enjoyed a lot of other things in the park, including the Shrek and Minion experiences, the Revenge of the Mummy, and the MIB Alien Attack (coolest shooter ride/game ever). Here my kids did not mind waiting in line, they were the masters of entertainment while waiting. One caveat, our first day started with an hour and a half wait at Gringott's without getting any further than just behind the main hall before we left. Apparently the ride broke down (and we were told by a local that it breaks down 5 times a day), but we couldn't hear the announcements about it while we were in line because people are so loud (they need to turn up their announcement volume). So we had bunches of questions, but no team member was around to explain what was happening and then when one did show up, he didn't have any information. They need to make sure that ride works, or get someone to come in and give those waiting in line Express passes to come back and to shut the gates so that no one else tries to come in while the ride is VERY broken and wait for no experience. We never went back to experience that. The dragon on top of Gringott's never breathed fire while we were there. I don't know if it's timed and we missed it or if they shut it down on a regular basis. But after all that, we spent 2.5 days enjoying both Universal Parks. The rest of our experiences only went up from there and in the end Universal was my kids' favorite attraction.

We visited Studio Theme park and Islands of Adventure with our two twenty-something daughters following a cruise.  Had a blast. Went for Harry Potter because it is new since last visit and because my kids are really of the Harry Potter generation.  My list of do's  1. Stay at Hard Rock. Get express pass. 2. Use the early entry. 3. Do all the Harry Potter stuff early before it is too congested. 4. Drink alcohol. Because you can! Great benefit of this park.  Best rides -- in order.  1. Minion ride 2. Dragon Roller Coaster -- red one 3. Rockit Coaster 4. Mummy ride 5. Simpson ride 6. Gringotts ride -- kind of a stomach turner 7. Hulk coaster 8. Other Harry Potter ride 9. The wand thing 10. Spiderman ride 11. Transformer ride  Thing is the simulation rides start wearing you out. So you gotta space them out. Food in park is good and cheaper than City Walk. Plus there are bars and alcohol in park. Happy Hour at Backwater Bar.

Returned to both Studios and IOA aftre a 6 year break and forgot how much I love this place. The Parks have a more chilled out feel than Disney, but in my opinion they are as beautifully created and maintained, if not more-so. As there were only 2 of us this time, we invested in the Express pass which cost about $200inc taxes and I wasn't sure if this was a wise move as the Parks were pretty quiet, but on hindsight I think it was indulgent but smart because we got to do all the rides on both parks, many of them 2 or 3 times in one day, literally walking on to every ride with the exception of the Potter rides. But we didn't mind a bit of queuing for these as Universal have thoughfully created a true experience from the minute you arrive at the ride.I'm not a HP afficienado but their attention to detail was incredible, and I would imagine if you are really into the HP franchise then there is tons of quirky details that would keep you entertained as you wait for the ride, The rides themselves were really good, and Universal have really perfected the 3D interactive ride experience - one cannot compare say. Soarin at Disney with the HP Forbidden Journey ride albiet they are similar types of rides.Well done Universal!! One quick tip - on our 2nd visit, we didn't invest in Express and did single rider on both HP rides and walked straight onto the ride, but you do miss the overall experience - at least you have the option, which Disney have stopped on a lot of their busier rides. Transformers 3D, Rocket and Despicable Me were all new attractions to us and all awesome in their own right.Plus I was really glad that old the old favourites were still there with the exception of the Jaws ride which is a shame as I am a huge fan of the film, but it was a very slow loading ride and I can uinderstand why Universal have utiilised the space with the new attractions. Really, really impressed with what Universal have done with these two parks and in stark contrast to the Disney Parks where little has changed in 6 years and if anything they have gone back-over with their new Fastpass system. Our No 1 Orlando destination - no question,.

Extremely clean,well run facility,exceeded my expectations,all the staff was friendly and helpful.Food and drinks were all top quality,Harry Potter side was amazing,the attention to detail,including the construction fit and finish was impressive.Enjoyed all the rides,including the crazy roller coasters!Don't go here if you are looking for a cheap day out,they are not shy with the ticket prices,all in all,was an excellent experience,definitely way more to see and do than can be done in one day!
Great rides, great shows, great food and all around great family fun with something for all ages. A definite must.

We went with our 9 year old, 7 year old and my inlaws over Christmas. To keep our sanity we bought Express passes which were well worth the money but expensive - albeit cheaper than a divorce lawyer! Harry Potter is very crowded but worth the queue for fans. Gringots ride worth a wait. Some imaginative merchandising saw my wife spend a fortune. Away from that we enjoyed Transformers and Simpsons rides!

This park has less rides than IOA, but my kids love the ones they do have. If you have younger kids, definitely check out Fievel's play area. If you are going to Diagon Alley, plan on it being very crowded. Check out everything...lots of people miss out on the quirky stuff because they are in such a hurry. Relax and look around. Be aware that Knockturn Alley can be a little dark for the little ones. If you haven't watched the movies before, you will still enjoy Diagon Alley, but you will enjoy it more if you watch them first. The train ride from Diagon Alley to Hogsmeade is different than the ride from Hogsmeade to Diagon Alley so take both of them...look out the "window" but also keep your eye on your door "window".

99% over priced shops themed around their various media properties and a few rides you can wait hours to ride. Did I mention the crowds? And the lines? Even to get into a shop? The highlight was duff brewery cause after paying what we paid to get in I needed a beer and to say "dooh"!

rides are great, fun, but lines are very long during peak season, popular ones like Harry Potter, Dispicable Me, and Transformer are at least an hour wait, sometimes can be two hours wait time. Get Express ticket if you want to avoid the long lines and ride as many as you want during the day.

It is worth the trip just to see the new Diagon Alley area and experience the new Escape from Gringott's ride. Really well done. Get a wand that allows you to do magic at many shops, try the exciting flavors of ice cream, and just be a kid again. lots of rides for the hard core thrill seekers. Be careful when you go, it can get very crowded. If staying on site, definitely take advantage of early admission and express passes.
had a really great time first visit will definitely return everything exceeded my expectation family fun for everyone

If you want a real adventure and want to the get the best of all action and sci-fi movies from Universal, this is the place. You will get to experience the best of everything related to Universal at this place. Transformers, Shrek, Harry potter, just to name a few were the best rides i enjoyed. Apart from that the water park that was another end of the park. Paid $175 for it and had a lot of fun and excitement. All worth it. The best rides, 3D theatres, Water park, Roller coasters etc, all come packed in this place. I experienced 4 different Roller Coasters and it was amazing. It has restaurants into it going with the theme of the ride. For Example If you are touring Harry potter, The place will look like a complete copy of what you see in the movie. The restaurants and the people look as if they have come out of the movie. 1 day is not enough to experience it all and i didn't have time to go through all the rides. I was lucky to have as there were not many people in the queue. Harry potter was the one in demand as you start the ride from an actual Train so had to wait for an hour. Overall Great Experience. The best part is Universal changes its themes every few months so as new movies come in, so does a small real world for them and we get to experience it. Their park was so detailed and the staff was awesome. Will definitely go Again.
Lots to see and do. Rides are excellent. Something for everyone, from little kids to adults. Lots of roller coaster and simulator rides. My teenagers loved it!

It took over 30 years to get to Orlando and it was all about getting to see Mickey and the gang (which was a disappointment - read in one of my other reviews). Lucky for us, we also wanted to see Universal. Universal ROCKS! Both parks! We had so much fun, we are planning to go again next year and make it a full week of it. I'll try to stick to the Universal and do up another review for the other park. Everything about Universal is down to a science. From arriving at the multilevel parking lot, to the security checks, to the ticket booths, CITY WALK, and finally going through the turnpikes. It is all well executed and planned. Then utter chaos as thousands of people go nuts at the park! When you walk into Studios, make a beeline for Despicable Me! Get into it early and experience it right away, the lines will not get smaller as the day goes on. Other must rides - Transformer, Crustyland, Hollywood Ripride Rockit, and the must see Diagon Alley and the Gringotts ride! Talking about Diagon - Potter World on both sides is amazing! My wife isn't even familiar with Potter but she was thoroughly impressed with the remake of the villages at Universal. I can go on about all the stuff to do but I think I will share with you the survival strategies. If you want to spend the cash, get the Express pass - it helps on most rides except in Harry Potter's world. If you want to save some cash, you can do the single park tickets but that means you can't ride the Hogwarts Express Train. This is where they sucker you for a bunch of bucks! If you want to experience Potter, you need the Park-to-Park pass. Oh BTW, the more days you buy the cheaper per day it gets. Now, arrive early! The earlier the better. Be the first ones in the park if you want to get on any of the rides - especially in peak season. If you can go off-peak, you will have the park to yourself. Arrange to take a long lunch break and maybe get in a nap during the high-temperature hours. Go back late afternoon until closing. You will find that most people with small kids will be leaving as you are returning to the park. This helps reduce your wait times and you get to see the park in a whole new "light!" The park really is fun once the sun drops! Especially in Diagon Alley! Pick up your marauder's map and Swear to No Good and have a great time! Orlando is UNIVERSAL! Sorry Mickey - at least you have your Princesses.
Very expensive but express pass well worth it. You get to enjoy day. Only ridiculous waits were harry potter experiences where express passez not accepted. The train was cool but unreasonable wait

An excellent place to spend a few days on your vacation. The two Universal parks are very different in nature, so prepare ahead of time by looking at the online guides and maps. Hollywood Studios is more shows, medium thrill rides, and places to sit and relax/eat (with a couple of roller coaster rides). Adventure Island is geared more toward rides and thrills. Hogwarts and Harry Potter spans both parks, with the majority of the shops and atmospheric street section on the Hollywood Studios side. VERY dark and wonderful area. Even the crowds added to the atmosphere..you really feel like you're shopping for your owl, wand, and "stuff" to make your stay at Hogwarts more comfortable! Escape from Gringott's is spectacular fun. Hogwart's Express Train to the other park is great fun. **Warning**: there are a LOT of stairs to climb..both up and down. If you have anyone in the party who has trouble with stairs, there are lifts.  We had 2 seniors who weren't keen on rides, but loved the shows and walking down the "old time" streets, 2 adults who loved everything, and 3 adult mentally challenged men who were in 7th heaven all day. As with Disney, there is a lot of walking to do to get into the park, and around, but it's certainly worth it. Buying tickets online and either printing yourself, or picking up at the "will call kiosk" saves you $20 off the gate price and is easy to do.

Well, Since 2005 I've been at Universal 9 times so it is clearly our favorite theme park. This time we had a few issues, but the gust relations service is taking very good care of us. The Harry Potter atractions are simply amazing, and I only miss the Back to the Future ride, which turned into The Simpsons ride a few years ago. It's a nice one, my wide loves it, but BTTF was just awesome. For those who have lived the 80's it was a very nice one. The one I can't explain how can it still have people interested on is the MIB. That one is not worth a 1 minute line for me.

This place is seriously well made! I prefer this to Disneyland as it's cheaper, and well suited for older kids. Disney is more for younger children who still believe in magic (Unless you're going to the studios part..) I love the food, the kindness, the atmosphere! Too amazing! I love this place and I will be coming back soon!

We've been here quite a few times before but were lured back to see the second part of the Harry Potter expansion. Our adult children had not been to the parks in quite some time and we only had one day and they wanted to see both parts. The cost was almost $600 for tickets for that one day; an extra $35 each to be able to ride the train and go to both parks. Diagon Ally was essentially one new ride (The Gringotts Bank ride lasted all of about 90 seconds) and a bunch of shops and atmosphere. Hogsmeade is essentially one new ride (Hogwarts), a few reworked old rides and a bunch of shops and atmosphere. I felt like I spent $125 for the four of us to ride a train. Worth one trip, period. You have to walk through the entire park to get to the HP areas (very smart, Universal because a lot of the other stuff is truly bogus or meant for small children). The other thing I noticed is that there were not many benches or other places to sit if you had to wait for others in your party to get off of a ride (I think this is to keep the visitors spending in the shops).  I don't think I will be back.

My family and I absolutely loved universal studios.We loved it so much we returned in Nov/14.Bring plenty of spending money as food,drinks, etc can get pricey like any theme park.I would recommend universal studios to my family and friends.

This was my favorite park of the two. I like the 3D animated rides that tell you a story. They do have a few older rides that really need updated, but the newer ones are very cool. I would recommend doing the park fast pass if you can. We got it included with our room staying in Park property hotel and it was so worth it. I think there where only 3 rides you could not use it on and they where all in Harry Potter. The rest you can and you just show it and get in a special line. We never waited more than 20 minutes and some of the rides had posted 60-90 min waits. We where easily able to do everything in one day and a few rides twice with these, not the case without.

We only had one day to visit, so we paid $229 PER ticket for an express pass to both parks figuring that we could get in most of the attractions faster and ride most of them. It wasn't until we got to the Harry Potter attractions and asked the attendant where the express pass line was, that we were told the outrageously priced tickets that we purchased did not cover the Harry Potter rides and we would have to wait in the regular lines, which were 60-70 minutes all day. When I told the attendant that we were not told this, he said "it's written on the ticket." Hello Universal, how can you read the ticket until you have purchased it and they give it to you? And it is buried in the rest of the fine print along with the verbiage that you can be injured and die and you accept full responsibility. I really feel this was deceptive, deceitful, sneaky and greedy. We likely won't be back. Fair warning to everyone else. Other than that, the new part of Harry Potter was well done. Some of the other attractions definitely need replacement or upgrading.

Universal is so much fun! There's so much to do and see and is perfect for all ages - would definitely recommend getting fast passes if it's not too expensive as they make the day so much better because you save so much time in the queues and it means you are more likely to go on every ride you want to.
We had fun at Universal just wished we had booked two day at their parks. We didn't get to do everything

We spent three full days at the park and were very impressed with how clean and how enthusiastic most of the workers were. We stayed for the movie and fireworks the first night and it was very enjoyable. By far being Harry Potter fans we enjoyed Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade the most. The Forbidden forest ride was awesome--even enjoyed walking through the castle to see the things along the walk that entertain you as you wait. Dragon challenge added fun roller coaster thrills and Escape from Gringotts was also great. Everytime we went on the train between the two places we would see something new. We enjoyed the food at the three broomsticks more than the leakey cauldron as one of the party loves turkey legs--which were excellent. We tried all three types of butterbeer and liked them all. In the other part of the parks we liked the transformer ride, and the animal actor show a lot. We did the ET ride for nostalgia as we all loved the movie. Some of the rides were awful though--Twister was the worst as they herd you into one area and then another area and then you get to stand to watch a lame storm and lightning and trees falling over. We did not have small children in the group so have no information about the rides for little kids. All in all we had a great time and would return again. There is a lot of walking involved in the park experience so make sure you have good shoes.

Loved the newest attractions of Harry Potter! WOW! They've done such a wonderful job from the beginning when you walk around the corner, you're transformed into a different world! They've tied it all together and the Gringotts ride is amazing! We ate at the "Leaky Cauldron" and had a beer there too! We also did the thrill rides too, very, very good! You have to have a 2 park ticket to ride the "Hogwart's Express"! Fun for all ages!

We've been coming here for years, but we usually only get either a one or two day 2 park ticket. This year we were staying for the whole week, so we got 7 day 2 park tickets. That was the best thing we couldn't done. We came specifically to go to the new Harry Potter park in the Studios park. It did NOT disappoint! It is a fantastic park, better than the Hogwarts one in islands of adventure in all but one respect. The Forbidden Journey ride in the Castle is still fantastic after all this time, but the Gringott's ride is not worth the wait. It's boring and the time you spend in line is boring as well. I know no one expects the time you spend in line to be fun or interesting, but the line for Forbidden Journey is fun once you get into the greenhouse. While the greenhouse could use some more interesting plants, etc., the castle is fantastic! I love going through Dumbledore's office and the part where they have a video of Harry Hermione and Ron talking to you and it starts to snow. That is definitely magical, even though I've been on that ride several times. I'm telling everyone I know not to bother going on the Gringott's ride unless there is NO line. Other than that, everything is incredible! I do not know how they could've possibly made it better. The only things that had disappointed me the first time we went to the Harry Potter park at islands of adventure was that they had very few stores with stuff you could buy and they didn't have a train ride. They have addressed both issues wonderfully. The train ride is fun to take each way and the new Diagon Alley park is so much fun. It is full of stores where you can buy all kinds of wizarding supplies. My favorites were Quality Quidditch supplies and Fortescue's Ice Cream. The ice cream was delicious and you can get strawberry and chocolate, just like Harry. I like that you can get all kinds of quidditch related shirts at Quality Quidditch Supplies, including t-shirts from the world cup! Tons of people were purchasing entire wizard outfits and walking around the park in them, so that, of course, added to the fun. There are also interactive things you can do in the streets(alley) and you can also go looking for dark things down Knockturn Alley. It was so much fun. We used our 7 day pass by going first thing in the morning every day as soon as they opened and going on as many rides as we could before 10 am. If you stay at a Universal hotel you can actually get in an hour earlier than that. Around 10 am, the park starts to get more busy, but since we've already filled our ride cravings, we just relax and walk around the park for a while before heading out. A few days, we ended our park day by going to the movie theater next to the entrance and seeing a movie before heading back to our hotel. A tip: we do not bring any bags with us so we do not have to stand in the bag line. It gets us on the rides much quicker. The one thing I was sad about was how hard it was to find my favorite Harry Potter candy, Pepper Imps. They were not to be found in any of the Harry Potter stores but, thankfully, I found them in one of the stores in the other side of the park.
We had a great time spending the day at the park. The park was only open till 6 so it was a bit rushed but the day went by quickly and everyone had a great time..

Not only is Universal awesome, its simply a better value than Disney. The one day ticket is about the same but when you expand it to a 3 day ticket its hard to beat. The Harry Potter World is simply the best attraction I have ever seen in any park in my 37 years of life. Incredible and not to be missed. If you have children that are 7 or older, you might want to consider this park instead of the traditional disney visit.  We had a great time and we will most definitely be going back.
This was our third visit to this park. We see something new each time we visit. It is best to go during the off-season if you can. The crowds are much smaller and lines are shorter.
Shrek, Horror Make-up, Disaster. The restaurants were pricey as expected. The lines were short this time of year.
