So many worlds to explore. Just enjoy yourself and do as much as you can. Try not to rush and pay attention to show, parade and ride times
Guess I hit it at the right time, the most time waited on a line was 15 minutes! Transformers 3D was Excellent!

Stayed at Cabana Beach Hotel. Plain rooms, ugly dining area, nice pool, good bus service to park. Park has great architectural features, especially in the Harry Potter area, and was very clean. We were very disappointed with the downtime of some of the features. In the two days we were there, the escalators were down twice as were the moving sidewalks, the Hogwarth Express between the parks went down after we waited in the line for a half hour, several of the rides were down when we were in the park (Twister, Disaster, Transformers). You understand machines may have downtime, but when you pay this kind of money for a limited time to enjoy all the available features, you don't have to accept it.  Make sure you understand all the options when you make your reservations. The reservation people in St. Louis have probably never been to the park and don't understand how all the options interact. In retrospect, we would have chosen the upgraded hotel which includes some of the options for which we paid extra.  Also, we would not have gotten the dinner package. In order for it to be economical, you need to use all features completely. We tried to get a drink at one of the food carts. Turns out this particular food cart only accepted cash. The next one was out of the product we wanted. Just too much trouble.  In summary, very neat place but go but get a book before you decide to sign up. The park doesn't provide much detail, so we picked up a book by Kelly Monaghan that was very helpful.

I had a great time when I went to universal studios, and the rides were great. The lines got long but that's the same at every park. It's a great way to become part of the movie excitement or experience. Go ahead and take your family!

It's a nice place in the off season....Just don't go during Halloween nights or around Christmas weeks until after New Years, it's good for a few weeks until mardi crowded nights on the weekends. We have a season pass. Been too all the Disney stuff but we like Universal the best overall the parks here in Orlando. Disney parks are okay if ya never been there, animal kingdom is just like abig zoo but not worth the money to me but a good time is had with kids. For teens go to Unaversal both parks with at least two day pass but three days is better to make it through long lines in the busy season. For example you can wait for Harry Potter rides for 3 hours during busy times or during off season can wait for 30 min. My favorite rides at Universal is all of them! Universal city walk has great places too eat too but bring a big wallet. Everything is overpriced in the whole place, just bring in your back pack a lot of snacks and just split meal. It's all fun.

Can't event repeat how much it cost our family of 5 for the day for just Island of adventure park. 75% of the park is food or stores while only 25% are actual rides. We bought the fast pass so the kids wouldn't be discouraged waiting on lines but not sure we actually needed them for all that money and the lines weren't as bad as they could have been. The Jurassic ride the kids were forward to closed. We could have done so many things with all the money we spent for only one day in Universal.

This amusement park is top class, with a theme that is nicely held together through the entire park. The attractions are top class and in a good variety. Our 5 year old tried everything except the Mummy. The tour around the film sets was all about selling of course, but was a great tour still with a lot of interesting things to see, from film sets, attractions, filming tricks and some history.

Went to Florida in the middle of winter to escape all the snow in Jersey. I enjoyed all the rides and Harry Potter was my favorite. 2 Hulk and 1 Spiderman ride made me throw up but the fun didn't stop there. I had water and ate a little and I was back in action! lol

Is the park expensive as pointed out by some disgruntled reviewers? Sure! But look at the expense of keeping the park up to the expected standards of cleanliness, and reliable operation; not to mention logistics and staff/performer pay. Is it a cash cow with opportunities to give up your cash at every turn? Sure! But what business doesn't charge what the market will bear? The entertainment provided was almost uniformly good and, despite the fact that I'm 62, I thoroughly enjoyed my time here - So much for one reviewer who feels that this is no place for a childless couple! I don't enjoy thrill simulators, but my wife does so I found other stuff to do, and we both enjoyed the "kiddie" entertainments. I would go so far as to say that, if you can't find a couple of days fun and entertainment here, without necessarily spending a dime on anything but food/drink, you may be a humorless grouch. Personally, I even had great fun in Woody Woodpecker's Kidzone and the Simpsons section of World Expo, which were primarily intended for a younger demographic or Simpsons fans! The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was so exceptionally well-done that it was probably our favorite area. Having seen everything we wanted to see, and knowing that changes would be minimal in the near future, we might not be back; but we still had fun.

Universal is a great park for families and people of all ages. Our family first visited this park when our kids "outgrew" the Magic Kingdom. I was astounded at how much better the rides are at Universal. The first time we went on the Spiderman ride I'm sure I left my jaw on the floor of the cart. Most of the rides are fast and furious, so buckle up, hold on, be amazed. The only show I would not see again is the Sinbad stunt show, which was seriously so boring that I felt sorry for the actors. A word about Harry Potter. We visited for the first time when the Harry Potter rides were only in the "Islands of Adventure" park. The last time we visited in November 2014 the newest Harry Potter rides were open in Diagon Alley, WHICH IS IN THE OTHER UNIVERSAL STUDIOS PARK! SO, to do all the Harry Potter rides in one day, you will need a two park pass. You will not be able to go on the Hogwart's Express train unless you have a two park pass as this is the "ticket" to get on the train. This doesn't seem to be explained on their website, and I would think it would be disappointing to not be able to go on the train, especially as it is one of the biggest Harry Potter icons. We made the decision to spend the extra money, and were able to purchase an "upgrade pass" to the other park at the Hogwart's Express ticket booth (an extra $140 for 3 people). Since we did this after lunch we had to wait in a very long line to board the "train" to the other park as most people were switching between parks around mid-day). I would recommend at least 2 days, as you will need two days to do it all (we did 2 parks in one day, but only went on the major rides, used the front of the line passes, and race-walked from one ride to the next. We left at close of day, just in time to see the fireworks out the rear window.

We have actually placed our review on both Universal parks already. And sharing our opinion of recent stay at Hyatt Place near Universal we mentioned that it was just a short walk to the Parks, but forgor to provide you, folks, with a navigation. Here it is. If you happened to stay at Hyatt Place Universal or Holiday Inn & Suites Main Gate, to get to the Parks you first have to cross Major Blvr, then (Double Tree Hotel at the Entrance to Universal's guests can join here), right there, cross Kirkman Road and keep strait along Major Blvr. until next crossroads (just two min), and there turn left on Universal Blvr. for another 2 or 3 minutes walk. Follow Valet Parking sign to make your walk shorter. From Hyatt (the most distant of all three hotels) it took us less than 20 min. to get there. Enjoy it!

The parks and city walk were great. Wish the weather was warmer and there was more sun. We celebrated our 36th anniversary. The hotel gave us buttons to wear and all the staff wished us good wishes. We loved the Harry potter @ The Island of adventure, but the one at Universal park was closed for repairs. The parks were very clean and welcoming. hope to return in better weather. We definitely recommend the express pass and meal plan card. We would like to stay at the park in a hotel again...maybe one a bit less expensive that Portifinio
Loved Everything! Lines were not outrageous and loved that they created lines inside with atmosphere to keep you occupied while you wait. It also keeps you cool! Harry Potter was amazing!

For the third year in a row my wife Sarah & I visited Orlando and Universal Studios is a must-do for me as a huge movie buff and also for Sarah who is a big fan of the Harry Potter books & films. We visited in June of 2014 in the hope that Diagon Alley would be open but alas it was not to be. We returned last month and finally rode the Hogwarts Express which was not a disappointment. Diagon Alley is an amazing achievement (as is the whole park!) and even as a non-Potter fan it's difficult not to get caught up in it all. Try the peanut butter & strawberry ice cream from Florean Fortescue's - it's fantastic. I had to try a Flaming Moe in Springfield USA but was disappointed to be charged nearly $10 including tax for what is essentially an orange soda with a little dry ice in a themed cup.  Photo ops with various Universal characters are common - I had my obligatory pic with "Doc Brown" by the DeLorean - and the superstar parade is great fun. Looking forward to going back in a few years when we will have our first born to take with us - he's due in May (this trip was our last hurrah before parenthood!!!).  If you're travelling from the UK try magicaltickets.co.uk for your park passes - we have used them for all our Orlando trips with no problems and the prices are very competitive.

I was so excited to visit Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. I went with my almost-eight-year old and her cousins and aunt and uncle: 10 people all together! My eight -year-old was just barely tall enough for all the rides so I caution families with young children to watch out for the height limits and make use of the child swap lines in some of the rides. We did all the Harry Potter and hit the highlights at Universal Studios in one day. All other reviews are correct in saying that it's too much to expect to get all parks done in one day, but I felt we did everything we wanted to, and still ate at the Three Broomsticks and had ice cream later. So, I loooooved the new Diagon Alley It was too fabulous. You must go. Hogsmeade and the train ride were also a delight. The Forbidden Journey in the castle in Hogsmeade was perhaps the "urp"iest ride... Still way cool and exciting and scream-inducing but also your lunch might jiggle around a bit and make you feel sick. We also loved Transformers and the rest of the party loved The Mummy Returns as well. Really awesome 3D effects in all of them. Will so go again. And maybe take it easier on the butterbeer before riding the Forbidden Journey!

My adult daughter wanted to see the Harry Potter, so unlike our usual trips to Florida to visit the Mouse, we went to Universal Studios. Since Harry was our main reason for visiting, I'll talk about Diagon Alley first. The facades that make up the stores, restaurant, and ride, are beautifully detailed. That being said, there are not enough places for nonriders of Gringott's to wait. There are very few benches. My daughter commented that since there are so many facades that do not have stores, seating could easily be added. There are wands for sale, generally between $36 - $44. The wands are interactive at numerous spots throughout the section. However, after waiting your turn to do the same action as the previous half dozen or so Wizards, there is no mystery as to what is going to happen. The requisite robes are available from child size to adult 4X. Most sell for $109. They are made of polyester, which I think would be ridiculously hot to wear in Florida weather. But, not only did we see whole families with wands and robes, many also had scarves around their necks. I suspect heat exhaustion is a common occurrence in Diagon Alley. The only ride in Diagon Alley is in Gringott's Bank. The theming is remarkable and the chandeliers are gorgeous. My only regret is that you can't carry a camera with you to take photos of the queue, because all loose articles must be left in a locker or with a non rider.  Several of the rides throughout the park require that loose articles be placed in a locker or with a non rider. When we first got to the park, since our hotel room wasn't ready, we took the carry on with us and put it in a locker at the park entrance. I would suggest that you take a picture of the locker number, if you take advantage of one of these lockers because at the end of the day, after using about 6 lockers located at individual rides, we couldn't remember the number of the original locker. We almost couldn't get our stuff back. If we hadn't finally remembered the locker number, we would have had to wait until our things went to lost and found after the park closed, to be retrieved the next day.  While I am still a Mouse girl, I did enjoy my visit to Universal Studios.

Valet parking is excellent but universal is noisy, dirty and full of long queues and fed up looking staff. Really disappointed by the whole experience couldn't find anywhere to sit and eat so left about 3pm. Spent my whole life believing the hype and saved long to bring my children. I will try Islands of Adventure as I have stupidly bought 14 day passes for the whole family but have no idea how anyone could spend more than a few hours in this place without going nuts, never will return.
With the new add ons this park is better than Islands in my opinion. I loved the Transformers Ride and the Simpsons area. Looking forward to going back!

We had been at many of the attractions around Orlando all week and were looking forward to visiting Universal Studios.  We queued up for a while (not too long) and noted the cost for 1 park for a day and though that's a bit expensive considering the size of a park against Disney.  Secondly we noticed that you don't get any free fast passes for rides so have to pay nearly double for this making is ridiculously expensive.  I decided not to go in due to the crowds and price, I'm glad I didn't as fellow travellers said that unless you got a fast pass you waited forever to get on rides.

Had a wonderful time at Universal Studios is a great time! The roller coasters are so much fun. The new Diagon Alley section of Harry Potter World looks just like in the movies. The food is just like an English Pub. We really enoyed it and the entire family had fun.

Good old Universal is still awesome, more so than ever before. Remember that Islands of Asventure is a separate park that requires a separate ticket, just 5 minutes walking over the bridge from Universal. You can do both in one day if you purchase the express pass (highly recommended) but you should probably start with Islands of Adventure in the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and ride the Forbidden Journey because that ride gets long lines and does not accepr express passes. After you are done with Islands of Adventure come to Universal and ride: despicable Me Minion Mania, Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit, Revenge of the Mummy, Transformers 3D, Springfield, Men in Black Alien Attack and E.T. Adventure (because it's a classic). If you have spare time you may also consider Shrek 4D (show), Terminator 2 3D (show) and Twister (show). Overall great park with tons of dun things to do.

Our visit to Universal Studios was great. My husband and I had a great time. We enjoyed so much TRANSFORMERS, HARRY POTTER, SPIDERMAN, THE SIMPSONS, SHREK...and if you are into more adrenaline you cannot miss HULK.

Ive been to Florida and the parks quite often with my own family. U we never took our kids as infants and I see why quite clearly now. Anyway you cut it the day is long and juggling having an infant is tough on both mom and grandparents. I must admit the park staff was gay about allowing parent share which is having one parent ride then once exited the other parent can ride. Better than waiting in long lines all day. We hit all the main attractions but took us with walking and waits from 9am to 9pm. You couldn't do this any faster without Express Pass which is cost prohibitive in my opinion. Renting an electric cart is a blessing and to be honest I'd get one, without canopy, even if it was for you ger families. Great place to relax and sit when only concrete is available. So in a nutshell, go in offseason, rent electric chair, don't buy Express Pass and kids should be 12-13 at least for Universal.

We came here primarily for the new Harry Potter area - Diagon Alley and were not disappointed. Honestly, could have stayed in just one area and never gotten sick of it. The amount of authentic detail was amazing. I probably spent way more than I should have as every shop had something interesting and must-have (if you are a Harry Potter fan). We also loved the puppet and singing shows by the Gringotts money exchange. My husband is a huge Simpsons fan so we did eventually venture out of this area and he really loved that area as well. I would recommend getting the unlimited express pass if you plan on coming at a busy time of year (especially if you have kids) as the lines for some rides were very long (at times over a 100 minutes). Had a blast and can't wait to come back again.

We went on March break and spent 4 days at Universal and 5 days at Disney World. We stayed on sight at Cabana Bay and used their shuttle service to the park. You can walk to the park but it is quite a walk for an onsite hotel. Their are 2 parks at Universal so if you don't get the park hopper you CANNOT go to both parks and you CANNOT ride the Hogwarts Express which takes you back and forth between the two parks. I prefer the main park Universal over Island of Adventure and it seems that more happens at that park. They also have two Harry Potter worlds one at each park. Diagon Alley at Universal and Hogsmead at Island of Adventure. I prefer Diagon Alley but both places are Great. We took advantage of the early entry perk and went straight for Hogsmead and went on the rides there. Then took the train over to the Gringotts ride at Universal. Only Hogsmead is open for the early entry at this time. When we arrived at the Gringotts ride we had to wait until it opened. We would be in the middle of the line so once the ride opens it's about a 15 minute wait. You should go to HP early in the morning or you will be waiting in a long line. My kids would go in the single rider line in the afternoon which was faster than the stand by line. I find most of the people are in the HP worlds so the rest of the park wasn't to busy. This amusement park isn't like other parks with a lot of thrill rides and coasters. They have more simulator rides which are very good. For those interested which Park is Better Disney or Universal. Well I had poor customer service at Disney World and not 1 but 5 incidents and you can read 2 main ones on my Disney review. Universal we had 0 incidents. I would say if you have teenage kids and older Universal. If your kids are smaller Disney. My teenage kids enjoyed Universal better and asked me when we can go back to Universal and not Disney. Also I found the food to be better at Universal and more reasonably priced. We had the dinning plan at Disney and the average sit down meal was close to $200 for dinner for the 4 of us. For that price I'd expect wow that was good. Not it's OK. And the quick Service Burger at Disney are pretty much all the same a regular burger at McDonald's which would cost you close to $11. Anyways hope you enjoy Universal Studios as my family did !!! WILL BE BACK

This was my first time in Universal and I wasn't disappointed. First of all if you want to see all of Universal in either 1 or 2 days buy Express no matter what. Although it is expensive you get to skip the queues which usually saves you around 2 hours. Universal is split into to two parks, "Islands Of Adventure" and "Universal Studios." Both of the parks are brilliant and defiantly worth a visit. "Islands Of Adventure" has more rides while "Universal Studios" has more simulators and isn't so busy. I would really advise to get up early and get there as quickly as possible because when a rush of people come it is very hard to get from one place to another.

Great, personal, friendly help! Anne, any Tamika were working the guest device window at the entrance to universal studios, and went above and beyond to answer question on a future trip. Very impressed! Thank you.

Loved every second of my time there. Both parks are great especially if you are a Harry Potter fan! Get up early to do the gringotts ride. We did and the queue was still an hour long. Get up early everyday and make the most of your time there. Our hotel was close by so a small nap each day had us regenerated for the evening when everyone else is leaving and the rides are quieter. We ate at 11 and 4 each day so as to avoid the crowds...very handy. Bottles of water are allowed in. Your bag is checked on the way into the park each day. The single rider queue is a great time saver too. If you are going on the rip rocket ride pick your song quickly or the ride picks it for you. See the dragon in diagon alley by night!

I visited 4 years ago in Islands of Adventure.... A total Nightmare. We were never coming back. Being huge Harry Potter fans, we decided to give Universal a chance this year. Beside the cotinuous Harry Potter break downs, our day went very smoothly! Ate breakfast and walked across the street from our hotel to the park which is the way to go, being much cheaper than on site. They let us in early and we got through the Simpsons, Men in black, and revenge of the mummy in about an hour. Be prepared to use signal rider line sometimes. But not on Harry Potter: it moves very slowly and you miss the whole experience. Ate great food and the leaky choldrin and got through everything In 1 day except dispicable me which stayed above 70 minutes all day and did not feature a signal riders line. Overall a great day! Do not miss the animal show or fear factor. Get as many pictures as possible!

Went as a family of three adults and two children (ages 8 and 11) over spring break 2015, Booked a vacation package with US airfare, hotel (Universal's Cabana Bay) and three day park passes. No express pass included. Cost:: $7000 total. Express pass was going for $184 per person per day at our hotel. That would have been extra. Went because of Harry Potter attractions. Experienced that, enjoyed the frozen butter beer, and the interactive wands, but won't return This is an uncomfortable park to say the least. We have been to the Disney attractions, Nickelodeon, SIx Flags, Sea World, and Atlantis over prior years spring break. I would return to any one of them but not this one. First, it is Florida and the sun during the day is very hot ( oppressive humidity in the summer months also), You will walk miles and miles in the heat at this park ( one reviewer's pedometer clocked it at 11 miles per day). You will find very few places to sit and rest ( most people were sitting on the curbs in the sun). There were lines for everything including cold drinks. Harry Potter attraction was so mobbed you could hardly walk without banging into someone. The stores there are small so you are standing in lines to get in. Where is the shade and the air conditioning, Universal??? 70 to 120 minute waits for rides (on your feet the whole time) is daunting and longer when a ride malfunctions and several seem to do so every day. Granted, spring break is busy but there needs to be a better way for crowd control, moving people from one end of the park to another, and respite from the sun. Arcade games like you see at state fairs cost $5 per person for a 30 second event. Kids enjoyed the pools at the hotel more than the park. Not all that much to do if you don't like extreme roller coasters or getting soaked to the skin on the water rides. This is a park best enjoyed by teenagers and young adults. For the price, Atlantis was a better value and far more enjoyable.

Had a really memorable day out, and could easily rate 5 stars. The only reason to "downgrade" to a still-impressive 4 stars was the big food lines (and pretty horrid turkey legs as fast food) and the long "Express" lanes. Having paid almost exactly $900 for the four of us (two adults, a ten and eight year old), we thought the Express lanes would save more time. They WERE still worth it overall, but they weren't quite the time-saver they arguably should have been given they were a whopping 120 green backs per person.  But the rides were great, the Simpsons we loved, Transformers was really impressive, and Harry Potter’s coaster was truly amazing. Moe’s Mexican in the City Walk on the way out was great (and the Saporros from across the way were incredibly good value).  Highly recommended this place, and really a must when coming to Orlando.

Universal Studios is fantastic! As a massive Harry Potter fan I thoroughly enjoyed Diagon Alley/Hogsmeade. The Rip Ride Rockit and the Mummy rides were highlights as was the general atmosphere of the parks.

Dear all, Save up some extra money and visit Orlando Universal Studio. It is 100% worth it! Our family had so much fun. The rides are thrilling and the water rides really get you wet, but no worries you quickly will dry. There is so much to do and to see, so go early and get the VIP pass for front of line, coz the ques are long and waiting time is up to 90 minutes, but with the special pass no more than 5-10 minute so. Please go and have a blast, I promise you will never forget it! We loved it❤️❤️❤️

Visited Universal Florida with my husband and 3 kids (6, 10, 13) during spring break/April 2015. Park was very crowded and lines were long. We did not purchase express passes as they were very expensive ($89-99 per person per day). In fact, the passes were more expensive than the park tickets themselves (we bought 3 day base tickets from AAA for $150 in advance)! We enjoyed all the rides here -- Return of the Mummy was my favorite. Unfortunately, we didn't ride the Despicable Me ride as the line was 110 mins (I'm patient, but not that patient). Didn't stay for the fireworks at park closing -- we could view them from our hotel (Point Orlando --highly recommended). Probably would be best to visit park early or go during non-peak months to avoid long lines. Also, consider staying at a Universal deluxe on-site resort (Royal Pacific or Portofino Bay) b/c express passes are included --> we wanted a larger suite so we decided to stay off-site.

We visited both Universal Studios and Island of Adventure over 3 days. We had a lot of fun and there were a range of rides for all kinds of ages. We bought unlimited tickets for 1 week so we could go on any rides we wanted for the week. I would advise you download the Universal Studios Orlando app which tells you how long the wait will be for the ride. The Harry Potter rides were fantastic although in the afternoon the queues get much longer. The Revenge of The Mummy ride was my personal favourite because it was enough for me to handle (coming from an 11 year old) and I'd totally recommend it. The Dragon Challenge and Incredible Hulk Coaster were the scariest rides there. I'd also recommend you get there a bit earlier in the morning because the queues get really long in the afternoon unless you have a fast pass.

Purchased a joint pass with the adjacent islands of adventure. Do your research and plan the day . Expect long queues at the most popular attractions. If you can't wait ( in some cases queues were over 2 hours) be prepared to get the fast pass. Get there early and leave late: pay for the preferred parking as you will be tired at the end of the day. Take minimum bags ; they get heavier as the day becomes longer

This wasn't my first time at Universal. Loved that they had a buy two days get the third free special (altho I did not use the third day, it was still nice to have the option). I also like that even though you tend to wait in line a lot, much of that waiting is in places that are air conditioned. I found many folks had no problem hanging out and lounging just about anywhere so we could cop a squat when needed for a rest. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is so worth it for us Potter-geeks! So much to see and snap pictures of. Nice rides. Overall a very enjoyable experience.

The Universal and Disney parks have implemented practices where for an extra fee you can join the exclusive club of the “Line skippers – First-Class Customers”, one problem though is that the majority of us, hardworking middleclass, who have made an effort to pay the already hefty entry park fees are left as a second-class customers, enduring increasingly longer, slower and more convoluted lines. In the country where everything is for sale, the customer respect is too. It is not, I that I did not expect lines, but the fact that they were unfairly longer and slower just because, the “First-Class” had always-absolute priority over us: The Second-Class.  The park attractions are fantastic; however the parks management by implementing this customer differentiation is creating inequality and customer resentment, is it worthwhile for an extra dollar to risk the overall experience quality of the attraction park?  I have enjoyed the park attractions; yet, I did not appreciate the sub-standard feeling of being a worthless-second-class customer.

As mentioned, the lines can be pretty lengthy, but my family (including 2 middle school kids) LOVED the "Rip Ride Rock-It" roller coaster, the Dragon Challenge roller coaster and so many other attractions at Universal. As an American Express cardholder, we enjoyed the AMEX Lounge that is near the Shrek attraction. It's a little hard to find, but it's a nice air-conditioned lounge to relax in with granola bars & potato chips to snack on and refreshingly cold bottled water to cool you down.

We bought a 3 day/one park a day pass to Universal. We went Easter Monday and Tuesday and the following Tuesday. Even with park crowds rated at a 10, we were still able to do everything we wanted, without the Express Pass. We considered staying at one of the Universal hotels to get the Express Pass for free but was not willing to pay $500 a night since this was not the main reason we came to Orlando.  I was a little weary not having an Express Pass when the parks were going to be insane but we made it work. We arrived at the park 30 mins before it opened (730am) and made sure we went straight to the Harry Potter area. We waited in line until the ride opened and got right on. After we did the Harry Potter area we went right to our other main rides. Since we knew we were going to come back to this park for a second day when crowd levels were not so high we did not stressed about doing everything. We did a couple shows when crowds became overwhelming then left after lunch time, went home and napped, then came back around dinner time since the park was opened until 10pm. The crowds were so much better at night. We were able to ride The Mummy coaster over and over without a wait. We had a 10 min wait for the Simpsons Ride and my daughter got right on kiddie Simpsons themed ride (forget the name).  When we came back to this park on the following Tuesday (when crowd levels were going to be far less) we arrived 30 minutes before park opening (opened at 9am) and was able to get right on Despicable Me, Transformers, Men in Black, E.T., The Mummy (3x), and The Simpsons Ride all before 11am. We then walked over and ate at Hard Rock Cafe and then went home. We enjoyed both Universal parks and as long as you plan your day, you can definitely get everything done without a Express Pass.  My daughter was 7 years old and was able to do almost every ride, she was a 1/2 inch to short for the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket but we were fine with not riding that. I wouldn't recommend bringing children much under that age because they would not get to ride many of the rides.

This is an update to a previous review. While the park will do just about anything to make more money off you and you are bombarded with high end chain restaurants as soon as you enter, I think our daughter was the right age for it this year at 12. Long lines and very crowded especially at Harry Potter whose rides my daughter and her friend did care for. The people on top of people trying to move around. They enjoyed it overall so we hD a good time and will go back to the other side likely next year.  Do yourself a favor though and don't buy both park passes for the same day. You will never get through both parks in one day to pull this off and they know this.  Also don't buy the overpriced expedited line tags. They don't guarantee better line placement. It is the biggest rip off.  This is NOT a good park for small children.

The Dislike first! Too far to walk from parking lot to activities. Now, the fun. The Rides were great... and the TRANSFORMER didn't disappoint---once you got to the ride, except we were in line at least an hour and a half---OF STANDING...TWISTER had a few surprises. Enjoyed the Mardi Gras parade

upon arriving at the park we encountered an immediate problem, parking. We had up to about 20 minutes waiting just to find a parking space which is unacceptable. However after this it was plain sailing until we reached the ticket desks to enter the parks amusement area, we had a 2 and a half hour wait to get our tickets, despite it taking mere minutes for others. I strongly recommend not visiting this park.

My wife and I visited Orlando for our Honeymoon in April this year (2015) and I can honestly say we had a blast.  This was a first time visit for both of us and we were quite excited about visiting the big parks - first on our list was Universal.  I've read through a number of reviews on here (mainly the poor / terrible ones) and I think I must have been at a different park from these people. Although the two Universal parks didnt seem to be as big as I expected (maybe because I was still remembering wanting to go there as a kid, where everything was 10x bigger!), I thought the places were fantastic. From coming through the entrance into the CityWalk, then on into Islands of Adventure and finally Universal Studios itself, the visit well met how I imagined it would be.  I must admit, there aren't as many rollercoaster-type rides as I first thought and there seems to be an over-use of 3D / 4D rides these days, but that doesnt take away from the fact that the parks are above and beyond anything we'd been to before.  We had a great time wandering around the parks, having a go on various rides, but we were both amazed with the Harry Potter areas - the attention to detail in these areas of the parks is just fantastic and the Hogwarts train between the two parks is an added bonus (some people have raged that it's a con to get you to pay for tickets to both parks, but it's not a necessity, you dont HAVE to go to both, but why wouldnt you?) Yes, there are a number of shops, which sometimes comes across as just another way to get you to spend your money (t-shirts, wands, etc, etc), but let's be honest, we go to these places to enjoy ourselves, so if that means getting some overpriced souvineers, then so be it.  We had mutli-day passes for both Universal and Disney and both my wife and I found that we enjoyed the Universal parks a lot more (maybe the majority of the Disney parks were a bit too kiddy for us and Universal more adult). I could spend the next hour or two going into more detail about the rides, but have a quick Google and try them for yourself - you definitely wont be disappointed. We're already in the process of planning a revisit next year!  Overall, I can't really fault Universal at all - the staff were always pleasant and helpful, the rides were fantastic, the place wasnt too busy (we went at a more off-peak time....if you're going to complain about the parks being busy, dont go when all the schools are on holidays!).  I'd definitely recommend Universal Studios Orlando to anyone wanting to visit an excellent theme park :)

It is all you would expect. Having the express pass that comes with the hotel stay was super helpful. Only rides that don't accept the express pass are the Harry Potter specific rides. Don't bother with the extra morning hour if you stay at an onsite hotel. They feed you to the Hogwarts ride. The line was much less early morning line. Only the Hogwarts area was open, so it wasn't as helpful as we had expected. We returned to their Diagon Ally just before closing and almost no one was there. Young Wizards who want to test their wands would have more fun at the end of the day.

Where a party of two, both 29. Rides are OK, Busch Gardens is better. The shows are OK. Universal is very expensive, also has different prices depending on the weekdays. What's nice is that you really dive deep into the shows, especially the 3D and 4D rides. Took us two days to see the things we wanted to see on both Universal and Island of Adventures.

I must say between our visit in 2008 and this week, Universal has really upped the ante in regards to Customer Service and Guest relations! I rented an ECV which made life for the day BETTER! The price wasn't bad and the authorization for the hold came off quickly and without delay.  Ok, now for the not so good- Universal, it's time to retire T2. Yep, I said it. The guy playing said character missed queues, could barely get up onto the stage from the floor, and the overall experience, while good for something from the 90s, is tired! One of the soldiers didn't work, which drew your eye to it, the wait time in the Cyberdyne Presentation area was long and very little was done to accommodate those who were without wheelchairs or ECV's! I gave my seat to an elderly lady after we were in queue for at least 25 minutes. The Mummy died around 4ish while we were in line, so that was a SUPER bummer- and we couldn't even return to ride it later because it closed that day at 5:30! We arrived on a Sunday morning and mostly everything was slated to open around 11 or later...  Also, please improve the quality of the Transfer wheelchairs...or make all the lines COMPLETELY accessible for ECV's!  VERY DISAPPOINTED NO MARVEL ITEMS FOR PURCHASE ONLINE! I waited to buy items because we'd not preplanned to have baggage (due to fees on the flight).  Otherwise A+! Ride attendants were beyond wonderful and helpful! The beautiful young lady working The Mummy had personality plus!

The staff was very helpful and they let us in on inside tips but the wait for Despicable me was 100 minutes and Rip ride rockit was 45 minutes and the park was a little messy BUT I would recommend you come to both parks.

Believe me, I'm not into theme parks or rides and get a sweat on from the motion of a bus, but Universal completely changed my opinion. It's quite simply brilliant.  We were lucky and could go at low season, in mid-April, when the crowds were probably pretty sparse, so my review reflects that and we didn't experience any horrific queues or lines to ride for 4 minutes.  Universal for me was like being transported back 40 years in time to when I was a kid and I found the whole park magical. Harry Potter and Diagon Alley is unbelievable - it's like walking into the book and being a huge Harry Potter fan, I was both really moved and ridiculously giddy about the whole thing.  The park is spotless and for somewhere that really only has perhaps 10 blockbuster rides and the rest is gift shops and food retail places, they do it SO well.  Our wait times were bearable - the longest was perhaps Gringotts at Diagon Alley one afternoon and that took about 45 mins but I consider myself lucky with that when I read some other reviews!  Walking through Platform 9 and 3/4 is breathtaking - make sure you take the train to and from Island of Adventures because the ride is different with each journey.  Transformers and Revenge of the Mummy were my other 2 favourite rides. Loved them both.  And surprisingly the Simpsons was highly amusing and the lard-boy donuts really tasty!  My big tip for Universal is to take a bum-bag/fanny pack - not so much a fashion item any more but I loved mine and think they should come back in! Some of the lockers are chargeable and having a bum bag removes the need to use them or worry about where to keep your valuables.  Great experience - it's a blast for any age. I loved it so much that we're going back to Orlando next March!
You hop on your bike and go on an adventure to help E.T and his friends return home safely. A lot of fun and you are thanked personally by E.T at the end.

We purchased a 3 day park to park ticket (special was buy 2 days get 1 free), for a long weekend trip to Orlando. We stayed at Universal's Cabana Bay Reaort, which allowed early entrance into Island of Adventure's Harry Potter. We took advantage of that the first day, and the 2nd day we arrived at the park before 8:30, based on a tip that they would open up at least 30 minutes early, which they did. We were able to ride every ride we wanted to in the park within 4 hours, but by noon, the park was jammed and the lines were long. You need 2 days to see both parks, although it's only because of the long lines later in the day slow you down. The technology of the rides are amazing with the 3D/4D experiences - it is worth the trip.
We visited the wizarding world of Harry Potter and it was AWESOME! !!! We drank butter beer and saw Gringots! This is a MUST SEE 4 HARRY POTTER FANS!
What a great day. Plenty for all age ranges . allow 2 days to do it justice, 1 day Harry Potter the other everything else.
everything!!! What is not to like?? I love the bars around the lake. Love the park and the rides. I really loved going at night and walk around.
What an excellent experience we had at this wonderful place, could not fault it one bit. Keep up the good work.

I just loved it. Every 3-d ride that we had time to ride was awesome. The minion, transformers, shriek. Loved the mummy ride. Loved the scenery. I wish we had more time to ride more 3-d rides. We did not even cover half of the park. The Harry potter train from park to park was really neat. It is a bit over priced. It is ridiculous that you have to pay per day for the souvenir cups. You spend 10.00 on the first day and keep adding an extra day for 7.00 dollars more. Plus there is a chip in the bottom of the cup so they are ripping you off on that purchase. The food is way over priced. Be prepared for a lot of walking and major crowds. But it was great. I hope we can go back and experience it again and maybe get to the rides and shows and sight seeing that we did not get to. It would take a good whole week if not longer to cover it all.

Harry Potter was different and something worth seeing once but not worth the price for a return trip here. The staff and park were not the greatest and do not compare at all to Disney even though they profess to be.

Again an amazing park never feeling overcrowded. Loads to do loads of places to eat and drink. When we were visiting there was a closed set for American Ninja so it made it more difficult to negotiate and we missed some things. Beetlejuice graveyard mash up is well worth a viewing and would highly recommend a visit to Flannigans bar. This is a great park highly recommend.

An amazing park with thrilling rides that the entire family can enjoy. Customer service is a bit lacking at times but not terrible.  Visitors should download the "Universal FL" app prior to your visit. It has great info like the current wait time for the park's attractions and a handy GPS-like park map that will give you turn-by-turn directions through the park.  I don't recommend opting for the preferred parking as you're basically paying extra to park in the same parking deck as everyone else, just on a lower level.

Visited Universal Studios for the 2nd time this year and loved it just as much as our first visit. We are a family of 3 and our little one enjoyed The Simpsons area and the Men in Black Ride. So much to see and do that you can fill your whole day and have a fantastic time. This ear we got to do the Transformers ride as it was not open on our last visit in 2013 and we all loved this ride. Wait times were not long wither 20 mins for most things, our longest wait was for Despicable Me which was 40/50 minutes but worth it to see our little boy enjoying it and meeting the minions after it.  Would recommend to everyone and we will be visiting again on our return trip.

I went with a group of 4 adults and 2 kids and it happened to be the 25th anniversary of the park. The lines were quick. The only thing we didn't get to ride was the new Minions ride since there was a 75 minute wait. The kids loved it. The parade was cute and the Celebration of 100 years of movies was great, fireworks included.

This was our first trip to Universal and we loved it here the most. This park had it all. It had good places to eat, plenty of room so you were not shoulder to shoulder all day and it had great rides and attractions. We ended up eating breakfast 3 different days in this park and we found the best place. It is right past the entrance to the park. It is teh Boulangerie Bakery. They do have baked goods, but they have eggs and sandwiches as well that were all very good and not too pricey. of course we visited Diagon Alley a lot and each time it was fun. Our children bought their wands at Olivanders and made spells around the whole section. The Escape from Gringots ride was excellent, we went on it twice and it was worth any wait you might have. Diagon Alley has all the shops that you want as well. Another section of the park that is great is over on the far right as you walk in the main entrance. There is the Horror Show Makeup show that was really fun. There is the ET ride, the Terminator show and eventually you walk through the Simpson's area. The Simpson's ride is very good. Also we loved the Men in Black ride. Minnion Mayhem was excellent as well. Stay away from Shrek. That was horrible. The Mummy ride was really good, we went on that three times. Just an overall excellent experience here.

Second time here (well we visited at least 3 times both trips!) and never gets boring! We have a 6 year old and a 13 year old, both were thoroughly entertained. I prefer this to IOA, although that's also pretty awesome. Mummy, Spider-man, Simpsons Land and Curious George land for when you need to cool of, are all brilliantly done! Of course DIagon Alley is a must, fantastic attention to details and Escape from Gringots is an amazing ride. I find this park quieter than IOA although that could just be because it is laid out better, wider paths etc. We visited through 1st and 2nd week of June and as long as we arrived for opening, we managed to get all all the big rides pretty speedily (Max wait 20mins). Although we never manged to do the Despicable Me ride as queue was always 60mins plus. We ate at Mel's Diner, as we have before, love their shakes and burgers!  I highly recommend Valet parking. It may seem a bit steep at 35 bucks but the time you save getting into the park and the ease of bag check etc is well worth it if you ask me! Plus when you are tired after a full day, it's really nice to just sit and wait for your car to be brought to you, then whip out, no traffic at all. I budgeted it along with my spending money for the trip so it didn't seem to much of an expense.  I can't rate this place high enough. We have nothing to compare it to in the UK. It's absolutely awesome!

This is a great park for the whole family. The park has great rides and simulators that allow the family to share rides together. Teenagers will have a great time here. This was my son' third or forth trip here.

Thanks to Islands of Adventure, Universal studios is so much quieter and overall much nicer and enjoyable, not too busy, except for Minions, could wait over 90 mins for a ride so get in real early. We visited four times with our multi ticket, used the H.P train to visit H.P world, but always felt more at home studio side, we love it, all the old faves,Twister, Mummy, Simpsons, men in black, Shrek, and many more, miss Jaws though! Diagon alley is something else, you don't realise it's there until you get directed to go through this wall, you then enter another world, absolutely breathtaking, try the Butterbeer please! God I feel homesick already!
I liked all the Parks very well run prices inside for Food , drinks a bit expensive but overall the place in run very well would return again.
2 days atleast amazing for all been here 3 times and seen all movies been made gone on all the rides and interactions truly amazing place will be visiting again

The only thing I really have to say is get the front of the line pass but make sure it's a day where rain isn't predicted because i paid $125 Australian dollars plus my $145 entrance fee for front of the line and we got rained out and everything closed. If your a thrill seeker go the the second park first incase this happens!

Visited here beginning of june and queues of all rides was between 10-30mins with the odd technical difficulty with the harry potter ride which was 1hr and half. Lockers are free for a certain amount of time. No drinks are allowed but people still take them and put them on the side of the ride. Unlimited drinks start from 12.99 prob worth it as drinks are from 2.99 for water and then coke and powerade about 4dollars included VAT. Simpsons land is amazing! Their ride is out of this world. Food is about 10 dollars plus. Overall great day out. With queue times being short an gettin on majority of the big rides was worth money!

Really great attractions. This is not Disney. The rides can more intense and themed more towards PG. Universal does some things better than Disney. The humor is targeted and an older audience. Many rides are scarier and rougher than you'd find at Disney. The worker aren't there to create magic. Everyone was kind and helpful and seemed to enjoy friendly talk. There aren't as many atmospheric freebies as Disney. Diagon Alley is FANTASTIC! This is a part of the park where you are really immersed in magic. Theming is very good and will bring back many memories. One negative, they really seem to be chasing your money more throughout the resort. Be prepared to evaluate the value of your options. Unless the park is really crowded, I wouldn't recommend the fast pass for $89. This is in addition to park admission. Three days is plenty of time to see everything even when it is reasonably crowded. I had a great time and hope to visit again.
Like all the other Disney parks it was quite crowded this time of year. The climate can be hot during the day too. Expect the occassional shower. Fun for all ages and great photo opportunities.

My husband and I took our 13 and 10 year olds here 5/29/15-6/1/15. Overall we had a good time, but there were moments when I thought it was little more than a glorified Six Flags and I could have stayed home for that. We almost bought tickets for Disney World the day of to go there instead of another day at Universal that was already paid for. There were some rides one or both of the kids wouldn't go on (babies), but my husband and I managed to go on every ride at least once in one day at the park. This park has some rides for younger kids, but overall it's better for adults and older teens. There was an afternoon parade which most park go-ers treated as an inconvenient foot traffic disruption. Not anything like Disney World where there is a crowd of people watching the parade. Hardly anyone seemed interested in the parade. There are some shows worth seeing. I liked the horror show one. Citywalk is a big draw for adults. Harry Potter ride was good and Revenge of the Mummy. The dining plan is not a good value! the food is not good either. We also went to SeaWorld and Aquatica during this trip and preferred them over Universal. All of the rides that have any element of water in Islands of Adventure will get you drenched which makes the rest of the day very unpleasant. It was hot and I would not have minded getting wet except for the fact that my socks and sneakers were soaked and made my feet hurt. Overall good for adults and teens, but doesn't have the magic of Disney.

Was very and I mean very hot. The places where you stand in line should have more fans and maybe even shades besides sitting in the sun and baking while you wait in line for several minutes to hours. Prices of some things were a little high! Need to have more signes on the road to help navigate the place better, but was by far a great place to visit and get away for a couple of days. Loved the rides they were great and all the staff was very helpful!

Absolutely loved it~ The layout of the place is very similar to other Universal Studios (but that is to be expected) but most of the staff I encountered were friendly and polite. Food booths and location of help stations were convenient and useful; everything was extremely organized! I went there for an event where some of the Harry Potter cast came to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter section of the Park and the organization of the lines and management of customers and staff was well done! No unnecessary lines or space wasted.

We had just one day free to select a park to go to and having been to Orlando on many occasions we selected Universal Studios.  Best Ride - The Mummy (so good we went on it twice!).  The Harry Potter area is fantastic, but very easy to miss. Look behind the brick wall to the right of the station, you will not want to miss out on that.  Although it was very expensive to buy a one day ticket (with Express Passes), it was a great day out, as always...
Fantastic park, with lots of wonderful things to do and see! The rides are great and the Park was very well kept  We cannot wait to return!
don't forget to get one of those yummy turkey legs while enjoying the park. great place for family fun

I've visited the Universal Studios in Hollywood, California and loved it. I had high hopes for this location and I can say I was not disappointed. In fact, I can say that this is my new favorite theme park.  As a disabled traveler it's important to me to be able to get out and enjoy as much of what everyone else does and that includes theme parks. I purchased a 3 day park hopper pass and was impressed immediately.  The handicap parking was close by. All the rides had handicap accessible lines with most being through the exit. The staff at the rides were amazing and very helpful. The only one bad experience was the Harry Potter restaurant. I am on a mobility device and do not walk unassisted. The restaurant has a cue to go through similar to the regular rides. My mobility device didn't allow tight turns required so I had to ask the people behind me to please back up so I could get out. I asked at the front if I could just go in and find a seat while my companion went through the regular line to place our order. I proceeded to find a table and was immediately told by a wait staff that I had to leave my mobility device outside and transfer to a table. I explained I do not walk unassisted and she replied by rolling her eyes and asking me again to park my mobility device outside and walk in to a table. I left. I felt humiliated. It's hard enough not being able to walk unassisted but to be chastised for it by a wait staff at a theme park was humiliating and rude.  The remainder of the park was amazing. I went on the Incredible Hulk ride immediately and loved it. There were storms in the area so they had to shut down the rides periodically but we were able to ride most over the 3 days we were there.  I would recommend this park to those who are handicapped and able bodied over Disney World. This is cheaper, is handicap accessible and has working rides. Two thumbs up!

Universal Studios Orlando has plenty of fun and entertaining rides and attractions that are great for all-day family fun. Best time to go is November through February when the Florida weather isn't nearly as oppressive as summertime. It's also considerably less overcrowded during these months as well... with the exception of course being the few weeks around the year-end holidays.

The Harry Potter attractions are great! Our kids had so much fun. However, the handlers for the characters such as the Simpsons and Despicable Me characters need to be friendlier with kids. They treated kids as if they were a secuirty threat or nuisance.

Just a magical place for any age. You can not do this in 1day. We went for 3days and would have happily done 4 if we had the time and energy. All the staff are lovely. The themes just fantastic. The thrill rides are great and worth the wait. The water rides are just as thrilling as the coasters.  It's worth the money.  The only negative is the line cutters. Not the parks fault as it happens everywhere.

We enjoyed our time at Universal Studios this Summer. The wait time for the majority of the rides was under 30 minutes. The expensive express pass upgrades are worth having if the wait times are excessive. Its best to wait until you get in the park before buying the express pass upgrades. If the lines are not too long you can enjoy the majority of the rides without spending the extra money. Also, if you purchase the express pass after 4 pm it is supposed to be half price. If the lines are long at the Harry Potter ride we suggest going on the single rider line that is found in the locker room inside the gift shop. Lots of great attractions in this park catering to everyone in the family.

Harry Potter brought to life! It's amazing and I'm so glad we went! We visited Islands of Adventure/Hogwarts the year it opened up and were so excited to read that Universal Studios opened up Diagon Alley! It looks just like the movie and how you would imagine it from reading the books. All the shops are creative and imaginative and just amazing to see. My kids were so excited to visit Ollivanders because they watched so many You Tube videos of kids getting picked to test the wands. I warned them they might not be picked! It's not random! Whoever the first kid is in the room, the Wizard will line about 5 of you up on a row, positioning kid #1 in the front of the room. That kid is the one who gets picked to flick the wand and say the spells. It's very cool. We went through twice and timed it so we were first in line. Luckily it was a rainy day and not too crowded. Gringotts was cool mostly because it brings you into the movie. They've made the wait in line an experience by itself with all the goblins around and special props. That aside, the Transformers and Spiderman sims were our favorite! So much fun. The Minion sim is funny. My best advice is don't forget stuff like sunblock, an umbrella...because if you buy the stuff in the park - which is fun to do but SO expensive - you will pay triple the normal cost. If you're not staying at a theme park hotel, invest in the fast pass! It was so much fun to jump to the front of the line. It sucks to wait in line for so long. And this is Orlando, so expect thunderstorms in the afternoon.

Never had a great moment and fun with my wife since we married 2 years ago ! Like this time at universal studios ..it was really so fun we had a lot of fun and laugh ...little of scared ...lol for Rollercoasters :D we get wet too !! Just love it <3

Went mainly for the Harry Potter areas and loved it. The kids were in heaven and since they serve beer alongside the butter beer my wife and I were happy too. The level of detail is incredible. The ability to "use" the interactive wands all over the park was great too. The kids were never bored, tired or grumpy. Definitely looking forward to the Los Angeles Universal Studios getting this.

Wow wow wow, this place is one of the best I have ever been to. Not a dull moment to be had fills me with excitement and sure does get the adrenalin going. This year I am going for the forth time. Cannot wait. Fun for all ages with plenty of excitement to be had.

This park was smaller than expected but we thoroughly enjoyed our time here. We absolutely loved the Simpsons section and had a 'big pink' donut from lard lads which was huge but tasted good. The Simpsons ride was one of our favourites. Diagon Alley is one of the most amazing things we have ever seen, the kings cross/ London bits outside are very realistic. We loved roller coasters but found rip ride rocket was quite rough and threw us around. Great day out.

Universal has improved this park a lot over the years, and I love it every time I go. The live shows are wonderful, and the rides are very well done. Dining options are also good for a theme park. Love it.

Worth the money. I had an amazing time there. Great rides. Best theme park in the world. My top ten rides: 1. Harry potter 2. Hogwarts Express 3. Gringotts 4. Jurassic Park 5. Mummy 6. Simpsons 7. Spider-Man 8. Minion Mayhem 9. Rip saw 10. Popeye  U have to do these rides if u visit the park.

Amazing day out, lots of rides and shows and 3D shows. You will leave the park amazed. A lot of work goes into each section of the park. You can see many characters walking around, most of which you could swear they are the real people. Absolutely brilliant day out

We visited Universal Orlando in June15. We were staying at Loews Pacific who gave us fast passes plus early entry both days. The early entry meant we could visit the very popular harry Potter area before the gates officially opened. The multi dimensional 3D escape from gringotts ride is truly amazing and one of the best ride experiences you will ever have. The line was lengthy however you enter thru Gringotts bank so there is a lot to see on the way. We got to all all the rides in both parks over the 2 days we were there. One day we left the park for a few hours and came back in at night when it was a bit cooler. Both parks are very clean with lots of food options. Many of the rides also have free lockers at the ride entry which is very handy. Something I found very handy was the "universal orlando app". This app shows you real time where you are in the parks and also helps guide you to attractions and is very handy in finding the nearest bathroom. It also has descriptions of the attractions and wait times. As much as they add to the price, especially a family, the fast passes are well worth it. Some rides had 60min wait times and the fast passes brought the time down to 10-15mins.

Great!! We saved a bundle with the express pass. You can go all year long, multiple times a day. Another great thing is the free parking when you're a passholder. Otherwise you will find out its $17 a visit. The new Harry Potter section is well made. Full of excitement for all ages. Rip rocket roller coaster at night was a sight to see as well. Every night at 9:45pm there is a light show in universals lake next to the Transformers ride. Worth the visit at night. Wore the family out each day whether we arrived first in the morning or early in the evening. Have fun and save $$ with that annual pass (preferred annual pass). $152 down and $14 a month on a credit card.

My two daughters thoroughly enjoyed all the Harry Potter attractions and the Dr. Seuss ones as well. We remained outside the park and went to the movies while they entertained their selves. It was a terrific afternoon for all of us. the park is very spacious and has much to do.

If you have young children who watch the latest cartoon characters or are an adult who is in to roller coasters in a big way, the this park and "islands of adventures" is for you. However the rest of the park relies on past, and not very classic, films. The most annoying aspect for me was, having taken a huge amount of money for entrance tickets, they then bombard you with shops, eating places and long queues. You can avoid the queues by purchasing an express ticket but even that is not cheap. The quality of the merchandise in the shops was not high and the quality of the food was equally disappointing. The highlight was undoubtedly the hogwarts train journey between the parks. It is exceptionally well done as is the Harry Potter village. Beautifully constructed and the attention to detail is outstanding. The downside? You guessed it nothing but shops, eateries and three roller coasters - none of which appealed to my family. Even the "family friendly" ride was far to physical. Incidentally the cost of a simple "wand" is almost USD 100!!! So if you take you junior lovers of all things Potter, expect it to be a very expensive visit!!!  If this is trying to vie with the classical Disney theme park, it fails miserably. If it is trying to appeal to "Minions" enthusiasts then it probably passes. Hugh  PS I had never heard of Minions until this visit!!,

Universal is a great theme park. every time you go back there is always something new. The first time we went the King Kong ride was the must do ride, but that was way back, then they had back to the future ride, now all gone. But they have been replaced by rides which are relevant for today, such as Harry Potter, Despicable me, That's what i mean its always reinventing itself. This is a must see theme park, every bit as good as the Disney parks. it seemed to be fairly compacted and easy to get around. we didn't do Universal islands of Adventure, much too old for that, when you pass 30 (+ another 37) it passes you bye. But I'll get one of my granddaughters to go and write the revue for you. In the mean time enjoy this park it's great.

The park was amazing! Everything was clean, it was separated in sections that made sense. The rides were great, ranging from thrill to peaceful enjoyment. If you are looking for Adventure you have to ride The Mummy & The Rocket roller coaster. If you are seeking a blissful ride you have to ride ET. Get on the Simpsons ride, if you enjoy that show. They have a section for kids. The Shrek & MIB rides were not that amusing, it was a bit of a waste of time.

One of my fave places in the world! Love it here, so many different things for all ages.The Mummy ride is one of the best! If visiting in Sept/Oct make sure you go to Halloween Horror Nights, not for the little ones but if into horrors and getting a fright then its the place to be.
LOVE the Transformer ride. So worth the wait. It might be my all time favorite. Be mindful of the temperature and dress accordingly.

So much to see and do, go to an onsite hotel overnight to get express passes for all rides - well worth it in July as wait times topped 75 mins in normal queues ( 10-15max in express). Favourites have to be the new Harry Potter area. The kings cross station and London street facade is so authentic, then you turn into Daigon Alley and and it is too amazing for words. Loads to see in each of the magical windows, and if you get an interactive wand you can perform magic at various places. Gringotts bank is brilliant from the bank workers, the chandeliers, the lift taking you down to the vaults. The escape from gringottts ride is excellent, as you would expect. Go to Olivanders wand shop as there is an unexpected wand master who performs magic, amd you can also choose a wand with properties that suit your personality. The Howarts express is not just a ride on a train from one park to another, it is a magical journey where you walk through the wall into platform 93/4 and the carriages are the old fashioned train carriages and you will see your journey to Hogwarts through the windows. So amazing!! Best rides are the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket - INSANE and you get to see / buy a video at the end and the revenge of the mummy is also fab. Lots of 3d or 4d rides here also which are great - minions is sooooo busy, so either do first or later the evening. Enjoy!
I go to this park 2 - 4 times a week and I am a local. I love everything about Universal Florida! It's the best place to hang out with friends, meet new people, make new friends and enjoy the park!

Ah Universal Orlando. Hello my old friend. Nothing quite says "welcome home" more than briskly strolling through City Walk in the morning sun, surreptitiously cranking up the pace to beat the excited multitudes and entering the greatest theme park on earth through that iconic yellow arch. This is - blimey - the tenth time I've been here, maybe more, and each time is even more special and every bit as electrifying as the first visit back in 1991.  The evolution is extraordinary. Since the last time we were here one of my favourite rides (Jaws) has been retired and replaced by the colossal expansion of Harry Potter, and The Simpsons Ride has now expanded into Springfield, complete with Moe’s Tavern and Kwik-E-Mart. We had much to explore and this time we had a supplementary almost four-year-old in toe.  In many ways this review is as inane as it is bias. Mardy bums look away now because (spoiler alert) there’s nothing critical to say about this astonishing park. It’s so good. I mean it’s SO GOOD. Universal Islands is as close to perfect as you can get, and just when you think it can’t possibly maintain it’s dreamlike zenith you discover brand new qualities that are as reassuringly reliable as listening to the second half of ‘Abbey Road’; you’ve heard it all before a hundred times, yet it still gets better.  So instead of trying to cram every single highlight of the resort into a single review (you can take it for granted that the roller-coasters are world class, the staff are impossibly chirpy and the dinosaurs in Jurassic Park still look convincing), I’ve picked out a few unsung highlights that don’t often get a mention but are important to us.  The child swap system is better than in any park we’ve been. Instead of waiting at the ride entrance, you queue together as a family and when you get to the front of the line one of you takes baby to a comfy, air-conditioned area usually with a TV and plenty of seating while the other enjoys the ride. You then literally swap (high-fiving is optional) and the other parent joins at the very front of the queue. This way you only ever queue once.  A place that we’ve rarely visited in the past, but where essentially became home base for us this time, was Woody Woodpecker’s Kidzone. Our boy LOVED the Curious George Goes To Town splash area – so much so that we ended up spending much of the day doing laps of the splash zone, Woody Woodpecker’s Nuthouse Coaster and the nearby E.T. Ride. We didn’t mind as the hours we spent here under shady trees meant we gave our feet a much-needed rest while the boy ran around lapping it all up.  I could go on and on about the quality of Universal; it’s mind-boggling scale, the watertight service, and an unwavering desire to make everything faultless, but that would be dull so I’ll wrap it up here (I haven’t even mentioned the thrill of meeting Spider-Man, the astonishing detail that’s gone into creating Harry Potter and the Escape From Gringotts or the remarkably real interpretation of Kings Cross train station, all of which deserve pages and pages of reviews just on their own). Plus as if to tease me into coming back for more, a new King Kong ride is set to open soon, and judging by the view from the Pteranodon Flyers it’s going to be every bit as insanely detailed and breath-taking as Diagon Alley.  So I’ll just say this: don't waste your time or hard-earned holiday money going anywhere else. Although Orlando has plenty of other parks and attractions they are all inferior to the unreserved master. Universal remains the summit. And we can’t wait to go home again.
Fantastic with brilliant rides more suited for teenagers than small kids.The only down side us the long queues and the fast track us nit worth it as not as good as Dusney Magic kingdom, a rip off.
Holiday 2011  Stay for a three week break and visited this park during this time. I was amazed by the amount of ride geared up for every ages. Overall a experience not to be missed😀

I was speechless, it was so fun and amazing. Spectacular for the whole family, any age and anyone would love it I'm sure. The rides are top notch and especially the Simpson's, I will not spoil it but it is INCREDIBLE! It is My favourite ride of all time, the queueing isn't too bad either. Such an enjoyable experience...10/10

Universal was on our list for the new Harry Potter experience, as well as some of the other rides we had not seen since we were last there, like Spiderman. The Harry Potter ride was so good that, on exiting, the four of us looked at each other and all said "Yep, guess we have to do that again." The park was clean and the service excellent. It should be noted that there are two components to Harry Potter - one in this park, and the other in the Islands of Adventure park. In order to ride both - and both are great - you need to have the park hopper pass. You get to ride the Harry Potter train between the two if you like. The ride in this park, "Escape from Gringotts" is well conceived, the wait line takes you through a Goblin bank, and every detail was taken care of. Also, you simply MUST try Spiderman. We really enjoyed the trip!

Stunningly detailed themes, exhilarating rides, lots of stuff to see and do when you want a break from standing in queues to take a ride. Rides are terrifyingly fun - that oxymoron is what you want to describe a roller coaster though! You want that adrenalin rush, that fear factor and a great time all rolled into many fast rides - and you will get your wish that's for sure! On the cute side Toon town and Dr Seuss Landing were my favorites. My least favorite ride was the one from Hogwarts - though the castle is spectacular, the interior detail is awesome, the Herry Potter experience ride made me so nauseous I was sick for the rest of the day and couldn't do another ride till the next day. All that in your face graphics was awful. Diagon alley is a not to be missed part of the Islands of Adventure park. Great parks, great value.

We only went for the one day and wish we had brought the ticket for two days as we had so much fun. The rides were brilliant and we loved everything there.Very busy with lots of people waiting to go on the rides. All well worth the wait. It was great and a lovely way to spend the day.
We had Unlimited entry to tree theme parks and my kids had a blast. I had a great time at "wet 'n' Wild.
Our visit to Universal Studios was full of fun. Transformers, Minion, Rockit and simpsons are must. Harry Potter attractions are the best.

I can't say much about universal studios that probably hasn't been said a thousand times before:  1. The attractions are superb. Terminator, Harry Potter, the Mummy, Men in Black, the Simpsons.....WOW!  2. For a one day trip this place is remarkably expensive, ($100+/person), but I guess that isn't much different than Disney, a ski resort, or an NFL game.  3. This place is CROWDED in the summer, even on a Monday.  4. The experience would be so much better if they would do a fast-pass system like Disney. The lines are horrible, and to offer an "express pass" for $80/person is simply insulting.

Have visited this place many times and it is always fantastic.. Very easy and layout has a great flow. Have never really had to wait a long time but understand it does happen.find it very well organised and would defo recommend over disny which is a nightmare.

We had 4 day park to park tickets with unlimited fastpass. Although this is expensive it is definitely worth it. The queues without fastpass were between 60 and 120 minutes for most of the bigger attractions, with fastpass the longest we waited was 20 minutes! The Transformers 3d ride was a big hit with my teenage sons as was the Mummy roller coaster. The live shows around the park are very good and the singers can give most professionals a run for their money. Don't waste your fastpass on the great movie experience or Shrek. Although they are ok you would feel cheated if you don't have unlimited. Lots of iced water stations around the park all free of charge. You do need to buy a lanyard for your passes but only buy 1 per couple as you can put them back to back and save some dollars. The terminator show is well worth it.

This place is incredibly overrated. The rides are minimally interesting at best, save for the fact that the themes are based on Universal movies that are well liked and remembered. There are no truly scary rides, therefore it is a park that is best suited for young children and people who scare easily.
Excellent rides and food. If only the afternoon Thunderstorms would have held off. Love the express option!! Way better than Disney's!! Just pay the extra money and get in line!!!
Great rides..we didn't do fast passes and never really waited in lines more than 45 minutes. Take ponchos they are $8 each at the park. Lots of things for all ages!

Went during haunted horror nights and had an absolute blast. The lines were a little long but they made the anticipation of the rides a little greater. The actual haunted attractions were a little sub par in my 2nd trip but still fun. If you go buy your tickets online vs at the gate you will save a ton of money. Never go in the summer. Off season trips are always the best route

These parks are definitely worth a day trip, especially for any Harry Potter fans. But i think really a day is all you need for both parks. And there just isn't the same feeling as Disney. Now that Disney offer three FREE, pre bookable fast passes per day in their parks it really puts Universal to shame. Going from no wait in Disney to having to wait around an hour for pretty much every attraction in Universal it really puts you off. I also found wait times inaccurate. We cued for the Popeye water ride which was supposed to be a 20 minute wait but we were waiting double that, in enclosed and hot conditions. I felt like i was about to pass out by the time we finally got to ride. Please sort out a better fast pass system!

A 2 day park to park passes were great as gave us the flexibility we needed. Both days enjoyed by all. Take advantage of the dining package. It's worth it. If driving, $17 to park, however you can leave and return later when parks stay open longer. The larger park is "Studios " so plan ahead. Harry Potter sets are amazing & the rides are incredible especially "Escape from Gringotts" & "Forbidden Journey ". Overall, we throughly enjoyed our visit. All staff we encountered were knowledgeable and helpful. Queuing for main rides was expected, but fast passes were to expensive @ $99 per person per day on top of entry price
This is a great place to visit if you like movie memorabilia, behind the scenes film making experiences, splashy shows from animated movies, and roller coasters.

So I just got back from Universal last night and I hated it so much that I felt the need to go out of my way to create a TripAdviser account just to type this.  First off, I could not believe just how unfriendly the staff was. At certain times I felt like I was at some town fair run by teenagers from Camp Crystal Lake. They seemed irritated all of the time.
