Now granted, not all of the staff was like this. For example, the staff at the WWOHP were extremely friendly. It was like I was at a whole different place.  Along with this, we had a terrible time with their fast pass program. For a family of 4 with fast passes and food and whatnot, it ended up costing us $1000. Even with the fast passes we still had to wait in lines that were 15 minutes long. You know what? That's not good enough. We expect to get on the rides immediately with no questions asked if we are paying a grand.  Secondly, and this one really pissed me off:  Universal seems to have some sort of unjustified anti-filming policy when riding the rides. I am a videographer and whenever I go on vacation I always film our experiences. Oh no, but not at Universal. They don't allow filming. Allow me to elaborate. On the ride "Jurassic Park River Adventure" I was filming this ride with a Gopro hero 4 strapped onto my Gopro extreme heavy duty chest harness built for extreme conditions such as mountain climbing and in this case, riding rides. So here we are, riding the ride and everything is fine, or so I thought. All of a sudden, we reach the final climactic drop involving the T-Rex. Just then, the ENTIRE ride stops and we here one of those Camp Crystal Lake employees over some sort of intercom telling me to put my Camera away for supposed safety's sake. There were so many things wrong with the situation:  1. I was unaware of this film rule. When I got on the ride nobody told me to put my camera away. It took them until the very end of the ride, right before the final drop to tell me to stop what I was doing. This not only destroyed the whole ambience of the ride but horribly embarrassed myself and my family.  2. I was told to put the camera away for "safety". Now granted, if I was carrying some sort of giant camera and flailing it in the air that's different. But this wasn't the case. This thing was strapped to my body like superglue. And when he told me to put it away I scrambled to find a way to get the camera off my chest. I ended up pointing the camera downwards because that's all I could do. I couldn't remove the camera from my chest unless I got out of the boat. So they had to stop the entire ride for that!  3. Lastly, I believe they might also be worried about "spoiling the ride" which is another reason why they might have this rule out in place. To that I say go on YouTube, there's dozens of videos of rides from the park.  Now to those reading you might be thinking "well rules are rules" to that I say, Disney World does not have an anti filming rule. I got on every ride at Disney World and was able to film with no questions asked. Not only that but the staff is extremely friendly no matter where you go.  Moral of the story? Take your money to Disney World because Universal is just ridiculous.

Spent a couple of days here as usual - new Harry Potter was interesting even as a non-fan. Saw the Goo Goo Dolls for the final night of the anniversary of the park which was really great - feet were killing by this point tho after long day ;) Rides are great and staff always helpful - see you again!

First time to Orlando so we visited all the main parks and attractions on our stay and thought Universal Studios was by far the best! It had something for everybody. The 3D rides were out of this world!

I have a prolapsed disc and cannot stand for long periods. Why go to a theme park then? Well, mostly for the kids but also, with my stool in hand, it's not a problem as i can sit during the long queues. Not so here though. Apparently a 2 ft stool is potentially dangerous to other guests whereas 3 ft umbrellas and selfie sticks are clearly ok.  The security guard clearly feels sitting is dangerous but umbrellas and selfie sticks are fine.  So i pay this money to sit down on the ground whilst my kids go on the rides.  Looks like I'll be spending the remaining days of my vacation at Disney where they are more accommodating.  Shame on you #kickingsomwonewhentheyaredown

We used to view Universal as Disney's poor cousin. It never felt as clean as Disney, the staff were often lacklustre and we couldn't wait to return to the Disney bubble. No more !! Universal now delivers on all fronts. Staff are pleasant and well trained, park is clean and the theming of Harry Potter can teach Disney a thing or two. Universal is now well worth a visit. We tend to stay in one of the onsite hotels and use Express pass along with early entry. Universal has become a must do.

Best theme park ever,me and my family had tickets over 2 weeks so we went quite a few times so we could fit everything in.If your planning to spend a day there,please be aware that you won't be able to fit everything in because there is soooo much to do.
Passed the extra for the fast pass , able to go on all the rides that we want to go on in both parks in one day. Harry Potter rides impressive.

This place is ok and has some good rides like The Mummy. But the place doesn't come close to Disney Majic Kingdom. The express pass system does not function because it is badly operated. Basically everyone buys them and can use it at any time which means all the big attractions have big ques in the express pass lanes. Most of the attractions are short 3D films which have seats that bump up and down. These simply do no entertain me. The whole place is a rip off. The staff are poor and do not look interested. DO NOT buy movie and a meal deal. I did , I thought it meant that I could eat in any restaurant in city walk, but no, it meant I could eat I n a select 3 restaurants on restricted menus. one day is enough
Every ride was wicket cool! Already can't wait to go back. The park was just large enough to spend the day there.

Great rides but long waits. You can pay double to get the fast pass. I constantly felt like they were taking every dollar they could. They charged much more than the products were worth but there were memorable events.

A totally different park to Disney (of course).  Harry Potter section was very good.  The whole park was very clean and tidy.  It gives the impression of loads of streets and you keep expecting cars to drive down them.  Plenty to look at and even if the park is busy you still have room to move.
My husband and I are movie buffs so we opted for a honeymoon at Universal. Totally worth it! The park had everything we could ask for. We're already planning our next trip :D
Tons of fun! Our favorites were Escape from Gringotts & The Mummy. Wish it was closer to the parking. It takes forever to actually enter the park.

We had one day with our son at Dr Seuss' park at islands of adventure. Our 4 year old loved it all, the train through the restaurant and over the park, the carousel, the squirting fish, the thing 1 and 2 ride was a bit "saw" like and freaked him out a bit!

We loved Universal!  Great selection of rides for all ages and Harry Potter land is amazing. We also loved Simpsons & Transformers rides. The queue for minions was always at least 2 hours and after queueing up i personally didnt think it was worth it but the kids did!  The dining card is great too as it allows you 1 meal, 2 drinks & 2 snacks so is def a money saver!

Universal has added many new attractions. One reason why the park is full on a hot August day.  Three day pass for both studio and adventure island offers the best deal. Consider buying the express pass if you only have 1 day to visit.

This was my first trip to Universal since 2002, and my was I impressed!  Universal has continued developing and adding key attractions such as Rockit Rollercoaster, Simpsons land, Shrek, Transformers, Harry Potter world, and more, where Disney has added nothing.  The City Walk on entrance is an awesome place with great atmosphere, while the park itself is constructed excellently with impressive buildings and worlds. Harry Poitter World is truly something else and even for those who don't know their Harrys from their Rons, it has something for everyone and is unbelievable.  The only downside here is the huge wait times for rides - you need to be there 45mins before opening and go to all key attractions early or you'll be sunk - or by universal's fast pass.  I can't say enough good things about universal and I cannot wait for my next trip!
Loved Universal Studios, Despicable Me and Transformers were the best rides ever! My boyfriend was able to take a picture with Optimus Prime.
Love love this place always a wonderful family day we go back every year Very clean and the staff is very pleasant

We loved going to universal studios and seeing the great rides and Hollywood heroes. The terminator ride was brilliant and the spiderman ride was great also.  The NASCAR cafe is a good place to visit also.  For me the back to the future ride was something special.  Over a great place to visit.

My company booked out part of Universal Studios one evening and it was the best company gather that I have been to in 40 years, and I've been to a lot of them. The staff was great and having the rides and area just to ourselves made for a great evening of bonding and fun.
one of the ebst holiday destinations in the world. I went with my girlfriend, family and my two year old sister, and it was amazing.
We went on a Saturday and it was extremely crowded with the longest lines I have ever encountered. One ride broke down and we have to get off and walk after waiting in said long line!!!!
Both parks are fantastic for all ages.Good fun. Get an express to skip the queues as its well worth it
Have been there a few times and will be going back again The new rides were awesome and can't wait for new ones next year Harry Potter was great Fun for the whole family

The whole universal experience is amazing top to bottom, the rides, shows and atmosphere can't be matched even by other well known parks!  Honestly, if you're looking for a theme park you'll have more fun here than anywhere. Fun for all ages.  My only issue is that I couldn't fit on one ride so if you're a big guy that could be an issue.

Picked a good time to visit as the crowds were not too large, weather was not too hot, and no storms. Kids were kept happy throughout as there was a good mix of character meet and greets and simulation rides to keep them entertained. Lots of places with air conditioning to rest and recuperate. I would highly recommend getting the meal plan.

Third trip to Universal first To Diagon Alley. I cannot say enough. We were in Orlando for 10 days and I did not expect to spend to most of it here. But we sure did. The second we walked into Diagon Alley it felt like another world. I had to stop and take it all in. I was not expecting it to be so big or detailed. Everywhere I looked there was something amazing to see and do. The interactive wand areas are fun. Specially the one in knockturn. And Knockturn itself was crazy. It was about 90 degrees out that day and Knockturn was a good 20 degrees cooler. Covered so when it rained it was neat place to hang out. I bought so much stuff it was embarrassing! We went back a lot at night because the area thins out before close and got some stunning photos. I wouldn't want to go back to the hotel give me a tent and I would of slept right there :) Also get some ice cream! The strawberry and peanut butter is like nothing Ive ever had before! Not Diagon Alley- Universal its self is my favorite side. I love the Mummy ride as well as Men in Black. We always have a blast on those. Simpsons itself is neat. I don't like the ride too much as it makes me a little sick But the detail in area is awesome. We had a good lunch and some nice drinks. I don't like the 1 beer rule. I get the reason but most places are 2 which would make it easy for a couple. Also if you go back to this area a little before close you can get some really neat photos. Transformers was a fun addition and I look forward to the Fast and Furious ride.

Hi we visited the Harry Potter gringotts ride with one terrified 12 year old boy after lots of persuasion to no avail we we leaving the ride and spoke to Heather one of the park crew well she couldn't do enough to allay his fears so much so that he eventually went on the ride. Heather you're a fantastic person and a credit to the Universal team. Many thanks.

Already did Disney so headed to Universal when we went back to Orlando this fall and saw on the tickets that we could purchase add-on tickets to Halloween Horror Nights. We had NO idea what it was like or what happens. This is the funnest event with nine haunted houses (names like Insidious, Great American Werewolf in London, Walking Dead, The Purge, etc.) and with scare events surrounding different areas. No costumes are allowed on visitors, so the only ones dressed up are Universal workers (which is nice so you know who is who!) They have really turned the park into a Halloween dream and it doesn't even look like the same place. All the rides are open too! But let me give you two very important tips: eat somewhere else before you go and arrive past opening time (lines are long long) and we were able to leisurely walk in. Second, BUY THE EXPRESS PASS for the evening. You can wait in lines for a long while, we bought one after our first house wait and it was worth every cent. Got to do everything we wanted to in just a few hours. The express pass is also good on the rides. (Remember, your express pass from earlier in the day is not valid at Halloween Horror nights, you have to purchase a separate one). They cut off the number of express passes they sell as well. Final tip, try not to go on a Saturday night if at all possible. We went on a Friday and the lines and crowds were much better.

Universal Studios is a sure bet for fun and entertainment for all ages. There are rides from easy to thrilling and stage and street shows. They even have a make up / horror show that's wonderful. The new Harry Potter additions are a sure hit as well and Gringotts is well worth the wait in line. Enjoy your day! !

Visited the two parks four times during our two week stay. Queues were well handled and airconditioned. Staff were always so pleasant and the parks were spotless. Don't try to stay all day it's too tiring. Go for it opening one day to catch all the rides before it gets too busy. Next time go about 4pm. Crowds start dying down about 5ish so you can still get on rides without too much queuing and you get to see the fireworks at night. Buy the refillable cups. Saves so much money and if you bring them back the next time you visit they can be reactivated for even less money. Bargain. Also you can fill them up every ten minutes from one of the machines round the park. Water is free from these machines if you prefer to take your own bottle. All in all two wonderful parks with great shows and rides. Be prepared to have to use one of the drying machines if you go on the water rides though you do get soaked. Lol. The Mummy and the Hogwarts Express are a must.

A big group of have just been here & we love the place. Something for all kids, big & small. So much to see & do. Kids had a awesome day. We'll be back again in a few days. Can't wait to go on the Jurassic Park ride.

This was my first trip to a Universal park in at least 15 years. Much has changed. I was very happy with the ride selection they have here now. More than I thought. The Harry Potter section is very well done. Make sure you stop here first thing in the morning to avoid long waits at Escape from Gringotts. Men in Black is outdated but still fun, especially if you have kids. Simpsons ride is alright but not worth a long wait. Transformers is exactly like Spiderman at Islands of Adventure, but not as good in my opinion. E.T. is a very old ride, but still enjoyable if the line is short. Twister has also been around for a long time, and if you have never seen it, then it's cool to check out. Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit does not really fit into the parks theme at all. It really feels out of place, but its a decent coaster. I wouldn't wait too long for this attraction. The best ride in the park by far is The Mummy. Great special fx and a great coaster. Definitely worth the wait.  If you want to visit this park, September is a great time to do it. Very light crowds. You could easily knock out the whole park in half a day and head to Islands of Adventure and do the same. Will be coming back in the near future for sure!
Great park. Had fun with the family. Would definitely recommend the park. Of course it gets a little expensive staying a few days, but it is vacation.

First and foremost. The park is definetely worth the visit. The attractions and themes are well done. The employees are very friendly and happy to help. That being said, both universal studios and island of adventure could easily be considered one park. The only real distinction is the majoriety of rides in the studios are motion simulation. With a small mixing of actual rides throughout. The parks are traversed by the hogwarts express, which is in effect a ride. With a wait. Or by simply walking out either front gates and walking roughly 3 minutes to the other gate...  We did purchase both the park to park pass and the express pass. The express pass is well worth the extra $.  Ultimately i would advise people to visit both parks, however 2 days is plenty of time to see both. Additionally i found it somewhat aggrivating that the studios park closes at 5 pm to later re open for the 25 nights of horror. Which costs an additional fee starting at approx. 50 dollars , if you paid for the full day admission already....  In my opinion they should discount the full day passes, since in effect they are closing the park roughly 1/4 of the normal hours. And making an additional charge for the nightly visitors. ( kind of double dipping!) Of course they wont, but i am entitled to my opinion.

What a great park!!! The park is wonderful during the day and the Halloween Horror Night is amazing. I never could have imagined a more "thrill" seeking attraction. The horror houses are awesome and you still have access to most of the main rides and Harry Potter. The park closes at 5PM most nights during October (Wed-Sun) then reopens at 6:30 for the Halloween Night and stays open to 1AM or 2AM. My advice would be to try to purchase a Express Pass for both the park and the Horror Night. We stayed at the Hard Rock so we received a complimentary Express Pass for the day. If you want to do the Halloween Horror nights, my advice would be to purchase a Express Pass. If you do not purchase one, then you need to arrive to the park at 6:30 and you can probably make it through 3 or 4 houses only.
We went in the evening and we're in a cordoned off section for the group that include the Bob Marley bar. Definitely worth a visit if you're a Bob Marley fan.

Have been to Halloween Horror nights before and this recent trip was the best! Haunted house were scary and fun, lines moved fast (we had the fast pass), costumes were amazing, overall great trip! I will go back next year!

We don't do roller coasters so managed to do almost everything we wanted in one day. Check when park closes as it closed early for Horror nights and made us miss a few things. Longest line was for Minions. It was broke first thing in the morning and 45 min. wait later in the day. Harry Potter area was crowded but did the ride 3 times and tried the overpriced frozen butter beer. I was disappointed in the Hogwarts Express. it was more transportation then ride. Pay attention to the inner and outer windows to not miss anything.

We'd been wanting to try this for years and finally went for it. Glad we did, as it was a lot of fun.  We read up on how to avoid the crowds, as it gets incredibly crowded. (Getting in early was the trick for us.) If you don't have a game plan, you won't see many haunted houses, as the lines pretty quickly get to 60+ minutes. If money isn't a concern, get an express pass and you won't have to worry too much about the lines.  While the haunted houses were pretty cool, they weren't all that scary. They would have been much scarier, if we didn't have people directly in front and behind us. Remember, the saying "safety in numbers"... Universal could improve this by pacing the people entering the haunted house.  It would help for Universal to post ratings of the various haunted houses like other attractions I've been to do, and have at least one "It's Scary as Hell" haunted house.  We actually really enjoyed just walking the streets and going thru the various "scare zones". These were almost as scary as the haunted houses.  Of the two shows they had this year, Bill & Ted's was definitely our favorite (more so than the Carnage show).  Between the haunted houses, scare zones, and shows it was a really good time and worth the money.
Epcot is amazing with some great rides, but all the countries around the world showcase are really good. Fun for all ages.

They can really do theme parks here. The set up catered for everyone. Loved the valet parking no queues and no finding your car afterwards. We really needed the two days to experience it all. We would have missed so much if we didn't. Harry Potter world was exceptional. The ride on the Hogwarts Express is a must. This really is fun for all the family with so much you just would not think possible. Big thumbs up from us.

There was a lot to see but not a lot to do. It was a good break from running around all day I did the whole park in half a day. A good thing I had gotten coupons for the entrance free because I first whent to see timesharing condos so if you go listen to them for thirty min you can get into parks for free !!!

First things first, the park is just amazing. You will be blown away with all the rides, the fun shows and the magic you feel by visiting this park.  Make sure to check out the opening times of your day of visit, as the change depening on the season and the day of the week.  I personally felt a bit dissapointed coming back to Universal after being there 3 times in the past. Mainly because of the prices. Entree free is over 100usd, parking is 20usd, having a picture taken with one of the characters (sold at 29usd)... avg burger price range is 12-15usd.  That would be all not so bad, but the rides have not changed much over the years. Out of Back to the Future became the Simpons Ride. Out of the Jetsons became Minions... and so on.  Also, if you want to explore the full Harry Potter rides, you need access to both Universal parks, which is barely impossible doing all in 1 day... so you would need a 2 day, 2 park access pass.

October. School in the US is in session, its not spring break, its not a major holiday, or summer vacation. Theme parks should be wide open, right? Nope. None the less, Universal, despite the lines, is a blast. Rides are great. The Halloween horror nights special event is outstanding. Wear your walking shoes, go ahead and pony up for the speed pass, it will be worth it. Particularly check out the Harry Potter world exhibits(one on each side of the park.) For food, got to Mythos in Islands of Adventure. There is a reason its been voted best theme park food last 6 years in a row. The grilled salmon I had (yes, in a theme park!) would not have been out of place in the fine dining establishment of your choice. For drinks, go to the Leaky Cauldron in the Diagon Alley area of Universal. Think 300 year old English pub, cold pints, and pub grub.

Universal Studios Orlando was so much fun! Easy to get in and the Expess Pass was great as we never waited any longer than 30 minutes for any ride and those rides were The Simpsons and Shrek. The Simpsons was the most surprising ride to us; my sister got a tad woozy, the only experience that created such uneasiness. Plenty of food options digging the turkey legs, churros etc. We loved the following five experiences: The Minions, The Mummy, Rip Ride Rocket, Transformers and Harry Potter. So much fun and well designed as it was easy walking and orderly picking your route. The Makeup Show was fun and gave you a break.  Such a great day. Enjoy Universal Studios Orlando!

I've been to Universal Studios many times. Every time that I go is better than the last time. I find the rides to be much more fun and exciting than they are at Disney. It's also less expensive. Since it's much smaller than Disney, it's easier to get around with kids, or people with disabilities.  The staff members are so much fun. They aren't required to be overly polite like they are at Disney, so they poke fun at guests and at their competitor. They crack me up!  The parks are meticulously clean and safe. The restaurants at City Walk are great and cater to all tastes. Dueling pianos at night at Pat O'Brien's should not be missed! So much fun.  There's so much to do, including shows. Blue Man Group is my favorite. Have fun!
we had a very good day out here!! So much to see and do!! We really enjoyed the Harry Potter Ride and Men In Black and the queue was not bad at all!!

5 seniors, with 2 using wheelchairs, enjoyed their trip here. Universal has done a top notch job with all of the attractions. The express pass was worth the money. We got to go to very short lines, saving us much time. We allowed for 2 days, and it was just the right amount of time. The first day we did both Harry Potter sections, and the 2nd day we did Universal Studios. The Island of Adventure is more geared towards children. If you want to cover that park as well, I'd suggest a 3 day park-to-park pass with express passes. Expensive, but worth it for a better experience and to maximize your time for all there is to do.
I enjoyed very much the park, I went to Harry Poter word by train it was amazing., I became a Miniom I loved it all so much.
love the rides, express pass is worth it always. it's expensive as hell for everything but thats a no-brainer because its a theme park

It was a very nice park with the best simulators! The problem is that you must pay to put your sutff in lockers for some attractions and I don't felt secure by doing this (due one locker have opened for me and it already contain someone stuff. I close it fast when I saw what happened and it was scary!).

We went with my 8 year old and spent a decent amount of money to get in. Did not get the fast pass and regret that we did not. We played hurry up and wait ALL DAY! For food and rides. The waiting in lines was enough to ruin your day. I will go back but will save up money and buy the fast pass for sure!!

We took our family, including our 9 year old grandson, to Universal Studios. He loved the Harry Potter village. However there was not much in the park for adults unless you like the very high roller coasters.Almost everything seemed to be geared to children. Also, there was very little seating around the rides so if you were waiting for someone to get off from the ride, it was hard to find a place to sit. Having been to Universal Studios in California years ago and we loved it, we were very disappointed in Universal Studios in Orland.

Well worth the cost of admission to be scared silly! Considering most haunted houses these days are $10 and up, the $58 for high caliber frights, sights, and scares was well worth it as only Universal studios can muster! I will be back for more tricks and treats next year!

This was our first visit to Universals parks. Rides times were signifigantly less than Disneyland's due to the ride sizing. Prices on souviners are absolutely outrageous and fr more expensive than Disney, this is not only gouging the consumer, but quite classless. Rides were all working, Simpsons ride has the longest wait. Rides here are more motion simulation 3D style, then the Disney style, both are good, just different. Not enough proper shopping if that is your think, lots of junk. Overall nice park with some different rides to excite. Most rides are fast moving, so if this bothers you, this isn't the park for you
This was yet another INCREDIBLE Halloween Horror Night put on by Universal, already looking forward to next years

We went to the Halloween Horror Night and it did not disappoint. The shows and haunted houses were very well done and very scary. If you are in Orlando at the right time of year put this on your "things to do" list

this park was fun for the thrill seekers and the young ones. it had lots of shows and rides. the 3D rides were the best and the food was fairly good. the park has 2 parts one has lots of thrill rides (island adventures part) so check the height requirements before planning to go. holloween is not a good time for little ones because universal really does it up in a scary way.

Myself and three other family members went to a Halloween Horror night on a Sunday in October. The theme park was decorated brilliantly, it was very realistic and very scary. I have to be honest though that I was very disappointed that we only got to do one of the haunted houses as all of them were at least a 2 hour wait. It was so busy. We looked into doing fast track but it's $100 per person on top of the $100 for the theme park ticket, it's a very expensive option!! I also witnessed children as young as 5 coming out of the haunted houses with their parents, crying in sheer terror. Leaflets state recommended ages for this event is minimum 13. It is ultimately the parents responsibility but I feel their should be a no kids allowed policy for the haunted houses. All in all Universal is one of my favourite theme parks and I would go back to Halloween Horror but probably with the view of not getting the full experience.

We decided to take our kids to Disney World Orlando at an age where they would remember it (ages 10 and 11). We missed the magical period people! Kids were not interested in Disney - bored with the baby rides - and 80 minute lines. We popped over to Universal Studios! What a breath of fresh air! We LOVED Universal Studios. The rides were more suited to tween kiddos and adults. It was somewhat of a rainy day (which I highly recommend going on rainy days) as it scared all the crowds away. We didn't have to wait in line more than 30 seconds, and got right back on the rides again. The new Harry Potter ride was amazing - even for 45 yr old parents. We rode it so much, the 3d effects were great, we almost barfed! Yes peeps, IT - WAS - AWESOME! If your looking to get away from the crowds of Disney world, and more grown up rides, I would most definitely recommend Universal Studios in FL!

So we are glad we went, we did feel like we got to sink into "real" Harry Potter world and had a great time sharing that with each other and our photos are life long keepers.  BUT with the exception of some great employees, what a horrid place. Nothing interested us except HP World. It cost so much money to do both parks, but we finally bite the bullet and decided to ignore that money has value. The parks themselves were brutal on us, no places to sit and except the Hogwarts express, no real transportation between attractions.  Also, technically things were brilliant except the sound quality was so bad EVERYWHERE that we could never really follow what was going on. They might as well not have had plots. And they know where your head is going to be down to the inch on those rides, but we still couldn't understand any but about one out of 10 words.  But bottom line, it all worked just well enough to bring delight to me and my 80 year old potter-head Mom. (Mom is not a roller coaster fan. She did both rides, loved Gringotts but thought Hogwarts was a little much but was glad she did it anyway. The lack of seating around the park was really punishing on her though.)

Universal Studios and Universal Islands of Adventure is a must if you visit Orlando anytime of the year. This review is for the Universal Studios though !!  We were a group of 4, all in late 20's and we purchased a 2 day park to park ticket, which I think is sufficient to cover both the parks. If you have kids / elderly people, maybe you'll have to rush if you take 2 day ticket. Take express pass if you want to jump to the front of line (It costs roughly $70 per person). We skipped small rides and kids section to cover famous rides of both the parks.  Despicable Me Minion Mayhem, Revenge of the Mummy, Harry Potters ride, Shrek 4D show, The Simpsons ride, Transformers 3D ride, Rockit ride are must. These are the best rides / shows in this park. MEN IN BLACK Alien Attack is an interactive ride. If you have a park to park pass, you must take the Hogwarts Express train that connects Universal Studios to the Universal Island of Adventures.  There are wait times for most of the famous rides. Over the weekends, the wait times will be even more. So, carry ample liquids to keep yourself hydrated and wear comfortable clothes. Be sure to check the weather. Rain ponchos and umbrellas are available for sale inside the park. If it rains, some of the rides like Rock It may be closed. I suggest not to carry big cameras and big bags as it may make you slow throughout the park. Some rides don't allow you to carry bags or loose articles on you, but there are some places where you can rent lockers free for an hour to store your bags.  Small amounts of food is allowed inside the parks. So, take your favorite food to avoid spending time in lines to buy food inside the park.
This attraction is a movie theme park ride adventure! The rides are based off universal films! Nice!

Great park for kids older than 7. Most rides are 4D video. Not many characters about. Get the express pass, otherwise you will just stand in queues all day. Restaurants were much better than at Disney.

So I just realised I got my review mixed up with Island of Adventures lol, any who they are both amazing. Transformers was wicked, Halloween Horror Nights was crazy scary. Always have to visit this park everytime we come here.

We went to Universal Studio Labor Day week. My family and I had a wonderful time. The rides were unbelievable. The attractions especially Harry Potter action. I thought I was really in England. Universal studio was a perfect theme park for the entire family

We had a great day in the park, and have visited this and many other parks in the area over many years. The different areas are well designed and it is great fun exploring. Unfortunately we witnessed a few issues with people behaving badly and with no respect for other guests and families. Security sorted them on each occasion, but we have never witnessed this anywhere else.

Car parking is expensive . $20 for general parking or $25 for preferred parking. I think the preferred parking to closer to the park. It took about 5 mins to walk to the park for general parking. We did Universal Studio first. The park was amazing and the atmosphere electric. We went on all the rides. Most of them were simulator rides. The mummy ride was great. It was a rollercoaster, but not too extreme. The Simpsons and The MInions ride were the best. Also the Transformer ride was brilliant. The only ride that we weren't impressed with was The Terminator. They kept you in a room which was quite crammed and warm for about 20 mins, as a woman talks to you and then you watch a short film. You are then led into another room where you sit and watch a show. I wasn't very impressed. There were lots of eating places and we ate in the American Diner which was good. A disappointment that the little jukeboxes on the tables never worked. We went in November so the park wasn't very busy and the rides were only half and hour wait. We found that when we went back in an afternoon the ride times were a lot shorter. Some of the rides you only waited 5 mins. So we only went back in the afternoons. With the parking, if you decide to leave the park and go back later in the day, you don't have to pay again. If you buy bottled water in the park, you can use the filling stations around the park to refill your bottle which saves you money. Some of the rides you have to put your bags in lockers. The first 50 mins are free,after that it's $5. It took us about 7 hours to get round the park. Be prepared to walk loads !!

While we went mostly for me to check out DIagon Alley, the newest addition to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, the park is fun to have as part of the two park pass. I wouldn't recommend only doing one park. While one of the reasons to do so is so you can take the Hogwarts Express between the parks (which is handy even if you're not into Harry Potter), there isn't quite enough in either park to really occupy. Universal is relying too heavily on the 3D rides. They're an interesting experience, but they aren't as fun as traditional rides. My husband and I weren't fond of them as the disconnect between what you're seeing and what you're feeling caused some discontent, but as motorcycle riders, we may be more sensitive to it.  The Rip Ride Rock-it was a blast of a roller coaster. Definitely don't pass it up if you like thrill rides. It starts with a vertical climb and then you drop down the other side going 60+ mph. It was so much fun.  Diagon Alley was so immersive, it made the rest of the park pale by comparison. While there is only one ride (Escape from Gringotts) it's fun to explore the area. There are lots of shops to go in and explore. It feels like you're really there which for fans is cool, but then when you explore the rest of the park, like Simpson's town, it just doesn't feel as put together. They seem to be overhauling a lot though, so in the coming years, that may not be as pronounced.

My husband loved it. We loved Jurassic Park and had pics taken with a dinosaur who tried to eat my hat lol. The whole Harry Potter part of the park was wonderful, from the train ride both ways, Gringott's bank ride, the roller coasters, and the interactive wand experience. My husband and I enjoyed universal much more than Disney. Wait times were fairly reasonable.

It is a great place for families especially with children. It is worth the money and time to come here. We enjoyed everything there. The food is delicious. The staff was very helpful. Plenty of things to do and places to eat for everyone's needs.

Plenty of rides - Revenge of the Mummy, etc Shows to entertain you. If you go around Halloween buy the frequent pass as it is not to be missed. Being chased by a clown/zombie brandishing a chainsaw is truly terrifying and fun too!
I have to say I loved the holly wood rocket and the building where u make a hilarious movie commercials I highly recommend it:-)
went with my 3 daughters. we had an absolute blast. we did the 2 parks for 2 days pass and went back and forth between Universal and Island of adventure. magical.

I love this place, and with the opening of Diagon Alley, I love it even more. This year I went to Halloween Horror nights and I thought it was great. Pretty scary, but not quite as scary as some of the people who get really into that kind of thing! I have always had nothing but the best experiences with the staff, and even during really busy times I don't feel like the waits are that long. I know people complain about wait times, but I always feel like Disney's are so much worse. My favorite rides are The Mummy and Escape from Gringotts. Always a great time.

Mini vacation with sister and niece. Loved the Simpsons and the Mummy rides! Enjoyed the park generally. Did a lot of shopping for Christmas. Many different places to eat Close to 3 different major hotels with water taxi service

This is a place specifically designed for movie fans/fanatics. Very limited rides (for adults), but it is a shoppers paradise. In fact 70 percent of the entire attraction is themed shopping; Simpson, Harry Potter, to Men In Black. I am sorry to say but this attraction left me wanting something else.

We stayed at the hard rock and got in early and had a free fast lane pass. Plan this park carefully and do the things before the lines start. Also eat before you go as it is a bit pricy to eat. Bigearinc.com
This park wasn't to bad. It has a ton of 3D rides. (Which I'm not able to do often) 😲 But nevertheless I got a kick out of some of them.

What a place to be..completely fun filled & entertaining..thanks to the day we selected..hardly crowded so we were able to cover everything without an express pass..very well managed..hospitable & friendly staff..I have been to the one in Singapore but this one is a charm on its own..a must do place for people of all ages if visiting orlando..very clean and have enough shops for eateries..the Macys parade was fun..revisiting childhood..Harry potter ranks the top amongst all the rides seconded by Revenge of the Mummy..They have this wonderful system of providing free lockers for a duration depending on the crowd at the rides..Keep up the good work guys..

We had our first trip to Universal Studios Orlando December 2015. We only did the one park, Universal Studios. We did not go to Islands of Adventure. So, ~$100/person to get into the park. The park was at full capacity rather quickly and the lines came out of no where, so we decided to buy the express passes. $180 more/person on top of the admission already paid! We still had to wait in line, but it cut the wait time by 50%. The express pass is not valid on any of the Harry Potter attractions - we waited 2.5 hours to go on the Harry Potter ride (it was a great ride though). I highly suggest you get to the park at open, and go straight to the Harry Potter attraction in the back of the park to avoid a very long wait time. We rode a few of the rides twice, thanks to the express pass. Without it, I'm not sure we would have even been able to get on everything once. The merchandise was rather disappointing as there wasn't much that actually said "Universal Studios" on it other than some plain looking shirts or hats. Many of the shirts looked like something we could have bought at Walmart. We had forgot our Universal gift cards in our hotel room, but I had pictures of the back of the cards with the numbers on them, but we still couldn't use them as the clerks said they had to have the physical card. One gift shop was able to type the numbers in successfully, but the others would not even try. So, I have a lot of money in gift cards that I guess we'll be using online instead. You are not allowed cameras on any of the rides unlike Disney who is not real strict about gopros, phones, etc on the rides. Several of the attractions, you had to lock all your belongings (purses, bookbags, phones) in a free locker. The lines for the lockers were crazy as there's only so many and everyone is trying to get one. I can understand the safety concerns, but I had a small, flat crossbody purse that I couldn't take on the rides - had to be locked in the locker. Waiting in lines for the lockers throughout the day to get in to rent a locker and then get back in to get the stuff back out took way more time that I would have liked.

Except from the Terminator which I highly recommend skipping, there are a lot of great rides at this park. The best ride in my opinion is Transformers. Universal does a great job with placing characters around the park too including a huge rendition of Optimus Prime. The night time light show is so-so in my opinion, but if your still at the park at night enjoying rides its worth staying for.

We were nervous about going during Christmas week - but figured out some tips to help in the future. #1 - go early. We got there about 930 each day (2 day passes) and left by 3pm on Thursday & Friday . The wait times were no problem at all before noon - in fact only waited 30 minutes at the longest. However, we noted via the phone app wait times that earlier in the week (Monday & Tuesday) the wait times were way over 120 minutes in the afternoons. Food is extremely expensive ($50 for two) - we took our lunch the second day. Simply wandering around Diagon Alley was extremely fun. The detail in the design is amazing. Enjoyed other parts of Universal as well - especially MIB, NY, etc. A wonderful park!

We flew through this park from ride to ride where we waited and waited. And then waited some more. Express passes are a must in this park. The food is super expensive.  We stayed on site and got in early which helped but only for one ride. The rides were really well done. Everything was nice and clean. Plenty of bathrooms. Most rides are covered so rain is less of an issue.

If you are a big Harry Potter fan probably a must do. If your kids are younger than about 13 I wouldn't come here. Not enough for the younger kids for the price. Few young kids were here so most have figured this out. For the roller coasters all purses and backpacks need to be put in rental lockers. System is a disaster, not enough of them and spaces too tight where they are located. Another reason not to bring preteens, recommend traveling light with no bags. Which also means shop after the rides. Overall, I thought it was fairly well done, comparable to Disney. Comes down to the movies and characters you like. Glad I saw it, but would not go back. I have done Disney World twice and Disneyland once. Not inclined to go back to those again either for what it's worth. All too crowded. Went with my wife and son and daughter who were on college break. Came down to run the Disney Marathon the kids wanted to come. All depends on your perspective on crowds and theme parks. If Disney is the gold standard, Universal was much closer than I would have thought in quality and cleanliness. Hard to actually differentiate unless being very particular. If you just want to ride roller coasters, go to Cedar Point, Ohio in the summer.

Family of 9 travelling from the UK - 8 Adults 1 child. I have visited this park several times over the past 25 years during the christmas holiday period and I have never seen a park so busy with ridiculous wait times for all attractions. Harry Potter world looked great from what we managed to see of it amongst all the crowds. Literally could not walk yet alone attempt to push a stroller. Staff not able to control lines, we left after just one hour. Do not waste money unless going off peak!

After reading multiple Trip Advisor reviews to try to figure out how to Navigate the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, I'd like to do my part, having just visited.  First off, they have taken a page out of Disney's book, and separated the Harry Potter attractions into two different "lands," - with two separate admission prices. If you are bothering to go all the way out there, just suck it up and buy the "park hopper," or whatever they call it. At least this allows you to ride the Hogwarts Express train from one land to the other.  Do not, I repeat, do NOT plan to visit Universal Studios the week after Christmas and before New Year's. My husband and I went on December 29th, which was the busiest day of the year for them, and it completely ruined my experience. The park was in complete chaos - we had to wait in a line (that was impossible to find), to obtain a ticket just to GET IN to the Islands of Adventure. If you are traveling without children, you can absolutely do everything in both lands in one day - assuming you heed my warning and attend during a non-peak day.  Here is something I didn't read anywhere - a good portion of the attractions at Universal rely on screens (simulators) to provide the thrills for the consumers. My husband and I went immediately to the " Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey" ride, because we heard it was the best in the park. I'd say that 60% of this ride involves the passenger watching a screen, as if you're flying behind Harry Potter on his journey, all the while being jostled in the strapped-in seat. My husband ran off the ride to the nearest trash can - the only thing that prevented him from throwing up was the fact that he hadn't eaten anything yet that day. We were both so motion sick afterward that it took us nearly 4 hours to recover.  Be warned that if you are sensitive to motion sickness, a lot of the attractions with simulators will be difficult for you, so ask ahead of time before waiting in a line.  The last tip I will give is that some of the rides (definitely "Forbidden Journey" and "Escape from Gringotts") require riders to place all of their belongings into lockers, which are secured by scanning your index finger. These lockers are free for up to two hours - it was nice for us to walk around, unencumbered, for a time, before going back and getting our belongings out of the locker.  If you are in the Orlando area, I'd highly recommend a visit to the Kennedy Space Center - it was inspiring.

We visited on January 3, hoping for somewhat reduced crowds versus the holidays. Unfortunately, the crowds were really bad. Any Harry Potter attraction was so crowded that it was uncomfortable to be there. We bought an express ticket (for about $100 extra per ticket) and were disappointed to find that it was useless on any of the Harry Potter rides, and of limited usefullness on a lot of other rides.  Having said that, some of their rides/attractions were really incredible. The Hogwart's Express was disappointing, but the Hogwart's castle ride was the closest thing to actually participating in a Quidich match I could imagine. The Spiderman 3D ride is extremely realistic and immersive. However, the Transformer 3D ride is an exact copy (with different visuals)! Go to one, but not both. We rode two coasters. The Harry Potter dragon roller coaster was our favorite. We rode it twice - once in the front seat and once in the middle. I highly recommend waiting a few extra minutes to get the front seat, because otherwise all you can see is the back of the person in front of you.

Universal studios is worth visiting if it's your first time. We bought the tickets to Universal Studios and the adjacent theme parks for 2 days, express pass for a day and wet N Wild for 14 days - paid as package online for almost $1K AUD for 2 people. Expensive yes as we went on Christmas break and the lines to get into the rides is ridiculous. We bought the express pass to by-pass the queue but there's still line regardless, so buying express pass is sort of a moot point. Better I think to go on off season - cheaper and less lines. If you are keen on still wanting to go to theme parks, buy your tickets when you get there as it's cheaper than buying from Australia online. Most of the places in Orlando offers timeshare presentation and included in a much lower rate tickets to theme parks. If you don't have kids or keen to do this, you can get the tickets cheaper. Wet N wild pass for 14 days is worth it but they will be closing the park as it's been bought by Universal to be converted to another waterworks theme park; best to wait after June 2016. There are other new rides being completed as it seems to us that there's more food stalls than rides in the park. Paying for$99 AUD for fun pass for Seaworld is also expensive. Not sure if this is because we went during Christmas break. If you are going on cruise to Bahamas, best to buy food and other entertainment outside the package they're offering as it'll work out to be cheaper but planning ahead is required.

We visited Universal and bought a 3 day pass that allowed us to park hop. We probably only needed 2 days as we didn't go on many rides and also the parks were not too busy. The busiest ride seemed to be the Despicable me ride with wait times up to 110 minutes while we were there.  Springfield was my favourite because you can go into the Kwik-E-Mart to buy gifts and souvenirs; note this is not set out as the 'real' Kwik-E-Mart. I enjoyed ordering lunch from Krusty Burger and eating it in Moe's Tavern, where you can buy Duff and see Barney! Oh and buy a big pink if you are hungry, it's the donut Lard boy holds and is delicious.  The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was amazing. We've been to the Universal in Japan which is much the same as Hogsmead here. However, the Hogswart Express was MAGICAL (haha!) and lots of fun. Young and old were so excited lining up. Diagon Alley was really cool and not in Japan so that was extra fun for us.  In my opinion, the best thing about The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is the interactive wands they can be purchased. They are not cheap at about $50 each but you can choose any characters wand and walk around the park casting spells. If you do it correctly, you can see the magic unfold! (If you go to Ollivanders, you may be chosen and given a free wand)  The Macy's parade was on when we visited. It was gorgeous. The blimps were huge and the show was very colourful. Santa even lit up the lights on the Christmas tree when he passed it.  There are lots of characters to take photos with like in most theme parks. The lines were longish and the staff would tell you if characters had to leave and told you when they'd be back. Most people seemed happy to wait for characters to come back.  Lots of see, lots to do, lots of fun!
The details in Diagon Alley are totally amazing. Lots of shops and interactive things to do with wonderful people working there.

Horrible place, dirty nasty! The day we were there you couldn't get anywhere...too many people! The wait times for rides were 3 hours long. If there would have been an emergency, people would have been trampled and emergency people would not have been able to get in. Hogsmeade area was way to busy couldn't see anything or do anything wall to wall people. Terrible place will not go back again!!

Went in October 2004 as this was the last time I was in America. The rides and everything about universal studios is out of this world!! The staff were very friendly, plenty to see and do for all ages. Will definitely visit next time I go to USA! 💗
Diagon Alley was such a special place. It was exactly like the movie and so fun to walk through. I highly recommend visiting if you are an HP fan.
Universal studios was an amazing theme park for all ages. The city walk attached made for a great ending to the night as well, i would recommend this for 21+.

Me and my partner cannot stay away - We have visited the park 6 years in a row from 2009-2014 and it just gets better and better. There is so much to do in the park. It's clean and well kept. Food is great with loads of places to eat - The Irish restaurant is fab! Overall fantastic experience - I personally believe it's better than Disney :) Island of adventures if equally as spectacular and now you can get the Hogwarts express across from one park to the other - well - mind blowing :)

I absolutely love Universal Studios. I am a big film buff so as soon as I walked up to the gates and could hear Back to the future soundtrack I started to tingle. It's full of Nostalgia and great rides. Go early and stay late and see everything because there's so much OR if you have unlimited access through your stay .. All the better.  We stayed on international drive twice and it's really short taxi ride away if you don't like to be stuck to bus schedules.  Overall I love this place it's great!

Universal is by far my favorite Florida park. The attractions are fun and interactive and the park is very clean with friendly, helpful staff. We stayed at the hard rock hotel and upgraded to fast passes which I highly recommend.

We were here last year and enjoyed ourselves immensely. We came back this year and enjoyed it every bit as much. It is ridiculously expensive but the fast pass was worth it. I personally hate waiting in line for anything and waiting at both Harry Potter worlds and for the Hogwarts express was about enough for me. None of these are included with a fast pass. Everything else in the park is however. The Simpsons ride was hilarious and the Mummy was very surprising. Can't comment on the roller coasters etc as that is too much for me! Just wish there was better food in any of the venues. Not a great place to eat but still a must see in Orlando!

Visited both parks and got exactly what i expected. -Up to date entertainment, apart from a few rides (like Men in Black which was absolutely awfull). I still like the California park better, because of the actual tour through genuine movie-sets, like the clocktover of Hill Valley :)
It has been a few years since we were there but I was surprised how much it had changed. They have a Harry Potter section that is a must see!!

I recently moved to Florida and just got around to visiting universal. I adore it. If you're a Transformers and Harry Potter geek like me, you must go! The parade is nice and there's the Fear Factor show live. There's so much more fun stuff going on in the parks, go on and make the trip!

The last time we came to Orlando was 15 years ago and my kids were 10 and 12. They weren't very impressed with Universal Studios and they absolutely loved Disney. We decided to go to Universal Studios again with the 14 day unlimited ticket and we did not regret it. The rides at Universal cater for the older generations as opposed to kiddies and the Wizarding World of Harry Potter is just amazing. (as is the Simpsons area). Would definitely recommend.

This is a great park. And if you only have one day to visit a park I highly suggest this one. Like most parks unfortunately the food prices are outrageous. Only complaint I have are the people who are in groups going into the single rider line. Making the line a lot of times just as long as the main line. My favorite rides were escape from gringotts, the mummy and transformers. Though most of the rides were great. I would definitely come back here.

We always get the 2-day / 2-park pass when we go to Orlando and we've been going back to Universal for almost 20 years. Now our kids are teens and we all love it more than Disney. My son is a huge Jurassic Park and Harry Potter fan. Here is the good and bad: Bad: You will pay $20 for parking, it will be 1-2 hours from the time you park, get through security, walk to the park, wait for the entry where thy use a finger print reader that doesn't work, then stand on line for your first ride. Very frustrating. Good: The rides are awesome, it is a much more adult place than Disney and the rides are more thrilling. Universal pays attention to intricate details inside the rides so you are amazed by the sets while you wait online. Tips: Use single rider lines if you have older kids (and no kids) and don't mind splitting up. That could mean the difference between a 60 minute or 10 minute wait. You'll still get on and off at the same time. Don't come with a backpack or bag. Seriously, why do people need so much stuff? It will only burden you - security will take longer and you will often have to stop at a locker to check your bag before getting on rides. Get the Butterbeer in any Harry Potter area. The frozen kind is delicious in the Summer, the hot kind is great on the rare occasion that it's cold in Orlando - it's like melted butterscotch.

We went to see the Harry Potter attractions. While the rides were good, in a way they were the same: 3D, move to another location, see another scenario. We enjoyed walking around the sites supporting the Harry Potter theme; nicely done. For off season on a Saturday we were surprise at the wait times of 50 minutes even at 9am in the morning. We did try using the singles line once and had a 25 minute wait instead. Pricey because to see all the Harry Potter stuff you have to get admission to 2 parks. There were local places or AAA that got us a better price than at the park.

Me and my boyfriend went here because I'm really excited for him to try the Transformers ride 3D. The rides were awesome since Universal offers more rides in 3D making the experience way better. I just hope that the park is bigger. Even though I know that the second park Island of Adventure is just beside the main park I still feel that Universal Studios should offer a bigger size theme park to make the park fee worth it.

Being a Harry Potter fan I suppose it is to be expected that I would award 5* for this attraction, but really it's fantastic.... With one exception... Paint the Hogwarts express a brighter red! Eating in this park is far superior to that of any Disney park. I particularly appreciated ordering food, then being shown to a table and my very acceptable food being brought to me. Train ride between parks is amazing. I suggest dressing up so as not to look too much like the muggles we are.
We love going to both of these parks. Going to both is a lot of fun. Two days is plenty of time to go. Depending on your energy level.

Universal Studios was a nice outing. They are constantly updating the attraction to make it more up to date, and they need to! As my group of adults and I walked through some of the attractions I couldn't help wonder if today's kids had any idea of who some of the characters even were (Dagwood? Popeye? Really?). But the Superheroes were up to date (Transformers, Hulk and such). We really enjoyed the live animal attraction (dog actors). The rides using 3D were great. Non-3D rides now pale in comparison! If you have a chance to get a skip-the-line pass, do it.

BUT... have deep pockets. You are gouged at every corner. From my 60 dollar lunch of burgers dogs and dry fries and gross pops, for 2 people, to my 13 dollar hot dog, to 6.00 popcorn, this place is engineered for one thing only. To seperate your money from your purse or wallet. SOOO expensive. tickets 500 busks, hotel 700 a night, dinners, around 200 a couple for a sit down nice meal, express passes 120.00 a day. And they are not express. Your only promise is "half the time of the regular line" So if the regular lines wait is 3 hours, your 120.00 passes will cut that down to 1 1/2 hours, which no one monitors. One time, I can't recall the ride, we walked past a family in the regular line to get to Express, and I happenned to recall them, they got on before we did in Express. These big theme parks are way more expensive than they should be. Also they should be limitied to how many people they can allow in the park. On our second day, we were in line to get in for over an hour and a half. Thats a good part of your day. It's off the bucket list, would never go again.

I had not visited Universal Studios-Orlando in quite a few years and was surprised at the amount of growth that the park had accomplished. I only allotted 1-day to visit the park and found that it was impossible to experience all that the park had to offer in that time period. I think that a 3-day visit would be a better plan. The Harry Potter sections of the park are fascinating (not just for children). There is much in the park to attract adults. The location of the restaurants outside of the main entrance to the park is an example of the genius the was used in constructing this facility. Although I am not a great Theme Park fan, I do plan to go back to the park sooner than later in order to experience all that the park has to offer.

Great day out for all the family! Lots of rides and things to see. There is something for everyone here regardless of your age. Water rides are great fun long as you don't mind walking around wet for a few hours
The ticket price was confusing on-line and the staff at the ticket counters took forever and seemed to be car salesmen. Long waits and unfriendly staff. Would not return or recommend to anyone.

The positives: Transformers - brilliant! The so-so's: Terminator - dated. The negatives........ Most things else!  We wanted to go on The Simpsons ride, but a queue of 75 minutes ruled that out as we were only there for a day & couldn't justify so long a wait (especially when I had heard people complaining that often waits were longer than posted). Other rides also had crazily long waits..... It a all started on arrival: drove straight in having paid the $20 parking fee, objecting to paying more for higher priced parking. Walking to the entrance, we joined the queue which took 45 minutes to actually get into the park - crazy. At the ticket desk we were urged to pay another $80 each for "Express" passes - on top of the $325 entrance for both of us: we declined, thinking it was expensive enough anyway. Once inside, the queues were longer still. We talked to one family that had queued over two hours for a ride! We did several,rides during he day, but our highlights were the terrific Transformer ride & the Animal Actors show - which wuss good old fashioned fun! We lunched at one of the many burger bars - and it was terrible! We took the cold burgers & fries back to Havel them replaced with tepid ones. The burger was the cheapest, most tasteless burger I can remember enduring. The whole park seems to have sacrificed customer service for customer hard sell. Instead of gearing up to extract yet more money, I think they need to invest in actually giving people what they have paid for - and that is not queue after queue after queue! It is twenty years since I've been here, and whilst I do remember queueing it was never even remotely as horrendous as now. Would we return? Sorry - doubt it.

Universal Studios is not to be missed! We had so much fun at all of the different venues. I was very impressed with each spot, but I really loved Springfield! The afternoon parade was worth the wait. The park keeps everyone entertained for hours. Don't miss this place

My 7 year old boys loved Universal! The park was clean and the staff was great! We had our faces painted by Max at Universal Studios! He did an amazing job and we never felt rushed. He was the absolute best! We did Harry Potter and the staff couldn't be nicer. Food was really good in Diagon Alley. Stay away from the "Monster Mash" restaurant. We went there our first day and the food was terrible. Tickets and food are pricey, so be prepared to spend some serious coin. We Would go back again.

It's one of those gotcha entertainment places of course that for a family to go there like Disney, costs an arm and a leg. Was it worth the update in time. Yes. Didn't go to the water park at all. The new Minon ride would have been better with an electro magnetic push for the start. Still going thru buildings was fun. Potter area was okay unless you are a Harry Potter fan. Then it was over the top. Spent the day there and City Walk at night is breath taking.

Had fun! Very expensive! I would suggest splurging for the express pass as it drastically reduces wait times ( which were easily an hour + per ride). Transformers ride is the best!! Could use some new rides for the older crowd. But had a great time. Would definately go again.

I was so excited for Universal. I have 3 boys... 11, 9 & 6... The two oldest were definitely growing out of Disney. For what I paid.... For 2 days (got 3rd day free)... NO PARK HOPPER (that would be additional $50/ticket.... And no fast pass)... It was $900.... Add parking & food... Omg!!! AND HONESTLY... besides the Minion Ride.... That had ATLEAST a 60 min wait... The mummy roller coaster, and the Rock It roller coaster.... It was OUTDATED!!!!!!! The 3D (& 4D) technology for Shrek, Simpsons, Terminator, and Transformers is old!!!! It will be awhile before (& IF) I return. Not impressed at all.
Overpriced and most of the park is in dire need of updating. several rides were down. Wouldn't go again.

Had a wonderful time at Universal. We rode many rides loved Harry potter and The Transformer was my personal favorite.I' 61 years old and had a blast with my 5 grandkids doing rides. BY FAST PASS expensive but a must have for most rides.
top theme park with loads to do i could go on ofr ages here about how good it is but you really just have to go yourself and immerse yourself into the amazing rides and shows

OK my love for this park is only for Harry Potter lol. Im kidding... but have you noticed all the rides are the same?  The Minion Ride is a 3D motion ride, The Transformers is 3D Motion Ride, Escape from Gringots is a 3D motion ride, Spiderman at their sister park is also a 3D motion ride....notice a pattern?  Being someone that wears glasses its just annoying to have to wear this 3D glasses for a ride! And it seems that all these rides are the same lol.  I did like to walk around Diagon Alley, the stores are just too cute and my daughter got a wand that she got to play with there. My favorite is the train which we took back and forth. lol.
Great theme park for both kids and adults. Some of the rides are outdated but worth it. Mummy ride is the BEST!!

We went to buy our tickets and knowing that we might not make the other park in one day we wanted to buy a one-day, one-park pass. It was not posted on the sign board and when we asked, the gentlemen said that they don't encourage that ticket. That they want people to buy the park hopper since they have already paid 80% of the price (totally untrue - $105 vs $155). On the way in to the park American Express had a promotion going that if you sign up for a credit card you have a choice of two flex passes or two dining passes for meals, snacks, drinks, etc. We each signed up for a credit card so got free lunch, drinks, snacks and butterbeer. We also used the flex passes which was a nice feature.
We spent the majority of our time in the Harry Potter world - which was very, very crowded (the rest of the park almost seemed deserted comparatively).

Our 9 & 11 year kids prefer Islands of Adventure, but they also enjoyed Universal Studios. The Harry Potter world is impressive. Kids had lots of fun in the ball factory in Curious George section. Minions were a hit as well. I am a fan of the Simpsons so I enjoyed Springfield and all the show references.

This was our 1st visit to both Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. You can do the parks in 2 days (even on Spring Break, if you are not that "into" Harry Potter stuff). We did 3 days and saw everything and rode several rides more than once. Park was clean and staff were Excellent and helpful. Not as crowded (less people with strollers, wheelchairs & scooters) around the park compared to Disney. We did stop by the younger children's area that was practically empty - beautiful play equipment with Barney theme, Curious George, etc. The Dr. Suess area is very cool too. On the 2nd day, we noticed that any 3D rides we went on started to effect us and made us nauseous easily so we had to slow down and stick to other rides like Rollercoaster, water rides, etc. but there doesn't seem to be too many. The Harry Potter section is crowded, you have to "try" the butter beer as it's popular and sweet. Don't be scared of the long line time that is displayed as you can always head to the single rider line and get on quicker. The park has Free lockers to put your bags in during the time you are on a ride so this is a nice feature. Finding characters to get pictures are pretty easy -- I think most of them are around between 10 am and 5 pm. One of the coolest rides is in Jurassic Park area that is like a zip line, but disappointed that it's only for 54" and under unless you are with a child. I'm sure the employees are tired of telling people that as it doesn't display it as you enter near that ride. Cute Parade around 5 pm and it's not crowded so you can see it easily without fighting for spot. The park closed at 8 pm with fireworks. Nothing extravagant as it ran a bunch of clips from movies while there were a few pops of fireworks and a little bit of water fountain..if you missed this, you aren't missing much.
We like Universal a lot because we are Minion fans. Even though the park gets very busy, the Unlimited Express helps shorten ride waits. The best way to go is to get a VIP tour

I took my daughter and her friend to Orlando for two days over spring break, and Universal jacks up pricing to $166 per person, and that doesn't include FAST pass. When I tried to upgrade to fast past, they wanted another $114 per person! That's ridiculous and should be reported to the BBB or some state agency for price gouging, it was spring break, not New Year's Eve or Christmas week! spring break is about 3 weeks in March depending on what school and level, and these are middle school girls. The parks are great, and the Harry Potter ride is fun, but the Hulk is under construction and two other rides had malfunctions and were out for more than a couple of hours, so did they give us money back, heck no! The good is lousy, unless you go to Finnegan's and have lunch. Otherwise fast food done poorly, and long lines and high prices. Overall, it was nearly 10 years since I last visited, likely another 10 before I go back and by then you will need a loan! The hotel is cheaper than the theme park!

Having trawled the internet we got a package which gave us 2 days in Studios and 2 days in Islands of adventure for $330 dollars for the 2 of us. On three occasions the accommodation we were staying in offered free shuttles to and from the parks. We drove just the once which was very easy with sat nav. Parking is $20. We were there during Mardi Gras on a Saturday and watched a very colourful procession with strings of beads being thrown into the audience. Kool and the Gang provided live music once the parade had finished- all included in entry price. The rides were of varying types. Roller coaster, trains, merry go rounds and a lot of 3 and 4D experiences. Queueing times can be up to 90 minutes on the more extreme rides and anything to do with Harry Potter. You can buy a fast pass but do not know how much this is as we did no bother as we knew we had return visits. If you can take your own food as snacks are expensive and time will be wasted sitting in restuarants. Note you cannot take alcohol into the site it will be confiscated at bag search. -it is a law of the Orlando Police Department or the OPD as like to be known as.

We did enjoy the rides we were able to get on. We bought 3 day passes. However we still didn't get to see everything. We can't believe that they charge 40.00 for express passes EXCEPT during vaca and spring breaks. then they charged $150.00, that's right 150.00 for one pass for one day. So try to plan your trip so you don't get robbed. Also don't fall for the premium parking. The first day we paid the extra. The next day we paid reg. and our parking was 2 levels up. All it saved us was 2 escalator rides. Not sure this was worth the trip.
This is a very fun park to visit for adults and kids, great shows and plenty of rides and attractions

We had a blast riding rides all around the park. Let me just say that if you are subject to motion sickness DO NOT get on the Despicable Me ride. It made me so sick. I had cold sweats and thought I was going to vomit. It is not like the other motion rides. You are sitting, but the only thing that really moves is the 3D screen. It moves a little but is not a track ride like most others and combined with the 3D = No Bueno for me. MIB is old ride but still very cool. Woody Woodpecker coaster was fun. ET was awesome. I got my 8 yr old to ride Rip Ride ROCK IT roller coaster and it was so awesome. It was his first scary roller coaster and he said it was fun, it was scary and he didn't want to do it again.

Long lasting family memories are created spending time on places like this,Chicken fingers at Mel's drive in are awesome, during daytime most of the rides has long lines, about 1 hour wating time, after 7pm lines are shorter for all rides, and after 9pm the get low to 15min and some just 5min. so take your day slowly and enjoy the rides late night
Harry Potter is the major draw. The rock and roll rollercoaster is also amazing. Could use some updates to older park areas but still amazing fun.
Kids love going to these parks - all are so much fun! We need to get down here more often, but when we do...too much of a good time! Recommend to all!
Absolutely fantastic a must for the young old you wont be disappointed,although the lines are long for some of the more popular rides it is well worth the wait.

March 31st, 2016.  Geared towards adults, but this time we have a little one and we were really pleased with the child swap option at some of the popular rides. This was super useful. There were also a couple of child friendly areas like Dr Seuss, Curious George and a few play structures. We came by the end of March (spring break) and no need for Express passes).  I'm not big on the Potter books or movies but I have to say what universal did was truly amazing. It is a must see for everyone but if you are into Harry Potter your going to love universal!  All around Universal is one of the best amusement parks and has some of the best rides and themes. If you are visiting Orlando I would suggest going to Universal.

Universal has two parks next to each other. Both have amazing rides, shows, entertainment and food. You can buy a single or multi park ticket-the latter allows travel between the two parks on the Harry Potter express. If the parks are busy, an express pass is available so you avoid the ride queues, although these are expensive, so use the internet blogs to find the quiet days.Ideally as a first time visitor allow at least one day for each park, and wear good, comfortable footwear. Enjoy!

Came here as a party of 6 ready for a great day of fun... Which it was, mostly. 2 of the kids didn't have skip passes so I bought them at the gate, and was sad to see they were more expensive because of Grad Nite... Okay fine. I bought them and we went in. Everything was going fine...eventually we made our way to the next park and continued the fun. At 6:00 we were told we had to leave, the parks were closing for an event. What? There was no mention of this when we bought our full priced tickets, no mention when we got on the shuttle in the morning, no mention when I paid EXTRA for (2 hours short) skip passes. Thousands of dollars spent between the 6 of us, extra money for skip passes (like double price) because of the event just to be kicked out before the event begins 2 hours before the park closes!? It completely threw our evening off and I just don't understand...we will definitely take our thousands of dollars somewhere that appreciates our business next time. Fun... But not worth it.

The superheroes and minion really spent quality time with my son. Captain America actually remembered his name by the after the second time of seeing him. We saw him a total of 4 times and each time he really talked to us. The minion was great - danced around with us, the stood for pictures.

Hi visited over the busy Easter period so some allowances need to be made for the big crowds. Both parks provide some good rides and even allowing for busy time the lines werent to bad. Bit of overdosing on the retail outlets. Biggest gripe was the breakdowns perhaps we were unlucky but 5 in one day inc. 2 complete shutdowns was very frustrating. Most staff very pleasant but equally some very abrupt.

We had a great time here , it was busy but did manage to get the kids on some rides, the only poor bit was Harry Potter which I reviewed separately as so disappointed with , they also had quite a lot of street entertainment and we meet a few characters unlike Disney , they seem to have something for everyone

Park is great but Universal and Islands of Adventure need to do something about the crowds in the Harry Potter area such as giving a specific time to visit this area. The interactive wands are incredible but cost over $100 for two kids and then to stand around and wait in lines in front of store windows to use them is just a waste of time when it is limited. We only spent time in this area later in the day when the crowds had died down but the rest of the park has some rides that are not to be missed.
