Universals original park doesent fail to thrill with lots of fun thrilling attractions to visit and ride on its a magical place to be in and has my very favourite ride/attraction the escape from gringotts in Diagon Alley definitely blows everything else out the water for me

Three days in the park is perhaps one day too many. We loved both Harry Potter areas in the park....thank you Universal. The rest was take it or leave it. Was there with the kids 20 years ago; some of the rides have been retooled with modern themes (makes sense). The 3D rides are all very similar in the ride (obvious movie theme different). Soda refill was a good value but carrying the cup is a hassle  Many rides for safety precautions require empty pockets; which means using the dreaded locker rooms. Universal you need to figure out a better system; particularly in the areas of Harry Potter attractions. I did not mind the lockers; but the rooms are overcrowded and shoulder to shoulder. Suggest one way flow of traffic and encourage one person per party to use the lockers.  Safety never a concern at the park  Family friendly.  Staff at park extremely helpful and friendly.  I do suggest to families to eat at the restaurants and avoid the hot dog type vendors. Restaurant offer a better value, better food, a seat, cold water etc.

I visited the park twice in the evening and didn't feel this is a park that creates a sense of contemporary delight. Most of the stuff look ancient. For the Harry Potter portion, the color was on the dark side, making it a little bit depressing.  However, I saw the daytime photos of this park people posted and found that they are bright, vivid and cheerful. Therefore, I think the best time to visit the park is daytime not night time if you like to be amused.

We liked that you could walk into shops with a drink, and there is so much to enjoy even if you don't take in the rides. Unfortunately we did go on a Harry Potter ride at Wizarding world and both of us were sick for 45 min. after the ride, never again!!! So much to do an little time, we would return and be a little wiser.

All of universal is amazing. My family preferred universal parks to the Disney parks. Simpsons ride is really good. If you have a disabled guest with you you can get a ticket at guest services and go to a ride you want and they will write you a time to come back so you don't have to queue. Disney didn't offer this service. Had to queue for hours with wheelchair there. Blues brothers were brilliant! Such a great place.

Me & my son had a blast once again in Universal Studios-Island of Adventure theme park. The wait times in April or good nothing longer than 35 min...The crowd was not over whelming & the weather was just right..Just wish him & I was able to witness the new King Kong attraction this summer & the Hulk rollercoaster that is being reconditioned.But other than that everything else was great..being that my son is older now he really got a feel of all the rides.Last time he was just a pup running me around in Kiddie land.

This place is amazing.  It has two main feature park attractions, both are fantastic.  I prefer this place to Disney land.  We must have visited this place on 4 days out of the 10 days of our holiday!!!  There are many rides, attractions, theatrics, restaurants, bars, snack joints, ice cream parlours and much more.  There are rides and attractions for all ages, something for everyone.  After a fun packed day, I enjoyed the dinners we had at bubba grump shrimp and hardrock cafe in particular.  This is a must do !!

We love to visit Universal Studios Florida. I just do not like the two separate parks. Universal Hollywood seems to be a better bargain. But we HAD to see the new Harry Potter attractions. It was worth it. You feel as though you are at Hogwart's. It is amazing and the rides are awesome and so real. The other attractions are also a blast. We love the ET, Men in Black, The Mummy, The Rock'n'Roll rollercoaster, all of the attractions and shows are Great - you have got the meet Shrek, the Donkey and the Transformers along with all of the other characters. It's worth the trip.
Great rides, fun for all ages. Lots of walking, plenty of food choices. Nice memorabilia for purchase.
The Simpsons ride was our absolute favourite. Myself and my girls went on the 3D ride every time we visited the park.

I took my girls to Universal mostly for Harry Potter World. Let me just say...It was AWESOME! The look on my girl's faces when we walked through the brick wall in Diagon Alley was pricless! We loved the books and to see the books you love so much come to life is an expression that has no words. From the continuous music to the food and the people working in the shops and the ones playing characters, it was truly prefect! The Butterbeer was everything I dreamed it would be! And the rides were unforgettable! Definitely a must even if you aren't a Harry Potter fan. This place has fun for everyone.

The parks are next door to each other and I started in Universal Studios. The rides here are generally either big rollercoasters or 3D / 4D experiences. Most of the rides are good but I'd especially pick out The Mummy which is a smaller indoor rollercoaster with some great fire effects, and Diagon Alley, Escape from Gringotts. In fact, Diagon Alley is an amazing addition to the park and well worth a visit although it's very crowded (even when you're not there at peak times). One of the best things is that you can now catch the Hogwarts Express from Universal Studios to Islands of Adventure which is a real bonus... no need to walk back up to the entrance and switch parks. A brilliant, brilliant idea. Overall Universal is well worth a visit, it's fun, it's clean and the rides are great. One comment I have is that as most of the rides are 3D, you can get a little nauseous after going on a few in a row. The second is that there aren't too many healthy eating options. Other than that, it's a wonderful day out.
Loved universal studios Florida, my partner and I went for my birthday and had a fantastic time going on all of the rides and getting pictures and just enjoying ourselves highly recommend
Great rides here too! Avoid Despicable Me, the line is not worth it. Other than that, fantastic rides. Be sure to get a two park pass to be able to ride the Hogwarts Express, which is incredible!
Too much to do in only one day but excellent experience. Too long queues to get in needs improving. Once inside really good with a very good parade.

Universal Studios has far surpassed Disney in every way. Customer service, staffing, cleanliness and fun. Every staff member smiled, asked if we were having fun, asked how they could help, knew the park and smiled always. The express pass was easy and priceless. The park was clean and the food was very very good no matter where we ate. The rides were way too fun. We gave up some of our "free" days of relaxing because the parks were way too much fun to miss.

We spent one day at each park, no need for anymore. Disappointed that Hulk coaster was closed, it's the key ride in Islands of adventure . Other rides were good but warning the Jurassic Pk water ride you get soaked in the front . Also the log flume and family tube ride you leave looking like you took a shower in your clothes, good thing it was a hot day, but still not very comfortable to walk around soaked. Harry Potter rides were good. Worst part of many rides is putting things continually in lockers, many times totally not needed, same type rides in Disney you are not required to get lockers. Regular Universal side was fun , but a lot of Car , virtual reality type rides, after a couple it wasn't really fun anymore. Two roller coasters which were good . The photo pass photographers were hard to find. Food was more expensive than Disney and not 1/2 as good. It was fun, but no need to go again for a long time.

We just finished a trip to Universal. We purchased the Photo Connect photo package ahead of time to get the cheaper rate. Since we weren't going to the park on consecutive days I ended up purchasing the 14 day plan, even though we were there only three days over a seven day period. It would have preferred the three day pass. All in all it was still worth it. We were there with my daughter and her boyfriend. We were able to get all the ride photos and a few good shots at the front of the park, near the globe and a couple of other spots. We noticed more photographers early in the day than after lunch.  Helpful hint, when they ask you to put out your hand and you expect something to be added to your photo, you will not see this automatically on your phone when the pictures are uploaded, we found that if you go into one of their photo stores, they will add the characters there and they you will have the updated picture to download. Also on Spiderman they take your picture at the beginning before you get on the ride, it's on a blue screen, if you ask to view the pictures at the end of the ride they add all the special effects and add that to your photo connect star card. On the Rip Ride Rocket roller coaster, you don't get the video included, but you if you go to the photo booth at the end of the ride they will give you a code to download your still photo taken during the ride.  This could all be so much better as proven by Disney, but overall, I still feel having the ride photos and the other group shots we were able to have their photographers take made it worth getting.

Had a great time visiting Unviseral Studios. It had been several years since our last trip. We saw the new Harry Potter and Transformers rides. They were both done well. It was hard to tell which was computer generated, and which was live. We has lunch at Flanagan's, was very sorry to hear they did away with the beer flights, but that's just business once.it was explained how much time some of the beer pours took. We were sorry to hear none of the restaurants gave a military or first responders discounts. We were told it wasn't in the companies policy to give such things...seriously?! For the amount the parks charge per ticket and they can't give a discount... that was the stupidest thing we'd all day. Our server went back to her boss and asked.id she could give her employee discount and he said yes. That was very sweet of her to ask and we made the difference up in her . We went on a monday was as it turned out it was a really good day to go. The lines were not longer then 30.mins all day.

After being annual passholders, we came back 5 years later. The customer service has definitely declined which is disappointing for the price you pay to enjoy the park. With that said, we still had a great time with our 4 and 7 year old boys. The new Harry Potter Diagon Alley is SOOOOOO cool! The magic wands and interactive parts are so cool for Harry Potter fans. The train ride is really neat too; you need to go both ways to see it all.
So much fun the rides were all amazing however the Harry Potter rides were a hit! We got the park to park hopper but in future wouldn't buy this again!

I love going here, especially when they have new rides. Going in May was the best ever. The lines were quick. I was able to get on everything. The new exciting ride was the Harry Potter ride. Although I'm not a Harry Potter fan, my son loves it. Oh and how can I exit the park without getting a turkey leg. Omg!!!! It was the tastiest.

I don't even know where to start!! Universal was BY FAR the best theme park experience we had!! And we did them ALL!! The lines were much shorter and faster at both of the Universal parks. The rides are MUCH more fun and even more kid friendly. I found Disney had one extreme or the other for rides but Universal had it all! I LOVED all of the motion simulator rides as did my child who is afraid of everything haha. The Simpson's ride and Transformers were among my favorite's at Universal and Harry Potter and the forbidden journey, spiderman and the bilge rat barge at Island's of Adventure.....  my best ride overall in all of Florida was Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey!! Loved it! I am not a fan of going upside down but this particular ride was so much fun!  The service and interactions with the staff was unparalleled anywhere else. We were treated awesome here by everyone we met. Definitely #1 on my Florida recommendations.
Other than the park hopper pass to see the whole attraction, we had a great time. Graduation gift for our daughter as she grew up reading the book series

An exciting day at Universal Studios. I had an a lot of fun with Caleb and my daughter Danielle. I was disappointed with the very expensive tickets over $200 each with limited park hours explanation given they had rented out park.

I love this PARK - great for all ages. Shows and rides are terrific. Purchase your tickets with American Express and you can use the AMEX Lounge (across from Shrek 4D) Relax in AC Lounge with free water & snacks, after 4 hours in sun this "SAVED" my wife & me.
We brought two teens and they never complained once the entire trip. We stayed on the grounds and loved it.

This was my first visit to Universal Studios. A better rating for me would be "good", not "average or very good" Most of the attractions were great, but some were odd. For example, I thought the Krusty attraction (totally kiddie oriented) was good until I learned that this character from the Simpsons set a bad example for children with some of his habits. If you don't know what I am talking about, just look it up. So, I was a bit confused about what purpose it served. The doughnut food place, well, there are certain things I don't engage with even on the remotest level anymore since becoming more health conscious. However, people are free to make healthier food choices and options are there. It is a different ambiance. This is a place I would take teens, not little kids. I'm not a smoker, so standing or walking when it's hot outside with plumes of smoke is a bit nauseating. Staff did not smile as often and one was quite rude, but no wish to possibly cost her her job. I let it go and chalked it up to her having a stressful day-we all have them. The MIB, Horror Make Show, and Transformer attractions were awesome! Free lockers while you ride (my kids, not me) high velocity attractions were a winner.
Paid for a one day ticket, not nearly enough time to enjoy all the attractions here but we're still had a good time!

We were lucky enough to get the Fast Pass and I recommend you do so too. It makes a massive difference with wait times down to about ten minutes. Be aware, it's not cheap though at about an extra $90.  Be sure to be waking into the park exactly when it opens and make your way straight to Harry Potter. Do the main rides and then go back to the entrance and start the park normally. This way, by the time you do get back to Harry Potter, you can afford to wait any time the main ride has to do it again. You can then see the rest of the world at your leisure and really enjoy it without time constraints.  The parks a lovely place to be. Kept extremely nicely and the staff are perfectly polite.  If you don't have a car and aren't staying on a universal property, here's some travel advice: USE UBER.  You'll see all the yellow taxis in Orlando are operated by a company called Mears. As they haven't a lot of competition, their prices are astronomical. Using Uber (an app you download) will save you hundreds of dollars. No joke. We saved over $350 on our trip and went everywhere.

What a great experience this theme park was to all of us !!  From the hulk to spider man to harry potter and so i can continue this park has just about everything for everyone from young to old!!  Only down side was as we are South Africans the exchange rate killed us from Rand's to Dollars but most definitely worth every cent spent here!!! Everyone has to go here at least once in a lifetime...

The park is clean, well-kept, well-organized, with helpful, fun employees and lots to do and see. The food can be very pricey, and we experienced long wait times in line waiting to order our food. When you see four registers, and only one is open during peak eating times, with over 15 people in line, management should open up a few more registers.  The rides, live bands, entertainment, are awesome. It is a great park and worth your price of admission to experience it all. Be patient trying to access the park in the morning. They only offer one park per month to open early....they should rotate between the parks to open early every other day so park goers can enjoy early access to a variety of rides. Also, it is VERY slow and clumsy to have their park admission employees scan your bar code on your admission ticket, and then scan your fingerprint. Why don't they just take your picture on your ticket, so you don't have to have the double check at the admission gate? It is excruciatingly slow and you wait a long time in line to try and get into the park. We had early admission and it was still SO slow. Not a good first impression, especially for us first time Universal park goers. We had a 3-day park to park pass, and every time we left the park and came back, it was very slow to enter. They really need to focus on this issue.  Fun park, however, once you get in. Don't miss Diagon Alley, hidden from the main road. The train ride between parks is a nice, air-conditioned rest with entertainment!

This is a great park and the addition of Transformers and Rip Ride Rocket makes it even better. The Simpsons ride is also really well done. Still some great classics though like Terminator. Definitely not to be missed while in Orlando

Our first trip to Florida and I cannot say enough about this park. Every employee was genuinely happy to make sure your visit was great. They really went above and beyond in cleanliness, technology and design.

We decided to give Universal a try, as we were looking for something other than the typical Disney Vacation. Our son is 5, and we weren't really sure how much he'd get out of the trip, so, we only planned for 1 day. We timed our arrival perfectly (accidently), as we entered the park, Optimus Prime walked out, and our son was amazed from the start. From there it we went to the Transformers ride, and thankfully, our wait was only 30 minutes, and our son quickly became bored, which sent us immediately to a vender that sold the express passes. There wasn't much to offer the younger kids, except the games by the Simpsons and Curious George village (we never got to see the Minions at the Studios). He quickly fell in love with the Woody Wood Pecker roller coaster, and we made multiple trips on it. I wasn't expecting much from him as we entered Diagon Alley (since he's never seen any of the movies). However, as soon as he saw the witches and wizards walking around, his attitude went from boredom to excitement. From there, it was to Hogwarts Express, and oh how I wish they'd allow the express passes there, as our wait was over an hour (it would have been faster to just walk out the front gate, and walk through City Walk to get to Islands of Adventure). We did return to the Studios after checking out Islands of Adventure, and thankfully, our wait was only 10 minutes, as the weather started getting bad. We'll return, but probably not for another 3-4 years, when he's older, and the park has more to offer him.

This was our favorite park so far. We only did the one side because we don't do roller coasters and we were able to do almost every ride. Loved Harry Potter ride and Simpsons simulator felt like a real roller coaster!! We did it in about 5 hours because we skipped minion ride, wait was to long.

Great value for money.. Busy periods are well managed.. So much to do so if you get the Orlando Flexi Pass you can split the attractions over a few days then come back and do shopping af end on a rainy day!  We usually stop off at Ihop on I Drive then walk over to the park. About 20 minutes.  Park itself is stunning. The rides are so good and the Harry Potter world is outstanding! You can take a ride on the Hogwarts express which is really cool, visit the Castle and greenhouses and say hi to Buck Beak at Hagrid's house! Great day out not just for kids! Make sure you take plenty of sunscreen with you and drink lots of water!

Our second summer visit to Universal Studios. We bought the vacation package from Universal and I recommend it. Add the meal plan and transportation and your vacation will be easy. We stayed at the Hard Rock again and it was great. We had early park admission and 3 day park to park tickets. I took my daughter and her boyfriend as a graduation gift. We all had a blast.

Great park! Despite being stuck in a tropical storm, my family and I still had a great time at Universal Studios! The primary reason for our visit was for my wife and daughter who are lovers of Harry Potter. Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade were fantastic and really made you feel like you were in the story. Escape from Gringott's was a really cool ride and one that I hadn't experienced at other parks. The Simspons area was pretty cool as was the Marvel area. Unfortunately, due to the rain, there were several rides that closed down. The Hulk wasn't even open yet, which was really disappointing. If you go here, you absolutely, without a doubt, HAVE to ride the Transformers ride. That is hands down the best ride I have EVER been on. Very well done Universal!! I hope to be back soon!
I went with 16 friends and had express passes and early entry.  Great day out if you have the above, if you do not you may have a stressful day  The attraction itself is flawless

Universal is just as good as Disney - it now has a few outdated rides that could do with a facelift or complete change but so worth a visit. We got the express pass which even though crowds were rated 4-5/10 this was an excellent time saver. We whizzed round every ride in one day - I could imagine this would start getting expensive with a large family though.

I haven't been to Universal Studios in about 5 years and the changes made this brand new to me again. Fear Factor was awesome and the street parade made this 49er feel young again (I danced and jumped with the characters). I had a great time with my husband, next time I'll have to do this with my grandchildren.

I'm from the UK, and after making the decision to go, O...M...G I'm so glad I did. It's great that Universal and IOA are linked up now by Harry Potter. You will not be disappointed, I promise you. Just walking through the park I can't help but be gob smacked and in complete ore of it all! Me and my whole family are completely addicted to this place, if/when you go...you WILL be too haha

We especially loved the Transformers and Harry Potter rides but the others were great too. Staff were helpful, friendly and we loved how they stayed in character with the area they were in. It really added to the experience. The only downfall with the park is the crowd. There were too many people and with manners at all. It seemed that most areas were over crowded and we found it hard to even find seating to just rest.  I would go again but plan it during a slower time.

Universal Studios is a fun trip for a day. We stayed at Universal and visited the studios as well as Islands of Adventure for 3 days and it was probably a day and one half too much, as the parks aren't overly big. The attractions inside however were wonderful and we were big fans of the Jurassic Park ride.
WOW ! This place is amazing a must see, friendly and helpful staff and the ride experiences are truly fantastic!! :)
Outstanding day out - the Harry Potter fans in our group were enthralled. we had a ride on the Dragon Duel roller coaster as well which was awesome. Brilliant day out.

I cannot wait to get back to Universal studios this was my first time here and I absolutely love it, mostly all of the rides were indoors and that is plus after being in the heat all day. I ate over were the Simpson's attractions was and had a chicken and waffle sandwich it was delicious. I will be back there soon!

Seriously good fun and the new set looks fantastic, so much going on this place never gets old. Wouldn't do the food package as it takes a lot of searching to find out where you can get your drinks cup let alone refills and it saved us nothing.

took family to universal studios cool was able to get to the major rides and shows in 1 day for both parks as long as you have a fast past, which i would recommend anytime you go during the travel season to any theme park...the only disadvantage is the king kong and harry potter does not use fast past since those are there newer rides so that is the only real waiting that we had to do, but overall was very fun!!!

Great thrill rides and fun shows throughout the park. Loved the Harry Potter attractions. Lunch at The Leaky Caldron, the shops and Gringotts was fantastic. Watch for the fire breathing dragon! Board the Hogwarts Express at gate 9 3/4 and travel to Hogsmeade. From ET to Mummy's Revenge there's something for every thrill seeker. From San Francisco to New York, Blues Brothers to Sponge Bob great fun. Can't wait to visit again.

Watch out when you purchase tickets on the site-they advertise that you get a coupon book but when you pick them up at the front office they tell you they never had a coupon book. When I picked up mine at the end of feb 2016 I didnt get one let alone the envelope supposedly that was waiting for me. All I got were the tickets. I only printed out 1 copy also -print out a second one to have on hand to verify that's what was said. I just went on their site to look at their deals for hotels since I am going their in oct 2016 and already have my annual tickets. It is again on their site about a free coupon book when you order the tickets online. spoke on the chat and told this and they wanted a copy of the reciept and what site I found this on. She didnt know it's on their own site. this is not right at all.
Its one of my family favourite parks. There was a lot of closed areas this year but i don't mind as they are putting a lot of new stuff in and it makes it worth visiting every year!!!

My wife promised to kick my butt again because she won the challenge in 2014. Well it didn't happen this time, cause our daughter spanked her. I couldn't compete due to bum shoulder (wink wink), but all in all the children thoroughly enjoyed themselves.

We really enjoyed this park but mostly because the crowds are much lighter than Islands of Adventure. This park by far has the better Harry Potter experience and rides but that in my opinion is the main draw. Much less thrill factor compared to Islands of Adventure if you are a roller coaster and ride fan. If you have the park hopper you don't want to miss this park but most with kids and teens will find themselves riding the Hogwart's Express to the other park. For those into 3D movie type rides this is your park. Leaky Caldron has good English pub type food but don't expect a fine dining experience anywhere in Universal.
This ride was the best! It was calm and sweet and nostalgic. Like it so much better than all the 3d rides in the parks. Old school does it best!

Stood in line on a ride for an hour, and watched them stop all but the express pass riders.  A disappointed 9 year old couldn't understand, and its is hard to explain the greed behind this.  On vacation again this year and US is not on the list.
I love this place far more than Disney. All of the attractions are just more adult and entertaining for me.
We go about once a month and it's a blast for all ages. There is something to do for everyone. The wait times are reasonable. It can be hot in the summer heat so make sure you drink plenty of water.

AWESOME day! We had a one day park hopper pass, so we could ride the Hogwart's Express. We went too hard from 8-6 and ran out of steam. All things Harry Potter were just perfectly awesome. If you love roller coasters and are REALLY brave, do The Rocket! One of my favorites was The Minions. You are in a seat in a room the whole time, but after you are done, you won't believe it!

Visiting the 2nd time to see the new Harry Potter. Loved it yes it's crowded but it is as expected. My twin 1 yrs old boys love the splash area especially during the hot days. Butterbeer Butterbeer is the best...

Love this park - particularly the retro feel with some of the rides/experiences. T2 still doesn't fail and is a family favourite. The transformers ride is awesome and when we first arrived the queue was only 10mins but later in the day was 50mins. Simpsons ride makes you feel a bit queazy but is a fun simulator for he kids. We did the Harry Potter stuff separate as you wouldn't fit everything into 1 day. Disappointed the Beetlejuice has gone now! Mummy is a fabulous thrill ride. Yet again the minions ride queue was horrendous - 70 mins as was rip ride rocket so we gave these a miss.
So much fun this was the best park in orlando. I can't wait to go back. I would recommend buying fast passes it's to dam hot to wait in line for a hour and half

The best park I have ever visited! It`s just amazing! The best thing is not just for children even you visit the Shrek, The Harry Potter part, adults can have a lots of fun there too. They have app to check the wait times which is so helpful not to waste so much time cos there is a lot of things to do. If you can, stay for more days. Most of the drives were inside buildings therefore we could escape from the rain and the humid hot weather. We enjoyed it so so much!

Personally, I enjoyed Island of Adventure better than Universal Studios. For my family (two kids: 2 & 8), Island of Adventure offered a bit more. However, there is still a lot to do here. Lines seem to be the longest between 10-5.

My son and I shared a great day at both the parks specifically for the Harry Potter experience. He absolutely loved it! I don't know much about Harry Potter but that didn't stop me from thoroughly enjoying the whole experience. My personal favourite was the Gringots ride. The queues at their worst were about 30 minutes but all inside, and so much to see during the wait. We booked express passes so our maximum wait for anything in the park was 5 minutes. Well worth it on a hot day but you did have to slow down sometimes because waiting in line is actually in some really great areas which you can miss if you are moving too fast. The meal deal was $21.99 which we upgraded to unlimited free non alcoholic drinks for an extra $6. So throughout the day we had a large pizza slice, bread stick and Caesar salad for lunch, Ben and Jerrys ice cream later in the day and unlimited drinks. Soft drinks are usually about $4 each and we must have refilled at least 6 times, so it was well worth the deal for us. The only down side was at the very end of the day when it was hard to find a machine that hadn't run out as it had been so hot! Staff were amazing and super friendly. My husband dropped us off at the drop off area and picked us up there at the end of the day, well sign posted and easy to do.
This is a great place for young and old. Great rides, great shows and great live performances. The free drink refills are a great idea.

Universal Studios is the best park in Orlando. The environment is full of happiness. The attractions are carefully done and pass the sensation of reality. The decoration is perfect. I came many times and I am always enjoying. I love this park!

Being an adult Universal Studios has a lot more to offer then Disney.If you are a Florida resident you get a much better deal on yearly passes.The parks are easy to navigate and the hotel options are very good. It is very easy to get in and out of parking and if you just want to go to CityWalk its still a good value.

Not a park for the faint hearted- great rides , we found not ideal for children under 1.2mtrs. We opted for transportation from the Hotel as decided to go later and heard the car parks could be busy- however not as busy as we thought- July seen as of season.
Plenty to do but very busy. Annoyingly all the new attractions that were supposed to be ready by the summer were still closed. EXTORTINATE, INEXCUSABLE and UNJUSTIFIABLE parking fees.

got there early on 4th of july.so got right on et and terminator no waiting though they asked if we had express passes we did not.but since there wernt much people they let us right on.that worked out.then later of course the park got busy.we stood in line for shrek.for a long time.never moved because all the express people kept getting in of course before all us non express people.we finally left the line was so hot.i had checked the price for the express pass it changes daily depending on how busy it is.the pass that day was more then the admission ticket to get in.blues brother show was great.got to take pics with some charaters.we left for a break from the park and came back later.did the minion attraction.long line but waited.not good for those of us who get motion sick easy but otherwise good.went to dinner at bubba gump.very long wait.waited for the fireworks were not on time we left never saw them.

It was hot, busy and the queues were there wherever you looked. But and its a massive BUT, it doesn't matter. The heat is fun, the crowds make the atmosphere, the rides, restaurants and staff all try their best. You're on holiday and you won't do it all in a day. It's too good to rush and my family love it.
Always a good walk-bring good shoes! Always expensive-water and drinks especially over priced! However we find it better than Disney-and a little cheaper!

We usually book from the UK but forgot. Paid $1250 for four adults with express passes only to find the new ride (Kong) was excluded (90 minute wait) and most others had 15+ minute waits with the express pass, Minions was 25! Hulk as shut and Harry Potter has taken over, also excluded from Express pass!

This was our 4th visit here. It is always a great day. Really enjoy the selection of attractions here and am always grossed out at the Fear Factor game played!! The new Diagon Alley is just fantastic!!

We came back, after having been there in 2012, to see Diagon Alley and it is amazing. We loved it. Get park to park so can ride the Hogwarts Express. We stayed at a Universal resort and could get in the parks at 7:00 and I definitely recommend that. Could do several things before lines got long. We did not have the Express pass as Cabana Bay guests did not get that perk and it is just too expensive for 5 people. Really though, we did not have terribly long waits and we were able to do almost everything we wanted. Do wish they did not have Express Pass and used a system like Disney Fast Pass. Utilized the single rider line when possible which helps although it is more fun to experience with your group and need to experience the entire queue at least once as the queue is usually part of the attraction. Most of the attractions are 3-D motion simulator type rides. Will come back again sometime but maybe not in the summer due to the heat and crowds.

We chose Universal as our kids had been to several of the other parks on previous trips to Orlando. Our boys are 8 & 9, so too old for the kiddie rides but not quite tall enough for the roller coasters at other parks. We thought Universal would be good because they were tall enough for everything they offer.  Showed up and two adult/two kids passes with FastPass came to $927. Sticker shock.  We entered and the FastPass lines weren't much better than the regular lines. Worse, the place is about as worn out as it gets....reminded me of a cheesy place somewhere in Myrtle Beach.  The roller coaster is good but beyond that, very unimpressive. The Mummy ride was okay, at best and otherwise it's just a bunch of those rides where they put a movie screen in front of you, 3-D goggles on your face, and the chair moves around in an effort to trick your brain into thinking you're on a ride.  I will say that the Harry Potter section is interesting but if you're not into HP, it's whatever. Even if you are into it, not enough to justify an afternoon there.  Finally, no energy whatsoever compared to any of the Disney parks. No music, no characters, nothing inspiring. Avoid at all costs.
Amazing experience seeing transformes and the simpsons walking around. Best rides in the world. Its the best money you can spend for entertainment.

Have visited here many times before and feel the addition of Diagon Alley and Kings Cross station with the Hogwarts Express between both parks is great. We moved between the 2 parks throughout the day and found it so much better as we could take the train each time and the queues were only about 10 mins each time. We were disappointed that the Hulk Ride was shut as its being upgraded, but really want to return next year as it was the best ride and so hopefully it will be even better.  One main criticism, please can the park provide more seats for people waiting for members of their party who are queuing for rides. I no longer go on roller coasters and have an injury and found that I struggled to find seating whilst waiting for my family. The worst of the lot is the ride Rip Ride Rocket, this is no where to sit, and NO SHADE so I felt quite ill by the time my family came off the ride.

This was our second visit in four years, and it didnt disappoint.  I have two boys, a tween and a teenager and clearly Universal is far better geared to boys their age, than Disney is. In addition, I personally feel that Universal is better value for money than Disney.  In case you plan to visit Universal Orlando often, I would recommend the annual pass. Not only does it give you unlimited access, but you can also use the valet parking, get a fastpass after 4:00PM and discounts at the stores.  The new Harry Potter park and the hogwarts express were delightlful, and we were fortunate to have been able to go for the Reign of Kong ride that opened. It was a pity that the Hulk roller coaster was shut throughout our stay.  Will definately visit again.

Had 14 day tickets and enjoyed the park as a family of 4 with kids aged 14 & 11. We did not have fast passes but did not have to wait too long for any ride by clever planning. I think the most we waited was for the Minion and that was only about 25 minutes as we managed to get in as last admission before it closed at 10pm. So we went very early or late in the day and went back to our hotel midday to recuperate. Because there is only so much of 3D rides you can cope with. This worked Out really well. I went on the Mummy ride 3 times in a row without waiting late at night using the single riders lane! so make the most of the single riders lane as you usualy end up getting on the same ride anyway. I loved the ET one, it was amazing setting. My 11 year old son loved the Transformers one and my daughter loved the big red roller coaster and went on it 4times. Ensure you have the app and make the most of it to work out waiting times etc. There is free wifi which is great.

Third visit this year and we thought Escape from Gringotts was a great new addition. Miles better than the King Kong, and with much shorter queues. Good planning and an early start means you don't need to pay out for fast passes.

After many visits to universal this year we booked our tickets with Virgin to get early access. On the day we arrived we decided to buy express park access for what we thought was on the day park access the a single park. Having bought the ticket feeling rushed by the sales person on the front desk we only realised getting back to the villa we actually paid for 2 park ticket express pass when only asking for one .  Really disappointed with the sales tactics by universal studios on this.  Had a great time in the park but just be aware if you are planning to do the same and check the ticket or buy inside the park !
Need more than 1 day for parks and express pass. Lines 20-120 minutes. Worth it! Bring drinks/ snacks in line with you. Weekdays lines are slightly shorter.

Easily the best theme park in the world. I would recommend spending more than a day here as there is just so much to see and do here! The best time to go would be during the week - try to avoid weekends as they are super busy times. The new addition of Harry Potter is excellent and really transports you to another world. Friendly staff and great location with so many facilities.

Now this is where the real magic happens!! Oh my, we came here back in 2009, but in 2016 it's just even better. Where else can you fly in a car through cities, have balls of fire thrown at you, get sucked into a vortex and get rescued by Spider-Man and bumblebee?! Where else can you ride 4 miles underneath gringotts bank in a cart fighting dragons? Or even better where on earth would you be able to fly over Hogwarts and play qui ditch with none other than Harry Potter?! Or ride through the jungle and get thrown around by dinosaurs and King Kong!!!! Universal costs a lot of money, but it buys you experiences you cannot get anywhere else, it is just amazing. Even in very hot weather universal have cooling fans and mist fans everywhere to keep you cool, the ques can be long but absolutely worth it! If you get there early you might find barely any que, next time we come I won't be buying other park tickets at all, it'll just be for universal!
This is a definite repeat destination for our family every time we go to Orlando. Your family will always enjoy a day at Universal Studios! Fun for all ages and lots to do!!

We are disney fans but after today I think we may to switch channels . Is been a while since my last visit and still fun . Harry Potter is a total addiction . The entire town is so real. The park is great some brilliant rides the Simpsons is fantastic but Harry Potter is just out of this world, walking behind that wall and seeing potter world was just unbelievable it left us all gobsmacked.

My family really likes this park. Don't send the Disney police after me - but we are starting to like it more than Disney.  It rained for a couple hours the day were were there but most of the rides are indoors so it wasn't a problem. We just bought a $10 poncho and kept on going

My favorite of all the Orlando parks. There is plenty to do for all age groups and if you stay a few of the onsite hotels you get free fast passes.

I have to say as a previous employee of Universal (which was over 13 years ago) I still love this place. I always feel like a kid when I walk through the turnstiles. So many things to do and see. Not been for a few years so we did ten heights are a universal hotel cabana bay which is a brilliant place to stay. We went to see the diagon alley as it wasn't built last time we went. Well I'm not a huge Harry Potter fan but wow wow wow it was amazing every single detail was fantastic .

Visiting universal studios is NO waste of your time and money. Your children will have a great time and you the parent will be happy because it is money well spent. The PARADE was done went it was still bright so we were able to record and share via Facebook and everyone that saw it said its a place to visit

I have used the VIP Services at Universal 3 times in Florida and once in California. It is truly the best way to experience a theme park. The Perks included in your experience: 1. Valet Parking - NO line ups, safe and convenient! 2. Continental Breakfast - Muffins and other sweet pastries, cereal, whole fruit, coffee, tea, hot chocolate. They also have free bottles of water for you to grab for the day. 3. Ponchos - for rain or for the wet rides! 4. Guide - this is the best part! I have never had the same guide and therefore, never had the exact same experience. They all come with their own tidbits of information though. Inside info and places that the rest of park goers cannot see or hear about. 5. Front of the line for all major rides - this is NOT Express Pass. This is back door into the attraction directly to the front of the line. No waiting. 6. Food Voucher Card - We were able to get 1 quick service meal (no sit down to be served restaurants), 2 drinks and one snack/dessert. I didn't end up spending a cent on food or parking the whole day. 7. Unlimited Express Pass - after the tour was over (about 5 or 6 hours) our VIP card allowed us to go through the express pass for all the rides that offer it for the remainder of the day. Not as fast as when you are with the guide, but 10 -15 mins wait, rather than an hour or 2. 8. Discount - after your tour, your VIP card gets you discounts on your purchases in stores.  Tips: a) Book ahead as busy times can fill up. b) If you have a big enough group, get the private tour c) Do both parks. You have the time, might as well save money and just go the one day. You will HATE having to wait in line after you haven't. d) If your guide does a great job, tip them! e) Be ready to walk a lot! You don't want to be the one slowing the rest of the group down. d) Shop and take photos after the tour. This tour is so you can get on as many rides as possible with the shortest wait. Do that stuff after, you will have time. e) Don't be late! This includes in the morning as well as after lunch. You are holding up other families :)  ***Additional ways to save*** -For anyone visiting Universal with an American Express Credit Card- *Use your card to buy your tickets and you will have access in to the American Express Lounge. It is a nice, air conditioned room with tv and couches as well as drinks and snacks. This was all free to us, just for having an Amex. -If you have an AMA or CMA card *Discounts given on food and merchandise purchases.

Please forgive my cynicism but I left two days of Universal Orlando thinking: I just don't get it. Sadly, I left the park each day thinking that the whole thing is just one giant scam to separate people from their money. I wouldn't mind if I felt as if I got value for the hours waiting in sweltering lines and up-sales around every corner.  While I simply don't see the magic, my kids (6 & 8) seemed to love the place. In the end, it's all about the family experience and watching the joy on your kid's faces. Universal Orlando (both parks) did make my kids smile a lot, and that may mean my review is moot.  I can only write what I genuinely feel and I just wasn't feel'n it! I really can't pin point why I enjoy the "mouse's house" so much more, especially when you consider the similarities between the theme parks. If you take your kids to Universal they'll probably love it, especially the Harry Potter areas, but this adult is one visitor who left the parks with an itch that wasn't scratched and a hunger that wasn't satiated.  One final note, every last employee I encountered everywhere at Universal Orlando were fantastically helpful, and friendly. The parks are very clean and felt very safe. I'd love to know the repeat customer numbers for the various big players in theme park entertainment because I won't be coming back to Universal Orlando.
Get there early to beat the long Harry Potter queues, waited almost 2 hours but was worth it. Loads of other great rides between the 2 parks.

However, the cost has become ridiculous! $!20 was our discounted cost. There is nothing about this park that is worth that. An average sized middle class family would have to save for years or go into debt in order to afford to bring their family. So sad....

Universal has the potential to be an even better park than Disney if they keep up with them on a few areas notably service and technology.  The Good: Rides are amazing. Staff working at check-in were not what is expected for this price. Had to go to 4 areas to get tickets and checkin complete, which seemed ineffective. With dozens of high quality entertainment options in Orlando, it's often hard to choose. However, absolutely DO NOT miss a visit (at least two days) to Universal Studios. We spent an entire weekend entirely focused on two Universal gems, Universal Studios and Universal Islands of Adventure. A two-day Park Hopper Pass provided the perfect combination of park access and connectivity. If you want the full Harry Potter experience, you'll need to visit both parks. Diagon Alley is located in Universal Studios. Hogwarts School is in Universal Islands of Adventure. The Hogwarts Express (fun train ride) conveniently connects the two parks. Again, two days is a MUST to fully see both parks and experience ALL the Harry Potter rides, shops and restaurants.  A few tips for your visit to Universal Studios Florida:  1) Parking is only $20 bucks per day. Traveling around Orlando is fairly easy. Get a rental car at the airport and lodge elsewhere to save money.  2) Be prepared for rain, humidity and water rides. Bring a light backpack with small umbrella, poncho, extra shorts, shirts and shoes. There are plenty of free (some paid) lockers to store your stuff while on rides or in restaurants. If not, be willing to get wet and walk around soaked all day. Not surprisingly, they offer human sized blow dryers all over the park... for a $5.00 per use fee.  3) Avoid the $21.99 Dining Plan. Food options are abundant but quality ranges from totally amazing (Mythos) to completely awful (Circus McGurkus Cafe in Seuss Landing). Generally speaking, the best food options are NOT included with Dining Plan. Don't waste valuable park time trying to figure out where the best food is located.  Finally, you can spend literally dozens of hours PRIOR to your visit searching for discount tickets. In the end, we found the best prices by contacting them directly. If you are staying three days or longer and want to include Disneyworld or another non-Universal park, then using a third-party ticket broker makes sense.
