When visitors arrive @ universal studios; there are security to thoroughly check bags & bottles for weapons & alcoholic beverages. Caucasian male security personnel searched our bag pack because rolls of quarters looked suspicious for unknown reason(s); also asked, "why do you have so many quarters?". When we replied that quarters were for tolls & vending machines; he condescendingly said, "just so you know; everything is digital now". After security check point, visitors walk through city walk towards universal studios & islands of adventure. Then tourists wait in winding lines to purchase park tickets. Finally, friends & families with children wait in additional but worse muddled lines to have park tickets & thumb prints scanned. There should be electronic kiosks available to purchase park tickets & park members for assistance. We prepaid two (2) park to park passes via AAA website but we still have to wait in line to obtain our passes which defeats the purpose of prepaying online. There should be separate wait lines for visitors who prepaid their passes. @ universal studios park entrance on 9.30.16 in the morning; we were promptly informed that ALL rides were inoperable until further notice. Therefore everyone was going to islands of adventure. There should be LARGE electronic signs @ city walk & park entrances (similar to traffic & amber alert signs on the highways) informing visitors that rides @ universal studios were inoperable until further notice. On 10.1.16, we surrendered & purchased expressed passes. Therefore, we have less wait time for MOST rides. Unfortunately, express passes are inapplicable for NEW rides & attractions such as 3D Hogwarts railways to & from diagon alley & hogs mead; gringotts; raptor encounter & leaky caldron pub. Warning: dragon above gringotts roars & breaths fire. Children & visitors with small bladders might accidentally pee their pants. Before riders wait & enter gringotts bank; everyone must secure their bags & backpacks in lockers which is complimentary is riders stored belongings less than 1 hour. Harry potter theme parks @ diagon alley & hogs mead have expanded & improved. Sadly, we were unable to locate 3D ride in Mr. Weasley's magical flying car. City walk, universal studios & islands of adventure are clean. There are plenty of clean restrooms, cafes, restaurants & gift shops throughout property. In addition, universal studios has a great phone app which informs visitors which rides are roller coasters; water rides; 3D & 4D rides; shows; wait time for each attraction; navigates where you are located on the park to the ride/show of interest; alerts when your favorite ride/show has less wait time.
So much to do here along with Harry Potter world. Totally worth it to get a park to park ticket AND take at least 2 days. Great rides and adventures.

We recently visited universal in orlando and had a wonderful time. I recommend taking a full day for universal and a full day for islands of adventure. There is so much to see and do. We had the best time. It is by far the best theme park I have ever visited. A must do for orlando.

We drove down from Minnesota for my brother's birthday, and we will never return. Staff was rude and egotistical, the majority of attractions were shut down or broke down during operation, food is overpriced, and wait times are long.

I visited the park with my 6yrs old son who is mad about transformers; we only visited one park as my son has epilepsy and it would be too much to do more than one park. I visited guest services after picking up my tickets as a friend had recommended getting a pass that allows him to get a time to return to the ride rather than standing waiting for a hour (if my son gets tired he can collapse and blackout). After a bit of grilling over my son's condition we were given the pass (which I did expect). We managed to go on about 4 rides during our visit (my son gets tired) and we did not have to wait too long for some of the rides the longest was 50mins to return back. The highlight for my son was meeting the transformers although he was a little shy he met his heroes. My only moan was when he met bumblebee I went to buy photos afterwards and the pictures were of the back of his head and they told me there is sometimes a glitch on the camera but lucky I had taken some on my own camera and I bought pictures when he met Optimus Prime. I bought the day tickets purely for my son to see the transformers and it made his day.  On a negative side anyone visiting any of these theme parks with young children like myself it is difficult for children to stay in line for upto 50 minutes and unsure what can be done to elevate these problems although I was impressed with Simpsons ride because as we waited there was some entertainment as you waited. It's s pity you can't have seating in queue but I suppose it would cause health and safety issues?  Good day at the park; expensive to buy transformers toys (get them a lot cheaper in U.K.) and was a bit disappointed there any transformer toys you can't get in the UK and I was looking for a transformers backpack for my son but when I asked in the shop they said they don't do them.
We enjoyed this place more than we even imagined we would. The rides were incredible. You have to ride the Transformers ride

I was a bit unimpressed with this park not counting the Harry Potter portion. Most of the rides rely on 3D or 4D technology and while it can be very cool to experience, it gets a little unimaginative after awhile. My husband and I were really only visiting the parks for the Harry Potter area which completely delivered in terms of immersing you into the setting. We loved the food, drinks, and entire atmosphere. Otherwise, there wasn't really much we wanted to do in this park. It's definitely nice to have the express pass though. Using that or single rider made waiting nonexistant. However I really disliked their bag policy for some rides. It's not very obvious and is a pain if you're next to get on the ride and have to lose your spot to go lock up your bag. And if a handful of rides do this then they all should since it isn't clear when you can and can't bring them and the staff seem pretty PO'd when you ask. I get that the intensity of the rides might make having loose items bad but it gets pretty tight trying to shove your Olivander's wand in those lockers.

I can honestly say I was expecting a little bit more. The haunted houses were done very well however whenever you see the monsters jumping out at the people three feet in front of you it doesn't scare you and it takes away the thrill. I did not pay for any Express passes because being a single mother I paid $565 for two tickets into Island of Adventure two tickets and two all day at Universal including Halloween Horror Night. This was just to get in this did not include the $20 per day to park and $20 per cup so we could have beverages. The only advantage of going all day was We Were released in the park and hour early before the General Public and that allowed us to go into 3 haunted houses for the lines got Crazy. However 12 hours on your feet it definitely brings a person. After the general public got in the lines became unbearable I missed out on a few houses because I wasn't going to wait an hour and a half. This was on a Wednesday night I could only imagine what it is like during the weekends. The scare zones were okay. I live near Chicago so I go to Great America Fright Fest quite often and they have the whole park decorated including the water turned Red, Scare crows and pumpkins all throughout the park it is definitely a more Halloween feel. I definitely would say the best part of the whole night was the Bill and Ted Adventure Show. Overall I am very glad I got to experience it with my daughter however my expectations were higher.

Once I got over the sore feeling from the price of the tickets, this was a great experience. There is something for everyone here and I don't ride roller coasters. Visiting this time of year the queue for rides was not bad, a few we just walked straight in, the longest wait was 35 minutes for the minions. Personal favourites were transformers which shows what the best modern technology can do for a virtual experience but I also loved ET, which must be one of the oldest rides and had no queue!

I could talk about all of the attractions but just enjoy Hulk and Harry Potter and the rest is almost irrelevant. However, it's all amazing.  A fantastic family day out and a must do in Orlando, even if I ended up doing it without my family!

I love the rides and the butter beer is yum!!!! The Mummy ride was fantastic! Didn't mind waiting in several long lines. But the food is such a ridiculous let down. It's very over priced, terribly over priced even for theme park food. The only food that was edible was at The Leaky Cauldron. It was breakfast and it was $16, but it was creative and good. Every place else was terrible. The absolute worse was, Thunder Falls BBQ. After spending more then $80 for cold cheeseburgers, dry chicken wraps, cold French fries, not only was my family let down but we left hungry. I'll visit the park again, but eat outside somewhere.
I absolutely love Universal Studios; there literally is something for everyone here. Fantastic time bringing so many movies and characters to life; chick full of fun.

Great experience and detail in houses was fabulous ! Could have been more scare actors and being a brit I just didn't quite get Bill and Ted show ! Fave house AHS followed by 3D house -lot of jumps and fun. Don`t show fear as they latch on to you !!
I remember this trip well. My daughter Sarah had so much fun! I would love to go back with my grand kids!!

Another great year!!! The mazes and scare zones were amazing. Can't wait to go back next year. If you are going to Universal Studios in the fall this is a must do!!! Just don't bring the little ones. This event would be way to scary for them.

The trip to Universal Studios was including as part of a large conference so I did not have to pay to attend. Since this was a private event not all the park was open. It was fun but the guides we talked to about the type of rides and what to expect was not helpful at all. The food experience was very lacking inside the park. We ate at Richters for hamburgers and would not do that again.
Even though the employees aren't has nice as Disney, the attractions and shows make up for it. This is our second time around!
Great park, not super crowded and the rides were awesome! Terminator 2 could go away as well as ET but the rest were fun!

This world has been done so well. So much thought has gone into every tiny detail. I loved it! Only downside was the price of merchandise... $110 usd for a robe or $48 for a wand was a bit steep. It was the busiest part of Universal too.....but still...fantastic experience!

I have to say that I was slightly disappointed with this Theme Park. There are 4 roller coasters in this park, the best being Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts. The other coasters are Revenge of the Mummy, Hollywood Rip, Ride, Rockit and the kiddie coaster Woody Woodpecker's Nuthouse Coaster.  Other attractions in the park are Terminator 2 3D (very disappointing), Shrek 4D (excellent), ET Adventure (OK), Men in Black, Alien Attack (a disappointing shoot-em up ride), Transformers The Ride 3D (average) and The Simpson's Ride (did not view as wait time was 50 minutes).  The best area of the park is The Wizarding World of Harry Potter and there is a train connection between this park and it's sister park Islands of Adventure.
I have found the new week to go. Arrive Friday after thanksgiving, no park Saturday, pool day. Then park Sunday and Monday. No longer than a 20 minute wait for rides. Even Harry Potter

Took a winter vacation. Got annual passes for Universal Studios in Orlando. If you get them get the preferred pass that includes the free parking ($20/day). Great time. Only ride closed was the original Harry Potter ride. Not overly crowded. Only issue was on Saturday December 3rd when trying to get into the park to get annual pass the computers were down and it took us over 2 hours to get in. This was not handled well by Universal. Some in line probably spent 3 or more hours to get in. That was the only negative comment that I have for the whole 9 day vacation. We went to Universal 6 days. First time on the relatively new King Kong ride. It was great. Grinchmas was excellent we went to it twice. Very satisfied and the annual pass has paid for itself already. Macy's parade was also very good.

There's a point where your children are too cool for Disney. That will pass but, meanwhile, teenagers love Universal. I'm a fan of trying to find the right to time of year to miss the crowds. It makes for a totally different experience. Once you've walked straight through to a ride, it's difficult to come back and wait an hour in a line.  Universal has areas for little children but, I can't imagine how that works well for a young family. The parks as a whole seem to me to be geared to an older crowd; people that ride thrill coasters and 3D rides. In fact, entrance to the park requires passing clubs and bars.  We do love it there; so much we have annual passes. Harry Potter is, of course, the big draw. However, do yourselves a favor and wait until 10 minutes before the park closes and walk right on the Spider-Man ride. You might get to go twice in that time.

Visited the park for one day to check out Harry Potter World with family. Let's just say I was "culture shocked" and we'll leave it at that. As a military vet with a few deployments under my belt, I had a hard time dealing with the hundreds of little fat kids running around in their Harry Potter capes screaming and whining. Not to mention I get a little anxious around large crowds of people. I realized I was in trouble after the first five minutes inside the gate. I did manage to suck it up for the remainder of the day. I'm not a big discount hunter, but was a little disappointed that the military discount was only $3 off a $160 ticket. If you're a yuppy family from the mid west with a couple of spoiled fat kids, then you may enjoy this park. I did not.

We visited universal and we had a great time. But there are some attractions like E.T and Simpson that are very old. You can even smell the old age of the buildings.  Download the app for the smartphone to reserve the fast past in advance for the attractions, also to have a map of the resort.  As a recommendation to the staff you should start including virtual reality attractions.
Tranformers was a very close second. This park was amazingly clean and unbelievable. The service is amazing and is very involved.

We've done Disney so many times with our family. Our kids are getting older,so we decided to try Universal this year. Overall we had a very good experience. A few improvements would take some of the annoyances away to make the experience go from very good to great.  First of all the entry into the park takes longer than it needs to. We had paper printed bar code tickets that took several tries to get them to register on their scanners. Everyone seemed to have a different sort of ticket. Converting to an RFID system could make this so much more efficient.  Secondly, the Express Pass system needs to be fixed. We visited at a very high volume time of year. The waits for the top rides were consistently between 90 minutes and 3 hours. You must spend an exorbitant amount more to get an Express pass. If you could afford it, the express pass would be worth it, especially if you are there during a high volume time. The system seems patently unfair to regular ticket holders. A system like Disney's would make a trip to Universal SO much more enjoyable. At least you would get a few rides on the top attractions each day. As it stands, you need to be there at closing to have shorter wait times.  To close, I must say the Wizarding World of Harry Potter is AMAZING. Even though we couldn't get on some major rides, we spent lots of time just enjoying Diagonal Alley and Hogsmeade. The interactive wands were fun to play with, and shopping at the stores from the HP books was fun!

Whatever you do in Orlando a trip to universal is a must, although I was there for a work function the first thing I got roped into was the hulk ride, absolutely thrilling even though inside I was very apprehensive. Ride before eating 😆

Me and my family went here for Christmas like we do every year and some things were good/excellent and others not so good. We love the Grinchmas show , the Mummy ride , the butter beer ice cream except the prices have gone up. All the Harry Potter rides are good. The new Hulk is ok except they make you put your stuff in lockers which is annoying. The KingKong ride could be much better. Overall Universal is just ok.

We had an awesome experience on 12/31/2016 the new year show was very beautiful and it was super fun. I enjoyed the park so much, it was worth every pain in my feet today. Ha ha  Some Of my favorite rides are minions,Spiderman ride, and Harry Potter
My husband and I had a great time. The rides were great and watching the Macy's day parade was awesome. We loved seeing the Christmas decorations and we had no problem.

We stayed on site so managed to get free express passes which you can use on all rides except 2 throughout the 2 theme parks (both rides are in Harry Potter). We made full use of the express passes and for December close to Christmas the parks here were very quiet compared to Disney. We were able to get on all the rides we wanted by 2pm and then spent the afternoon relaxing by the pool of our hotel. Perfect. There is a good mix of rides here for all levels of thrill seekers.

Visited in December 2016 with my wife and two teenage children and was disappointed following our experience of the Disney parks. The two parks are clean and there is plenty to do. The rides are great fun and there is something for all ages but..... The food is very over priced and the staff are not very friendly or helpful which is unusual for the USA as the customer service is usually great and why we returned. Disappointed and would not compare it favourably to the Disney parks.

Have visited Orlando for nearly 20 years and totally love this place. Universal Studios is always finding new ways to entertain families and I will definitely be back. Love all the attractions and entertain on offer and can't wait to do Halloween Horror Nights again

I love ❤️ Universal Studios. Great memories. I'm sad that I did not take a picture with the Marlyn Monroe. Next time I'll make sure to wait in line and get picture with her. I believe she only shows up during Christmas and New Years Parade.

We went to Universal Studios Florida over Christmas break. We spent 3 days between Universal Studios and Universal Islands of Adventure.  If you plan to go see the new Harry Potter attractions make sure you get the park-to-park passes so you can take the Hogswart Express train between Hogswart and Daigon Alley.  Of course you need to try the butter beer (tastes similar to cream soda) and any Harry Potter fan will probably want the interactive wands to perform different spells at specified locations using the wands.  Both parks at Universal has a variety of rides from slow rides to fast roller coasters. There's something for everyone.  The walk from the parking lot to the entrance of the parks are a bit of a walk unless you pay for the upgraded parking.  Universal City Walk area is right between the two parks and have a variety of food options if you don't want to eat within the parks.  If you plan to go for multiple days to the two parks do the math and it may be worthwhile to get the annual pass to give you more flexibility.  The week before Christmas was less crowded than the week between Christmas and New Years. Be prepared for lines for the rides and crowds (especially at the WizardIng World of Harry Potter). You can opt for the Express Pass which is an additional cost on top of you admissions ticket. We didn't get it. Instead we used the Universal Orlando app to check wait times and plan our day accordingly. We didn't get on every ride even with three days between the parks so plan accordingly to make sure you get to the must-see attractions on your list.

I flew in from Pittsburgh to visit my boyfriend and his family, and he and I decided to stop by Universal Studios. It was very cold, around 40 degrees but we didn't let that stop us! We saw that Fear Factor Live had an interpreter, which was perfect for me since I'm deaf so we seized that opportunity and watched the show and loved it! Our interpreter, Jennye, was fantastic and she gave us the list of other shows that were interpreted and we decided to go to all of them so we could understand everything. Our favorite part was the Horror Make Up Show - that show was hilarious! The hosts were very interactive and the whole room filled up with laughter! We tried to get on the Rip Ride Rockit, but they had a 75 minute wait at one point and then it got delayed! Diagon Alley was amazing, felt like the real deal! We got a regular Butterbeer and it was very delicious - it tasted like butterscotch cream soda. The Gringotts Bank ride had a very long line but it did not disappoint!

First of all it's very overpriced second of all half of the attractions were closed or the streets were closed and blocked because they're renovating the areas is very disappointing very overpriced I've been to all the Disney parks and they were fantastic . My advice to you is don't waste your money or your time going to Universal Studios Orlando. I seriously feel like I got ripped off. Oh and by the way do you think maybe 12.95 is a little ridiculous for a teaching I'm just saying

One of the best parks in Orlando. You'll find different attractions for all ages and interests. If you like ROLLERCOASTERS you have to ride the HOLLYWOOD RIP RIDE ROCKIT. You'll have lots of FUN at THE MUMMY. AND PLEASE GO TO THE HARRY POTTER SECTION!!!!!! IT IS MINDBLOWING!!!!!

At first was not impressed as firstly the entrance price was extremely high, we were there really early but already the queue for the rides was 45 mins!!!  Warmed to the park eventually when we Found Harry Potter what a fab attraction.  It was pouring with rain and extremely cold the day we Visited so was amazed that ride wait times were so long.  Loved the Simpsons and Dino land lots to do for the little one.  A ride on hogwarts train to the other part of universal is a must. Really felt like we were in the film with frogs on the windows.  Really good day out but costly

We felt we were living in the world the books created. Escape from Gingotts was a big hit with my husband and grown up daughter. It was too rough for a 60+ woman with an arthritic neck. I loved the Forbidden Adventure! My D and I spent an entire day in Diagon Alley if you don't count riding the Hulk twice in 20 minutes because the park had just opened and the train to London wasn't running...

I spent a full day there and had lots of fun. The kids didn't want to go on the big fast rollercoasters, but even without them, it was a great trip, and I could have gone back another day if I had had the time.

It's always an enjoyable day to walk around Universal. From the character parades to the rides (ET being my favorite), to the shopping, the day passes very pleasantly. We were a group of adults, and enjoyed ourselves!

Just returned from a amazing time. We loved both parks - all the rides were top notch. I can't say enough good things about the parks. Smaller crowds than Disney but much better rides. Would return for sure !!
The rides were great once you got on but the wait was sometimes hours. I don't think I'll ever go back.

My husband, 5 year old son and I visited in November. I was very impressed with the staff and the cleanliness of the entire park. Every single detail was on point! Diagon Alley was awe inspiring, and my son absolutely loved Seuss Landing. We especially loved the Parent Swap feature. We were able to shoot past the long lines using the single rider line and then one of us with sit with our son in a pleasant waiting room most with a video relating to the movie the ride is designed after (if not the movie itself). Big time thumbs up! There is something for everyone here.

We went to the Make-up show expecting to see a demonstration of horror makeup effects or just plain old makeup effects and got a funny comedy show instead. We enjoyed it, but the "makeup expert" spoke very quickly and I didn't catch everything he said. They really only did one actual effect, and that was neat. I don't recommend this for very young kids or those who are scared easily. There's some fake blood and a relatively tame werewolf.

We have been to 3 other Universal Studios but I think this is the worst. First, our family of 4 adults, got a ticket for a two days as advised so we can relax and be at ease no hurries for the rides around the park, one park one day. We chose to park nearer and that is coughing extra $10.00 on top of regular parking (total $35.00) even though we were there when the park opened 9am. At the door, we were offered front of line passes for extra $120.00. But since we thought 9am was early for us to go around and finish the rides, we opted not to. Besides paying $115 for a day ticket + another $120.00 seem ridiculous (total $235.00). Anyway, by 11 am, we finished 3 rides. By the time we got to the Harry Potter area, the lines were very long -- 120 mins. So we just let our teeners line up. My husband and I just decided to go around and wait at some designated area for our children. First I noticed that a lot of structures which I thought were stores turned out to be just facades, a little frustrated. Then after several hours we came to know that our sons had to line up 2 hours at most for each ride. We had no choice but to wait for them. Which made me think that if the waiting for each attraction was two hours, then the park has OVERSOLD ITSELF TO CAPACITY. Why sell that many tickets or allow a lot of people in if the rides cannot even accommodate them. 2 hours and more in line under the heat of the sun most of the time is ridiculous. So what they could have done was sell you $235.00 ticket in the first place. Which at that price I am sure nobody will buy. The marketing guru behind this entity is a genius. First they max out to capacity, then they sell you another ticket to make your life easier. So it is a win-win situation for them and customers end up grumbling. Hey and there's more, some rides require you to have empty pockets and bags be in the locker. Lockers are $3.00 for first 30 minutes. So the longer the lines, the more money you pay for the lockers. See I told you, they are the geniuses! So the next day, my husband and I did not go to the other theme park wasting our tickets (that was our choice though). I was telling my sons get the Front -of-line passes so they do not have the same experience as the day before. But lo and behold. The FOL ticket on that day turned out to be $180.00 per person and only the younger son bought as my older son thought it was just SO RIDICULOUS. So after 6 hours, they were out of the theme park. Younger son had 6 rides for $300.00 while the older son held on to his bags not to avoid the locker in some rides. We picked them up and we all swore that we will never go to this theme park again. And I promised to do a write up to make other families aware of our sad experience.
We had a great time! The park is clean, staff is polite and very helpful and at this time of year, it's not too crowded. I would definitely come back another time! There are attractions for all ages!

You can tell when you arrive that there is a lot of cool stuff to see and do here, but 10 minutes into the place, you quickly realize that the wait times for things you really want to see/do are going to consume a huge part of your day and that your visit is likely going to end up feeling more like a really expensive walk though a downtown-like setting. If you're into that sort of thing, go for it! If not, you may want to consider other options.

First off, waiting in line to get a ticket (and this was a slow day) took forever. Then they were charging an extra $65 per person to get express passes - we did not buy and noticed a lot of people didn't, we had no problem getting on the attractions. The Harry Potter area and Gringott's ride was excellently done. The streets and shops feel so realistic from the window fronts to the stores you can go into. There is a dragon on top of Gringott's who breathes fire every 10 minutes. A lot of the area in this park is themed streets (i.e. 1940's,e tc.) We did the Minion attractions and the Shrek ride plus a couple of roller coaster rides. Street entertainment was fun. Really enjoyed The Mummy ride and Transformer ride. Where one would always like to go back to Disney World, this one trip was good enough for all of us. When Disney takes the Marvel area away since they own the franchise now, Universal better have something to take its place to keep a person's interest.

Having time of my life walking around, The Blues Brother concert was a bonus. It's such an amazing place. The kid has a blast riding Transformer and other. Being Harry Potter fan walking to what you see in the movie is so exciting
The family finally decided to try this park and wow. So much to do. Minions, et,Shrek and transformers. Too much to do in one day. Definitely will have to go back. Highly recommended.

This place is huge and the theming of the newer areas of the park is something else. The Hogwarts Express linking the 2 parks shouldn't be missed nor should Diagonal Ally or Jurassic World over at Islands of Adventure. We went at Christmas time and the queues were frankly ridiculous, go early or stay late but don't expect to do much by way of rides if you get there after 10am.

My husband and I went yesterday and had a great time. The park is easily navigable and friendly to both adult and children. Rides are a combination of thrill and 3D/4D movie related. Would highly recommend!
I would suggestion to visit this park after going to Island of Adventure. Also, purchase the fast pass for this park. I was able to experience all the attraction by doing this.

Great place to spend a couple of days. So much to see and do, and all those iconic Universal attractions. Bubba Gumps, with Forest's shoes under the park bench to Harry Potter with a whole lot in between.

we went in january, so despite having premium tickets pushed at us to skip long lines, we bought standard tickets and queued for a maximum of 15 mins on each ride...Transformers kept breaking down and the Simpsons was closed, despite this, there was still plenty to keep us entertained

Don't miss this. Thrill seekers please go. Great coasters. Harry Potter lovers please go. I'm not a big potter guy but it was fantastic. A must see!! Of course food etc...over priced. Just like Toronto!! Fully recommend.

It goes without saying that these parks make for a fun day out and are very entertaining. I just wish Universal would cease their practice of trying to extract every last cent from their guests. I have visited twice in the last week. The first time I decided to use the preferred parking option which I was assured by the girl on the desk was much closer to the parks and far less of a walk. This turned out to be a blatant lie. I was parked in the King Kong lot at the very far end of the row. It was an extremely long walk to the parks. On my second visit I was parked in Jarrasic Park lot (standard parking not preferred) and was much closer to the parks. Avoid preferred parking like the plague, it's a complete rip off. YOU SHOULD BE ASHAMED OF YOURSELVES UNIVERSAL. NO WAY TO TREAT YOUR PAYING GUESTS!

I had a great time at Universal Studios Florida. This is a multiple day trip. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter will take a day by itself to see both Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade. So at least three days. One for Wizarding World, one for Universal Studios and one for Islands of Adventure. I also learned from my first trip to start the day early so that I can get as much in before the 5pm summer rain that seemed to happen everyday that I was in Central Florida. I will also take advantage of the express pass to help the lines go faster.

Universal puts Disney to shame much better rides fast passes work much better then disneys Minions ride is cool 4D Transformers ride is excellent, Shrek was not as good, the Hollywood ripe ride rocket ride was a lot of fun. A must do if in orlando

So. Much. F U N ! ! ! We had such an amazing time and got the quality couple time we needed. There are so many things for a young couple to do from rides to quiet sit down restaurants and just fun things to do together.

My favorite part was the "impromptu" SING OFF in the middle of the street! There are plenty of people around to help, the only thing no one seemed to know, was where to see your photos! Also be prepared to rent a locker. You can't bring anything on the rides, so you can either put it in a locker and leave it all day or put it in and take it out after every ride. It's annoying and hard because of the amount of people, but if you need your bags between rides, you have to deal with it!

It's hard for me to rate Universal after going to Disney. The staff isn't as friendly, the food is definitely not as good, and the whole atmosphere for me just can't compare. I do like the more thrilling rides here and Harry Potter world is great (although very crowded with small walkways). It isn't a place I say I want to come back to every year like Disney.
I wasn't sure what to expect entering Universal Studios. THAT immediately changed ! I entered the Transformers attraction, It was so exciting, I never experienced an amusement park ride so awesome.
What an amazing experience Universal was! We loved all the rides, although the one Harry Potter ride did make us a little dizzy! ;) Well worth the money!  ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

First question people want to know, do I need 2 or 3 days? Park to Park admission? Short answer, if you're not in a rush, 3 days and yes get the park to park. We arrived Saturday morning, after check-in were able to get to the park by noon. By end of day we were able to at least see the grounds of both parks and squeeze in a good count of rides which is why you want the park to park. Wait times in this season were 5 min for older rides, 15 min for the newer, even Harry Potter? What I couldn't understand was the constant 60min lineup for Minions? Sure it was a good 3D experience but not proportional to other rides. Nonetheless, do yourself a favour, stay at one of the resorts to take advantage of the extra hour before opening. You can get more rides in one hour than all morning after opening. Could you do this park in 2 days? Sure, but it would be very rushed, take an extra day, it's worth it. BTW, best ride, ' Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey.' I'm still trying to figure out some of the effects.

When I was younger, I visited Universal a few times, but I never truly appreciated it until now. I went for a mini 30th birthday getaway and had the time of my life! Going during the winter months was a great idea since the lines weren't ridiculously long. We arrived when it opened and for hours, the longest we had to wait for a line was about 20 minutes.  Make sure to visit Moe's Tavern for a Flaming Moe, Lard's Donut for a big strawberry frosted donut, and of course the amazing Harry Potter theme park...which as a Potter fan was amazing!
We went back and forth between universal and island of adventure so many times that hotels sort of run together but I'd do remember that the souviner shopping is better in. Universal

yep.for me it edges islands of adventure.just not going to see anything like this at home..never..again the entrance fee is bit steep.but in the end jus about worth it...try to go to the Halloween horror nights ..sept Oct November time..its that little bit extra aswell but again I've not seen this type of entertainment at home..enjoy

My family and I love Disneyworld properties. In my mind, Universal Studies was a decent alternative to Disney but not comparable. Last year, I purchased an annual pass to Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure because the price is so low (compared to Disney). Over the last year, my family and I have visited Universal Studios nearly 20 times and the park never gets old -- we are total Universal converts. We love the value of the annual passes. Here's a few things we enjoy about Universal Studios:  1. ET: ET is old as crap but this does bring up major nostalgia for me (I'm in my late 30s and ET was the first movie I ever saw in the theater). I will literally, not figuratively, die if something ever happens to this ride. 2. The entire area around ET: Barney. Curious George. American Tail. This is a great play area for smaller children (I have a four year old and he loves this part of the park). 3. The Simpsons: Again, I'm in my late 30s so I grew up watching the Simpsons. The theming in this area is incredible. Stop by and get a Duff Beer and a Flaming Moe (but don't eat a Krusty Burger -- so gross). 4. Kings Cross/Diagon Alley: Diagon Alley takes my breath away each time I walk in -- it is visually stunning. Drink the frozen butter beer. It is amazing. 5. The Mummy: Outdated theming (but of course, this is coming from the person who loves ET); however, the ride is awesome. I'm not too big on rollercoasters but I do enjoy this one.  There's a few things I don't like about the parks: 1. Just about every dang ride has some component in which you wear glasses/goggles and stare at a screen. Minions. Jimmy Fallon. The Simpsons. Gringotts. At a certain point, I feel like I'm riding the same ride. Plus, the screens make me a little sick. 2. Jimmy Fallon: This dude just sucks. There's nothing funny about him. The Roots are awesome, though. Bring back Twister. Or just demolish the Jimmy Fallon ride. Build bathrooms over it. 3. Height requirements: When we first started going to Univesal, my son could ride very few of the attractions because of his height (even in Dr. Seuss land in Islands of Adventure).  While my family and I still enjoy our Disney vacations, Universal is near and dear to my heart now. We just renewed our annual passes for year two. Can't wait for another year of adventures at this park!

I loved it here to, but after you finish with this park, you should do city walk, there were so many different places to choose to eat from in city walk, I will say I feel they go hand hand

This is not my first visit to Universal. The Harry Potter rides and Diagon are amazing. Men in black is also a favorite.

This is probably my 20th or more trip to Universal Studios over the years and this time my partner and I went without our kids, we are in our 60's...we enjoyed every ride even the Rockit Roller Coaster. This past weekend we traveled to Universal Studios to specifically go to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter for my elementary aged son who like many kids is a huge Harry Potter fan This was a first trip for us to the park (both Universal and Islands of Adventure) and admittedly we are accustomed to Disney parks. Here are some tips that we learned that I wish someone had told us before we arrived: 1. If you are a Florida resident and have purchased Florida resident passes or specials, every adult in your party has to show a Florida driver's license when you pick up your tickets even if you paid for them in advance. This created a huge mess for us - because one of the adults in our party didn't bring his driver's license. Nevermind that we purchased the tickets way in advance, both of our names on the credit card which paid for the Florida tickets, and that they mailed information to our Florida address - this all meant nothing. It was an awful ordeal to go through and really started off the day as what was very happy into an anxiety driven hot mess. Fortunately, we ultimately were able to prove that everyone in our party was legitimately a Florida resident. Michael at the front gate at Islands of Adventure with his smiling face and kind words was a welcomed sight and helped ease an otherwise chaotic and rocky start to our day. 2. We were given so many tickets for each "event" that it was hard to keep up with them. For example, each person is given a ticket to get into the parks; then there is a separate ticket for express lines; then there is yet another ticket for your room key; and if you purchase any meal plan, then there is another ticket for that. I counted we had 12 tickets! Plus, a Florida driver's license you have to have on your person, and credit cards! The Disney magic band has got logistics on Universal beat by a huge margin on this. Wear the magic band and all is magically taken care of! I missed Disney at this point. I heard several folks complaining about the ridiculousness of all the tickets. Bring yourself a good organizing wallet or neck pouch to handle all of your tickets and don't let the kiddos be in charge, because lose them and oh, well - good luck on that front ... and the tickets all resemble each other and aren't easily marked as what is what. 3. Be prepared to walk in the range of 4 to 6 miles. I knew there would be walking involved, but I had no idea how much. We stayed at the Loews Hotel thinking we'd be closer, and it was, but still we walked 4 to 6 miles per day, and we were focused on simply the area of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Even my husband who walks 10 miles per day said he never dreamed there would be that much walking involved from area to area. The boats do not drop you off in front of the Wizarding World - so they were pointless. Walking was the "closest" way to get there. The upside of this -- if you are looking for a weight loss, boot camp of sorts -- head over there. When I returned, I felt like I was ready to keep up walking 5Ks. So, that was positive. Even after eating what I wanted, I had lost 2 pounds with all the walking. 4. Shady spots to sit in and around the Wizarding World of Harry Potter (in both Islands of Adventure and Universal) are few. I was shocked as to how few benches or places to sit there were. We stood over other people waiting for them to move so we could sit down on a bench. Some people were sitting on the cement ground, but I couldn't bring myself to do that. 5. Bring your extra cash and credit cards because Wizarding World of Harry Potter is a commercial marketing mecca from start to finish. I was surprised by how much Universal charges in the Wizarding World for everything. Want to do the interactive game with the wand? Well, gotta buy the wand - my son, picked out the $40 one. Yikes! And there are the shirts, the food, the hats, the shops ... everywhere we turned it was another cash machine. Again, I think Disney is actually better than Universal on this one. At least, inside Disney there are some complimentary things your family can do without being hit up again and again. For example, you can pick up COMPLIMENTARY cards to play a sorcerer's game at the fire station at the entrance.  With all of that being said, I did rate the experience as "very good." The reason being is that you do feel transported to the area you are in - meaning you do feel like you are in Hogsmeade or Diagon Alley. Every area of the park was that way - whether you were in Springfield, Illinois with the Simpsons or Seusville. I just think Universal needs to figure out some better logistics and creature comforts for its guests, especially for those guests who are over the age of thirty or who are families with small children in tow. A tram or transport vehicle, more shady benches or sitting areas, and a few complimentary activities/items would go a long way, and put Universal on the same par as Disney parks, if not better than Disney parks.

Universal Studios is a great theme park. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is awesome! However, they are well aware that they have a captive audience and they don't mind making you pay for it. If you choose to save on hotel costs by staying off-site, a single day, park-to-park ticket can run upwards of $175 for an adult - without the Express Pass (essentially a shortcut in line for most rides). Park-to-Park tickets are the only way that you can ride the Hogwarts Express so that increases the cost. Staying at an on-site hotel can get very pricey (especially the hotels that include Express Pass), but you get into the parks an hour earlier than the general public and that can make a major difference in wait times for popular rides. We visited before they added Express Pass to the Harry Potter rides so I'm not sure how that will affect the wait times now. Adding the Express Pass to a regular ticket is SUPER expensive, and its worth is dependent upon time of year, how much you hate waiting in lines, and how many rides/attractions you want to do. Whether a visit to Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure is worth what it costs is definitely a matter of opinion. Everyone's idea of value is different. Overall, expect to pay a lot of money - for everything.
