If you are going to get the full Harry Potter experience, you must purchase park hopper ticket. Make sure to ride the train both ways from Universal to Islands of Adventure and then from Islands of Adventure back to Universal!

After spending a fortune at Disney, walking around in the heat, and riding boring rides, I spent a day at Universal Studios. Wow! The park is better designed and organized. The rides were vastly better, the lines were reasonable, and you can still get discounts in town if you are willing to spend 90 minutes in a time-share presentation. Go enjoy yourselves.
Visited in July was by far the best park not to big but everything in one spot there were lots to do and see lots of smoking spots about enjoyed the Christmas shop was really good

This was the best surprise ride of our trip. We were just trying to get through as many rides as possible with our fast passes when we decided to take a chance. It was awesome. If you are a fan of Fallon, you have seen him challenge guests to races of all sorts. This attraction combines that experience with popular New York City landmarks and takes the riders on a hilarious and high speed romp through The City. I will definitely take another turn on this one.

Very expensive for what you get. Is essentially an over priced strip mall with a few rides, which are not worth the waiting time, between expensive stores. Staff is unkind and in consistent. We were told different information by different employees. The entrance scans your finger print which is in settling. We were told we may not sit in chairs while we wait for a ride that you had to wait in two separate lines to ride. Would not recommend.
Young or old this place has something for everyone. If you can imagine a older adult, a child, and a kid enjoying the time of their lives....Its at this place.

what an amazing time. The rides were excellent my Favorite was the Simpsons ride, it was so funny. The best part was the refill cups I thought they were really handy and a good idea because you can have and fizzy drink or a slush. In the restaurants they had the drinks machines were you could fill up the cup your self but you could only have fizzy. All of the rides were really fun and I recommend this park.

We took our family to Orlando for Christmas. Some of the older kids wanted to go to Universal. We paid the inflated fee for both sides of the park so they could see all of Harry Potter. That is all we got to see. There was no way we could get on any rides as the wait lines were hours. Don't go there. At least at Disney you can get a fast pass to see your favorite picks and not have to pay extra like at Universal.

For me personally I feel the Universal is not worth the money we paid . If you purchase an express pass it can bring the cost of one day to over 400 dollars. And then if you wish to go to the or parks that's more money !!! And then on top it's 20 dollars to park !!! We did enjoy our day and some of the rides are fun . You do need a day to see it all. One thing in their favour was food is reasonably priced.
The park is awesome with favourite rides being The Mummy, transformers, simpsons, Hollywood rip ride rocket and minions! Get here early to avoid the queues on the minions rides!

Best part of Orlando . Loved Harry Potter World. Had an excellent time. The mummy,Jimmy Fallon and spider man were a blast. Enjoyed show at park closing and the parade A great time for young and old. If you can stay at a Universal hotel it is well worth it to get the fast pass. Saved a ton of waiting time.

Loved loved loved it! We had the park hopper which allowed us two days at both parks. Although Island's Adventure has the more exciting rides, but Universal Studios was just as much fun! Jimmy Fallon's Race through NY was a lot of fun, as was the Terminator show. MIB was fun and competitive :) Harry Potter is hands-down amazing. There is a dragon in the park that blows out fire every ten minutes, it's a definite experience. We had lunch at Monster's Cafe, which is a fun place to eat. We did several meet & greets and got to take pictures with our favorite characters. The Transformers ride is also amazing. There is A LOT of hype on the Minions ride, honestly if you don't do it you aren't missing a lot. We waited almost an hour in line at the very end of the day, and wished we hadn't. It's a 3D simulator as are many rides in this park and it just wasn't worth the wait. So if you don't do it, you aren't missing much. Everything was amazing and I would definitely go back!
Universal never fails to satisfy. There are rides for all tastes and ages especially if you are into high tech virtual reality 3D experiences.

Last visited in August 2014 and thought it was ok then. When you compare this to Islands of Adventure there is no comparison . Universal has a few food rides such as Harry Potter and The Mummy but the place needs updating . Rides such as ET and Shrek need getting rid or and replacing !  The parade was poor and lacked any imagination. If you have a choice head to Islands of Adventure!!

Visited both parks. Got there at opening and left at closing. All excellent. Rides were superb, no need for express pass. Lines were bearable. Had lunch at the Harry Potter restaurant and was excellent. Portions were huge. Great experience, awesome staff.
had a great time at universal as we had early entry to the parks so loved every min of it ,it did get very busy thou thats for sure
What can you say!? There is so much to see that you must take time to spend as long as possible on a visit. Dont' hurry and miss out.

We finally went to Universal after putting it off year after year to go somewhere else. Why did we wait so long! This was the best vacation ever. We stayed at Loews Royal Pacific Resort and got the free fast passes which was well worth it. We got the park to park tickets with a meal plan and unlimited drinks which was well worth it in the 97 degree heat. We are already planning our trip to come back next year!

Their are many great rides here, but Rock-It lets you select your own music and it syncs with the ride. I love rollercoasters and had never been on one that lets you play your own music, to enhance the ride. look up your song before you get on, and Rock it. I recommend 'Sabotage' by the Beastie Boys if you like that sort of thing.

Chris was a great worker, my friend and I did the doom ride consistently and loved talking with Chris. He told he has another job but prefers working at Universal because it brings him joy. Great and friendly guy who made my day.
I had a great time at Universal Studios with friends. It's a great tourist attraction with food, drinks, rides, shows and more....

We only had a day at Universal and so had to choose our park. We went for Universal Studios - not being 100% clear that the park is in fact split in to 3 parts. We went early and tried to do as many rides as possible early on. They quickly went up to 40mins+ waiting time. Minions was at 90 mins at 9am! Transformers was great and then we headed to the far side of the park quickly. Worth doing this. We then left at mid day for the hotel and came back at 7pm...we got two more rides in and there are lots of restaurants near by, so a good way of managing a day at a park.

This was the first day visit of our 2 week vacation. We are staying on resort so can enjoy the perks of early park entry and universal express. The early park entry was a disappointment (hence why 4 stars and not 5). Early park entry was advertised for select rides at each park. However we turned up at universal studios to be told that entry was for islands of adventure only. By the time we reached islands, it was already quite busy. Early park access was restricted to the Harry Potter area only, which again made the area very busy already at around 8.10. This really made the early park perk pointless. That all being said, we spent some time at islands until the studios, then hopped on the hogwarts train (fantastic ride) to universal studios. As we are travelling with a two and a half year old, a lot of our time is spent just soaking up the atmosphere, which is great. We spent a while at diagon alley and the London waterfront. Our boy loved the knight bus, and we enjoyed taking in all the details. I hopped on the gringotts ride, a fantastic rollercoaster/screen based ride, universal express was well worthwhile here. Only criticism was the dragon that sits above diagon alley is very loud and unavoidably intense. He roars and breathes fire every ten minutes, which caught my boy by surprise and really upset him. After leaving diagon alley we headed through the simpsons area and spent a few hours in the kids zone. The kid's area is a bit tired looking but still fun (rumoured to be replaced by Nintendo land in the future). Overall a fab few hours at the studios. Will be back for more soon
go early and beat the crowds and don't use the fast pass system its expensive and not much quicker. Use a shuttle bus or taxi and you will save a lot of time

Haven't been there in years, took my 5 year old for his first time. Once you get past the ridiculous entry fee and high prices for EVERYTHING, it is easy to have a good time. Long lines from 30 - 120 minutes, depending on the ride (we didn't have the express pass). My group and I all found the Rock'n'roll roller coaster too harsh and violent, not a good time. All other rides were cool, lots of fun. Takes a whole day to experience the entire park. Be prepared to walk a lot!

My favorite park. I went during a horror night event. I would suggest people to buy Universal Studio and Islands of Adventure for 2 days. Or buy 1 day with express pass. The lines gets really long and hot, so it's a good idea to do that.  MUST DO - HARRY POTTER WORLD! Eat at Mythos at Islands of Adventure.

Was very disappointed for the amount of money the tickets cost for a family of four. They have some new construction building new things somethings were close down and other things are just not there anymore

My 1st trip to Universal and it will be my last. This place has no atmosphere and I feel like I spent a lot of money for nothing. Of course Im comparing this to Disney. I've been to Disney probably 22 or 23 different times. Disney is far more organized and less chaotic.You get a lot more for the same amount of money. We had to wait 40 minutes to get our tickets at the entrance and they only had half of the ticket booths open. Some places in the park the workers awere rude to the ghast. Not to me personally, but I saw them snapping and other guest telling them to hurry up and get on rides without smiling or anything. Maybe I'm just spoiled but that is not the way it is at Disney. Of course you are periodically going to run into rude people everywhere you go, but here it seems like it's quite common. And this is just from one day at the park.
This is one of two parks that caters for everyone loved Hogwarts and all the rides. We keep on returning, five times now!!!

So we liked Universal Studios but like Islands of Adventure there were too many simulators! Our favorite rife was The Mummy!!! It was not a simulator but an indoor roller coaster!! Our next favorite was Men in Black where you got to shoot aliens. The guns could use some work but overall a great ride. The Simpsons, Terminator, Jimmy Fallon, and many others were simulators. Make more real rides!!!
I love it here I am a annual passholder! I'm always coming here with friends for fun! No matter how many times I visit I'm never bored there is always something to do. Best ride is the Mummy!

My child is a huge Harry Potter fan so a trip to both the Universal Studios and Island of Adventure is a must. This is a must place to visit for Potterheads. We were here for two days because we wanted to make sure we have enough time cover every inch of the Harry Potter World. We were able to do that and have enough time left to visit other great attractions in the parks such as King Kong and Jurassic Park.  We only cared about the Harry Potter world though to be honest. If we had to do it all over again, I would get an Express Pass, and do all the Harry Potter stuff in one day instead.

A gpod/great day out, the park attention to detail is amazing. Walking around some of the city replicas it's hard to remember the buildings aren't real. Springfield is mind blowing for the work they've put into it. Most of the rides are simulators, alot 3D. By the end of the day they are all getting a bit samey. The Rip Rocket is the only real ride in the place. They're good but there's just too many of similar rides. The customer service is ok but in the 4 days we were there only had a few staff were who were warm and pleasant. Quite a few made you feel as they were doing you a favour. I felt prices were a bit steep, I noticed a difference after Disney. Quite a lot of the time I felt as I was getting ripped off. $20 to park!!!!!! And there's still a huge walk to get in. If you finish your day at the back of the park it's a 45mins walk to the car. At least in Disney there are trams, monorails, parking staff & roads built to help you out... that's why THEY charge $20. Its chaos getting out of this place, no help at all and you have to fight onto IDrive! Universal is just greedy.  Would have been 3 stars, felt robbed & abandoned but Springfield won a star back.
Ensure you get park to park tickets and buy unlimited fast passes which are around $80 each. Yes expensive but it will make the most out of your day rather than queing most of it.
If you go to Universal do not miss the full Harry Potter experience. Gringots bank ride is amazing, as is the train ride from Universal to Hogsmead !

So not so much of a big deal as advertised. If your staying at one of the resort hotels there is bus transportation, the only drawback I see in this is there is only one drop off for all the hotels. The point that I'm making is from that point to the parks you have to go thru the City Walk, which is at least 1/4 of mile. This way they can get your food money right off. Mostly high end restaurants. It is a beautiful park with many interesting attractions and many places to eat. Our average for two days was at least $40.00 for two people. So if your on a budget beware. The Cabana Bay hotel not any cheaper. Bring plenty of money or be prepared to quickly max or stretch out your credit card. I really can say without a doubt I will not be back. I'd rather go down the road 4 miles and have more fun. This only my opinion and you'll have to judge this for yourself. One last note bring sunglasses and some type of head wear there's not much shade.

Visited Universal Studios Halloween Horror night on 17th Sept. A really good evening at the park. Didn't manage to see everything in the one night even though the queues wasn't that long, maximum one was roughly 30mins. The Horror Studios were very good with some brill actors. Quite a lot of walking so comfy shoes needed. A few of the rides were shut were closed for evening maintenance but it wasn't a problem. Staff was helpful and you need a map to pick the bits you want to see.

Absolutely loved it here! So much to do and the scenery and atmosphere is incredible. The Harry Potter part of the park is incredible and walking into the area for the first time is amazing, especially the huge dragon ontop of the building. Simpsons world is great fun and the Krusty burgers and big pink donuts are really nice! Cannot wait to return to universal studios one day.

Man, there was so much to do! So much so, that I have to go back as soon as possible in order to finish everything up. I was even invited to screen and survey some promotional trailers for shows about to premier this fall, for which I received a $20 gift card! This was hands down my best vacation, thus far.
This was my first time at the original universal studios park in a while. The rides have really improved. The Rock It roller coaster and the Transformers ride were the best rides.

40,000 (mostly) geeks descended on Universal for an evening of fun after a week long conference. What a great time we had. The park is clean, well organized and as expected, somewhat expensive. A great time was had by all.

Came here for our two week summer holidays and never got bored. There is so much to see and do. Love everything about this place. The atmosphere, the rides, the staff, the food. Cant wait to come back in 2019.

If you've been to any of the parks you know that although there are multiple restaurants the food menu is nearly the same no matter where you eat and the quality is typically mediocre at best. I don't know why, after having visited Universal studios so many times, that I had never tried this restaurant, but I'm so happy I did. The menu was different from the other "restaurants" in Universal and the quality was unlike any other restaurant I've been to in Universal. It starts with the fact that you actually sit down and order vs you get up and order and then sit down. This restaurant is located in the "wharf" area and there are other seafood restaurants in the same block/building there that I will have to check out next time I go.
We had never been but finally decided to this year. It was a blast! All of the houses and the theming were great. Good job universal!

We visited in September and managed to go to the first 3 Halloween Horror Nights - we really loved this, lots of scares, plenty to see and lots of rides such as the Mummy and Rip Ride Rocket stay open. We would definitely recommend but not for the faint hearted !. Great fun 😀

I gotta say, I overheard the gist of this ride and thought naa I'll go ride the hulk again. But then I decided to wait the line and ride this. I am really glad I did. It is pretty amazing how they have designed it to feel just as cool, rough, in the middle of it all, etc. I would have rode again if the line wasn't so long.

We stayed at a Universal Orlando Hotel for 14 nights, and spent our time visiting the three parks (Universal Studios, Islands of Adventure and Volcano Bay). Our 14 days were full of absolute fun. Universal Studios has an excellent selection of world-class rides and experiences, obviously with Diagon Alley being a major attraction. Visiting in October we experienced virtually no queues at all, meaning that we hardly ever used our Fast-Pass included in our hotel stay. We can't wait to return!

Universal was the original of the three parks. There are plenty of rides and theatre like experiences, but it is worth the extra to do HHN. Our favourite Haunted House was "Texas Chainsaw Massacre", when you see panic stricken young men out side the house, mission accomplished.

We had our first visit to the Orlando area at the beginning of October and we loved Universal! Our girls love Harry Potter and I was genuinely impressed with the rides - the technology is amazing, truly! Overall, I liked that there were a lot of food options, many places to sit down and rest, and also enough to keep you interested. Every park employee I encountered was very nice!

Very disappointed by my recent visit to your horror night event, clearly a case of profit over guest satisfaction. You had obviously issued too many tickets for the event which resulted in a very poor experience in the park, horror houses were basically one big line of people meaning there was no scare factor to them as you could see what was coming as it happened to the guests in front, express pass was a complete rip off as you still had to wait over 30 minutes in line for each of the attractions. Cast member were miserable and clearly not interested in being there. Not the experience I would have hoped for having spent $1000 for 5 of us to attend. Guest services on the night were not interested in dealing with complaints.
Universal does it again. Everything close together and all the entertainment was good quality. We went Sept/Oct so didn't need a fast pass as waiting times were good. I may actually return here.
Really enjoyed it, only spent one day here so definitely had to rush to see everything. Prices are expensive but a great day of memories for our family.

We visit the park every year for Horror Nights and this year did not disappoint! The haunted houses were good, scarecrow being the absolute best! Unfortunately it looks like Bill and Teds show will be done after this year, that is very disappointing as it has been so great, hopefully they will have something just as good in the future. We bought annual passes this time so we will be back more often and next Halloween this will still be a must!

For older children and adults, there is no place that can beat Universal Studios Orlando. We traveled with another family in October, the weather was around 82 every day with less humidity and only one half day of rain out of 6 (pack your dollar store ponchos and put them in your purse for this reason!). We stayed at the resort, so ease of moving back and forth between the hotel and arks was great, and we had express passes included, which meant we literally had no wait time on at least 90% of rides. On the few we had to wait for the max was 20 minutes. We rode everything, did everything, ate anywhere we wanted (no reservations needed) and well, had a wonderful vacation! Again, bring the tiny dollar store ponchos in case of a pop-up raincloud, bring a folded up plastic bag to throw belongings in for Popeye's Bilge Rat Barges in Islands of Adventure, keep your bags small to fit in the lockers required for may rides, wear comfortable shoes, and bring an empty water bottle to fill at the water fountains to stay hydrated, and you are good as gold. I cannot say enough about how much I love this place!

Go to all three parks and CityWalk. CityWalk has great restaurants nightclubs and stores. It is one of the safest places to go in Orlando. Everyone goes through metal detectors including cast members and hotel guest!

Any trip to universal Orlando is always a great time we had such a great time from the moment we stepped foot there. The entertainment is excellent and the food my god so many great places to eat. I love the food the resturants are awesome city walk is great just a good time all the time can't wait to go back in 2018 😀

Compared to the Disney parks the Universal parks are much better. A lot of the rides, and there are more here, are sims/3 or 4 D including Dispicable Me, Transformers, Shrek, The Simpsons, ET and the Hogwarts Express to Islands of Adventure. The most extreme ride is the Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket whicd starts by going straight up, vertically until your at the top then all speed round the coaster, a real thrill ride. The indoor coaster Revenge of the Mummy also good. The parade is small but very enjoyable but dont miss it as it was only one a day. The queue for the Hogwarts Express to the other park was over an hour but this may have been down to the time of day as we went at 16.15 as the park officially shut at 5pm and Islands of Adventure open until 8pm. It is only about a 3 min journey and you wear sim glasses as the windows are computerised. It would have been quicker to walk between the parks

10 years ago we brought my 5 year old grand son 9 and 12 year old grand daughters to Florida they all three said they lived universal so much more than other Florida attractions.  So this year we brought my 7 and 5 year old grandson and they were absolutely thrilled with universal and said they only want to visit universal and they don't even want to go at all to any other Orlando attractions . We are coming back in February 2018 and they are so excited! Non Of us Can hardly wait!
The lines to ride a 3-D experience were no less than 60-80 minutes. Red Rocket roller coaster would be fun if not for the whiplash and bruises.
wonderful park loved the rides thought that this was better then universal's island of adventure and the macy's day parade was great
We took our 4 year old on his trip to Universal he loved every minute of it and so did we as the parents. Looking forward to our next visit next summer.

We have been to Disneyland several times and have always enjoyed our experience with our children, however upon learning about Ollivanders at Harry Potter we were intrigued by it, after an hour wait we thought it was going to be worth it with good reviews about the experience, however it would have to be the worst time wasting experience ever- unless your a Harry Potter fanatic and even then it would surely disappoint many. Upon entry you are greeted by a lady who talks a few words about wands, then thinking we might be entering into an exciting room we are taken into the gift shop and that was it. I could not believe it. I won’t ever get my wasted one hour waiting in line again but unless you have time to spare this is a complete disappointment to Disney.
Diagon Alley, San Francisco, New York, Spiderman, Race Through New York with Jimmy Fallon, The Mummy. Lunch at the Leaky Cauldron was yummy!
Very nice and expensive lol. Overall a great place for family and to walk around. Definitely a lot of shops, lounges and restaurants.

On this ride, they make it very 3D and realistic that makes it look like you are speeding through the New York streets in a street car watching the fights between Spider-man and all of the villains, and with my experience, it seems a little scary for younger ones because there’s a lot of screaming, and there’s one scene where it looks like fire is coming towards you, but it’s really not.
Had such a fun time here. No lines except for the Harry Potter world. I can see the place gets crowded, so don't know if I was just lucky or if off season.

We had the 2-park hopper tickets and started our day at Universal Studios. With front of the line passes on a Friday in early December (park was not busy) we easily got through the rides we were interested in by 11 (entered the park at 9). Unfortunately one of the shows we wanted to see didn’t start until 12 and we were ready to head to the other park well before that time.  One thing that was rather surprising / disturbing…. I put my bag in a finger-print activated locker while we went on the MIB ride. I could not get the locker opened after the ride (that’s ok – technology is not fool-proof). I got one of the workers to help me and she just opened the locker and let me take the contents without even attempting to verify it was my bag.

This place has rides that will get people's adrenaline juices going, but they scare the devil out of me. There are 3D similator rides for Shrek devotees, ditto for Despicable Me fans (love those Minions!), New York street scenes, San Francisco street scenes, and all leads to Harry Potter World at Diagon Alley hidden behind King's Cross station. There are many restaurants and snack stands available between the Port of Entry entrance and the various parts of this theme park. If you get your mug shot taken at the Port of Entry, the pretty photographer will give you a ticket to pick it up at a store on the street. There's a holiday parade around 5:30-ish, but it's nothing to write home about: just red-and-white-Christmas themed musicians and dancers marching and dancing throughout the park: the lady dancers were cute to look at. I had a late lunch at Richter's Burgers in the San Francisco part of the park. Don't bother going here: their burgers are not as juicy as advertised: if you want juicy burgers, go to Wendy's or Burger King. I had trouble getting one of those refillable Coke cups at this place, which downgraded my impression of this establishment. Also, if families have kids who want to get their sugar fix, they could do so at the adjacent bulk candy store. I already satisfied my sweet tooth craving by visiting Honey Dukes, and I didn't need to satisfy it further by buying more candy at this store. At least it wasn't as crowded as Honey Dukes was. Overall, the visitors are nice, and so are the ride operators and service staff. They helped me form a more favorable impression of this park than the Richeter's Burger place did.

This was our second year of coming to universal for Christmas vacation. I was worried that we would get bored with this being a repeat. Happy to say we had a great time. Express pass is sooo worth it but not as good as the previous year. Looks like people are catching on. Rides are much better than disney for older kids.

Love these parks!!! Haven't been since they added Harry Potter area - we loved it all ;) The train ride was cool... We did a few new rides that we never did before, then went and did the old school rides the second day.  Shame to the people complaining in the last few reviews about the lines -- of course there are lines, its DECEMBER and the holidays - families traveling for Christmas and New Years - my Lord :) You get what you pay for and depends on how important you think things are -- yes, we waited on some lines - it was December 26 and 28th and the lines were LONG - we waited for the most important ones, some we by passed and went back too - first timers, I can see if you get overwhelmed.  We even had a wheelchair for my husband who hurt his knee the week before our trip - and a crutch - and NO... he didn't get special treatment with a wheelchair... no handicap accessibility -- we paid for the wheelchair so he can rest when we were on the rides, so he didn't have to find a seat on the side to rest and ice his knee. He still had to wait with us on the rides he did go on and was available to go on w/ a bum knee.  I will say people are inconsiderate... selfish --- all about them.. thats the sad part ;) I feel bad for people who cannot be considerate... that rant over! LOL  The christmas parade by Macy's was there - crowded, YES -- ONCE AGAIN, IT'S THE HOLIDAYS --- the resorts too - the traffic on i-4 - international drive too!! This is what happens you are a tourist and etc, just think if you lived here everyday and had to deal with all this traffic.  I'm sorry - you have to know what you are getting into when you come PEAK TIMES, Tourists - Europe USA anywhere, it's crazy -- Disney is the same - OK - Off my soap box now!!  We had a blast --- know before you go - we bought 2 day passes got 2 days free - 2 parks, had a TERRIFIC TIME!!! FAMILY TIME!!! Memories made!!! we didn't get fast pass lanes either...  Coming back in 3 months too for another trip - just us girls!! Leaving the boys home! LOL :)

I went to Universal on the 26th and the 27th of December and knew there would be crowds, but that didn’t stop me. I had an amazing time and enjoyed all of the shows, Sponge Bob, Pets, Dora and Despicable. The super star parade was awesome and the holiday parade was amazing. Would go again for Christmas even with the crowds!!

Defo more for kids, however, we went on rides, enjoyed food and drinks and made the most of our visit. LOVED the Transformers ride, and of course Harry Potter was amazing too. This resort is more for kids. Loved the area around the Studios though, great places for food and drink and to just chill while people watching. Great times!

Its been awhile. Jaws is gone. Back to the Future is the Simpsons. Hitchcock is Shrek. But everything they replaced the classics with are worth it. Obviously Harry Potter is awesome. The Gringotts ride was my favorite from both parks. Leaky Cauldron food was fantastic. Jimmy Fallon was a lot of fun. Can’t wait to go back.

This is the first time we had been back to Orlando for 9 years and it was a nightmare. They advertise as where dreams come true Orlando must change it too where queues come true. Disney,Universal and Sea world attractions have got it all wrong now with charging for car parking which you can now pay for VIP parking from an average 20 dollars to 40 dollars on top of the park entry ticket cost which has you waiting at the entry booths for up to an hour this is before you get into the parks. This is an average day at the parks there were two families of us and we tried to get too the parks about 09.00 and so did everybody else. When you do get to the park gates the first hurdle is the bag search that can also take up to an hour to get through them as there is not enough bag search people working. When through this another queue to get your fingerprint and photo taken for your pass so you cannot pass on to anybody else eventually get into the park 10.30. The fast pass carry on was not fully described to us on our first day and this is another shambles these must be booked prior to you coming to the park on the app or computer disney link to give you any chance of getting on any of the rides. The fast pass fiasco only gives you 3 rides that you can get early access too or you have to take your chance and sit in the queues which has now got out of hand letting too many people in to the parks with most rides over 200 mins to wait for. Disney and Universal have put profit before enjoyment waiting in excess of 3 hours for a 2 min ride is a farce. Be warned if you go at a busy time of the year you need to book rides before you go to the parks. Universal is the worst with the quick queue pass which was at 159 dollars each on top of your entry ticket and parking charge allowing you to half the queue times which was also a sham. Harry Potter,Kong,Spiderman and Hulk rides all over 200 mins when we arrived at the park a few were off due to the bad weather which adds to the misery. This is what you can expect on a normal day.  Most popular ride 200 mins waiting time which is around 3 hours for a 2 min ride is totally unacceptable and why should people pay over and above the admission ticket too still queue for over an hour too many people allowed into the parks during xmas and new year management have got it all wrong and we will certainly not be back to Orlando Parks again. The whole experience of Disney and Universal has lost its way to money grabbing profit and do not cater for the punter now a rip off.

We have had it with theme parks. We had some bad experiences with regard to excessive crowd sizes/wait times at parks in some other states, but we thought A world-class resort like Orlando Studio's would have figured out how to mitigate that somehow, right? Nope.  There was the 385 minute wait to ride the hulk coaster...over 6 hours...seriously? The shortest line during our 2 day visit was 30 minutes for E.T., which is an old, obsolete attraction that did not impress.  We did "pre-register for Jimmy Fallon's New York ride, which was awesome. We registered upon arrival, were given a time to return, and then the line was actually enjoyable based on the live entertainment, the video entertainment and so forth. The ride itself, while short, was excellent.  However, we only rode on 3 ride in 2 days, plus observed a live performance of "Fear Factor".  Universal Studios: Here's a thought....raise your ticket prices so that you reduce the load in the park while still maintaining revenues. Maybe if you double your entrance fee you'd cut your load in half?  Also, hire a flow analysis engineer to figure out ways to relieve bottlenecks at the attractions. Perhaps the Jimmy Fallon ride is a glimpse at the future?  Otherwise we enjoyed walking through the park, it really is a cool place. Was it worth $800 to do so? No.

We were so amazed with Harry Potter Worlds. If you are a Potter Fan then this is the place for you!! Our son was lucky enough to be picked at Ollivander's . The magic and the wizards and Hogwarts Express were so good. Tip: Go on a rainy day. We did and there were like no lines. We went on a sunny day and we could hardly get through the lines. We got the dining plans and they were worth it (get the one with the souvenir mug) Butter Bear is like $7 or $8 alone and it comes with the meal plan Eat at 3 BroomSticks! Way better food selections and better prices than any other place. The other Potter Restraunt was okay but did not have the same food choices. Go early, less lines Bring hand sanitizer  Overall, all of Universal Studios and all the parks were amazing. A lot of work and worth the money to go at least once in your life. I suggest going 2 days if you want to cover everything, especially if you land on a busy day.  One thing I did not find fair is the front of line passes. I think Universal should do the same as Disney with Fast Passes so that everyone has equal opportunity. It cost us like $1000 to go and it was like our money wasn't good enough to the people who had more to buy the front of the line passes. Some lines were 4 hours to wait on (so we didn't go) so if you had front of line passes you wouldn't wait that... not everyone has that kind of money to spend so much more and so it makes a person feel that the money they saved and worked hard to go to didn't matter as much as the people that had more. Disney gives Everyone the same opportunity. Universal cators to the higherarchy when it comes to rides that can afford to cough up more.  All in all, it is a must see and a place to go to

Loved our time at Universal. We had a 3 day park to park ticket which was great, as we went during the busy period. Our first few days were just after New Years. So still crazy busy. We did not have fast passes, so had to wait. Some wait times were 90-120 mins. Sometimes we went single rider. At times it was faster but at some rides it was slower. The first two days we went first to Universal then the second day Islands of Adventure. Didn't utilize the park to park. Our 3rd day was on Monday Jan the 8th. Weather was nice park was not so busy, wait times were short early in day which we took advantage of. We went to both parks that day. So much to see and do. Rides are amazing the whole atmosphere and buildings they are in like Harry Potter and King Kong so realistic. Harry Potter worlds were great. Loved the frozen butter beer. My Favourite ride was Hulk. Thought both parks were nice and colourful.

This place was absolutely an another happiest place on earth. It doesn’t matter if you are an adult or kid because this place is perfect for everyone. As soon as we entered the entrance we felt that we were still kids at heart. Me and my husband stroll around the studio and we experienced the Shrek 3D, Transformers and some of the hottest spots there. This place has a lot of choices whether you want to go on the adventure side or just to go for shopping and taking pictures at the same time. They have a lot of shows especially in the afternoon and they usually announced it or put it on their maps and itinerary so that you will not missed out any of the shows. The best part of coming here was the fireworks display at the end. It was fantastic!!

It’s a great park, BUT I have to tell you a pair of issues.  FIRST. As you buy the tickets, they will offer you a 3 park hopper ticket that is really expensive, the thing is that actually you will hardly finish two parks in one day; so, you can buy a two park ticket and it will save you a lot (most if you’re traveling with family).  SECOND. There were waiting times on attractions as long as 240 minutes (YES 4 hours). We actually only got to ride en 4 attractions. So, as you can see, it wasn’t a very fortunate experience.  They sell a fast pas ticket that cost twice as the regular, but you have that option...

For a great meal with the Jimmy Buffett feel this is the place. The food is good, the service was excellent. And you get a bonus of 10% off merchandise if you show your receipt that you ate there. Hint. If you just mention it they will give you the discount! Get onion rings on a little plane.
Fun Theme park. Lesser known that Disney parks but just as fun and has a great atmosphere. Love the ET ride, it's my favorite and so nostalgic. Can't wait to visit again.

Universal definitely has a wide variety of rides, most of which are really good. Some areas of the park are dated however for the most part most areas are well themed and very clean. I would recommend this for anyone over the age of 5-6. Many of the rides are much to intense for those younger and many will not meet the minimum height requirement.  The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was exceptional. The theming and execution is extraordinary and not to mention the rides, which topped off the experience and immersion. This is a must see for Harry Potter fans. Even if you aren’t a fan you will still be amazed.

Loved our time here compared to Disney World. The food was better (Monster Cafe), there are more places to sit and relax and it's cheaper. More rides for the teens and definitely a lot of magic in Harry Potter's world. I appreciated that most of the rides have lines that are in a building so you're not exposed to the weather. They have a refillable cup for drinks which includes Icees. We spent an equal amount of days here and Disney World and the kids and I agreed that the experience here is much better. This is our new park when in Orlando. No more Disney World, they no longer value their guests.

This place was amazing with so much to see and the Rides were Fantastic .We found it was more geared to adults not much but a little than the Magic Kingdom ,we spent 3 days covering Universal Studios ,with the City Walk and Bubba Gump Shrimp or Margeritaville ,So much for your eyes to take In and the variety of Foods to choose from .There were no long waits for the Rides here and the Rides were longer and so realalistic, and fun ...Would definately visit again

I highly recommend Harry Potter World! The simulation rides are all amazing! Very well put together. Speed passes are definitely recommend though other wise the lines. Jimmy Fallon, King Kong, the minions, transformers, rides were all great! All simulation though I wouldn't suggest if you get sick easily or have anxiety. Very large park with lots of options as far as food and drinks. Good for families and younger kids. Super fun, great for friends! I went for a friends birthday we all had a blast! Mardi Gras is happening now parade is awesome good alcoholic beverages. We will be back soon. Universal Citywalk is right there with great shops and tons of restaurants.

I enjoy going to Universal Studios pretty often. I was there for a day during Celebration of Harry Potter. I like the different events you can enjoy like Mardi Gras and Halloween Horror Nights. There’s plenty to do besides rides. You can go to the shows as well. There are plenty of things for the whole family.

Trip # 2 and counting. Stayed at an "On Property" Hotel and that helped us enjoy each of the three parks to the max. One benefit EXPRESS PASS That only saved about a week of queuing time! Hate queues.. Brits really don't like them, we just have world class ability to make them painful and slow.  Universal LA is the iconic one with the back-lot tour etc, Orlando resort stands on its own as a great resort to come and have as much fun as possible in a day or 10 in our case,  The place is just awesome on a planetary scale. If I was American, (which I'm not, but this place makes me wish I was) I'd keep it quiet before the whole of the rest of the world works out how great this place is and then turns up for a party!  Only downside, being north of 50.... the beans run out before I'm ready to quit!

My family and I try to come here once a year. Never too old for this park! Something for everyone. The fast passes are well worth it, and if you stay in certain hotels (we stay at Hard Rock) they are included!!
We had a great time, but the park was oversold. Hard to find the Harry Potter rides, and had to use Express Passes to get on rides. Otherwise a 30 min to 2 hour wait.
Thought our teen would go directly to Harry Potter, but he didn't. In fact, we didn't make it there until the next day! Great family fun for everyone. Absolutely as good as Disney!

Hated my experience! I took my family to Universal Studios. I read from experienced amusement park fans that to really enjoy the experience you need to pay the extra $69-99 Express pass. I figured $124/day/person/park was good enough. (X 4 people = $500). No. You wait for hours while the express pass people blow by you. So we would have to spend $800/day just to have a decent experience! Crazy! Of course lots of people do pay that and don’t mind. But despite being a nice amusement park, the overall experience for me and my family was NOT worth it. You really need to ‘upgrade’ to the 1st class experience $200/day ticket to avoid being disappointed. But of course that’s EXACTLY what Universal wants you to do. So it’s a rigged deal. 1st class = great. 2nd class = miserable. Unless you have the money to upgrade to Express Pass. Skip it!

My inner child emerged in the magical place.... the discarding world is amazing and so much went into the Hogwarts express.... however wish it was more disabled friendly... when I go again I will get the xpress pass as we waited too long in all the ques... me and my dad went on the Jurassic park ride just because it was a short line however I was so scared and my dad did not make it any better and maybe need some more heaters available for the winter... can't wait to go again and I'm definitely waiting on the trolls section

This is one of the best theme parks in Orlando. Going in Feb meant it wasn't as busy as the Summer months. Still recommend buying Xpress passes though so you can skip the line at most of the attractions. Staff friendly & courteous. We had smiles on our faces all day. Highly recommended!

We visited Universal Studios during Mardi Gras and the parade was awesome. Very beautiful floats and lots of beads thrown out.  The park was nice and clean but like some other reviews, I thought the number of 3D/4D rides were overkill. Having a nice mix of thrill rides that didn’t require glasses would have earned 5 stars.  The Hulk roller coaster is one of the best I’ve been on, yet, the red Rip one was rough and can make your head hurt. The Kong Skull Island and Spider-Man rides were great and the Jimmy Fallon area was fun. Overall, we had a fun trip and it was a nice change from the Mickeys.  We are not huge Harry Potter fans even though their areas in the park were cool but I would not pay extra for tickets that include the train ride next time around. It just wasn’t worth it to us. However, be prepared to walk a lot.  Citywalk is cool and having an actual parking garage is top notch. It’s worth $20 just to have your vehicle protected from the weather. Just know that after 6 pm, it’s free.

The big 'misser' of this part of the Universal Studios park is not being able to actually go inside of the Hogwarts Castle. The various other shops in Hogsmeade are fantastically realized in amazing detail, but I really wanted to see the castle interior. Perhaps the most entertaining experience I had was watching the park staff at the Raptor cage convince two young kids that the raptor was real. Never broke character once! The Skull Island ride had too much going on to catch everything in a single ride. Note: If you take the express lane, the wait is /really/ boring. They didn't add in the unique features that you get if you take the regular line. Of all the rides, I think I liked the Hulk roller coaster best. I waited to go into the front seat, but I think it would have been even better to be near the back of the coaster. Hogwarts Express was down nearly the whole day, so I was glad to have used my park-to-park extensively the day before.

Visited over several days. Most rides had relatively short wait times. Many rides combine 3D effects with moving rides. Also some fast roller coasters and smaller track rides. Some rides require lockers and some are not open to all body types. Enjoyed fear factor live and Horror Make-up show. Mardi Gras parade was fun as well. Would recommend for families with older children and adults.

I heard Race Through New York Starring Jimmy Fallon had poor reviews. The line was short so we decided to try it and I loved it! Not sure why the reviews were bad, it was an action packed flight simulator, lots of fun.

...but it is impossible not to have a good time. Totally recommend the express ticket, especially for grumpy old gits like me! We had a great day, despite my best efforts! That has to be high praise indeed.

This was the first time we have taken our two sons (8&11) to a theme park, and everyone had a great time. I didn't realize that so many of the rides were 3D/4D, which made me pretty queasy, which was unfortunate because they were so elaborate and well done, I wanted to keep my eyes open! Since we were visiting over Spring Break, we opted to stay at the nearby Hard Rock Hotel so that we could the Express Passes, and we were so glad we did. We waited at most about 30 minutes for the most popular rides while those without the passes were waiting 90 minutes or more. We spent a day at USF and a day at IOA and then went back to Universal for part of a third day for everyone to do their favorite rides again. Since we had Express Passes, we thought a day for each park was adequate. We loved the Harry Potter areas of each park, the attention to detail was fantastic. Unfortunately these are probably the most popular areas of both parks and were packed with people during our visit. We would like to return during a less busy time of year to explore them a bit further. We really enjoyed the Hogwarts Express, but if you aren't a HP fan, you could easily skip the extra cost of the Park to Park option. We were only disappointed by a couple of things, one was the lack of healthy dining options. There was a couple of stands with fruit and a few salads available here and there, but otherwise it was all fast food (pizza, burgers, corn dogs, pretzels, chips, sweets) at the "quick service" places. We opted to bring in healthier food for lunches/snacks, water bottles to refill, and were so glad we did. The second was the cost of everything at the souvenir shops. As I mentioned, having never visited a large theme park before with our kids, we expected prices to be high, but we were disappointed to see just how much Universal charged for all of the merchandise. My kids wanted to buy a few small souvenirs with their own money and there really didn't seem to be much they could afford, you were hard pressed to find anything for under $20. There seemed to be plenty of people who were willing to pay the steep prices for food and merchandise, so I understand that's why they charge as much as they do. We found the parks to be very clean, and the employees friendly, we will definitely return sometime in the coming years.

There will be plenty of other reviews explaining all the attractions, so let me try here to do something different.  First all all: the rides are all great. Universal went all in on the 4D experience, which means you'll see a lot of 3D (like) movies during which you're shaken around in your seat to make the experience more lively. Universal excels at this. The newer the attraction, the more spectacular the effects. But that does not mean that older attractions are not boatloads of fun either. The Transformers effects are the most immersive. The Harry Potter rides are the most magic. The Simpsons and Spiderman are the most fun. And do not overlook the Blues Brothers show - one of the longest running in the park.  Second, the fast-pass. I am no fan of the whole idea, but it exists so here we go. The fastpass allows you to pass most of the lines. A day was plenty of time in either park (we visited during Spring Break in March). Plenty of time to do every ride we wanted and some multiple times. Cool. It is worth noting that if you stay in a Universal hotel, your room key doubles as a fast-pass, and that you can really walk from the hotel to the park in 10 minutes, eliminating the need for a rental car and parking fees. It's still very expensive, so you'll have to do the math on whether it's worth it. It's worth noting that tricks that you can find online about the variations in the wait times during the day play out pretty well. Come early and go for the popular (Harry Potter) rides first. Lines are shorter during lunch and parades. A lot of people poop out towards the end of the long days.  Having said that, here are some improvement points for Universal.  First, it appears that Universal ordered most rides assuming that all visitors are under 6'2" and 200 lbs. That (rightfully) pissed of a lot of tall and fat people, and they wiggled in some larger seating, but as a 6'8" adult, I still didn't fit in the Mummy ride, and while I fit, I was not comfortable riding the Hulk. So, if you're on the taller or wider side, be aware: you will be squished. However, staff will accommodate you as much as they can. Most rides have one row of slightly larger seats and in some rides they'll give you two seats when you point out the obvious. We found staff very accommodating, even though they did shove us in the front row of the Jurassic Park ride and drenched us ;-) An unrelated tip is to avoid a backpack if you can. You can not ride certain rides with one. Wear cargo pants and shove a bottle of water in there that you refill at the water fountains.  Second, the food. We could see Universal is trying with the quality, but most meals remain the standard American staples of fried stuff with cheese with no veggies in sight. The portions are way too large. No one needs three of those meals a day. What is needed is small on-the-go snacks and meals. There is is copy King's Cross station, so go to actual King's Cross station in London and see what they offer train riders in the UK and offer that to your visitors. Fresh simple sandwiches. Fruit cups. Simple healthier snacks. Smaller snacks. Not all meals have to be supersized. Especially considering my point above.  Third, where are the female heroes? Harry Potter, Spiderman, Jimmy Fallon, Popeye, Hagar, Poseidon. Are all heroes white men? Sure the Minions and Simpsons are yellow, but in reality, the only non-white heroes are the Hulk, the Men in Black and Marylin Monroe. You can do better Universal, especially since we did note that your staff is very diverse, including some handicapped people, which was great to see.  And the same commentary goes for Islands of Adventure park.

For adults Universal is soooo much better than Disney. So many more adults rides. What else is nice is as you walk to each ride or adventure there's entertainment in the street. I love the Mardi gras parade at night and there is always big entertainment for concerts.

There are hundreds of ways to go about the park, but after today, here are some tips on what worked for us, or what didnt: 1. If you can do it, do get the past pass, it is worth every penny, we never stood in line for more than 10 minutes. 2. Do bring munchies, it helps a lot. 3. Dont rush in the morning. Most of us rushed in the morning, and rushed to go everywhere, and by 3 pm we were pretty much done... Take it easy, enjoy the park, the walk, the scenery.. 4. Sunblock, hats, hidration... Must! 5. Expect park food, lots of pizza, burgers, hotdogs, nuggets, etc...  We did go in peak season, and you can just do the park in one day, and enjoy it, without rushing.  The rides are incredible... Dont miss them.

Busy time during spring break. Harry potter world is excellent. Go early in the morning. Need park-to-park option to ride the Hogwarts train between parks. Each direction has different views and stories. During spring break, have the express ride option is very helpful to reduce waits. Would be worth staying at one of the Universal hotel to get free express passes

My husband, daughters(11,13), and I visited USF in early March. We were not sure what to expect, as I was the only one who had visited before, and it was many years ago. Due to budget restraints we visited both Universal parks in one day. We arrived early and headed straight to Diagon Alley. We walked right on Escape from Gringotts and were able to see Olivanders before the crowd started to grow. This was the highlight of the park. It was amazingly detailed and an exciting start to the day. The ride was my favorite from both parks. We left Diagon Alley and circled around the park with a goal of returning to ride the Hogwarts Express to Islands of Adventure by early afternoon. Most of the family enjoyed the rest of the park. In my opinion there were a lot of rides that were exactly the same (motion simulators) with only the theme being different. By afternoon we did not have time to ride some of the larger attractions (Minions, Shrek, Rip a Ride Rockit, Transformers) due to wait time and our goal of visiting both parks. This may have shaped my opinion, but overall I was disappointed in the majority of the park. The rides were repetitive and the food subpar. I wish we would have just spent the day throughly exploring both Harry Potter worlds and avoided the rest of the parks. I did give a four star rating because the rest of my family seemed to enjoy the majority of the park more than I did, and also because Diagon Alley is worth a trip all on its own.

A little busy because of spring break but we had great time. - arrive early (right when the park is open is ideal) - have your ticket print/ready to go (so you won't be in line to but/pick up, etc) - don't bring backpack or bags if you can help it (some rides required items to be lock in the free locker during the ride) so you can go directly to the ride - go to the ride you want to ride most so you won't miss it (for us it was harry potter escape from gringotts ride) - whenever possible, go to "single rider" line. You won't sit together with your party as they are filler seats...so you can save time (we did this to many popular rides and get to go twice back to back) - Do lunch early or late (avoiding the rush hour 12-1 pm) - stay for the night event (for us was the mardi gras parade)

Memories are always gonna be made here lets be honest I have had so many fab times here each is always amazing and always better than the last time I could spend my hole life there it would be amazing and so much fun the food is good for a theme park

This place is awesome..both parks. Great roller coasters and water rides. Very friendly employees..love the food. They have 2 Harry Potter areas..one in each park that are wonderful. Lots to do not only inside the parks, but enjoy the miniature golf course and many restaurants on City Walk. I highly recommend.

We just returned from celebrating my son's 7th birthday at Universal. Both he and my 9-year-old daughter agree it was a blast, my 40-something husband and I loved it, and my parents in their mid-70's had a wonderful time. It is truly a destination for everyone. Our favorite ride as a group is Men in Black. I think we rode it 10 times. On our very last ride, the operator had everyone in the queue shout out a "happy birthday" to my son, and we got our black jackets! What could be better?  I think between all of us we rode every ride, saw every show, and enjoyed every moment. Universal, thank you for a great vacation!!

I was there with my 9 year old daughter and wife for Spring Break. Prior to going, I told my daughter how magical this place was. I told her how you get to ride the movies and be a part of the movies. When we arrived, we were all very disappointed to find that most of the classic rides that made Universal famous, were gone. Now, every ride is simply a 3-d simulator. We went to ride the movies, not sit down and watch movies. Even my daughter was not impressed by the simulators. She watched videos of earthquake, jaws, king kong, twister.......it's shameful what has been done to this once amazing park. Disney has maintained its classic rides and added new ones.

We have been to Universal Studios many times and we are glad we went again. We went early in our vacation so the park wasn't as packed as we thought it might be later in the week so the lines weren't too bad and you could actually move without running into people! It was a beautiful day and we truly enjoyed our visit.

Universal Studios is a fun place for the entire family. Who doesn't like the minions and they're out in full force here -- both in their adventure and in a parade. Our whole family loves them from Grandpa on down. Lots of other fun things to see and do here as well. How about a ride through the jungle with King Kong lurking about? Or maybe you want to see how Shrek met and married Fiona. Again, lots of things for everyone to see and do here including a wild water ride.
Very interesting - and fun ! Lots of really enjoyable rides that all the family enjoyed. So brilliantly organised and we just drifted from one experience to the next.

We were there on a two day two park ticket. We added a one day express pass which was definitely worth the extra cost. The rides were great, but a bit much for my wife - she got nauseated in the Harry Potter ones. The food was relatively inexpensive compared to what we expected. We were also impressed by how much was new compared to ten years earlier.

Took my fiancé here as a portion of his birthday getaway. We had the express passes that made a TON of difference. We were able to navigate the park and ride EVERY ride during one day. It really makes a difference when you wait 15 minutes vs 1 hour. It is a bit pricey but it’s worth it in my opinion. We also had the food passes and that was also a great buy, one entree with drink and snack. We were joined by some friends which made it even better. It was nice to let loose, ride the rides, and just have fun. Universal will never get old and always be a good time.

If you like amusement parks and roller coasters - you will love this place. I only went for the Harry Potter World which was awesome but remember that only half the HP World is in Universal - the other half is at Islands of Adventure. You can see both sides if you do one park one day, and the next park the next day. If you want to enjoy the Hogwarts Express you need to purchase a park-hopper pass. Another way for Universal to take your money.

Had a ball at Universal studios.  Rides were fun. Don’t let the crowds put you off especially as you arrive at the first security check point.  My tip is to ride solo where you can and don’t purchase the fast pass before you go. You can purchase it on the day if needed from most of the ride gift shops.  You need to be moving to see it all and ride the rides you want and while you could do both parks on one day I would think to enjoy them allow a day at each of you can.  Heaps of fun for teenagers and their parents!!!

We have been coming there for over 15 years with our kids now our granddaughter, we love the fun and excitement, there was only one disappointing time and it was we were standing in line to meet shrek and donkey and it was hot, we were next in line and we were told they were not taking no more. My 5 year old granddaughter was red int he face from standing in the sun , i felt like they should have let who was in line finish before they went back in.

I travel the world riding roller coasters and theme parks. There are few places on earth I would rather be than at an amusement or theme park...and I've been to all of the major parks in the US and many around the world. Universal Studios Florida is my happy place and my favorite park of all!  First of all, don't compare Universal Studios Florida to any of the Disney World parks. They are two different resorts that are catering to two different customer bases. Disney goes after the families with kids ages 12 and under, whereas Universal targets families with teenagers. Disney is a resort filled with attractions that the entire family can ride together; Universal goes for more "thrilling" attractions. There are rides and attractions for little kids, senior adults, and people who can't handle riding rides...HOWEVER, their offerings for these demographics are a little on the weak side as of the time of this writing (May, 2018). Don't panic! Comcast (parent company of NBCUniversal...the owner of Universal Parks and Resorts) is shelling out BILLIONS of dollars on their US theme parks. Universal Orlando Resort (where Universal Studios Florida is located) is building major new attractions annually, along with its sister park, Islands of Adventure. Family attractions designed for all-ages are opening, and major new family attractions are on the way. Universal REALLY wants to take the fight to Disney and they are developing their Orlando and Hollywood properties in ways never seen before!  Disney fills their parks with attractions, meet-n-greets, parades and shows from their content. If you want to meet Mickey Mouse, Buzz Lightyear from "Toy Story," Anna and Elsa from "Frozen," or characters from the Star Wars universe, that's what you'll find at their parks. Universal reaches into their movies for experiences too...but you'll also find third-party characters and IPs from movies/TV shows that they didn't produce. Harry Potter is one of their biggest draws and The Wizarding World of Harry Potter: Diagon Alley "land" situated in USF is utterly amazing. The detail and design of the land will genuinely make you feel like you are IN the Wizarding World with Harry and the gang! There is a small "Springfield" section themed to the legendary Fox TV series, "The Simpsons" featuring a 3D simulator ride, numerous food and beverage locations and some limited retail and carnival game options. Their KidZone "land" for children is rumored to be closing in the near future to make way for a new land themed to the world of Nintendo video games. New family attractions themed to The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon (a 3D simulator) and The Fast and the Furious (a family ride) have opened over the past year. Thrills can be had with "Revenge of the Mummy: The Ride" (an indoor roller coaster), "Transformers: The Ride - 3D" (an aggressive 3D dark ride using the same ride system as the AMAZING "Spider-Man" attraction in Islands of Adventure), and the "Hollywood Rip, Ride, Rockit" outdoor roller coaster. Character encounters/experiences and parades are located all over the park. Exciting new shows and rides are on their way over the next few years. It's an exciting time to be visiting Universal!  While a day at Universal Studios isn't cheap, I feel that you get better value for your money than you do a day at Disney. Disney charges you for EVERYTHING and each year, they find a way to make you pay for something that has always been free. Universal wants as much of your money as they can get too...HOWEVER, they still give you more "bang for your buck" than Disney does. Spend a few days at Disney World, then go spend 2 days at Universal Orlando Resort and you'll see what I mean.  If I have one major gripe about Universal Studios Florida, it's that their ride offerings are far too reliant on watching video screens and wearing 3D glasses. At least half of their major ride experiences are in 3D, whether you are wearing 3D glasses or experiencing "glasses-free 3D technology" like you do in the new-for-2018 "Fast and Furious Supercharged" ride, it gets to be a little overkill watching screens all day long...especially if you suffer from motion sickness easily. Happily, new screen-free and 3D-free attractions are in the pipeline and will be rolling out over the next several years.  If you're a Harry Potter fan, a visit to Universal Orlando Resort is a no-brainer. With major Potter lands in both Islands of Adventure (Hogsmeade) and Universal Studios Florida (Diagon Alley, with an actual Hogwarts Express train ride to connect the two park lands seamlessly), the magic of Potter is alive and well. If you have very young children or your party consists of people who can't handle 3D rides (or rides in general), you may want to hold off on a visit to Universal until you can attend with people who will enjoy the rides.  Highly, HIGHLY recommended. It's my favorite place on Earth!!!

My only negative is before going to Universal I dowloaded the app, went to book tickets, selected 1 day, 2 parks, express pass - done paid. Lined up to be told no you just ordered the express pass ($200 USD for 2) If you now want entry you need to pay $370USD more! Why would I want express but not entry!? I even went back to the app to see if I overlooked it but no it’s not clear at all. Anyway we paid the extra and it was an amazing day. We did universal studios and Island of adventure. I recommend the express if you can. My absolute favourite ride was the rock coaster, I’m still amazed by it - any roller coaster with motley Crüe on the sound track is great in my opinion, it made me feel so much braver. If you go on the popeye ride be prepared to get wet! Still a great ride though. Would do it all again

went here three times last week thoroughly enjoyed it.  hardly any wait for any of the rides practically walked onto all rides including the new F&F supercharged.  all rides very enjoyable food was great and bought lots of gifts for family and friends.  Highly recommend.  and after the experience, I've had at Disney the same week its 100% better.  Definitely my the park of choice

Most of the rides are the 4D rides, which is nice. Plenty of places to grab a snack on the go, and so many shops to look in! My favourite was Jurrasic Park and interacting with the Velociraptor. Harry Potter park was fun, and enjoyed seeing the people perform magic "tricks" with wands. It is crowded (a given) but if you go earlier in the morning it isn't too bad! Definitely a huge target appeal for the younger kids. i would go with my children for sure!

We have been to Disney in Paris, Hong Kong, Japan, Orlando etc. and Universal in Singapore. But this place beats it all. We took the 2 days-3 parks-unlimited pass and it was absolutely worth it. With the unlimited pass we were able to cover both the parks in 1 day as the wait time was never more than 5-10 mins. You should check the opening time and closing time of both parks before you start so you can plan accordingly. Each day the parks open and close at different times. The following day the kids repeated the rides they wanted to and the other half day we spent at Volcano bay which is also a must do. It’s relatively new so very neat and clean. With Unlimited Pass you can save time and make the most of your trip. Universal is MUST DO!

My family and I visited Universal recently for my daughter's birthday. We had such a good time. It rained most of the day but one of the best things about Universal is that a lot of the rides and attractions are indoors so rain or shine, you can have a blast. The biggest attraction: Harry Potter (anything and everything).  Pros: -Indoor attractions. -The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. -Nice staff and clean grounds. -They have a Starbucks! (I know, you may be saying, "And?! Who cares about Starbucks!" But c'mon...it's coffee, right?) -Did I mention, The Wizarding World of Harry Potter? -Great food and plenty of things to do.  Cons: -If you go during summer you can and will sweat your booty off. -It is fairly expensive, especially if you get the "Park Hopper," which gets you into both parks (I highly recommend this, though). -The merchandise is super expensive so be sure to budget properly.  If you are like me, which I hope you are not, you suffer from motion sickness. With this being said, I rode almost ZERO rides. But, that did not keep me from having fun. If you are going there with your children, go into it planning on not riding much, but enjoying the scenery, the amenities, and the smiles on your kiddos' faces. If you do suffer from this, I recommend the Jurassic Park ride (river ride and one big, super fun drop) and the Hogwarts train from park to park is nice, too.  I hope you enjoy your trip and have a blast!!

We have been here several times before and it keeps getting better,came in March with a mad keen Harry Potter fan ( my 21 year old Son ); and ran about like children all day,the rides and shows keep improving,would they please stop building new ones as it makes us come back time after time,guess that’s the point,.Go and have a blast.

We visited the park again this past week. We always enjoy all that it has to offer. We pack our lunch and drinks since it's easier to do this than to go to one of the various restaurants. The food looks great but a little expensive on a budget. We recommend getting the park hopper pass as it allows you to go from park to park via Harry Potter experience or just walk from park to park. We love the various rides and activities throughout the park. The Mummy, Hulk, Spiderman, Men in Black, Rip Roaring Rapids, Jurassic Park, Harry Potter, ET, and others. The new ride of Fast & Furious and Jimmy Fallon are awesome rides as well especially F & F a must ride deal. Don't tell anyone about the single rider line is quicker for most rides unless it getting past 7 pm as that's when most people leave. The lockers are for all of the rides as you are not allowed to have items on them. It's a little crazy to get one sometimes but you must do this to ride. Hulk is nothing in your packets to ride and metal detectors. That was interesting to see people throw coins down in order to get through the detector. Take your time and enjoy! The waits are just part of the day.

Went to universal studios whist on holiday in orlando with my wife and what a fantastic day we had. We are going back again as to try and do it all in one day is impossible. Would highly recommend it to anyone young or old

From the parking, to the gate and with locker rentals, it's a mess. Super long wait times and the rides close if it rains even a bit. Lots of in park carnival games (that cost). Not impressed and won't be back.

I stayed at a Universal Resort Hotel for 2 weeks and due to this we had the express passes and entry into the theme parks an hour early each day. Don't get me wrong though, we didn't go into the Universal Parks every day.  1st tip - If you don't want to spend a fortune on drinks, take a sports drinks bottle with you. There are lots of water fountains located near the restrooms/toilets. We are from the UK so took diluting juice with us to add to the water.  2nd tip - I wasn't too impressed with the early park entry an hour early. Practically the only ride open was Harry Potter so everyone was heading there. When we got there, the queue was about 30 mins. Baring in mind we all had express passes, it was actually quicker to wait until the main park was open and go anytime during the day and we never waited more than 15 mins.  3rd tip - On your way out of Diagon Alley, stick to the left which is signposted as Exit. That was you can avoid the masses of people coming in through the main "wall" entrance.  4th tip - Definitely take advantage of the late park opening. Its an obvious one really but it means the queue's are less and its nice to walk around as it starts to get dark. Universal Studios doesn't open late often though so might not be an option.  5th tip - Use the Universal crowd calender before you plan your trip to make sure it's not going to be too busy when your there.  6th tip - If you're staying at a on site hotel, get any souvenirs delivered to your hotel room to save you having to carry them around the park. I'm sure as long as your not checking out for 2 days, its fine to do this.  When it comes to the rides, my kids loved the usual Harry Potter rides but also loved Jimmy Fallon which surprised me. It was actually really good so don't miss it out.  Other than that, the park was spotless and the staff were all great.

Universal tickets are always money well spent. The place is magical. Both parks have great attractions and plenty of space to lounge in the sun. City walk is fantastic for a bite to eat after a day in the parks. We never visited volcano bay, which was a shame, but for anyone visiting Orlando, ensure you do get tickets here as there isn’t a bad word I could say about the place.

What ever you do avoid the fast and furious ride. Without doubt the worst ride I have ever ridden. The que was more exciting than the ride. Biggest waste of time. I waited for this ride for 3 years when I first visited and I'm so disappointed

We originally were only going to do Universal Studios but ended up having time to also do Islands of Adventure and were able to upgrade at Guest Services at the discounted price. Of the 2 parks I would have to say I liked the layout and scenery of Islands of Adventure...but...Diagonal Alley was a must for me since I'm a Harry Potter fan. I recommend getting the unlimited drinks package which also comes with complimentary cup. They have character actors throughout the park and most of them you don't have long lines to wait like Magic Kingdom. The Men in Black guys called my husband Live Action Shaggy 😂. We missed the parade unfortunately. 1) Springfield: Home of the Simpsons was cool since my husband and I like that show. The Simpsons Ride made me a but motion sick. 2) Transformers 3D ride was my favorite ride at this park and did t male mme motion sick. 3) Hollywood Rip Ride Rocket I won't ride again. It jerked me around too much and I ended up with a splitting headache at the end of it. I've ridden a lot of roller coasters and this one was by far one of the roughest. 4) Diagon Alley. Talk with the Knight Bus conductor and and shrunken head they're fun to talk with. Go into the red telephone booth between Knight Bus and King's Cross for a message from the Ministry of Magic. As soon as you enter Diagonal Alley you're overwhelmed by how amazing this place is. I went into Gringott's, Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, and a few of the other shops. Butter beer tasted just like a cream soda but I hear the frozen version is even better. I didn't go into Ollivanders because of the line but it was neat to see other people using their wands to do "magic spells" at select locations. I was lucky enough to catch the dragon breathing fire. We tried eating at Leaky Cauldron but again lines were too long. I could've spent all day at Diagonal Alley!

really worth the visit. We love the Minions simulator and the parade of all the children's characters. It is a quiet park but I felt lack of being better visually signposted, even having maps available.

To start off it's so nice especially in the night. The only negative is there is nothing but one little area near barney land for 2year olds. I don't understand why they don't extend it to have some rides for kids. I also suggest them to have more rest areas that have shade and fans. Other then those two. My 12 year old daughter definitely enjoyed it.

Love universal studios and iOS, both gòod parks. Came last year and we was so excited to ride the mummy ride again, it's scary but fun at the same time and so different from most other rides, only thing was the fire effects were not working as down for maintenance. Bumble bee taco truck food really good and tasty. Pleased to see ET ride was still there

Great rides however, for me and the wife we found Islands of Adventure alot better. Some of the rides like ET need either replacing or updating but on the whole there is something for everyone. We love the CGI rides so liked the HP Escape from Gringotts, Revenge of the Mummy and Transformers to name a few.
