Expect the usual queues for rides however, we found that going first thin in the morning is best as the parks get busy towards lunchtime onwards. Also if you are non-US and are holidaying for a week or two its best to avoid the weekend as this is peak period for US citizens visiting for the weekend.
We had a blast at all 3 Universal parks. The boys had a blast. Simpson’s land and Jurassic Park were spot on! Harry Potter was everything I could have wanted! Great destination for tweens.
if you like thrill rides then this is the park for you. Forgot how bad they beat you up..lol..still a fun place

We just took my 11 year old grandson there for his birthday - we had an amazing time. Be sure to spend the extra money to skip the lines.. it's well worth it. There is so much to do and it's so much fun.... definitely recommend a family vacation there.

Universal Studios is a must see amusement park in Florida! They have great movie “rides!” Such as Transformers, Minion Mayhem, Revenge of the Mummy and many more!! This is really worth your money and I hope you will come to Universal Studios when you come to Florida, Orlando!!!! 👍

Universal Studios Orlando is a great place for friends families with children of all ages to visit for a day (or multiple days) of pure amazement and thrill! Whether you are into Harry Potter, the Simpsons, Hello Kitty, or Minions (plus much more), you are in for a treat when Universal transports you right into classic film favorites. The atmospheres of the streets and attractions, the decor of the restaurants, the thrilling rides, and the amazing shows and photo opportunities make for the most fun you’ll ever have. There is so much to recommend, and you probably won’t be able to do it all in one day, but some of my personal favorites are the Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringott’s Ride, The Leaky Cauldron restaurant, the Race Through New York Starring Jimmy Fallon ride, the Richter’s Burger Co. restaurant, the MEN IN BLACK Alien Attack ride, Universal Orlando’s Horror Make-Up Show, and Universal Studios Store.

Visited this 3 days ago, going again today, It’s our 5 yr visiting and it never gets stale, the rides are fast, the soccer is on big screens and the atmosphere is great. I recommend the Animal show and the chocolate factory for chill out time, oh, and don’t miss the Blues Brothers show! Fab
Universal Studios caters for all ages and has one of the best rides, The RIP-Rocket. If you go on it then play ‘I will Survive’ by Gloria Gaynor, the song is so apt for the ride.
This was one of the most amazing places I have ever been to! I loved every ride and every experiance. I wish I had two days to cover it all properly

Great place to spend a couple of days! Lots of rides, shows and food! There is enough for all ages young and old! The Express passes are a little expensive but they are worth having. Look into the Universal hotels where the Express passes come with your room.

My wife and I have older children and had the chance to visit both of the parks while in Florida. We decided to make it a fun for just the 2 of us. I enjoy the City Walk area and the energy of the parks. While I enjoyed the great rides and experiences I could help but leave extremely disappointed in the lack of service and general lack of concern for the guest experience. This is one area Disney cannot be beat. From the painfully slow and disorganized line to get our tickets to the disinterested wait staff at the restaurants in the park, It made it a poor experience. The line to get our tickets took about an hour. When we finally got to the window it closed for the worker to go on break. We waited again for the window to be reopened. At multiple times we stopped to get food or drinks. It was rare anyone made eye contact with the customer or (for most interactions) didn't even stop there conversation with their coworker. Money was just taken and change placed on the counter without stopping a sentence. The crowning failure was when a worker on a Harry Potter ride pulled us out of line rudely because my wife had a small purse worn cross body. He ignored the families in from and behind us that had diaper bags and back packs, and rudely directed my wife to the lockers and then sternly walked me out of the line area (like a 3 year old) and told me to stay there until my wife got back. I asked for his name and he said Noah. When I repeated it back to him he said Noel. I guessed he was lying about his name. When I questioned him about pulling us out of line like he did he got very upset, raised his voice and yelled "DO YOU WANT TO SEE MY MANAGER". I remained calm and told him how he was acting I would handle it through Customer Service. After going back and forth with him yelling, another worker came up (I assume it was his manager). He screamed in front of everyone “this guy wants to talk to you.” By this point my wife returned. I told the other person that I would deal with this later. Noel/Noah stood in front of me and would not let us rejoin the line and repeated that we wanted to talk with the manager. I repeated my statement and had to physically shoulder by Noel/Noah for us to get back in line.  I tried to let it go, but finally decided to us the customer service link and sent an email regarding my experience since we spent the extra $125 per ticket for the express pass. In my complaint I asked for the money back for the express pass if their staff can just pull us at will. The week following out trip I get a voicemail that customer service reviewed my complaint and since I had used my express pass multiple times that day I obviously had enjoyed the pass so she would not refund my money. She said if I called her back we might be able to “work something out”.  If you are looking for great customer service, this is NOT the place to visit.

Took the kids here for the first time in October. It was GREAT. We got the fast passes and it was not only worth it, but NEEDED. The park was clean, fun and there were lots of fun things for the little ones. (5 and 6) Also, Harry Potter world is AMAZING

No separate line anywhere. You walk through the garage and all that stuff is neat to look at. You end up being herded like cows with no lines and no organization at all. Then yes you are placed on a bus and the action starts. It seems pretty cool and just when its getting good, the ride ends. It just ends. And your left there thinking "what just happened?' The One guy I think Jamie was his name was super awesome and fully. He was the best part of the whole thing. Unless they improve this ride it really is a waste of time. Suggestion, walk through and see all the good stuff then find and exit.

Our family visited Orlando for a day at the park and while overall the experience was fantastic...on our first ride, the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit Roller Coaster, our daughter's very strong (and expensive!) prescription glasses fell off of her face! With no expectation, we made a visit to lost and found at the end of the day only to discover that they were not there. We were advised to call in and check though as the areas around the rides are checked for lost articles when the park closes. After seeing all of the articles retrieved in the past that were shattered and damaged, displayed in the case as a warning to those needing lockers, we had little hope. I was also told that in the event they were located we would have to make a visit in person to pick them up. This would have been possible but not ideal as we live a couple of hours away.  On a whim I called customer service a few days later only to be greeted by Linda, who turned out to be our guardian angel of lost glasses!! Linda took a lot of time, expressed true understanding and concern for our situation and then proceeded to not only locate our daughters glasses, but then went the extra mile to have them sent home to us. Whoever up there that is listening...Linda deserves a pat on the back, an employee of the month nod, maybe even a raise! Even if she hadn't been able to reunite us with the glasses she really wowed me with how empathetic she was to our misfortune and made me feel like I had a friend on the inside who wasn't going to quit trying until th eissue was resolved or at least every effort was exhausted. THANK YOU LINDA!

This is my second time to universal studios in Florida and I love it. If you like roller coasters and simulator rides this is the place for you. Harry Potter section in islands of advantage is just awesome.They have 3 rides there and they are so much fun.Get there early if you are wanting to see this section because it gets crowded fast.This is a real popular part of islands of adventure.If you get the hopper pass they even have a hogwarts train that will take you back and forth between the 2 parks.If you are hot and you want to get wet to cool off the popeyes river rapid ride is really fun(but you will get really soaked),also the dudley log ride is fun but again you will get soaked.The kong ride was good but they have long lines.Again get there early.My best advice is to plan ahead and go to the rides you really want to do first then you can go from there.But keep in mind that if it rains and they have thunder and lightening that they will stop the roller coaster rides till it clears up.That means that all the simulator ride lines tend to get really long and back up.

So so much to see / do.  I think it’s well worth sitting and planning before you get here to get the most out of it.  Despicable Me - you’re in the film so there’s a really great story. It’s an amazing simulator. Not scary at all. Massive queues, out longest. Even worth fast pass was 40 mins so worth going early.  Shrek - is in a cinema so chairs move etc. Lovely story. Quite gentle. Good One of you fancy a bit of a rest / down moment.  Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit - the scariest roller coaster I’ve ever been on. Amazing. Not for faint hearted. You choose which music you’d like to listen to for it.  Transformers - really good (I was quite surprised). Again has a story so you’re in the film.  Race through New York tonight - not at all what I expected and well worth it. A really engaging and thrilling ride.  Saw Sing it. They are brilliant.  Fast and Furious - was very clever. You’re in a bus in the movie. Clever.  Hogwarts Express - awesome. Takes you Between parks. There is a film experience whilst you’re on it. The experience on the way to Islands of Adventure is different to on the way back so if you’re a total Potterhead it’s well worth doing both ways. You actually walk though the wall. If you hold back and let kids go ahead then you can film / photograph them going through and then catch up. Opposite Kings Cross station is a bakery which we used for breakfast one day. Yummy.  Knight Bus - hilarious. Lovely photo / film opp. Right by Grimmauld Place. If you bang on the door on number 12 then Creature appears at the window.  Escape from Gringotts - AMAZING. First ride to open at 8am. Head straight there. All sorts to look at as you walk through to ride. Ride amazing.  Ollivanders - nice but Grace was expecting more. Interactive wands cost $52+tax  Gringotts money exchange - we really liked this. The goblin interacts with you. Talk / move. The dollars you change $10/20 are worth the same and you can spend them in the shops or swop them back.  Leaky Cauldron - fab inside. We had drinks and the juice is surprisingly reasonably priced.  Men in Black - really fun. You shoot the aliens and it keeps score.  Simpson’s Ride - I totally loved this and there was no queue at all. It’s so underrated. Really clever and funny.  ET - cute. You sit on a bike. The bit where you go across the moon with the stars etc made Grace gasp.  Superstar Parade - really sweet, lots for younger children to see and dancers etc in between.  Cinematic Celebration tonight - singularly the most impressive show I have ever ever seen.  On the real thrill rides you have to put your bag etc in a locker. They’re free. Make sure you remember your number and don’t put your fast passes in. They aren’t very big so I wouldn’t take a massive bag as it won’t fit.
FLORIDA JUST BLUE ME AWAY it has so much to offer. A FANTASTIC DESTINATION SO SO MUCH TO DO the choice is so so vast rodeo theme bars cllubs

No one knew so their service is genuine. They past my inspection with flying colors!!

Not sure how to properly organize a review of a trip to Universal Studios, so Ill just start with the weather:  Don’t go in the end of July. Unless you like bathing in your own sweat. If you do like that, then you’re sick, and Universal isn’t your cup of tea. Unless you are a devoted parent like me, then you’ll go anywhere/anytime to please your children.  So, with that out of the way, Universal was a great experience. We stayed on site at Loews Royal Pacific. The grounds are amazing. Pool is gorgeous, there is a beach with zero entry into the pool, and there are no less than 4 lifeguards on duty to give you a false sense of security.  Our kids (14, 12) said that the hotel reminded them of an all inclusive we frequent in Mexico. I agreed with them, except the all-inclusive part. For example, just yesterday, at the pool bar, I ordered a Jameson and Seven for me and a chardonnay for my wife, and it came to $24.00. The path to sobriety begins at theme park pools.  Anyways, I digress. The grounds are gorgeous. Unfortunately, as I stated before, July is a horrible time to visit Florida, as we had storms EVERY day, which led to the pool closing multiple times a day. Kind of a bummer when you pay a lot of money for the pools at your hotels.  Which leads me to getting to the actual parks. We opted for the park hopper, which used in conjunction with the “early entrance” is usually a good deal. However, you have a couple options to get to the parks from your hotel. You can walk 10-15 minutes. You can also take the complimentary boats which are much quicker, but also are subject to weather holds. Apparently there is also a shuttle?? However, none of the transportation options were explained to us when we checked in. We kind of just figured it out on our own. Which brings me to my main fault with Universal...  The employees just do not have the level of dedication that Disney employees do. We have been to Disney World/Land several times. We were spoiled by the level of attention that is offered there. There were also several moments that I thought “you wouldn’t see that at Disney”  I called for dinner reservations at one of the restaurants in City Walk. Apparently all calls to City Walk go through the City Walk operator. She was very rude and unprofessional. I called her out on her lack of politeness, and was promptly yelled at.  There was garbage and candy wrappers throughout both main parks  We rode the Hogwarts Express several times. There was always the standard safety presentation from the ride operator. On our last ride, the operator was obviously bothered by us and as the doors were closing to our compartment, she yelled, “there’s emergency unlock buttons in there somewhere”. End of briefing.  As we were leaving our room this morning, there was a large floor/carpet cleaner plugged in and charging, in the way of people walking, that was leaking fluid all over the floor. Nobody seemed to care.  Again, none of these are major, but...you wouldn’t see them at the other major park.  So, what does Universal do better? The rides. They have something for everyone. If you are the least bit interested in Harry Potter, this place is amazing. The attention to detail is incredible. Daigon Alley is impeccable. You really won’t believe your eyes. The main ride there is “Escape From Gringotts” which is a 4D masterpiece. If you have park hopper, you can then take the Hogwarts Express to Hogsmeade. Again, the detail is amazing. Definitely try the butterbeer.  Outside of Harry Potter, our favorite rides were Transformers, The Mummy, and the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit roller coaster.  So, in summary, Universal does offer great entertainment, but they lack in customer service. If you have young children and you aren’t sure where to go? Do Disney. They still set the bar. If you have done Disney or have older kids, try Universal. The rides are geared towards an older crowd. Just don’t go in the end of July😉

Went with my 13 yr old son last week. Both parks are good with a few really good coasters and thrill rides. Some of the areas are starting to seem dated however such as the ET ride. We were there 3 days but you could do it all in 2 or even 1 with a park hopper ticket and express passes.

Universal reminds me of an overpriced Six Flags (sorry Six Flags). If you are into Harry Potter you may be willing to pay more for the trip but we will not ever be back. By far my favourite theme park in Orlando. Great fun and we laughed the whole day. Some rides did have long queues but everything was very relaxed and friendly so the time flew by. We'll definitely be back because you'd never tire of this place!
What is there to say? Anything associated with Disney is fun of fun and adventure. We truly enjoyed visiting this park.
HAD A BLAST!!!! FAST N FURIOUS BREATHTAKING!!! Everyone was so friendly n professional. We will definitely be back.
I can only recommend the Harry Potter area of this theme park - every other aspect was terribly disappointing and not something I would visit again.

Visited both parks (Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure), great fun with 2 teenagers. Here are some tips I wish I’d known ahead of the trip -  - I booked the 2-Park 2-Day ticket; I was originally wondering if I could fit both in to 1 day but in the end we really needed 2 days to do it justice  - You need to visit both parks to experience all of the Harry Potter world and rides, since it’s split across the 2 parks. We found riding the Hogwarts Express train from Island of Adventures had shorter queues than riding it from the Universal Studios Park  - I booked unlimited express fast pass, but since we had 2 days we could have probably done without the unlimited since we didn’t really repeat any rides on the same day given there is much to do and the queues still take a while (see below)  - The express pass was worth the money during peak periods if you can afford it but note we still waited between 10 and 45 minutes for rides, it’s not instant access  - Try not to take too many (or any) bags as on a lot of the rides you have to painfully find lockers available to store them ; lockers get very busy in peak times  - Car Parking - you can queue in the car for a while to pay; best to get in the left most lane as it’s quicker. Only pay for the premium parking if you want to keep the car out of the sun, otherwise I didn’t find it saved us much time at all

Universal has out done them selves with this new ride. For fans of Fast and Furious they will love the walk through the garage area and the halgrams of movie characters Also the virtual line is a must to do, if you don't like standing in line .

We had a lovely holiday in Universal with our ten year old son. We spent 7 days at Universal, and filled everyday. Our favourite family rides were Men in Black ( shooting game like buzz light year one), Harry Potter Escape from GrinGoths and ET. The Harry Potter areas were very good, at the start of the day the park was not busy, and we never had to wait to get into these areas. The Harry train was extremely good and different in each direction. We stayed in one of the onsite hotels (Royal Pacific) which meant an extra hour, hoverever there were only a few rides open In this time, a good time to do Harry Potter. The hotel meant you got free express passes, so worth considering. 10 minute flat walk to Universal or a boat. The drink refill mug was worth doing, $14 day one the $8 to refill after. Lots of choices on drinks at refill stations. With a ten year old we personally preferred it to Disney but our son was tall enough to do all the rides. His favourite thrill rides were Hollywood Rocket and Hulk. I also enjoyed The Cat in the Hat area, although childish, fun!

If you have never been to Universal then make the effort. Fantastic park. The only ride I wouldn't bother with is Men in Black, rubbish and not worth the wait. Transformers and Harry Potter rides are fantastic as are the dragon race roller coasters.

Something for everyone. Older kids loved the roller coaster and the Mummy ride. Younger kids loved Shrek and Minions. We all loved Harry Potter world! Some lines were long, but we used the Universal App to check on wait times and make the most of our visit.

This park is truly a fun for all ages!My daughter had a blast.We rode almost all the rides,except the roller coaster.I thought with my motion sickness,I wont ne able to ride with my husband and daughter, however I did a lot of rides,and I was ok! If you wanna laugh,the horror show is the best! Park to park pass is worth it,especially if a family member is a Harry Potter fan. Would definitely go back here.We love this place!
We have enjoyed this place 4 times over recent years. For a family with teens it hits the mark for best entertainment. If we could we would go every year.

I'll start by saying this is a pretty great place to spend the day. The wait times are very reasonable, especially later in the day. I have not had a day where it felt too crowded. Where I deducted a bubble was from the customer service. The difference is night and day compared to The Mouse. The Harry Potter land, although, has Universal's BEST customer service. The rest of the park? More on the average to poor side. The park is clean enough for a well traveled space and the restaurants bring your food out in a reasonable amount of time.

I've been to universal studios many times.....I guess I'm just amazed at how they update the parks and the rides so frequently.....the Harry Potter rides is over the top but to walk into this section of the park is amazing....the transformation makes you feel like your in the movie....but I think the train at 9 3/4 is even more clever...it brings you to island of adventure to the other Harry Potter attraction.....not just a train ride but a visual experience to make you feel like you just went to another house ...just amazing...oh yeah there is plenty more to see worth the price of admission
I fell in love with Harry Potter all over again because of this place. So much to see and do, never a dull moment. So worth the ticket.
we were 2 adults in 20s overrated maybe for teens its fun long lines and overpriced nexttime we'll stick with nature
The queues wet too Long , food and drinks too expensive some rides were okay , some a waste of time , i was expecting so much.

We enjoyed our August adventure to Universal Studios Florida. We had park-park-park tickets and we spent most of our time at this park.  First of all Diagon Alley (Harry Potter) is far better than Hogsmead. The level of detail from the Knight bus outside the alley to all the interactive wand spots is worth it. Far more people wandering around helping (cast) and even hidden wand spots. The nice touch of having movie music in the background to even Kreatcher looking out the window at Grimmauld place is worth it. For food in Diagon Alley you have the Leaky Cauldron. It was ok but I actually preferred the three broomsticks better. For rides here you only have Escape from Gringots. At 6'6" I could not ride it. When I sat in the test seats my knees were already at the front of the car seat before even thinking about pulling the bar down over my legs. Nope, no go. At least I could ride the other Potter ride.  The other rides in the park were fun.  Men In Black: Fun laser shooter game, but forgettable.  The Simpsons: Ok. So we thought it was ok. Glad they had the original cast voices back (BoB) etc. We felt it was a bit of a crappy ride. Then we realized that this is what they were going for with it being Krustyland. So then we appreciated it more. Don't pay for a Duff Beer later on in the area, it is forgettable as coors light is.  Ran into Doc Brown from Back to the Future. Great interaction. Great Character.  Fast and the Furious: Ok ride. Good theme. Origional actors back. Not a big fan of the show so it was ok.  The Mummy Ride: Wife and child loved it and said it was wild. Once again I had the leg bar issue of not fitting in the seats. Almost like me being in a sports car, love to drive them just have way too long legs to do it.  Transformers: Awesome.  Minion Ride: AWESOME again!  Shrek: Forgettable. You have to wait WAY too long to actually get into the real ride and not the staging area. Feels tired and in need of renovation or removal.  Rock'n Coaster: Shut down due to storm the night we were going to go on it.  ET: Fun little ride. Wife loved it! Showing it's age but good for memories.  Get the popcorn bucket that is a souvenir. The cheap refills help you stay hydrated by giving you salt. We loved the Blues Brothers driving by and singing. Seen the real car/etc in Chicago so we felt it was good but could have been better.  The silly finger print reader to enter never did work for me. So I had to constantly show my ticket and my ID to get in. Not the end of the world but just interesting. Don't forget your ID if you are staying in park.  Overall we'd go back here and just skip certain rides next time.

First time in the park for over 10 years. Some rides totally changed others not. The reason for 4/5 is the poor ET ride which is very outdated and also lots of similar simulator style rides. Plenty choices and attractions and also the Hogwarts express to go park to park to Islands of Adventure. Plenty of food and drinks options although very surprised that none of the NY outlets served hot dogs only corn dogs. Highlights would be Wizarding World of Harry Potter - Diagon Alley and the Escape from Gringotts ride. Also Men in Black, The Simpsons, Revenge of the Mummy and Rip Ride rocket. Be mindful some rides go off when weather poor. Also a very good evening show - the cinematic celebration.

Of all the rides in Universal and Disney, this was my favourite. If you are a Harry Potter fan, you MUST go on this ride. We rode it 6 times in one day, and I never wanted to stop. This ride is the stuff of my dreams, and absolutely raises the bar for theme park rides in general.  One word of caution for those unaccustomed to modern thrill rides: your first ride will be very disorienting. Go on it a second time right after your first, and you will have a much better time and become used to the movement and sensations of the ride.

We went to Universal as a last minute stop on our week long vacation in Orlando. We got the 2 park pass but were soundly defeated by the size of the park on a hot muggy day. That being said, the park has something for everyone yet we suggest you plan your visit carefully. Plan first for the size of the park as we went directly after getting off a cruise which was not wise. Always take an opportunity to plot the timing of your visit as we had an opportunity to get on many of the rides due to the low off peak season attendance. Plan for the activities as we went early but much of the shows are later in the afternoon/evening. There are some rides with restrictions due to the size of the seats but there are sample seats outside to try so you do not wait in line for nothing. Only real complaint is that there is not an outlet or charging station in sight to charge cell phones which was the primary reason we left earlier than we wanted to. We could have brought portable charge packs but it would be smart for park to think about this going forward.
We adored every second. Especially Diagon Alley. Memories for life. Outside of the Harry Potter areas, The Hulk and Rip Rocket were our favorites. Get the express passes. Life savers.

This park is designed with the entire family in mind. There are rides for the teenagers, smaller children and adults. We only went to Universal Studios and not to the other two parks. The park is like being on a movie set everywhere you walk. There are of theme restaurants on every corner, even Mel’s Diner and, of course, plenty of gift shops.

You can't go wrong with taking the family. Recommendation is that you purchase either a meal plan or if you don't plan on eating in Universal that you buy the refillable cups at 15.99 you fill all day long with no extra cost. Universal now has Coca-Cola products and use the Freestyle so you can choose from over 1,000 varieties. We like Sprite Zero and it is hard to find but with Freestyle you can get it. If you go with your family try to stay at a resort that is affiliated with Universal as you can get in 1 hour prior to opening, makes it easy to get on the popular rides with little ones.

had a 14 day ticket and went most days, had the onsite early hour entry which made so much difference. highlights were the two sides of harry potter. i enjoyed all the simulaters except fast and furious which is a waste of space, gringotts was awesome

I went to Disney & Universal as a "bucket list" gift to a dying friend in 2014. Disney was great. Universal Studios was horrible.  From the moment you pay to get in, your wallet is under attack. (and I thought WDW was pricey??) Everything is ridiculously over-priced. Food drinks, souvenirs...  And the wait-times for rides were insane (and the displayed times at the entrances completely inaccurate) We ended up going on only one ride: Men in Black", and it was boring. OH! And guess what? You can't take ANYTHING with you on any ride. No no, not so much as a purse or fanny-pack. You have to RENT a LOCKER before getting in line. Over and over again, for each ride!!!! Talk about a scam!  Worst of all was "The Wizarding World of Harry Potter". And I say this as a die-hard "Potterhead". Sadly I didn't go to BOTH theme parks (and yes, you have to pay EXTRA to get a two-park-pass because "Diagon Ally" is at Universal Studios Florida, and "Hogsmead/Hogswarts" is at Islands of Adventure)  But my visit to Diagon Ally was a HUGE disappointment. From the fact that virtually EVERY "shop" is just a souvenir store or restaurant, to the nasty "butter beer" (Vanilla cream soda with some chemical added to create 3 inches of never-ending butter foam) to the FOUR and a HALF hour wait to get on "Escape from Gringots" (The sign at the entrance cheerfully LIED to us, saying the wait was 90 minutes, and in the end, we left the line before we got to the actual ride, due to dinner reservations).  After 3.5 hours in line we reached a security check-point where people who had not put their belongings in storage lockers were being searched, and we asked the very young man how much longer we had to wait, and he said at least another hour! I said "we were done", and he simply said we had to "go back the way we came in" (a 3+ hour long line of people behind us, packed like sardines!!!) I put up a stink, pointing at the door in the corner marked "Exit", and the boy reluctantly took us thru it, past a card table with a 1/2 eaten sandwich (Oh noz! The illusion is shattered!) and in 15 seconds we were outside. Really? You wanted us to fight our way upstream against THOUSANDS of people, so we wouldn't see your sandwich???
This place is great every ride the way its all laid out. I will def go here again . Staff friendly nothing to much trouble. Food was nice here weather great.
We love this park but too many 4d rides,fast and furious is awful,you need to change that and i wouldnt wait in a long quene for it,my fave is the blue brothers singing

I looked all over the internet trying to find reviews for coming here with kids with ADD and anxiety. I was not sure if we would qualify for the pass that allows them to NOT stand in line the whole time, but come back at a set time similar to a FastPass. I should not have stressed over it! All I had to do was tell the Guest Service person that it is difficult for my 13 year old to be patient without throwing a tantrum and causing a scene. Being able to explain to them that they can ride something AFTER we do this or that was helpful when they don't really have a concept of time or waiting for long periods. Each ride is also labeled with whether it is loud or dark, etc which are other things that can bother my child. Overall, great experience, although expensive, and cant wait to go again!

We still love this place and all the rides even though we are a mature couple in our fifties. Parking is free after 6pm so if you plan well you can visit the park most evenings when the queues are shorter. This meant we didn’t feel the need to pay extra for express passes and got on most rides within 15 minutes. Atmosphere is best during the day when the shows and parades are on. A must do park when in Orlando.

Absolutely brilliant park. Love it here every year something new opens. Harry Potter is fabulous. If your going next year it's well worth looking at an annual pass. We paid $5.00 last year. As long as you go 2 weeks before it runs out.

Both this park and Islands of Adventure are worth the ticket price. There is lots of walking so wear comfortable shoes! My general advice with any Orlando theme park is to limit the time spent there are go on several days as it's hard to cram everything into a day. We did a full day across both parks and stayed for one of the Halloween Horror nights and this was too much. Please note that my rating is for the parks during normal hours and not for the separately ticketed Halloween Horror Nights. The food and drink in Universal is more expensive than Disney and OK but not amazing. Disney allow packed lunches to be taken in whereas Universal don't and the rules of what you can take in are a little ambiguous.

Some of my friends asked me why I went to Universal when there is so much to see and do at Disney parks. I responded that Universal is awesome and generally focused on adults and not young kids.; however, the quality of the rides and shows are remarkable for almost all ages. The Harry Potter rides in both sections are very realistic and detailed oriented that you feel that you are part of the story. Likewise, you have to spend a lot of time on the rides and visiting shops and areas to appreciate all of it. Every time I rode a ride I found things that I had missed before. Again while in Orlando visiting the Disney parks, spend a little more time to visit both Universal parks in Orlando. You will not regret it.

Universal park size: personally I was a little surprised about the actual size of the two parks after estimating the need for four days to do both. In reality we did both parks in two days. They really are not that big!  Food: over priced and under sized, $5 for a donut - $30pp for a main.  Water: $4.50 Ummm....  Parade: Simply a joke when compared to magic kingdom.  Attractions at both parks: majority are motion simulators mixed with two good coasters and lots of children's rides.  Water parks: tapu tapu is stupid, the system dose not work as it should for a million dollar plus company. You end up spending the majority of the day sitting around waiting for a 2 second water slide. They actual park looks impressive and the slides are far better then either of the Disney parks, however the day was a little ruined by the tapu tapu system.  Parking: PLEASE if you are staying outside of a universal accomodation you must read this!!! For some reason universal feel the need to charge a parking fee of $25 per day for either universal studios, island of adventure or volcano bay!!! So for a 14 day vacation expect to be paying an excess of $350. ( Bare in mind this parking charge was $22 per day, just two days ago...)  Conclusion: obviously the whole experience is good, but the reality is that by the end of the day you feel robbed and a fair amount of frustration for Universal's greed and lack of ability to deliver.  Thanks for reading and I Hope this helps you decided on your vacation.

First time I went on I was so mesmerised by this ride, I thought it was amazing!  The theming throughout the castle is great and doesn’t feel like you’re waiting long.  The ride itself is fantastic, I absolutely loved it. Needless to say I went on it a few times during our visit to the park.

Spent two days at Universal Studios with the family; two adults, teenager and kid. Everyone had a great time and is wanting to go back again, but next time with an express pass. The two parks at Universal Studios are enormous in size and offer a huge range of entertainment for kids of all ages. As to be expected, the lines for rides can be quite long and that can try the patience of young and old alike. Also, the food places can get very busy at times. So, while visitors should by all means enjoy the great park, arriving early and staying late can reduce wait times and eating outside traditional meal times makes the food more enjoyable. As an amusement park, Universal Studios is great fun and very much worth a visit (or two).

This is such a fantastic park, I visited with my children, my teenage daughter loved the hulk, as did her grandad ..,we all liked The Mummy and Harry Potter was the highlight for us. Don’t miss Harry Potter and the forbidden journey , also the escape from Gringotts. Try the cinnamon pretzel nuggets from Aunty Anne’s , very tasty.

This years visits to universal were on the whole average we enjoyed the et ride as always and the Simpson kang saucer ride the over to men in black went on as single rider fantastic in and out in 10 minutes got some photos taken with Marylyn Monroe what have universal done with the beetle juice character and betty boop not seen her for 2 years now the transformer ride was missed as queues way too long even single rider onto fast and furious this was a joke I decided to get ticket for the time which was return at 1230 the time then was 1140 I saw they had single rider so opted for this instead well I walked in joined the back of a queue and waited and waited and waited seems the person letting people on was only letting those in the main queue on leaving seats available but not filling from single rider queue the ride itself was ok but I when I got out it was 1225 not impressed by the wait we missed minion ride as queue too long having been to the park many times we knew what to expect some of the rides are a bit dated know and too many little shops selling same merchandise (maybe universal needs to spend more on the parks and less on building hotels all over the international drive area) will return as we find Disney to full on in your face
Great park. Great rides. But without an Express Pass you will be in line for most of your day. Costs extra but it is a necessity. Can make or break a vacation to Universal studios!

HHN: We would have appreciated time to really see the haunted houses properly. We took small-ish children with us, which is it not recommended, but they LOVED the 4 houses we saw and the scare zones. The chainsaw roaming horde was their favourite. The grown ups in our party felt rushed through the houses. There is no time given to take it all in and we were badgered by staff in the houses to keep up with the people in front - we were nearly running at some points! Within a couple of hours of opening, all the houses were at 45 minute+ queues. So after wasting precious time watching the thoroughly awful academy of villains (total rubbish) we left.  2 week visit to parks: too many simulator rides for us, all the newest rides are disappointing - jimmy fallon and fast and furious declared rubbish by the kids and they wouldn’t ever get on them again. Kong is the same style of ride too - please bring back more big roller coaster rides Universal. 2 of best 3 rides of our holiday now at SeaWorld (rip ride rocket at Universal came in at number 2). We have high hopes for the new park that seems to be in the works - but we won’t be back until that is open. Oh, and don’t bother with Volcano Bay - go to Aquatica.

Came in the evening as part of a convention group. Hard to figure out what was open. Got the harry potter ride which was great. Most stuff already closed. Got to listen to some cute singers lead by Hermionine. Though we would die before we figured out how to get out and then had difficulty finding our bus back to the hotel. What a zoo. Hope never to go here again.

This ride is absolutely amazing! If you and your family are Harry Potter fans then this is definitely the ride for you. The line alone was worth it! The attention to detail is amazing. The only regret I have is that I didn’t get to ride it 100 more times!!

Universal studios is a must great day out for everyone lots to see and enjoy the Harry Potter is a great experience great theme park overall we went Christmas time and the parades were great the kids love it it really made the holiday
Ithought thr tickets were a little pricey I could not have paid for us to do universal and disney on the same trip

This was our annual family getaway - and it was fun as usual! We saw the Blue Man Group at City Walk! It was fun as well! There is always so much to do: rides, shop, eat, live music, photos, and so much more!

We really had a wonderful time here, although it was VERY expensive. We had to buy admission to the two different parks, plus fast-passes (which really are a must if you don't want to stand in line for hours.) and it topped nearly 650 bucks for just my husband and myself. That aside, it was a great experience. I do not recommend the dining plan, didn't really seem to save us time or money.

Have visited Disney many times with family, tried out universal (original) and was a worthwhile experience, not as busy as disney, parking is closer, and moving walkways are nice, but the experience is more 3d virtual...best rides are 1.mummy- cool roller coaster effect ride with one medium drop, speed and effects, goes fast but cool 2.transformers- the first time on this ride, whoa! After that it's cool but not the same 3.fast and furious- unexpected, but very fun and immersive 4.simpsoms-funny story type 3d .. Harry Potter was a little disappointing, the world seems like a giant cash register experience for the park Worth a visit with kids 7 or older!

We went in August for thr first time and had the best vacation ever. Fast Pass was well worth the money. Park was very clean staff seemed to be very helpful. Fopod is pretty pricey no matter where or what you eat not really worth the cost. gettiong in a hour eary was a great bonus we did not expect. Harry Potter was mind blowing so realalistic. Ride were pretty good Hogwarts Train has to be experenced round trip, Butter beer was fantastic frozen was the best..Pl;anning our nest tri[p to Disny will update after our trip is complete..
Amazing day out. Got a 14day pass for around £260 but so worth it. A must see if your in florida. Island of adventure is the better side but must do both.

Before you think I am bias please keep in mind I’ve lived in this area and have visited all the attractions for the last 31 years. I have 2 daughters now ages 10 & 6. In this last decade the Disney theme parks was our thing primarily because the girls were to young and small to really enjoy the rides here at universal studios. Now I thought “YES!” finally I get to have fun with my daughters on a more grown up level... Finally I get to ride real rides again!! Lol! ;-) Honestly the rides are awesome!! The place is kept clean!! Except every restroom (wife said women’s was the same) that seemed like a truck stop. BUT.... the employees are so rude and nasty. Please and thank you is not in their vocabulary. They are not polite. Don’t ask any questions because you will be met with aggravation that you’ve asked. The wife and I made no remarks so the children wouldn’t notice, but both my daughters asked on several separate times as to why were we being spoken to rudely. Even poor elderly folks trying to move on and off rides were told,” sit down it’s not that hard”. Honestly I was hoping to be an annual pass holder and move up from the kiddie rides to the pre teen and adult rides.... but no thank you. I don’t want to be treated like a piece of garbage and spoken to like I’m nothing. We spent well over $2,000 on 2 days between tickets, food and Harry Potter stuff. This was our 10 year olds dream birthday and we pulled it off and had a ton of fun. Just ignored the indifferent employees. Retraining would go a long way. Or take a page from Disney’s guest relations play book.
We had a fantastic time. Love the rides and the park is very clean. Staff was extremely helpful and friendly.

We were so excited to check out Universal .... it seemed expensive... we knew it would be busy .... we had no idea it was ridiculous. People were completely jammed ... everything was so expensive and wait .... wait wait wait. Wait for a beer wait for a ride wait to get in wait to get there... not fun. It was like $13.00 for a pizza slice... for Canadians that’s $17.50 ... there’s 5 of us. It cost us $77.00for lunch. 🤪 . We got the buy 2 days get 2 day pass... one day we went on 3 rides... we got there at noon and gave up at 7 pm .... 3 rides. That to me says they just want to make money and do not care about your experience. The staff aren’t friendly. They are just putting people through ....next.... Some of the rides are really fun .... Harry Potter part is so neat but it was claustrophobic it was so busy. We had a super cool experience with Beetle Juice I guess that made it worth the $2000 🤪🤪🤪🤪
Universal had something for everyone. The teens loved Island ofAdventure and especially the Harry Potter rides and attractions.

Saw several shows and rode a lot of rides. Some favorite rides were Men in Black, Transformers and Despicable Me Minion Mayhem. I definitely faced my fears riding Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit. I was excited to finally see Diagon Alley. Loved the dragon on top of Gringotts that spits fire, seeing the knightbus and seeing Kreacher peeking out of Grimmauld Place. Was a little disappointed in Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts. It was short and I thought they could have done more with it. The Hogwarts Express was great. Be aware that you have to have tickets to both sides of the park to ride it.
We had a really good time here. I am a big Harry Potter fan so I was always going to be fairly happy but the rest of the park was actually very good too. We had a good day.

My sister and I have come back two years in a row at Christmas time because we’ve had so much fun. This year my sister in law joined us for then fun! Harry Potter World is amazing and I would recommend it to anyone fan or not.

The family loved this park, with 2 parks there is so much to do that you will Need more than a day to visit and do the rides! The restaurants are great...a bit expensive but it’s a theme park so to be expected... food was decent and for marvel lovers it’s a must!! Well worth a visit

Great rides and if you're a Harry Potter fan this and Islands of Adventures park is the place to be. Good rides, themed roller coasters and a mix of virtual reality. Fun park but be prepared - the in park restaurants are very overpriced. It's an expensive day all around parking is ridiculous at $25+, then the tickets, then any meals - but it's still a fun experience.

Universal is much fun. The trick I’ve found is to stay at a park hotel that offers a fast pass just for one night and you get the shorter lines for two days. But we went in both March and December and even the lines without the fast pass were relatively short. Another thing is if you get the meal plans in the end it saves you about 5 bucks. I’m gonna be honest, we did share some of the food because the entrées are large, but I feel guilty about it.

Universal Studios Florida has lots of 3D rides that can give you a good adrenalin flush. Fast & Furious, Racing thru New York with Jimmy Fallon, scary rapid Mummy ride, Transformers battle ride, Minnions Despicable 2 wonderful ride, upside down vertical up and straight down roller coaster and the not yo he missed Diagon Alley where you get immersed in Harry Porter's world. Lots of other places to go and have fun. Do enjoy and do whatever you fancy. Be brave. Go have your optimum adrenalin flush

Went on the Orlando informer meet-up night. 1 price gets you in and gree food and beverages all night with free play in the arcades. No waits for the rides as its limited access. Best way to do the park but anytime the park is still great.

We visited for the second time this year just last week. It was such a great time even though the weather turned a bit cooler than expected. The Macy’s Christmas Parade was simply gorgeous and we enjoyed the Grinch performance so much. The costumes and acting and music were so professional. Wizarding World never disappoints and the closing ceremonies in each park should not be missed. We definitely visit Orlando during off seasons since crowds make me crazy! My only request is that a bit more seating is added in the Wizarding world. I want to just sit and enjoy the area especially in Diagon Alley! And enjoy my Butterbeer.

We purchased annual passes for our family of 5 which had a deal for 3 additional months, we decided to go to both parks December 18-19, 2018. The Harry Potter world at both parks were fantastic, they truly out did themselves. We were only able to ride a few rides including Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey 👌🏾, Hogwarts Express was perfection (different train show each way), Diagon Alley is everything and in my opinion the only reason to visit Universal Studios which is where we spent most of our time including dining there at Three Broomsticks 🧹 🧹🧹. The food is on point, healthy and the venue is something straight from the movie. The entire town transports you into the fantasy world of Harry Potter 💯.  Please listen to me carefully and stay away from the Fast and the Furious ride, it’s a complete waste of time, a total let down and it should be removed completely. I suggest the Harry Potter double decker bus with the Caribbean talking dead heads as a ride 👊🏽😎I know Universal has the money and the power to make that happen. In case you’re wondering because you will be if you don’t know but the Butter Beer tastes like sweet butterscotch, you can get it cold or frozen, we got 1 frozen and shared among the 3 of us which was more than enough. You’re welcome!

It had been raining the day before and we were excited to get to Universal Studios. We got to the park early and it was a made rush. Going through the security checkpoint was a madhouse. There was not really a line just a mass of people pushing towards the security checkpoint. Had to work to keep my family of six together. Once we finally made it pass security it was free reign as you walk to the park of your choice. We of course chose Universal Studios. As we walk through the City Walk we saw a lively area that was fully staffed and full of tourist. Be sure to take a picture in front of the Universal globe.  After that we came to another checkpoint that turned out to be the gate. Again this area was so packed and unorganized it seemed like we were just in a mass of people going no where. After about 20 minutes we made it to the gate. They checked each ticket and scanned the fingerprint of my family members to associate with a ticket. I asked if they purge finger print info. The gate attendant said they do once the ticket expired. I don’t want my finger print held by a private company so I hope that is true.  Once inside I took the advise of other reviewers and went to the back of the park. The best rides for us were the Mummy Revenge and Fast and Furious. We tried the Simpson’s ride and found it to be very dated and it seems the simulation is not synced properly. The movement of the ride did not match the screen which resulted in motion sickness. After that the kids waited in line for 45 minutes to ride the Woody Woodpecker rollercoaster. It was a 2 minute ride and they said it was not worth it. I appreciated their honesty.  The big catch was when we were hungry and didn’t want to leave the park so we decided to eat at Mel’s Diner. Big mistake the food was very basic and we ended up paying 80 dollars for food. I get it it’s park food, however they should do a better job with the quality of food. We ate because it was warm and we were hungry. The next day we planned accordingly and ate outside the park at City Walk and had better quality food at a cheaper price. Overall our visit was good and feel like we got what we paid for.

Overall experience was fun and for a family with a special needs kid the day was great and smooth  But OMG the prices , we had to say goodbye to over $400 US for 1 day, 2 adults and one kid just to get in.  Lines are crazy (some over 3 hours) as well as the restaurant are all packed up.  Never again on the high season

We came here during the off season during mid September. We also bought the express pass for an extra cost, but wasn't needed during the off season. We could have probably also done two parks in one day. It is probably recommend it during the high season though. Universal parks are more movie and more adult oriented than Disney. The rides were amazing, and the environment was very nice to wander around in. It felt like being on a giant movie set. There were also live acts around every once in a while and I enjoyed interacting and taking pictures with some of the characters. the rides that got crowded the quickest were the Minions ride and the Harry Potter rides. Either way, I would definitely recommend coming during the off season. It's a much more enjoyable experience whizzing through the lines and riding everything in one day.

Getting fast pass in USS is a must even though it is pretty expensive. Nonetheless, it was worthwhile otherwise the queuing time is really ridiculous.  The parade was nice with good performance on show. The only lacking in this theme park compared to Disney which was their competitor is the fireworks.

We visited New Years Eve. Great way to end the year and ring in the new. Lots of activities for families or for young adult clubbing. Expect a long day and be prepared to wait about an hour for each ride during peak season. Loved they have free lockers to store belongings during rides. Would go back again.

As you can imagine there is a pile of walking here. We did over 10,000 steps in the park. I have problems walking. We were four adults (Granny, Grandpa, Mom and Dad), plus two children 6 and 2. So, helpful hints: 1. Go Early, if you book your tickets online you can access the park earlier (8am). 2. Make sure you have downloaded the PDF on your email for the park entrance if you want to do it electronically on your phone. They don’t like screenshots. I had to open up my email and show them the original PDF. 3. Head to the back of the park to see the Harry Potter stuff first. Even so, the queue is about 50min long. Remember you have to dump your back packs st a locker first, or use Grandpa as the walking locker for all the gear. The queue for the lockers was about 10 minutes plus. 4. When you get through the entrance veer to the right and go up through the Simpsons area and then across the bridge. It is not crowded going this route. 5. Work your way back to the Minions ride and if you want to cut your wait time down, use the stationary ride queue. 6. We then went to the Simpsons (Krusty Burger) and had lunch, then did the ride. I would recommend doing the ride first, then lunch, as it is a bit bumpy. 7. Then do the ET ride, it isn’t busy. Bags can be taken on this ride. 8. Then do the Woody woodpecker roller coaster ride, again using Grandpa as the locker for all the packs. 9. Bring a small stroller, even if the kids may not need it. You can use it as a shopping trolley, carry all thing. 10. Walking back out of the park, don’t stop until you get to the boardwalk tshopping area, then stop and get an ice cream. Take it to the Starbucks outside seating, as it is in the afternoon shade. This gives you a break, before the final push to the car park. Enjoy!

What can I say about Universal Studios. It brings out the child in you. I enjoyed every ride or set. I enjoyed transformers, fast and furious set . I would advise buying the express pass. But be forewarned, Universal Studios is an expensive place to go to. But the experiences are outstanding. and I can see why it so expensive in one way. But they need to bring down prices some. If you are a Harry Potter fan, this is the place to be. If you have walking issues please get a scooter to get around. This is a large place. Do one park a day.
Wife and I had so much fun. Much bigger than Hollywood CA. Would come back. Rides are awesome. Lots of food options. Do recommend paying for the VIP tour.

Lots to do here but note that many of the rides are actually in a stationary vehicle with a 3D screen in front. The cars shake around and jerk from side to side and you still get the roller coaster effect but after 2 or 3 they all feel a bit repetitive (for example minions and spiderman are similar.
For those who love movies, this is the place. Although in December the lines were way too long, it worth the visit.

Once you accept to pay the price for it, you can enjoy a wonderful day at the Universal studios! You are plunged into the atmosphere of all those different movies, from Hulk to Jurassic park and off course the unbelievable Harry Potter! You have shops, roller coasters, sceneries all perfectly in the themes. Seeing the potential waiting lines, I would still advise to miss the busy days to enjoy the park at the fullest.

Although we did have a fun time I found that the rides were pretty much all the same. Yes they have different themes but most of them are 4D where you wear glasses, which goes with the overall idea of universal but you can get a better mix at some of the other parks. Also the prices were absolutely outrageous. In order to not have 2 hour wait times we decided to purchase the express pass (which if you don't expect at least hour long waits for every attraction) with that said - my husband and I went just the two of us for one day and spent almost $600 I find that completely ridiculous and not worth it.
This place is amazing, it makes you feel like in a movie, is perfect for family trips, the best part is the world of harry potter!

This one is definitely meant for the teens and adults in the group. We had a two year old and could only do a couple things with her in Simpsons and that was about it. Harry Potter is an absolute must see though
Excellent lay out and parks and rides. Great prices and fair prices on food and merchandise. This place set the bar for expectations of theme parks.

Here’s a list of good and bad attractions if you had to queue more than 15 minutes. Good:- - Ripe Ride Rockin’ Rollercoaster - Escape from Gringots - Transformers - Shrek - Simpson’s Ride - Mummy Ride - Men in Black Bad:- - E.T. - Fast and the Furious - Jimmy Fallon Race through New York  What’s good is that if your only adults then you can easily do the park in a day by just going on these key rides. If your with kids and the weather is good then just do some of the rides but spend time in the Curious George splash park in the kids area. This and the Horror Makeup show are the best things about this park. Beyond the splash park there’s an indoor play area for smaller kids. An easy hour of fun. My top tip is to go on the disposable me ride as soon as it opens as it’s always got long queues and therefore haven’t been on it because I didn’t want to wait an hour with kids.

The layout is massive, plenty to do for every interest, LOTS of walking. Very relaxing way to spend a day. Expensive, but once in a lifetime trip. Harry Potter lovers will be in heaven! Street shows like Blues Brothers awesome!

As a Florida resident I go to Universal Studios/Islands of Adventure more than I’d Like to. When I first went, many years ago, I felt like it was all fire in my face and head thrashing. I didn’t care if I ever went again. Years later a group of friends wanted to go, so I went, hesitantly. It was better, maybe because it was friends and not family. I ended up getting an annual pass. The pass ran out and I again stopped going. Last year I went once, and again last month. I’m back to feeling like it’s all smashing you around and banging your head. It’s just not for me.
Go to universal at least 3 times a month as we are pass holders. We love it there between and rides, shows and parades. We love watching the blues brothers show. We always have a great time there

Second visit to Universal. Tried different rides to previous visit. Transformers ride was out of action for about 40 mins until announcement informed us the ride was broken, with no advice of resume time. Left the ride, and of course so did many others, making the next rides a huge wait. Not a great experience that day. Really good idea to plan what you’re doing, and what you can’t go home without doing, it alleviates the walking around aimlessly, and safeguards your time. Do the Fast n Furious, it’s NOT scary, but great fun.

We loved this section of Universal Studios. All of our favorites- the Simpsons, Diagon Alley, transformers, and the Mummy were in this part. I highly recommend staying on site so that you can take advantage of the early park entrance.

I was able to experience Universal for three days in February. I traveled with two daughters age 13 and 11. I was surprised by the lack of variety in the rides, everything is pretty much virtual reality. I was also surprised by the adult nature of the rides. They were loud, intense, scary, and slightly mysogynistic, really Fast and Furious, is that what women look like going to a party? There was a lot of public drinking, which leads to a lot of public intoxication. Though I will say the park is nicely laid out, and can handle crowds well, and Harry Potter is amazing, the experience was nothing unique or spectacular. All the employees we saw, with the exception of the Harry Potter employees, were high school and college students who seemed to be going through the motions rather than happy and excited about their jobs. In all the Harry Potter locations that was different the employees really were enthusiastic, helpful, and of a variety of ages. I also couldn't help notice how unaccessible it was for anyone in a wheelchair.

Had one day to visit Universal. Huge fans. Then get up to the gate and it is just shy of $1000 CAD for a family of four for one day! 10 hours, 1000? Such a rip off! Come on. Why do you hate us Canadians?

These cost extra to the standard park tickets, so just another way to get more money. Don’t go over Halloween if you plan for a normal visit basically, your day is cut short and price is the same.
