My husband and and I were starving after a day in the parks but all cafes were closed. When I asked a member of staff if I can buy an ice cream, they said I’d have to leave the park to do so. I was told by Universal customer services that the reason they shut all their restaurants 2 hours earlier is so staff can get home in time.  RUDE STAFF!! The staff were SO RUDE which I found disappointing as everyone we came across in Florida prior were lovely. I’m from London so I’m used to people being rude but it was a huge shock even for me!! We were shoved on and off rides, people were actually shouted at by staff, they’re short tempered, extremely rude and very unhelpful. They’re busy fooling around with each other and generally don’t want to be there! Generally ruins your experience and your left feelings a bit bullied.  CR*PPY FAIRGROUND GAMES $$$ Too many fair ground games. They had lots of basketball hoop games, the ones when you win a cr*ppy prize for getting a ball in the hoop. For some reason there were loads of these scattered round the park. You had to pay extra for them and the prizes were terrible!! I can get that at Brighton pier, don’t expect to see it at such an infamous, expensive theme park like universal studios. You already pay enough for entry & they want you to spend money winning a cheap nasty teddy. Really ruins and cheapens the whole experience.  DOESNT LIVE UP TO THE LEGACY! Took away their classic movie ride!! I’ve always wanted to visit universal studios, being a huge movie fan, it’s been a dream of mine. They took away the jaws ride, terminator ride, back to the future ride & other classics which was quite sad. After saving for our anniversary trip, I can not stress how disappointing the whole entire day was! Please PLEASE beware before you go! It’s far too much money for what you get! And universal studios DO NOT REFUND regardless of your experience. I’ve had to give it 1 star purley because of the price compared to experience/ disappointment

Our 3rd trip here, and again we had a great time. The Harry Potter areas are fantastic, especially now that your Express Pass works on those rides too. We have always stayed at the Hard Rock to take advantage of the included Express Passes, and HIGHLY recommend it. Not inexpensive, but the wait times can get very high without Express.. The Fast and Furious ride was a letdown. Could have been so much better. Food choices are noticeably better than at Disney. It's nice to not have to plan ahead to get into a restaurant.
Great venue. Great rides. Get the Express Pass to move up in the lines ($50 but worth it). Don't miss the Harry Potter attractions. Great fun.
Always worth it for 2 reasons. Harry Potter rides and The Hard Rock cafe. Never disappointed in these areas.
If you're a Harry Potter fan, which we are, you'll love it. Jurassic Park, Kong and Spiderman we're good too. I feel like it's all about Harry Potter though.
Went there with my family and the top attraction was the world of Harry Potter, it was like being a part of the movies!
You'll have to save your pennies, as this park gets more expensive every year, but Harry Potter soothes the sting a bit.

I thought there was no way I could spend a day and a half st Universal, but I was really wrong. In addition to the rides, there are pop up shows in the streets and lots of parades. There’s always something exciting happening there! Diagon Alley is breathtaking whether or not you’re a Harry Potter fan (and be sure to try that butterbeer!), and many of the rides are excellent — worthy of riding more than once. The roller coaster requires that you use a free locker before you get in line, and there is a metal detector, so be sure to use it. The Mummy was surprisingly good, as was the Transformers ride. And don’t miss the Escape from Gringotts! However, I highly recommend that you get a Universal Express pass. We were able to ride three to four rides an hour while regular park patrons were able to ride that many in one whole day.
amazing 3D rides like transformers,the latest Jimmy fallon ride, harry potter- efg but 3 hour wait time. Must go on thrilling rides such as revenge of the mummy
We love making Universal Studios one of our theme park choices when we visit Orlando! Lots of simulator rides. One of our all time favourites is The Mummy. Can’t wait to visit again!

Been 10 years since our last Orlando trip - so great to see changes to the two parks universal has. The Harry Potter additions are very popular with all ages and have to say well worth the trip.  Tips: if you are going - do take a lanyard with card holder as the way the express fast pass system works now it will help if you have them so you can have your passes easily to hand. The rides now need you to stow your gear into lockers so keep your stuff small so you can use the free lockers.

Universal studios Florida is a great vacation destination for the family. I have 3 kids 10 to 15 and they loved this place. There are different ride levels for all ages. Great food choices and selection and we found that the food venues were very helpful for our gluten free needs/allergies. We had tickets for the two parks (not the water park) and easily spent two days trying to do it all and there was still lots to do that we will have to do next time. This is a great place but it can be crowded and so be prepared to wait.

Lots to do, see & eat for all ages. We stayed at one of the resort hotels to make the most of our 2 days there. The Harry Potter light show was amazing! We had a 3 day pass so chose to go back on the way to the airport to kill some time, just avoid the water rides if you do so. Would go back for sure

I am writing this review while I wait in a 120 minute queue for 7 Dwarfs Mine Train at Magic Kingdom... yes, 2 hours! My husband and I are late 20-30 somethings, no kids, and we were totally spoiled by our visit to Universal Studios earlier this trip. The single rider line is AWESOME! We went on Escape from Gringotts TWICE in about 20 minutes when the park first opened. We also rode Rock It Roller Coaster 3 times using the single rider option (and once we even got to sit together!)  Diagon Alley is awesome, go to Ollivanders at the end of the day, no one will be there. People say the staff at Disney is more enthusiastic but so far that has not been the case for us, the staff at Universal were awesome! Special shout outs to Mr. Ollivander and the Knight Bus conductor, Jimmy Fallon’s barbershop quartet and Hashtag the Panda, and the guys doing the Fast and Furious pre-show.  Be warned, if you get motion sick (I do) there are a lot of simulator rides that might not be super fun. I survived the Mummy and Transformers (which got stuck twice when we rode it but they offered single use express passes to compensate) but Race Through New York was hard to get through and we skipped the Simpson’s altogether. ET was super cute though. If you stay later into the night you can get through the lines faster... and DO SINGLE RIDER WHEN AVAILABLE!!! :)  Ultimately I wish we had done 2 days at Universal so we could have also done Islands of Adventure and Hogsmeade! It’s expensive but it’s good value for your entertainment dollar (cheaper and less crowded than Disney, too.)

This is a Very Good Attraction; Advantages: Lots of Nice Restaurants! Fun Rides! Excellent idea of a Park-to-Park Train! Nice staff! Good idea of Kid-friendly amusements! Disadvantages: It's Expensive! It's usually very Busy! It takes at least 45 minutes to get on each Ride! There are even massive queues to get (a) Snack(s) and/or Drink(s) (about 30 minutes)! It's quite difficult to find a place to park a Car!

This was a great day for all ages, we had my eldest nephew 14. Then my sister was there with my other nephews 7 & 9. Also their in-laws - this place is amazing, for all ages! A variety of rides and really is something for everyone. Jimmy Fallon racing through New York is super fast though I was shaking after!

Took family here for the day, 2 park ticket - YOU ABSOLUTELY NEED FAST PASS. Queue's were long but with Fast Pass manageable. Lots of 3D/4D rides which suited me. Harry Potter World was quite amazing - Castle and train was superb. King Kong ride long queue and not worth really time, - Transfomers good, Shrek Good, Despicable Me good, Simpsons good, Kids liked Mummy ride, they didn't rate Fast and Furious. Tip bring sandwiches or food as expensive and queues very long for food in park.
The rides rock in the park. You must do Rip Ride Rocket, The Mummy and Diagonally. Harry Potter area is much better on Universal side.
I have been there with my family , it was amazing and both children and adult were happy over-there.

My wife and I wanted to see the Harry Potter rides and shops. So we visited Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure on a Saturday. I enjoyed the Escape from Gringotts ride. We rode the Hogwarts Express in both directions. We did walk though the brick wall at Platform 9-3/4 at the King's Cross Station. I called the Ministry of Magic from the phone phone outside the train station, but the Ministry was closed.  I did many of the thrill rides (Men in Black, Revenge of the Mummy, Fast & Furious, Transformers, etc.). My impression is that the rides were imitating each other (go forward, go backward, spin around, stop, etc.), but with different scenery. That made the experience a little less enjoyable.  I was disappointed in the quality and variety of the merchandise at the Despicable Me Minion gift shop. I was hoping to buy some t-shirts or other items, but didn't find anything that appealed to me.  My wife and I enjoyed several of the shows such as Blues Brothers, and Celestina and the Banshees.  We opted to eat dinner outside the park at City Walk. There were many good restaurants there at reasonable prices.

We've spend a few days between Universal studios and Island of Adventure this May. We bought the tickets for 14 days using the 3 parks(the previous 2 and the Volcano bay which is a water park and was in the price ) and for 2 of these days we’ve had an express pass . (Which was a life saver).Universal is a place for children older than 6 for most of the rides and its very fun. The Harry Potter area is really nice but the train connecting the two parks is not worth the money. In general everything there from food to toys was very expensive.If you wanna avoid the crowds go there after 1800 and then you don’t have to pay for the parking

This was my third visit to universal. Stayed at cabana bay for 11 days, using their transfers to the parks, with our own early access entrance to volcano bay.  We did early access once but mainly went back in the evenings, walking straight onto rides. We did Disney a bit but now, as no kids, that universal is my favourite. I find it so much more organised, more space to walk around, better food outlets, better ques especially entering the park. I love the atmosphere and everything about universal. Roll on the new park coming in 5yrs time!!! Disney have nothing on this place

We absolutely loved Universal! It was expensive to get in but well worth it. Make sure to pay the extra to get into both parks on site. We went from open to close. The rides were fantastic! Not sure I’d recommend for small children but definitely great for 10 and up.

This was our 4th trip to Universal. We are not roller coaster people but we always find lots of great rides here! We love the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Get butter beer you won’t regret it. There are many great places to eat. Recommend Mythos and either the leaky cauldron or three broomsticks. The crowd size and lines are always better than Disney even on busy days and we love that you can buy express passes and skip the lines.

We went to USF in December to celebrate both Christmas and my wife’s birthday! The highlights of this park were for our family!!  #1 Draigon Alley #2 Despicable me Minions! #3 The Christmas parade! #4 The Revenge of The mummy roller coaster!  We highly recommend these rides and experiences when you visit USF!

The atmosphere of the place is pretty fantastic. The scenery is amazing all around the premises, especially the Harry Potter district which is truly astonishing. A must visit for fans. Although the attractions are not for people with motion sickness as almost 85% is 4D with high speed or high altitude changing simulators.

We started our day going to guest services to find out about accommodations for my daughter. She was just diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. Her doctor said to bring a letter to get a guest assistance pass. Dean, Kelly and Miguel said she didn’t need one. They were condescending, rude and talked down to me. They told us every que was inside with air conditioning. That was a complete lie. We were in several lines in direct sun and others inside that were stifling with no fans. They said workers would be there to give us a wheelchair if she needed to sit down. They said a worker would let her leave to go somewhere private to give herself her shot or to go to the bathroom and could get back in line. That wasn’t true either. We went from 40-60 minutes without seeing someone in multiple lines. We were told there were many places to get a drink or fill up water bottles in the lines. We saw a couple water fountains but they were hot. We were told we could bring our bag and use the medical locker. That was the only thing that was true but that added up to 10 minutes to our waiting each time. I feel like I was lied to about the “accommodations” just to get me out of guest services. Disney helped us with no questions asked. Stay away from Universal if you need accommodations of any type. They will not help you!

My experience in Universal was amazing! The people in the shops and conducting the rides were very welcoming and friendly. The roller coaster "Escape from Gringotts" is the number one ride you should try. It takes you through the scene when Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Griphook are stealing Gryffindors Sword from Gringotts. Take the magical Hogwarts express to Hogsmead! Visit Honneydukes to load up on some magical sweets! Or the Post Office to make an owl delivery! And to wrap it all up, go reward yourself with a steaming hot mug of Butterbeer! This is the best vacation Me and my family ever had!

🧹 🏰 UNIVERSAL STUDIOS 🏰 🧹  We did the VIP experience, with Sean today and highly recommend it. *Saved waiting in ques for 60minutes *covered everything we wanted in the two park *best seats on the ride (for effects or the seats less likely to get wet) *walked around the back lot studios *learnt how the rides operate and safety measures taken *breakfast and lunch included  Was such an amazing day, the detail in the rides especially Harry Potter was mind blowing. Most rides were 3D/4D - simulators and felt like you were part of an experience. One of my favourite rides would have been the Harry Potter forbidden journey where Harry takes you on a trip high above Hogwarts and the castle grounds, where you are chased by Hagrid’s pet dragon, while the Whomping Willow and a hoard of dementors try to spoil the trip. It really did feel like you were flying over hogwarts and trying to get away from the dragon. Another good one was the jimmy fallon, where you actually felt like you were racing through and over New York City. Just amazing the feeling you get.

Had three generations in the park. All enjoyed most parts of the park. Kids liked the Harry Potter exhibits. Adults enjoyed the rides and shows. Finally got to ride the "Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit" roller coaster, it did not disappoint, it was quite exciting!! Other rides liked by all were: Transformers, Minions, Simpsons, Men In Black, Race Through New York starring Jimmy Fallon. Of course it is very expensive to eat and even grab a soda or water, but what can you do. We all enjoyed the park overall.
My favourite part is the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. I could just hang out in Diagon Alley or Hogsmeade all day!

Staying in Universal Cabana bay we visited frequently over a 2 week period. Only took advantage of the extra hour once, it’s not as you would think as many rides still don’t open until 9am.  Queues were varied depending on time of day. Gringotts ride was the longest we experienced - just over an hour. We found going to the park later in the day was best as it was less busy. My daughter aged 11 loved the Simpsons and Men in Black rides. We didn’t think the Fast & Furious rise was worth the wait and wouldn’t go back on this in the future.  We bought refillable souvenir cups, you can use them throughout stay recharging them each time for about $10. I thought food/drinks and merchandise was expensive in the park.  Light show around the lagoon at Park Closing time was fantastic, sorry I only stayed to watch it once on our last night. Really recommend this.

There is so much to do, you definitely need at least 2 days to do everything - unless you get an Express Pass. My kids, 8 & 11, loved Rip Ride Rockit and Diagon Alley...just be prepared bc the wands are between $46-52. The ice cream shop on Diagon Alley is fantastic.

On our holiday we’ve done the 4 main Disney parks, sea world, discovery cove and both main Universal parks. Universal Studios definitely won over Disney. It wasn’t too crowded, the facilities were well kept, the rides were fun and it didn’t come across like such a money grab as Disney where everything is there to get you to buy something.  My only real complaint (and this is true of Disney also) is the over reliance on 3D/4D “rides” where rather than build a proper ride, they cheap out and whack a screen in front of a “simulator”. This can work well (transformers, Simpson’s) or it can be just awful (fast and furious, jimmy fallon). It’s a shame to see rides like Jaws replaced by these simple, less creative ride types. Fast and Furious was probably the worst ride of our vacation due to its long boring build up followed by sitting in a “bus” full of other people to then just watch a screen while being bounced around a bit. Sitting st the front you’d assume would be the best position to rule out looking over everyone except I could see the rails the bus sat on so had next to zero immersion.  However overal, impressed and really enjoyed it

We visited both Islands of Adventure and Universal and had a great time. Food was good, the rides were a lot of fun. We had a pretty wide aged group(7-70) within our party and everyone seemed to have a great time. We only ran into one ride the closed down while we were in and we were able to use our fast pass on everything we wanted and had a blast.

Bought the military appreciation tickets that allowed you to visit both parks for 4 days. You can honestly get done with both parks in 3 days unless you’re trying to do the new Harry Potter ride. That ride will make you wait for hours unless it rains then all outdoor rides stop due to safety reasons. Do the popular rides first so your wait time isn’t as long during the middle of the day. The last 2 hours in the park you can do more rides in a shorter wait time due to everyone leaving the park by that time. Stick around at the end of the night for the fireworks in either universal or island of adventure.

Before visiting Orlando, everybody said, that Universal Studios was a "must see". Because of the very high price, I DID doubt whether it was worth it. It was! Yes, it IS expensive. And it should be cheaper. But I wouldn't have missed it. Out Family consisted of three kids (15/17/19) and they all loved the experience. I was warned about the waiting time. Expect one Harry Potter-experience, that had a wating time of 180 (!) minutes throughout the Whole day, everything was decent (=waiting times from 30 to 60 minutes). In general: Don't miss these themeparks (we went to Island of Adventure and Universial Studios … you can do both in one day).

There is a lot to do in this park. Diagon Alley is an awesome addition. Some classic experiences still hold up. There are several fun entertainment shows (Horrow Show, Beat Builders, Animal Show, Blues Brothers, Parade, etc). The light and fountain show at the end of the day is great. If hot, go to Fievel's water slide (great for kids of all ages, and an easy head dunk fountain for adults). The movie characters roaming around are fun (especially the Men in Black). Schwab's was a good ice cream stop.

We visited both Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios. As a couple with out children we loved visiting both Universal Studio parks. This was our first visit in about fifteen years. We had always enjoyed all the rides both thrill and non thrill rides. We were very disappointed that some of the old rides had been retired: Jaws, Earthquake, Twister, old King Kong( which the new ride is awesome!). We couldn’t get into Hagrads ride after five days of trying. We tried early, late, mid day etc. what was so disappointing was they couldn’t give us an opening day or time. Couldn’t tell us if we waited in line for two hours if it would stay open or close abruptly. That wasn’t even our biggest disappointment!  We loved some of the less thrill rides as a break like jaws twister Earthquake etc as a ride to take a break from the roller coasters. We have the disposable income and not many of the rides are set up for us aging ex roller coaster folks that like a break between rides. If I’m spending 5 thousand dollars for five days of fun it needs to be a bit more balanced. When you teenagers want to come back to enjoy your favorite rides in ten twenty years or so and there all gone? Oh well enjoy being an old fart. We are still into some new rides but also a few of our old favorites too.  The hotels at Universal are much better and have awesome services now and we loved that just the parks are in a transition. Maybe all the construction might be a positive but too many areas are closed to construction or are simply boring now. Eric and Adele
We had a fun filled day. Seeing the characters was a highlight. The water rides were a must on a hot day. We had a great time.

Visited as a family of 4 with 2 children age 4 and 7. Great for my 7 year old just frustrating paying almost an adult price ticket for my 4 year old as she was only tall enough for about 3 rides which felt like a waste of money for her. On the other hand if your travelling with children older it's brilliant myself and my son loved the thrill rides. Waiting times are quite long especially if you don't arrive at the park on opening. Some great shows for the kids they loved the parade seeing some of their favourite characters.

Great location that draws many people. I would recommend looking up area details so you do not have to ask security. They seem to be preoccupied and very rude. I asked two questions on my trip there about directions and was met with very rude comments. That is sad as this place is vibrant and great for all ages. It probably explains why it has taken second place to Icon Park and Disney.

Having pre purchased a ticket for all 3 parks in advance and not liking to queue, I discovered if you book a room at one of Universals top 3 hotels you are given unlimited "express passes" for your party. Seeing the purchase price of the passes was $600 for our family of 4, the price of our one night stay was $450! No brainer and hotel duly booked. The Studios and Adventure Island are a must visit if you are in Orlando and both offer a great mix of thrill rides and 4d rides. These are world class rides and you will come away smiling for sure. We loved the Harry Potter experience with the Hogwarts Express proving transport between the parks and The Simpsons land, the Crusty Burger and Duff beer were to die for! It is worth getting to the parks early, however, with the unliited express passes the longest queue we experienced was 15 minutes when regular queues were in excess of 1-2 hours for the popular rides. We didn't manage to visit Volcano Bay but understand it is a top water park. All in all, take a minimum 2 day visit to Universal and you will be blown away. Cant wait to go back.
Timely to declare Universal Studios the number one amusement (theme) park just before DisneyWorld opens the Star Wars themed park in August?! Just wait acouple months and reassess that determination.

My partner and I along with his sister, her fiancé and 2 daughters spent the day at Universal back in August 2018. We were staying at Disney World resort but when booking the holiday we planned a day at Universal and booked tickets to go and when we arrived we paid extra for a single fast pass to each ride so we could get through as much as possible so although it was expensive if you only plan the one day if you can get it it’s worth getting, there’s no way we’d have done as much as we did with out it. Our hotel booked a private car to take us and pick us up as there was 6 of us this worked out cheaper than getting the coach that picks up from the hotel. We enjoyed all the different areas of the park, loved the Simpsons area and ride as well Harry Potter World and all the rides there and walking around the different parts and going on the Hogwarts express to get to “Hogsmead” was magical. We had disappointment on Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey as it stopped on us a few times during the ride and we weren’t given another go which was annoying as we only had one fast pass for it and queues were ridiculous. Other favourite rides were the Rip Ride Rockit and The Hulk which were brilliant and other rides like The mummy and Spider-Man were great too and many more. All the rides were but we did expect there to be more big roller coaster rides but the majority were more virtual reality rides which I suppose makes sense as Universal is all about movies and shows etc and they were actually good rides apart from maybe the E.T. ride (sorry). The park also boasts plenty of places to eat, drink and shop in all areas and staff were great we had a great day from start to finish.

Been there with friends after experiencing Universal in California 3 years ago. Incomparable! Nevertheless it is still Universal Studios. So My tips are: 1. Don't go in the summer, the combination of high humidity and crowd is bad. 2. If you do go in the summer buy the park to park ticket. 3. Although expensive, buy the Express ticket (unless waiting in endless lines is your thing). 4. Don't be tempted to premium park, walking a few more steps never hurt anyone. 5. Enjoy

you'll regret wasting your money! it is 90% commercial and loud stupid music with 5% content of the actual footage of the ride! it was a wasted $36 USD! and time spent speaking with the incompetent attendant that use "no" and "i don't know" as the standard response.

I visited a lot at Universal Studios, but Harry Potter World blew me away! I loved the attention to detail, I really felt like I was inside the books! I have to say, the employees were very friendly & helpful.

Bought tickets from the official office. Explained that we wanted one day at each park, plus a half day at each, but not bothered about the Hogworts Express ride. Was told that a 4 day ticket was best option and that on day 3 we could use a day in each park. When we tried to do this today we were told that we couldn’t without paying another $50 each. 3 rides had been closed due to ‘technical difficulties’ for the whole day (including Spider-Man which is indoor) It was pouring with rain, and we had only 3 hours left in the park - all we got from customer services was that we had been given incorrect info when we were sold the tickets. No apology. No compromise. Just pay $50 or go away. We will go away and not come back. The food was also appalling. After 20 years of visiting every year, we will not be giving you our cost on again. Shockingly bad treatment of your guests.

As our kids have gotten older they just don't feel the same about Disney as they used to...so Universal was a great change that seemed to be more inline with where they are age wise and interest wise.

Come dressed to walk a great deal and have fun, especially if you have kids with you. My grandkids enjoyed the rides and food. Plenty to do and see. Be prepared to spent the whole day. We started at the Cowfish Restaurant where we met as a group to celebrate our first annual company picnic. The food was great for the adults and kids. The deserts brownie with ice cream got us all sugared up for the long walks through the park. By the end of the day the my grandkid were tired and slept on their way back home.

We went numerous times over our 10 day stay at cabana bay hotel as park tickets came with the package.  Although it was so hot and humid we loved visiting here and would come all the back from London again. From blues brothers shows on the street to harry potter experiences it has it all here. Great merchandise shops throughout. Purchasing an unlimited drink cup for the day is recommended and great value. Loved the rides, from a 3d transformer to a faster paced to a inside roller coaster The Mummy, great fun for the family.  Cant wait to go again to be honest!

I loved the fast and furious ride along with the hulk roller coaster. The lines were long but these were my favorite rides. The Simpson doughnuts were huge and delicious! I wish I lived in Florida I would definitely get annual passes! Halloween horror was a blast.

I love universal so much. This place literally has something for everyone!! Wether it’s riding rides all day or watching shows or just wandering the park looking at all the wonderful details. I grew up here and I can’t wait to bring my family here for generations to come! I love all the new attractions and the classic ones *cough cough* E.T. The team members always make my day and I truly appreciate them for their hard work!

Don’t get me wrong, I love Disney World! But let me tell you, Universal Studios is the place to have fun with adrenaline! All the marvel rides, the Mummy, Simpsons Land and Harry Potter… I mean you can’t go wrong! Prices are fair and generous and customer service is utterly fantastic… Stay on one of the properties and take advantage of the amenities. Highly recommend!

We've been coming to the Universal theme parks in Florida for many years. The roller coasters, waters rides and entertainment are good. However the costs at the parks are getting ridiculous. $26 for parking then we were over $70 for 5 hot dogs and soft drinks. I see these prices as unjustified and I don't think we'll be making holiday plans here for the next few years.

Haven't been here for a few years. Visited for the two parks and horror Nights in our 14 day stay. Parking is ridiculous what a rip off $26... Cheaper to get Ubas if your doing the park and horror Nights. Food prices weren't cheap and the quality was poor. Drinks were way overpriced, people are thirsty they have no choice but to purchase them. The rides were the same and we had fun on them and carefully selected unpeak times. Never managed to get on Hagrids, not sure why they are making people queue why not use virtual waiting times. Horror night times too busy now and we won't do them again, over priced alcohol and rude security bossing us about unnecessarily. The queues were awful and seemed on purpose so people would buy fast passes which they were. Whole place is a cash cow for maximum profit and to fleece holidaymakers of hard earned cash. Never going back.

This was our third visit. Cannot believe how the food and drink prices have escalated. The average price for a bottle of water was around £3. Also, the queue for Hagrid's Motorbike Ride was three hours one day and unavailable on the other days we visited. The Harry Potter parts of Universal were heaving with people whereas the rest of the park was fine. There were several breakdowns, which then had a knock on effect to other rides. We generally love our visits here but this year was a bit of a disappointment. The park was very clean, and the staff friendly.

Came here will visiting Orlando. Great park and lots of rides to go on and things to do like Harry Potter wands.  Had a great time while here came a few days. Did not go onto hagrids ride as too long a wait just around 3 hours. But won’t complain it’s a new ride and everyone wants on. Went on all the other rides and enjoyed it worth the money.  Only negative thing I would say was $21 dollars for 2 hotdogs and staff attitude at the hotdog stall was not good and price is a bit steep but apart from that good rides good park and will be back
Been coming here every year since I was a baby, best theme parks are universal studios! Something for everyone.  HP World is unreal!

The two Universal parks have been family favorites since their inception. Still prefer the original park over the Islands of Adventure one—especially when the weather is cooler—the water rides aren’t fun when it is cold out and they are all at Islands of Adventure. The Harry Potter themed parts are quite magical—even for people like myself that are not manic about it and aren’t too familiar with the story details. Fun to watch families try their wands at the various windows. Gets VERY crowded by late morning so best to go super early or late in the day—not just for the rides there but just to enjoy the experience. The flavored drinks and ice creams are worth a try for sure!! Miss the old Back to the Future, Twister and Jaws rides. Skip the new Fast and Furious ride unless the line is short. We were all very disappointed that it was all pretty much computer graphics and not much else. Just not too exciting. Fear Factor, Animal Acts and Horror Makeup Show all worth seeing. Men in Black is still a fav and lots of fun. Great to see all the characters out and about. If you go, ask about a scavenger hunt—we found out about it from another guest and they were having so much fun with it. Disappointed no one told us when we arrived. So much to see and do. Will go back—we always do.

Many of the rides were 3D ride-through special events, rather than true rides. I'd rather visit Six Flags or Cedar Fair parks, pay less money, and enjoy more thrill rides. I'm just not a "special effects for the sake of special effects" person.

If you r going to visit Universal Studios/Island. It's best to get the PARK TO PARK passes. That is what we did and we had a BLAST going from one park to the other any time we wanted to. We WASN'T STUCK in one park all day. We can't wait to go back and do it all again!! # LOVE IT

This is my first time coming to universal as an adult and overall I like the park and would definitely come back when they open their 4th park.  What I concluded from my trip:  Do not compare universal to a six flags or highly known rollercoaster park. This is an entirely different kind of theme park. If you do, you will be disappointed.  They do not have a diverse group of rides. A lot of the rides are the same thing. Either a 3D ride in a moveable car or giant team with a story theme around it using giant screens. Or a movie theater type ride with moveable seats. The exception would be the Hollywood rip ride rocket, mummy, and Men In Black.  They all love to squirt you with water on the ride. Not a lot but where the ride has a character “spit” and they squirt some water at you.  A lot of the lines have a giant room or “elevator” in the middle of the line where you are no longer in line and it allows the people behind you to move in front of you. Not sure why they couldn’t keep the queue line in these rooms so that doesn’t happen  The positive We went during a slow week and waited 5-10 min per ride. Seeing how much of the line we didn’t have to wait in, I can’t imagine how disappointed I would be if we had to wait hours for these rides. Definitely do your research and find a slow week. No need for fast pass. We were able to do the whole park in a couple hours.  Harry Potter world was pretty much the only crowded place but even the ride wasn’t a bad wait. Mostly people running around with their wands and robes yelling spells at things.

For those Harry Potter fans you need to experience this. I recently took my son to Universal Studios for vacation. Entering Diagon Alley and touring Hogwarts Castle made me lose reality for a bit and to see my son's eyes light up in wonder and amazement was worth the trip alone.

I really enjoyed universal. Eat riding the bike and helping ET get home. Also the TV animals stunts. Meeting the characters and getting a photo with each one. Disappointed couldn’t just see Harry Potter train platform without paying extra. Would have been fun if the dirty home had opened door just to shock you.

This was my first visit to Universal Studios. While I liked the rides better at Island of Adventure, I liked the Universal park better. It was less crowded & laid out better. I came in to this trip thinking it would be similar to Disney, but it’s not even comparable to Disney. I felt that the park, the attractions, & the rides were more similar to Six Flags; just on steroids. Just like I thought with Islands of Adventure, Harry Potter’s Daigon Alley was the best attraction. The Simpsons attraction was a close second. The wait times at Universal were not as long as the wait times at Islands of Adventure. I enjoyed my time at the parks & would definitely go back

We have been to HHN at universal studios several times. Our Disney/Universal expert, Robyn, with Dream Makers Vacation Services, really came through for us on this trip. I consider myself pretty good on knowing the ins and outs of Universal, but Robyn gave me some great advice on new restaurants at Citywalk, and rides at the parks. Stranger Things and Us were two of our top houses this year. Always get the express pass for HHN. And the new Hagrids roller coaster is the best I’ve ridden!!! Amazing!!

My family LOVED Volcano Bay. Loved. Everyone had such an amazing time, there were activities for all of us (5 people). My thrill seekers loved the drop water slides, while my oldest and I found our happy place with the water coaster and wave pool. The staff were helpful and pleasant, particularly Carl. We met Carl our first day assisting with lockers, and again another day offering help to those who needed it. When we booked our trip going to Volcano Bay was not high on our priority list, as it felt like an unneeded bonus to Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. It quickly became a favorite and was our first stop Christmas morning! Highly recommend for anyone one the fence about going to Volcano Bay...do it!!! PS We had no little ones (9 was our youngest) but it seemed there was plenty for them to do. Yes there were rides that catered to older kids and up but the area for the littles looked fun. I’m sure if our kids were younger they would have still enjoyed Volcano Bay.

When we plan a trip to Disney world, we usually set aside a day for Universal. But many things disappointed me this time and I wanted to post this review to have people consider if they really want to spend the money for a day there. At least so your homework. 1) First if all - if you want to see all of Happy Potter - you will need to pay to get into 2 parks. We payed $185.31 ($174+tax) for a 2 Park one day ticket per person. It costs more if you buy at the ticket booth in the park. I used a mobile delivery and had the ticket delivered to my smartphone. That’s a lot of money for a family of 4.  2) This time of year - the park is only open until 7pm. A lot of ground to cover for 2 parks and considering how much you are paying g for a ticket. 3) So you would expect the rides to be in good working condition. Especially the widely popular Harry Potter section. When we got there, the 2 rides in IOA: the new Hagrid’s Motorbike ride was closed. Harry Potter and the forbidden journey was experiencing delays. So we headed to The Eacape from Gringots ride at Universal. Wait was posted as 55 minutes. The line went slowly. We wished we had our backpack with some drink and snacks - but we had to put it in a locker ! We got to near of the end of the line after waiting in the queue for more than a 90 minutes and they “flushed the queue” due to technical difficulties! They did give us a FP on the way out - but it didn’t seem to cover the time lost (I could have went on 3 Other rides), sore feet and back from waiting in line that long (hey that’s messing with my Health and ability to do other things as a result of pain); needless to say - everyone was very upset. Not to mention that the People in line flooded the streets and now everything else was impossible to get into. Even Hogwarts express train - wasn’t an express and had a 55 minute wait. So we quickly Rushed to the Leaky Cauldron - which had really filled up. We were able to get some good food and rest a while. My Cottage pie came with a salad and was very good. We also got the bangers and mash - and my so. And his GF enjoyed those. Hubby got the fish pie and enjoyed that. We also got a kids Mac and cheese with a side of grapes and applesauce which also was good. They do seat you - maybe because it was busy. But we ended up getting a seat against the wall that was quiet. After we were done - we checked the time for Hogwarts Express - and it was still long ! So we headed to the front of the park where we could use the Front entrance to switch to the other park (IOA) since the Hogwarts Express lube was too long.. Disappointing. I used the opportunity to visit with guest relations.  4) Guest relations and what they can do: I’ll start out by saying the young woman who assisted us was very nice. However, the best she could do was offer us each another FP. I would have preferred a partial refund or another FP. I also brought up the fact that we had to pay for a locker for the ride - she didn’t bring it up on her own. Practically had to beg to get the $2 back. But She did give us $2 cash.  5) which brings me to the lockers. Most of the thrill rides have the lockers. It’s a pain and time consuming to get your stuff in and out. It requires the code from your ticket - but the code doesn’t work from a smartphone and you need to get a paper one from an attendant in the area. On top of that - If you need a Large locker - you need to pay $2 for it. We had a large backpack -So we had to pay it. They don’t take cash. You need a credit card. And you need to spend this $2 for each ride !!! What a way to make even more money after robbing you the cost of your ticket !  6) we finally got into IOA thru the front entrance. We bypassed the Incredible Hulk and the Spider-Man ride so we could get to the back of the park to check out the Wizarding world of Harry Potter before it was dark. On the way - we also noticed the King Kong ride was partially outside. So after taking some pics in Harry Potter world I’m the daylight - we back-tracked to the Skull Island King Kong ride instead of using a FP to ride Harry Potter and the forbidden journey. Since the line was long and the ride is inside, we figured we could come back. We waited a little while in the FP King Kong line - and it was very cool - albeit a bit shorter than I expected.  7) the Hagrid motorbike line was over 100 minutes and had closed on and off thru the day, so...  8) we went back to Harry Potter to find the Forbidden Journey ride closed !! It was 6pm and they were closing in an hour and we had not ridden any Harry Potter rides! We made a bee-line for the Howard’s express - but we first had to wait in line to go thru the ticket line to go to the other land in Universal. After waiting for 10 minutes in the ticket line we the. Went to wait in the Hogwarts express line. I checked the wait times one more time to see if Escape from Gringots might have reopened - holding out little hope - since it was closed most of the day after our wait. Miraculously it was open with a 25 minute wait. We made a bee-line to it after our Hogwarts express ride. We barely made it Into line at 6:58. And after waiting the allotted time - we finely were able to ride the ride! So we didn’t go home totally disappointed.  8) on a positive note - after we were done the ride - we wandered around a mostly deserted Diagon Alley. We also finally saw the dragon breath fire. The dragon didn’t breathe fire thru the day. Which is another negative. I believe the dragon breathed fire all thru the day when we were there last 5 years ago.  Thru the day we also managed to go on the Mummy, MIB and the Simpsons.  That’s 7 rides in 8.5 hours. That’s $26.47 a ride. I guess you have to also account for lunch and ambiance... but still... I can understand that the new Hagrid ride might be done because it’s new - but the other 2 have been around for over 5 years ! They shouldn’t be down. If they need maintenance - please do the maintenance in the Off-hours when no one is in the park. Also note that I read that one of the Harry Potter rides will be down for maintenance Jam 16-17 - so consider that if you plan to go on either of those days.  9) did i mention that you can save some time and get FPs for all the rides by staying on property ($$) or buying a FP ticket for all the rides for a mere $96 on top of what you’re paying already... thanks Universal ...  10) we won’t be going back any time soon. The old rides we’ve done and we’ll wait for the Harry Potter rides to be fixed or for the popularity to wean... if you really need to go - I recommend you do your homework. Download the “Universal wait times” app and monitor it a few days prior to going... check and see thru the day if the rides remain up. And buy your tickets online a day or so before you plan to go when you know the weather will be good and the rides are running. You can use the ticket they send you to your email from your phone.  Good luck !  ... And I hope to see some better ticket discounts and or longer hours from Universal for their customers. Otherwise I believe they are just thinking of making the most $$ for themselves.
Crowded beyond belief..prices has gone sky high. Tickets and food was 1500$ for a day of parkwalking in Line.

Very sad pay a lot of money, spend a lot of time To see my Kid cry like that. You destroyed our magic Hogwarts memories today.
Harry Potter was amazing! It was absolute perfection! The rest of the parks are very fun as well. Everyone is friendly and it is clean

We went at the end of January. The temps were chilly in the mornings and evenings, but very nice once the sun got up and going. Jeans and long sleeved shirts would probably be enough for most people but, if you’re cold natured, take a light jacket or sweater. Going early in the year avoids the crowds of Summer. I think the longest we waited for any ride was twenty minutes. For most of them, we walked all the way to the front of the ride without stopping.
Amazing place to visit and takes pictures everywhere. Super magic and fabulous park in Orlando......

We have been coming to this park since our kids were teenagers and 11 years later we still come as a family along with our seven-year-old granddaughter. The most popular part of Universal is definitely the Harry Potter theme area. It gets busy fast so head there first if you are interested. I don’t have any interest in Harry Potter but it was still really cool to go into this area. We missed the entrance to this so pay attention to the map. When you enter, you are in a whole different world. You feel like you are actually in the books\movies. Make sure to try some butterbeer (we prefer frozen) and ride Harry Potter and the escape from Gringotts! If you’re a fan of The Simpsons, there are rides, restaurant, and a whole section dedicated to the show. The rip rocket is a fun roller coaster and you get to pick the music you want to listen to while on it. The Men in Black ride is another favorite and if you go in as a single rider instead of a group, you get on quicker and avoid the longer lines. If you are in a wheelchair, you can ride this. Universal studios has 3-D / 4-D attractions that I was able to go into with my wheelchair. They include the Despicable Me Minion Mayham, Shrek, and The Jimmy Fallon ride. There are other rides and shows that will help fill up your day also. We usually spend the shorter day at Universal and we will spend a longer day at Islands of adventure. There’s no way we could ever do both parks in a day with our whole family so we always get the 2 day 2 park pass. We always make sure to catch the Halloween horror make up show and The Animal Actors on location. Both are great for all ages and very entertaining. The animal show uses rescue animals and showcases their different talents! Some of them have even been in movies or TV shows. My husband is a big Blues Brothers fan and they have a cool little show with actors singing songs from the movie. The universal superstar parade is also worth checking out while characters from different movies and shows dance and sing. There are several different theme restaurants to check out. They are not cheap when it comes to their meals. However, they have a family meal deal and a refillable cup deal. The refillable cup deal is great and definitely saves money on drinks! You are allowed to bring in bottled water, sandwiches, bags of chips, etc. (full details on website). This is definitely a money saver.

We last visited about 5 years ago, so there have been many additions to both parks since our last visit. We love the new additions for Harry Potter. We enjoyed Diagon alley and Escape from Gringotts, the train ride connecting the 2 parks and our favorite was Hagrid's motorbike ride. We love that there are also food chains within the park so you don't have to eat the same old park fare. We had pretzels at Aunt Annies and a turkey leg at Thunder Falls. We enjoyed riding some old favorites, like Men in Black, The Mummy, Rip Rockit, and The Hulk. Be sure to get a fast pass by either staying at a resort hotel, or purchasing since it allows you to get on many more rides and avoid the long lines.

Universal studios is the place to go! Spent several days at Disney (unfortunately) and were very disappointed and felt cheated. Universal was wonderful! No ridiculous lines, lots of fun rides intermingled for all ages. Good restaurants with nice variety and fair prices. Can’t say a bad thing about. Employees were friendly, helpful and playful.

Universal receives A++++ in regards to their customer service. My son has a seizure disorder and the Park was amazing handling his needs. He received a card with return times for lines greater than 30 minutes. If line was less than 30 minutes he was able to get right on; and they gave us multiple return times at the same time so we could do an area of the park and move on to the next when done.  Hats off to you Universal for making my son feel like a King for two days. He finally felt like he was “special” and not “different” I wish I could say the same for Disney.... where we could only reserve one “fast pass” with the DAS at a time. We spent most of our day sitting around doing nothing.

Our son loved it. Our pockets hated it :) Yes, its like in the movies, yes you feel the magic. However, for me, an adult joyning my son and not interested to get into any of the carousels or other experiences, I felt extremly frustrated that I had to pay 170 USD just for being a pedestrian in this park. I think there should be lower price for the accompanying adult who is not interested in the experience as such. I spent anyway money on food, merchandise etc.

Our family LOVES Universal! Here are the favourites for us... Harry Potter World (all of the rides, the feel of the area, the Hogwarts Express between the two parks, and the dragon), Transformers, Shrek, Minions, Marvel everything, the Simpsons, and MIB.  The food options are great! The parades are fun for the entire family. Unlike Disney the characters properly interact with the kids and will stand still for a photo op where you don't have to buy a photo package.  Wait to purchase the Express Pass until the day of your visit. If the park isn't packed, then you may not need it. Here is the comparison of Express Pass vs Disney's Fast Pass. Because Disney allows you to select your Fast Pass uses up to 60 days in advance you may not really get the fast pass experience for a lot of rides. The day we went we could only use fast pass for 2 rides. Universal has Disney beat on this where all of the rides (except for the new Hagrid's Motorbike) are eligible for Express Pass. It is so much more value and simple to use than the Disney system which is prone to a disappointing experience.  At Universal there is just so much to do and it is fun for all ages!

My husband and I just returned from 5 fun-filled days at Universal Orlando. I've been on a ketogenic diet (low carb/high fat) for seizure control for more than 5 years. I was concerned when I looked at their online menus bc everything is high carb. I emailed Universal prior to going and asked about keto options and never got a reply so I packed my KetoVie just in case there was nothing I could eat. Turns out I didn't have to be concerned. Starbucks prepared my 2/3 coffee, 1/3 heavy whipping cream every morning. At the on-site restaurants (Leaky Cauldron, 3 Broomsticks) I learned that when you order the cashiers/waitstaff at Universal can not stray from the printed menu items but will gladly call for a head cook (who knows whats in the food) to come out and discuss your needs with you and have the food prepared just for you. I have been on keto so long that I follow rules and don't need explicit carb counts so if you are counting carbs it might be a problem. For example, at the 3 Broomsticks I ordered the American breakfast and they substituted bacon, sausage, and sauteed mushrooms for the potatoes and bread. They did the same for me at Citywalk's BigFire restaurant where I had delicious grilled brussel sprouts, grilled mixed veggies, and trout. My order included only the veggies I can eat - no picking out potatoes, carrots etc... BigFire had lots on their menu I could eat and the food was delightfully fresh and simple.

So we came here because we had a cheer competition to attend and decided we’d make the most of trip and stay at one of Universal’s premier resorts so we could get free express passes to skip the lines. We also purchased Dining passes since there is 5 of us, 3 children and 2 adults which my son son who is 10 is charged as an adult. That is $69.95 per person per day for the full dining plan. We purchased 2 days worth. I thought that would help me save money rather than paying the overpriced food at the park but I wish I just would have paid while at the park because we would have paid less. If you do the math on what I just said for the dining passes it comes up to $700 for 5 people in 2 days. When I added up all the money of what we actually ordered with our passes including some expensive meals at Margaritaville 2 nights in a row with some meals that cost over $20 a pop, it only came up to like $495. So really I feel like I’ve been robbed of $200. It’s all good, I know now. Thanks Universal for everything that you do to overcharge families. Everything else about the trip was great, but I don’t like the feel of not getting my money’s worth or feeling cheated which is what I do in this situation.

We enjoyed visiting this park, even during the Covid crisis. It was not crowded as capacity was limited. With three kids including a four year-old we were able to enjoy pretty much all there is to do and see. Wearing a mask and adhering to the health and safety protocols we felt pretty safe. The Hollywood roller coaster is an absolute must.

Be forewarned, if you are a person size, as I am, you will not be able to ride 50% of the rides. I can ride every ride at WDW without issue, the rides at Universal were made for people no taller the 5' 6" and under 250 lbs. If you are outside of those dimensions you are out of luck as far as rollercoasters, or strap in rides go. It's a shame their main competitor can accommodate individuals of all shapes and sizes, but Universal decides to cut out people of size. If you have a choice, go elsewhere.

Universal did a great job with keeping the parks clean! Here are the things they did: - Morning parking is every other space, so when we got out of our car, we are distanced from other cars. Eventually the spots are filled, as there are cars next to us when we return. - temp check upon entry - Continuous disinfecting of moving walkway railings. There are people at one end of each walkway, continuously wiping the railings - 6ft social distance on most places - using ID (instead of fingerprints) for the ticket identification - virtual lines for long lines, so even if you wait, most of the waiting is outdoor. The queue move swiftly indoor, limiting the time spent in a crowd indoor - 12 ft distance on indoor queue, often skipping a row, so you are always at least 6ft away from other parties - mandatory hand sanitizer prior to boarding every ride - roller coaster: roughly 3 rows apart between parties - theater like seating (shrek, bourne, etc): at least 3 seats apart between parties and every other row seating - compartment ride (hogwarts express, gringotts, simpson, spiderman, etc): one compartment per party. - Rides are sprayed after every rides. - Most store doors are open to minimize touchings - door knobs, surfaces, railings are wiped often - order food via app and we take the plates from the tray to minimize touching - everybody wears masks inside the park - some decor are removed to provide more space for people - reduced crowd, I am not sure if this is intentional. There might be a crowd entering the park, but once inside, the crowd dispersed throughout the park.  We had a great time there and felt safe. Thank you Universal! We especially love the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, the low crowd really enabled us to enjoy the details of Hogsmeade & Diagon Alley.  And Bourne Stuntacular is really awesome! They just opened last week and it is a must see!  I hope this helps with your decision whether to go during this time!
Our trip to universal Studios was very awesome the characters and the rides was great.seeing spiderman. dinosaur s and all different characters you can imagine.

My wife and I went to Islands of Adventure and found that social distancing was largely ignored. The rides seem to be a bit better, but people can't seem to read where the social distance line is and stop piling on top of you. A couple of the rides weren't even wiped down after people exited the ride. We thought the access to the parks were supposed to be limited at this time, but that did not appear to be the case. Universal should take a hint from Disney and keep people who are drinking and eating stationary. The wait times for rides were ridiculous. You really can't get on most without a long wait unless you spend the extra money for the express pass. The Hulk coaster had an 85 minute wait 2 hours after the park opened. Hagrid's ride was a 2 hour wait. We are Florida residents and probably won't go back for a while.
Overall, lots of fun, but make sure you get the two-park pass and take the Hogwarts Express between the two parks. This "ride" is a hoot@

The magic was gone with all of their restrictions. Certain attractions were closed almost no characters walking around and interacting with the kids. Better to wait until worth full price. It’s a scam I felt cheated out of my money.full park price is not worth it.Face painting is still full 15$ price for half the face when it should be whole face. Also the new policy of keeping masks on during your ENTIRE stay in the hot Florida heat was very very difficult. They do have rest areas where you can take your mask off, but that didn’t make the experience better. The entire time we were there we were being harassed by employees about the masks. You can be 10 ft away from someone or no one around at all, and there will be someone to harass you about pulling your mask up. It took away from what could have been a waaaay better experience. My husband was playing and talking but with our daughter and they told him to not lower his mask. He flipped out because he was enjoying the moment counting owls in the Harry Potter side of park with our 2 year old and the moment was ruined. Felt like we were in jail or school. Definitely won’t be coming back until restrictions are lifted.

There were many rides to go on and with the fast pass I was able to do many rides over the curse of the day. I loved going to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter as I felt it was a good representation of the movies/books and was very cool to see. The lines however can be long sometimes and the food is expensive. I feel as though it's worth it for the memories you make and the overall experiences you gain from this park. I think it is very worth it, to visit and travel here and you will not regret your decision.

I was a little nervous going back to Universal as they have begun to re-open their parks again, but I greatly appreciated all of the precautions they have taken on their behalf to allow everyone to feel safe. Before we are allowed to reach the main area that checks our bags, everyone's temperature is taken and if it reaches a certain temperature, they will not allow the members to enter the park. What was great was the way that at each ride, there are painted markings on the ground that express where each person must stand to be 6 feet apart. I thought this system worked wonderfully without anything needed to be said. Everyone followed these guidelines the 4 days I was on vacation. What is also great is the way that the staff always has hand sanitizer on them and squirts a fair amount in everyone's hands right before entering the ride. Masks are required as well and everyone was doing their part. Wonderful experience overall and I felt super safe the whole trip with everyone doing their part to take the precautions that include the guests and staff!

Going to Disney in Orlando is a confusing and problematic affair. Above that the parks have been neglected for decades. But there is a new king in town and it is Universal Studios Florida. Both Universal Studios, the movie park and Islands of Adventure are worth a visit. Customer service does remind you to the old days when WDW was amazing. The team members are a delight and a spontaneous exploration of the stunning attractions and food offerings is just wonderful. Both parks offer Harry Potter themed lands and yes they are the new standard in theme park experiences with stunning decor and world class attraction and shows but the resort has so much more to offer and you would do yourself a disservice not to visit the many wonderful attractions these resorts have to offer. My favorites In Universal Studios: Harry Potter Escape from Gringotts, The Hogwarts Express (you need a 2 day or hopper pass for this one, take the 2 day pass and thank me later) The Jason Bourn stuntspectular, The Mummy, Man in Black, Transformers and E.T.. And please don't miss the Horror and Make-up show and The Blues Brothers. My favorites In Islands of Adventure: The Hulk, Spiderman, Popeye, Kong, Jurassic Park River Adventure, Hogwarts, Hagrids Motorbike Adventure and the high in the sky Seuss trolley train ride (especially at night when the Christmas decorations are up).

We got here since 8.20am after long walk and lines to get in we found the theme parks are at capacity since 9am. This is the 2nd day happened to us. We bought 2days tickets but we couldn't use any and we have to leave and go home. Poor customer service! They only let people in their resorts in first. We want our money back!!
Excellent it was well worth the money. Be careful though. We accidentally entered Adventure Island and meant to enter Universal Studios.

The workers were rude and spent the entire day yelling at the few people whose masks fell below their noses instead of actually doing their jobs. I never saw any of them cleaning. Wait times for food were much longer than ever in the past. The park didn’t seem any less crowded than usual. Their covid measures seemed to only entail lazily yelling at guests all day. Most people really had masks on appropriately and the policing was unnecessary. The rides were also ruined with them constantly calling out over the actual sound provided for the ride to remind people about masks. They even reminded guests who had masks on appropriately. It was crazy. They need to remember that some guests may require a break with all the walking to catch their breath, especially older guests. How did they know whether or not some of the people they were yelling at had medical conditions. I was shocked at the way people around me were treated.

Wait in long lines everywhere. Ok so there is a lot of hurdles at the parks and it takes you more than 1 hour to just get in the door. They have added a metal detector and they take temperatures as well. (Maybe use temperature screening camera's to speed things up?) In addition, their software at the park to allow people to enter the park is less than satisfactory. You must give them your fingerprint, and it takes 30 seconds per person to just scan a ticket and get in the doors. (another long and slow moving line) To pick up tickets at Will Call 50% of machines did not work (another line).  Notes for their mgt...fix the terrible IT infrastructure, and you don't need my fingerprint!

My husband and I visited Universal a couple years ago and had a fantastic time. This trip didn’t meet those expectations. The rides IF/WHEN you got to them met our expectations. Several were closed for most of the day. Temps hit 95 all days we were there. You were forced to wear a mask all the time except when you were “actively eating or drinking in a stationary spot.” The Express Passes ruined our visit. I get it the Express People paid extra, but there needs to be limits to give the Gen Pop a fair chance at the rides. A 25 min wait at the train turned into a 70 min wait in the hot dungeon with our faces covered. People were dropping from the heat.  Places to eat and drink experiences long, slow, never-ending lines of people waiting in the sun. Since our last visit, Universal has added two huge hotels and two new, modern rollercoasters, but no new places to get food and drink. The park has limited infrastructure and the visitors needs need to be addressed too.  We stayed at Endless Summer hotel which was very nice, but the lobby stayed warm due to all the people. (It was only 1/2 full too.) Pier 8 offered some reasonably priced food items. Some items we wish we could have used, but we had no microwave in our room. :.( Staff members were friendly and courteous. We also had to buy coffee in the park since we don’t drink Starbucks and we also didn’t have a coffee maker in our room.  We chose this time because school was still in session. Ha! Can you say “virtual learning!” We cut our vacation short by a day. Between the heat, masks, and crowds, we’d had enough.
Here you can run with the Terminator, chase dinosaurs in Jurassic Park, fly with E.T. or kill big white sharks with enourmous Jaws!

This is the second time i have visited here with my partner and teenage daughter. Last year i learnt that to enjoy the park it is better to buy a fast pass. Although they are 4500 yen extra each we found it was well worth it. It was so hot and busy and queues for rides were around 1 hour each. There are 2 kinds of fast passes on for 4 rides (not sure how much this one is) and one for 7 rides. With the pass you can walk straight onto the ride. The first time without the passes we didnt get to go on much whereas with the pass we went on everything. I would also recommend taking your own drinks and food as it is quite expensive. There is a good selection of rides suitable for all and parades for those that like them. A great day out. I would also say get there for when it opens as its not so busy.

It is smaller than Tokyo Disneyland, but much more action-packed attractions for those who love it.  I personally really enjoy taking pictures with the characters, although sometimes you have to queue especially for Woody Woodpecker. I tried to search for Pink Panther but failed. Looking for Snoopy but he was busy taking pricey shots with the kids, so no free photos. I should have searched for information first as to where and when the characters would come out and be available to take photos with. The characters won't come out around the time of the parades (obviously they will be busy preparing for the parades).  I arrived in the morning, just right after the opening hour of the park. Unlike Tokyo Disney Resort, unexpectedly there were not many people in the morning, so we can get into half of the attractions without any queues. It got very crowded after lunch time though. It was our first visit, so we want to try all of the attractions. If it'll be your first visit and you want to try a lot of attractions, do come in the morning and visit the attractions that are located far from the gates first because everyone would be queuing for those nearby the gates.  We stayed there the whole day and we weren't bored. I definitely want to visit it again next time!

Found overall experience to be great. Some of the attractions were a little scary and traumatic for my 7 yr old. Wish there was translation head sets for the movies as we missed the gist of some things.

Would recommend this place a must to visit for those who are looking for fun and enjoyable theme park! The rides in there although are all in Japanese, but I really enjoyed myself there! I was so amazed by the cleaniness there that you can literally sit anywhere on the floor! I would highly recommend to get the express tickets which is a bit more expensive but still affordable to "cut" the long queue for the rides! By the time of the noon, I have already finished all the rides and was enjoying myself and taking my time to take photos in there! The time I went there, the weather is really nice and the place was unforgettable.

Universal Studios Japan in Osaka is a great day out. I went with my 11 year old son in June 2011 and we had a blast.  The secret to success is 1) buy entry tickets before you go, for instance at a JR Ticket Office and 2) invest in the Express Pass Booklet 7.  The Express Pass 7 can purchased inside the park at the gift store when you walk in. It can be a bit steep (our were about $50 aus each) but you avoid long queues on most of the major rides. We used it on a Saturday and did most of the rides we wanted to by early afternoon.  In terms of the rides, the new ride that has replaced ET, Space Fantasy, is pretty good. It is an indoor roller coaster not unlike Space Mountain but with spinning pods! The coaster, Hollywood Dream, is worthwhile and Spiderman is great. Backdraft is pretty dull especially if you don't understand spoken Japanese well and I suspect it will be decommissioned soon. Back to the Future and Jaws are not as cutting edge as they once were but still fun.

It is our first time to visit universal Studio Japan. We haven"t visit the one in Singapore and in US. In spite that we just stayed there for 6 hours and find it expensive, we enjoyed our stay there. If you are in Osaka, don't miss this place whether you are in your mid 20 to 60s. It's the experience that makes it unique. You can travel in space and in fantasy. You will be amazed and mesmerize with their ride. Do not mind if their rides is old and way back to the 80's. Most of the shops and restaurant is closed maybe because it is weekday and is cold. Still we have long lines. The theme park closes at 5pm. Imagine that. It was maybe a little rip-off but still we had a blast. Their newest ride is The Space Fantasy. And wow, must a exclaim.It was very fast and very entertaining, you can feel that you are in outer space. You must try this ride. it is a very different experience not like a Space Shuttle or the scary roller coaster. It is unique.

I found this version of Universal Studies to be much better than the one in Hollywood that I have visited numerous times over the last few decades. As a person not as young and flexible as I used to be, the flat layout of Universal Studios in Osaka, Japan make for a much less physically-taxing adventure. Additionally, having the Japanese culture demonstrated throughout the park with the food, drinks, and themes made for a great day.

My fiancee and me came here just last week, Sept. 9th 2011, and we could spend the perfect first day of visiting Osaka here. We were first looking into getting a ticket from online, but couldn't find any, or any with discount. So eventually we decided to just buy the ticket in Osaka when we arrive. We bought the ticket at the tourist information desk at the arrival floor at the Kansai International airport in Osaka. We paid 6200 for two adult tickets.  So we went there the next day and we could almost just walk through the gate with our tickets we bought in advance the day before, so that was a smart move. Definitely would recommend this one! When we got in we went straight through to the Guest Center desk to get the Express Pass for the park. Which basically makes you pass the normal line of people waiting for select attractions and puts you in front of all those still waiting. A little note: it's only for the main attractions listed in the booklet, and you have a choice of a ticket for 4 or 7 attractions. It cost about 4200 JPY per pass but it's definitely worth the price.  Make sure you go to the following attractions in the following order of excitement level: 1. Spiderman, The Ride 2. Jurassic Park, The Ride 3. Jaws 4. Universal Monsters Live Rock & Roll Show 5. Hollywood Dream - The Ride 6. Waterworld show (make sure you bring a raincoat if you wanna be on row 1-15) 7. Space Fantasy - The Ride  Also if you wanna go out and have a bit outside the park make sure you tell the people at the gate you wanna go out for some food and they will give you a stamp with which you can enter the park again. They might tell you it's not possible to enter the park again once one has exited the park, but if you mention you just wanna go out for a quick bite at Mos Burger or MacDonald's then they will give you the stamp.  We had a great day there and surely something we would go back for if we would come back to Osaka for another travel. Best tip I can give to others who are going there: Get the Express Pass in the park to avoid waiting endlessly in lines!

We went here at the begining of October 2011. We should have purchased tickets beforehand as we had to queue for over an hour to buy the tickets in the blistering sun before we even got to the separate entrance queue.  This was on a weekday and there were still ALOT of people including heaps of school aged children when it wasnt a holiday.  The rides were good even the older ones, but most had a 90 min queue to get on.  After waiting over an hour to buy tickets, we went for an express pass which was rather expensive, but without it, i think we may have only got on 2-3 rides the whole day.  With the express pass for 4 rides, we only managed to get around 6 rides. When we used the pass sometimes we didn't have to wait at all, and other times we still had to wait 20 mins. Without the pass the average queing time was around 70-90 mins per ride....we thought this was ridiculous as even forking out extra for the express pass for SOME rides (doesnt include all of them) we still didnt have the time to go on everything we wanted.  I really did enjoy the rides here,,,,,but you get the drift, the day was spent standing in queues with people sneezing on the back of your neck and teenagers clearly skipping the queue but no-one stopping them. I found this very frustrating.  If you want to go my tip is : buy tickets beforehand to save time at the entrance. Buy the Expresspass booklet, its worth the extra money, otherwise there isnt enough time in the day to get on all the rides. Be prepared to spend an arm and a leg on lunchtime food. If your not used to crowds and queues you will hate this place!!  PS even though I dont understand much Japanese, i still understood and enjoyed most rides when I got on them!

My husband and I timed our travel plans to that we could head to USJ on a Tuesday, on recommendations from our friends because Tuesdays are non-peak and hence, you would get to take the rides faster.  But boy, were our friends wrong. I believe February is the time when Japanese students go out for field trips/school trips - because even on a Tuesday, USJ was packed to the brim with students running around!  And we love the Japanese and their wonderful manners, but nothing beats having to be in 2-hour queues, stuck between hormonal and fidgety teens and tweens. So, a word of advice, do your background check on the good dates to head to USJ and you could save yourself hours of waiting time.  Quick trick to covering the USJ well - head for the furthest start attraction ride on either the left or right of the park first and work your way back to the front of the park. People tend to veer to the start of the park of the extreme end of the park first. So heading to the left or right would be the best.  Also, if you have no qualms about splitting up while riding the rides, you should tell the ushers at the queue that you would like to ride as a single rider - you'll get to queue with your friends and your buddies, but just not ride together as they will use these single riders to fill in odd spaces on the rides. With this trick, what took other 3 hours, only took me 45 minutes to ride, twice.  But all in all, the USJ is a very old theme park and so are the rides. Coupled with long, arduous queues, and that makes for a hardly memorable trip to the USJ.

Visited Universal Studios Osaka in December 2011. We didn't find Universal as wonderous or as big as Disneysea in Tokyo. The selection of rides was a bit more limited and it felt as if the park is aimed at the local market rather than an international one. There was lots of opportunity to buy souveniers from the myriad of shops about the place and the Waterworld show was well worth watching (but be careful where you sit as you are bound to get wet and the posts do get in the way of your view if you sit in the wrong spot - however an attendent will come around and tell you if you should move to a better viewing location). We did spend a whole day wandering around and stayed for the Christmas light show in the evening. We stayed at Universal Port which had a reasonable view over the park and was a short walk away.
We used the Fast Pass but compared to Disneyland, the rides here are not as thrilling nor do they have many rides. The parade was as good but the night fireworks was a complete letdown,,,,,,

I went last year with my family and we spent half a day there. The rides and shows were quite fun and quite interesting. I recommend that you bring a camera and good walking shoes because the area is nice and quite big. There aren't many shows and rides but they were quite enjoyable. The food there was also really good but can be a little pricey, as are the drinks and snacks on the stalls. If you go there I really recommend the cinnamon or chocolate bread sticks because they taste amazing and aren't too sweet.
Phenomenal rides and fancy technology to dazzle you out of your mind!

Having gone to both Universal in Hollywood and in Orlando, it was fun to see the differences and similarities at the Osaka Universal Studios. The biggest difference (besides the obvious speaking in Japanese) was that although it was a US holiday weekend, since we are in Japan, there were no crowds!!!!
