What a wonderful experience getting in line for even the most popluar rides - like the Hollywood Dream roller coaster and the Space Fantasy ride (think Space Mountain but in spinning Haunted Mansion-like buggies).  It was great to take my kids on Back to the Future since in Hollywood, it has been replaced by the Simpsons. No offense to Simpson fans but I prefer the Back to the Future story, even when I couldn't understand it since it was all dubbed in Japanese.  Side note - the Hard Rock at CityWalk is a must do - the same overall character but with the wonderful Japanese service experience.  From any of the 3 Osaka airports, travel was relatively simple by airport bus and by train. We took the train in and the bus out. Worked like a charm! Both are conveniently located right outside Universal Studios.
Exceed most of our expectations. Spiderman ride is the best. The kids love it!

Yes, we arrived exactly 9:00am when the gate is open but we end up queueing for ticket for 1 hours. Even all 20++ ticket counter is open, it still drag 1 hours to serve 20++ people in front of me before i can reach in front of the ticket counter. We go there on weekday but did not expect so many people. Average 40min to 1hour queue for each atrraction. So, end up we miss some attraction like terminator, hollywood dream and animation character. Anywhere we still enjoy the whole day until 9pm. No english speaking, all japanese but we still able to have fun.

If you're going to Osaka make sure you allocate a day to this fun-filled theme park! I went with a group of friends, all twenty-somethings, and it was one of our most memorable visits in Japan. Highlights were the rollercoaster, and the 3D spiderman-themed ride (like the Batman ride at Warner Bros. Studio on the Gold Coast, QLD Australia but about 10000 times better!). Next time I'm in Osaka, I will definitely go back to Universal Studios.

Friends generally grade "Spiderman" best. Yes, if you only opt for degree of excitement. For us, "Space Fantasy" is full of surprises and the ride is more than fun and beauty. "Jurassic Park" ride and parade suspended because of bad weather. "Terminator" average; "Animation Celebration" wonderfully designed and impressive; both suitable for those not ready for heart-attacking rides. "Back to the future" also enjoyable and thrilling. Convenient stores and tons of shops and restaurant/ food stores outside USJ. We took our dinner outside. Average meal (drinks not incl.) 1420 yens inside theme park.
Like the dancing and singing performance. Dislike the food....

This theme park is rather family oriented and very suitable for children. It is also very well manage, clean and updated. We went on Friday, rather crowed and surprisingly no long Q. Averagely it took about 15 min for each ride. We enjoy the Wonderland (Snoopy + Hello Kitty), Jurassic Park ride, Hollywood Dream ride, Shrek's Adventure, Terminator 2, Backdraft, Spider-man, Back to the future ride and Jaw's ride. There is lots of food outlets all over the park and the ground crew is helpful. Communication might be an issue and all the video shown in the park is in Japanese.

We arrived at 8:30am which I think is the best time to go. Lines already busy but to buy tickets fairly easy. Park opens at 9:00am and the process is very orderly. Then the Japanese started running, for the shows I think. But my husband and myself take it slow and browse through shops for some souvenirs, this place is empty. We then head to the jaws attraction on the other side of the park no one here and we take our first lot of pictures at Amity town, the big replica shark hangs and it's fun just to stick your head in and pose for the photo. We then get on the first ride in the jaws bay. Yes it's all in Japanese but we are in Japan and they do talk a little English to get us directed to the right ques. Yes once boarded on the boat the boat captain, talks in Japanese, but even if you do not understand, you don't have to be Einstein to work out what's happening. It's a fun ride and we all know the film of jaws and the story line, so it's not an issue. After this we walk to Jurassic Park, this is lovely and a replica of the movie, we line up for this about 15minutes, we see lots of people with towels and plastic rain coats, so we figure out you must get wet at some point, thankfully we have rain jackets in our backpacks. It's also a hot day so we don't stress too much. This was fun and amusing, with the life like dinosaurs throughout the ride, at the end of the journey sure enough a roller coaster at the end gets us all wet. We then move onto Back to the Future, this takes about 25mins, all in Japanese, but we go with the flow, boarded onto replicas of the delorian we take this fantastic 3D journey. This was truly amazing this was the best so far. Next Terminator, close to the previous ride. This perhaps was the most interesting ride/attraction, we are herded into a room given 3D glasses. Some over the top Japanese actress went on for about 20minutes, we are all still standing, which was a little strange. At last the theatre doors open and we take our seats, for this show. It ended up being good with a Japanese Arnold which was very amusing. We had some lunch and headed on out. By this time it was very busy for a Monday, people everywhere. Do recommend a trip here though

Agreed with the other reviews that all the commentaries are in Japanese only. Thus whilst everyone is laughing, you kind of just look around and wonder when the commentaries will end so that you can start the ride/ show. JAWS and The Mummy rides were closed during our trip. Bit of a bummer as my kid was looking forward to the ride. Was rather frustrated with their height restrictions. I can understand for the more adventurous rides such as Jurassic Park but the Snoopy Ride??? A kid have to be at least 92cm to ride. Over at Disney, no such restrictions. Thus my 2yo pretty much had nothing to ride on. Everything is more expensive as compared to Tokyo Disneyland and DisneySea with way shorter hours. Similar items but will cost an extra JPY300-500 more per item. Disney closed at 10p but Universal Studio at 6p. Thus not much time to ride every single ride, given the long waiting lines. In addition, single riders were not always available, even though the normal waiting time can be 20-30min. Do not allow re-entry during the time we visited thus "forces" you to dine in the Park. We had fun as we went all the way there and tried our best not to let the down side affect our trip. But will unlikely return. The highlight for us was the Spiderman ride :)
You must watch the parade in the night then leave!! It's amazing!

Caveat emptor: writer had been to the ones in Hollywood (twice) and Singapore.  Seriously speaking, this theme park seemed to cater only to locals (Japanese). Although there are Guide Maps and signs in English, most of the park's staff have minimal or zero command of English. (I cannot compare this to Tokyo Disneyland, as I had forgotten whether the crew there speaks English.)  We went as a family (husband, wife, teenager and pre-teen), and attended most of the shows and rides. The shows we went to were Shrek 4D, Terminator, Spider Man, Jaws, and Back to the Future. ALL of the shows were in Japanese, with NO sub-titles whatsoever. My spouse fell asleep while STANDING during the Terminator pre-show, when the commentator was trying to be funny and perk up the audience, asking if they were from Osaka or Kansai, whether there were any school kids and if they would be scared (I understand a bit of Japanese). Actually, it was kinda neat watching Arnie, Sarah Connor and John Connor yapping in Japanese. The Terminator 3D show itself was enticing enough, so that not understanding the language was OK.  For Shrek, fortunately my kids had attended the show before (in Singapore), so they sort of remember the story, and went in the show for the air-con and the fun. For the other shows, we just guessed the story. Spider Man 3D was the latest ride/show, and we queued up for about an hour. Despite not understanding the comments, the ride and show was fun and exciting, well worth the wait, but I felt a bit dizzy and nauseous (motion sickness) afterwards, ditto for Back to the Future. Jaws was different from what I've experienced in the USA. One could get wet, but it was OK, because it was summer. And of course, commentator was in Japanese, and we didn't know we can't take photos. He at once could speak English !  We wanted to play Jurassic Park, but it was pouring, and the ride was closed. We played Hollywood Dream as a family -- it was scary for me and my younger child, but the teenager loved it, and wanted to play again, but queued in the wrong lane (express) and didn't know it (didn't understand what the staff was saying!) and didn't get to play it. The kids loved Space Fantasy and played it twice, both times queuing about 45 mins.  We had lunch at one of the many cafes, and had pizza and spaghetti (at the typically exorbitant theme park prices). Despite the menu being bilingual (Japanese & English), my spouse had to mime and point to what we wanted. And after ordering, had to queue in another line, and waited for at least 15 mins for the food, definitely not typical "fast" food. BONUS NOTE -- bags are not checked these days (too many people queuing up to enter the park), so you can bring your own drinks and food inside if you want.  We wanted to watch the parade (at 8 pm), and so we began to find a nice covered spot at around 6:30 pm. If we had understood Japanese, we would have left early, because there were announcements every now and then. Seemed that the parade was cancelled (owing to rain?). When we tried to ask the staff (in English), one of them ran away !!! But it didn't matter, as the kids wanted to play another ride. Then at 8 pm, some of the dressed-up crew came out and danced, and kids were invited (in Japanese) to take photos with them. This was when mayhem started -- the Japanese moms simply shoved their way forward and urged their kids to stand with the cast, while my younger kid was pushed further and further back in the crowd. Talk about Japanese courtesy !!! This is the real face of the Japanese, when it comes to the benefit of their children, they will do everything to grab it, no matter how rude they become !
A fun place for adults and kids, great rides and things to do and see. Loads of entertainment

Day Visited: Sunday 5th August (Which is considered peak) Arrived: Around 9:30am Tickets: Bought 2 adult and 2 x express booklet7  Between about 10am and 4pm we were able to get on everything once and some things twice (the 2 coasters and Jurassic Park) all queues were less than 30 minutes long.  After 4pm the queues went up to around the 40-65 minute mark mainly: Hollywood Dream (65 mins) Space Fantasy (60 mins) The other main attractions around 40 minutes. We never saw Jurassic Park's queue go above 25 minutes all day.  We queued for anything which said 30 minutes (as in reality it takes about 15 minutes, the staff were fantastically efficient). Once the 60 minute mark came up we pulled out the fast pass booklet and started using these.  Another point is...we didn't find the waiting times to always be accurate and in most cases slightly shorter:  Hollywood Dream - Wait time 50 mins - Actual 25 mins Space Fantasy - Was approximately right Jurassic Park - Always shorter than advertised  If we were to go again I think we would only buy booklet4 as it covers the main rides for adults.  The following attractions were fairly crap as it was purely in Japanese: Shrek 3D/Backdraft/Terminator  The food is very expensive (you can get a stamp at the exit and eat from the boardwalk eg: Planet Hollywood), we did this around 4pm as its when the park hit peak.  Would highly recommend sticking around for the starlight parade as it is very impressive.

We've been to universal in singapore, la , and orlando. While this park is bigger than singapore, it's really sparse compares to the states' universal. We went in at 9 , and by 12 pm we were bored 0_0 ....It was super hot and the queues was long ( average 50 mins in line ... even for the universal wonderland part). Toddler was less than 100cm , so there're just a few rides he could ride on ..( the boring ones). I was looking forward to the hello kitty and the sesame street play areas , but turned out they are just so-so ( the snoopy area is better). If you're pregnant and you're not bringing any kids with you to enjoy the park, I say dont bother ,,, because they wont let you in even for the shrek 4d +_+ hahaha... I had better experiences with disneyland/ disney sea tokyo. On a lighter side, they offer cute merchandises, but boohoo ... please bring your own plastic/reusable bags , because they only provide paper bags, you have to pay for plastic bags. Bring your strollers, the park is stroller friendly.

I've already went to LA, Orlando, Singapore Universal Studios before and Osaka Universal Studios is the best in my own opinion. The size of the theme park is not large enough, smaller than LA but larger than singapore, which will not drain all your energy after a whole day of staying in the park. For adults, beer is sold anywhere (which I like) and you may drink it anywhere you want. Many attractions are different from other universal Studios. The only down side is that many shows uses only Japanese language.

My sister and I decided to be a kid for a day. Unlike the other Universal Studios which I've been, this one is by far the best of them all. I particularly love the music they were playing the whole day... it made me wish for a Universal Studios, Japan soundtrack. ^_^
Got all the rides... Old and new... Especially Jaws, Jurassic park. Luckily not full crowds during my visit... Manage to ride all...

We were rushing and had forgotten to bring our coupons from Osaka unlimited pass... otherwise we could hv purchased the tickets at a discounted rate :-/ It was really a great enjoyable and fun experience. I personally loved the Jurassic Park ride and back to the future ride. Don't forget to watch Shrek's 4-D Adventure too. Ideal for a whole day visit so that you can enjoy as much as possible from your visit.

...and I've been living in Tokyo for several years.  After reading several comments here that lines were shorter than Tokyo Disney Land even on the weekend or during the summer, we were really excited about visiting the park on a Monday.  However as soon as we go there at 10 am we felt something was wrong. Long lines snaked away from the ticket booths and we had to wait over 30 minutes just to buy our tickets and enter the park!  After entering, we walked around the park for an hour looking for a ride that didn't have a 60+ minutes waiting line and finally gave up and went to see some shows (30 minutes wait each). What was really surprising was that there were so many children of all ages - on a school day!  Lines for the popular rides slowly rose to 100 minutes in the afternoon. We ended up getting an express pass for the Spiderman ride - you can get it for 650 yen when ordering a lunch set at the Discovery restaurant in the Jurassic Park area.  I figured that the crowds would drop in the evening (the park was open till 9pm) since all these kids surely had to go to school the next day. I couldn't have been more wrong. It turned out that as part of their Halloween special (runs from Sept 15 to end of October) the park had some temporary attractions open in the evening (for example Jason's Blood Diner, a sort of horror house) while some other attractions were converted into scarier versions (for example Jaws became the Ghostboat).  Between 5 and 6pm we just walked round the park since all the lines were insanely long (Space Fantasy was 150 min). After 6pm, the zombies came out in various areas of the park. That was probably the highlight of the day (think lots of screaming, running schoolgirls). In the end we gave up at 7h30 and went back to our hotel. I think it was the 200 minute waiting line for Jason's Diner that finally did it for us (we didn't wait).  I guess the moral of this story is - avoid USJ late September and October even on a weekday (unless the park closes early). Even if you get the express pass, there are long lines for restaurants and food stalls and it's hard to walk around.  As for the attractions, Terminator was the best show (impressive effects and not too much Japanese). For Backdraft you should probably get into the first row to get a kick out the flames (that's the line most on the right). The same for Waterworld - sit in the splash seats (the blue ones), otherwise not that great (nice action but too much talking). Unfortunately I didn't really enjoy any of the 3 rides we tried. Jurassic park was mostly tame (apart from the very big drop at the end). Spider man was just too intense. Back to the Future made me feel nauseous (other people around me were saying the same thing after the ride).  All in all somewhat of a disappointment because of the massive crowds tempered by the fact that we got to enjoy the special Halloween atmosphere.
Have a good range of attraction, lot of spots for taking great pictures, better than the one in singapore.. Price : ¥6400.

The new rides are of course very very good and entertaining but the one like Back to The Future and Spiderman are in desperate need of upgrading, HD is a must in Japan. While all the TV I've watch in the hotel already provide the best view ever (even cooking lesson), how come I have to pay more than 6000 yen to see the oldies.  We went to the Sanrio land and the kids are loving it, the car ride is a must, not just driving in a square box, real street here. And the tidbits, souvenirs, well, not as great as Tokyo Disneyland but still so cute and lovable. Those hooded towels seems to be the must have items here. From Hello Kitty to Cookie Monster, it's all here.  The night, light parade, is a bit disappointment, I meant disney characters are here, are they lost or something?  Final word: Try all the rides you can except the Spiderman and Back to the future, must ride: Hollywood roller coaster, insanely addictive. Tips: Be a single rider and skip all the queues!

If you've been to other theme parks in America, this is no different, but everything is in Japanese, even the jokes, so don't expect that you'll get it. Remember that not many Japanese speak English, including the theme park

We went on a Friday afternoon without getting an express pass. We got our tickets from JR ticket office to avoid queueing for tickets at USJ. Still, it was very crowded with many student groups. There were queues for everything, everywhere...from buying tickets, getting into the park, taking rides, buying food and even toilets.  Perhaps it's the Halloween Horror Nights this month because we don't remember it being so crowded when we were here in the past. That said, it looks like the fun will start when it gets dark as many youngsters came dressed in Halloween costumes and we see some sections transformed to Raccoon City (Resident Evil). Too bad we couldn't stay as we had a night flight to catch.  In the end we only managed 3 rides/shows and our feet hurt from standing long in the queues. We queue an average of 50minutes for each ride but by the time we left about 6pm it is showing more than 2 hours wait.  Overall ok but typical of a popular theme park, avoid weekends and holidays if you can help it. You need to get there early if you intend to cover more rides/shows. And start with the rides you don't want to miss, in case you run out of energy to queue at the end of the day. Be prepared to stand...for long period.

the japanese spare no expense when they prepare for halloween, it makes going to the theme park extra fun since you get to see not just the mascots but the other visitors in sometimes even prettier costumes. the spiderman ride is ofcourse the must try, the terminator and the jaws ride are also great.

It is bigger the the Singapore one. There are a lots of games and shows to have fun. I cant finish to explore the whole Universal Studio is one day. The ticket price is 6400yen for adult. When i visit there is halloween month. So there is some special and scary event held on that night. Is fun and exciting!! There is also parade at the noon. Each and every single game or show is awesome and adventurous.

I've been here twice and I loved both times! Sometimes the lines can be long, especially on weekends and holidays, so try to go during the off season or on weekdays. There are tons of thrilling rides to try as well as a few more laid back options for kids and those less adventurous. Can't wait until my next trip!
It was an awesome experience to be at USJ. Exciting games and friendly staff but most of the games are in japanese so for foreigners, u better have japanese speaker as a companion with u.

there are more restaurants than attractions and the attractions are super crowded and lunch time is crazy, there are literally blocks of lines, i end up eating in hard rock, outside of the park and it was the best choice. but i ate at 4 pm

Got two kids 7 and 5 years old. Enjoyed the Kids section of the park with the Hello Kitty and Charlie Brown/Snoopy sections. Some rides are more suitable for kids below 3 years old. Larger park than the Singapore version but smaller than the ones in the US. Some rides are really showing their age compared to the new rides in Universal Studios Singapore. But overall the experience was very enjoyable as the staff were extremely hyper and friendly despite us only knowing simple japanese phrases and mostly not knowing what the heck they were staying. Pity about the overpriced food and drinks and you can't leave and re-enter the park to eat the more reasonable priced food at the food outlets outside the park. My advice, pack some food and drinks before entering the park.
funny theme park.There are a lot of 3D ride. At night have fantastic parade. Will back there again :-)

Not to be missed ride: Space Fantasy, Hollywood Dream  Service staff were really friendly and helpful! =)  Some rides like "back to the future" desperately need a revamp.  Use the Single rider option as much as possible. Finished almost all the rides in the park within 3-4 hours thanks to the single rider option.
i could'n found a dirty spot area in such big theme park, don't forget try "spiderman" and "jurrasic park", it's so much fun. Hard rock cafe osaka just ouside the theme park area.
Besides USJ, there are many shops and eateries that for you to choose from cheapest to the most expensive. You can easily to spent the whole day there because USJ's operation hour from 10am-5pm.

In the summer of 2012, Universal Studios Japan had a special summer event to tribute the popular Manga/Anime, ONE PIECE. Universal Studios was transformed to be themed toward One Piece for the summer. In honor of the event (and cause it's more fun), many of the guests dressed up as characters from One Piece. For full pics/video of the event, visit the Danger Avoider Blog.

We didn't know whether it was the holiday season because we still saw some kids in school uniforms, but it was seriously packed! We arrived at 9am, but already the lines were extremely long and people have started entering the park. So at the last minute we decided to get the 4 rides express pass. It was pretty pricey (this would made Universal Studios Japan the most expensive US to visit!) but as soon as we entered and saw the crowd, we were totally glad we did! And those passes worked very well too. We were afraid that if a lot of people bought those passes, then it wouldn't be express anymore, would it? But no, we didn't have to wait, which was excellent! Trust me when I say it is totally worth it, we waited for 3hours for a ride in DisneySea the next day, which totally ruined our trip.  Our favorite rides were Hollywood Dream and another one with 'Space' in the name I forgot what it was called but it had us in awe. We have been to US Singapore and Hollywood and thought these 2 were pretty refreshing. The others were just like what they had in the other US's. We also quite enjoyed the Hello Kitty, Sesame Street and Snoopy areas as we never saw those in other US's.  Food in USJ would be more expensive than those in Disney, but quality is still pretty good. I wouldn't mind going again if not for the price... (including the express passes of course).

We visited on a Monday in October yet the queues were still very long - 45 minutes for the Snoopy ride and just over 3 hours for the Spiderman ride. The grounds were interesting and well kept but the highlight of the day was Carnival Parade - very spectacular.

it's a disappointment, this universal studio seems like sold too many ticket in one day, and for every attraction we waited average of 1 hour plus. It should have control the visitor count so that everyone get to enjoy. This Universal studio was like a weird combination of universal studio and disneyland, too much pinks and candy color. Another thing is the 4D studio should be clearly mention that what is the next show, perhaps a lot of people do not mind whether after one hour waiting you get Shrek or Sesames streets, but we do. When after long waiting time we get into another waiting hall, the screen is previewing Sesames Street, we were like "OMG should we go out or continue???" as we were queue for Shrek 4D not Sesames street 4D. At the end, we wasted another hours to queue for Shrek 4D after the schedule board put on the notice saying no more Sesames street 4D for that day. As summary, USJ do not give us an universal studio experience, as compared to Universal Studio LA. It's too pink, too sweet, too creamy, but not so Hollywood. By the way the starlight parade is a good conclusion for the day.

The rides are really fun, BUT we were there during a school holiday and the waits for most rides were about 2 hours long. I would only go if it's not a school holiday. Also the place is very small, which may be a contributing factor to why the lines were so long.  There is a lot of staff walking around, so you can get help any time you need, and the restaurants, while expensive, are delicious. We had fun at USJ, but would never go again during vacation time, it was crazy.

I had previously been to the Universal Studios in Singapore, and I had a lovely time there (even though the Jurassic Park ride was closed, which was my most anticipated ride). US Japan was bigger and better!! The universal studios walk from train station to gate is exciting enough! There was no waiting to buy a ticket. We got there just after the park opened. There is one of two rides that you arent allowed ANY bags etc and must rent the locker, dont be put off, that is just for a couple of the rides, and if u hve a friend/s who dont want to ride, they can hold your things and browse elsewhere while you ride. The decor is exciting, it has a lovely undercover over the main street area, good to keep the sun off and also rain! Rides were all excellent, I was so happy to go on the Jaws ride, as I heard it has now closed down at all the other parks. Jurassic park ride was good, Spiderman ride was really fun, a kind of 3D simulator, like Transformers ride at US Singapore. The terminator show was interesting, if a little dated, as was the Back to the Future simulator ride. EVERYTHING is in Japanese, so if u are a foreigner like me, you wont understand exactly what is happening, but they are all pretty animated so you can guess. There was plenty of street theatre, parades and a Hello Kitty music bus that went around. The food was typically overpriced, but had some exciting choices like Sesame street characters food, Snoopy, Hello Kitty, Spiderman buns. We stayed from around 10am till it was almost closed at 8pm. It was great to see they kept the rides going even after dark, as I know some places the park stays open, but all or most of the rides close. It began to rain heavily after sunset, and they cancelled the electric light parade.. which was a little dissapointing. They still brought some of the characters out in their light suits to the undercover area for photos, so, it was ok.

this is the 2nd theme park i visit in Japan. USJ is almost same like USS, there have the same theme like Jurassic Park, 4D movie, Water World and etc.. There also have some exciting ride like Spiderman, Jaws... There are 2 different lanes to queue on certain rides ; Group Rider & Single Rder on the ride. Single Rider queue save time. Must try the very delicious Turkey Drumstick at the Jurassic Park, i queue for half an hour. Overall the theme is well maintain and clean. will be back to USJ.

Universal Studio Osaka was very enjoyable for my family . As previous bloggers mentioned, very few spoke English (if at all). All narrations were in Japanese, which may test once patience. But of course it did not matter on rides . We were lucky as we were there on a week day (Monday) so lines were not that bad. Waiting time ran for an average of 20 minutes -the more exciting ones about 30 and the smaller ones for about 10. We arrived later in the day and discovered that there is a twilight rate starting from 3 pm. Rates get a big drop. It worked out for us since we had a good lunch before and need not eat much while at the park-concentrating on getting on all the rides we wanted. It was doable , as the park closes at 8 pm. But you want to end by 7:30 to watch the night parade. The Night parade was fantastic! Loved it !! I recommend bringing light rain jackets in your bag to keep dry when riding those water rides. For those needing wheel chairs or baby strollers, they are very reasonable at only about $5 for the day. Taking in food is prohibited but we managed to sneak in small bite snacks and water- just to munch on when in line. My family enjoyed the day. Just be mentally prepared to have Japanese narrations on 3D or 4D shows ( just enjoy the effects). Lots of Food establishments right outside the park. Most restos close at 10 pm but want to have their last order before 9pm. Enjoy!

An excellent Japan holiday experience ! We love USJ! My daughters enjoys it a lot as her favorite characters are all there Sesame Street Gang! When we went there was a fun month as they have the surprise holloween costume party theme celebrations! Very colorful and everyone was in costume. Rides are fun too ! We love the Spiderman and Back to the future...Better get your quick pass ticket to quickly get in as it has too many people in line...cant forget the hollywood dream rides insanely fun!
I reported to them for my lost glasses. The staff were so helpful. Finally, they found my glasses. Love the 4-D movie of Shrek!!!

Located in a relatively smaller place, this attraction brings out how hollywood movies are made with special effects and doable things that attract kids and elders. Avoid week-ends as you may need to wait in long lines!!  Anyone visiting Japan, should plan to visit Osaka and make it a point to visit this attraction.

We rented an electric cart for $30 and we go priority entrance to all the sights and rides including those walking with you. You don't get tired from walking too much. Eat at the Diner...they have great burgers.
The Hollywood Dream ride and Backrop are such a thrill! A must try! 3D and 4D theatres are presented in Japanese language, didn't understand a word when everyone's laughing out loud.

Universal studio Japan is wonderful place . I like the cartoon characters. Mainly from Seamestreet ... Pink Panter and woodpeckers. I do not know where is the spiderman and super- friend Heros ? May they work at night times!! Ha! Ha! Personally, I prefer Movie world in Austrlia?

The crew working here are super duper friendly. We received so many surprises from them. One of them even wrote a personalised note to my child on the back of a sticker. Apart from that, this is the ONLY Universal Studios in the world where you can find the little cute, pink Sesame Street monster, Moppy.

Guaranteed fun for your family, the park has attractions that will please all ages. They have a lot of souvenir stores. There are restaurants for different tastes. Finally, a place for the whole family!
Many fun rides, although some weren't open on the day and the roller coaster was available on and off throughout the day.

We arrived at 2.30pm and realised they had a special entrance fee and saved S$100 for the 5 of us if we entered after 3pm. There was still sufficient time to see most of the attractions and it was cooler. However, the queues for the popular Spiderman was 100 min long so had to forego that attraction.

The queue can be long but some rides has single riders line and it's relatively faster than normal queue since you're the fillers for rides that requires rider to ride in pair or in even numbers. Sometimes the ride show a 40 min waiting time but I only wait 15 minutes. The famous ride can have wait time of up to hours so be prepared. There's a mall in front of the train station and also Lawson. You can buy drinks and snacks there and bring them in.
We didn't go into the park after already doing two other thyme parks but went through the walk and all the stores including the Hard Rock at the end.

1. Buy express tickets. While waiting in line for 30-45 mins per attraction isn't that painful, seeing express tickets holders zip pass you, is VERY painful.  2. Once you get in, don't waste time taking photos etc. Head straight to queue up for the Hollywood Ride (one and only roller coaster). My Husband and I did just that, and were surprised that we joined a 5 mins queue and eventually received a coupon indicating 5.00-5.30pm. The timing we are allowed to take the ride. Being orderly is good. But it really made us wonder, how early would the public had to queue up to get on the earlier ride timings?  3. Pls do the following - Hollywood Dream The Ride, Spiderman ride, Jurassic Park, Shrek 4D.  4. Pls don't bother with the following - Back to the Future  Conclusion: If you visit Osaka, there is absolutely no reason not to go to USJ. It might just be the most pleasant Universal Studios you can visit, given that the Japanese are so polite and well mannered. :) Prepare to spend a fair bit on souvenirs as everything were soooooo cute. (Especially Moppy - Elmo's pink friend & Sunfairy - the yellow space dude)

Having travelled all the way to Japan, we were not going to miss out on Universal Studios (Even if it is the middle of summer and 38 degrees!). The lines were huge just to buy tickets, and the entry to get in the gate just as long. From exiting the train station to entering the actual park, it took almost an hour and a half. The rides were very dated (Back to the Future, Backdraft, Jaws etc), and I feel that they need to become more current given that their park is based upon movies.  Seeing how long the lines were just to get in the park, we figured the lines for the rides would be just as long, so decided to purchase express tickets. So, for 2 guests, entry and a 7 pass express book (one ticket can be used ONCE for 7 different attractions, this cost us $260 Australian Dollars. We were glad we purchased the express book, as although it only entitles you to jump the queues for the 7 different attractions, the average wait time for the major attractions was 1.5 hours. We did not get to go one one of the main roller coasters, as the wait time was 2 hours and the express book did not give a ticket for this. I am glad we went, but would not do it again.

Traveling with young children, they had a great time in the Wonderland area which has rides for 8 years and below. Snoopy, Elmo, and of course the favorite for girls... Hello Kitty... All the staff are well trained with the greetings and how to look after the kids and so it is a great experience for them. Generally it is busy all year round but we normally take a hotel nearby and go early in the mornings and then in the afternoon about 4 - 5... This is generally enough for the kids and going 2 - 3 days in a row means it is not overly taxing on the kids or us. THe park is small though and the kids have fun taking the same rides over and over. The whole place in fact is very small and I think the tickets are over priced... The price went up again this year. Also the fact you cannot enter multiple times on a standard ticket sucks... We end up buying the annual pass and using that. It is about 3 times a standard ticket price and only visible on the Japanese language version of their website. This ticket allows you to enter and leave as often as you like and so you can lunch at the universal walk restaurants which have much better food than USJ and at lower prices...

I came to Japan to see temples, shrines, and castles, but my wife got bored of them. We went to Universal Studios on a whim, and we have no regrets.  Even though it was a Saturday in August and it was crowded, we were able to get on every ride we wanted to do. I particularly enjoyed the following rides: Spiderman, Hollywood ride, and Space fantasy.

Overall:  Pros: - Clean and pleasant environment. - Fairly enjoyable rides. - Access; not too tricky or expensive to get to. - Helpful website (although some info is missing from the English version)  Cons: - Size - only about 6 actual rides. - Cost - over 6000 yen for an adult ticket, plus an extra 3000 or so for the express tickets. Food and drinks are at the premium prices you'd expect. A small discount can be applied if someone in your party has a birthday in the month you visit, but you'll need to get a coupon in advance. - The queues. Long (e.g. over 2 hours for Spiderman) with no seating and hot with nothing but a periodic blast from an air-conditioner. Buy an express ticket (about 3000 yen) if you can afford it - Not very foreigner-friendly. Signs largely in Japanese, and English videos dubbed. Obviously completely reasonable since it's in Japan, but worth bearing in mind!  My honest impression is that given that there is not much else worth doing in Osaka* then Universal Studios is worth visiting. However, it's not worth going out of your way for, and it's not a must-do if you're on a budget. Budgeting for the costs of the day really should assume the cost of a ticket to include the express pass (think 10,000 yen total for the day) - otherwise you will waste the majority of the time queuing.  *I went to the tourist info office and asked for advice on what to do with a day of sightseeing in Osaka and was told "go to Kyoto"!)

It's a really great amusement park that I've ever been maybe it's operated by Japanese. Because I lost my belongs somewhere which is not an important thing. Before leaving I went to the counter of information and it's like a miracle that I got it back! They even gave me a special gift. And I went to watch the show of water world but in the middle of the show, suddenly the speaker was broken so the show would not be able to continue. In the end they apologized with one express passport of one attraction. Their service is so good! All the attractions that I ride are so amazing especially jaws and the amazing adventure of spider man. But I recommend to buy the express passport otherwise you'll waste a lot of money lining up.

Very disappointed with Universal Studio Japan. The attractions (besides Amazing Spiderman) are movies and cartoons from the 1980s. Rides and attractions available such as: Back to the Future, The Jaws, Snoopy...these are all from the years back when there was no mobile phones. Seriously, someone have to look into this attraction site and do some upgrade.

Definitely a highlight of my trip. We went on a relatively quiet day, and most rides had a 1-2 hour wait. The rides are unique and very good, and though some are clearly from the 1980s and are looking rather dated, they're still incredibly fun. The state of the art rides are as amazing as one expects. Great popular music blasts the entire park adding to the experience, but even with Universal's large portfolio, repeats can be heard. Don't miss this great park, especially if it's a quiet day for the park.
This place is wonderful place ... all 3Ds are well performed ... Space fantasy let you feel that you are outside the planet and between stars ... Water world shows you how the movie is recorded

When most of us travel to Japan with our family or with kids, Tokyo Disney is probably more well known. That said, we have been to Disney Tokyo and Disney Sea. This was our first to Universal Studios Japan (USJ) - it was Fantastic and had rides for young kids, preschoolers and adults.  The only problem we faced was that 99% of visitors were Japanese and so all the staff mainly only spoke Japanese. Brochures and maps were mostly in Japanese. There were a few English speaking guest services staff and they helped alot.  We bought 2 day passes and eventually upgraded to annual passes - Our family really enjoyed USJ.  Its worthwhile staying at the hotels near USJ - you can just walk in and out, and sneak back for a nap if the kids need one.  Dont miss the night parade at 830pm. Spectacular.

Although it was really hot and crowded, my bf and I had the most fun here because there was simply so much to see and buy. The dream rollercoaster was super exciting and totally adrenaline tripping for us.  Definitely would wanna go back in a different season!  Loved the One Piece Summer Special!

How can you miss this?! Variety of rides and tasty food. It is a definitely must visit place when you are in Osaka. Since it is popular, you will expect long queue for rides. Try to come on a weekday (as early as possible). Oh, I forgot to mention that the snacks they sell there are adorable and tasty! Do not forget to grab some!

a great family day out, if you can stay longer in the night be sure to watch magical starlight parade, our son loved it! elmos imagination playground is a must for young children and had no problems with the queus in that area. if your jumping on other rides be sure to purchase express tickets before hand to save waiting in line. lines can increase in the blink of an eye.

This is a MUST destination for family traveling with kids. They will surely enjoy all the attractions inside the park. During peak season, I strongly recommend to purchase your ticket ahead of time to avoid the long line. There are vending machine in convenience store that sell USS tickets (Lawson is an example if my memory serves me right). It is also advisable to purchase a fast pass during super peak season to shorten the waiting time.

we stayed at umeda, so caught loop subway from nishi umeda to inshikujo then got on ymesaki line to unversal city stop. on the way all cars full of people, luckily only short ride. still after got there, took lesser than 3 min to get our tickets(6600 yen adult price).  we did most of tractions apart from too baby ones like hello kitty sesame street. done spiderman 3 times and space fatasy twice. saw the parade around 330pm. a fun day.  don't know it was because the japanese managed it better or just lucky,or not too many people that day, did not feel wasting any time for lines.

No so recommended if you been to Universal Studio in Singapore! A little disappointed. Staff literally speak English & everything in Japanese make most tourist that don't understand Japanese feel left out. When ask for assistance & they couldn't answer, 1 just tell me "wakarimasen" and turn me away.

It wasn't as spectacular as Disneyland nor Disneysea, but it's a good place to go if you are family with young children or teens.  They have a different characters there such as Sesame Street, Hello Kitty and Snoopy which my daughter loved. If you are Hello Kitty lovers and you don't have time to go to Puroland, you can come here. They have this room full of Hello Kitty's fashion stuffs called Hello Kitty's Ribbon Collection. You can also meet and take picture with Hello Kitty character inside.  We don't understand Japanese language and some of the attractions especially the one in theater are in Japanese. However we loved the Woody Woodpecker show. It was very entertaining.  The parade was again not as great as the one in Disney Resort, but it was worth waiting for. It was full of lights and enjoyable for any kind of ages.

VIsited this theme park in the middle of October. For the celebration of Halloween, Universal Studio have organised various activities for Halloween. I super like the idea of Zombie wonder around in the park at night to "attack" visitors... the screaming and running are great fun. Love it. At one of the restaurant, they have arranged staff to dress like a female ghost (a character very popular in the japannese horror movie) to "scare" guests that having meals there... I was shocked by the "ghosts" as she suddenly appeared from my bacj while i having my dinner... it was really fun.

The best attraction - Biohazard The Real, where we shoot live Zombies (just like in the game)!! This attraction is only limited to a number of patrons for a day, thus we need to line-up to collect the entrance tickets as soon as we reached USJ. Other attractions was the Backdrop Ride and The Amazaing Adventure of Spiderman. Not to mention that the Zombies will appear during the night during Halloween!

Bought the express pass as i am with my son who is quite impatient with long lines, enjoyed the whole day with him, superman 4D ride, Jaws, Back to the Future, Space Fantasy, Jurassic etc.... Had fun the whole day only had one gripe was the expensive but unappetizing food, for what you pay you would expect delicious food. All the shows were in japanese which we did not understand a word but still had much fun.

Most of the japanese who came were gesr up with Halloween costume so that creates the mood and everyone were in the sport celebrating Halloween. The only thing i found a bit lacking is that the language. There are rides like Spiderman was in Japanese and that kinda put off the mood since i dont speak the language. The staff too should upgrade their english skills since tjey are the frontliners. I was asking about where ro buy the entrance ticket and the discount when i bought the 2 day pass...i end up buying a train ticket instead of an entrance ticket. But above all that the staff's effort is appreciated regardless the miscommunication.

Tokyo have Disney-land and Osaka have Universal Studio. The rides are amazing, if you are tourist with kids like me than please don't forgot to take Fast-Pass to skip the big line. I have 2 kids 5 yrs and 2.8yrs, They enjoyed all the ride which made my every $$$ worth while. its less crowded in compare with Tokyo Disneyland. Its not too far from Osaka I paid approx 3000Yen Taxi. Public transport is easily available using JR Pass  Good Luck

This was a disappointment from start to finish. After spending 4 amazing days in Disney, we were hoping that Universal would be amazing too. We started off arriving at the park at 8.30am, hoping to buy tickets and then be able to queue for the park opening at 10am. This was not the case, there were huge queues, it took us 2 hours to get tickets, by this time all of the express tickets were sold out, we then had to queue to get into the park. I have a disability so I was given an access support card. This was where I was given a time (the length of the queue) but I am able to sit out of the queue until the time allocated where I then can go on the ride. I waited over 10 minutes to a member of staff to sign the card then the member of staff refused to sign it and then totally ignored us and signed other peoples card. Eventually we were given a time and waited 2 hours to go onto the ride. I asked for a locker (these were available) to put my camera, video camera and bag in. I was told there was no need and to take them on the ride (Hollywood Dream). When we were just about to board the ride we were told to leave out cameras at the side of the ride, this was not very secure so I asked why we were refused a locker. I asked if my husband could go on first, so I could hold the cameras etc, and then do a swap. One of the staff members agreed and my husband got onto the ride. They first insisted we emptied all of our pockets in-front of the members of staff as they didn’t believe they were empty (this was totally unreasonable and rude). Anyway, my husband got on the ride as I waited but the ride didn’t go. It was a good 15 mins and the ride still hadn’t started. My husband was then asked to leave the ride, this was after he had his belt on and checked. I them asked to see a manager. A male member of staff then agreed we could have a locker, and to our surprise, they were all empty! The staff members that were manning the lockers had gone and no one was able to use them. We got a locker and went on the ride, altogether it took 3.5 hours. This was our first ride of the day! We then thought we would go on Spiderman – the queue – 5 hours long! So we went for lunch. Again over an hours queue and then we were served the large drinks and they were half full, when we asked why, they said without ice it is the parks policy to serve drinks half full, even after complaining we were told this is what they did. So after that we bought bottles, which without ice, were full! The park was a total disorganised mess and they treated non Japanese with a total lack of respect and many times were rude and ignorant. We put a complaint in to the customer services team but it made no difference. This park was the total opposite of the Disneyland and DisneySea that were well run, had amazingly kind staff who were always willing to help. I would not recommend this park and I will certainly never go again. I will visit Japan but will stay away from Universal.

Although Universal Studio is closer for us, Universal Studio Osaka is still better than Singapore :-) Osaka is bigger and has more rides and attractions compared to Singapore. My two teenage boys love Universal Studio Osaka despite the long queuing during the day. We were fortunate that we arrive here quite early in the morning .......

Universal studios Osaka is meant for specific groups of people. School going kids going with friends, hardcore merchandising guests and young couples with young kids. Unlike Disney, which has a more ubiquitous reach, USO appeals only that much. This is worse when visiting from countries with a US eg Singapore. The comparisons change expectations The 4D rides/shows were of good quality but were in Japanese. Hollywood Dream was tame by US roller coaster standards. Jaws was a serious yawn especially if you queued for 72 mins when the sign said 30 mins. Mind you, we paid for the express pass which came in handy but the fast pass at Disney's is a better system. Unless you belong to the above 3 categories, I would give USO a miss

My family visited USJ on Wed, 11 Dec 2013. Arrived at the entrance around 10:20am and queued up for tickets.  Saw a ticket counter with 2 staffs, thought it was the one with an Intrepretor. It was the biggest mistake, took us about 40 minutes to get our tickets because one of the staffs was very slow, probably she was a trainee and the other must be a supervisor or trainer.  Purchase the express passes for kid and adult, both staffs at the ticket counter could not explain the usages well in English. I expected the leftlet should give more info. But, great disappointment, everything was in Japanese.  Not sure what went wrong, most of the shows such as Animation Celebration and WaterWorld covered in Kid's Express pass would only start after 12:40pm and 13:00pm respectively for that day. Then, what is the point to have the Express passes? It ended up the Kid's Express passes were not used and we brought them back as souvenirs.  Attended the Terminator2:3D. Everything was conducted in Japanese. A good experience if you want to feel like an alien and don't understand what is going on. Luckily, I watched the movies before and able to explain the background to the kids.  The queues for the ride were long. After 1 ride, decided to call it a day at 13:30pm. Eldest kid visited Universal Studio Singapore last year during school graduation trips and suggest to visit there.

I went to USJ on 15 Nov (Fri),the first day of Christmas event. The park is very crowded (Many attractions had wait times of around 1 hour) but it is very nice with many Christmas decoration.  I highly recommend the night projection show "The Gift on Angels II - The Song of an Angel", it is a 20-min-long show with great songs and light effects, it is the most beautiful one I have ever seen!!!The Christmas, having 356,097 lights and breaking the Guinness World Records, is also marvelous and stunning!!!  The night parade is also very attractive and colorful, the number of floats is much more than what I expected!!!  For the attractions, I like 1. Spider man 2. Space fantasy and 3. Terminator 2 the most. I had no time to ride the Hollywood dream roller coaster and Jurassic park boat ride.  Because I can speak some Japanese, I understand at least half the Japanese content, so I prefer it more than Universal Studios Singapore since Japan's park is bigger and has more entertaining factors.

Went into USJ with the heavy feeling since raining from early morning. Anyway, just relax & forget about rain for the whole day. My wife enjoy it very much since that day is her birthday :-). I have been LA Universal Studio, comparative USJ is much smaller & language is really the barrier. But is expected... enjoy!

Had the best Christmas in my life in Universal Studio Japan. Value for money. Paid 6500yen and it's worth spending. Beautiful lightings, all the store are decked wth pretty x'mas fittings. They have fantastic long parades, all beautifully light up Must go!

Don't go. Biggest disappointment. Is it don't even have a good T-shirts. We tried to go on the rights it was impassable the waiting lines was from one hour to 4 hours. I decided to have fun shopping but it didn't work out too the didn't have any good product to buy.
Everything the rides and attractions , but get a fast pass if it a busy day, will go every time in osaka

Universal Studios Japan puts me off because of the language barrier, but it took me years to accept the plain fact that USJ does a better job@ theme park management as compared to Universal Studios Hollywood, judging from my visit to USH in 2006 & i was appalled that some facilities were dilapidated...so my first visit to USJ was in 2 words...FREAKINGLY FUN!!!  even my mother, who doesn't fancy theme parks, enjoyed the extraordinary theme-ing found throughout the park!!! WELL DONE USJ!!!

Universal Studios in Japan is a fun full-day experience with fun attractions. Just walking around the park and seeing the themed design of the streets and buildings is an experience in itself.  The only downside is the time you have to spend in queues. We spent an average of 1 1/2 hours in queue for each attraction (the longest being over 2 hours for the Spiderman attraction), which stretched my patience a bit. Granted, we did visit during the Japanese holiday (Obon), so if you visit outside the weekends/holidays it might be less crowded.  Expect to spend a full day there if you want to see it all, so come early. Try to get the express tickets if you can (they were sold out already when we got there at 11:00). I recommend seeing the parade at night but you don't have to buy the seat tickets like we did - we moved out of the seating area and could easily find a better viewing spot down the road. Bring a handful of patience, possibly a book to read while queuing, and you'll have a lot of fun. Tip: Around closing time you can get into a last few attractions quite fast (15 minutes waiting).

This is very similar to Universal in Florida, but enough is different to definitely make it visit if you have already done the Florida one. Be wary though, it can get very crowded. We visited on a Friday at 10am, fast passes had already sold out and there was already a 600 minute queue for the Spiderman ride!

Great theme park! its a good thing they still have the jaws ride. the express booklet is well worth every yen! breezed thru the rides and thoroughly enjoyed and had a great time! Food is delicious! marvellous theme park! space fantasy is my top ride!

Feels like you are in Hollywood, except the rides speak Japanese. the Hollywood dream ride is the best. Just keep getting back in line. The diner with had the best burgers we have had in Japan. Didn't care for the back to future or spider-man rides, made me a little sick. We did this on the way back to the airport from Kyoto. It is right off the JR line. You can put your luggage in a locker right at the front gate of the park for 800 yen. It was a good way to spend the day waiting to go to the airport. It took about 30-45 minutes to get to the airport from there.
Made me turn to younger day again. Love everything in there. Recommend to visit. I love all the ride, atmosphere and all staff.

I visited USJ on 23rd April with my partner & 4.5yr old Son. It was our first time at any Universal Studios & we all had a fantastic day. Other reviews have said that this park is smaller than other Universal Parks, which may well be true, but rest assured that USJ is not tiny by any means. You will most certainly fill your day. We arrived Just on opening time, we queued to purchase tickets for only about 5mins & went straight into the park without any further wait time. All of the staff were really friendly. We only speak VERY basic Japanese, and had no problems. Staff are exceptionally helpful with the kids & make a point of saying hello & high fiving them. The Spider-Man ride & Jurassic Park rides were our favourites and the longest line we were in was about 20 mins and we didn't purchase a fast pass either. The section for younger children babies to about 8yrs was fantastic. Our Son loved the Snoopy area & surrounds. He played for hours. There are several photo opportunities & the staff OFFER to take a photo with your phone or camera once they have taken theirs. This is great,especially if you want to share your photo on Facebook,text or email. We had a truly amazing day and I would recommend Universal Studios Japan to everyone.

Awesome place! Food wasn't crazy expensive either. Lines aren't so long if you get there early. For old and young people. All the rides are in Japanese but you pretty much get the point of it i guess with what's happening during the ride and all. Most people there can speak english so that's a good thing for tourists.

Worth spending a day or two. Must buy the Express Pass to enjoy all the rides. Recommended rides: Hollywood Dream -The Ride Space Fantasy The Amazing Adventure of Spider-Man Backdraft May skip the following if time constraint: Back To The Future- The Ride  We tried some adorable snack and find Elmo bun is tasty and a bit spicy while Snoopy bun and Hello Kitty bun are more suitable for kids. Fried Chicken in Amity Landing Restaurant is also yummy. Definitely will go again and hopefully will be able to watch the theater shows as we had skipped for the rides.

It is a little far from the city, don't take a taxi, the trains are easy enough to navigate, staff are helpful. The theme park is well set up, clean and staff very friendly. We didn't go on the rides as the queues were long, but we enjoyed some of the shows and took plenty of photos. Lots of eating places of different themes and some good shopping too.
The place is very nice but crowded. I spent a whole day but attend only 3 attractions. Next time I won't miss to buy a fast track for saving my time.

Went here with my kids and nephew a year ago. We really enjoyed our experience because its my first time with my kids. I can see their happy faces. They are all thrilled to see different characters and take pictures everywhere! We love the hollywood dream ride!! It was the best!! We didn't wait for long queues because we purchase special pass aside from the regular day pass. We were able to try most of the rides/ attractions and the money spent for the pass is worth it. The only thing I've notice is that they don't have much mineral water (for drinking) available. I don't like tea and thats all they have on their food stand, so my kids and i are always thirsty after every ride. But all in all its a perfect day for us esp. when we saw the sesame street characters. It was a fun day for all of us :) highly recommended.

One of the best parks in the asia region, but some of the rides like Backdraft are japanese only. Lines were acceptable, not too long, and had signs to tell you average wait times for each ride around the park so u can strategically plan your next move.  So i visited this place in august, when they have the one piece summer event, and various areas of the park is decorated in one piece themed stuff.  My mind exploded when i saw someone dressed as smoker, and he HAD SMOKE COMING OUT OF HIS CAPE.  The restaurants also serve typical theme park priced foods with one piece themes, which made me feel better for dishing out cash for it. They also had a hour long one piece show and a booking-only restaurant show, where u can eat and sanji comes and hits on your girlfriend. Downside is japanese only.  I bought my tickets at a lawson at the start of my trip to avoid lines at the park entrance, but again, park ticket vending machines - japanese only.  And if youre going in summer, i suggest you bring a sweat towel or an extra tshirt, cus it is HOT.

nice place. not too big not too small. rides were kid friendly. weather was nice. unfortunately the down side is everything is in Japanese. The hotels around the theme park are well priced. Looking forward to Harry Potter

Universal Studios Japan is definitely better than Universal Studios Singapore but everything is in Japanese and we are Lost in Translation especially for the shows and the rides. The Hello Kitty attraction is a plus. The staff are always smiling and polite.

The park itself only has 2 rollercoaster rides (the same tracks - one carriage going forwards and ine backwards). We took half a day to do through the park.  Most of the shows are in english but still fun given the audience participation and reactions on the ride. This made the day for me more than the rides.

Almost everything you hear is Japanese, but who cares? It's still a great park and the kids had a blast. The lineups weren't as long as expected and there is a lot to see even while you are in line. Since we were with young children we skipped the shows but our elderly aunt went to see a few and she says she still likes them. We've been to other Universal Studios in Hollywood, Orlando, and Singapore and although it doesn't match up to the ones in the US, we already like it more than USS. We'll definitely be back here in our future trips. Oh, one gripe is the food isn't all that great for the price you are paying.

Went here in June. Weather was great. Not too hot. Crowd was tolerable. Bought the fast pass booklet 7. Simply worth it. Cut down our time alot. For the games, our favourite was the Jurassic Park ride. A bit different from the one in Singapore but enjoyed both of their rides so far. Cause you get wet at the almost end of the rides. Too bad Jaws was under maintenance. Hollywood dream ride was cool. Didn't take the backdrop. But taking the dream ride was already wicked. Should come here at least once if you are in Osaka.

Went to USJ in June. Weather was not too hot and windy. All attractions were in Japanese but our children had an enjoyable time. Some of the rides were too scary and exciting for my 7year old son. But overall, it was a great experience. The staffs were extremely helpful and friendly. It was a pity that Jaws was closed and the magical starlight parade was not available on that day. The park closed at 6pm but we did manage to visit quite a lot of attractions. ( Practically ran our way to the next attraction in order to visit as many as possible ). We were allowed to continue snapping photos in the theme park after the closing hours. It was a wonderful day out for the adults and kids alike.

I visited USJ as part of a school trip to japan, I should probably comment on the fact first that I am 6 foot 1 tall so even in Scotland I'm tall so, being in Japan often made me a bit of a spectacle, whilst we were the Halloween celebrations were starting. There was the parade and the loop track of about 3 English Halloween songs including 'the time warp' which we did dance around the park to. The parade was better than the ones I've seen in US Florida, as they were bigger and more eye catching. We were all given mardi gras type beads by the dancers and most characters came to hug us. I'm quite scared of rides and luckily so was another boy but we were tricked into going on space fantasy (I think) which was quite confusing as the rides were (obviously) all in Japanese but the scare factor was still there. Back to the future was good (it's the exact same as the Simpsons ride in USF) , spider man is also there along with Jurassic park and jaws. Like I mentioned previously myself and another boy don't like rides so we waited outside with bags for most which was fine as it was warm and there was definitely plenty to look at, however there were large groups of school children that seemed to be more interested in the two westerners than the large attractions so we did find ourselves in several awkward moments where hand jesters were the only way to ask for pictures, we felt like something of celebrities by the time it go dark and we went home. The park was immaculate like everywhere else we visited and there was a large selection of vending machines, eating outlets and gift shops which passed our time nicely. If I ever go back to japan I think I'll go back.

Only new ride is Spiderman. Terminator 2 is still nice to see, but the movie is like ages ago. Of course when you consider Amity from Jaws, most other attractions seem newer. Take great consideration when going for theatre type shows as everything, and I mean everything is in Japanese. They're currently celebrating Easter still so some attractions have been touched up and lots of eggs around. Not sure if some characters have been told to run around during photo takings, but certain characters like Shrek, Snoopy spend half their time running from park goers avoiding taking photos. Go once if you've not been before.

Plentiful people had to wait a long while for the more popular rides. Everything is in japanese, although the attendants do speak some English. The peanuts, hello kitty and Sesame Street was extremely kawai. There was a night parade unfortunately there was only 3 character float. Think most people wanted more peanuts, hello kitty & Sesame Street. Overall, the usual attractions like jaws & Spider-men drew the crowds.

A truly world class theme park, worth a visit! Be sure to purchase a ticket at any main JR station before heading over to the Universal Studios. This will save you loads of time queuing up at the ticket booth. With the tickets purchase from JR station, one can enter the park directly without exchanging any ticket at the ticket booth. Rides are superb but everything is in Japanese.

The only unique ride I enjoyed is Spiderman.  I would have given it a higher rating if not for the language issue. It is hard to totally enjoy the story or the ride if I can't understand what is happening as the stories are all told in Japanese.

We spontaniously decided to go on a day trip to this park, being tired of all the temples in Kyoto and we were very happy that we did! Bare in mind we were the age of 42 and 20 when you read this review. We went on a saturday around noon and there were hardly any lines at the entrance. Being one of the busiest theme parks in the world make sure you utilise the fastpass system. I enjoy Universal theme parks and the attractions and rides they have to offer. Good to spend the day here and easy to get to by JR and other rails

The rides are thrilling. Kids are very excited. There also hello kitty in there. Try the spiderman. Its new so i waited for 1 hour to ride. I went on Monday and found some main shows were not in schedule for that day. Also found some restaurant were closed, or closed earlier.  Overall, the ridings are great and and fun. Coming from Singapore, where we also have Universal Studio, and also I been to the park 8 or 9 years ago, I have high expectation of this theme park. And it didn't let me down. Although the park was very strict with the height restriction, my 4.5YO son did manage to get on most rides, although he would have love Jurassic Park. He was too short, so my hubby had to take him to the Backdraft show, while my 6.5YO daughter and I went for the splash down that dino ride. There were still some attractions we didn't have time to visit, it was such a pity.

The park itself is nice to see , but all the story about the rode are in Japanese with no English subtitles !! Furthermore the rides are a bit old apart from Spider-man which stand out but once again the whole story is in Japanese !

Of course, narratives on rides are Japanese. What were you expecting???????  The JR took me a long tie from Kayobashi, with long platform waits taking over one hour end to end. Wasting precious time at the park, would recommend a taxi.  Entered 10:10, after running from the JR Universal City I only had a short line for tickets. Bought a carnet of 7 fast pass tickets, but some rides had short queues on Tuesday. Anyhow, at Y4500 approx. It saved us about 2 hours of waiting.  Everyone ran to Fe Hollywood Dream on entering,a 40 min queue turned out longer. Later in the day was only 20 mins  Big people have to 'prove their add can fit in a test chair, so lay off the donuts  Spiderman the Ride is fantastic, a mix of ride,4D. I couldn't tell if it was moving or not.  Back to the Future was old tech, not much good  Backtrack was wasteful, with long Japanese narratives the part one and two, which spoiled the storyline. Last part 3 sort of cool. Needs English audio headsets to enjoy  Jaws ok, but again narrative would have made it fantastic. It is better than Universal Hollywood  Space Fantasy is a medium sized fun coaster with rotating cars, a surprising enjoyful ride  Jurassic park exactly as per Hollywood  Skipped Harry Potter Avoid Terminator with long narrative

After 10 years time, USJ still stays the greatest place to visit. Enjoyed my time at its best! The only recommendation is to get express booklet 7 with the tickets. Waiting time for the most popular attractions is more than 80 min... So do pay extra money for quick queue to enjoy. Do not waste you time with shopping, just visit universal studios!

We went on July 15, the day Harry potter opened. I was expecting the whole thing to be insane, but they opened at 8am and it was very quick through the ticket gates. All the express passes had sold out, but that was actually a bonus in the end as my 5 and 7 yr old were too scared to go on most of the express pass rides, and also, the wait times were pretty short. if you want to see Harry potter then here's a tip.  Go straight in and high tail it to the allocated time ticket booths, which are located down opposite from jaws. We had to wait 5 hours for our time slot. And you need your original ticket so don't lose it like I did! The wait times in there built up massively over the day.  We had a great day. We stocked up on onigiri and took in water bottles so most of the day we snacked and filled our bottles up at water fountains. The lawson in universal city also has long lines.  The only proper ride my kids braved was space fantasy. It is fantastic, quite scary for kids but just enough to not make them spun out. Take Y100 for the lockers. They adored the wonderland section and spent loads of time in there.  We did the 4D cinema and waterworld shows. In Japanese but still enjoyable and daring. The jaws and waterworld are big on guns and fire, which freaked my dudes out, but they also loved it.  Frozen pineapples are a great treat and not too junky.  Harry potter section looks amazing but it was insane. The ride wait tine for hp was 230 mins. We lined up for 70 mins to enter the gift shop. I wanted to tear my eyes out in disgust at that, the steeples waiting and the mad scrounging for goods once inside. Then another 40 mins waiting to pay!  The good side was everyone was in there so the rest of park felt quite manageable.

I haven't visited Universal Studios since I was a child in Los Angeles, and I don't go to many amusement parks so I don't have any idea how Universal Studios Japan compares to other parks, but irregardless, my daughter really loved it.  I am long term resident of Japan, and have been here long enough to realize that the surprisingly persistent stereotype of "polite Japanese" can certainly be a misnomer in many parts of Japan where some people can be surprisingly passive-aggressive, and friendly service can be quite rare. Though Osaka is well known in Japan for having a more friendly and outgoing culture, the staff at this theme park are among the friendliest and most professional I have encountered in all of Japan. My 5-year-old was almost overwhelmed with cheery waves, sincere smiles, and free stickers which certainly added to her enjoyment of the theme park. Japan is not known for second language ability, and despite reviews complaining about a lack of English, the English signage and language ability is well beyond most places in Japan. You will find a surprising amount staff members with better than average second language ability and they will eagerly try to help you. The Starlight Parade was much better than expected. The park is good about posting accurate wait times, so if one is long try another.  Like any theme park, it is far more economical to purchase a season pass if you are going to be in the area for any length of time, or plan to make return visits. Three visits to the park will pay for itself. Like any theme park, it is a little pricey. Like any theme park, it is far more enjoyable when it isn't too crowded and the timing is essential in Japan. These kind of attractions are normally crowded in Japan, so like anywhere, traveling off-season or mid-week is naturally a good time to visit—particularly since locals are less likely to take advantage of these times. Weekends can be tremendously crowded. But, in the case of Japan, for inexplicable reasons, the crowds will often magically disappear around 5 in the evening even though the weather is starting to cool down. The later the better if the park is open late. If you time it right, you will even find 5 minute or less wait times on many of the children's rides.

The JR line to Universal is relatively cheap fro Osaka station. Take the train to Sakurajima getting off at Universal City, this aviods changing at Nishikujo.The entrance gate is just a short walk. Entrance fee is about $75. Though the leaflets mention bringing in food and drink is not permitted, we found that bags were not checked. The food inside is relatively expensive with a turkey leg costing $8 and a small ice cream cone $3. There are plenty of drinking fountains dotted across the park, so empty water bottles can be refilled. If you have visited the Universal Parks in the USA, I would give this a miss. The commentary is all in Japanese (cant expect anything else), but does spoil the rides and there is a lot of queuing. Go to the Harry Potter ride first, as they limit the tickets on an hourly basis. We ended up queuing for over an hour. The ride was good, pity they did not do the same as Spiderman and make the visuals in 3D.

fun place. looks like most of the attractions have been picked up and shipped from the californian studios. identical to what we saw there 20 years ago. Still fun though. Having only japanese commentaries was a bit frustratingh. The harry potter attraction was awesome. very very well done. worth a visit just to see it and I am not what you call an avid fan of the movie.

We arrived at USJ at around 8.15 on the opening day of the Harry Potter World to find the gates had been opened earlier than the official time and there were no queues by the time we arrived. Of course our main aim was to see Harry Potter World, but after all the trips to Osaka we have made we have never been to USJ due to listening to people who had told us that it was not worth going as they did not cater for non-Japanese speaking people. How wrong they were!!! I only speak a little Japanese and did not find any problems. We quickly found out that you needed a fast pass to get into Harry Potter World and after standing on a queue that moved very quickly we got our fast pass ticket but could not enter for another 3 hours. No problem....time to explore the rest of the park. This was a good time to do this as everyone was interested in the new "world" and the queues for the other rides were not long. We loved the ride in Jurassic Park, did not expect it to be so much fun. Went in to see Hello Kitty and my daughter had a photo taken with her. Hello Kitty was very surprised that my daughter is fluent in Japanese. Even though we don't have any young kids we enjoyed this area too and watched the children having so much fun. At our designated time we entered Harry Potter Land. There were so many people here. Fortunately the queue for the Harry Potter ride was not too long and we were enjoying the excitement of the ride. Be aware that this ride is not for those with weak stomachs and also be prepared to pay 100 yen to put your items in a locker as you can not take them on the ride with you. After the ride we stood for 90 minutes on a queue to Honeydukes to purchase "Bertie Bott's every-flavour beans and chocolate frogs", but be prepared to pay for it!! The lunch areas were full and had long queues so we decided to eat elsewhere, as we had a two day pass we would return the next day. On the second day we were more prepared for Harry Potter World and our fast passes allowed us in much earlier than the day before. We decided to purchase goods from the shops and my daughter wanted a robe, scarf and tie etc. These were selling fast and unfortunately they had sold out of the ties for the house that she liked. Not to worry as we will return again soon with my husband and youngest daughter next time. We tried the butter beer and had lunch in the "Three Broomsticks" restaurant which served more English type foods such as Shepherd Pie, Fish and Chips and Cornish Pasties. The queue here on the second day was not so bad although we decided to have an early lunch and arrived at 11.30am. The food was a reasonable price and staff are very helpful with finding you a table, even taking photos of you with the castle in the background. After lunch we watched a couple of street attractions and then decided to say goodbye to Harry Potter World and check out some of the shows in the rest of the park. We decided on the Universal Monsters Live Rock and Roll show and thoroughly enjoyed it. At 8.30 at night there is the Magical Starlight Parade and worth seeing. There were many other shows you could see to but we decided to leave some for our next visit.

Timed entry ticket is needed to visit the the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. For detail, please refer to this USJ web page: http://www.usj.co.jp/e/enjoy/  If you are Snoopy and Hello Kitty fans, the Universal Wonderland should not be missed.
