I loved 'The wizarding g works of Harry Potter", Space fantasy, Jaws, Spider-Man, Wonderworld, just everything about it....

very much like the Orlando one, but much bigger than the Singapore one (the SG one is so small). USJ cannot be compared to the LA one. USJ also has City Walk with restaurants and shops. And the new Harry Potter experience has opened. You will need to wait over 1hr for most popular rides, so if you have the money, the express pass is nice.

Attractions almost the same with other universal studios. Best visited on weekdays when there are small amount of people. Best to buy yearly pass so you will not be pressured to finish everything in one go.  I love USJ especially on cold weather.

Average entry price is around $70, but be ready to pay an extra $60 for the express pass.  Besides this, it is an incredible place! The park is split into several different themes. Ranging from Jurassic Park, to Amity, to New York, and finally the Wizarding World of Hogwarts. The park is immense, filled with many shops and restaurants to choose from. The immersive 4D rides are quite worth the wait. Feeling the heat from flames, being sprayed with water, and having your vehicle shake and bounce all over the place. It was possibly the most fun I had while I was in Japan.  All non themed parts of the park are designed with a retro 1950's-60's American architecture. At night there was a huge parade with several beautifully lit floats and dancers. The highlight of the park right now is the Harry Potter attraction. You can visit the Hogwarts Express, buy yourself a wand at Olivander's, buy some quidditch equipment, or try some pumpkin juice or butter beer (non-alcoholic, kinda tastes like root beer). You can also go to Honeydukes Sweetshop and buy some every flavour beans, or if you have times you can go to the Three Broomsticks for a meal. There is also the Hogwarts choir that performs several times a day.  As expected, almost all merchandise here is expensive and will empty your wallet. But if you stick to attractions, I won't be as bad.  My words cannot do justice to the amazement I felt when visited USJ. The only way you can understand is if you go yourself.

Universal Studios Osaka Japan is the third Universal Studios park that I had visited besides the one in Singapore and Orlando, US. It is always so exciting to visit a theme park and Universal Studios Japan was no exception! I had a great time with my friends. The Spiderman ride is highly recommended. Love it! I also sat on the JAWS ride, had a butterbeer @ Harry Potter (queue up like 20 mins under the hot sun for this, but it is worth every sip :)), Jurassic Park (This was fun! It is different from the one in SG and yes, you will definitely get wet, but not soaking wet :)), Space Fantasy and Back to the Future.  I went on a Monday and it was extremely crowded! The queue for the Harry Potter ride was like 3-4 hours? Madness. It was due to the summer/school holidays + the recent opening of Harry Potter section. The Harry Potter venue is pretty amazing. Just like the movies and the books, however it was just too crowded. You have to get a “pass” to get in to the Harry Potter section due to the huge crowd. This pass have the timings that you are allowed to enter in to the park, so remember to get it first or you will not be allowed in to the park although you have the entrance tickets or Express pass.  How to get there: Take the train on the JR Osaka Loop line and head to JR Universal City station. Alight and follow the signs :)  Tips: I bought my entrance ticket on Saturday, for entry on Monday to avoid the queue. Didn’t managed to purchase the Express Pass (was looking for the 5 rides one). Apparently they don’t sell the Express pass in advance even though you go to the park to purchase it. You can only purchase it online, or on the day itself at the entrance (don’t bother trying. I was there at 8.00am on Monday and there was already a queue and it was sold out) or at the convenient stores in Japan, but this is also limited as they only allocate an X number of Express passes a day. But overall, the queue was pretty manageable (except for the Harry Potter one) as we queued up at the Individual lane (to fill up the gaps during the ride, so you wont get to ride with friends/family). The longest queue was like 30-40mins? So it was pretty good at the end of the day, we saved like SGD 30-40 (didn’t managed to purchase the Express Pass). For these from SG, it is cheaper to purchase the tickets in JP vs JTB.  Go early. They open the park like at 8.30am on that day I was there.  The weather was extremely hot as well, as I visited this park in August, therefore remember to bring your sun blocks, caps, hats, etc  Have fun! Review of WW of HP at USJ.  I visited USJ today while on a biz trip to Osaka, despite some rather discouraging reviews. I had read here that they often open the park as early as 7:45 even though the official open time is 9:00 and people who come late often end up disappointed so was at the gate with my ticket pre-purchased (can be purchased at Lawson, even the night before) at 7:00 to be safe, Kindle in hand. 7:30 even would probably have been fine as at that point there were only maybe another 20 people behind me, although in each of the 20 entrance lines=400 people).  At 7:20ish, we were asked to stand up and line up properly. At 8:00, the staff finally started letting people in, but all us early risers watched in horror as a huge running mob of 1-2000 people staying in the USJ official hotels were let inside first from a separate entrance. At 8:10, I started to worry that they would give them an hour head start or something, but at 8:15 us common people were let in as well (lol).  I made off for the area towards the middle of the park where you can receive a timed ticket to enter the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, but when I confirmed with a staff member halfway there she said they weren't necessary this time of day!! So you could technically go in twice if you wanted to see how it is at night as well (once in the morning, once with timed entry if it's still available when you come out.) I arrived at the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and slowly walked through taking lots of pictures. The detail is absolutely amazing.  By 8:45 I was lined up in the "castle walk through"/Forbidden Journey ride where the wait was too fast for my liking as there was so much to see *SPOILERS*walking by the herbology green house, dark halls, and Dumbledore's office among other things. However, I felt like it would have been even better if they had included more details in the wait (walking through the dining hall, other classrooms, etc.) as they only had some "floating candles" near the start of the ride. The Sorting Hat was very cool though!  In 15 minutes I had reached the locker area and another 5 I was on the ride! Less than half the posted wait time. The ride itself was pretty cool, but not jaw dropping. 4D effects from the dragons fogged up my glasses. Water droplets occasionally splashed. I was surprised it wasn't colder when the dementors appeared. All in all an older kid/adult friendly ride that felt more than worth the rather short wait.  After that I took a look at Honeydukes and the other shops while the wait times weren't too long. Honeydukes was crazy overpriced--1200 yen per chocolate frog and 1800 for a medium size box of every flavor beans! However, when I decided after leaving the attraction later that the every flavor beans would be fun for "batsu game" I was not able to find anything other than the chocolate frogs at the regular USJ souvenir shops outside the attraction so it is NOT the case that you can buy the sweets outside the area later if you change your mind!  By 11 the lines for shops were about 4 times as long (maybe 45 minutes?) so go early if you don't want to wait just to enter Honeydukes or Ollivander's (the latter of which has a separate entrance for those who don't mind missing the short entrance video clip). Sound effects in the girls bathroom of a certain female ghost were fun as well so worth it to use the 30+ stall bathroom in Hogsmeade just for that!  Butter beer at the Three Broom sticks (all the Japanese kids were taking selfies with cream on their upper lips lol) was nice for a break and still not at all crowded at 10 or 11AM. It was far too sweet though between extra sweetened creme/caramel(?) soda and a caramel flavored creme topping. At 1100 yen, it's definitely not cheap, but comes with a simple plastic souvenir mug (much cheaper than buying a "house" coffee mug for 2-3000 yen in the shops!). Better to share just one and take a pumpkin juice home as a souvenir if you like (pumpkin, apple, and apricot with spices, it's slightly less sweet than butterbeer and might be nice hot like spiced cider.) You can also buy either at the kiosks outside, but I wanted to enjoy the awesome atmosphere of The Three Broomsticks with it's high ceilings, wooden staircases up to who knows where, and iron chandeliers.  After taking in some shows and walking around a bit more to let the surroundings sink in I had a snack of soda bread and split pea soup and ham for 600 or so yen at the Three Broomsticks, this time outside to enjoy the view of Hogwarts over the lake. Some girls at the next table were enjoying the 2000/person "feast" plate, a massive platter of corn on the cob, various meats and veggies, with a large side salad.  Feeling a bit tired already at 11:30, I said goodbye to HP world and wandered toward Hollywood Dream to check out the wait time and decided to give it a go at 11:50 despite the 80-minute posted wait time. It was also one of the rides I had wanted to try when visiting the park in 2007. I had a Kindle to deal with the wait, but was on the ride in just 25 minutes.  I thought about checking out some other things given that the other ride wait times were probably not as long during lunch time, but felt pretty satisfied and with a 3 hour journey ahead of me, headed home to Tokyo.  I would say if you want to enjoy this park, and are already paying almost 7000 yen to get in, go by 7:30 and don't bother paying the obscene extra cost of the express passes. Enjoy the rides in the morning and eat outside of regular mealtimes or bring your own food. I saw tons of people eating outside food, so it's not necessary to spend 2000+ per meal although I imagine it is more fun to eat the theme'd meals and snacks, even if they do add up.  All-in-all a fun half-day and definitely felt it was well worth getting up early, even if my wallet is rather empty now...XD

Visited the park on a Tuesday, 7th October. I had planned to reach there well before 8am to ensure I get my hands on the Express Pass to skip the long queues. Reached there at 8am sharp, people were already queuing at the Ticketing booth and also outside the gates.  Managed to catch a staff to asked where I could purchase my Express Pass. She told me that the pass can only be purchased in the theme park once it opens at 10am. I was disappointed as I read previous reviews from here saying that the park will open much earlier than stated. So I waited.....  Up till 8.45am, the ticketing booth and Guest Services was opened. Tried my luck at purchasing the Express Pass from the Guest Services and they directed me to the ticketing booth. True enough, I managed to purchased my Express Pass but I was a little too late. The Express 7 was already sold out in a matter of MINUTES (at 9am)! I only managed to get the Express 5 - it was sufficient as it covers the 1 ride from the Harry Potter world. My timed entry to enter was 12.50pm-1pm.  Overall, the park was really fun! The rides was amazing and thrilling. Food was good - especially the popcorns!  My advice - go early! Grab the Express Pass from Ticketing Booth and go on the rides early to avoid the queues. Do only visit on Weekdays as the crowd was already packed. Cannot imagine what would it be like on weekends.

Get there early, get the express passes. Even though a lot of the rides are in "japanese" I feel that I get what I need. Of course when Harry, Dumbledore and the others talk to me I don't understand, but that did not take away anything from my enjoyment.
Everything is perfect about the theme park. If you only have a limited time for USJ, also buy Express ticket to pass through the waiting line. Harry Potter is included in Express 5 or 7 only.

Extremely crowded even on a weekday! Got there at opening but express passes already sold out. LONG LONG lines for every ride. On the other hand Harry Potter world was magnificent despite being crowded. Definitely go if you are a Harry Potter fan - the ride inside Hogwarts is definitely worth the 2 hour queue!! Had the time of my life!

My love for Harry Potter was the main reason i visit the park. Unfortunately, most Japanese/park visitor came to see the newly opening Harry Potter arenas. It was very crowded in Wizarding World of Harry Potter (WWHP) as it just opened in July 15th so i bet the Japanese were still very excited. We were lining up for every ride, shop or even to buy the famous Butterbeer. It was very time consuming and tiring. Unlike the WWHP, the remaining park was not really crowded so the line was only 15-20 minutes waiting. The best ride was Spiderman. The souvernir shops are great and the staffs were helpful. I love my day in USJ.

I'm not a big fan of amusement parks, but Universal Studios was pretty awesome. I visited on July, the day after the great opening of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. I spend a few hours waiting to get inside Hogwarts, so I walked around Universal Studios for a few hours. There are MANY shops, and they all sell pretty much the same stuff (at a very expensive price), the food is kind off the same (I recommend you to eat outside, or bring something inside...). Hogwarts was AMAZING. I'm not going to let you know any spoilers about the place, since if you visit, everything should be a surprise for you, but believe me: if you love Harry Potter as much as I do: you'll cry. What bothered me the most was that all the dialogues were in Japanese, but it makes sense. It's Osaka, after all! But all the activities are made with British actors who speak Japanese and English. There are good places to take pictures and magic food to eat! :) (as long as you have a lot of money).....  PS: Girls and woman, I recommend you to go to the bathroom near the exit of Hogwarts castle!

Visited in September, got there just after it opened on a Friday but it was still very busy! We opted to buy the 3 ride fast track ticket that allows queue jumps on certain rides, this came in handy alot especially with the queue times on the big rides. BE WARNED THAT HARRY POTTER RIDE GETS STUPIDLY BUSY! I would recommenced to anyone going here just for the Harry Potter experience to head there straight away! If not you have a time slot given to you to let you into the harry potter area! the rides we went on before going there were fun but a little out of date. Jurassic Park was very fun! Food and souvenirs are extremely expensive but we expected this! Harry Potter land is quality but busy beyond belief!

I went to Disney just Sunday before the park is full they stop selling ticket we went back again on Tuesday and it was good. Universal should do the same if the park to so full that people can't walk. Stop selling ticket just don't let us in. Don't take our money

queued for the snoopy ride, took almost 1hour plus, eateries are crowded too, everywhere is queue queue queue, long queue, worth visiting once, but no more second time, though, the wonderland is a plus compared to singapore US
Too many people! waiting in line for over 2 hours. if you visit osaka, don't waste your time here! go someplace else

Visited USJ last year for honeymoon. USJ is one of the must visit places when you visit Osaka. The game and attraction just great, even though its seems outdated, compared to USS. But still having a great time. You need to spend one whole day here, and fascinated with old design buildings and attraction. Please try mango ice cream.

One of the main reasons for the Osaka trip was to visit Harry Potter land in the USJ. While Harry Potter was not a disappointment, the rest of the USJ was. We were there on a rainy Monday thinking that the first day after a weekend should be fairly quite – we were dead wrong. Maybe because it was going to be Halloween in a couple of weeks, the place was “crawling” with university kids dressed-up as zombies and creatures. While it was very fun to watch, the volume of people there put pressure on everything. It was especially bad during lunch time when the restaurants were all jam packed, and it took me closed to an hour just to get a Halloween hotdog! Another unfortunate thing was that we arrived at around 11am and went for Harry Potter land’s timed entry ticket right away. Guess what – our entry time was 7:30 in the evening! We then tried to get timed entry tickets to other attractions such as Spiderman, Transformers, Terminator 2, WaterWorld, etc…, but they were all full for the day. Despaired, we ended-up taking it easy and went to the attractions that did not have long lines: Back to the Future, Backdraft, etc… – the old ones from Hollywood (I think I was on these 30 years ago). The 3 hours leading-up to Harry Potter was more of visiting stores and seating around people-watching. Even Hello Kitty land was full of kids. I was so tired that I didn’t even bother to watch the parade (but had a very nice ice-cream instead). Finally, we entered the Harry Potter land and all the waiting and disparity were all worth it. The Diagonal Alley was great, the School was marvelous, and the Harry Potter ride was good (it took another hour for the line-up though). Unfortunately, it was dark when we entered Harry Potter land, so no nice photos. Here are a few tips if you are going to USJ. 1. Don't go on a Monday 2. Get there as early as possible and then either visit Harry Potter right away or get the timed tickets right away. 3. Lockers are limited in USJ. So don’t try to carry too much if you are not going to get a locker. 4. For the main Harry Potter ride, all bags (even handbags) must be stowed away (they have temporary lockers). However, the place for stowing was narrow and full of people all the time (putting things in and taking things out). Again, try not to bring big bags or you will struck in more line-ups. 5. Food is expensive. Try to bring some snacks yourself if possible. In conclusion, it was worth it. If you are a fan of Harry Potter, what are you waiting for?

We visited USJ as a family of 4 and despite it being busy we had a great day. We loved the fact that they had the Jaws and Back To The Future ride which are no longer in Universal Orlando. Old school but still great rides.  We got our tickets to get into the Harry Potter area at 12pm but the tickets weren't valid until 5pm. It was so busy you even had to queue for ages to get into Filch's Emporium gift shop. We weren't too bothered about rides as we had already been on them in Florida and it's a good job that we weren't as the queues were huge. We did get on the Hippogriff but beware of you are around the 6ft mark. You will have to ride at the front as the bars don't go over your knees on other parts of the ride. It was rather embarrassing as we held the ride up while they sorted us out. My husband and I are both tall so we had to take turns to ride at the front with a child each but it took the staff ages to figure this out!  Snoopy and Hello Kitty were an added bonus and my 7 year old girl loved meeting her. We got some super photos. The gift shops were reasonably priced and even though there was a huge queue for the Harry Potter one you could still get related merchandise in the other gift shops without the wait.  It was such a humid, hot day that we welcomed going into the indoor kids areas as an escape for a couple of hours and the kids had a blast in the large construction and ball areas. The best time to miss the hottest part of the day outside.  We stayed to watch the parade which was still busy but easy to get a good view.

USJ is worth visiting! The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is worth every money you paid for. Just make sure you go at the park an hour before it opens then rush to get free timed entry tickets for the Wizarding World. While waiting, you may visit the other attractions. It's best to visit the other attractions in the afternoon since the waiting time is shorter. Wait for the Magical Starlight Parade before the park's closing. It's worth the wait & its really magical!

It was a enjoyable day out, Perfect for children. I enjoyed myself, There were many shows, many cosplayer dressing up as Movie superhero, Anime character. However the only downside was entrance fee were costly, about 3,600 JPY. The rides were fun and enjoyable but you have to pay additional fee if you want to enter some rides, Harry potter studio and so on. The other downside is the queue and waiting time, It takes average about 40-60 minutes and can take up to 200 minutes waiting time to get on a single ride. They have restaurant and cafe all over the theme park but somewhat costly, typical theme park pricing. Some may will enjoy this, some won't.

Went on a weekend with the children so it was really crowded. Enjoyed looking at so many teens in their halloween costumes, though. Visited the Hello Kitty but was a bit disappointed as i had a high expectation and there really wasnt much in it. Harry Potter is a new attracton so the line is really very long, You have to get a ticket first before you could enter on a scheduled time. Even their food stalls have long queue. Overall, it's a fun place to visit but i think it's best to visit on a weekday to have lesser crowd.

Not the first time there but this time is different. Characters like batman disappeared, but sesame street guys were everywhere. Don't know why!!! All attractions were full of people and waiting time could be up to 220 mins. Express tickets were sold out at 10:30am. Crazy, it was a Monday though!!! The Harry Porter part was good but it's even more crowd. There was a candy shop where the line was forever even at 7pm.

If you're not so great at waiting patiently in line for 90+ minutes for a ride, you may want to reconsider this theme park. What is essentially a queuing simulator probably isn't worth the $70 admission. They over sell tickets and there are lines for everything; toilets, food, shops, other lines. A polite business practice would be to have screens up outside alerting people to line times, so prey can make up their mind on whether they come in and line up or go do something else in Osaka.

After a somewhat disappointing visit to Universal Studios Singapore, I walked in to Universal Studios Japan without much expectations. We arrived an hour before the ticket counters open (they open at 9 a.m., an hour before the theme park opens) and managed to score ourselves the Express Pass 5. Unless you enjoy queuing for up to four hours (applied for Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey & Hollywood Dream when I visited), go early and get the Express Pass. Plus, you wouldn't want to miss having a go at the locals for running into the park when the gate opens. Bewildering, yet so funny.  We went on eight out of all the rides available. I'm a bit of an adrenaline junkie, so for me, they were all just ok. Nothing truly exciting, what more when everything is in Japanese. We find the roller coasters here aren't as fast compared to others we've experienced. Stepping into the Harry Potter world was pretty cool, but I couldn't really take my time and breathe it all in as it was super packed. Best to visit when the hype has died a bit among the locals I guess.  They're plenty of souvenir shops, but don't bother looking for one with "Universal Studios Japan" written on it. We went to the biggest store they have by the entrance, and there was none.  For Muslims who's concerned about a place to pray, we prayed in the nursing room at Hello Kitty. The area beside the vending machines at Snoopy would make a good spot too.

I really like the Harry Potter Land in Universal Studios Japan. I looked forward to it a lot and it did not disappoint me a bit. The ride was fun and innovative. The castle and the town made me go KYAAAAAAAA and crazy about everything that I saw in the movie appeared in real life.  We didn't manage to finish all the rides in USJ. Personally, if I were to give advice, I would highly recommend you to get the express pass. It is not going to be cheap. You need to pay the basic price to enter the park and on top of that, you need to pay an extra amount of money for the express pass.  We went on 31 Oct 2014, and there was Halloween celebration at night as well. Perhaps that was why it was exceptionally crowded? But when we asked a staff, she said it was almost so crowded everyday, even people holding express pass need to wait for 40 mins to an hour for a ride too.  It was really crowded with the locals, not so much of tourists, I feel. Be prepared to queue for everything from entering to the Harry Potter Land to the rides to the souvenir shops to the restaurants, EVERYTHING!  We only managed to take 3 rides with an average of 3 hours waiting time for each of the ride. Although we didn't manage to take all the rides, we still tried our best to walk around the place. The park is huge and nice! I really think it would be worth while to get the express pass.  I definitely need to visit again! <3

We visited the Universal Studios Osaka last May, so sad because the Hogwarts theme park is still closed to the public but we still enjoyed everything in the park. The best rides for me are: Amazing Spiderman, back to the future, and the 3d and 4d rides. Tip to save time, line up in the single rider even though you're a group of 3 or more, just make sure to pretend that you dont know each other ;) but the consequence of it is you'll not sit beside each other.

All the negative reviews seem to be from people who neglected to plan ahead! I went to USJ on a Wednesday and did everything I wanted before 2pm, including Harry Potter! Pre-preparation is a must. I bought my entry ticket the day before at Kansai Airport, then arrived at the park around 8.30 to join the ticket lines in order to buy an Express Pass (only sold at the park or online in Japanese). The lines for tickets were already a few people deep, as were the lines at the gates of people with pre-purchased tickets, even though the park wax not scheduled to opem until 10am! You definitely want to arrive early. The ticket counters opened at 9 and I had my Express Pass 5 after another five minutes. If you want to go to Harry Potter and have the money, I strongly recommend buying either the Express Pass 5 or 7 as these come with an entry time in Harry Potter, and because the entry times are distributed in order of purchase getting an Express Pass means you get in earlier in the day and can miss the worst of the crowds. My entry time was 11, and they opened the gates early at 9.30 because of the huge crowds, so I wandered around the park for a while. This is the time to buy food and do your shopping because everyone literally runs for the Harry Potter tickets! The shops were dead quiet, and the ones at the front of the park have many of the Harry Potter souvenirs (you can try on robes in peace!). I headed over to Harry Potter at around 10.45 and was let in early. And there were minimal lines when I got there! Only Honeydukes was really crowded, but there's nothing special about it unless you really want overpriced souvenir sweets. The Butterbeer line was only a few minutes and with the Express Pass I was on the main HP ride within fifteen minutes (plenty to look at in the line though). This ride was AMAZING - they've really put a lot of effort into it and it is well worth even a 2 hour wait! You don't need 3D glasses like a previous review says, and the seating orientation means that it's like you're on a private ride - you can't see anyone else. I did some shopping (shops were crowded but never had to wait to pay, got lucky!) and by the time I left at 12 it was really packed - lines everywhere! The Express Pass 5 was worth the ¥4700 just to get earlier entry! It also got me onto Hollywood The Dream with no waiting. So my suggestion is get there well before the park opens, and definitely Express Passes. The park was much more crowded in the aftenoon and would only have gotten worse after 3 when the Starlight cheaper entry began, so I left. Money well spent, my only negative comment would be that they need to set a limit to the number of people that can enter the park because it really does get ridiculous, and I was only there until 2! But I felt there were plenty of staff, almost too many!

My daughter loves Universal Studios especially in October. She likes it because in October they have Halloween theme and there was a Zombie performance in the Zombie Zone. She was afraid but she likes it and asked to comeback again in October. While mom and dad loves Harry Potter :D

The park was already full of people even though we arrived before the opening hour! We wanted to get an express 5 or 7 pass but it was sold out before 930! In the end we settled for a day pass plus an express 3. I know that to access the Harry Potter attraction, we had to get an timed entry ticket.  Most people must be at Harry Potter and the roller coasters and we didn't had to queue for the ride at Jurassic Park.  The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was amazing. The snow covered roofs, the castle, Hogsmeade, everything. It was really impressive. You had to queue to visit Ollivanders, buy butter beer, go inside Honeydukes, and the rides. I went to the studio tour in London last year, so I don't mind skipping a few attractions as we also want to have time for other rides.  Hollywood Dreams the Ride, Backdrop is super fun! Although the queue information said the queue would be 140 mins but we only queued for 60 mins and it was our turn!  I happily chose Battery for the Backdrop and had so much fun! My friend found it too scary as you are unable to see what comes next and the lady beside me was screaming all the way and even cried after the ride. As we had the the express pass, we immediately went for the next ride, Hollywood Dreams the ride. I was happy that there is another SMAP song and did not hesitate to choose Amazing Discovery. With the BGM, the backdrop is now my favourite roller-coaster!

It was just no more fun in USJ of spending more than 2-3 hours even 4 hours queuing for 2-3 minutes for rides or attractions. Even tough you spend more money with what-so-called 'Fast pass'. My family say 'No More USJ anymore'.

The wizarding world is a must visit definitely!  The amount of detail they put in decoration and interior and basically everything would make you cry. Even the toilet has Moaning Martyle grumbling about her life. Oh, I feel lucky to visit their toilet. Seriously, every step you took would feel magical.  Do not missed other attraction too, and visit their store. They're worth your money.  And staff, oh my God, how could you not love the staff? They're so nice and warm and willing to make you happy and have a good time. And I'm envious with their costume.

Universal Studios wasn't originally on the itinerary but with a day up our sleeve, we went on our last Sunday in Japan ( mistake). Make sure you go on a weekday.  The wait for most rides were about 30 mins to an hour and later in the day upwards of 2.5 hours, so we didn't get on everything.  Harry Potter ride and Spiderman rides were super and the 3D were the best seen.  Train from central Osaka was very convenient and direct to the door

Harry potter park is the main aim of our visit to the USJ. The decorations were as if they came out from the movie itself. But it was seriously too overcrowded. You cant even move a feet at all inside the shops. Everyone was squeezing and frantically searching for their souvenirs.  But the customer services were excellent. All the staffs were with smiles and they serve with ultimate politeness.  Harry potter ride was the ultimate best and the very best that I had ever ridden.  Would suggest to someone who wasnt a Harry Potter fan to give the park a miss unless they don't mind all the squeezing. Oh, and please book your ticket online way beforehand because admission tickets into the harry potter park is always sold out on that day itself. And you got to have a specific timing to get into the park.

We went on a Thursday end of Nov 2014 which is on a weekday and it was massively crowded especially in the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and area surrounding it. Full of Japanese teenagers some in their school uniform which made me wonder aren't they supposed to be in school on a Thursday morning? The other side of USJ where the Spider-Man Ride, Space Fantasy etc. are, was less crowded. So head there if you want to get away from the crowds.  We managed to buy the 5 express pass at 9.00 am which is an hour before the scheduled opening time. The express pass is a must if you don't want to wait for hours for the rides. So try to get there early to get the pass so that you won't get stressed with all the queuing.  Having said that we managed to get on the Space Fantasy, Jaws and Back to the Future Rides without the express pass with very short wait (under 20 minutes). That was before 11.30 a.m. Perhaps it is because everyone was rushing to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter while we made our way to these rides since with the express pass, we managed to get our time entry to WWOHP only at 11.30  The WWOHP was extremely crowded that it kind of spoilt the experience. The Forbidden Journey ride was great (since we could use the express pass for it) but would have been better if the characters were speaking in English. Harry, Hermione, Dumbledore etc. speaking Japanese is just ... not right. Didn't manage to enjoy other attractions because there were just too many people.  Over all an average experience because of the crowds.

I went there with my parents on a weekday. Arrived as early as 8:15am to avoid the long queue at the ticket counter. I had to wait for another half an hour to get my ticket and another 15 minutes or so to get into the theme park. I bought the express pass 7 to avoid long queue and I did. Most of the attractions had long queue especially the roller coaster ride. The express pass includes a timed entrance to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Although when it was my time, there are still many people there especially at Honeydukes. I suggest to those who have no time to spare to buy the express pass to skip all those long unnecessary queues. 😃

No express passes. Bought our normal passes at the Japan Tourism Board in our country before arriving in Osaka. That was helpful. We arrived at the gate at Universal Studios 45minutes earlier on a Tuesday. There were already throngs of people waiting. Gate opened at 9.50am and we made out way to Harry Potter World. Queued for 15 minutes into the ride. All other rides - Jurassic Park, The Dream (roller coaster ride), Spider Man etc - had moving queues. All under 15 minutes queue time. Lunch was quick too. No long queues. Loved the mid day parade! No issues at all. Glad we didn't buy any express passes. The Japanese were absolutely gracious. Park superbly clean.

Easy to get to on the local train and a great day out. There was enough cool stuff to keep the three of us occupied and the language barrier was no issue. Staff where very helpful with my wife in the wheelchair which they provided from their mobility section. They have a very good queuing process for disabled persons where the give you a place holds and tell you what time to come back to get your equivalent spot in the queue.

We came arrived in the afternoon on a Saturday in November and found the park to be crowded! For those used to being at similar parks in the US, there is a world of difference in terms of how many more people were packed in to this park in Japan.  That being said, we went primarily to go see the Harry Potter world and managed to get tickets. Wait times were around 60 min per ride (some as long as 120min!). One thing to note for overseas visitors - rides are in Japanese.  We had spent the morning at the Aquarium in Osaka before heading over and were able to pay a discounted admission since we arrived after 3PM. The ferry between the aquarium and USJ was very convenient and got us from one to the other in about 15 min.

Visited on Friday, 28 November 2014,the park was opened at 9.30 AM while it was scheduled to be opened at 10 AM, arrived there at 9 AM and found out the fast pass 7 has been sold out. Fortunately fast pass 5 still available. Everything is quite expensive, foods, merchandises, tickets, etc. But the rides, especially WWOHP are fantastic!! Me & my wife spent more than 3 hours just for WWOHP area to stroll arounf the super crowded shops. One thing makes me dissapoint is no english subtitles at all so you don't know what the characters and staffs said (not a problem if you speak japanese). Buying fastpass is a must!!!

Be prepare to spend ALL DAY waiting in lines. DO NOT fall for the Harry Potter castle walking tour near the entrance to the forbidden journey ride - turns out it is literally the queue for forbidden journey, just without the ride at the end. At the end of the day, Hollywood the dream roller coaster makes everything worth it, and remains my favourite roller coaster I have ever been on.

We, 8 of us had a good time in USJ. We went on a Tuesday, in the afternoon after visiting Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan and not as crowded as per previous reviews of other tourists. Entrance fee was 5600 yen per person. Waiting time for each ride was less than 30 minutes. Though it was in Japanese language, we enjoyed the action. The Jaws was very interesting with the commentator's lively action but need to wear rain coat to avoid getting wet. Harry Potter motion master was too drastic for me but for some others, they enjoyed it.

My wife is Japanese and we have a 4 year old and at the time a 3month old. for my sons birthday we took him to USJ. we stayed in the hotel across the road and the room was like a kids playroom, we all slept on one long bed my son loved it. next day we entered the Theme park earlier as we had a special pass from the hotel, my son wanted to see harry potter attraction, we had made a booking for 12:00 but we still took him to have a look at the village.  We stood at the gates of the castle in aww of the magnificent detail. The young girl at the gate asked if we wanted to come in, my son jumped at the chance, they sent us down a side entrance and we finished up in areas not normally accessible to general public and we were alone it was amazing and my son still talks about it. We stayed until the parade and the fireworks and then caught the train home to Kyoto. what a great day, lots to do very friendly staff and children's wonderland is great. Go and enjoy I highly recommend it

The park is a world class park for sure. Super clean, good layout but English is so poorly spoken that it is very frustrating. A simple question like 'what is inside this dish' can be met with a puzzled (yet always smiling) face. And they will continue to speak to you in Japanese even when you speak English, 99% of the time.  Rides/shows are all in Japanese so yeah. Get pumped for 'Backerdrafto' aka Backdraft.  Another flaw is Harry Potter's Kingdom. The main ride's locker system can only be described as abysmal.  Still, it gets a 4/5 for the fun factor. If only they spoke English, it'd be a perfect score.

We went there on a Thursday morning and there are a lot of people queueing up outside. The staff are nice and friendly. Just remember to get a Express pass for the Harry Potter area or you will have to run there to exchange for a free admission ticket.  The Harry Potter ride -- the Forbidden Journey is super fun, but since the ride is quite new so we did not have a chance to play it for a second time unless you queue for another 3 hours (no queueing is needed for an express pass!). The locker area is super crowded, and dun forget to put down your cell phone or it will be fell out during the ride.  The other parts of the park is fun, but no rides are as exciting as the HP ride! The 4D technology is super great and the ride is 99% re-presentation of the setting in the book! The Butterbeer is a bit sweet though.  Great staff in the restaurants and rides!

This is our first trip to a universal park studio theme park. We are there on the 15 Dec 2014. We arrived early at around 9 am as advice. There is already a huge crowd at that hour. Nevertheless Everyone are in waiting in order and patiently for the gate to open. Bought the basic ticket + 5 way express pass as advice. Cost of the ticket + express pass can be very expensive if you travel in a family. It cost us ~ 38 K JPY for a family of 3 which is a hefty sum of money. It would be very frustrating for you if you just buy the basic ticket as the queue can be super long even on weekdays unless you are veteran theme park goer with lots of patient and did all you homework prior to the trip, timed all your rides right down to the spot and run fast ! For family with kids and first trip to universal studio, it won't just work. Express pass is a must ! The popular rides can be as long as > 120 minutes which we saw on the Harry potter ride. Personally I think the 5 way express pass is good enough. Only the 5 express pass and 7 express pass allowed you timed entry to Harry Potter. Harry Potter is definitely the biggest attraction here. When the gate open, there is mad dash to the Harry a potter area. Express Pass by default will allowed you to go for Harry Potter. our ticket had preset time at 11:30 am to enter Harry Potter area ( yes, the place is so crowded that they even limit and time the number of people at the harry potter area) and the ride at from 11:45 to 12. When we reach the Forbidden a Journey ride, the queue for those with basic tickets is already at 150 minutes ! I will never wait that long for a 3 minutes ride! However I can understand why Harry Potter area is such a hit. The area is unbelievable! The buildings and the overall atmosphere is just out of this world. The rides is as good as it get. For those who is prone to dizziness, you may want to give the ride a miss. I am not a Harry porter fan but was pleasantly surprise when I saw the place for the first time. It certainly has a wow factor!  We were at Universal Studio the whole day till 7pm at nite. Had a good time although the weather was very cold that day we are there. it was also very windy. Could not really understand how Japanese teens who seems to be grossly underdressed (I.e. wearing just a sweater or only in school uniform, skirts with bare legs, etc) are able to withstand the freezing temperature ( 0~4 deg C). The rides are ok. My teenage daughter prefer the rides here as compare to Disneyland. For me I think otherwise. As expected, Everything is in Japanese with no subtitles or translation. For the rides, I will think the following would be recommended;  - Harry Potter and forbidden journey ( a must!) - Spider-Man - Jurassic Park - backdraft (not exactly a ride, but interestingly different) - jaws ( average. We prefer the Arica ride better at Disneyland) - back to the future (old. Go if you have time. Otherwise you can skip this)  For shows, - terminator 3 D - shrek 4 D - waterworld  We did not wait for the music show at 7:45 pm as the area around the show are super crowded even 1 hour before the show begin. I have been to Disneyland Tokyo on Christmas Day 2 years ago and even then it does not feel as crowded as Universal Studio.There are queue everywhere even a more than 30 minutes queue for the popular 'dinosaur' turkey drumstick which we saw everyone was chomping down at the Jurassic Park area.  Overall I would say it is a pleasant trip but a bit pricey. Personally I think Tokyo Disneyland is better and more value for money.

To get here by train is not hard, took me less than 15 minutes from JR Osaka station. Always asked the station attendance which platform to go, easier than guessing or stressing yourself out in the already super busy station. From station there would be another 5-10 mins walk to the entrance but shops along the way to distract you  It's not as huge as Disneyland but big enough to spend the whole day here. It's crowded and queues everywhere but I found them to be not as bad as Disney and we had more rides taken. All the presentations were in Japanese, Didn't bother me much, just enjoyed what's to come  It's handy to have the Fastpass as it helped you to cut the queues on popular rides and only FP 7 allowed entry to Harry Potter castle at specified time. Strictly for hardcore fans!!!!! Too crowded and even to enter shops you had to queue or get squeezed. Browsing is out of window unless you wanted to get bumped all the time with constant stream of people behind you. I ended up not doing the HP rides because waiting time was like nearly 2 hours and my children just couldn't put up with the crowds anymore. The butterbeer? Can have it hot or cold, not as good as promoted.  Anyway I'm disappointed that the FP can only be used once per ride not multiple use, after spending so much on the. The least they can do is multiple usage except for Harry Potter  Many eateries and queues not so bad. More suitable for little kiddies too

By far, this was the best amusement park that we've visited in Japan! Words can't describe every experience. I love sharing this moment with my daughter, and glad that we've stayed until closing because they have this amazing Magical Starlight Parade. It also took me 19 years to come to Hogwarts, finally! Don't forget to buy your butterbeer. Too bad the real-life owl was not on sale, haha! Loving my daughter's laugh while enjoying the rides in Sesame Street Plaza. Nostalgic in seeing my childhood cartoon characters come alive as well. Definitely coming back next year because Evangelion in 4D will be released!

Sorry Universal Studios but we were disappointed with our visit. We found the attractions to be dated and eating options were limited. We weren't able to purchase an express pass. They sell out very quickly at opening time so you need to be at the gate when it opens or you can expect long waits at the attractions This theme park is aimed at the Japanese audience. If you're a westerner who doesn't speak Japanese; I'd suggest you visit Universal Studios in the US. .
I have been to Universal Studio Singapore but I enjoyed The wizard world of Harry Potter in USJ more Than USS I feel like I'm entered the real magical world :)

Went there on a rainy day, yet it didn't spoil it for us. This place is great for adults and children, the rides are awesome. Even if you're not going on the rides, the place is great to walk around. Its really well done. Sure the waiting time can be like 2 hours or more. But instead of queuing around, what we did was go look for other things to do while we wait. Then just running back when the gates are opened, and once they are open, the queue despite being long, kept moving. Check be sure that you're ( or you're kid is ) within the height and weight requirements for each rides. They are quite strict about that. I highly recommend this attraction, the rides are the best. Just be aware that some of the rides might be closed depending on the weather of the day.

We booked the admission pass and the express pass through the official and were sent to the hotel (if the total is more than 30,000 yen they will not charge for delivery)  We visited USJ for the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Remember to buy express 5 or express 7 so you don't have to wait in the line to get into the wizarding world, and also it will include a fast pass for the awesome 4D ride. Without the fast pass on the same day you have to wait in the line for 310 mins.

Harry Potter was on the top of our list to visit during our Japan tour. We decided to visit USJ on the New Year Day 2015 since the park opened earlier than usual after the countdown party the previous night. We reached the USJ as the first Sunrise on the new year day.  After entering the park, we immediately went to the Express Pass Counter and found that they were sold out. Then we queued up for the Spiderman Ride which took 80 mins. Realizing that we forgot to get HP’s timed tickets, we immediately went to get them before 9am. The timed tickets we got were for the 2:30pm. By that time, most of the queues for rides were a minimum of 90 minutes. We managed to get on the Back to the Future ride which was a bit old and disappointing. Our Children were able to see the Kitty. That was all the attraction we could access. We had our lunch at the Jurassic Park Restaurant where we had to find tables for ourselves. The foods were tasteless, cold, and expensive. The Turkey drum sticks and the hot dogs at the kiosks were much better tasting.  When we finally entered the Harry Potter area, we found people on almost every square inch of the ground. The queue for the HP ride was 230 minutes and 90 for the Hogwarts Castle walk! The queue to enter the little magic wand shop was 45 minutes. There were also long lines to buy a mug of Butter Beer! There were even long lines for the toilets!  By the time we left HP, it was very cold and windy. Then, it started to snow and our children were very excited to see snow for the first time of their lives. We left the park just before sunset and missed the parade. We figured with all the crowds in the park, we will probably see little comfortably.  Overall, the theme park itself is very good, but the problem is simply it is too crowded.  When we visit USJ again, we will be sure to pre-purchase the express passes and will avoid holiday seasons!

We went to USJ during the new year since it opens its door early at 2 AM. Initially, I tried booking online but was not successful. Based also on the online information, express tickets are already sold out so I know that before hand.  We took the train and luckily, the train we took went straight to the USJ station so we need not change train along the way. We arrived around 3AM and the crowd is already building up. As suggested by others who have gone to the park, we bought foods and water at Watson just beside the subway station. The line at teh cashier is already long so I expected that USJ is already crowded.  A day before that I already purchased my USJ ticket from a Watson store near our hotel(Dai-ni Sunny stone Hotel), I asked assistance from the store clerk to operate the Loppi vending machine, as it turned out, you also need to input a Japanese name, so the store clerk called the Loppi customer service and verified this requirement. So he just typed in a Japanese name sounding like my name ( last name and first name).  As we get near the entrance, the line for ticketing windows is still not that long and since we have our tickets with us already, we skip the windows and went straight to the gate.  Immediately, we grab a map and proceeded to the HP timed entry ticketing machine which is located near the Jaws attraction. USJ staff are waiting to assist you with the time tickets. The available time slot is either 10:20 AM and 10:30 AM, so I choose the 10:30 AM slot.  We then proceeded to the Spiderman ride, the queue time is already listed at 90 minutes. Actual queue time took us more than 60 minutes only. I really enjoyed this 4D ride and for me this is the best ride in the USJ. better than the HP ride.  After this ride, we tried the Back to the Future ride which is really not exciting, the video is like watching an old movie. The queue is around 45 minutes.  Next is the backdraft, this is simlar to the Steven Spielberg act on USS. Since everything is in Japanese, I would rate the USS better than this one. This is just a waste of time. Queuing is around 30 to 45 minutes.  We also tried the Jurrasic Park ride, which I think is better that USS. Then next is Jaws.Nothing to be craved of. Both rides queing time is approximately 30 to 45 minutes.  Finally, we went to HP to try the ride, we enjoyed taking pictures of all the castles. The waiting time is almost 3 hours at 220 minutes. I did not enjoyed the rigde as there were a lot twirling and twisting which make me dizzy and get headache.  Food are really expensive inside the park so if you can bring foods, just bring foods since no one is checking at the gate.  e

Second time here, last time was in 2002! still enjoyable but the only main difference - the crowd! its so much, so much more crowded now ....just queues everywhere. perhaps this is also due to the Harry Potter world than just opened in July 2014.  Harry Potter is a must visit, yes there are waiting lines everywhere from rides to shops but they have recreated the british town so well, the shops and details, the school...its amazing, u feel like u have entered the UK.  The Back to the Future ride is also still at USJ (yay!) for all you 80s fans. And they have this cute mascot called Moppy - part of sesame street that is only here in Japan.  Easily spend a day here - the merchandise and food packaging as usual, irresistible...so still a good visit for all theme park lovers. Only caution, please plan your day well, study the map and show timing and rules, and you will be fine.

Awesome fun. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter alone makes the visit worthwhile!!  The recreated village of Hogsmeade was magical, as was Hogwarts. It would've been fun had there been more "insider" surprises to find, like Moaning Myrtle in the ladies toilets or a basilisk in the men's, but it was absolutely amazing, all the same.  Do note that a timed-entry ticket is required for visiting the Wizarding World. It's a special enclosure within the Universal Park and they try to control the volume of visitors as best they can, so if you don't have one (you may pre-book online) or try for one too late in the day, you'll be put on a special ticket that let's you in by... luck. (Ie. you'll be allowed in if the crowd has thinned as you're waiting.)  The other feature that was my favourite is the Back To The Future ride. It gives you the amazing feeling of riding a roller coaster in a De Lorean, all the while never actually leaving the confines of one room.  As always, the lines for the rides were interminable. Lines were much shorter at the end of the day as opposed to the early hours of the park, but you run the risk of missing out on some of the rides if you start too late in the day. The park closed at 6pm when we were there but they stopped all rides by 5.30pm.  A two-day ticket would be best, if you can afford the time!
Universal studios was Awesome! Harry Potter world was the best, the rides were fun and meeting the characters was cool. you have to go on the spiderman ride!
N o t h i n g! The Park is amazing. Great people. Very Accessible and the Universal City Walk is something you might not like to miss

Actually my last visit to this great theme park was on September 2013, my primary purpose is to taste the thrill of the rides that not available anymore in The US nor in the Singapore. When I have a little freetime I came here for the Back To The Future Ride and The Jaws Ride, both are classic rides that still available in this park. The park is very good, big and high tech. My suggestion is if you want to try all the rides better using the fast pass, because the que is stunning, takes you very long to wait. It's natural, that's the sign of a fantastic ride. Better to spare a whole day long to spent your time in here. Going there is really easy with the Osaka's world class rail system, one of the best for in the world for me. The rides are fantastic, but the best thing you should keep mind, everything here mostly using the Japanese Language.

Definitely worth a visit if you enjoy theme parks but I would strongly recommend that you book tickets for the fast pass before hand. We had to wait 30 minuets in line to gain admission and we arrived right at 10am. When we reached the ticket counter the 7 pack fast pass was sold out. I would also suggest going straight to the Harry Potter ticket booth to get a ticket for the staggered entrance into the world.

friendly staff, clean and super fun park. food is a bit pricy but lots choices to choose from. go first to Harry Potter ride otherwise you wait forever. be an early bird and git on when the park opens and straight to Harry Potter ride. my favourite actually was Jurassic Park
It took me the whole day here at Hogwartz area. Wonderful! and after 6pm, you dont need to wait for more than 10 minutes for almost everything. (spiderman, back to the future and so on...)
Harry Potter land is a must visit though the queue can go up to 3 hours. Ticket is very expensive considering you have to purchase separate universal pass to expedite entrance to some attractions
a must see but my one comment is there are no english translation of the featured rides and events. go to singapore instead.
Very well maintained but very crowded, especially Harry Potter Land. Not a lot of restaurant are opened for dinner.
I went there with family on October 2014. Great place to have fun, however too much crowds. Hardly can play all the games there.

I love USJ - we went on a weekday and it was still very crowded. If you don't want to wait in queues (it could be more than 180 minutes if you want to go on the Harry Potter ride), invest in an Express 5 or 7 pass - both will give you access to the Harry Potter area at a set time and the Harry Potter ride (the one inside the castle).  PS. The Harry Potter ride is AMAZING and is rated No. 1 dark ride in the world!

Universal Japan is fabulous, and the the opening of Harry Potter it got fabulouser ... been there many times, love more each time I go!  (And by the way, it is one of the most handicap accessible places in all of Japan ...)

Went with kids aged 8, 12 & 13. Older ones loved Harry Potter. Youngest one found the chair ride a tad too thrilling. He was quite pale after the ride, though he insisted it was not scary.  Reserved the spiderman ride at the end, as we heard it is one of the last to close. But got quite stuck as the main roads were closed at night for the night show. Had to find alternate routes to get to the spiderman ride!  Did not have time for a nice sit-down meal, so had a huge turkey leg with beer (not for the kids of cos). Enjoyed ourselves very much.

i've been in disneyland in america 30 years ago. this studio is not big developed compairing with disneyland of that time. also, facilities are not more and not much decorated as dreamland. it's failed for children for dream and for adults for rests. just a plain playpark. we enjoyed harry porter journey and bought frog and jelly beans and drank butter bear. we entered toilet and saw everything was the same as in the movie, we worried hand would come up from the commodor. terminator 4d was great, too. actors moved in and out of the screen. we wanted to see shrek 4d, but closed. we bought 7 express ticket but 2 facilities were not worked. padade was cancelled, and woody woodpecker only walked around for taking picture with children. little and small and poor facilites and their poor minds.

This is the 2nd universal studio I ever visit. Due to Osaka weather, queuing for entrance are not as hot as Singapore. The park also bigger, if budget enough, this is better universal studio to visit. Harry Porter just open July 2014, the queue for it are 240 mins for morning, 150 mins during the evening. People are discipline so it doesn't make the queue as tired as some other country. The part are clean, food are not bad. If you are planning to buy the express ticket, you need to buy earlier, don't expect to get it on the same day.

We went to Universal studio at Japanese New Year so there were lots and lots visitors. The advise to visit there is to avoid holiday so that you can enjoy the facilities. However, this place is nice, and we like "the Wizard World of Harry Porter".

We went there on a weekday in February, it opened from 10.00-18.00, queues were long, 60 to 200 minutes wait for popular rides, really not enough time for all rides on one day although we´ve bought express pass. We all had so much fun, The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was so exceptionally well-done that it was probably our favorite area. Some rides were closed for maintenance such as Jaws, Sherk 4D. Do check it and plan well before you go or spend two days there, then you may explore everything.

I wonder whether every Japanese teen has better place to go or all of them have the annual pass?  First day i reached there at 1pm and 2nd day 10am. Express pass sold out! I cant help but queue everywhere for shows n rides. 1st day only got to play harry porter ride first coz queue for 170 min to give way to express pass holders. Then spiderman and space fantasy.  2nd day was saturday, sea of people, mostly japanese teens. Also got to play 5 rides only. Anyway just enjoyed ourselves strolling in USJ. Regret that i didnt take photo with hello kitty coz rush to another show. Phobia taking photo with the characters as they kept playing with kids instead of focusing on taking photo with us. Hello! We dont have plenty of time to kill, we need to queue everywhere! Waste of time waiting to take photo, especially hate the yellow sesame the most.  USJ made us standing for about 10 to 15 min for introduction to some 4d shows. End up clueless and more confused as in Japanese language, no translation. Also very disappointed that jaws and shrek were closed for no reason. Ops, general reason: close for maintenance. I wonder the maintenance workers are there for 2 days.

If you've done Universal Studio in LA, then it's pretty much exactly the same stuff. I went there with my daughters (12 & 9) and we had a great day, despite the Christmas cold ! The attractions are nice, though a bit outdated for nowadays teenager (Jaws, Back to the Future, Backdraft, Jurassic Park, Water world)... None of these movies triggered any memories for my kids though Jurassic Park will soon ! The biggest draw was of course "The wizarding world of Harry Potter" with a fairly nice re-creation of the movie atmosphere, though thoroughly over-commercial of course. Luckily we had purchased priority access tickets but gave access to the attraction in very fast lanes at appointed times but unfortunately, the area was so overcrowded that it took away most of the "magic"... Be ready for crowds, big crowds, huge crowds but very orderly in a typical Japanese way and if you don't mind too much, you should have a most enjoyable day !
very near universal city mrt station lots of restaurants cool globe with fog or mist effect lots of kids very cold and windy in march since its 7 degrees celsius

If you like theme parks, you'll love it! was worth the ticket price! stay for the light show after dark and make sure you try and get all the big rides! Jaws, Jurassic park, back to the future are all incredible! As someone who grew up loving harry potter, seeing Hogwarts in the distance made me teer up. and the wizarding world of hp was one of my favorite things to see! though it was incredibly crowded the castle and the butter-beer were all you need to feel like you've run into hogsmede village. Cant wait to go back!

Worth it only for Harry Potter World  Express passes were sold out before the day I went. You can buy them online - just not on the English version site. There are tutorials online, and some travel agency's can purchase for you. It's a must if you plan on going on any rides.  The rides are pretty basic - make sure when visiting Harry Potter you go on the castle tour. The entrance is very close to the forbidden journey ride and is easily missed. Wait time today was 300 mins...  The park isn't set up for non Japanese speakers - and it's not a typical tourist attraction, as its still mostly locals. Everyone was nice as always.  If you're looking for rides - don't come here.  But a must for any Harry Potter fan.

Universal studios Japan was amazing. the entrance from the Station is awesome with tons of shops and lights. Inside the park was PACKED at some instances it was very had to walk but this was to be expected. If your going there hoping for Thrilling roller coasters don't go. There are a few scattered around but only a few were good. The park it self is very nice lots to look at and experience. There was the Universal cool japan exhibitions for attack on titan and Neon Genesis plus more which were cool.  The Park Has very limited english sometimes you will luck out and get a staff member who speaks good english otherwise most just have a very small amount. But you are in Japan so you should have learned some basic's before getting here. otherwise just keep a phrasebook on you and you will survive.  Lines in the park can be good some days with about a 1 hour wait on rides and also bad days with 5 hour waits on rides. we chose a bad day with 5 hour waits on all the big attractions but luckily we had gone online and Pre booked our entry tickets and express passes to a few rides. so on arrival we walked straight past the GIGANTIC hoard of people trying to purchase tickets and once inside at our pre selected times walked straight past people who had been waiting hours.  Some notable attractions for us were the Harry Potter ride, hollywood roller coaster, Attack on Titan exhibition. we actually had the 4-D Evangelion movie break down just before the end (it wasn't that great) but for the disturbance the staff gave everyone a free Express pass valid for one ride which was great!  PRE PURCHASE YOUR TICKETS AND EXPRESS PASSES through the universal studios Japan website. It's not easy but can be done with patience, some guessing and Help from Google Chrome's auto translate feature. (took us about an hour) but easily worth it.  Do that and you'll have a great Day otherwise just show up and hope for the best.
Large, entertaining theme park with lots of rides. We used the fast pass but yet couldn't experience more than half the rides. Best ride was the Hollywood dream... if you dare

It was winter when we hit Japan for the first time. And Osaka was remarkably cold when we visit Universal Studios in Osaka. I believe this USJ is excitingly different because of the Harry Potter attraction (though there's already HP in US now). In fact, we went to Osaka just to see the Harry Potter attraction! And we were not disappointed. The Forbidden Journey was amazing due to the hologram technology that they used which makes the flying ride seem so real! When you ride the coaster, you feel like playing the Quidditch game with Harry Potter and friends! USJ is surely a not-miss spot when you go to Japan, especially in Osaka. You better get there early in the morning so you get to see other exciting attractions like The Evangelion. The park closes at 8pm which is odd to tourists like us, coz most of the US closes at 9pm or 10pm. We brought home the Harry Potter's wand as a souvenir, which you should not miss when you go there. Souvenirs are expensive, as expected. But there will always be something you will surely bring home as a remembrance together with happy memories during your USJ visit.
Without understanding Japanese and without a fast pass this amusement park isn't very amusing. It's just an overpriced shopping mall with a lot of food stalls. Good churritos though

This was one of the first few places for my trip to Osaka. I didn't have high hopes at first and I thought the place would be similar to the one in Singapore. However, I found out it is a wonderful and magical place at the end of the day. Everyone works with a big smile on their face and provides friendly yet professional services. There wasn't a lot of mascot but every each of them are really in their characteristics. They didn't just stand there and wait for people to take photos but greet and approach nearby people, and even play London bridge with kids. This made me feel magical and fantasy of the theme park. The night parade also very good. One of the downside is the food they serve. The taste really hmmmmm Another thing is the staff doesn't understand English well and all the explanations are in Japanese. I'm like thanks god I know Japanese. One day is enough if you have a express pass or the queue will be crazy. I bought Express Pass 7 online and it sold out the day before. Be fast if you need an express pass.

My partner and I went as part of our Japan holiday. We went in off season so wasn't as busy as it could have been but still packed! Our only advice is to get express lane passes which you pre book (your hotel should be able to help you) as some lines have up to 5 hour wait times!! Which is crazy! The best ride is the Harry Potter one and don't forget to go to the three broomsticks for a meal and butter beer!

We have been travelling in Japan for 4 weeks. We have saw many different things. But one of the best things was our visit to Universal Studios in Osaka. Buying the ticket took some time. It was'nt that efficient. But once in the parc. As the world of Harry Potter was very popular, we had to get a time ticket. This ticket could we get in the area of Jaws. And well, if we are there, than why not get on the ride. Jaws was fun. The ride itself was alright, but what made a positive difference was the actress and the Japanese. The time ticket will get you access to Harry Potter world on a specific time. I do believe that you should leave after one or two hours, but not sure about this. And this was defenitly not checked. If you go there, please try some butterbeer. I loved it, would like to get the recipe. But my husband did not like it at all.  A very handy thing to know when going to Universal Studios are the concept of single lines. If you really want to sit in the ride next to the person you are visiting the parc, than you should not go in these lines. But if it does not really matter to you if you sit next to eachother, or not, than the single-line might be super handy. They fill up empty seats on a ride with people in the single line. Not all employees understand the single lines, or perhaps they think those tourist don't understand the single lines. So we could sit togehter very often, while waiting a lot shorter, without doing anything illegal.  The coolest ride was stardancer. But spiderman was also very nice. Terminator can be skipped.
I had so much fun! I felt like I was 10 years old again! You would see people wearing costumes and it is so cute. I wish I could have more than a day in USJ.

Unlike in Los Angeles and Florida, Universal Osaka is compact yet full of excitement and surprises. I suggest to get a timed entry upon arrival at the Harry Potter. We arrived an little after 10am yet we were able to Get in around 530pm (weekday). Rides will take around 240-280 minutes. There is also queues to get the famous "Butter Beer"( which I feel expensive), sweets and souvenir shops. As for the Other rides, queues are also long (60-200 minutes depending on the ride). Since we are the adventurous type, we queued in Hollywood Dream, a fast thrilling rollercoaster ride. It took us 180 minutes to get in. The famous Jaws, Back Draft, Terminator and Spider Man had queues from 60-180 minutes as well. Sadly, I did not understand anything since they speak inJapanese language (they shuld put english subtitle). Another famous attraction is "The Jurassic Park" which is also a timed entry. It will take you 15-20 minutes to queue once you enter. We were not able to watch any shows as queuing up in the rides are time consuming. As a general, I suggest to be early to beat the crowd, get time entry for both Jurassic Park and Harry Potter, go on a weekday and line up in Single Lane. An added Info, it's cold in Universal especially In the evening, bring scarfs and extra jacket . The price of the ticket around ¥7000 or $55-60 half the price for children 11yars and below.

Thanks to TripAdvisor I got plenty of tips on planning my USJ trip now it's my turn to return the favor. First of all when you arrived at Kansai Airport asked for the Tourist Ticketing Booth and make sure to purchase your USJ ticket there where you can avail the ticket in discounted price and you also avoid the looong looong queuing of line for entrance ticket in USJ (promise you'll thank me for this!).  Inside the park the first thing to do is to go straight The Wizarding World of Harry Potter to get your Free Timed Entry Tickets since this ticket is limited you better secure one for yourself since this is the main attraction in the park. While waiting for our turn to visit Hogwarts we lined up first for the best ride I've read here which is Spider-Man and it was indeed the best we had blast and enjoyed the ride so much!  At the Wizarding World of Harry Potter you will really feel the magical vibe and all HP fanatic will surely enjoy this place like a paradise where your imagination after reading the books or watching the movies comes alive right there. Btw a butterbeer is a must try, a visit to Hogsmeade is not complete without trying this one.  Overall, we didn't get the chance to try all attractions there but still so happy and say that our trip is worth it coz we're able to do and try all the best attractions that I've listed and plan to visit in USJ. Also, bring snacks and games with you since all the attractions in USJ requires a minimum of hour waiting, it's the best time for you to enjoy your snacks or games while waiting.

The place is great but to enjoy every single bit of it, get the express pass ahead of time...they get sold out easily. How do you get hold of the pass? Go to the USJ Japanese website and use google translate to be able to understand and buy your pass.  If you weren't able to get the pass, here are some tips: 1. Go early. 2. When you get there, immediately go to all time ticket booths/lines (Harry Potter, The Real, Jurassic Park). When all timed tickets are out, they do not let people enter already. And yes, you don't just line up for the rides, you line up for the tickets as well. 3. Try using the "Singles" lane for shorter waiting times. I'd say sacrifice staying together as a group than sacrificing your legs and your time.  Overall, if it was my first Universal Studios visit, I'd be disappointed but since I have rode other rides in other countries, I just got enough time to do the new rides, so I still had a great time.

Great day out! Went in April 2015, with a little rain but did not take away from the experience at all.  Arrived 1 hour before gates open to buy tickets. Recommend buying an express pass as we ripped through all the rides by 1pm.  Great atmosphere, fun attractions, great day out.

This theme park is comparable to the one in Hollywood, if not more interesting. Even the City Walk was impressive with lots of interesting shops and retaurants. Since my family have been to Universal Studios Hollywood and Singapore, we went straight to the areas we haven't seen yet. First was the Wizarding World of Harry Potter which was very impressive. It was the most crowded place in the park though and you need a timed pass to get in the area. The pass is free and can be easily obtained near the entrance of the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The main ride in the area had a long line and had a locker area where you are required to put all your belongings in. It was chaotic in the area and you might waste a bit of time trying to find an empty locker and loading your stuff in so if you have companions who are not riding, it would be better to leave all your belongings with them so you can go straight to the ride. If you are planning to purchase Hary Potter items, you should buy them before you exit the area since you won't find them anywhere else in the park. The stores were crowded even on a Thursday. This was the highlight of our visit but we also enjoyed the Spiderman ride, and even the cute kiddie area where Hello Kitty, Snoopy, and Elmo was.

Going there mainly for the Harry Potter part but the rest of the USJ are still awesome! We didn't get the express pass but the longest queuing time is less than an hour (for the Flight of Hippogriff). I arrived at the entrance 45mins before it opens and there already many people waiting. It will open about 15 mins early for early birds. Run straight to Hogsmeade for the forbidden journey then you can play straight away. Lunch at three broomsticks were quite pricy but were expected for a theme park. Went back to Hogsmedade just before it closed and no one was waiting for the forbidden journey. Hogesmeade is even better after dark. Apart from the Harry Potter part, there is a space ride that's really fun. The best ride of all is the backdrop of the Hollywood Dream. It has such great view and going backward is just so much fun!! Had a really great day at USJ, definitely recommend going!!

In terms of attractions, if not for the harry potter, the Universal Studios Singapore is definitely better (never been to the US or Paris studios), I'm particularly dissapointed with the Spiderman ride. Harry Potter makes all the difference though, they did a very good job replicating Hogwarts and the stores, the merchandises also looks good (abit overpriced but if you're a fan...). I like the ambience of the HP attractions, from the moment I entered it, it's like I'm in the movie. The HP ride makes it even better, it's definitely the best attraction I've ever ridden on a themepark (even bested transformers in USS), you definitely have to come for the Harry Potter experience alone. Oh and the queue was not as bad as I thought, maybe because everyone flock to the HP attractions or because I went on a weekday,

My expectations were exceeded in this wonderful theme park! I must compliment 5 star for their excellent crowd management, queues didn't feel that long as they let you enjoy some edutainment while you are queuing. As far as the attractions are concerned, each Universal Studios around the world isn't identical, but Osaka has Hogwarts School of Witchcraft & Wizardry from the sequel Harry Potter- its a hit here! Proved to be the highlight of our trip too! Roller coaster ride will give you more adrenalin thrills if Harry Porter didn't work for you. Souvenirs are plenty and most are made in Japan! Restaurants' food quality is acceptable and if you're fussy, the Hard Rock Cafe is just outside the park on your way out! This place to be is an assurance of your money's worth!

I have planed to go to universal studio as I love Harry potter and can't wait to see what's inside. I have bought an express tickets before hand and the attractions in the Harry potter are included which is awesome. It saves so much time as the lining time was 130 mins. The day I went was heavy raining...which was not good as I was very wet but on the other hand the park was not crowded as usual. Rides must try are Harry potter and the roller coaster ride called backdrop which rides backwards and you will not see anything! I have a great day and can't wait to go back again already!

I have been to Universal Studios in Osaka 3 times and all those times haven't been on all of the rides due to the very long lines (perhaps it's the time I chose to go) and compared to places like DisneyLand USA (LA), it doesn't really impress me that much, I only went again and again because of my soon.
