Food wasn't that impressive either and due perhaps to the language limitations, didn't really understand what the workers would be explaining to me when I asked them a question about something. All in all I wouldn't go again to be honest, quite boring for me.
Had a great time with family and friends! Enjoyed the rides and place... but unfortunately, it closed too early.

i've come on wrong date..huaa...its Japanese school holiday..i need to queue almost 4 hours to ride roller coaster... pls check their school/public holiday or else u will not get ride/enter all the park 😢😢

It seem I went at the wrong timing. It was so full of children. I Arrive right on opening time according to their english webpage. But apparently it was opened earlier and all express pass was sold out. And the result is we have to queue for every single thing. Manage to see the spidey show (great show, loooooonnnnggg queue), Back to the future (great show), Terminator (bit boring, bit sleepy during the movie part). And since their english brochure is so simple, we almost missed our Harry potter area visit because apparently it need seperate just to get in the area. You dont have to pay for it. But you have to scan your entrance ticket to some machine in the middle of the park and get your special ticket in certain times. We arrive since the morning, but only manage to scan it at afternoon when we got rejected to enter Harry potter area. But enter the area at the night is quite magical. Dont expect to enter the first store where the sell all the Harry potter food. It was so crowded and jammed. But you can always try other store. Didnt manage to enter the hogwarts or take the ride. The queue is 4 hours long according to their sign. But we do shop alot in Harry Potter area. Can not find too many characters walking around to take picture with you. And apparently in japanese you dont queue to take picture with the character. Bit confusing since they even queuing to but some popcorn. But it seem like people just gather around the character, adoring them and whoever feels like it, can just grab them and take picture with them. Bit chaos for me.  Maybe if I am come at some other nicer time the experience could be nicer.

We visited Universal on the last Monday of March (considered peak season) and it was packed. Upon entering the park (9:30am), we made a b-line to get our timed entry tickets for the Wizarding World of Harry Potter (return window of 4:30-5:30pm). By noon, queues for Jurassic Park, Spiderman, and HP: the Forbidden Journey were 240+ minutes long. Restaurants were also very busy, with queues upwards of 30 minutes. With all that said, there was still fun to be had in Universal. The smaller attractions had reasonable wait times and there were still a lot of interesting things to see. We enjoyed our day at Universal Osaka, but we also knew we weren’t getting the full experience.  Some high-season park tips: It is packed, crowded, and there are lines for everything. If seeing all the major attractions is important, don’t go without an Express Pass. Before doing anything in the park, get a timed entry ticket for WWOHP as they sell out fast. Outside food is not supposed to be allowed in the park but no one seemed to care about our snacks. The coffee we bought was terrible, avoid at all costs. All the attractions are exclusively in Japanese.  Some park info: To get into the park, you need a Studio Pass. In addition, you can buy one of three Express Passes (3, 5, or a 7 ride Express Pass) which allow you to wait in the drastically shorter Express queues at designated attractions. Seems that Express passes sell out days in advance so make sure to reserve them early – we learned this the hard way. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is an area inside the park that requires a timed entry ticket to enter. If you buy the 5 or 7 ride express pass, the timed entry ticket is included (you also get to choose what time you’d like to enter WWOHP). Otherwise, you will need to get a free timed entry ticket from the machines inside the park (which should be one of the first things you do upon entering the park). These tickets allow you to enter WWOHP- once inside, you will still have to queue for all of the attractions.

Having only a short time in Osaka, we purchased our tickets in advance at the hotel to avoid the entry queues. We also got the Universal passes to make lining up not too time consuming. That's the advantage when you do your homework and learn the idiosyncracies of any theme park. Since our time to go into the Harry Potter park was still after lunch, we had time to go around the other places, eat caramel popcorn and ride the Spiderman ride. When we finally got to enter the Harry Potter park, it felt as if we were in a different world! Our sons lined up right away for the HP ride which we heard was a dizzying one but most enjoyable one, while we parents enjoyed a mug of ButterBeer along with chocolate frogs and everyflavor jelly beans. What my kids were most excited about though, was getting their own magic wands and wasted no time twirling it around and casting their "spells"! A magical day indeed, albeit a short one! With a promise to return for a longer time, we left the park to catch our train as it still was a long way off to our hotel.

Being a fairly large non-guided tour of a country with very few locals able to fluently speak english, it was surprisingly easy to get around and enjoy Japan, and UNIVERSAL STUDIOS JAPAN (USJ).  It was 2 in-station train transfers and a short walk away. English speaking information officers are present at the station exit and were EXTREMELY helpful, accurate and thorough.  USJ was very very very clean. ALL Park staff were SUPER POLITE and always HELPFUL. Food is a little more expensive inside the park but not exorbitantly so.  As for the attractions, Jaws, Jurrasic Park and back to the future are a little dated but still fun for my kids. The HARRY POTTER area was superb! Butter beer was the best!  If you don't mind hearing all the rides in Japanese and don't mind waiting in line a bit, this is worth going to. Not very Japanese, but fun to visit anyway.  My family got express passes and this was so worth the time saved from lining up.  Better than Universal Studios Singapore because of the cooler weather and the EXTREMELY POLITE park staff.
No rides, people skipping queues everywhere and compared to Orlando, Florida, a very poor experience.

Of course Universal Studios is beautiful, clean and bright to match your fantasy, and that's where it all stops. Waiting 2 and 3 hours to go on a ride leaves little time to do anything. Unfortunately we didn't know about the internal tickets to get a time to go to Harry Potter had we had realised it might have made the day especially with two children. If you don't speak or understand Japanese don't line up for the theatre shows. There are far more Japanese supporting this business than overseas tourist so save your time and see something else.

I've visited 2 Universal Studios. One in Singapore and this one in Japan. I prefer the weather here. There are a lot of attractions and rides here, to describe each and every single one I've visited is impossible. The Hogwarts School Castle and area surrounding it makes me feel like I'm in the movie itself. What i didn't like about this USJ is that it is hard to find fridge magnets with USJ logo on it, since I'm a FM collector, I find it little bit disappointing.

if you are in Osaka, you really should spend the day there. Visiting Harry Potter World was my highlight. I learned I am not a fan of butter beer but, hey, I tried it.  The shops and restaurants at the City Walk are great too.  There are several new hotels right there at the City Walk and the train station. Yes, there is a station right there, it's: Universalcity

This place is always going to be busy, no matter when you go. I've been twice at different times of the year, and I've always had big waits for the big attractions.  If you're interested on going on a few rides, check out the pass available from the front desk. You have to pay an extra fee, but you'll be able to skip the lines for certain rides. Make it your first port of call to get a timed ticket for Harry Potter world. You want to get in there early, as this place gets really busy.  There are some shows happening during the day, which is a nice break from waiting in lines for attractions. Many of these will happen on the street seemingly randomly. Throughout the year, the park also changes themes - Halloween theme and Christmas theme. They'll put on some themed shows during this time and some of the themes of the attractions may change. Eg: A halloween themed restaurant will be open only throughout the time of the Halloween campaign.  The park is really well looked after and the attractions are not at all run down. It's a great day out to escape and become a kid again.

If you are in Osaka then Universal studio is must . Veg burger at Hard Rock Cafe is must (i loved it ) . harry potter , spiderman and a lot to enjoy for kids its a dream come true . do try dinner at USJ(theme park restaurent ) .

For theme park addicts, this is a must visit. They opened Harry Potter attraction but we did not even attempt to go anymore, the crowd was just huge. The other attractions also had 2 hour waiting time. But for little kids like my girls, the play areas in Snoopy, Hello Kitty and Sesame Street were enough to keep them busy. We were able to take pictures with Snoopy and Lucy. We went there around end of March and to our delight, Easter decorations were already up!!! Sadly, we did not stay to catch the parade anymore. There are stores and restos outside the park which are fun to visit too. If you have the budget and have little kids, I would advise that you stay overnight at one of the hotels. I would also like to commend the first aid station staff... my daughter had a wooden splint (we think she got it from a chopstick when we had breakfast, not in USS Osaka), the nurse helped us pulled it out in just a few minutes.

Early 20's daughters decided as we were in Kyoto a 40 minute train ride via Osaka to Universal would be a good idea to spend an afternoon. The five hours there was not enough time and if you go make sure you have a fill day, particularly with the waiting times for some of the attractions. If you go on the "Back to the Future" ride be prepared to be thrown all over the place!

We went to USJ on a Sunday. We were ready for the long lines but we didnt expect to be on line for 2 hours for Harry Potter ride, same with the roller coaster rides. The long lines took the fun out of the rides. On a positive note, we loved the banana flavored popcorn near the Minion area. And my kids seem not to mind the lines and still had a great time.

We never expect that there are more crowded at early morning. We queue up for the rides more than 2 hours. Not worthy to wait. It drain your time and energy. The best theme is Harry Potter. But the rides is too long to wait. No choice to walk around and enjoy it! :)

We stayed in Osaka an extra day to visit the US Japan. It was nothing special. The lines are huge, and it was a midweek day. I could only imagine what's on weekends. For Harry Potter, which is a new attraction, the waiting time was over 3 hrs. Luckily we managed at the end of a day to visit it with around 1 hour waiting. Among others, the Superman is great. Other attractions, old and already seen, specially the Jaws and Jurassic Park. There was some Japanese cartoon character attraction with long waiting time, later reduced, but total waste of time. The fast pass tickets cost around the double, and are quickly sold out (although I wouldn't buy them). So, if you don't have time to go to the US don't regret.

To avoid queuing up for a long time, we bought entrance tickets+fast pass online (only Japanese version available) and got a QR code. Just needed to show the QR code in entrance. Fast pass 5/7 guarantees you to get inside Harry Potter land without queuing tickets on that day and allows you to play Harry Potter ride inside the castle. The ride was extremely good. Can choose up to 4/6 games with fast track other than Harry Potter. Recommend buying fast pass to save time and guarantee getting into Harry Potter land. Otherwise may need to queue up for a long time for each game. fast pass also a bit pricey but I think it worths.

Upon waiting in line at another theme park for 3 hours to go on 1 ride, then we made the decision to buy the Express pass. Yes it does cost extra, but with that the most we waited in line was maybe 10 minutes, and managed to go on nearly every ride there throughout the day. Because you can only use the pass for certain rides, compare each first before deciding on what ride you want to line-up regularly for. They are very thorough in updating wait times so it does help in prioritising. Nice day overall.

The Wizarding world of Harry Potter was awesome, especially for Harry Potter fans. It is crazy busy so arrive early and get your tickets as soon as you arrive so you don't have to wait for too long. We were really lucky, we went to the machines, got our tickets and were able entry to the park 5 minutes after we got our tickets. Yes you will need to get extra tickets but they are free, they can take hours to get access when it's busy but the tickets will say what time to come back.  The castle was super cool! You can walk through or you can take the ride through. It's also a fabulous place to hide from the rain.  There are plenty of cool shops straight from the movies where you can buy souvenirs.  Olivanders was amazing and you can go in and watch a 'show', exactly like in he movie. The choose one child to give a wand too. The wizard speaks both English and Japanese which is really helpful!  The rest of the park was ok. The minion shop was cool and there were amazing minion baos to eat!  There were plenty of Sesame Street characters, Hello Kitty, minions and more to take photos with but some are really cheeky and hid from the camera which was very frustrating!  All in all though, a good day even for big kids!

We went during the golden week but was surprised that the park is not over-crowded. We bought tickets at the airport upon arrival but didn't get the fast pass tickets because no sched for hpw is available. Got at the park super early 730am and gates opened an hour later. People are literally running towards the hp world ahead of us and we got worried we cant enter hpw but another surprise came when no timed tickets were issued at that time and all gained entry. We entered the hp and the forbidden journey first in no time at all. Park is super clean and attractions are all excellent even parents like us enjoyed. We ate earlier than usual so its comfortable with all the available seats around. Jurassic park needs a timed entry ticket but only a short waiting time and this ride is a winner next to harry potter. We didnt wait for the magical parade to avoid long queue for the train.

I can say that this place is quite big and 1 day seems not enough. So many attractions and it's a quite crowded. My fave one is Harry Potter area. You can buy ButterBeer with reasonable price and take home the cute Mug, found Harry Potter merchandise, send Postcard to your friends and enjoy the attractions provided. Not only that, you can enjoy interesting attractions at Jaws, Jurrasic Park, Water World, Back to The Future, etc. And for those with small children you can take a look cute Hello Kitty, Snoopy or Universal Wonderland area. I really recommend this place for those who visit Osaka.

I'm a big fan of theme parks but I'm also the kind of traveler that would prioritize heritage sites/cultural spots/food hubs. Given the many beautiful sites in Kyoto and Osaka, it's a huge sacrifice to devote 1 day in USJ out of our 8-day trip. But the huge Harry Potter fan in me can't let this chance pass also.  Thus, we came up with this plan that worked for us: Arrive very early (before 9am) at USJ; purchase tickets and the Universal Express Pass 5 for the Harry Potter access (expensive but given you save a lot of time, not a bad deal); take train to Dotonbori for some touring, great dining and shopping; return to USJ and enter theme park at 4 PM, shopped items stored at a locker; use Express Pass in all the rides.  We got to enjoy all the rides that we wanted and lingered at the Wizarding World of Harry Potter in 4 hours and had a great time.
It is an enjoyable park. Love the rides and food. The Harry potter ride was the best. It seemed like you were flying and being a cast of the acclaimed movie/novel.

We went during Golden week and weren't quick enough for the express pass. The park said it opened at 9am so we got there just before 8am and already it was packed. They started letting people in at 8am which was great so we ran to the roller coated ride first, but in hindsight should of form to HP to avoid long lines later. We managed to wait in normal line and only waited on average about an hour a ride. We did do the timed entry to Jurassic Park which was great and only waited about 5mins, we got into HP with a timed entry and wondered around was packed but fun. Had a great meal at the Three Broomsticks which was great value, food and service. We didn't do the HP ride as it was a 3hr wait so that was a disappointment. We didn't know about getting tickets for timed entry so next time I would do more investigating. We did lose our camera and have tried calling toll free number with no luck (a recording) and I can't find an email....can anyone help? We are now back in Australia so desperate to make contact.

We arrived around 8:30pm was good enough time got to do most rides we liked Harry Potter the most space ride was pretty cool I'd purchase express tickets unless you want to be waiting amongst the crowds of people heaps fun walking straight past them people just run fast for no reason whatsoever when the gates open between 9:00am and 9:30pm don't know why some were let in earlier than others that was annoying and rude. On a sunny day take a hat and umbrella as it does get very bright and hot walking around Jaws was pretty good and Spider-Man as well 3d effects were awesome if you plan properly you can fit most rides in the day they have there own train with universal all over it that takes you right to the grounds makes things easier:) will visit Disney land next year

Prior our visit, I tried to read reviews and forum regarding USJ to maximize the time and the experience. We had been to Disney Sea and Disney Land last December 2013 and all I could say was I should have read forums before regarding fast pass!!! So lessons learned OH SO WELL!  Going back to USJ, we decided to be there by 8am since we did not have the entrance tickets yet and we felt that it would help to be early to ensure that the queue won't be that long yet. But due to unforeseen circumstances, we arrived 30mins late or @around 830 am! To our surprise, the rides were all busy and there was a sea of crowd already hurrying inside the park! Mind you that in the website, the start of their operation is 9am! So we hurried to the cashier and really it took us no longer than 2mins to avail the tickets! There is a long line of ticket booths so it would not be a problem if you avail the pass on the same day.  We never paid for the Express Pass. The reason why we went here was we wanted to experience the Harry Potter attraction and given that we came in early, the higher our chance to achieve that. And yes we did! Reminder: Get a timed entry ticket! That is a requirement...crowd control probably as this is one of the most popular attractions in USJ. Secondly, Jaws is just right beside th HP attraction so my advise is to not put it on 2nd priority as it is the "catch all" of those who went to HP. There is a chance that queue is really ling! Check out the cool all the cool 4Ds! If you are not into so much the kiddie stuff, skip Sesame Street 4D! Don't miss out Hollywood ride, Backdrop. If you have fear on heights, don't do it! It really scared the hell out of us!:))) But soooo fun!  The parade starts at 8pm...don't miss this out as well. We have experienced about 10 rides/4Ds/shows without the pass. In fact, at 5pm we are idle already:) So we used this time to buy some souvenirs. We went last May 2, a holiday in Japan. So just come early and you won't get disappointed:)

As someone who has live in Japan for 2 years, going to USJ was like a taste of home: trash cans everywhere, American music etc. definitely worth the trip, especially because it was much easier for me to get to Osaka from my town than it would be for me to get to California or Florida from Chicago. If you are touring Japan and have only a few days in Osaka, this is not a must-do stop. The Osaka park is much cleaner then the American versions, which is lovely. It has its own subway/train stop for public transportation, so if you are staying at a hotel further away, leave the car there! We took a day bus there from our town and arrived around 9:45 ( on a holiday) and there was maybe only a 10 minute wait to get out tickets and get inside, which was fantastic. I recommend getting there as early as possible. The staff were all incredibly helpful and gave really excellent directions. We both speak Japanese, but I heard multiple people speaking English for other guests, so you should be okay. Overall, it's a theme park, fairly standard, but with the Japanese omotenashi that adds extra to the atmosphere.  -Harry Potter World Their websites say that they will have timed entry to Harry Potter World "if necessary", but they were already doing timed entry when we arrived within the opening hour of the park. This should be your first stop. Right between Jaws and the 50's cafe there's a little alcove where you can get timed entry tickets for HP. Also, if you don't care about the ride, but still want to see the castle, ignore the line that is often at 200 minute wait, and do the castle walk (our wait was maybe 2 minutes) you get to experience almost everything, just without the roller coaster at the end. Another heads up is that there is a line to get into Ollivanders and Honeydukes, so go there early.  The only other wait longer than 10-30 minutes was for Jurassic Park, which also sells timed entry tickets, so that's should be your next stop. All the other attractions are pretty open.

If you've never been to the Wizzarding World of Harry Potter in Orlando Fl. then I recommend visiting Universal Osaka. What you've probably read in the other comments is true, you need to arrive early to buy tickets (if you haven't already). Lines get very long but everything moves quickly. They opened up the park early and we were able to get in no problem.  In order to see the Wizzarding World of Harry Potter you have to go to another machine (once you enter the park) to get a ticket time to guarantee entrance into the W.W Harry Potter. So as soon as you enter you'll want to start heading that way, they will hand you a map when you buy tickets so you can see the directions from there.  My husband and I went on a weekday and it was still relatively busy, however people were still able to get into W.W Harry Potter even after guaranteed times. So I wouldn't freak out if you didn't get a time (just try really hard to).  Make sure to also check out the Attack On Titan section, its only their for a limited amount of months (until june? I think). You can take pictures in front of the big titan eating people or in front of the two huge statues.  Also try out the Space Fantasy ride! We had no idea what it was but it was only a ten minute wait, they make you take a picture before getting on the ride. The ride is basically the Japan Space Mountain! Very fun ride!  Overall good fun, clean, extremely friendly staff. Wait times for certain rides/shows are extremely long. Would recommend going, however if you're on a time crunch traveling to Japan I wouldn't put it high on a priority list.

My friend lives in osaka, so she took me that place. I'm just big fan of USJ !!! I read pretty lots of review that had to wait for a long time to ride, especially Harry Potter . But i think those people don't know that rainy days and weekdays are good to visit. You should avoid weekends!! And this park is closed at 8pm, so you can ride attractions without waiting around 1930~!! Anyway, it was amazing place. Sights are wonderful , attractions are so fun!

Keep in mind that USJ changes its themes by the season. I was lucky that I was there for their Halloween festival (Fall). Souvenirs, including Hello Kitty, Peanuts Characters and others were decked out in Spooky gear.  Do not speak Japanese? Bring a guide or a friend who can speak the language. Luckily I can understand the attractions, though. Universal Studios California and Singapore have similar attractions -- Terminator, Shrek, Jurassic Park. But everything in USJ is dubbed in Japanese. Otherwise, the rides are almost completely the same.  One tip for Harry Potter. Enter the park earlier, around 10am, and proceed immediately to the 'timed tickets' booth. Present your entrance ticket and you will be given a timed ticket when you are allowed to enter the Harry Potter attraction due to the volume of people. My suggestion is upon entrance, stop by the choir, then head for the Hogwarts castle queue. There are 2 queues, one for sightseeing and the other for the 'ride.' You can see the Fat Lady, Portraits and other characters in action, but they are speaking in Japanese only. The Trio are also dubbed by their respective VAs (Kensho Ono for Harry for example). Then afterwards, another queue for the souvenir shops. You can buy wands, clothing, scarves in the shop immediately after the castle exit. Honeydukes is always full, and queueing will take around 1 hour. Once inside, I recommend grabbing the chocolate goodies and the beans (there is no actual earwax or vomit flavor, promise).  As for transportation, it depends where you are staying in Osaka. If you are coming from Kobe, there is a bus every hour until 9pm. Else, you can stay near at the partner hotels, or leave early at around 830 on the last train out.  Don't forget to buy butterbeer! You can get hot or cold butterbeer, in a normal cup or with a souvenir mug for a slightly higher price.

Having arrived in Japan is a dream come true and entering USJ is a big bonus. Japan lives up my expectation with a clean and punctuality culture. USJ provides something that i really demand in theme park, "fantastic line management." You will definitely happy in line knowing exactly the time you can have a ride. With the inclusion of harry potter, the visit is a must.

Maybe it's just because I visited Disneysea a few days ago, but I've been totally underwhelmed by Universal. The atmosphere is not as magical, staff are less friendly and the rides just aren't as good. Lots of things are extremely outdated, like Backdraft and Jaws and various graphics. And the effort that goes into things just isn't quite as good. There are a lot of rides that rely heavily on 3D and motion master rather than actually building impressive sets which just isn't my cup of tea.  A word of caution, this park does NOT cater well to westerners. When I went to disneysea I had zero trouble getting on any of the rides at all. The first ride I tried to get on here I was shoved into a test seat and couldn't get the barrier down far enough for their liking. I'm a big girl and this is Japan so I did understand and had expected that my size may hold me back from some things, but it had never been an issue up until that point. Then when I went to the Harry Potter ride I was denied to enter the ride there after being shoved into a test seat in front of people walking past. It was humiliating. Even though we had paid extra for the Express 7 pass I wasn't allowed to even walk around the castle and just skip the ride. What a huge waste of money.  As I said I do understand because I am larger especially by Japanese standards, but I wasn't even questioned for any rides at Disney, so this came as a shock. I only ended up being able to go on 4 out of 7 rides after spending $150NZD just to get in and get an express pass. There were no warnings when purchasing the very expensive passes that it might be an issue either. Clearly it's down to the way they operate their safety checks as the Disney rides are way more extreme and my weight and size were never an issue. There's no privacy when you're denied either and no alternatives offered. A girl skinner than me was denied entry to Hollywood dream, I would've said she wasn't bigger than a size 16. She was clearly very upset too.  The Harry Potter world is cool, but extremely busy. Most of the reason we got the Express 7 pass was that it ensured entry to the popular attraction without rushing at the beginning of the day to secure timed entry. The shops were really cool, but it was impossible to move through the crowds. That's not their fault, it's just a popular attraction.  Things that would be cool are lame because there are no English options. Backdraft was mostly us listening to Japanese dubbed Ron Howard. We found out you CAN in fact get an English audio guide, but this was not offered directly to us by staff members or when purchasing our tickets. I did later see that it was in small print on a pamphlet but it was too little too late. As we didn't get the guide I'm unsure as to what exactly it translates (i.e specific rides or tracks or what) or how helpful it actually is.  The Attack on Titan attraction was really cool, mostly because the wax figures were incredible. The actual walk through was very limited for those who are not fluent Japanese speakers. This won't be around for very much longer though.  Shops are average, music is obnoxiously loud and plays the same 15 tracks over and over again all day. Crowd control is messy. Staff do not communicate well with foreigners, unlike disney. This is also WAAAY more expensive than disney in every aspect. It's hard not to compare it to Disney as it attempts to emulate the feel in every way. I wouldn't rush to come here at all. I would much rather go to Florida and not feel self concious about fitting into the rides. I've been large for a long time and never ever ever had an issue at theme parks until today.  In saying that, there were things that were fun. LOVED the magical Harry Potter world and the attention to detail. Jaws although very outdated was quite enjoyable. My boyfriend enjoyed all the rides I couldn't though did say they were very 3D heavy and nothing was exceptional.

Alright rather than join in the sea of review on USJ in general, ima focus on the seasonal theme, Cool Japan 5 featuring Shingeki no Kyojin, Biohazard, Evangelion and Monster Hunter. Visited on 13 May 2015, and it opened late somwhere 9:15 am.  In short you can skip everything under Cool Japan 5 besides Biohazard escape game, roughly 3000Yen unless ur otaku in which case you would not even need a review for convincing. Biohazard or Resident Evil for international release, takes place in a 4 storey building staged as a TV Broadcast office. Its basically escape room-esque concept except its out of a 4 storey building. Beware there are zombies hidden or tucked away in the shadowy corners ready to pounce on you. This typically leads to japanese girls hugging nearby guys as they scream for their lives.  In conclusion this is a super fun 90 min activity and requires ticket purchase in advance to assign the players into appropriate groups of 4.

As a first time visitor to any universal studios, I was quite surprised with how non-universal it was...many of the attractions had no English or Chinese, not even subtitles! This took away from the overall enjoyment. Considering that there are many Chinese tourists that visit, they should at least invest in making it more foreigner/ tourist friendly. But then again, the employees' smiles and waves are easily understood!

We've been to Universal Florida and had fun as a family of 4 (2 girls of varying ages) and this had fun for all of us to experience. A lot smaller, but we walked and walked through the day, maybe we got lucky due to overcast; as crowds here make the U.S. parks look unpopulated. However, like all of Japan, everyone is courteous, and it's somewhat organized. We invested in express passes, so that is a must. We got through everything rapidly. But even rides without xpress moved steadily without event. We got on the space ride 2 x, but our kids kept going on it 3x more at evening without any wait. We stayed through 9pm when park closed and the parade ran. Food was a wide variety, we found a sit down restaurant that was some of the best park food I've ever had. We had a blast and glad we visited osaka from our location in Tokyo (my company relocated me here)

We're a family of six and we all love it! Trip from our hotel required three transfers, so you do need to get used to train system, with most signs in Japanese it is not easy, the best way is to ask the station personnel near the turnstile, they all speak English and can even show you how to use the ticket booths. Anyway, USJ seemed much bigger, newer, cleaner, better maintained than the one in the US. It was a Friday, lots of people, specially students, long lines ranging from 110 mins to 10 mins, but were reasonable as you can expect. My kids did around 7 rides. I did two. The best part was the Harry Potter, I truly enjoyed this whole area, every store were an experience, from the stores for magic wands, to the owls, apparels, I'm usually not a sucker for these things, but I had to give in this time. The butter beer, the bathrooms. I found myself alone in one of the bathrooms at night and started hearing moaning myrtle ! But the best part was the castle, I didn't mind the line since you pass by amazing rooms before reaching the ride. Don't miss this ride! Amazing. The only problem is that are the audio was in Japanese. The parade at the end was fantastic with all the lights on each float. We didn't finish the whole area, need to come back. my two teeners and two smaller kids loved every moment.  After closing we there were so many Japanese restaurants just outside the gate, it got crowded right after the closing, but it gets easier an hour later.

I highly and STRONGLY recommend getting the fast past though because at one time the wait time for the main Harry Potter ride was 3-4 hours! We paid an extra $60 on top of our tickets but it was worth every cent!!!! Lines for the big roller coaster Hollywood Dream, and Hollywood Dream Backdrop were 90 minutes minimum. Butterbeer was soooo yum, but I wouldn't have more than one as they are very sweet.

Went on a day which was pouring down... but since the area isn't that big (compared to US and Singapore), you can literally visit everything in one day! The staff in USJ are very helpful, though really, they could do with some English conversational training... The highlight was definitely Harry Potter, and the more recently established Minions "Corner" (I'll call it a corner, because there isn't much related to the Minions apart from a little shop and a few photo spots)... The Harry Potter ride seems to be ultra popular, and it was really quite good I must admit! The queue was for 140 minutes at the peak... We bought a Fast Pass (Express 5) so we didn't need to queue up much... Some rides will have lockers for you to temporarily store your goods because they were not allowed on the rides! This was particularly useful, and there are also some lockers where you can store your stuff in for a longer time, so you don't have to bring everything along with you! There is an area just for children, and they had small rides, slides, playgrounds etc just for young children, and you can even join in with them! There is also a special area called "Cool Japan" and I would say that this is really just for the Japanese anime fans... Finally, the souvenir shops had far too many cute items that you just want to take them ALL home!! They even had a store JUST for Spiderman products! Being a fan, I could have easily spent hours in there... (Not for everyone, I know) If you are still wondering whether it is worth a visit... Go! See and experience for yourself! It is great fun, a big range of activities for adults, teens and children!

We came here to visit the Harry Potter world. Once we were in it was really, really good. We hadn't planned it in advance though and when you get to the park, you get a timeslot to get in and we had to wait 7hours until we could enter~ so worth planning in advance. To pass the time, we went on the Jurassic park ride, which was very busy. When it went dark they had a zombie experience throughout the park, which was very scary. The Harry Potter world was excellent- it had Hogwarts and the lake. Good rides. Extremely busy though.

We visited on a Tuesday in first week of June, which is not the school holidays season. Without express pass, we still managed to ride the Spider-Man twice and completed all the major attractions. Even the Harry Potter does not require timing ticket. However, for the Harry Potter 4d ride, the wait time is 80 mins, the longest wait time on that day. The rest of the rides' wait time range from 10 to 20 mins. Although some reviews said that you are allowed entry earlier than the opening hours, it is not true from my experience. I was there an hour before opening hour, but only allowed entry exactly at 9:30am. However, there are some people being allowed entry earlier around 9:00am which I guessed having special kind of pass. Once allowed in, everyone was running towards Harry Potter but I just went against the tide and did Spider-Man first! Wait time 5 Mins only! Then I did the terminator before having early lunch at Saido Japanese restaurant, just adjacent to the minions fever location. Although most people said that the food in USJ kind of sucks, but I had one of the most delicious food in my Japan trip in this restaurant. So I would recommend you to try out this if you have budget (2000 to 3000 yen for each meal set). After the lunch, it is exactly the show time for minions just outside this restaurant! Then, we went to Harry Potter and spend a couple of hours there and of course the butter beer is a must try. Then we did the the water world show and jaws before returning to do Spider-Man and backdraft. Wait time approximately 10 mins at that time (around 5pm). On the way back, we still managed to do a 4d show (anime) and leave the park at 7pm.all in all, a great day for my whole family.

Brought my 3 kids and they loved it. We bought the express 7 pass and we were able to finish all the major rides less the long lines in 1 day.  Harry potter rides took as long as 180 mins waiting time without the pass, while flight of the griffindor can take up as much as 60 mins waiting time.  We tried the famous butterbeer. I personally didn't like the taste but it was worth it for the experience.  Terminator show was a bit of a challenge. It was full japanese with no sub titles. Its a good thing i know the story. I had to interpret it for the kids to appreciate.

Overall, it was an okay compared to the singapore one. The studio was huge until I had to ask the staff the directions. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I didn't manage to try all the attractions as the waiting time was long especially the Harry Potter which was 240 minutes! The terminator 3D show was narrated in japanese so i didn't understand at all but luckily this was an action show. The studio was very crowded since I came on Saturday. All the shops was very packed. I didn't had the chance to really take a good look at all the attractions shop. Compared to universal studio Japan and Singapore I think I will prefer the Singapore one as I can understand the theater show and the queue was not as long as in Japan.

i think this park would be a big hit with you if a) you are an enormous harry potter fan, b) you like "grown up" non-sissy heart-stopping rides, or c) you are a toddler. i am none of the above, but more of that in a while...  we bought our tickets at the tourist information counter at the ground floor in kansai airport, since i didn't want to waste time in line at the park buying tickets. i was also too lazy to buy them in advance using the japanese website and google translate, which others have advised here. and we did not buy fast passes either, because yes, we are cheapos.  on a friday, took the hanshin line to nishikujo station from osaka namba, then transferred to the jr line going to universal city (the experience traversing the subway deserves another review on its own!!). reached the park entrance by 9am and there were already HORDES of people waiting in line. as soon as the gates opened at 9:30, people started running east to get the HP timed tickets, but being old fuddy duddies, we took our sweet time walking the opposite direction where very few people were heading. this proved to be a good decision as we managed to take in spiderman with only a 5 minute wait and back to the future with a 20 minute wait. i almost had a heart attack on the spiderman ride, the moving cars whirl you around like you're in a washing machine, the 3d effects are super in-your-face and the blaring sounds were enough to give me panic attacks. i think the younger ones enjoyed it, though. the back to the future ride was quite tame compared to it -- and very, very vintage. it was the exact ride i rode on more than 20 years ago at universal studios florida!! quite unfortunately, english subtitles were sorely missing from doc's intro video. next up was jaws, which entailed a 30 minute wait, but which was quite bearable since the line was moving fast and we munched on snacks while waiting (snacks which were actually "smuggled" as outside food is not allowed in the park). the intro video was similarly purely in japanese, as well as the boat-guide's spiel. it was another vintage ride -- i vaguely remember riding it more than 30 years ago in the US! just a tip -- try to sit on the rightmost part of the boat, because when the fake gas tanks explode on the left, it gets REALLY, REALLY hot!!! my kids got scared more from the fire than from the mechanical sharks. for a while there, i thought all us passengers were going to get roasted alive.  we headed next to the kiddie wonderland, which was ok -- if you're three years old. it was all right for taking pictures and looking at cutie stuff in the boutiques, but we didn't spend much time there. after catching some street shows and grabbing lunch, we finally got to lining up for the HP timed tickets. i don't remember any visible signs pointing to the ticket vending machines -- we just followed the people heading towards this area behind a forest. try to ask any of the park staff if you need directions. they are all quite helpful and extremely perky too. (keep your entrance passes, because you will need to scan them at the ticket vending machine.) we were able to get tickets for 12:20-1:20pm, which wasn't so bad considering we lined up pretty late in the morning already. (you're supposed to enter the HP world only within the specified time frame, but you can stay in there as long as you want.)  and now, onto the HP world... if you are not a fan, as i am not (i have never read any of the books nor watched any of the films so i have ZERO idea about the story or the movies, so sue me) you will not relate at all to the attractions nor the souvenir shops. when we went into one shop, for instance, i was surprised to see an entire room dedicated to magic wands. really, JPY1000++ for a wooden stick?? the costumes were the most expensive things i had ever seen for sale in japan. JPY14000 for a replica of harry's coat!! the only thing we bought was a bottle of pumpkin juice (i did mention we were cheapos), which was basically very sweet apple juice with a bit of spice. we couldn't be bothered to line up for the butterbeer (i'm planning to google the recipe and make it for much less).  my kids were only able to ride the hippogrief roller coaster, which took a 40-minute wait. the 4d ride required a 180-minute wait -- this is where your fast pass would most come in handy. this may sound sacrilegious to some, but we opted to skip it.  we headed next for waterworld, which was the exact same show as the one in US Singapore, but in japanese. even the jokes were the same. we decided to skip backdraft and terminator, given the so-so reviews and the fact that both shows were entirely in japanese. the hollywood dream roller coaster was a no-go as well since our middle aged bones would probably not survive the ride. so all in all, that sums up our pretty average day at USJ. if i had a choice, i would much rather have shopped at Shinsaibashi, and if you must know, US Singapore was way, way, way better for me. but hey, different strokes for different folks right?

I've been too many parks including Universal Hollywood and the rides in Japan are fantastic. The Spider-Man ride won best ride for 11 years or something only to be de-throned by Harry Potter -- both rides are at this park!! Also Jaws is here (only place in the world now) and even in Japanese is a great kitch ride!! Go early during the week and have an amazing time :)

The best way to enjoy USJ is to get express passes. The problem is they cost almost as much as the park tickets themselves. A bigger problem is that they may not even be available for sale on the day you want to go. That's because they are also sold online, but only on the Japanese website of USJ. We were able to purchase these with the help of a website (just google it) which shows step-by-step how to do it. Google translate wasn't very useful because there are many untranslatable japanese text on buttons. You also need to google translate your name to Japanese (in advance) as the website wants a japanese character name. We kept getting timed out just trying to figure this out. Anyway, while the express pass was quite useful for us, as were were able to do all our favorite attractions twice (hp/spidey/rollercoaster).  In hindsight, we might have gotten away with not using express passes, and still not have to queue up too long. With no express pass, this is what I suggest: 1. Pick a weekday and check that the kids are in school (e.g. not summer or holiday) 2. Get there at 7am. Have breakfast while waiting in line. The park officially opens at 9 but they will open at 8:30am if there are lots of people--and there always are. 3. Run to the Harry Potter world immediately. Ignore everything else around you and go straight to the ride. The wait should not be too long this early. 4. After taking the ride, exit Harry Potter and head straight to the Spiderman ride. The wait is short in the morning. 5. Go back to the timed entry machine for HP and get a timed entry ticket for later. This will allow you to re-enter HP world. You'll most likely get an afternoon time. 6. Go ride everything else in order of your interest. Note that the Jaws, Backdraft and Back to the Future, Terminator 3D are exactly the same as the old US versions, but in japanese. 7. Go back to HP world on your timed entry ticket. Check on the queue for the ride. We went back again at 6pm. Although it said 80 minutes, the actual wait was just 60 minutes. Spend the rest of your time in HP world. Almost everything (except the ride) has no more queues after dark. 8. Get butterbeer at the takeout counter at Hog's Head. No lines! The frozen non-alcoholic butterbeer is too sweet. Yucch! The regular one is okay. 9. If they're making you line up just to get in to the wand shop, there is a side entrance where you can get in without waiting. Weird! 10. While lining up for the HP ride, you will be given a card. It tells you to put all your things into the locker. Don't put the card inside the locker together with your things. The card is your entry pass to the ride itself.

Universal studios is amazing and so is so worth visiting. I went on my own and so I got to skip the lines as I was a single rider and did not have to wait in a queue throughout the day. Would recommend.

We visited with our 1 year old son. There wasn't many rides that he could go on. It was an expensive day as we didn't go on any rides as he was too short and was not allowed to sit on our laps. It's not as child friendly as Disneyland tokyo.

I had been to USJ several times as a child but recently returned with my wife. We had booked our tickets and 5-attraction fast pass in advance and it was just as well, considering the long queues at the ticket booths.  We would recommend buying the fast passes as well because it would save you a lot of time, especially for the Harry Potter rides. When we were there, the waiting time for the Harry Potter Wizarding World ride was 220mins long. In contrast, we got in with our fast pass in under 15 mins.  We did find some parts of the park to be slightly tired-looking, especially those rides that had been there for a long time (such as Back to the Future). Also, the lack of English translation for the attractions was grating and prevented us from enjoying the attractions more.

Excellent park. If you are Harry Porter fan, it is a must to visit. I'm not a fan, but Harry Porter section was awesome. All the rides were fun, but I will suggest to buy a VIP Pass if you can afford it. The lines are crazy long like you can't believe, even though we went on a Tuesday. People lined up before gates open and teenagers ran in like crazy right after they gates open. VIP pass will make it possible to ride most of popular rides in one day, otherwise it will be hard to ride all popular rides in one day. The lines are THAT long. The park is huge with all different sections from kids to adults. All rides are in Japanese, so you wouldn't understand anything if you can speak Japanese, but it was still fun. We didn't stay for the parade, but I heard it is a good one, so try to check it out if you can. VIP Pass has different options, so you can choose if you'd like to pay more to get in VIP lines for more rides. The most expensive VIP Pass is for 7 rides I believe and it is about $65 extra on top of regular ticket. Trust me that it is worth to pay more. It will make your experience much more enjoyable there.

PROS: Harry Potter World! Enchanting place. Park is compact so easier to go from one place to another Super Clean Park   CONS: Shows/Rides are in Japanese (would have enjoyed the show/rides more if there were English subtitles)  We went on a Monday so it's not as crowded as we expected it to be. But the lines are still long. Good thing we bought fast passes in advance :)

This is a great place for the whole family!! Do not miss!! Specially for Harry Potter fans the Wizarding World of HP is a heaven!! The Amazing Adventures of Spider-Man, Hollywood Dream – The Ride, Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey, Back to the Future - The Ride were awesome!! But make sure to buy an express pass, otherwise some of the queues are 210 minutes wait time!!

Harry Potter Park is the biggest draw. We got there at 10.15am when the park opened at 9.30am... the ride wait time was already 170mins! I did expect HPP to be bigger. The rest of USJ is spacious and just a happy place. Having the roller coaster rides wrap around the park is a great idea - you are constantly hearing the riders screaming away (in glee for most I am sure). Minions is a huge draw for the kids. Just a happy place

Everything is in Japanese, so as an English speaking only tourist it was difficult to enjoy. We bought 2 entry tickets and a 5 ride fast-pass for 268,000 yen. Way expensive for Japan standards of entertainment. The fast pass also only allowed you 5 limited rides with limitations THIS or THAT...I didn't know that and could only used 3 of the 5.  Food was also expensive and they try as much to get you to buy their products, photos, foods and souvenirs as part of their program.  However, I have not been to Universal Studios so it was a great experience. If you have been to US before I probably give this a miss.

nice theme park especially the harry potter attraction. even though need to wait for about 3hours, i feel it is worth it. need to booked the time to enter the harry potter attraction to avoid over crowded. the butterbeer drink is a must to try. it is only available at the harry potter attraction. will be better if they can close the park a bit later on weekdays. when i went there, the park close at 6pm and eventually do not have enough time to finish all the attraction.

I visited universal studios on a Monday. It was extremely crowded and the fast passes had already sold out when we arrived, or else I would have purchased one. The lines are crazy. The rides are really fun but there are size restrictions. To get into the wizarding world of Harry Potter you need to get passes (free). They are a bit hard to navigate but it is still a great experience.

The Harry Potter theme section of the park was the main attraction. There is a mad rush once the park opens towards this section. Besides the wow factor of this place it holds two main rides. One is a 3D ride the other a small family roller coaster. The remainder of the park was just ok. Having visited Disneyland Tokyo prior I think this had a dampening effect on our expectations of Universal Studios.

Although we arrived 15 mins early, there were already long queues, but if you run fast, you can enter the harry potter world! But only the first 15 mins of opening time.  if you miss it, thats okay, just head to the time ticket machines past harry potter and onto the left side  time tickets depends on the number of people in the park that day.  jurassic park is the same as the one in singapore.  the kids world was very nice with themed souvenir stores and hidden medalion machines to try  the harry potter ride in the castle is a must go, one of the best roller coaster rides i have been to. even inside the castle the view is just amazing. If you have kids who cannot ride, go for the castle walk, its just as beautiful.  the spiderman ride was very similar to the transformers ride in singapore as well.

Harry Potter castle and the attractions there is the best so far with the building and setting close to the movie. The queue is 1 hour minimum to the attraction. While others are not quite crowded considering it was a weekday visit.

It was similar to the park in Florida, but definitely a lot smaller. The food was very expensive ( maybe even more so than in the States) The Japanese people line up very early to enter. Although the park didn't open until 9:30am there were people in line at 7:30am The park is clean and well maintained

So I understand I went here in a different country, but being universal studios I thought there would be some English... but alas I was quite wrong, the rides are all in Japanese with minimal (mostly none). Harry Potter world was amazing. DEFINATLY get thwre early and head straight there to avoid the 3 hr line. Most of the rides were a lot of fun tho, even if u couldn't understand too much of the story lines! If u have a spare day in osaka I recommend a visit!!

Wery new nice and lovely park; don't go there sundays( up to 250min waiting line for a Harry Potter rollercoaster)be prepared for no or only very little translation/ everything I Japanese or a little in Chinese the Hogwards castle was fantastic.
Size of the Universal Studio is just fit to have a one-day fun! Staffs in the park are all professional as actors. We did enjoy those games then.

Lots of fun! Plenty to keep busy with. The lack of decent dining options is just like any other theme park.  Pro-tip: Don't get caught waiting in a 2-hour line if you don't have a fair idea you will enjoy the ride.

This was an amazing day for us so much to see and do . Great for kids and adults alike very good service throughout the entire park . Food and refreshments available throughout or a great selection of restaurants or fast food available just outside . Subway takes you straight to attraction

if you do not speak Japanese prepare to only go on the rides! Youll waste your time standing in line to go to shows that you don't understand. Also most of the rides are in Japanese like spiderman so good luck! NOT WORTH IT IF YOU DO NOT SPEAK JAPANESE. The customer service was poor as compared to the Universal in Orlando FL The most exciting part was TGI Fridays restaurant - which was extremely expensive for frozen food heated to its customers pleasure- They start closing the park and hours early by the way! The gift shops are so poor .... no candies or anything worth remembering a trip over..... just hats and towels...

If you are a Harry Potter fan , this Park will intrigue you . Simply because of Hogsmeade - being able to buy Harry's wand ( or Dumbledore's wand or anyone else's ), having a taste of butter beer and bringing a box of chocolate frogs home .  It seems that most people at osaka universal studios are there for the same reason ! An impt tip - don't forget to get a time-stamped access for Harry Potter World when you get to the park - it's free and not far from the main entrance . This dictates the time that you will enter that part of the Park rather than queue to get in .
Terrible English speaking staff. You would expect a decent English speaking staff in an international theme park

First, I am not a fan of amusement parks, not at all. But I have to admit USJ knows how to do things. The atmosphere is everywhere nice and friendly, the marketing is never stressing, the attractions are spectacular - amazing Spider-Man - and very different.  The Harry Potter time control is a bit annoying but I guess necessary to control the flow as the place is really fun, feels like UK in middle of Japan. Really a must go if you are in the region with kids. Do think though to reserve early so you can get a fast track ticket, that makes the day twice more fun !

Universal Studio is great for family or lovers. many rides and shops, the price is expensive and the restaurant food is not great. i recommend to eat at universal city walk after closing. the Express tickets are sold out 1 week in advance.

the park as expected is big, clean, with many exciting attraction like harry potter. I go on saturday and dont know if it is because holiday season or weekend, but the place is so crowded almost every ride you must wait for 1 hour or more. so a bit of advice, if you want to go on holiday season or weekend and you really want to be able to ride many attraction, buy free-pass ticket, a bit pricey but worthy.

Harry Potter World was absolutely great- both rides are definitely worth waiting for and Harry Potter fans will love the attention to detail in this area of the park. We read many reviews before we went to USJ which were mostly negative and said we would experience hours and hours of queueing, however the most we queued for a ride (Hollywood dream) was 1 hour, which I would expect to wait at any theme park across the world.Although it was busy there are plenty of rides and attractions so it never felt overcrowded. There are not many roller coasters which I found quite disappointing, but I would still say USJ should definitely be visited if you are in Osaka/Honshu.  Also there is great luggage storage for a small fee- we took our backpacks and got the overnight bus to Tokyo straight from USJ. There are plenty of places to eat in the park and nearby.

The park is the same as the one in Florida minus a couple of roller coaster. It still had everything else everything is moderately priced and the food is cheap. Had a great time no long waiting at the lines. This place was very clean and everyone was very friendly. We enjoyed ourselves very much. It is a must see if you are in this part of Japan!!
If you wanted to try all the attractions, you need to spend at least two days here. Especially when you travelling with small kids.

Maybe we can blame ourselves, but getting there on time is too late to buy a fast pass into the park. We bought tickets the previous day and meant to get the fast pass tickets on the day, but no luck. Buying fast-pass tickets online through the English website redirects you to travel agents from other countries. I only later learned that if you use the Japanese website and Chrome's Google Translate, that you could buy the tickets without that. They are sold out a month in advance though.  Without fast passes, you are resigned to having one ride every 2-4 hours and standing in line in between. Food is not allowed in the park, though they don't check bags too thoroughly. To get food you need to stand in queues too and it is obviously over-priced.  Some rides are definitely a lot of fun, and maybe worth the wait. Our favourites were the Hollywood Backdrop and Harry Potter World's Forbidden Journey. They both have more than 3 hours of waiting in line, and you need a timed entry ticket to enter Harry Potter World. If you get the Fast Pass 5, this comes with the ticket and you get to skip queues for both the aforementioned rides.  As for the staff, they work very hard and are very friendly and accommodating. We had a situation with a friend and they made special allowance for us to leave the park but allow re-entry. I then lost one of the tickets and with much discussion, they replaced it for us too! I was impressed with the friendly people I met there.  Nevertheless, be prepared to shell out big cash, or else be prepared to get sore feet for some momentary fun.

It was a very sunny, hot and packed USJ when we were there. Took the JR Line from Osaka to USJ, fairly straight forward to get there.  Unfortunately some rides and part of the park was closed. Shrek and Jurassic Park was unavailable. You need to get a ticket (only 1 time) to enter Harry Potter and wow it was packed. The rides waiting time that day took either 100 to a whopping 230 minutes. You can get a "fastpass" for some of the rides but only 1 at a time.  Spent most of the time at the kids area as the rest was just to packed. Other rides are not very suitable for young kids unless they are the adventures type.  Food was ok but small in portion. Couldn't say we tried a lot as it was too many people around.  Overall decent park but probably the attractions are a bit old with Back to the Future and Jaws which younger generation might not relate.
I came here in the afternoon. The park was very crowded, waited 2 hours for the Harry potter ride. Not worth the money.
It was wonderful experience there on July 29.My wife,my 10 year old daughter and I love USJ.It was great place than other Universal studios. Harry Porter's castle and many excited games were great.

We went to OSaka this summer for Universal Studio Japan. We bought a 2-day pass so that we could have plenty of time in the Studio. My 11-year old daughter liked the Spiderman attraction most, but me and wife liked the Harry Porter most. The Harry Porter attraction is a must to visit. We lined up for nearly two hours to experience the Harry Porter ride. It's fun and exciting. Also, the Blackdraft attraction is so real and amazing. You wouldn't get tired of it. We stayed at Namba Nakai but it is so convenient to take the subway and changed at the Osaka station for the JR circle line to USJ. The journey takes less than 30 minutes. We would go there again.

Handy to train station & Universal Port Osaka Hotel. The Harry Potter section was over-rated, it becomes quite busy, as no-one is leaving (probably trying to find out what the hype is). The only part of HP that I did enjoy was the butter beer, and it's not beer. The rest of the studios was great & the staff were fantastic. The lady driving the boat on the Jaws ride was very animated & entertaining. I had no idea what she was saying, but she did it well.

I think the worst thing about Universal Studios in Osaka is the Queuing for a ride takes too long. Some of the rides takes 2 hrs to line up. It's wasting so much time just for a ride especially when it is very hot summer in Osaka. I wouldn't come to Universal Studios Osaka again. I prefer Florida Universal Studios and LA Universal Studios.

.. I think this would not appeal to me at all. But we did brave the lines for my friends to experience how fun the Harry Potter Ride was (been to Orlando, Florida). We also did the Jaws ride and then went home. There is nothing much to offer us since most of the rides were of old movies or themes. But it would be great for kids for they would enjoy the cartoons and the rides. But as the other reviewers say, bring lots of patience as the lines are extremely long! Well, there is the fast pass if you want to go that route.

Whilst visiting Japan with children I thought this would be a good break from the wonderful culture of this lovely country. I researched online, I knew I wanted express pass, was unable to book online, do arrived 9.30. All "sold out". 😟 Ok, timed pass for Harry Potter at 17.10 - over 7 hours later! No problems except this does not enable you to get on ride. 300 minute wait. My kids aged 11 & 8 were so disappointed. Thankfully Jurassic Park timed ticket meant just that - straight on to a fun ride. Overall, too hot, too busy and too much waiting which was made worse by the poor website.

It was quitte good. Small and indeed crowded. Make zure you get the time passes for jurassic park and harry potter. Use single line if possible: the line is 20 minuten at max, sometimes no line at all.

I was in Universal Studio in Florida and Singapoore. This was the third one and definitelly the worst one!  The park was open at 9:00 am. We came at 11:00. All fast track were already Sold out. I was in different amusement park but I Have never seen such big queue like here! Besides the queue the park is not clear at All. For example to get to Harry Potter attraction or Jurasic Park before Entering you need to go and collect ticket for hour go Enter specific Area. (arround 12:00 we wanted to Enter Harry Potter and the nearest aviable time to Enter Area was 16:30). Plus the waiting queue for attraction was 190minutes!  All Universal Studios Japan attraction are in Japaneese. No English at All so you cannot really enjoy the attraction because you cannot understand.  Most of the STAFF working there do not speak English. Basicly This attraction is made for Japaneese people only.  As Universtal Studio Singapoore is amazing and I reccomend to visit to Have amazing memorie, This one Universtal Studio Japan I do not reccomend at All. I would say waiste of time and energy.

We were warned about the crowds. We were prepared for the crowds. Visiting Universal Studios Osaka is like the theme park version of the Tokyo subway in rush-hour, and required a bit of patience. I am certain mid-August is the busiest time to visit. While the official opening is at 9 AM, the park began opening as early as 8 15 AM to let the hoards into the park. We arrived around 8 AM, entered the park around 9 AM, and were able to secure a 9 50 AM entrance time to Harry Potter World.  The Wizarding World of Harry Potter exhibit does a great job of capturing the essence of the films with the ambience of Hogsmead and the towering Hogwarts castle. Olivander’s wand shop includes a little quaint and intimate performance of wand selection for a lucky young participant, exiting into the wand store – it was generally well done. The Butterbeer and frozen Butterbeer were one of the highlights of the visit. This cool, smooth concoction is lightly carbonated with caramel flavor that’s just right – not too sweet. The frozen variation almost had a creamy texture. We walked through the Hogwarts castle, which shares the same route as those waiting to ride the Harry Potter’s Hidden Journey 4K3D ride, so patrons can forgo the 3 hour wait (yes, you read that right) and still experience the exceptionally adorned interior consisting of the Gryffindor common room, Dumbledore’s office and more.  The waiting times for the rides were quite long. But, we managed to experience the Back to the Future ride driven by Omni-Max style technology, the classic Jaws ride (which was quite amusing in Japanese), ride the Hollywood Dream roller coaster, and have a picture taken with Hello Kitty.  The best tips I can give for Harry Potter fans wishing to visit Universal Studios are to get there very early, secure the earliest possible entry time, and ride the Hidden Journey immediately. In peak season, an hour and a half wait would be considered acceptable, so get it done first. Also, you should buy the express pass which I did not realize were sold in limited quantities. Plan early and spend the money to get the Express Pass. The vast majority of rides and shows are in Japanese. With our family being avid Harry Potter fans, we were generally happy with the respite from temples and Japanese culture – and I would only advise going if you are a true Harry Potter fan who needs a break with your kids.

The rides here are awesome! I love their halloween theme. Roaming zombies at night, scaring people.  Hollywood dream coaster is awesome. Try the backdrop as well! The queue can go up to 3 hours for this ride, so if possible, try and get the express pass online.  The harry potter attraction is crowded but their 4D ride is great. Do not miss it! Spend a whole day here, from opening till closing. You wont regret it. Try their food as well, though beware, queues are long but they move fairly fast.  If you're interested, come early and queue for the tickets to the biohazard attraction, where you can kill live zombies from resident evil. The attraction only accept timed tickets, so you would need to queue at a designated place to get your tickets.  I spent my birthday here so I asked the staff for the birthday sticker. She didnt ask to check my ID so perhaps you can try asking for one even if its not your birthday. Awesome day ever! Performers paid extra attention to me and the staff wished me birthday! Everything is in Japanese. If you understand nihongo then it's great. If not, you can still enjoy the rides!  If you have a few days in Osaka, be sure to visit USJ! YOU WONT REGRET IT!
I have been to Universal Studio in many countries and found the one in Japan is the best. Harry Potter is the latest rides and very attractive rides. The que is veryyy long but worthed :)

Great theme park with many types of rides and shide shows. They have Japanese themed section/rides which you can't find in any other Universal Studios (e.g One Piece / Bio Hazard).  Try not to go during week ends or holiday period, the queue will waste lots of your time (popular rides can have 3+ hours queue). Or at least buy an express pass if you are planning to visit at the above period.

I have never seen Soo many people in one place before. The park was fine even with the amount of people there. Some rides had a 2 & 1/2 hour wait, but it was on a holiday, we would come back again outside of the holidays. Definitely worth seeing if you like theme parks.

Much smaller than Florida but the bits they have got are exact copies of the bigger park. It's a great experience and very popular with the locals. We went in August. Harry Potter ride queue was 170 minutes, and you need to get a "timed ticket" just to be allowed to walk into the Harry Potter themed area! I've never seen a park so busy, it was ridiculous. Nevertheless the theming is great and without the queues it would be a great day out.

I suggest getting your tickets in advance from any Lawson convenience store ( The lines to enter the park are already long to begin with. So save some time and get your tickets in advance to skip that part.). They have a machine called "Loppi" where you can purchase your tickets. Go to this site and print out the directions (it's in english) so that you can easily navigate the machine: http://l-tike.com/leisure/usj/english/  The park opens at 9am but they let people in starting 8:30am. So it's best to get there early. I suggest 7am. Then get a map of the park and start mapping out where you want to go. So once you actually enter the park, you know exactly where to run. For me, I really wanted to see the Harry Potter world. So I ran there first to get my timed ticket. I got it for 10:30 am and then went straight to spiderman and then to Jurassic world to get tickets there. Those 2 rides finished just in time for me to return to Harry Potter. I spent about 2 hours in line for the castle ride of Harry potter. So I suggest getting a butterbeer before entering so that at least you have some sort of refreshment while waiting. This ride is worth it. So be early. By the time I finished the ride, the wait time to enter was 4 hours already!  Mind you I wasn't able to purchase an express pass because it was sold out. If you don't mind paying more online to get one of those agents to buy for you, you can. Though I survived without one. I spent the money on Harry Potter wands and food instead! :p  I spend a whole day here then ended it at the Takoyaki Museum right outside of the park. Best takoyaki I've ever had in my life! Check that out as well! :D
I love USJ even more than that of Singapore. We enjoyed strolling around the theme park esp Harry Potter's.Would definitely be back.

This place is amazing!!  I love Harry Potter and the reason my trip to Japan is to visited and try all Harry Potter ride in USJ.  I read all the books and movie and its a part of my life.  When me and fiance decide to go to Japan for holiday in 2014. I straight away try to find how can I enjoy the best out of USJ. After all research and asking questions to friends and travel agent. I found the best travel agent in Indonesia who sold express pass 3, 5 and 7. And also i found a website who sell Summer express pass which you cannot found in USJ website as well for this pass information.  We got really excited when we arrived till we decided to spent 2 days in a row at USJ and its worth every minutes and penny.  Love the whole sets especially Harry Potter. It makes my dream come true being in Harry Potter world!  Thanks USJ. We love you!

I'm a huge Harry Potter fan- I loved it! Definitely spend the extra money for the fast passes (or whatever they are called!?) so you don't have to line up! There was a 5 hour wait for the Harry Potter ride- we spent the extra cash and lined up for 15 mins. we went on a Monday and it was still sooooo busy but it's a great day out and definitely go on the roller coaster that goes backwards- that's worth the line up. If you can't speak Japanese, don't worry about the terminator 'ride'.

Great theme park! Worth every penny! The forbidden journey ride is the bomb diggity! MUST RIDE! Buy the express pass. It will make your visit a lot better. Expect a lot of visitors and long queue for most of the rides. Only gripe is that it can get really hot during summer. I hope they would extend the fiber glass roof to more areas of the park.

My tip: go later in the day on a weekday, and if a line is too long, try again later.  While staying in Osaka, my husband and I decided to visit Universal Studios. It was a rainy day and we had been tossing up whether to go or not, so it was later in the day when we decided and after the short train ride we were at the gates. And we are so glad we went, it was truly an amazing day.  Initially we were worried about long queues, but walked straight into a 4D Sesame st (which was sweet with excellent 3D visuals). The longest we had to wait for a ride was just over 1 hour for the Amazing Spider Man, but the ride was well worth the wait. Initially we couldn't get into Jurassic Park as they were only accepting reserved tickets, and we weren't prepared to wait 3 hrs for Harry Potter, so we went on Space Fantasy, with only a 25 minute wait, and it was one of the best rides in the park. We went back to Jurassic Park a bit later on and were able to reserve a time, and only had to wait 30 mins when we returned at our designated time.  We also went on Back to the Future, and it was the only ride we didn't enjoy. As it is quite old (2001) the seats were poorly designed (I kept sliding sideways into the person next to me) and the visual very dated and nauseating.  As it was now night time the park was getting quieter and we decided to take a look at how the Harry Potter line was going, and were rewarded with only a 20 minute wait (spent walking through the magical rooms of the castle) and then we were in the most popular ride in the park, we couldn't believe we hardly had to wait at all!  After a butterbeer and a sit down in Hogsmeade (exhausted by now) we walked back to the exit and was greeted by the Magical Starlight Parade, which was a lovely end to a fantastic day.

Universal studios is one of the must see attractions in Osaka. This is the best Universal Studios in Asia in my opinion. Of course, Harry Potter is the most in demand attraction but everyone needs to be aware of the big number of visitors that this world is getting so prepare accordingly.

we were here in July. It was very hot and humid. There was no fast pass available and the queues were very long - but still enjoyed it. The highlight is the Harry Potter ride. When we arrived the queue was of over three hours so we skipped it - but when we returned in the evening we went right in. Walking through Hogowarts was great - my 9 year old was in seventh heaven. The ride itself was amazing. Worth the trip.

With experience visiting USJ last year, getting an Express Pass 5 or 7 is unlikely at the park ticket booths. The English website showed nothing about purchasing tickets online but if you can manage a little Japanese, you can purchase tickets online.  You have to create an account and join as a Club Universal member (free) before you can purchase any tickets. You also get discount off park entrance tickets if it is your birthday month. You can print out your express pass and entrance tickets and head straight to the entrance gate. True enough, no express passes were available when I arrived at the park 30 minutes before opening.  With the Express 5 and 7 passes, the ticket to the Harry Potter area is included and you only have to select the time you wish to take the 3D ride during the purchase.  I only had to queue for the backdrop for about an hour and the rest of the rides I wanted to take are covered with the express pass and the longest I had to wait is about 20 minutes. Getting the Express Pass will definitely cut down a lot of your waiting time. You can queue up to 3 - 4 hours for the Harry Potter 3D ride.  The backdrop with BGM is still my favourite ride.

My entire family loved this theme park. Being originally from Orlando, FL this theme park brought back so many memories. We enjoyed the 7 ride Fast Pass as we got to go ahead of the lines and were able to do child switch without any problems. Wonderland was so cute for our 2 year he really enjoyed it. We met several of the characters and the Harry Potter area was incredible. This park was more enjoyable for us as a whole family than Tokyo Disneyland. We plan to visit this theme park again before we leave Japan because we made great memories here.

If you don't have the fast pass for the day you're going to the park, don't bother going! Even as a single rider waits were as long as 4 hours! And averaged about a 2 hour wait. Even the little kid rides had signs up for 100 minute waits! There was time ticketed entry to Harry Potter world but still it was crowded.  Arriving early didn't seem to help either as folks were lined up to get in. They even admitted people to the park early! It was so busy!
