The 4D ride is world class and defnitely a must try ride in USJ. All the shops and setting are so real and beautiful. We spent around 5 hours (3 hours for the 4D ride) and it was not enough. Of course, we tried to legendary butter beer and it really taste good.  Before we leaved USJ. we managed to watch the beautiful starlight parade. If you come to osaka for few days, it is definitely a must go place!

Great Theme Park... very interesting.. when you go out from subway you will see Universal City first The best thing was Harry Potter 4D..you must try it.. for anime lovers also had 4D movie such as evangelion, etc.. about the food a little bit expensive but because of the staff was very friendly and lovely.. make me happy to buy Definitely will come again...

The park was beautiful in both daytime and nighttime. I enjoyed to park but it required long waiting for everything (1 to 2 hours waiting). I also have found the souvenir too expensive. I would prefer visiting the Tokyo Disneysea instead which is the best park I have visited ever.

Some of the very best rides (Harry potter/flight ot dinosaur/Hollywood dream fwd).got there about 7:30am on a Monday. Was close to the front of the line for buying tickets. Despite this the express pass 4 was "sold out", even though the screen above the booth showed availability. In the end I was I didn't buy it as I was able to do most of the attractions and all ones I enjoy. Firstly we went straight into hogsmeade (Harry potter world, we ran straight for it as oppose to getting a timed entry ticket so we were lucky with our choice) and was on the "forbidden journey" ride in only a few minutes. Thereafter we did 1/2 of the 4D cinema shows, spiderman, 2/2 of 4D shows, Hollywood dream forward and finally the "Flying dinosaur". Queue for flying dinosaur was insane. I opted for the single rider line but still took roughly and hour to ride.

Osaka Universal Studios is waaaayyyy much better than Singapore Universal Studios!!!!!!  It is definitely a place you can spend whole day there and definitely must go if you go Osaka.  We bought the Universal Studio Pass and Cool Japan 5 Pass (the exclusive Express Pass for their domestic purchase) through the Japanese Universal Studio website online (you need to understand Japanese in order to purchase online). We did not get from any travel agency as after comparing the prices, purchasing online through their website is more worth it.  Do take note that the Harry Potter World is timed entry visit, meaning only those who have the Timed Entry Ticket and those who purchased certain Express Passes can then visit the Harry Potter World. There is also a magic show where you relive the day when Harry Potter chooses his wand. Drink some Cold ButterBeer in a souvenir cup and also munch your lunch in the Three Broomsticks.  Our Cool Japan 5 Express Pass consists of Attack of the Titans 4D Theatre Ride (not very good), Entry to Harry Potter World, Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey Ride (this one is awesome!), Kyary Pamyu Pamyu XR Ride (great ride), Evangelion 4D Theatre Ride (nice but the story ended slip-shot).  Be prepared to see a lot of "Hogwarts" students in Universal Studios! (Well actually a lot of people buy the Hogwarts Cloak and wear on the spot).
Long line in most attractions, but the long wait are very Worthed. Pick your priorities cause 1 day won't enough for all

I have been to Universal Studios in Singapore so I knew what to expect but if it wasn't for the Harry Potter attraction I would have made my biggest financial mistake so far. The lines were huge, 120 minute wait times to get in and everything was in Japanese so the Terminator 2 show was pretty much a waste of waiting.The food is about 1800 Yen and there is merchandise everywhere that is overpriced and junky ($15 for a pen)The Harry Potter attraction was awesome, the collectibles that you can buy- again are overpriced but they are cool. There are huge crowds though, no good opportunities for photos without a bazillion people. If you have young kids I probably wouldn't recommend it, the lines are just too long.

Been here 3 times in the past 7 years and this trip I was excited to see to new additions and improvements. New roller-coasters up. Went on a Monday and little to no wait times. Most wait was a 40 min wait on Harry Potter. Excellent.

Universal Studio Japan is one of my main destination. Because of the Harry Potter attraction. (Im a big fan of Harry Potter). I came to USJ on my second day in Osaka. It was on Friday and my japanese friend told me, that i should go there earlier. Then i come at USJ about 06:30am and i see the queue line infront of the USJ gate. Im so lucky, when the main gate open i get the front row queue. And i wait until 09:00am, when the enterace gate open, people just go run to the attraction. I run with another people for Harry Potter!! So excited but, i lost energy because it took about 5minutes run from the enterance to the Harry Potter attraction. Well finally after Harry Potter i ride the Spiderman, Jurrasic Park, The Flying Dinosaurs, Jaws, Terminator, 4D animation, back draft, water world and back to Harry Potter for the second time!! Haha And the evening i watched the Parade. It was great to spend my full day in USJ. So much fun! So if you want to ride more attraction, just come earlier!

For those who are fond of rides, you must plan accordingly because waiting in line will consume your time. For those who don't like rides however, you will still appreciate the structures in the park. There are also a lot more food there but just like any other park, it would more expensive than outside. There are also games with plus toy prize around so that's something else to do also. The shows are in Japanese so it will bore you and sometimes let you fall asleep if you don't understand the language. The starlight parade was very nice, that was a nice way to cap of my day in USJ.

for FOREIGNER/Locals using AMEX, Be informed The Universal Studios Japan and shops/restos at The Universal City Walk, (Except convenience store) ,DOES NOT accept American Express card which is kinda disappointing if you are an Amex user. Better ask the staff first before paying  Universal Studios is a movie based theme park so to those complaining, it is exactly what it is. and to those complaining that it is too crowded, you're on a theme park! That is exactly what you should be expecting The crowd at USJ is nothing compared to the number of crowds at Disney.  It is Our first time at USJ, and we are already planning to go back. The long lines of waiting is already given (Just the same at other theme parks), but we were lucky We went on a Sunday, from Kansai Int'l Airport (domestic flight) Exit at 1st floor. (Int'l Flight exit) then find Bus stop number 3, Universal Studio route. Tickets are available inside the airport or at the bus stop ticket vending machine round trip airport limousine bus tickets are cheaper, valid up to 14 days  We checked-in at the Hotel first and had lunch that is why we entered the park a little late (around 12 noon) (Better to buy tickets at The Hotel (just like we did, and Hotel accepts AMEX) or before-hand at convenience stores,or at the online ticket store to avoid waiting inline at the entrance) surprisingly it may have been crowded at the entrance ,but once the people dispersed and do their own thing it is not that bad as others pictured it.  We didn't purchased any express pass tickets at all, because it is absurdly over priced! We took the risk of actually going without expecting anything and it was worth it.  From 12 noon til closing and in between ,here's what we've accomplished with no express pass (I included the number of minutes we waited in line)  We were greeted at the Entrance by the Minions!  Jaws 45 mins. ✔️ careful not to get wet!  Harry Potter and The Forbidden Journey 45 mins!! ✔️, one of my favorites no english sub-titles but you'd get the idea. (keep a look out for the camera) Ride souvenir Photo is worth ¥2800  Woody WoodPecker (Animation Celebration) 15 mins. ✔️,would have been better if they atleast provided sub-titles for foreign guest. Since there's alot of guest complaining about not having sub-titles for every attraction  Terminator 2 3-D, 15 minutes ✔️, for me it's totally boring its like watching a movie at home but only with stage actors. I commend their performance ,but still it didn't make up for the lack of excitement of the show and again with NO english sub-titles Nothing exciting about it.  SpiderMan The Ride, 20 minutes✔️, another favorite 3-D ride this one i would love to ride again (keep a look out for the camera) Souvenir ride photo is worth ¥1500  Back To the Future 20 minutes✔️,cool but a little too bumpy, as in literally bumpy ride  and Our last was Jurassic Park, The Ride✔️ better get a timed ticket first, before you can actually ride,but totally worth it! another favorite  Flight of the Hippogriff is also 45 mins but we decided not to ride it Everytime we would stop by Waterworld our timing is always a miss, there's an alloted time for it in the end we decided not to pursue it any further.  We were able to see the Parade at night too, at 7 pm the park is almost half empty to think that it closes at 9 pm.  Better check the Park Website,for schedule because some of the attractions is closed  As for the snacks inside , if you've been to Disney many times you'll know that the prices isn't any different.  The Souvenirs and Other collectible items or memorabilia is really overpriced, yes! i am really comparing it to the ones being sold at disney, a pack of cookies here at USJ is about ¥1000~ almost every item starts at ¥1000~¥1200~¥1500 and more while on Disney you can find atleast a pack of cookies or candies at ¥500~¥800  All in all,even if the souvenirs is a bit pricey we did had fun the ambience of the park is different, it has it's own unique mark We will definitely come back again.

If you like "pushing the envelop" on your vacation time, if staying in Tokyo, then a day trip to USJ might be the ticket to fun.  We purchased the JR Pass for our trip to Tokyo because we decided to try and do day excursions from our base in Tokyo. We considered Kyoto but opted for a one day trip to USJ. We took the bullet train from Tokyo to Osaka and then the local JR train to Universal. It helps if you learn how the trains operate in Japan so that you jump on the right one. The bullet train drops you its Osaka station and you take a local train to the local Osaka station. There you hop onto the JR train taking you directly to USJ station. Walk off the train and you end up in their City Walk shopping area and shortly thereafter right into the park. I used Google Maps to route my clan all the way. Worked great. I misread the platforms and ended up on the wrong train and by watching my path on Google Maps was able to quickly jump off, go back, and reboot that path. We live near Universal Hollywood and hesitated going to USJ. We thought "maybe" we'd spend a few hours there just because we had the train pass and thought the bullet train trip would be the fun part. We found ourselves enjoying the whole park and, luckily, the crowds were too big and we got in a full adventure before needing to head back to catch the evening bullet train back to Tokyo. It was a long (time wise) trip. Up at 5 am to catch the 6:26 am bullet train out and returning on the last (JR pass free train) bullet train at 8:36 PM getting back to Tokyo near midnight. We figured the walk back to the hotel would be "spooky" that late but there were lots of people still out walking and at restaurants. Maybe a couple day trip to Osaka would have made more logical sense but we didn't have the days to spare. BTW, whatever you do, if you have a smartphone - either bring a portable wi-fi unit (I use XCom global) or order the Docomo traveler sim card that gets delivered to your hotel by them. My daughter and sister got the sim data card and they had unlimited service for 14 days and it worked great.

Do you yearn for the feeling you got from a mid-1990's visit to a Disney park? Did you enjoy the long lines, overpriced tickets, overpriced food, and confusing navigation (this was before Disney created the free FastPass program and remembered that they were all about their guests)? Then you are going to LOVE Universal Studios Japan!  For the entry price of 7400¥, you will get to cheerfully wait 3 hours (on a supposed "slow day") to enter the Harry Potter 4K3D ride, or you can wait an hour in the single-rider line for the Backdraft ride.  What's that, you say? "Backdraft", the unmemorable 1991 movie about firefighters?!?  Yep, there is a ride dedicated to it. Not enough nostalgia? Don't worry, there is also Jurassic Park. They also still have the closed-down Back to the Future ride on their park map (because, why bother providing updated info to your customers?). In case you would like to return to the 21st century, not to worry, because you will be assaulted on all ends with Minions. It is like drowning in a mumbling sea of yellow.  You say that you don't like standing in hour-long (or longer) lines at a park that is open for not even twelve hours? Well, for nearly the cost of a second entrance ticket per person, you can buy the "Express Pass" and get head-of-line privileges to four, five, or seven of your favorite rides. If you want head-of-line privileges for Harry Potter, you will have to shell out for the most expensive Express Pass.  Okay, so the one shining spot at USJ is the food. While the price is high, even for theme park prices, the quality is FAR above any other theme park food I have experienced (including Disney).  My final word is this: If you are looking for a theme park that aims to give a unique, authentic feel at every turn, and create a magical day each time you return, all for the cost of a single entry ticket… you are better off going to Disney. If you want to be monetized and feel like you are being shoved around, you might just dig Universal Studios Japan.

Universal Studios Japan has pretty much the same themes from other universal studios parks (Spiderman, Jaws, Jurassic Park, Terminator) except for the Resident Evil, Attack on Titan and the Wizarding World of Harry Potter (maybe a few I missed).  The attractions here are usually in Japanese so be aware of that. But the rides and attractions were still fun even though they were in Japanese. What won me over was the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Definitely beautiful and satisfying place for Potter-fans. I do recommend that you arrive before the park opens and buy tickets (fast pass if you can). When they start letting people in, go straight to The Wizarding World and secure your pass since they only allow certain time/people to go to avoid overcrowding. Try the butterbeer, The food in Three Broomsticks, and the Forbidden Journey ride (240min wait time, so go to the restroom beforehand). Of course, buy some HP merch to commemorate your visit and take plenty of pictures since this place is definitely magical.  I also like that they have Attack on Titan but a bit disappointed at the merch. The designs weren't really much to my liking.  All the other rides also tend to have really long queues (at least 130mins) since USJ really gets crowded. We were also there on a weekday (Tuesday) so I guess it would have been worse on the weekends.  Overall I'd say USJ is still a great place to visit, a must if you are a Potter fan.

We went on a Tuesday and because we had the Express Pass it was very enjoyable. We purchased the express pass prior to our trip on the USJ website with the help of a Japanese friend. Other comments have said that it's expensive - however if you compare the Universal Hollywood ticket with front of the line pass at $219, the USJ ticket with express pass is a steal at 13789 yen including tax (7400yen for the ticket and 6389yen for the express pass). Our time for our first express pass ride was at 11:10am so we didn't get to the park until 10:30am which was nice because there were no lines. We leisurely spent the day going from one express pass ride to the next and had a great time not waiting in any lines!  When we got to Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey the wait time was 200 minutes, but with the express pass we went right in. The confusing thing about that ride was the locker situation once you get inside. Be sure to keep all of the cards they give you and not put it in the locker as someone in our party did. They had to go back and get the card before they were allowed to get back in line for the ride. The ride itself was awesome! We would have ridden it again but the wait was too long.  The other rides that were awesome were the Flying Dinosaur and Hollywood Dream. After taking Hollywood Dream, we wish we opted for the backdrop. We thought we could do the single rider line for that but the wait was too long and the kids were spoiled from not having to wait in line all day.  Overall, it was well worth the investment to get the express pass. I don't know how you could ride all of the popular rides when the wait times are between 100-300 minutes. The Japanese are very patient and don't seem to mind. We would have a hard time waiting that long.  Another thing that impressed us was just how clean USJ was. We remarked on how spotless it was when we first got in and noticed that they wasn't even a speck of trash on the ground anywhere! We were even more impressed after we saw the parade which blew out millions of small confetti strips that floated all around the park! Imagine having to clean all of that up to prepare for another spotless day!
First, there were very long lines, even for a fast pass. The attractions were not actually that fun. The food was okay though.

I went on a Monday. I was prepared to queue to enter the park, so I went to the entrance at 8am, queued for an hour to enter the park at 9am.  I'm quite used to running in parks because I realized that Japanese fans are really hardcore and they run in parks as if it's a marathon. I joined them in the running, and ran with my family all the way to the Harry Potter world.  One word about the Wizarding world of Harry Potter, AMAZING! The theme song was playing, and Hogsmeade village and Hogwarts castle really look so beautiful and it made me feel so nostalgic. The first ride I went on was the Forbidden Journey ride. The queues are really long. Just fifteen minutes in the park, and the queue was 90 minutes long already. I guess it's still considered okay, as I heard some people had to queue for up to 240 minutes?? And hearing Hermione speak in Japanese was really funny and weird for me. And I didn't understand them too. :(  However, I would prefer if there were people guarding the queues, as there were a small number of people who liked to cut queues and would happily push those in front of them when the line wasn't moving fast enough.  The shops in Hogsmeade were really interesting, and butter beer was delicious! The food at Three Broomsticks was a bit expensive, but they were really yummy too nonetheless, and we enjoyed sitting at the deck where we had a nice view of the castle.  After lunch we went to Jaws, and again, the queue was long. The entire ride was in Japanese and I couldn't understand one bit, but it was really fun. I really loved the Spider-Man 4D ride even though it was a cartoon one. I expected it to be childish, but man was I wrong! The Terminator one was great too, but I couldn't understand too because it was in Japanese.  As I was not really a fan of minions or snoopy or hello kitty, and my main purpose of coming to USJ was for Harry Potter, I didn't really stay for the parade. I know there were events about Anime at the park too, but I didn't go either because I wasn't a fan.  We had turkey leg at tea time. I have to say, the turkey legs were quite small compared to those in Tokyo Disneyland, and they were really overpriced! On the bright side, they sold beer in the park!  Toilets were really clean everywhere in the park, and staffs there were really friendly and nice. I wore my ravenclaw tee, and many staffs in the WWoHP came to talk to me. However, as I couldn't speak Japanese, I couldn't really understand what they were saying, and could only smile and thank them (I assume they were compliments). Chocolate frog was expensive, Every flavour beans even more so. And everywhere was so so crowded!  Overall, I enjoyed my time in Universal Studios and would love to come back again soon. Hogwarts is my home, and being here was really a dream come true for me. Japan is such a great country with great people, and as I'm a great fan of HP, I would really love to come back to Japan and also to USJ again in the near future.

I loved it! It's awesome and I came on the 15th anniversary which was awesome! I had an awesome day at universal studios. It was so cool and we were having too much fun. It was too awesome to say but Hollywood dream is the first ride you want to go it because the lines are long and the sun is striking so backdrop is awesome, so as Hollywood dream! I loved the rides. The experience in universal studios was awesome. I hope I can visit again.

This is a major attraction in Osaka, and even on a rainy weekday during school time, it was pretty busy with some rides featuring 2hr queues. I can't imagine what it must be like on the weekend, school holidays or in nice weather.  As others have said, English is not well catered fore but it really was no problem. We avoided any "shows" and kept to the rides. All the signage is in English.  The main attraction is Harry Potter World, and the Japanese go crazy for it. The quality of the attraction is just exceptional, and any HP enthusiast will wander about revelling in the many details accurately reproduced. As you may read elsewhere, the HP ride produced extreme nausea for us, and it took about an hour for us to feel "right" afterwards. That said, how could you not do it?  We bought our entry tickets beforehand, which is a good puzzle because you can only do it in Japanese. You'll find instructions if you google around, and its a bit challenging because you can't use online website translation (one of the steps fails if you've translated the page), and one of the steps requires you to enter your name in Japanese script. But the detailed instructions we found worked just fine.  Do be sure to get a priority pass. As I said, even on a "quiet" day, all the good attractions had 1-2hr queues. The priority pass will also get you an entry time to Harry Potter world. If you leave this stuff until you get there, you may find the priority passes are sold out or the HP entry time is absurdly late. We purchased online about 5 days before, and even then found availability limited.  A side attraction at USJ is just watching the Japanese people themselves. Lots of them dress-up to attend, and you see packs of Minions wandering around and any number of Harry and Hermiones -- not staff, just people out for the day. Some of them dress as other things I couldn't recognise. It really adds to the vibe.  This is better than Universal Studios Singapore, but not as good as the ones in the US. Harry Potter World is definitely the highlight.

Prior to visiting the Universal Studios Japan, I read a lot on Tripadvisor as well as other blogs to figure out how to buy the tickets via the online portal (which is in Japanese). For those who are keen to visit USJ, I highly recommend that you buy the tickets online prior to going... and get those express passes as soon as you can. I had procrastinated in getting the tickets that one week before my visit, the express passes were no longer available for the date of my visit. Hence I decided to buy the VIP tour option which turns out to be a very good decision even though it was very expensive! Google translate helped a lot in navigating the Japanese website for buying the tickets online. :)  After printing out the tickets and invoice for the VIP studio tour, I arrived at the studios early in the morning with my friend, and got to enter via the special entrance for VIP studio tour guests. We were given a badge to wear (to distinguish us as VIP guests), 2 express passes, a free poncho, studio maps and instructions to return to the same room 10 minute before the studio tour timing. The 3 hours tour included the Spider-man ride, and all three Harry Potter related attractions. The tour actually comes with 3 express passes but one of the express passes is utilised for Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey... and so we only got 2 of the express pass slips to use for other rides.  It was nice to get ahead of the crowd that were still queuing to enter the USJ, and we got to take two rides (spiderman and space fantasy) with very little wait time. At the DragonBall 4D show, the wait time was about 30 minutes as most of the morning crowd had already gotten into the theme park. We decided to use up two express passes so that we can go for lunch by 11.30am and be on time for the 1pm studio tour. (Note that there are many different timing for the studio tour and not limited to 1pm.)  There are actually performances taking place around the USJ with specified timing, but we missed the performances as we busy trying to cover as many rides as possible. Without the express passes, the wait time for the more popular rides can go up to 100 minutes or more.  The VIP tour privilege also included 10% discount at the restaurants in the theme park... I also got a discount on the Butterbeer drink.  The tour was conducted in Japanese and so I have to admit that I did not understand anything that was said in Japanese. All the rides were also in Japanese.  The tour guide tried her best to communicate to us in English when necessary (e.g. on where and when to meet her after we were done with the Spiderman ride, and different Harry Potter attractions).  My favorite part of the theme park must be The Wizarding World of Harry Potter as I'm a huge Harry Potter fan. The Ollivanders wand shop was entertaining, the Flight of the Hippogriff looks friendly but was actually quite thrilling... and of course the best part must be the Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey. The ride is within the castle and we got to see the Moving Portrait Corridor before taking the ride. The tour guide also brought us to the toilet with Moaning Myrtle's speaking in Japanese.  A thoroughly enjoyable visit despite the pricey ticket, and attractions that are in Japanese language which may be a challenge for people who do not understand Japanese.

USJ was a highlight of my trip. It was a great day and if you get there early enough the crowds really aren't much an issue. 100% recommend to those travelling to Osaka, it's a great stop and the atmosphere is amazing.

We visited Universal in mid-June with one clear priority: our kids have to see the famous Harry Potter -themed area. Our friend warned us to buy Express tickets that would guarantee us the entry to the coveted Hogsmeade and Hogwarts area. He had learned it the hard way that this is not necessarily included in the regular one day entry tickets.  We used tips found in the internet and Google translator to navigate USJ website and purchased our tickets in advance. This service is not available in English (why?!), only in Japanese, but you can manage if you try. The bill for the four of us was 419 €, including a timed entry to Harry Potter area and The forbidden journey ride plus express tickets for three other attractions. Our tickets were QR codes we could print and present at the entrance and at the attraction gates. This system worked really well.  Our day turned out to be a rainy one, probably making the queues a bit shorter than average. Still, The forbidden journey had 110 min line (that we passed with our tickets) and Flying dinosaur 90 min, too much for us. Hollywood dream roller coaster had just about 40 minutes wait time right after the park had opened so we took it first, got to the ride in just about 20 minutes and had maybe our best roller coaster experience ever. We were really lucky to do this early, since later on the day we found Hollywood dream to be closed, apparently due to the rain.  The closed rides were one clear minus to the park: we knew well beforehand Jurassic park was undergoing maintenance, but could not fix our schedule to avoid this. But just on the day of our visit we learned that Shrek 4D and Space fantasy were closed too. If I understood it right, their hardware was used for other rides we were not that interested in (and the queues were long).  The park was not too busy so everyone got to enter Harry Potter area whenever they wanted and stay as long they desired. So we paid for this in vain. We also noted that except for the Harry Potters Forbidden journey, our express tickets were almost useless, since the lines for those rides were short even without express: for instance Jaws had 15 min queue, 5 min with Express. Consequently, around 4pm we realised we had taken all the rides we wanted to (that were not closed for some reason) and had the stamina to queue for. So we left, wet and tired, to retire to our hotel (of course, we can't blame Universal for the weather).  All in all: really expensive! Better have galleons with you, sickles won't be enough! Entry tickets cost around what you can expect, but Express passes, food, memorabilia, all leave the bitter aftertaste you get when you realise you are being ripped off. On the other hand many attractions and souvenirs are unbeatable fun (the Minion pop corn container!) and something you can't find elsewhere. Go for it if you're loaded, cheapo travellers should consider other options (available in Japan).  If it wasn't for the Harry Potter area I would need to rate USJ as **. But with Hogsmeade that really was created with ambition and good taste, we did not leave outright disappointed. Both kids and adults enjoyed the village, Three Broomsticks with butterbeers (strange flavor and really sweet foam), the whole package. So if you are a real Harry Potter fan, go for USJ and make sure you get to enter the area even if it cost you some extra galleons! If you do not like HP, you could save your money and go elsewhere.

So, I've been fortunate enough to go to Universal in Orlando a number of times. And that is just truly spectacular, as are the rest of the parks there. It's a bit unfair to compare the two, but you kind of have to.  It's very easy to get to, with a direct train from Osaka Centre. Ticket prices weren't that bad either.  We got hit with a rainy day, so it was umbrellas in hands for us the whole time round there. Everything is all in Japanese. And I mean EVERYTHING. Whether it's Hogwarts and the dialogue within this attraction, or another ride.  But still! I love stuff like this and it was great to be in such an environment still. I thought it was a fun day out followed by a nice dinner, typically at the Hard Rock.  If you have a few days in Osaka, I'd go. especially if you're with kids or a nice group of friends.

Yes, the place is a wonder to be in. You can spend all day taking in the magnificence that is Hogsmeade OR, you can make the most out of your day pass. For a fulfilling one-day visit, here are the 10 commandments to follow, timeless, tried and tested.  1. Pre-purchase your tickets. You can do it online in the Japanese version of the website. Use Google translate to get yourself through. Time spent queueing for tickets is time wasted.  2. Get the express pass 7. Your ticket price virtually doubles. It is worth every penny for ride lovers.  3. Plan your visit. Be early, enter once the park opens, and go immediately for the ride you do not have an express pass for, (in my case, the Flying Dinosaur). It will be your shortest queue of the day.  4. Pack food and drinks. Things inside the park are expensive. Though some are novelties that you may want such as the stein butterbeer mug.  5. Get the USJ waiting times app! It is a godsend to choosing which rides you want to go next!  6. Be aware of events. These events may have separate tickets sold. These events have schedules. Check the schedules online. Pre-purchase your tickets online as well. In my case, I missed the One Piece 2016 show which happens only on weekends, and I couldn't buy the Death Note escape room tickets.  7. Always have your Map and Timetable. These are your Marauder's Map to USJ. Especially the timetable. In between rides, we got to check out an Acapella Frog Choir in Hogsmeade, the One Piece water battle, Monster Rock Show and Minion Rescue. They run about 15 to 20 minutes each!.  8. Prepare for weather. We went during summer. So Umbrella and Sunscreen were a must. I also went during early spring, when an extra layer of clothing was a must.  9. Spend. Sure, we have limits. But you've already paid about 6500 yen for the entrance, and another 6700 for the express pass. Buying merchandise in USJ will never be the same as buying from ToysRUs. Spend and be happy.  10. Enjoy yourself. There is no fully exploring the studio, but there is a good chance you will cover all the adult rides (like we did) and it will be a wonderful, glorious day. Stay back and enjoy the USJ walk, Hard Rock cafe and Eggs n Things before going home.  Now, go forth, and see the Universe, padawan (wrong theme park reference, but who cares)

There aren't too many rides in this park for the larger kids and adults. Lots of stuff for the little ones. Minions Rebooorrn water party is a blast if you are prepared to get totally wet! Don't know what they are saying but everyone gets soaked. You can still watch the celebrations from the side if you don't want to get soaked. Harry Potter land is a lot smaller than Universal Orlando but for Potter fans, it is still amazing. More things to buy here so have your credit cards and cash ready. Great place to visit when it isn't too crowded (which is rare) but there are some days of the year when it has reasonable crowd levels.

You'd better get the ticket from the website; it's much easier. Moreover, if you apply a member of the USJ, you will have a discount in your birthday month. Buying an express package also a good idea as you don't have to queue up and waste your time. I recommend Spider man; ok for every age, but for Harry Potter: the forbidden journey, not recommend for elder people or those who have motion sickness or neck and back pain.
Very commercial. Extremely lot of people when we visited. Very long queues to the different attractions. The Harry Potter world was very good.

Am amazed at how USJ keeps reinventing themselves to keep the park attractive for returning customers.. Harry Potter, Spiderman, Space Fantasy, etc are great and Hollywood Dream is an evergreen attraction. The heat & brightness was searing in July... but the waits were not that long - esp. as we knocked off HP 1st thing in the morning. So all in all a good experience !!  Key improvement areas - vegetarian food & snack options - express pass availability every morning for at least an hour

My husband and I went to Osaka from Tokyo with the main goal being to go to Harry Potter attractions in USJ. I'd never been to any US but i'd been to Disneyland in Anaheim & Tokyo. I thought I loved Disneyland, but this was by far a better experience.  The wait to get inside the park was a little long, but this was the only time we really had to wait long at all. We purchased tickets and the 7 Express Pass prior to arriving and exchanged the vouchers on arrival. The express pass was 100% worth the money. When you only have a one day ticket, you want to make the most of it. Not only did this give us express access to 7 attractions. There were multiple where you had the choice of 2. So if you weren't too keen on Jaws, you could go on the Spider Man ride. Also I loved that not ALL of the express entries were timed. We followed the time tables for the ones we had to and then did the others when we felt like it. It was generous to, you had an hour for each timed attraction to visit it.  The Harry Potter Forbidden Journey was without a doubt, our favourite ride. The whole Harry Potter world was beyond belief for us. It was unforgettable as a massive HP fan. I highly suggest anyone who is going to the park with this as their main focus, get the Express Pass to fully enjoy it. I have heard when it's busy you have to get a ticket to enter HPW at all but it must have been a quiet day because we walked straight in.  Lunch was reasonably priced but merch was craaazzzy expensive. If you want to buy souvenirs bring a credit card lol.  A little tip to those who purchase the 'Magic' wands in Harry Potter World. I didn't realise when I was there but the wands work only in the park, once you leave they're just an ornament. Because I had no idea, I didn't actually use it in the park. So now I have a $50 wand sitting in a box at home hahaha.  The 4D (5D?) cinema experiences are amazing fun without having to go an anything that moves. I suggest those for being like me that aren't fond of roller coasters.  All in all, I loved it and can't wait to visit again.

If you hate waiting in lines, give this a miss. Even on the week days, USJ has become overcrowded. Try some of the other lesser-know theme parks around Kansai - they are more uniquely Japanese and fun!

Big dissapointment- nobody here speaks english. The staff gives misleading directions, if you are white , you have to wait years. All japans goes first, nevermind that you have expresspass. It is soooo crowded that waiting time for some of the attractions is 3 hours in narrow hot corridor. Disneyland in Tokyo was so much better!
It was really hot summer in Osaka when we went to USJ. Me and my son enjoyed the spiderman show, we went 2x! We would have enjoyed it well if there was an English translation. Or at least a subtitle

There is surely irony in the fact that this is a theme park designed for your entertainment and much of the day is spent in utter boredom queuing for the rides. Some of the day felt like an endurance test rather than a pleasure. I'm probably just getting old. It's been a very long time since I have spent this long in queues at any theme park in Europe or the US. Were the rides worth the wait? In all honesty yes but a little lacking in value for money due to the queues.

I just visited USJ in July 2016 and I never planned and was so nervous about one attraction or theme park. You hear of all nightmare queues in USJ and yes they are probably true. It's really the luck of the draw anytime of the year. One day it could be a 2-3 hr line up and next day 1 hr. Who knows. If you sort of want to keep some sanity and assurance it may be worth spending the extra for fast passes. That's what I did and paid 4500 Yen pp x 4 to get them. It's difficult to get esp if you are a foreigner. You can't get it thru USJ English site but only Japanese Site. So get your google translate ready or find a nice Japanese friend. I had so much trouble as they kept delaying ticket sales of FP on line during went I went. You have to buy 3 months in advance if you want to make sure of it. Next to impossible buying at door. You may luck out by having a hotel help you out if you arrive in Osaka /Japan before visting USJ. FP can range from 4500 to 12,000 depending on time of yr and how many. 4500 only got you 4 rides which ain't much. I used it for Forbidden ride (save me 2 hrs), Spidermans (saved only 40 min), Jaws (save 20 min), Jurassic park (saved 1 hr)  There is so much strategy involved and I didn't sleep for months thinking about best way to attack this beast.  Strategy:  Make sure you are there before opening. (we were there at 8am despite 9am opening) but with our luck they didn't let people in til 8:45  Do most popular rides first and furtherst first. Depending if you have fast pass or not. Most run to Harry potter world or Flying Dinasour. Since we had timed ticket for HP we went to Flying Dinasaur. We literally sprinted like running of bulls. Everyone from kids to grandma ran as gates opened. Crazyness. We did well and did flying dinosaur with no wait when arriving. That was a big relief.  Do popular rides right at end 1 hr before closing. We managed to go to HP world 1 hr before closing and did the Forbidden Journey for 2nd time and twice on Hypodrome rollercoaster. It was great plus atmosphere is nicer as no crowds around  Bring some lunch (onirigis) as no one checks and it save you a bundle. Let's you justify butter beer at 750 or 1250 with souvenir glass (frozen is best) but too sweet for my taste.  Do the singles line for rides like Space Fanatsy and Jurasssic.the ride and spiderman. Despite 1 hrs line it took 10 min in singles line esp Juraassic (did that 3 times in addition to the time with FP).  Waterworld was ok but you can go right at the time to bypass pre show where they try to wet crowd.  Try to survive til after closing and then eat along City Walk. Save you a lot as normal prices and lots of chains like Ootoya (slight prem 100 Yen from reg ones)  If you are staying til the end buy JR ticket before hand not when masses leave. I had JR pass so no problem  If it's your birthday tell a staff they will give you a sticker and then you will have 100 people hi fiving you and saying Happy Birzzzzday to you all day long  Attack Hollywood dream early - Fwd is fine... not worth extra time for Backward version. It's not a really fast or high one compared to ones in north America  Terminator was pretty boring for first 2/3 of show.... last part ok so no biggy if you missed out. But good place to take a nap in huge AC theathre for last part.  You may need gravol for some rides. Forbidden Journey is 5 min of simulation which can get some people. Space fantasy and Flying dinasour can also do it to the weak  KIDS loved it and thought it was the best part of their 3 week trip to Japan but they are harry potter fans. For me it was good and as long as they had fun you will too  So we did very well considering hitting about 8-9 rides attractions and doing multiple rides of Forb Jouney, Hippodrom, Space Fantasy, Spiderman, and Jurassic Park the ride  Favorites would have to be  Forbidden Journey (surprise sursprise) Flying Dinasour Amazing Spider man Space Fantasy  Ok was Waterworld Jaws Hippodrome  So so was  Backdraft Terminator  Hope this helps you plan and strategize. If you don't you can be in for big disappointment and waste of time  It was a very very tiring day....
Was great experience but without express pass you might have to wait for over 1 hour for some attractions.
We really enjoyed our visit to USJ! We all had fun. It's just really hot due to summer time. Would like to come back someday when it's spring, autumn and winter 😄😄😄

The park is in the city of Osaka, the roughly 500km from the center of Tokyo. If you are Shinkansen, Japan has the bullet, will spend an average of 3hs, making it impossible to make a hit and back, but being hosted in the city is very easy to get there. Then I'll tell you more about Osaka, but I say VERY worth the visit, just loved the city.

A great attractions. Easy to reach by public transporation. Attractions for all ages, however, you need to plan it carefully so that you get the most of your day. Reasonably priced and you have enough to keep you and your family excited for the day, if not 2 days actually. A lot of hotels adjacent to the park and plenty of restaurants in the park and right outside as well

My experience at USJ was SO MUCH FUN!!!  Just a reminder though, I recommend buying tickets (specifically ones with an express pass!) online instead of at the door as it saves a lot of time and prevents express passes to get sold out at the door.  If anyone enjoys thrill, I recommend these rides: The Amazing Adventures of Spiderman 4k3d, Flying Dinosaurs, and Jaws. I went to spiderman as my first express pass ride (around a 15-20 min wait with the pass) with NO expectations but I was truly shocked with how amazing it was. It was REALISTIC and I felt that I was literally on an adventure with spiderman. My second ride was Flying Dinosaurs and it was a 3 HOUR WAIT. Sadly, it wasn't part of my express pass and it was SUPER hot (be careful of summer weather everyone!!) but was it worth it? HECK YA IT WAS. I was impressed and shocked with how thrilling a ride could be!! Jaws was my second to last ride here but I had to include it as my captain? tourguide? was an impressive actor. His acting made us excited, scared, and breathe a sigh of relief after the ride was over. As my time here was great, I wish I understood Japanese as most rides were in the original language and I couldn't understand most jokes they were talking about but this place deserves praise!! I hope to come again to USJ in the future!! C:

I like themed parks, so really enjoyed here. Smaller than Orlando, Florida, but still worth it. I went in a holiday in October, and it was very amusing! Some people dressed in costumes, and zombies at night. There were really long lines (Harry Potter = +3 hours), so I skipped a lot of attractions, still it was a nice day.  This was my first horror night in a theme park, and I enjoyed a lot! The zombies wandering around at night, the attenction to details, it is really worth it!  I took 1hour30mins to Back to the Future ride and got a pleasent surprise! They change half the show to suit the Halloween! I wonder if others attractions would have these changes too, but could not check it out.  Next time, I'll try to go in a normal week day!  Tip:: Buy tickets before!  Bring an blouse that you can leave in a table to save your place. (I mean it! It was really hard to get a table to lunch! And everyone leaves something to "mark" the table... I had only my bag and did not want to leave it alone in a table, even though some people do it).  There's a lawson at the entrance of the park. But: At morning, it is crownded, have a very very long line. At night, there's almost nothing good left in the shelves...

We arrived at the area around 9am. Thanks to Tripadvisor, the hint of buying USJ tickets in Lawson (there is a big one just after exiting the train area) saved us from falling in line for the entrance. There are a lot of people since its summer and despite the super hot day.  We went straight to the Harry Potter area and you have to get a timed ticket (included in tue fare) to enter the place, its on the left side of the Jaws shark. The Harry Potter ride ate up 3 hours of our time and our patience was really tested.  After that we were hungry and thirsty and decided to go out. Once you are out of USJ you cant go back even if you request for a stamp in your wrist.

Universal Studios is a fantastic amusement park. The wizarding world of Harry Potter alone is worth visiting with fascinating shopping and wonderful food. The rides are spectacular and the recreation of a New York street in the 1950's was just magical.

As you'd expect, the park is fantastic. Having been at normal times, Halloween and Christmas, I can say it is entertaining regardless of when you go. Avoid public holidays- it is absolutely crammed. However, it's still fun if you're clever about queuing. Queues can get seriously long- especially for the Harry Potter rides. About four hours! They are enormous fun, but the only time I've decided I have enough energy to go on them is by getting a fast pass. They're expensive, but really worth it in my eyes. The Jurassic park rides are my favourites- especially the newest one. If you don't want to shell out for a fast pass (understandable), my advice would be get there early. The queues are still long, but at least you'll have time to queue for everything when you get in. Get to the free fast pass machines asap- particularly for Harry Potter world. Mind you, we've turned up at midday and still done pretty well. We almost never miss out on a ride.  If you are larger than the average Japanese person, check that you'll fit on the ride. They pretty much all have a test seat. The staff are really sweet- they will warn you that the seats are small, and offer to test you. Don't take offence- they are trying to save you from waiting for hours only to not fit and come away. The seats are almost all discreet, too, so don't feel embarrassed. I decided to just flat out ask on most of them, it saves time.  I 100% recommend going, it's excellent fun.
Universal Studios Japan is amazing.One of the more adult theme park. must see ..... We tried Harry Potter, Spiderman ride, patience is needed for the super long queue in Harry Potter
It was simply sees! Lots and LOTS of people. The lines are out of this world, the VIP pass is worth it, really. Went there just because of Hogwarts and I wasn't disappointed
One of the best place I have visited in Japan. Surely, you have to enjoy all of the rides in US, Osaka, Japan.
It's hot, it's crowded, and you queue for hours…. You even queue to purchase water…. Save your sanity and money and stay away.
Harry Potter attraction is a highlight. Otherwise superb just like any other Universal Studios. Easy to access with great parade show late in the afternoon.

Actually I just visited here for the WWOHP. The ticket was way expensive because August is peak season. We also bought the express pass, which you absolutely have to buy because the amount of people visiting is astounding. You have to wait in line for about 2 to 3 hours for the famous rides. My only problem here is that the shows are all in Japanese but given that maybe 90% of their visitors are locals, it's understandable.  If you have money and want to visit WWOHP, I would just recommend you go to US where it would be more enjoyable since you can understand what the heck is going in during the rides and shows. But since, for us Japan is easier to visit, we just went here. Despite the difference in language, I can say that I really enjoyed USJ!

It is big enough and entertaining enough to spend your full day there! Well everything inside was a bit pricey and especially the food wasn't very good for the price you have to pay so you might want to bring your own food but other than that, great! Especially Harry Potter section!
Place is great with the new added attraction Harry Potter. Place was too crowded went there during Sakura season. I suggest book on line and get express ticket.

Place that you can't miss if you are Harry Potter fans, like me! Purchase your ticket in advance or you will have to queue for 30 minutes to buy your ticket there. Suggest to purchase Express Pass if you have extra budget to spare so you could save hell lots of time to queue for rides. We ran to Harry Potter world first thing once we entered the park. It was so AMAZING! Had a very satisfying Butter Beer and lunch in Three Broomsticks. Not to forget they have Minions too in USJ! Well spent day!

We went there it was raining I hope they have something for rainig season. And the line is too long and staffs are bit slow bit good manner. It is fun I hope it was not raining and some of their staff a bit good. But it is good place to visit I liked it

We visited last June 2016. It was a Friday but to our surprise, the place was packed, mostly local tourists. If you are a Harry Potter fan, go straight to the castle since the queue for the ride is really, really, really long. If you won't ride, you can head straight to the souvenir shop. (But you won't be able to see the inside of the castle. As for us, we queued to see the inside of the castle, but we did not took the ride hehe.) If you are a Harry Potter fan, you won't regret it. The set is really amazing.  Just be prepared for the crowd. Long queues and all. I feel like its always packed all year round. (Except maybe for the winter)  Souvenirs are really expensive.

Great place to become a kid again. But the lines are a test of anyone's waiting skill thingie. If you have a serious injury or disability they will treat you with open arms. You will receive a special card that allows you not to line up. But you will still have to wait the required time like everyone else but you can sit down elsewhere or walk round and see the scenery.

For what it's worth, I only managed to catch Backdraft the performance. The queues & waiting time were too long for the rest. The Harry Potter enclosure was well presented with a well researched layout. Be there early & get an express ticket for your favorite rides, together with a corresponding time. It was Easter time & Snoopy was decked out in festive best - I bought a replica from the huge souvenir store. Hard Rock Cafe onsite was great too!

To be honest, it was quite a hassle to get to USJ - given that we had to transfer trains a few times and upon reaching there the weather just wasn't helping. We arrived there at around 1 PM on a Wednesday afternoon, bought the normal 1D passport and immediately went to get the Harry Potter timed entry tickets near the JAWS attraction area. We only managed to get the time slots for after 5 PM entry... Since we did not intend to go to other attractions, we stopped by the Pizza shop just next to Harry Potter's attraction.  If you are there, you should definitely try the truffle oil and seafood pizza !!! It costs about 2,800 yen + taxes for a huge pizza (6-8 slices). The taste was so unique that I still can't forget it now...By the time we got ourselves inside Potter's world, it was already evening time so it became much cooling!!  It was in fact, our second time there but the shops as usual were so crowded. They do sell a lot of the souvenirs on the pushcart shops outside the castle and within the castle shop after you have exited from the ride. There are actually two different queues at the castle - one for the ride, another for the castle walk. The two queues would intersect at the lockers area within the compound itself so that's where the things get messy. They could do with better crowd control in the future though.

I've only been at Universal Studios Singapore, but my friend who was a traveler and have been to other Universal Studios taught that this probably is the biggest Universal Studio theme park she had seen. Harry Potter was indeed a place/kingdom of it's own. Sad though because when we were there, it was raining the whole day (typhoon I think) but rain or shine, this trip is a go!

It's extremely popular so be prepared to wait in line. USJ is celebrating their 15th anniversary so there are a lot of people but they also added some shows.  A good way to avoid the line is to buy the Express pass. Buy ahead of time as they only sell a limited quantity per type for each day. Price of express pass also varies depending on the date of visit. Sometimes it can be really expensive. If you get the pass with the Harry Potter and Wizarding World rides you can choose the time for your entrance to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter.  Avoid weekends and holidays. Try to open the park to avoid the crowds.  They limit the number of people in the Wizarding World of Harry Potter so if it's a priority make sure to head there first, they usually require timed entrance tickets when they reach the crowd limit inside. Even the stores inside can get packed. Enjoy the frozen butter beer if it's available (Spring and Summer only). When you send a postcard from the Owler, there will be a commemorative Harry Potter stamped before it's sent to the post office.  Narrations inside the park will be in Japanese.  small kiosks close earlier than the park but those near the main entrance are open until closing. You can get Tax-free redemption for souvenirs you purchased near the main entrance.
Advise pre-booking fast passes for many of the rides. Wonderful day out and we got to ride all the rides we wanted. Just a great experience that was well worth the cost. Excellent rail access too!

The place was awesome. We went there during August, so it is hot since it is Summer in Japan. Tickets were bought from a travel agency, we bought the 1-day pass.  The first ride we went for was the Harry Potter: Forbidden Journey and then after that we went to tour the whole USJ and rode the attractions. It is just sad that we didn't get a chance to ride the Hollywood Dream and The Flying Dinosaur because when we decided to queue, the ride is already closed and they are just finishing the queue inside and letting those with the express pass to ride.  We went there during Summer and their 15th year anniversary is on-going, so there has been a lot of plays going on. AKB48 was there, the minions have a show, One Piece also has a show, there are rides and attractions opened just for the anniversary, and there are water guns everywhere (prepare to get wet).  Our day at the park was awesome and fun, the only thing we regret is not riding the extreme roller coasters. Tip is, if you have a one day only ticket to the park, get the map and assess how you'll ride each one. Make a pattern and take note of the waiting time. Rides like the Harry Potter: The Forbidden Journey, Spiderman, The Flying Dinosaur usually takes the longest queue. Have fun!

My family and i went to universal studios osaka and had such a great fun time!! my kids just loved all the rides and cannot wait to go back next year! love it xx

This place is cool. It has all the attractions you would expect. Jurassic park, Jaws, San fran. My favourite was the Harry Potter area. Which is identical buildings and hogwarts castle to the movie. One thing is to definitely get the express pass. The lines here are a but crazy even on slow days.

We have just arrived back to our hotel after the day at Universal. Was excellent fun! I recommend paying the extra and getting the express pass. We got the standard 4 and found it perfect for the rides we wanted to do (harry potter, jaws, jurassic park, spiderman). We are pretty tame and weren't interested in the big roller coasters so those rides suited us . All the speaking is in Japanese and a lot of the rides have stories that go with it which you can't understand if you don't speak English but this didn't detract much. We went on a Friday and it was pretty busy but if you don't like busy and crowds, why go to a theme park? Also take snacks, food is very expensive there!

dining there is definirely recommended and the restaurants there serving us is just wonderful, the friendly staff are just really really nice and im out of words to describe them. However the crowd was just too long and we had to queue a few hours just to get seats in each ride and upon looking at the other attraction's queues we just gave them a miss as the queue was just overwhelming. I highly recommend this place to you if you can survive the long queues, some are definitely worth the wait.

My daughter and myself spent two days here, my daughter loved the place so much she didn't want to leave. Even after 15 years the place is well maintained. Make sure to buy express tickets while you visit here or the waiting time for major rides is more than two hours on the weekends.

I went to Universal Studio Japan (USJ) with my husband and two kids (10 and 8 yo). We were going on 3rd week of September 2016, on a weekday, but just happened that a Typhoon pass by USJ on that particular day! Luckily we read the weather forecast a day before (make sure you always check the weather forecast before going) so we somewhat prepared both physically and mentally for the heavy rain and strong wind. The strong wind makes umbrella did not really work, so if you happen to have a typhoon on the day you go to USJ, make sure you also bring a long rain coat. Of course you can buy it inside USJ, but the price is not cheap, mind you! Probably it also help if you have plastic/rubber boots to wear on rainy day, because our shoes (and feet) were soaking wet. The good thing about heavy rain and typhoon is that I think we can consider USJ is not too crowded that day. Why do I know that? Because no timed entry tickets to go to Harry Potter wizarding world the whole day!!  Because of the heavy rain, we can not move fast, and the express pass came to the rescue!! It surely was very useful in saving times. So if you have extra budget and you are planning to ride the "best attractions", then I suggest you to buy express pass. Do not waste your time to but it on the day, try to buy it beforehand like we did. We need to let you know, though, that it was not easy to buy the express pass online, because the web is in Japanese. We got it with the help of our relative who can read Japanese and she sit beside us through the whole process of ordering.  We came in quite early, around the time the park is open. The theme of the park is already for Halloween, so it is "different". Some of the attractions also special only for Halloween period, but we skip those and only see the "normal" attractions. We can see many local visitors wearing Halloween costumes and scary make up despite the weather.... it is quite entertaining.  On that day we were able to go to Wizarding World of Harry Potter thrice; in the morning, in the afternoon and at night. We LOVE it there!! We had lunch on Three Broomsticks, try the Butterbeer there (it is a must!!!), my kids tried to use the wand (your own) to light up fire, we see owls that were used to send mails and packages, take photos infront of the Hogwart express, and many more! We only took The Harry Potter and The Forbidden Journey ride there, using our express pass, so it takes only around 5 minutes of waiting. Without express pass, the waiting time is around 90-120minutes! This ride is WOW!! It is a must!! But they are very strict with height restriction. So if you have little kid, pay attention to it. My personal opinion, for this ride alone, the express pass is already worth it. We did not waste our time queuing up for the Flight of the Hippogriff. We skip that attraction.  So, we got other express pass attractions. We had only 4 attractions (we bought the 4 standard express pass), so other than The Harry Potter and the forbidden journey, we choose The Amazing Adventure of Spiderman, Terminator 2, and Jaws. Out of those 3, The Spiderman is the winner. Terminator 2 is oke, but the long prologue by the comical Japanese woman, we can not understand it at all. Other than that, we queued for Jurassic Park The Ride (my kid loves it, so they went twice!), and spend quite sometime at indoor playground at Snoopy Studio in Universal Wonderland, because it was warm inside :-). There is a small roller coaster inside, so my kids play it a couple of times (very minimal queuing). When the weather cleared, my kids took the flying snoopy (also twice) just outside the indoor playground.  One thing that made us a bit dissapointed and found a little bit disturbing on that day is how difficult for us to find a restaurant that open after 3 in the afternoon. Every restaurant is CLOSED. The one that is open is only the snack cart for takeaway, and the line is awful!! We finally found one restaurant that open and we had our early dinner there, it was Mel's Drive In at San Fransisco area. I dont know whether it always like that or because of the weather or what, but it sure is a big minus for USJ :-(  After dinner around 7pm, when we walk outside, there were zombies (literally!!) everywhere. It was kind of fun, seing people fleeting and screaming when approached by zombies.... :-)) Before going back home, we stroll again to Wizarding World and saw Death Eater performance there. Not too special in my opinion. But the ambiance of Wizarding World at night is very special and more mysterious. And I suggest you to try going back there again after dark.  All in all, despite the weather, soaking wet shoes and difficulties to find opened restaurant, we had much fun at USJ!!! Do we want to come back again?? Absolutely!!

Entry tickets are the same as any Universal Studio around the world but the express tickets are expensive. We were there on a Friday and it was crowded. The express ticket is essential as waiting time for the popular rides are like 120mins. We chose the 6 rides express tickets but this was not excessive. The 4 rides express tickets are more than sufficient. Some of the rides like Backdraft, Space fantasy waiting time are not long. Also rides like backdraft is narrated in Japanese so for non Japanese speaking customers is a let down.

As a fan of amusement parks, I am always eager to try all the trilled rides, therefore an express pass is a must!! With the express pass, we don’t have to queue at all for the selected attractions.  Below are my comments for the attractions:  Jurassic Park: Flying dinosaur: extraordinarily exciting!! I really wanted to experience it again yet the waiting time for a second ride (>3 hrs) was simply tooooo long...and I would rather spent time on other attractions.  JAWS: unexpectedly fun as my seat was the closest to some of the sharks that popped up (my clothes became the wettest as well).  The Wizarding World of Harry Potter (P.S. The waiting time would be much shortened during nighttime): Forbidden journey: A bit unpleasant as you would encounter loads of dementors and spiders... Flight of the Hippogrif: Quite nice and excited The Dark wizards—The Death Eaters (Halloween only): The death eaters just walked straight to the stage without interacting with the audience and the performance was boring (some wizards waving the magic wands and gas/ light appeared).  New York & Hollywood & San Francisco: Spiderman: To me, this 4-D ride is more exciting than Forbidden journey. However, we were unable to focus on the ride as we were constantly disturbed by the crazily screaming ladies behind us. If we didn’t cover our ears, for sure our ears would be damaged by their high-pitched screaming. Space Fantasy: The spaceship would speed up unpredictably and revolve at times. I had so much fun riding it!! Terminator 2:3-D: We stood and listened to a staff member speaking in Japanese for more than 15 mins before the screening started. We had no idea what she was saying but the Japanese audience seemed to enjoy it. Backdraft (Halloween version): Not at all scary as we do not understand Japanese…  Universal Wonderland: Snoopy's great race & Elmo's Go-Go Skateboard: Fun for both kids and adults!! Hello Kitty's Ribbon Collection: The worst attraction in Universal Wonderland as I don’t like Hello Kitty at all  The only regret I have is that I was unable to get on Hollywood Dream as there were simply too many ppl queuing (>2-3 hrs). So, I will be back!!
An excellent place to unwind and enjoy the rides, food, entertainment. Need good pair of shoes to do all the walking. Fun place.

It was always going to be packed with people (which means the queues for rides will be terrible) BUT with a calculator and a game plan, it's possible to ride every single ride, and even repeat some of them.  Go early, right when it opens. Head to your favourite rides and instead of queueing up, get a Fast Pass ticket. Then queue up for 'lesser priority' rides as these will have shorter lines (under an hour). With a little luck and a Fast Pass plan in place (it allows you to get one every two hours), there is almost no downtime between rides! It's also okay to eat in line, but do this in the rides that don't turn stomachs upside down.  Bring an empty water bottle, so you can refill at many water stations and avoid the overpriced drinks in the park. Food is okay to spend on though, as the quality isn't too bad. A hat, a packable umbrella, and a fan is a HUGE help especially when lining up at Harry Potter World (separate review on that).  Souvenirs are expectedly expensive, but hey, it's a once in a lifetime thing for many of us.
-i really like the park and the shows are good. -The main event show was canceled, so i was very disappointed about that -too expensive; this includes entrance fee and food/drinks inside

Some lines we were straight in and some were longer, shorter depending on the time of day. The Harry Potter ride for example, we got in line for at the beginning of the day, it was about a 50m wait, however at the end of the day, around 8pm there was no line at all. The food is expensive but you're allowed to bring a backpack in so just stock up before you enter to save on money. All in all it was a great day and I would recommend. If, however you're expecting to go to an amusement park of this nature and complain about crowds and lines then maybe this isn't for you.

Other than, not being able to see all the horror nights attractions, it was a great experience!

We purchased the 7 ride express pass and it was well worth the money as some of the rides had over an hour wait time. Just outside the park are a large number of restaurants however if you leave the park you cannot reenter, food in the park was expensive and average I noticed a lot of people had brought food in with them I would recommend doing this.

This is the worst themepark I've ever been to. It's quite small and there was no issue whatsoever having time to do all the rides, we even went on some three times! The fastpass is an absolute waste of money, it's twice (!) the entry cost. The staff are also very inefficient, and even grabbing some popcorn will take you 45 minutes. The staff work very slowly, most likely to try and stop you from going on all the rides by having to queue for ages. Comparing to the usual Japenese efficiency, it's almost a disgrace to it. I would never visit this park again.

Japanese precision meets movie lovers delight. The rides are amazing! We loved the Flying Dragon, the Jurassic Park ride, the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, the Superman ride and Jaws. Make sure you buy the extra passes so you can skip the lines, but get these when you first walk in. Some of the wait times can be over 3 hours.

The main purpose is to visit the Harry Potter land. The place looks great but I personally find the rides and castle walk average only. The castle visit is too dark and not fantastic. There is no need to go for the castle walk if you take the 3D ride as you get to see part of it as you queue for the ride. The family roller coaster is suitable for children and those who can't take thrilling rides.  The wonderland is great for children and adults who can't take thrilling rides like me. The great race (roller coaster) is better and more thrilling than the Harry Potter roller coaster ride. The skateboard ride is fun.  I had seen the monster show years back and it was better. Maybe it was the performers. The shows were the same, even the songs seem to be the same.  The water world show is the same since years back. It will be good if they can change the show.  There are places whereby you can spend 500 yen and get a lucky sure win dip. The prizes are not fantastic but it is fun since it is a sure win. Suitable for young children. My girl had gotten 2 containers of wet wipes, 2 files and 1 lunch bag for 1500 yen. Not a bad win.

This theme park is very big. We can meet different characters such as minions, spiderman. There are many different kinds of roller coasters also, some of them combine with 3D such as the castle wallk in the Harry Potter Land. Although the roller coasters there are really good and exciting, we have to queue up for more than 45 minutes per game. I think it is not good for people to queue for such a long time, especially waiting in winter. I would suggest people to visit Universal Studio only once because it is quite expensive and waste time for queuing up.

Exciting place...its Fun..don't forget to take your photo in front of the Globe and pink cafe. Make sure you are full before you visit,because the snacks inside are slightly expensive then what you buy outside. Road parade is must watch..something similar to what they do in Disney land but its more fun ..

We visited here on a weekday in May, the week after golden week so we thought it may be a bit quieter. The park was still very busy and we had long queues for all of the big rides but still managed to get around and do everything.  I don't buying the extra fastpass tickets but would probably recommend other people do as it would have definitely helped a lot with the queuing. If you get there very early you may be able to skip queues on some popular rides too.  There is a great shopping/restaurant area just outside the entrance/exit.
Super duper fun!! Enjoyed the roller coaster rides and all the sights! Many pretty photo opportunities! One full day of fun!

First you pay a fortune and no one explain how the park works. My daughter(8) wanted to go to the elmo skate ride and because we were waiting for a long time, we thought we will go on the snoopy ride, only to be told is one or the other(wasn't unlimited rides?), so we had to cancelled the the elmo ride to be able to go on this one. Hardly anyone at the park understands english, every time I complained they gave a sticker! a lousy sticker, this place is a joke. The only saving grace was the Harry Potter Village but huge queues(1h20m). Couldn't even access WIFI. Very poor customer service

Think back to your childhood: Was there anything you did endlessly that parents or others had to tear you away from for mundane things like meal time or sleep? Not to mention the long waiting lines, I would say that this theme park is huge and offers so many fun places to explore. I spent most of my day at Harry Potter's area exploring the magical world of J. K. Rolling. I imagined that they invested heavily to create this place to reflect what was in J. K. Rolling's mind. You would never want to miss this place during your visit to Japan.

I've been to this theme park before and it was great. This time it was a total disappointment. I arrived just as it opened to find no express passes available, then inside the wait times for the rides were 180 minutes. After paying as much as you do to enter standing in line all day to get on a 30 second ride is not a fun experience. Universal need to limit the amount of people per day so everyone can have a good experience, this is just money taking.

Despite the similarities it shares with other Universal parks like Spider-Man, the Hollywood ride and Harry Potter World, USJ has its own quirks that make it worth visiting if you do have spare time. For example it has Jaws, which is extinct in the US, and unique rides like the Flying Dinosaur, the backdrop on the Hollywood ride and Space Fantasy which is super Japanese. Plus, even adults will enjoy exploring Universal Wonderland, themed around Snoopy, Sanrio and Sesame Street as it is so quintessentially Japanese. However I docked one star for 2 reasons: 1) the food is really overpriced, even more so than Disneyland and 2) maybe it was just me, but the staff that I had encountered were rude, especially by Japanese standards
One of our main destinations. USJ is not to miss. The Hogwart feel is so real. My family had fun. OTHER attractions are equally exciting
I guess a must do for harry potter fan, did enjoy myself except everything is in jpn. Also this is my first time to any universal studio, getting there is easy.

Special comment for harry potter forbidden journey, a very nice entertainment ride, better buy fast pass to avoid very long queue, but it's worth enough. Don't forget Try butter beer when in harry potter area.

We visited USJ on a Monday when the operating hours was 9 am to 8 pm. Queues for rides esp Harry Porters was loooong (2 hours on a weekday)...... but worth the wait. You need a special ticket to enter the Harry Porter zone. To get the special ticket ask the park guides for direction to the ticket machine. The other amazing ride is the 3D spiderman. Don't miss the live appearance of the dinosaurs at Jurassic Park. The kids will love it. Stay for the Christmas show. Its is called Angel something.... See Angels (real people, not robots) hover over the rooftop of the building The one day metro pass does not cover the entire trip on metro to USJ.

A group of six spent the day here and had a fun time. We did get fast passes which made the day considerably more expensive but it was great avoiding the long queues and meant we had time to see everything. We all agreed the Harry Potter ride was our favourite!

Universal Studios is an absolute must when visiting Osaka. There's lots to do and makes for a great day out. Harry Potter world was fantastic. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Don't worry if you don't speak Japanese. You can get the gist of what's going on on any given ride. Will definitely visit again when I'm next in Osaka.

Butterbeer is a must try drink at Harry Potter site. One drink with souvenir Mug costs ¥1,100  We didn't managed to q for the rides as the wait is simply too Long.  At least we managed to take a nice Spider-Man photo which costs us ¥1,500  Food is expensive thus sharing should be sufficient. You can also try to buy the cute Elmo (Xmas design) and hello kitty bun at ¥550 and ¥450 respectively. Do take a photo before eating!  Overall, I find it too crowded hence not worth the money especially a visit during the weekend.  Enjoy!

Be prepared to wait in queues for all rides. Went on Tuesday and not yet Japan school holidays and the average wait time was around 50 minutes without express pass.  Express pass could almost double your entrance cost per person and if you can afford it , it makes the trip more enjoyable and your wait time is reduced considerably. We got the standard 7 express pass and it included express pass to The wizarding world of Harry Porter which I reckon is the star attraction for most people.  We enjoyed the Flying dinosaur, Hollywood roller coaster, amazing Spider-Man and Harry Porter and the forbidden journey rides. Some are not for the faint hearted especially the flaying dinosaur.  The staff are well trained and they do speak English.  As expected food in theme park are not much value for money. Even the food outside Universal Studio are on the high side. If you can wait have meals away form Universal city.  The Gap department store outside Universal Studio has great bargains and extra discount for tourist showing passport, when we were there just a few days ago.

Went on a weekday (Fri). Arrived about 45 minutes before opening and queues were already super long. Crowded but orderly. Loads of students and tourists in queues.  Theme park opened about 25 minutes earlier. Though the park was crowded, single rider queues were pretty fast. Completed 4 rides before noon- using express pass or Single rider lanes.  Will be helpful if you plan the order of the rides. Some rides have really long waiting time- e.g: Backdrop. it can go up to 2 hours and no single rider lane. hence only express. But the express pass can be sold out really fast. Hence if you wanna try this backdrop ride, do get an express pass for this.  Went for the Harry Potter world of wizarding at around 2pm. On the day I visited, there was no queue hence its free entry for all. The crowd wasn't really that bad too and it was quite a fun experience. Really nice for Harry Potter fans! Just like you are in Hogwarts or Hogsmeade, just that its a bit small compared to the Orlando's. Had lunch inside the Harry Potter area. The queue at the restaurant can be quite a wait. the queue won't be visible from the outside, hence be prepared to spend some time waiting. Food wasn't really that fantastic, but it's kinda cool to be having butter beer in a dark restaurant looking pretty much like you are in one of the movie scenes.  The rides were quite fun. Roller coaster- flight of the hippogriff wasn't that scary, as it was more for kids. the other 2 rides and the castle tour were quite entertaining too.  You can return to the Harry Potter land at night, to catch a glimpse of how the place looks. So much like the movie, with the buildings and castles lighted up.
