Unless you bring your own, you'll be held captive to the long lines for expensive food. I bought a simple pizza for ¥3850! And it wasn't even very good.  For teenagers, I would recommend the following ; the flying dinosaur, Jurassic Park, The American dream, Harry Potter world, the flight of the Hippogriff. If there's time, check out sing on tour, terminator.  All in all, a good experience. But once for now is good enough
I love Universal studio especially the Harry potter castle. There’s are so much to do here and you can’t finish it in a day. If you want to enjoy your Osaka travel it’s a must to visit this place.

I would recommend that you buy the tickets ahead of time to avoid the long line at the ticket booth. There is a line also entering the park and lining up at the popular rides takes 45 mins at least. They are very organized so the waiting is not that bad. There are many restaurants inside which sold good food. The park is not as large as Universal Studios in LA, but it's big enough that you can try all the attractions all day.

You would need 2 days to experience everything. Son particularly enjoyed the sesame street stuff and spiderman. The harry porter world was surreal. Highly recommend that one would reserve a time ticket to enter. Went in the morning without much fuss. However, come evening, was refused entry as we did not get the time ticket. The wand was not fully utilized. Till next time, expecto patronum...

We went there on a weekday in October with two young school aged kids and I thought I’d leave a few tips for others who may be visiting the park while in Osaka. - Ticket purchase: buy them online in advance to save queuing up on the day. - Consider using ‘direct-in’ with QR codes on your phone. If you have small children and have to use only your phone to enter, this isn’t an issue either, just make sure you display each QR for each child at the gate. - If you have a Japanese friend, you can also ask them to help you order tickets through Lawson (Convenient store) and pay in any Lawson Loppi machine rather than ordering from Klook or Voyagin. - If your birthday is a month before or a month after the planned visit day, you can get discount, though to get this discount you have to go into their official web page which is in Japanese so this might not be easy. If you speak Japanese or have a friend who does, this could save you a bit of money. We saved 500 yen per ticket (family members are also entitled to the same discount). - Express Pass: choose the date/day of your visit and you might not need this. We considered spending £700 on the day pass plus Express pass 4 for four of us and in the end we didn’t and it worked out more than ok. (More details as below) - Pick a normal weekday and make sure it isn’t a local holiday etc and check the crowd forecast before booking your tickets - Arrive early because they often open earlier than the official opening time. We arrived at 7.10 for 8.30 opening and the gate actually opened 45 min earlier than expected so we managed to get in before 8am, gaining the valuable 45min to make a head start! When we went, the park was a lot less busy in the morning but as the day went on it was busier and by 1pm it was double the amount of people or more so use your morning time well! - Use your lunch time well, eat early or eat much later as people tend to go to take time away from going to attractions around this time. Strictly speaking no food from outside is allowed, and they do indeed check your bags from time to time, but you can sneak in a couple of rice balls or sausage in your jacket pockets (there is Lawson around the corner) to save you both the money and time to queue up for food at lunch time. - Use the board to check the waiting times for different attractions and be flexible in your plan - Take bottles to fill up water with so that valuable time isn’t spent on queuing at a cafe to get drinks etc - Check out the time for the parade and be at the start of the parade at least 30 min before to get a good spot - this is particularly important for those with small children as they can’t get a good view with too many people in front of them. The leaflet shows the route for the parade. - Harry Potter area: Previously you needed time entry pass to this area but these days it is a free entry area unless it is exceptionally busy. We had no wait time at all to get on Forbidden Journey first thing in the morning by just making a dash to the area (with two young kids too!) and going straight in. - Take disposable water proofs from 100 yen shop so that you don’t get wet when you are on some of the rides! - Don’t miss out the castle light up at Harry Potter area! It was meant to be at 18.55 (for the first showing) but it actually started at 18.30 presumably because there were a lot of people gathering already. This is in front of the castle, in the open. I would recommend you to get there at least 30 min early but if not, note you don’t need to be right at the front of the crowd; most of the entertainment is the light effects on the castle which you can see from quite far back so don’t panic if you don’t manage to get there early to get to the front of the crowd. - Wait time: remember that the wait time sign is often overestimated. This is the times and time we spent queuing at each attractions we went: 7:55am HP Forbidden Journey - no wait time 8.35am Jurassic Park the Ride estimated wait time 25 min but got on the ride in 10min 8.55am Jurassic Park the Ride (kids wanted to go on it again) same again 10min 10am Sing on (show) Got there 15 min early and we got in ok 11.15am Minion Ride - estimated wait time 50 min but it was only 30 min in the end 12.45am Amazing Spider-Man estimated wait time 75 min but got on the ride in 40 min Had Late lunch 14:00 am Went to get a good spot for the parade staring at 14.30 am. Already people taking up their spots and regretted not coming sooner. We spent the rest of the day visiting different areas covering different street shows etc. My final and perhaps one of most important tips that I can give to families with children visiting USJ... Do take your kids to toilet before queuing for each attraction! Despite taking kids to the restroom regularly, we still got ourselves in a situation whereby one of our kids went, mummmm I need to go to the toilet half way through a very long queue with no option of going back!! Luckily the queue moved quickly and she managed to hold on till the end of the ride, but it was pretty stressful!! Oh and have a chat with kids to decide on a memorable location to meet in case you get separated. We decided that beside the dinosaur at the entrance of Jurassic Park area was a good place to remember at the start :) We enjoyed our visit to USJ (though it was VERY tiring lol) and hope you will too!!

We took my sister for her birthday and it was the best birthday ever! You can get a birthday sticker from any staff member in the shops and when staff see you wearing it, they wish you a happy birthday! All staff, in the street, at rides, at shops and even serving staff in restaurants (they list it as an item on the receipt so when you collect your food, all the staff know).  It rained a bit while we were there which kinda sucked but it wasn't heavy rain so it's didn't stop any rides or shows.  If you want to make sure to get on every ride, you should definitely buy the Universal Express Pass (you can buy tickets online even if you don't live in Japan, you just need a credit card). The queues for most rides are in excess of 120mins at any time of day. Express Pass will have you on the ride in less than 15 minutes.  Best rides to experience: The Flying Dinosaur (roller-coaster), Hollywood Dream (roller-coaster) , Spiderman (4D moving cart on a track) and Harry Potter Forbidden Journey (4D moving chair on a track).  Merchandise is far more expensive than other theme parks in Japan (such as Disney). But it's very good quality in most cases. You can get very cool light up goods for the night time, unique goods exclusive to the park and many fun headbands and hats to show your appreciation for characters.  The food is very yum, we really enjoyed eating at the Three Broomsticks in the Harry Potter area. It was very western cuisine such at pot pies, salads, whole corn on the cob, chicken with mashed potatoes etc. Felt a lot like being a student at Hogwarts for sure! And of course, during winter the hot butterbeer was a delight.

Before you enter the park , they need to check your bag very detail. You are not allow to bring food, drinks, some camera and video equipment and a lot of other rules. You should check at the website. The park interior is so cute and pretty for christmas. A lot of ride is challenging for adult than disneyland. Before you come check the schedule carefully. May be because we don’t come on peak day the park close earlier and there’s no night parade. They only have christmas show not parade which make me feel dissapointed at this point.
Great place for kids and teens. The rides were fantastic although queue was long. But still enjoyable

We arrived at 9.30am (normal entry opening time) the entry was jam packed and people were everywhere, but the staff were efficient and lovely. I would recommend going to Lawsons' just after getting of the train to grab snacks and lunch as they have a great variety which is fresh and healthy but also at a great price. We headed straight to Harry Potter and were able to get on the rides there within 30 minutes each. The trip around the studio was fun however, line up/queue times were what we spend the bulk of the day doing. If you can afford it get the express pass available. You could actually spend a couple of days here if you have the time. We all agreed that the best ride was Hollywood Dream the ride, this also goes backwards but had an extended wait time. All in all a great day.

What more can I say...it's a magical place to be! We were fortunate to come when there not too many people. We didn't even have to line up for the Harry Potter area. The attractions did not disappoint. There were places where we could refresh ourselves from the heat, love those water mist sprayers. Clean. Super cheerful and attentive staff.

I enjoyed our visit at USJ. This is not my first time but I still had a lot of fun. The rides will either make you go scared or crazy with its twists for you to enjoy. Although it’s a given that there will be a long line to some of the rides still, we’ve managed to try out a lot of rides. Regarding souvenirs, food and other stuff..there are some that price is reasonable. So no worries, you will still enjoy USJ without getting broke

Visited USJ in late November. I was contemplating whether to buy fast pass. However, due to the high cost, i have decided to give up the idea. Arrived USJ before it opened. Waited outside for almost an hr before we are allowed in. Once in, we proceeded to the popular rides first. To our surprise, though there's queue, we did not wait long to get on the rides. On average, we waited for an hour or less to get on the rides.

We had an extra day in Osaka and decided to visit Universal studios with our 7 year old. It is highly recommended to buy entrance tickets ahead of time (available here on trip advisor) and show up at least 30min before opening to take advantage of the first 30 min when waiting time is low. We bought the 4 ride express pass at the gate and while it saved us about 30 per ride on a rainy Monday in December I believe this is a must for weekend visitors during peak season. Harry Potter ride and experience was great and very impressive, we also enjoyed the minions and Spider-Man as well as the traditional roller coasters.
Absolutely fantastic day and a half spent at Universal Studios Osaka, Harry Potter Wizarding World. The activities with the Universal Studios wands is just magical.
Do come early. Many people running at the start to get on the rides with shorter queues. You snooze you lose

Got to get there early before the park open. Japanese are crazy about the amusement park too. So there will be a long line at the entrance. The Harry Potter section does not require special admission so you can go in. But super long line for the line. At least an hour or more. It is very tiring to go during summer time. The weather is hot and th Elaine is long. Be prepared to suffer😂

Our second visit. We did not spend time on the rides and our main purpose was to spend time on Harry Porter area and to watch their Christmas show. It was fun for the children at the Harry Porter area to use the wand for various actions. The special effects of the show were commendable.

Universal Studios Japan is enjoyable for both young and old. The attractions here are different from what you will see in other places. We were particularly awed by the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Most of the performances were in Japanese but the staff should be able to help you with anything. A day will not be enough to see all the features, 2 days should be enough. The lines for the rides are long and so it is best to go early. There are plenty of food stalls and restaurants in the resort. Try the Butterbeer!

- all great experience, actually in comparison to US Singapore it seems more spacious and more well maintained - we enjoyed most the Minions, Hello Kitty & Harry Potter - it was Christmas season so it seems extra special as everywhere playing Christmas songs although it was chilling 🥶 cold

Worth to go, I suggest you buy the express pass, really worth it to skip the long queues since they limit the pass (200 per day), so plan ahead which ride you prefer the most and buy the express pass accordingly, my kids can cut 50 mnts queue to only 10 mnts with the express pass

Went here on 31 Dec 2019, family trip with 2 small children (8&5).  As any major tourist attraction in high season, it is very crowded. Everything from entrance, rides, restaurants and toilets needs queue.  As a very large park, USJ managed well with the crowds. But unfortunately is very tiring to get from one place to another.  We entered and went directly to Harry Potter ride inside the Hogwarts castle. As a huge fan, almost all of the things in the HP world brings a smile to my face (but butterbeer is overrated to my muggle taste).  Next to Jurassic Park, had lunch which is expensive and tasted average, but no other option. My wife who is an adrenaline junkie loves the Flying Dinosaur. Using single line, we didn’t wait too long for her. While waiting, the kids enjoyed My Friend Dinosaur parade. Then we all went for Jurassic Park the ride and got a little bit wet and cold (winter, duh).  After Jurassic, went to Snoopy area, and queue to flying snoopy, but as the Express pass holder entered and entered the line, the reguler line didn’t move at all. We then gave up for the flying snoopy and went indoor for the snoopy roller coaster, a little queue there. My little boy enjoyed Elmo’s car. Then we went up the carousell but after a 10 mins delay, they announced that it was broken and we were asked to dismount.  Then we went to watch SING theatre, quite entertaining and a good rest as it is sitting down for around 10 mins.  Unfortunately we just found out that on that day, the park closed at 5. We misread the info that the park is open for 26 hours. Indeed it is open till midnight (fireworks show) but after 5PM, you will need another ticket to enjoy the park after hours.  So after finding out that the park is closing, we only got the chance to ride one more which is Minions Race, just a spinning ride.  Overall, the park is very enjoyable eventhough crowded. All of the staff is very friendly and making the guest experience very enjoyable.  Recommended for everyone, and if given the chance I will come back again with my family as we only rode less that 25% of all of the rides.

It is a beautiful park, many attractions. But if you are an obese person, you will not enjoy it much. Because in many of the attractions you are already invited to sit in the chair to know if you fit or not. I understand it's a security issue, but intimidating and an embarrassing situation.

We buy the ticket thru online. Well this place is a must if you come to osaka. You will love everything inside here. Till today i still remeber everything. Keep in your mind this place will be full with the people. Just que, wait your turn and enjoy the ride. If you have an extra money, please buy express ticket if you dont like to waiting too long.
Gosh the Japanese really know how to make people feel welcome! Everybody were smiling. Rides were cool. Food is expensive but really legit yummy! Loved everything!

We were there at 8:30am and the lines were okay for an off peak day. The problem was that unlike Singapore, they bag check everyone. So once the doors opened, it was another 30mins to get in. Unfortunately the Hollywood section was closed which was really disappointing. The lines were insane - even on an off peak day when the park was at 15% capacity lines were still over an hour. We had a fast pass 4 and that was worth it, the rides we used it on had 60-70min lines and we lined up for less than 10mins each time.  There are minimal places to sit down around the park and I got told off quite a few times by staff for sitting on a garden bed edge or on a curb due to the lack of seating. I have an injury so the lack of seating was a real issue for me.  Be aware everything is in Japanese - none of the rides or 3D sections have any English parts. This means terminator, Harry Potter, backdraft, Spider-Man and jaws have NO ENGLISH at all so you have to just enjoy the ride with no idea what’s actually being said.  It was good fun for a day but at close to $200 AUD each for entry and a fast pass, the Singapore one is much better.
Very good. We are planning to go for the second time in this japan trip. Trust me this is worth the money and time!

Our 11 and 8 year olds picked this cos of Harry Porter and it was worth it. I personally am not a roller coaster fan but by the end of the one day, I must admit it was lots of fun. Plenty of screams and adventures and would advise the purchase of express pass unless you have lots of time to sit in the queues

I've visit disneyland and disney sea last with my family..and have a great time there..while universal from my personnal point of view is giving a different taste. Enter this park just loke you've been taken to the hollywood side since so many ride which related with the hollywood movies however the explanation is in japanese.. Really have a great time here...
Veryy nice to be here and everyone's dream world . Feel crazy when met a snoopy, sesame street,driving Spiderman Race and Harry Potter

Nice place to be there but there was so many people. If you intend to play, its best to buy the fast lane tickets so that you can enjoy it. I didn't have the time to enter bcos of so many people there & the queue was terrible.

We visited on New Year's Eve and bought a pass for the day and the party that followed. The park is definitely similar to the US equivalents but a fun place to be and high quality! We went on the Jaws ride and it was fun. Of course it is all in Japanese but that is fine. After all you are in Japan. The Back Draft experience was fun for us but there is a lot of fire so if you have small children it may not be for you. Spiderman was very fun. Terminator 2 was okay but Spiderman is better if you have to make a choice. Sing the musical was okay but more so for kids. The Harry Potter ride was really fun but a lot of motion. My stomach was a little queasy but only for a short time. Great ride overall. Be sure that you understand whether the ride is open or not, We ignored a sign (or missed it) that said it was only a castle walk through and we waited in line a long time only to have no ride. We went later and it was outstanding! It would be nice if they had a fly over ride that had a big screen overview of Japan like California Disney has but alas, there is not one. Nice park and lots of good restaurant choices there as well. Expect Universal prices in the stores, but the restaurants were not overpriced as far as we were concerned. Of course we do not have children.

We bought a ticket to the park so we could go during the day for a bit and then we left when they closed the park for an hour and rentered with the party entry ticket. Fun to walk around and see all the decorations for Christmas. The live entertainment was fun to watch from a distance but we did not stand in that area for very long as we wanted to experience the park. It was cold and crowded, but we were dressed for it. I did buy a Jaws Hat and would have liked to have the royalties on the hats as they sold thousands of them! They do keep your head warm! It was crowded but we worked through the crowds and got on the rides that we wanted to. The Minions and Harry Potter was where the big crowds were. The fireworks were fun and it was great that the park was open all night! Overall we had a great time. We had my niece who is 27 so 3 adults. Glad we went in during the day and had fun at night! Only giitch was the tight crowd pushing and shoving toward Harry Potter when the fireworks were over. We enjoyed it!

If I was rating just the park I would of given a 4 star but due to the staff all being fantastic it’s gone up to a 5  The actual park is not the biggest and several rides are very dated now and need changing eg .... Back draft ride ... I’m 40 and even I don’t remember when that film came out or what’s it was about .... apart from fire lol Terminator 2 ride was very slow and dragged , jaws classic ride can’t fault it , Spider-Man great , The pterodactyl ride in Jurassic Park was amazing and Harry Potter world didn’t disappoint  The late night parade was good and great effects  We went on Feb on a week day and the Qs were only half hr max so no issues there  Would recommend for a day out lots of fun and the staff were all fantastic

Went there on Monday. Booked tickets from the Klook app and got the special entry. Managed to go in 15 mins early than the others. my first ride was the Harry Potter ride! took a lot of pictures with less crowds in it. love the butter beer (Non alcoholic drink) will definitely go here again in the future!

Make sure to get an express pass ticket because there are long lines at Wizarding World of Harry Potter, and sometimes they only allow a certain group of people to come in here during peak hours even if you already have a ticket. The rides are also quite long so the express pass comes in handy

My experience in this park is better than the original Universal Studios in Hollywood. The waiting lines are not crazy and the rides are so worth it. My favorite is Wizarding World of Harry Potter. It's like you literally stepped into the movie!
Your Osaka trip is not complete if you not coming to amazing place. Great rides, great game and movie. The environment is just like the movie!!

We live in Kansai and were able to visit in July 2020 during the restricted entry for local residents. We went on a weekday and there were no lines or large crowds. Everyone of the USJ staff was very happy and friendly. It was remarkable and added to the fun experience. **TIP** Download the USJ app on Android or iPhone. The map feature is excellent, you can save favorites and there is real-time information about wait times for the attractions. The Harry Potter Journey was incredible. It did make me dizzy and nauseous afterwords however. Overall it was a very fun day and we were able to see/do everything we wanted in about 5 hours because there were no lines or wait times for any of the attractions or restaurants.
The experience was the best we have had at an park attraction. So many cool rides and Harry Potter was out of this world...I'd pay just if it was only that section.

This was for my sons 10th birthday and my wife is also a pretty big Harry Potter fan. So the The Wizarding World of Harry Potter was the main reason that we went but there was plenty of other things to do and see. The rides we enjoyed were: Despicable Me Minion Mayhem, Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey and Flight of the Hippogriff and Jurassic Park the ride (the last 2 were actual roller coaster rides, the other were 3D/4D rides). All of there were lots of fun but I prefer the actual rides to the 3D/4D rides. Make sure you get some Butterbeer - it tastes awesome. Also another tip is to go early or late for lunch as there can be a bit of a wait (also depending on where you go it can be a little expensive) Over all a fun filled, exhausting day that the whole family enjoyed

We went Universal Studio on Monday 3rd May. I purchased the tickets online http://www.rwsentosa.com/Attractions/UniversalStudiosSingapore . As it was a Monday, so the adult’s ticket is $ 68 and child’s ticket is $ 48. We bought the express tickets @ $ 30 each. We actually printed the tickets from home.  The official opening time was 10.00am but we were allowed in early at 9.30am for photo taking sessions. The 1st session of the park is Hollywood. It had the merchandise shops such as Universal Studios Store, SuperStar Candies, Star Characters etc.  Total 22 rides but only 18 were open now.  Our experiences told us if we start from the RIGHT side of the park, we should beat the crowd. However we turned LEFT and joined the crowd.  The 1st left turn from Hollywood, we came to Madagascar. I thought the ride King Julien’s Beach Party-Go-Round was really child-like. I found myself fighting with other kids to sit on Melman the Giraffe.  Next we came to Far Far Away. The 2nd ride we sat was Enchanted Airways. It was a junior roller coaster with height limit of 92cm. Because of the express tickets, the wait was 5 mins. We managed to get front row seats at Shrek 4-D Adventure. Besides having waterdrops splashed onto us, we also had wind blown onto our ears. The scariest part was when the spiders in the 4D show escaped, they sort of appeared like that they were on both my legs. While I don't really recommended the front rows especially if you have kids with you, I think a better choice will be 3-5 rows so that the screen will not be too near. Donkey LIVE is an ok show, more for the kids. Skip it if you have no time for it. We also sat a miniature ferries wheel Magic Potion Spin which is in Godmother’s potion Shop. This spin is really more for the kids.  We had lunch at Friar’s. Their generous servings of the potato chips were delicious and the chicken wrap was huge. Each Combo meal cost $ 8.80 and comes with a wrap, a drink and generous serving of potato chips. The kid’s meal even came with a lunch box. I would also recommend lunch at Goldlilocks for its fried chicken, fish & chips and chicken sandwiches.  At the LOST WORLD, we queued for a ride on Canopy Flyer and had Dino-Soarin rides, more meant for kids to pilot their Pteranodon, up and down into the clear blue sky.  I love Ancient Egypt!!! We were transferred into the ancient world just like in the show MUMMY. The ride Revenge of the Mummy has a height limit of 122cm. You have to lock your bags in the lockers for this ride. Such a thrill!!!! We were plunged into total darkness on this indoor roller coaster! My 8 yrs old girl never once opened her eyes. When we looked at the photos taken during the ride, you can only see our heads not our faces because more than ½ the time, our heads were hung low.  At Sci-Fi City, the 2 BIG RIDES – Battlestar Galactica – CYLON & Human were closed.  Next we sat on Accelerator that spin and whirl you round and round like the little tea cup that you sat when you were tiny….  Back to Lost World, we caught the show WaterWorld. I don't know what to say about this show. They had some fun bits where they splashed water on the audience. Other times, the effects on the bombs and “voices” did not really match….overall it was still a big show and they only showed it 4 times a day. Be sure to catch it.  We saved the best ride for the last…..At the LOST WORLD, Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure is 1 ride that you can get all soaked up! While it was not a MUST to have the raincoats…it depended very much on which side you were sitting when you went down the slide and there was no way to determine if when you pick your seat. So good luck…. We were facing downwards on the slides….poor guys…I practically saw water poured over the 3 of them (not us)…they were soaked through LOL.  Overall, the park was not big and with express passes, it still seemed everything was done in a rush…..We were practically running to the next ride after every ride. We only stopped for lunch for maybe 45mins.  A pity though....They do not have many characters on the streets for photo taking. I only saw kong fu panda, betty…then there’s some silly mummy guys and robots type walking on stiles….  Plenty of choices on your meals and no Q at the toilets…..I would even rate the rides as COOL……  Without express passes, the wait is about 25-70 mins, compared to the 5-10 mins wait. Express pass can only be used once per ride. It cannot be used again for the 2nd time.

I went there with my 4 year old son and he had a great time : ) We couldn't finish everything in a day so I upgraded my ticket to an annual fun pass as we are staying near Sentosa and I could easily see myself bringing him there more than 5 time in a year. In addition, I enjoyed looking at the merchandises in the shops as I've not seen such items sold elsewhere. Maybe because it was my first Universal Studio experience.  I was not disappointed that some rides were closed as it was clearly stated on Universal Studio's website and again on the notice board before the enterance. It's their soft opening and Universal Studio compensated ticket holders with food and retail vouchers. Thus, I could not understand why there were reviews complaining about the closure of rides.  The Sherk 4D adventure was great and I loved it. I felt that it was comparable to Hong Kong Disneyland's 3D Mickey Magic show. The difference is that Sherk has more thrill factor while Mickey Magic has more fun factor. My 2 year old girl had her first 3D show in Hong Kong Disneyland and enjoyed it tremendously but I can't foresee myself bringing her for Sherk 4D in Singapore as it could be a little too scary for her. Guess she will have to wait till she is 3+. FYI, children age 3 and below do not need a ticket as they get to go in for free.

Be warned that if you plan to go to Universal Studios on Sentosa Island then you must pre-book your tickets. We didn't find this out until we had paid to take the monorail across, walked all the way to the gates and found a Booked out sign ! Our girls were terribly disappointed and it completely wasted a whole day. There was no warning, signage or advice that tickets were limited and as seasoned travelers to theme parks all over the world I have never come across this before. In a way were were relieved as we found out many of the rides are yet to work properly and that the park is not yet fully functional. Sentosa Island is still very much under development with lots of construction zones and not really worth the bother - the only highlight was the MegaZip and Climbing ropes at the Adventure Zone. All the other attractions were very expensive and short thrills. The beaches are clean but the water is very murky and no-one swims.

The US version is definitely better, but for most people who can't fly to the US, this is probably the best and safest theme park in South East Asia. It is very family and disabled-friendly, so people don't have to worry about wheelchair access.  It is also a blessing that the theme park is rather compact. I could not imagine walking around a bigger park in hot tropical weather. Of course, it also means they can pack less in.  Rides are quite tame, probably to suit cultures that are not used to roller-coasters. The Mummy and Lost World rides that I enjoyed in LA have been toned down, but are still thrilling. These two are probably the best rides in the park as a number of rides, including the Battlestar Rollercoaster, are still closed. I did not try the Shrek Rollercoaster due to long lines.  What I did enjoy were the performances. I enjoyed Monster Rock, a 20-min dance and song performance, enjoyed in the comfort of the theatre. Water World is still as fun, but wetter. The actors obviously enjoyed getting normally straight-laced Asians to scream, shout and play along. Donkey Live was so-so, but Raoul was a great MC and added a lot to the show.  All in all, I had good fun and was entertained for a good 8 hours. :) Check ticket availability in advance, or buy them online, as the tickets are often sold out.

I was very disappointed when the ride I wanted to try; Cylone and the Human were both closed.Then to add insult to injury,when I decided to go on the Mummy ride,it was closed too!I just wish they could open all the rides at the same time!

Went to Universal Studios Singapore with our 3 Children 7, 5, 21 months. Its a decent sized park but you can cover it all in one day. It's more geared at kids 5 and up, not a lot for 2 to 5. There is a merry go round and 1 car ride. The park is broken up into different sections- Madagascar- There is a Merry Go Round and the Madagascar charcters do a dance there every so often. Crate Adventure is opening soon. - another ride. Far Far Away- There is the Shrek in 4-D , which really is a 3 day movie with some wind /rain effects . Good for all ages. Kids roller coaster -fun 5-13. Donkey live is a intercative show with the Donkey from Shrek. Not bad , not great. Kids liked it. Lost World - Water World . Stunt show based on the movie.. Its a must see! Canopy Flyer- Cool roller coaster ages 5/6 and up. Warning! long line for a short ride. Dino- Soarin - Little ride for 4/5-10 year old. Jurrasic Rapids - Is a very cool ride. Age depends on your kids my 5 and 7 year old were a bit scared of the last part of the ride. Not crying scared but when asked if they wanted to do it again - Thats ok was the answer. There is also a rock climbing wall- which we did not do. Ancient Egypt- Revenge of the Mummy Roller Coaster- Indoor coaster ( ala Space Mountain but scarier) I think your child would need to be a tall 7 year old height wise., but they shoudld probably be a bit older really otherwise I think too scary. Treasure Hunters- A car goes around a track verrry slowly- if the line is long give it a pass and try back later. Sci Fi City - Battlestar Galactica ( Roller Coasters) - have not been open in along time . There is a technical problem which they are still working on. Accelerator- A ride for older kids/adults that spins and spins/.. Tarnsformers is opening next year. New York NY - Lights Camera Action - Is a sound stage show - Pretty intense and could frighten the younger ones. We did not see the Monsters of Rock Show ( Although our VIP host - which I'll explain later said it was just ok) Dining- there are a bunch of different kiosks selling food all of which looked good. We ate at the Brown Derby its sit down Americam style food, pretty good not cheap around 15-25 Sing per person. Directly outside the Park there are a bunch of restaraunts and shops. We ate the Big Easy - which was very good and they were quick, especially with kids food. There is a Chili's and a Hard Rock but I would call for reservations in advance. Tickets Tickets Tickets Tickets !!! Get your tickets on line ahead of time. They actually only sell a certain amount each day, so you could turn up and not get in if you dont have a ticket booked. I found this out the hard way. Ticket Prices and Express Pass Weekday Adult 66 SGD Kids 4-12 48 SGD Express Pass 30 Weekend Adult 73 SGD Kids 4-12 52 SGD Express Pass 68 They also offer 2 day passes at a discount. I have not been on a weekday , so can really comment on crowds. On a weekend however I think the express pass a must ( EXPRESS PASS lets you bypass the line to eevry major attraction 1 Time only - but this can save you 5 to 6 hours!! ) if you have young kids unless you are happy to wait in very long cues. I suppose if you were planning on spending 2 days you could attack the park strategically. ( Starting early working the back of the park first - going back to the hotel and coming back to the park after 4:30 etc... ) There is also a VIP option which is very $$$ 298 adults 238 Children . So pretty much 150 SGD more than tcket plus epxress pass. They raised the prices since I went and I only did this because we flew to Singapore to go to Universal and I was unaware tickets sold out in advance. Anywway- you get a host for up to 12 poeple- they will pair you with another family. You then go on a set tour of all rides / attractions. Some of the rides you do twice.You bypass every line. You get the best seats at all the shows and a 25 meal voucher per person. Its a nice way to see the park but its very pricey. When we go back I will just opt with the express pass it essentially does the same thing. Its a very nice / new clean park and my family had a great day.

USS is well presented but has few rides of interest for teenagers. It is very expensive and when we went neither Battlestar Galactica nor Madagascar were open. We didn't need a full day to see the park so the value for money was poor

i went to USS wit my kids,and we already standby the gate at the opening.it was fun,free drinking fountain are everywhere so u dont have to bring ur bottled water.but for budget traveller,i recommend u to bring ur food from home or buy from other place..because the price for the food here is so damn expensive! and dont forget to take ur discount card at the gate,u can get discount for 10 dollars for stuff and 5 dollars for food. oh yea..before playing at the jurrasic park ,u better buy rain coat ($2 for adult and $1 for kids) since ull be soaked!! better buy the rain coat than u have to buy a new cloth there and still have to wear ur wet underwear..

1) Already bought the tickets online and earlier from arrival to avoid disappointment. 2) Peak Hours is the best time to visit USS as it will be opened till 10pm and more attractions for the visitors like Hollwood After Hours which was entertaining during my visit. 3) Mummy the Revenge was the best ride for me as an adventurous adult while River Rapids Adventures was quite interesting with surprising ending. 4) My other family members enjoyed Shred 4D Adventure,Donkey live and Water World shows tremendously. 5) When the Battlestar Galactica and A Crate Adventure open, the USS will be more attractive in future.

On my first visit we booked a hotel package which included tickets to universal studios. We printed out the booking ticket which stated in bold :"THIS IS YOUR TICKET" and went to the entrance after we checked into Festive Hotel, with 3 small kids in tow. When we got to the entrance we were told, no this is not your ticket, although it says that it is. We were made to wait 20 minutes outside while they went to verify that our tickets were valid. The fact that they let us in eventually didn't help our already marred experience, plus watching other visitors have the exact same experience as us.  So while booking another visit with my husband, this time to celebrate our anniversary, I already had low expectations of customer service but decided to just bear with it for the fun experience following. With my already low expectations I wad disappointed to an even lower low. We did an online booking for 4th march, paid by credit card and submitted. On submitting we didn't encounter any confirmation page, some glitch in their website, and were brought straight to the receipt. We checked, and they printed the wrong date! We sent an email and called them immediately and were told they didn't give refunds. But we didn't want a refund, we just wanted our date correct. The customer service officer Michelle Choy said she'd check and call back. She didn't, but we received an email the next morning saying that she checked the system and there was nothing wrong so we couldn't get the refund. But we didn't want a refund! So with our integrity insulted, we called again and were asked to forward them the email they sent to us! We spoke to the manager who eventually gave us the refund with the usual apologies. But we didn't want the refund!! And they didn't change the date, so we're expected to book again?

We recently took our two children to Universal Studios Singapore. Like any amusement park one expects to have to line up for the rides. We lined up for our first ride for over an hour and when we were nearly at the front they closed the ride due to bad weather. All outdoor rides were closed for over an hour. Once they re opened we joined the line for another ride, after lining up for an hour, you guessed it, they closed the ride due to bad weather. Every time they closed a ride the announced there were so many other things to do while the rides were closed, like shop, eat, or meet the characters (who were not out due to the weather) It is a lot of money to spend to eat hot dogs and buy overpriced universal studio merchandise. I understand there are safety concerns but why build outdoor rides in a tropical country that can not operate in the wet, it rains every other day here. Very dissapointing, will not go back. If it looks like rain dont go.

I was there with my family on 27 May, kids age 9 & 10. The rides and shows are enjoyable. However what spoils the day is the service of the staffs. Seem that USS has a long way in training them on how to serve.  This is suppose to be a FUN place, but when half the staff team pulls a long face it's a turn off. The senior(in age) staff generally do a better job, but the young staff has a long way to go. I was rudely ask by a young chap in charge of a ride "how many people? No smile, no excuse me, no please. This is not a one off incident as encountered this at various levels throughout the park.  Basically fun place if you can ignore the poor service.

Fantastic place to visit. This for the whole family, though we went for a single day trip, I would recommend a 2 day trip and it costs less in a 2 day trip. The best part is all the rides are covered in your initial cost and so you don't have to queue up. There is a better way, express tickets for quicker entries into all ride and it costs only 35S$ but will save you lots of time. Plenty of options for food and lots of sovegneirs. Don't miss the fireworks show in the evening... guss it is only in the weekends, if you are photographer get yourself a good tripod and get in early to take the best place.

Excellent day for all ages, lots to do. To get the most out of your day make sure you arrive by 9.45am, Leave yourself enough time to navigate through Sentos Island. Park is very quiet for the first hour - so plan ahead. Look on the website and choose the attractions that most appeal (Mummy ride, Lost World and Batlestar are the most popula adult rides) head to these rides first). In the first hour we were able to do three rides without queing. Be warned by lunchtime the queues (especially during holiday times) are long up to 80 mins. I would highly recommend an Express Pass ($30SGN) this allows you to bypass the queue for all rides and shows - special entrance for express holders which takes you to the front row. For those travelling with elderly, small children or if you don't want to queue in the heat then this pass is for you. With the aid of the pass we were able to do the entire park (rides) and most of the major shows by 4pm (this would have been impossible without it). Food is reasonable in park - try Spices if you enjoy indian. Highly recommend: Lights, Camera show; Mummy ride, Lost World ride, Madagascar ride, Monster show .... The park isn't large however take as little as possible, for several of the rides you have to use lockers for ALL bags. Great day out, don't compare it to LA as there is no comparision, go with an open mind and you'll have a great day. PS consider taking the Mount Faber cable car to Sentosa Island - fantastic views of Singapore and Sentosa Island.

We went to Universal Studio Singapore on a Saturday; we actually got into the park at around 10.30am. We managed to take the Battlestar Galactica: Human. It was awesome and totally loved it. The ride took about 1 minute or maybe slightly more than that however we queued for about 1 hour and 30minutes. But it was worth the wait. We managed to watch the ‘Lights, Camera, Action’ show which was cool. It gives you insight on how certain scenes in movies are made (thunder / storm / fire / etc). We queued for about 15 minutes for this one. Next is ‘Shrek 4D Adventure’ which is awesome as well. You will ‘join’ the adventure of Shrek in finding Princess Fiona. We queued for about 30-40minutes.  There are plenty souvenir or merchandise shops in any part of the park, so shopping for you or your little ones are never ending. There are also plenty F&B outlets / kiosk. We had Chicken Caesar salad wrap which comes with fries and a drink near the Shrek4d (forgot the name) and we paid SD10.80.  The park is suitable for any age. You will opportunity to snap pictures with some movie characters, which come out every now and then, eg: Betty Boo, Frankenstein, characters from Madagascar, etc. I would recommend spending nearly the whole day so you can experience every ride. The queue time for some of the rides can be extremely long, so be well prepared. Bring some sun block, cap and water.  Make sure you go to Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure towards the end of your visit and you will get slightly wet from the ride. If getting wet doesn’t bother you, then it is ok. Anyway, remember to have fun with whoever you with.

don't completely trust internet weather forecast, it had been reported thunder storm in Singapore for 5 weeks. When we arrived great weather, 28-32 degree C. 1 day pass will be enough to do most of the great or major ride. I hv a 5 years son & 16 years old daughter and they both enjoy very much. Food OK as usual amusement park, nothing special, queuing line is only 15-40 mins max, a lot less than I expect. Recomend to "Must Go".

We arrived there around 10am and did all the rides and shows available . THe kids absolutely loved everything. But by 2pm the heavens opened the it poured. Suggestion - go early when it opens to avoid the afternoon tropical downpours that are common in Singapore. Overall - a great experience, recommend it to anyone young or old. If you have kids, it is a must ! Allow at least 4-5 hours in total to see and visit all the rides/shows.

It was my first visit to these Universal Studios in the world. One day long I did enjoy the great attractions and shows there. Perfect timing and organization. Very friendly and helpful young team everywhere. I do recommend it to the Singapore visitors specially if they have children and teens with them.

Had known of lots of negative review of the Universal Studio in Sentosa, Singapore - e.g. it's too small, not much attractions / rides (as compared to other Universal Studios). However, as a Singaporean, I feel that I should support this attraction and take a look myself. The entry is about SGD $70 and if you're going after 7pm (no more rides, just shops and fireworks at 9pm), it'll costs you around SGD $10.  While I was spending a night's stay at one of the hotels in Sentosa, I seized the opportunity to see the Universal studio after 7pm for 2 reasons - avoiding the harsh sun and heat in the day, and for economical reason.  As I'm not a fan of rides, the night visit was not a loss to me. I get to visit all the shops though I must say that the merchandise are not as attractiive as other theme parks. Sad to say - the service crew/retail crew's attitude are not that 'festive-like' or 'holiday-like'. I remembered that staff at other theme parks are usually very friendly and fun-loving. Probably, Singaporeans are just too serious to have fun at work.  A section of the attraction is closed after 7pm (jurassic park, land of far far away etc), so there was really nothing much we can see/visit.  The fireworks at 9pm will be a disappointment if you're used to NAtional Day fireworks, or firework display in other theme parks (e.g. Disneyland). But for the 'fireworks-naive' friends - it'll work wonders still.  Overall, spending $10 to see Universal studio in my own homeland is quite worth the experience ... However, I won't be spending $70 to visit it again as I'll have better choice in nearby HK or in Australia

We spent one whole day at Universal Studios Singapore (USS). There was a heavy downpour in the morning when we were on our way there. Thankfully, the rain stopped shortly after USS opened its doors. It was a cool morning to do the rides before 12 noon but very warm between 12noon to 5pm or so. As we are locals, we can just tap our Ezlink card (as long as the card has value of couse!) to board the monorail to Sentosa at Vivocity. It cost $3 nett/pax to take the monorail. This is swift and easy on a normal weekday. We usually see long queues on fri and weekends/public holidays. We rented a stroller for a charge of $10 at the Guest Services located on the lefthand corner upon admitting into USS. We felt the stroller was not comfortable enough as it could not be reclined nor does it have any cushioning in it (it was just a hard piece of plastic) as such our child was not able to nap in it. But still its better than nothing. On hindsight we would have brought along our own stroller. There are designated area for stroller parking in each attraction we went to. The Discovery Food court variety is very limited if we compared it to Food republic at Vivocity in terms of local food variety. Loui's NY Pizza Parlor is better in IMHO, at least the pizza tasted great and value for money. We enjoyed all of the rides and show at Far Far Away except for Donkey Live show which we went because we wanted to escape the heat. Shrek 4D adventure show is the best. Lights, Camera, Action! show at New York is also another good show. Monster Rock doesn't really rocks. It is extremely boring to watch it more than once. So it will be good if they change the show seasonally if possible. Else as local it is not very attractive to return to watch the same boring show. Similarly for the Donkey live show. The staff were friendly enough and we did not receive any negative experience from their service. So keep the service smile! You did a good job. Even the waiters and waitress from Celebrity Cafe & Bakery were very friendly and chatty.

I visited this place recently and have always thought that this attraction was great. But there aren't many rides and the staff were super unfriendly.You could hear some of them raised their voices at tourists.Hope they can improve on this.

Visited Santosa while in Singapore. A must for all travellers. Why go to Changi Airport and not go into the City. That was my feeling. Worth every minute spent there. Lots to do at Santosa, too much to write about. Don't forget to go and see "The Songs of The Sea" on the beach. Pretty cheap to take taxi's in Singapore. Most drivers very helpful but there is an odd couple that are just doing a job. We would go again in a heart beat..

Universal Studios Singapore was opened early this year but me and my buddy was able to be on their official grand opening. The park is filled with tourists from all over the world. The ticket was kinda expensive but we figured that Singapore is an expensive city and we know it's gonna be worth it.  The rides were awesome and we felt like we were kids again... We really enjoyed the Mummy ride which to our surprise was a roller coaster inside a pyramid - the visual effects are just great and what's awesome is that you would really feel the heat in your skin every time there's fire there... Battlestar Galactica is our favorite... The blue one is a little bit slower than the red one but your feet will be hanging, the red one is much faster but this is the typical roller coaster - it was such an adrenaline rush that we have to make sure we go for another ride.  Jurassic Park was kinda disappointing because the line is just so long, falling in line for an hour and a half well I would say it was worth it, the only down side is we're soaking wet after the ride, we should've invested on those S$2.00 plastic rain coat and saved our underwear from being wet. We saw all the attractions there and spent the whole day checking what the place has to offer. I would highly recommend this attraction for kids and the kids at heart, it might be kinda expensive but it was worth it!

I enjoyed a lot in Universal Studios in Sentosa Singapore. Although there's not much rides but its Spectacular. especially the MUMMY! you've got to try it. Im not gonna tell what's in there, you have to try it yourself! So many items for souvenirs that you can buy too although its quite expensive oh well maybe for me but you wouldn't leave without buying one! hmmmm the roller coaster, i was thinking of my son so i didn't try it hahaha you know what i mean about it ayt? Singapore is really known to be very clean and YES im a living legend who can attest to that! I wanna go there again!

Universal studios is great for kids and young at heart. It is located in Sentosa where you will ride a train in getting there. The train ticket costs S$3/head and the entrance fee costs S$63/head. If you get a chance of their promo, it will just cost you S$5/head. Our first stop was the Lights,Camera,Action where you can feel and see the happenings in a real life studio. This was a great introduction to the theme park! Our favorite ride is the Cyclone and the Human. If I were you, you should consider riding the Cyclone first before the Human. (beware of the drops)  Bring with you a bottle of mineral water. The food inside the park is too expensive so you'd better eat your breakfast or lunch before going to the park or just bring some chips but don't let the security see your food :)  It was a great experience for us!  The park closes at 7pm so be early in getting there to enjoy the rides! :)

Firstly its not very big so one day is enough unlike those giant theme parks abroad which can take days just to cover the ground. Secondly doesn't have too many scary rides (barring the few big ones which are designed for thrill seekers) Thirdly has good variety - some musicals, some thrill, some street performances The only gripe would be the queues that can be brutal. We went on a weekday and yet 40-45 min was the normal queue time on popular rides

Universal singapore was a bit disappointing because i was expecting moree....the ride for jurrasic park wasnt functional on that day which was a big disappointment as we were looking so much forward for it.Shrek 3D was good and so were few adventure rides including "the mummy returns".The rollercoaster ride wasnt functional so cant say much about it but it seemed full of fun.Few shows on diff strrets were going on which were quite impressive.One most important thing that they never allow to take any bag or belonging to mummy returns and so they ask u to keep it in the locker near the ridre but NEVER EVER PUT MONEY in it more than the required amount mentioned because they r non refundable and yes i lost few dollars:((My kid was not feeling well and the staff there really helped me out to go and see the doctor within the premises of the park.God bless the guy and the doctor who help us:)

Amazing, thrilling and fun filled. this is the place to visit in sentosa island. Their shows, rides, plays, movies live performances are really amazing. Cyclone ride, mummy ride, Madagascar trip and shrek 4d movie are just amazing. Please avoid Donkey song performance that the only thing which i disliked otherwise its must visit if you have never been to universal studio before.

Good concept. Visited most of the attactions. Enjoyed it. Weather was little hot to keep energy for full day. Most of the theme were known and enjoyed it thoroughly. Quite clean area. Staff was really good and helping. 4D movie was good experience. Must see.

Having been to Universal Studios in LA I can only say that Singapore was a huge disappointment and rip off. If it becomes busier they just can't handle it. Line at entrance was not well organized, not enough cashiers open. You pay a fortune for the Express Pass which was really great in LA, but in Singapore it's just poor organized. At the main entrance you have to stand again in line to wait to get in, at main attractions you can use the pass only once and the entire presentation of the pass is not good. In LA you get a fancy VIP pass around your neck. Here you get another piece of paper which you constantly search for in your pockets. Restaurants are a disaster, it took us about 30min to make a simple burger order, even though the park was not very busy. The rides are ok, but with a 4 year old there are not many things that will work for it. A really disappointing experience that comes at a very high cost.

Good place to fill in 4 hrs, Shrek land was great, we arrived as the gates opened Lucky, rain pelted down 3 hrs later closing every ride for 2 hrs, not much to do when it's pouring rain.One for the kids.

Visited with my cousins and their 8 year old. Arrived at 11am . Kid wanted to take shots with cartoon characters but it was crazy! Parents were pushing and shoving, no queue, even staff looked flustered. Next the queue at the rides was ridiculous, Mummy, Lost world rides etc all 40+ to an hour! And guess what - all that waiting for a ride that is over in a few seconds! Not enough signs to the washrooms. Rained at about 12.30 - 1 pm, which closed off most of the rides and resulted in worse queues at the indoor rides. We are all vegans so brought some sandwiches for lunch. Found seats near Lost world , both to eat and take shelter only to be chased away by staff. Ended up taking quick bites on a bench in the drizzle. Lockers REALLY expensive especially as only first 1/2 hr is free. Then every 20min chargeable! No way you can do a ride in 1/2 hr when queue is an hr long! AT the end of a VERY long day we managed to do only 6 rides and take in 2 shows. SO not worth 60+ per head!

If your used to Australian or American theme parks then save your money and don't visit this place. You will be bored to death in no time. The 2 or 3 decent rides don't make up for the rest of the place. Its lame. Be interesting for kids under 10 though I suppose. Save your money for something else.

A great place to spend time with family and friends! Don't miss the water world performance! it's actually the best in the whole theme park! purchase VIP tickets (an extra of $40) to skip all the long Q

For those who have already been to the Universal studios at other places probably this might not be a bad experience either but for a family on a tour to singapore ( n around ) this should be a must watch.  The Hurricane : Sound & light show , Shrek 4D Show , Jurassic park , Water world stunts ( & the watery act by the cast ) , rides at the Mummy , Transformer , Madagascar boat ride etc will give every one a good enough to cherish the singapore trip :)
we had a great day at Universal Studios, very easy to get to and to get around. Loved the transformers ride

We were quite happy with our day at Universal Studios. I recommend to buy express passes so you can avoid staying in 30-60 minutes ques for the most popular rides. Since my children are older we did not cover all the rides and some of the rides were aimed for younger children, specially the Madagaskar so if you have to pick or choose, I would skip that one. However do not skip the Sci-Fi area, do test the Transformers and the Galatica. Shrek was good and the Waterworld show aswell. However, the food selection is rather limited and quite expensive but that's what all the parks are about anyway.

Even if you have visited the Universal Studio in the United States, USS will not disappoint you. Had a good time where I reached the park at 10.30am and left around 9pm. Enjoyed the shows, love the surrounding and conquered the rides. It was a bonus that the transformer show and ride were made available when we were there to compensate the Dino water rides closure. No complain on the hot weather as its not much different to Kuala Lumpur unless you compare to Australia or UK during spring. Love it and will go again...for sure!

Queues are very long compared to other theme parks. We waited 2 hours for canopy flyer only to be told that it is being closed due to technical problems.  Also Universal Studios Singapore has to be the only theme park to ban photography of any kind (not just flash photography) on the rides.

Never get bored visiting Universal Studio.This was my second time visiting USS. Safety and Security are the main issues that the management always maintain.Very good and safe.Well maintained facilities. Suitable for children of all age, toilets available everywhere. Just beware of the rainy season, some of the attractions would be closed. don't forget to bring the umbrella or at least the raincoat,so you still could enjoy some of the still open attractions. The things that we should concern are the closing time all the mean of transportation would be queuing heavily.But Still worth visiting.

We went on chinese new years day and before lunch it was not very busy, in fact we went on all major rides and shows before 1pm without having to line up for more than 2-4 minutes. After lunch was a different story, but the longest we lined up was 50mins to see Transformers (for the 2nd time that day) and it is worth it - that ride is incredible.  Foods and drinks are expensive but what else do you expect in Singapore. The waterworld show was very good.

world class theme park situate in sentosa island itself . full family fun frolics packaged with loads of entertainment. this has inspird many more theme parks but d original one oi definitely the best. we liked most WATERWORLD show, you should must take an umbrella for visiting any place in singapore. worth a visit of 5-6 hoursminimum to enjoy fully..
this is the smallest Universal Studio ever..maybe this place is best in ASEAN only..not bad for small country like singapore..few rides with pricey tickets, just need 2 hours to finished it all.

The whole family spent whole day from its opening hour till the very end at 10pm ... Tiring , yes, but no regrets !  The tickets and additional expenses (ie food) can be pricey... but, no regrets ... Great attractions and very short lines. The park was tidy and well organized.

Fun filled day with my BF,had 1 full day at universal studios. awesome experience! The best attraction in singapore! Don't ever miss the transformers ride, cylon rollercoaster and the mummy! Although i got disappointed with their parade, it's not at par with disneyland. But still, a must visit when you go to singapore!

we did have a good time and enjoy our day spent there...good location for family day out. good facilities and well organized. during weekend is very busy, however if you are there early morning you can manage...there are facilities for everyone and forget about small details...enjoy your day.
