i hate the rollercoaster :( the whole place is clean&vast but I think it's best for friends or couples rather than w/family
It's new and it shows. A lot of things inside, for adults and kids alike. Transformers and Battlestar Galactica are most memorable for me, but all the park is nice.

The theme park is the first international standard theme park in South East Asia. As such, it would be a bit pricey for first time visitors from this region especially for those with children. If you are a regular to this type of attractions from other parts of the world, though, you would find this to be among the cheapest. The size of the park is just right for a one day outing. You do not have to walk long distances from one ride to another, which is a big help considering the humid weather. There are plenty of shelters and outdoor fans, though. Toilets are conveniently located and there are plenty of food kiosks and restaurants within and outside the park. The best rides would be the Transformer, the two Cylon and Human Battlestar Galactica roller coasters (not for the faint hearted) and the Rapids Adventure at the Lost World. For the shows, I would recommend the Shrek 4-D Adventure and Waterworld. The Rocky Horrorshow is not that enjoyable (for me) but the theatre is air-conditioned, with comfortable seats. There are plenty of photo opportunities with the Transformers and Shrek characters. My favourite would be the Revenge of the Mummy where the actors/actresses were really into character. Be careful of the Beetleguise guy who can be quite mischievous. All in all, it was a fun day at Universal Studio Singapore. The queues were long at most of the popular attractions (being a Sunday and beginning of the school holidays in Malaysia) but at most you just need to wait for about 45 minutes to 1 hour. Surprisingly,the Battlestar Galactica roller coaster has quite short queuing times (less than 15 minutes at its peak on the that day). If you want to take repeat rides, I suggest joining the single rider queue. My tips: 1. There are water coolers around the park. You may refill your drink bottles conveniently. 2. For Muslim visitors, Halal restaurants are aplenty. There is also a small prayer room next to the Cylon roller coaster. 3. Disposable ponchos can be purchased from the vending machines (S$3 each or buy one from Watson's pharmacy, much cheaper. It's a must for the Rapids Adventure ride) 4. If you still got wet, there are drying pods available, at S$5 a shot. 5. Target the popular rides first immediately upon park opening. There'll be shorter queues. 5. If you are driving and parking your car at the basement car park, which is a very short walk away, you would need the Cashcard or the VEP toll card for the parking. These can be top up at 7-11 just outside the park entrance near the Lake of Dreams but you would need it to enter the car park. One day parking is S$26 maximum. 6. Avoid last minute shopping. The rides close around 7pm, right after the parade. Everybody would leave simultaneously so there would be a very big crowd at the souvenir shop next to the exit. I suggest you purchase your souvenirs earlier and collect it later outside the gate.

went there from woodlands. took the mrt til vivo city. bought a monorail ride to sentosa at S$3 @. first stop at waterfront station. this is where universal studio is. first sight is the rotating globe with universal logo. a lot of picture-takinh here. jst find a nice spot where there isn't much people near you for a perfect jump pose. fee is $68/adult. as you enter, you'd meet woody woodpecker for some fun and picture taking. helpful park attendants are there to take your picture with your camera or the park camera. we went to the madagascar ride, yes, all of us with my 15-yr old twin boys. a real family bonding time. of course my 9 yr old girl enjoyed it much. the jurassic ride is wonderful. makes you anticipate if you're gonna get wet. the line was rather long though. raincoats are available at the vendo machine, $3 for a pair. helpful if you dont wanna get wet with your cameras and watches and phones. the adventurous boys loved the galactica rides and the human. just by looking at these, i get dizzy! haha. the 4D shrek show is marvelous. and of course, the waterworld show, (only 2, 9:30am and 4:40pm) is awesome. full of action, not to mention the fun-filled water-hosing of audience prior the show. if you dont want to get wet, sit on the red benches. don't miss the light, camera action, the steven spielberg galore. watch before your eyes how hurricane "happens". it's humid all day, but the water drinking founstains are a-plenty, very invigorating. universal studios is more exhilirating than disneyland in hk, so we thought. very worth it!
Transformers ride, my partner and i were still figuring out how they did it and if we were only fooled by our eyes. :))

A short hop from the harbourfront MRT, via the Sentosa Express, USS is easily accessible. The express card saves on a huge amount of queing time and hassle. The 3-D transformer ride is probably the most fun. But the 2 roller-coasters and the water-ride are good fun too. But, roller-coaster officianado's be warned: the rides are nowhere near as high/long/fast/scary as many in Europe & the USA
Went there to check it out. Looks nice but very pricy...You feel if you are at the real Universal Studios but then the smaal version.

Visited USS today and as locals, we could sign up for RWSinvites worth $150 which includes 2 passes to USS, free parking, free room upgrade etc. The USS tickets includes 5 express rides so it's very worth it compared to solely purchasing tickets alone. We saved about $100!  The size of the park is comparable to HK disneyland. Small but one whole day is needed to cover the attractions. It's peak season as it's the local school holidays here but the park wasn't as crowded as we expected it to be, average waiting time was about 25 mins. Probably because we went on a weekday. We had Express passes for certain rides so they were much faster.  Recommended attractions: Revenge of the Mummy (roller coaster in the dark), quite cool!! It moves backwards at a certain point and we took that twice :) Battlestar Human, our hearts totally dropped when we rode this but since we already paid the expensive entrance fee, might as well! Dared not try the Cyclon as it goes upside down. Transformers was AMAZING. It was a simulator yet sort of like a mild roller coaster every now and then. Lights Camera Action stage show was interesting. Shrek was okay.  Was quite hesitant to try Rapids Adventure because we didn't want to get wet. But since it was on our Express pass, we went ahead. Bought ponchos at $3. It was a bumpy boat ride that gets u splashed wet, really soaking wet, esp the shoes!! We then paid $5 to use the Dry Pod to dry ourselves. I think this ride is really expensive because of the ponchos and drying. The lockers for this ride are the only one thats charged per hour so we didn't rent it.  Street performances are held at certain timings. Sesame street entertainment was short and fun. Character greeting and photo-taking was quite a disappointment. We queued, and when it was almost our turn, the characters bid goodbye and suddenly went off. Thought the staff should at least inform the crowd, instead of letting them queue for nothing.  Pros: Great place for family, better for older kids. Nice scenery for photo-taking, most lockers for thrilling rides are free for the first 30mins so we didn't have to pay at all. Water coolers, lockers and toilets are very convenient. Nice gift shops all over the park.  Cons: having to pay $5 for drying. This should be free. Staff don't inform the visitors that photo-taking has ended, making many people queue for nothing. They should at least do proper crowd control and not leave visitors disappointed after queueing up. No proper ending for the day. Disneyland ends the day with fireworks, USS has nothing. Once time is up, people make their way out on their own.  The feeling of USS and Disneyland is totally different. Disneyland is more of dream-like while USS is adventurous. Character photo-taking queues are only half of that in HK disneyland. In HK I ever queued almost an hour just to take a photo with mickey and minnie mouse. The longest queue here in USS was only about 10mins or so.  Worth the visit and would return again!

Went there with 11 of my friends. Was so fun! For adrenaline Junkie, this is the place for you. The Transformers Ride was really awesome, a MUST try. The staffs were nice and helpful. Lots of souvenirs sold here, so don't just buy something once you entered this place because every section offers many varieties of souvenirs. My sister bought Transformers watch but when she opened the case, the watch had already broken so we exchange it back to the store. Food courts were some with reasonable prices. Too bad I didn't have the time to play all games and watch all shows. Definitely will come again!

Went from KL to Singapore for the day ...Just to visit Universal Stuidos! It's 1000% worth it! I've been to Orlando back in 2001 ..So very familiar with Universal Studios ...But Singapore Park is SIMPLY AMAZING! The attractions are SIMPLY AMAZING! The layout, the crowd, the decor, the service, the security, the cleanness ...I tried the Transformers x2! It's Soooo impressive! The roller coasters ...Incredible sensations!!! For those looking for adrenaline boost....It's the place to be! (btw, they put at the visitors disposal locker box where you could put your camera, phone and other stuff before riding the roller coasters ...Free of Charge - for one hour!) ...It's really great!!! I simply loved it and it's worth travelling for!!!! Would love to go back again and again and again! Ps I went on Sunday ...My friends told me I was crazy going there on a Sunday! Believe it or not...It wasn't that crowded and queuing time were very reasonable!!

Bought the RWS Invite card which gave a voucher to redeem for admission for 2 to USS. It came with 5 express rides (using these will allow you to skip the queue if the queue is long). Others had to pay around $50 for express rides, which I feel, is extremely expensive. I have been to Disneyland theme parks, and the fast passes are given on a first-come-first-serve. Visitors didn't have to pay at all! I visited USS today and went straight for the 'must-try' rides. At one of the water rides, we were stuck for almost 20 min. Apparently, there was some technical problem, and we were stranded in the dark cave, waiting for the team to fix. The raft in front of ours happened to be located just beneath a curtain of thin water fall. The 2 unlucky visitors who were seated right under were wet through. I recalled a similar experience at Disneyland Tokyo, where our rafts were also stranded in a cave (think it's Pirates of the Carribean). We were stranded for about the same amount of time. The apology was broadcast over and over again, and even though it was in Japanese, we could feel the sincerity. If there was any broadcast made this afternoon, the annoucement was not clear, and we could not make out what was being said. When we got out, we were greeted with staff at the exit, issuing to every stranded visitor 2 fast passes each. Now that's what I call service quality. Also, I noticed the staff managing crowd control, or operating rides did not perform their tasks professionally. One of them was apparently chewing gum in his mouth. Overall attitude was very different from those I experienced, either in Disneylands or theme parks in Australia. Somehow you can feel their passion and commitment in what they are doing, they are proud of their job. I see this lacking in the staff at USS. Maybe the management should consider organising a learning journey for their staff, to learn good practices from others. This is not a complaint, but just my personal feedback. I believe over time, these gaps will be closed, if USS wants to go far.

This duelling coaster is insane! When you sit in Cyclon, you are sitting with your legs dangling and strapped at the chest. After that, you are just whirled around 3 times in 360 degree circles, while the Human coaster passes you by simultaneously A must mention is the 4D Transformers ride. It is amazing fun, where you actually feel you are falling from a skyscraper. No wonder the lines had up to 40 mins of wait Despite it being a Monday, it was packed, maybe because of school holidays. However, it can get very hot and humid so dont forget the sunblock and being hydrated!

Went to Universal Studios on a Saturday. I guess the busiest day of the week. The park is fairly big. Even though there were a lot of people, queue's were very reasonable. I think you can do every ride in 1 day and watch most of the shows. Get there early, and buy your tickets in advance. The park is squeaky clean. Most of the lockers are free for 30min or 1h. if they are not, go to another locker 'place'.  The places:  Hollywood:  The only ride/show there is 'Monster rock' The show 'Monster Rock' is not worth your time. The music is loud and ear-piercing. The songs are not very rock, and the performers are not very good singers. The experience was somewhat aweful.  New York:  The only ride/show there is Lights, Camera. Action!™ Hosted by Steven Spielberg. It was an interesting albeit short experience of some nice effects. If the queue is more than 15 minutes i wouldn't waste my time on it. Keep this as an extra, a rain escape or just something to postpone for when the queue is gone.  Sci-Fi City:  Accelerator: Didn't go in that one. It's basically the well known spinning tea-cups.  Battlestar Galactica: HUMAN vs. CYLON: These 2 rides are the 'heaviest' rides. Only did the red one. The queue was very short on both of them. Only 5minutes. I guess this was too thrilling for most visitors. Well worth it. Great rush. Great ride! Wait 2h after eating before going on one of these!  TRANSFORMERS The Ride: The Ultimate 3D Battle: Unfortunately had to skip this one as the queue didn't drop under 90minutes during the day.  Ancient Egypt:  Revenge of the Mummy: Awesome ride. This is a fast indoor roller coaster (no upside down) mostly in the dark. One of the best rides in the park! The queue here was very reasonable. +/-15min The free lockers are on the right side. the left side lockers are paying ones.  Treasure Hunters Slow moving car on a rail. Skipped this one. probably good for young kids.  The Lost World:  Amber Rock Climb: Skipped this one. you have to pay extra for this. It's a well done wall-climbing experience.  Canopy Flyer: Skipped this one as well. The queue was too long. Looked like a great ride. quite fast and not too crazy. Ok for kids as well.  Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure: Great fun. A rubber boat brings you around the water track. Great decoration around the track. Everyone on this ride WILL get wet. With the Singaporean weather that shouldn't be a problem. Some unlucky people WILL GET SOAKED on this ride. The equivalent of getting 5 buckets of water on you is very possible. Be prepared :)  WaterWorld: Best show in the park I reckon! A must see! If you don't want to get wet, go sit in the RED zone. Green zone might get wet, blue zone will get wet! The show and animation is well worth your time. The stunts are good. There is fireworks and jet-ski's, Great fun for young and old!  Far Far Away:  Shrek 4-D Adventure: A funny 4D movie. Worth the wait. Don't go there if the queue is longer than 30min! Great escape from the heat or rain as well.  Madagascar:  Madagascar: A Crate Adventure This boat-ride is a water ride, but you will not get wet! it's very slow paced and basically a story unfolds around you whilst you float through the course. Good fun for young and old as well!

Universal Studio’s Must-Dos: *) Lights, Camera. Action!™ Hosted by Steven Spielberg *) TRANSFORMERS The Ride: The Ultimate 3D Battle *) Battlestar Galactica: HUMAN vs. CYLON - 1 Human and at least 1 CYCLON *) Revenge of the Mummy *) Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure *) Canopy Flyer *) WaterWorld *) Shrek 4-D Adventure  Buy the One-Day Pass at Universal Studio online.  Ticket – SGD 74. Timings - 10 AM to 7 PM  Buy Online Ticket, print out the voucher and enter the park directly by scanning the bar code.  There's also a Hershey's Store and Garrett Popcorn Store outside the park for afterwards, yum! Their food court is so terrible. When you go there, you must go to the burger and milkshake place. They seriously, have the BEST MILKSHAKES in the world! And don't forget to stop at the hershey's chocolate shop, on the way out! We stopped for dessert and drinks at KT's Grill, in the New York zone. The most exciting choice was the apple crumble with homemade peanut butter ice-cream, which was delicious. Watch out for freshly made churros!  Go for Single Rider, fast and convenient express Lane without extra cost.  Bags can be carried on most of the rides except the roller coasters. You can leave your belongings in lockers, conveniently located near the roller coaster attractions and that will be free of charge for the first 30 mins. You can open the locker and then again immediately take another locker for another half an hour which is okay. The rides, especially Transformers, Battlestar and Revenge of the Mummy are quite close by, so you can leave your things there without worrying about the time limit and hop from ride to ride if there are no queues.  Toilets are wonderfully clean and always filled with soap and tissue paper to wipe your hands, while water coolers are aplenty.  There are also plenty of drinking water fountains located throughout the park, especially in the waiting areas of each attraction, so it's not necessary to bring your own water or spend a lot of money to stay hydrated. Very thoughtful. The park is rather small, and can be comfortably completed within 4 -5 hours, especially if you visit midweek and not during a school holiday.  New York Lights, Camera, Action! Hosted by Steven Spielberg - It’s only 10mins, so do hop on by.  Sci-fi City Battlestar Galactica: Cylon - the most awesome ride in the whole theme park, sit in the front, on the sides. (Each row sits 4.). This ride launches you straight into the fast speeds and turbulent turns. Although you may want to keep your glasses in the locker because they may fall off during some of the fast swoops and turns. Cylon is more traumatic, human is somewhat smoother than Cylon. Try once in both. Cylon is blue track, the red one is human. Transformers The Ride: The Ultimate 3D Battle – A must-must-must visit. My personal favourite in the entire park. You can bring your stuff with you; just put it on the floor of the car beside you on the seat. Each car thingy has three rows, no winners for guessing which is the best seat. But generally you can still see everything no matter which row you’re in, as long as you don’t get someone mightily tall in front of you. No pictures at the boarding area (this time, the staff smiled and made crosses with their arms) but please do snap away along the queuing area.  Ancient Egypt Revenge of the Mummy - sit in front. Once again you aren’t allowed to bring your bags with you, because it can get quite jerky. Lost World WaterWorld - I would recommend sitting in the middle sections because you’d have an unblocked view. If you don’t want to get wet, sit in the seats above the railings in the middle of the rows. Beware of seating too close to the front section, you are very likely to be wet. There are three well marked zones in the seating area. The blue ones closest to the stage are the soak zone, the green ones away from the stage are the spray zone, and the red ones further away are the dry zone. So if you are sitting in the blue seats, be prepared to be soaked mercilessly. Jurrasic Park - Do be warned that if you sit at the sides you’ll get drenched. Other than that, sit back and relax. Canopy Flyer - It gives you a bird’s eye view of The Lost World and can be a little scary especially if you’re afraid of heights and you sit in the seat that faces backwards (both of which I am guilty of). There are some dips and turns, but still smooth and enjoyable overall.  Far Far Away Shrek 4-D Adventure – Must try. I noticed that you get sprayed a lot. And the seats jerk pretty roughly at some point of time. The intro-movie that they do is pretty long, so stay patient! But the ride itself is exciting, if nonsensical.  Madagascar Madagascar: A Crate Adventure – Can skip. It’s a slow boat ride through well-made sets and maybe only slightly scary for young kids. Monster Rock – Do not bother. Nothing much. Enchanted Airways - No adrenaline rush.

The place is not as large as the one in USA but enough for families to have some fun. There are rides for adults and kids. You need to plan to visit each attraction as certain activities are time-based. Buying tickets in advance is advisable. Also be early to avoid the crowd. If you have dietary restriction especially Halal food, then you don't have that many choices. The cable car ride was great - nice views.. But not for the faint hearted. The night scene is great especially for avid photographers. I personally think it is better than Hong Kong Disneyland.

As I visited around 30 theme parks around the world, I was expecting a lot from the newest Universal "baby". Sentosa's universal park is smaller, but attention to detail and some unique rides makes up for it. Even i went on national day, the park easily swallowed all the crowds and thanks to the express pass ( 50SD) non, or minimal waiting was included in my day of fun. I rode every ride atleast 5times...and as one would expect the sci-fi city with its rollercoaters and fantasticTransformers ride is great fun. Each theme land is very limited but very nicely designed. Thru the day i saw few street shows and my only dissapointment was, the parade is running only at the weekend and these lockers for your belongines are computer operated and most of them out of order. They for free until 30min but be careful, they get quiet pricey once you leave your stuff there for longer. Foodwise is the park on average...with the usual theme park fast food options. Go there early in the morning and ride all the rides to enjoy the most of it and after just wander around and enjoy the themening and take photos. Sentosa itself it's great place. After visiting theme park you can enjoy big fountain show and bizzar dance of cranes, or maritime museum.

Nice place for kids and the young at heart. We went there on a Tuesday so there were no long lines. High Quality rides and shows. Fun! Fun! Fun! Check their official website to see if they offer discounts. We were able to get a 20% discount plus a $10 coupon.
Had a lovely time enjoying all of the rides. To our amazement the queues were short and admission was very quick.

nice place in singapore. When you ever go to singapore you must vist this place. you may need to spare a day for yourself to visit this place. you may find many instersting rides. Mummy ride ----awsome ride dont miss this one roller coster ---- thrilling exp transformer ride--- Shreek 4D show --- you must see that terninator 3D show --- good to watch and many other attractions  you will remember the day for coming year dont miss take your kid or family when you visit this place
Liked 'Songs of the Sea', Fort Siloso, Resorts World area, 'Cranes' light display, Underwater World, general exploring of the island on foot or by bus/monorail.

Its a park thats 'do-able' in a single day. Just be prepared for the heat and humidity of the mornings which does reduce in he afternoon. All the shows are worth visiting and most of the big rides worth the waiting-time if you are the thrill-loving kinds. There are enough rides to keep the tiny tots occupied too. The water-world show and the steven spielberg studio show must not be missed! The food options are decent and the fire-works show at the end of the evening( if scheduled) is a grand spectacle.

Although it was raining the whole day we were there, this was a really fun place. I suggest getting a fast pass to avoid the long lines - with the fast pass, the most we ever waited was 10 minutes (although be warned, the fast pass only works once per ride). This place is a lot smaller than the one in LA, but still worth a visit. Also, at this present time it has the best ride of all Universal Studios in the world, the Transformers ride.

I thought that this place was really cool, it was really close to the hotel, Shangri La's Rasa Sentosa resort and it took up a whole DAY of my holiday. My favourite ride was the red Battlestar Galactica rollercoaster and it was really fast. Go on the Mummy ride as well!  Food is a bit expencive but really good.  A must do place and i strongly reccomend you go there.
Amenities are very good, very clean & hospitable people are there to greet tourists. Very entertaining Monster Rock I enjoyed every minute of it.

You need an entire day for experiencing everything in Universal Studios. Rides were amazing. Especially the Mummy ride, Jurassic park ride and the Human and cylone rollercoasters. Not for the weak hard. But there are other less scary rides too...kids will enjoy them. Shows were very nice esp. the donkey live and 4D shows.

The concept and most of the rides are meant for children, not really an adult place. Except for the Transformer Rider that is good, the rest are pretty average. Can be boring for some, like me. They should put up signs where the performance / attraction is for young kids.

This is by far the best theme park i've been to.....the entire park is beautiful and well organised. The rides are fantastic, some of which is exclusive only to Singapore. The Revenge of the Mummy, Transformers the Ride, Shrek 4D, Battlestar Gallactica, Cyclon, Jurassic Park Rapids and Madagascar Crate Ride are a must try for adventurers.
Amazing place! It's small but don't be fooled by its size and the number of attractions. It's well themed and you should go on the mummy ride.

We spent a day at Universal Studios with our four boys ages 4 - 8. They had a great time - and by extension so did we. It is a well organized mass attraction, too many people, too expensive (50 bucks each, for the Mastercard special price, 12S$ for a chili dog), but still - for a day, worth the trip. If you have kids. The thing that amazed me was that the majority of people there were adults, largely people visiting from all over Asia... but then, I suspect you would find the same thing visiting Disney World.  A few recommendations. We went on a Monday, skipping the weekend. I would really recommend doing the same, as lines were acceptable. Still sometimes long, but ok. In order to knock off one or two of the more popular rides - ie Transformers - get there early. If the weekend is your only option, and money is not an obstacle, think of getting an express ticket. Note to Universal - I HATE THESE THINGS. You are standing there, waiting in line for 40 minutes, and along comes a group of ten, who then gets to cut line. How frustrating! They should cut it out - although it is probably a good money maker, it leaves many of their customers with a sour taste.  The park is basically a round circuit - start in NY and work to right - beelining for Transformers if there early. Or head to the left and start with things for the little kids, from Madagascar and Shrek. We went right, and started - and now mentioning it for the third time - with Transformers, a truly impressive combination of 4D movie and roller coaster. Very well done, but not for the very young or faint of heart. We went from there to the Battle Star Galactica roller coasters, both red and blue. Again worth visiting. And after that, it was the indoor Egypt / mummy roller coaster - again, well done.  After all this, you get into tamer fare. The Water World show is great, really impressive, and the boys loved it, sitting down in the splash zone getting soaked. Here again a note to the Park - don't have people queue up in a mass then drop the rope and let us race to our seats - it is a recipe for disaster. Some kid is going to fall and get trampled and you will be rightfully sued for half the value of the place. Find a way to have people line up in an orderly fashion and eliminate this exciting bit. And again, here, I found the opening of the gate first for express ticket holders really frustrating.  In summary, not worth more than a day, but worth a day. Enjoy!  Recommendations: Pack some food and bring water bottles - if you are going to be there for ten hours you will have plenty of time to enjoy one of the cafes or dining locations AND still eat some sandwiches. There are water fountains in many of the rides, so have the kids fill their bottles as needed.  As mentioned, get there early and go on a weekday. Or consider going late - perhaps there are discount afternoon / evening passes? The crowds seemed to be thinning quite a bit when we left at 5:00.  Ask about discounts - there were several when we went, the best being for MasterCard holders, including a lower price and free tickets to the sister attraction, the aquarium.  Download the layout and develop an action plan on what you want to hit during your visit, rather than under the hot Singapore sun.

I bought the tickets online as they had a promotional discount for mastercard users. With the promotion I got the Maritime museum tickets for S$ 2 only instead of the regulare S$10. It is an awesome theme park for young kids. Not as big as the one in LA but just right for under 8 years as you do not have to walk a lot. Only 3-4 rides had a waiting time of 40 min but they rest were a mere 5-10 minutes wait. If you have express tickets you can also be done in half a day. However with express tickets you can only use it once per ride. Very nicely made park and on the weekends there is a lot more happening than on the weekdays.

If you have kids or love rides yourself, it's worth it to really plan on spending an entire day here. The Transformers ride alone would make it worthwhile. They've really caught up both technology and content on that one. Expect long queues though, so if you don't mind paying extra, get the express ticket. There are enough rides and eats and stuff to do here to make for a full day well spent in Singapore. Just outside Universal is an almost authentic Singaporean food street where you can grab a quick bite to reassure yourself you're doing something local.

Don't start off with the Transformer ride !!! On the queue for 4 hours. Go to other attractions and come to popular rides in the afternoon. 5-7 the waiting time is minimum. Be quick after 5 and can manage 4-6 rides in the period.

Had a major fun time at USS, spend hours here and i don't even want to come home although i didn't hop most of the rides due to the scaredy cat me, but i have a fantastic time, what i like the most is they have a waiting time sign to inform you how long it'll take for you to get to the ride, which i don't experience this much, thumbs up!

I needed a day of fun and excitement and got what I needed here. OK it was expensive and I forked out the extra cash to get the Express ticket but it was worth it. For me this is the best attraction in Singapore.
It may be unfair to compare Universal Studios Singapore to other Universal Studios which I have visited. After 3.00pm, we were all done and left!

This is my second visit at USS. When I went there last year, there were no transformers and Jurassic park yet.  This amusement park is really awesome. I just hope it could be bigger. I hope they could expand even more. We went there in the afternoon and arrived at around 3 pm and we left at 7 pm. With this period of time, my brother and I were able to try all major rides and even watched some shows and walked around.  Aside from the rides, I hope they could also add some shows or other entertainments for those who can't take the rides. Though it is an amusement park, but there are groups that includes members who really can't take the rides. So if there could be some other things to do, it would be more suitable to all kinds of people.
loved everything from the rides to the stores and the food. However strollers store should be placed at many more places. other than that not much to complaint.
Really good - not too big - just the right size for a day's visit in a very hot climate. The new transformers ride was a total hit with the kids and they went on it 5 times! Brilliant.

They did a good job packing in a lot of rides for both adults and children into a compact park. You can get through all the attractions in one day, especially if you fork out a little more for the Universal Express pass that lets you cut all the queues!

I don't want to repeat everyone elses comments. I just wanted to advise people to go mid-week during Singapore, Malay and Thai school terms, and you can ride all day with barely any queues. I went on a Wednesday and didn't queue at all.

It was really fun and entertaining, the staffs were really nice and the park was beautiful, but small. Being Singapore as my second home, i've went to the park 4-5 times, and i still want to visit it again, But it has it's downside, i was lost with my cousins in the park, hoping to find our parents, we go to the information center and we didn't get much help, so if you go there with some kids you better not leave them out of your sight, especially small ones. I recommend to bring a lot of money there, since the ticket is very expensive, and that the food and the merchandise are also expensive.

We spent a great few hours at USS. Although hot it was not too crowded and initially we were able to get onto rides with little or no wait. Staff were very friendly and the theme park was very well laid out, with toilet facilities and cafes/restaurants in every themed section.

Although the place is brimming with people, you will still find yourself enjoying fully! There are queues obviously but the waiting times are not that long.The 4D's amazing. There are lots of restaurants, ample sitting areas to rest and a number of clean washrooms around. Awesome park attractions and rides and above all, because it's located at Sentosa, there are a lot of wonderful sights for adults to see. Just be prepared physically, as the place is huge, you will need to have a full-on energy reserve and spend the full day to get the maximum enjoyment. A must: comfy clothes and shoes, light bags, sunglasses and hat (if not the rainy session)!
The kids had a blast and the battlestar gallectica - cylon deserves a special mention for successfully managing to shake all your insides.
singapore is very nice place, clean environment, the place which you can relax and take a break for while :-) love this place

The entry fee was great value for money & the theme park quite easy to navigate. The rides were a lot of fun though there could have been a couple more child friendly attractions. The queues were not terribly long (tops 20mins) & were entertaining to make time go faster. The food was priced reasonably for a theme park, though the day we visited was very humid & there was little areas for relief from the humidity. Overall all a great day for all ages!

I am an annual pass member and have visited USS actively in the past year. Really tried all the rides and attractions in the park which information can be readily found over the Internet.  The Human and Cylon ride was the initial star, followed by the Transformers ride which was really state of the art. The 3D effect felt so real for once.  The Mummy ride was another not-to-be-missed. (Spoiler alert) I still remember how the ride nearly crashed into a wall, before reversing down a slope.  Together with the Jurassic Park wet ride, they make USS a fun place to hang out with friends, and a perfect place for lots of photography.  Do let me know if you need further details!

Spent 5hrs within the Universal Park with my family - not long enough. Amazing. Going on a Monday the crowds were somewhat lesser than during a weekend or holiday and queuing was relatively short. As with all of Singapore the area is spotless of rubbish. Staff pleasant. Plenty of shelter and fans to accommodate the heat. Attractions to cater for all ages and stages. Photos taken go for $20 each so can get a bit pricey by the time you complete all the attractions if you purchase everyone that has been taken. Food prices are usual for this type of place - take your own water if possible to help keep the costs down.  Would love to go again if ever back in Singapore.

This place is for all age groups... I wonder how they planned 2 make such a nice place. All the games are really different n for me it was really awesome All the games are theme based Buy vip pass whn u visiting in holidays n spl occations so tht u cover the whole place in one Day  U really need 2 move Fast 2 cover all the games in one day  The best is the water world that show is really worth.... it was a show tht i hav nevr seen b4.  Trust me Guys u ll love this place.... Few ppl may find this expncy but its really worth....  Varity of food also available... U can carry food along also Eat healthy b4 the rides.... Cheers enjoy.... u ll love it.....
amazing technology inside.. but you need an umbrella, sun glasses, hat, to cover up your skin, it's very hot out there..

We did not realise Universal Studios was open so we decided to go - wow, what a super day it was...very authentic (for a theme park) and one thing you have to do is for an extra $30 per person - buy the Express tickets - so you bypass the queue's - we got ours after waiting for 40 mins in the first ride...then go to the next - a 50 min wait - no ways - bpaid the extra and just walked past everyone...the next ride had a 55 min queue - walked right on and was on the ride in a minute - no waiting...it takes the stress out of it and you end up really enjoying it...so with that the adult ticket comes to around 100$ (SD) per head...but it is worth it.

Overall we had a great time. We paid extra for two passes to jump the line and loved the transformer ride. Did it 5 times. Got there early and so glad we did as we could jump on to more rides before all the queues grew. Food and drinks average and a little expensive but overall a great day. We will be back.
Great day out for the family. I was lucky enough to go on day the lines were all less than 5 minutes. The Donkey Live show was a little disappointing but for the most part this place is 10 out of 10

One day in this place is not enough, but good that we had our sister and niece who were working at Singapore and have gone to this place for the nth time, we were able to maximize the day that we alloted to this place. The Transformer ride was their newest attraction and it was trully an adventure of my lifetime. The long queue together with various nationalities was worth the wait. I would say that the amount spent to be able to have access to this place is worth the price.

Having been to the Universal Studios in Orlando as well as Los Angeles, It is obviously difficult for the Singapore version to match up due to its limited space. However, for whatever limited land it has, the park makes good use of it.  I've been here twice, once during the period it first opened and another time this year.  During the first trip, my experiences were marred by the fact that the key attraction, Battlestar Galactica, was closed. However, the other rides were still very enjoyable, such as the Mummy and the Jurassic Park one.  I ate pizza for lunch at the New York area of the park and the food was alright, but like everything in the park, obviously overpriced. I also bought a slushie that came in this long interesting bottle with a bendable straw that set me back more than 10 bucks.  Thankfully, I went to the park pretty early, around 10am when it first opened so it wasn't as packed and I managed to go on nearly all of the rides.  For the second trip, I went on a weekday so there were less people. However, even before the park opened, there were already long lines, mostly made up of tourists and student groups.  This time, Battlestar Galactica was up and running and I got to ride it 3 times, once on the human one and twice on the cylon. Very exhilarating, and definitely the star of the entire park. The queue for this was around 10 minutes, which was quite okay.  The transformers ride had also opened and this is definitely something for the kids to enjoy. The 3D effects are nicely done and the ride itself was just the right duration.  For lunch, I ate at this food court which served asian food. I paid more than 10 bucks for a sad plate of chicken rice and an unidentified brown jelly-like dessert. The chicken rice was not good, below the standards of most hawker centers. Both the rice and chicken were too bland. As for the dessert, I was fooled into thinking that it was chocolate pudding/mousse. It turned out to be some awful coconut jelly-like substance which I promptly discarded after one bite.  However, don't let the food discourage you. The fun you get from all the rides as well as the overall environment and atmosphere more than makes up for it. A great place for families to spend the day, or simply a group of friends to hang out at.

We spent an afternoon at the park. Having been to Disney world in Florida I was hoping for something spectacular. I didn't get that at all. I was expecting to see movie characters galore walking around interacting with customers. Nope, in most of the themed areas there were none to be seen. In Far Far Away there was no sign of a single Shrek movie character, nor in Transformers, Battlestar Galactica, Jurassic Park or The Mummy . I did get to see Beetleguise and that was it. So for me if you took away the rides, it would be a total waste of money.

The first time I visited Universal Studios was when the Transformers Ride just came out. Despite the park's small size, it was a wonderful experience. With Battlestar Galactica being the main attraction, I was especially impressed with its twin roller-coaster rides whereby both roller-coasters were specialized in their own unique styles i.e. G-force and loops.  However the recent implementation of shoulder straps to the "Human" ride has reduced the G-force effect significantly, thus defeating the purpose of the ride. I have also noticed that the speed of the ride itself was not as fast when it first came out. I understand that these changes could be safety regulations due to (possibly) previous incidents of safety breaches, but I consider the "Human" ride relatively safe compared to so many roller-coasters in the world. Thus, it would be better for RWS to monitor this ride and if possible, at least remove the shoulder straps once the ride is deemed "safer".  Overall, the theme park is still a great place to have fun and relax, but it can be made even better if the "Human" ride was changed back to what it previously was.  Hope this review was useful.

I am a big fan of US Hollywood. Went to USS before, was going to go there again, but after this incident, I don't think I ever wanna go there again.  I purchased 3 adult USS tickets with Mastercard promo, unaware that it was a single date ticket, because THE TERMS WAS NOT CLEARLY LAID OUT in the website. Technically I picked the date where I landed in Singapore, having prior knowledge that USS ticket is usually has window period validity.  Fast forward until today, I am getting ready to pack to Singapore, and how shocked I was to found out that it's a non-cancellation, non-alternation, non-refundable ticket.  Resorts World Sentosa should have made that clear in their website when we pick the promotional ticket, or put it somewhere one can easily read, but no, it turns out that the terms were contained in the tiny 'Terms and Conditions' link, and it was used against me by their Customer Service Representatives when I tried to raise the case.  Furthermore, the guy just advise me to 'transfer the ticket to relatives'.  I cannot follow his logic of saying that to a foreign tourist. Does he think everyone has distant relatives in Singapore whose doors we can just knock when we have useless USS tickets?  I am never going there again.  Thanks to USS/RSW ignorance, S$188 gone.
Like most theme parks this one is expensive but it was a lot of fun and the Transformers ride is a blast. I can’t wait to go back when my son is older and can enjoy more rides.

Had a fantastic time here. Only disappointment was queuing up for an hour for the Treasure Hunter ride which was quite boring and over in two minutes. Make sure you go on the Transformers Ride at Sci Fi City!

Just Wow. This place is great for family. The scenes and attractions we're arrange perfectly that it's easy to jump from one spot to another. Don't miss the Waterworld. It's a movie live in front of you!

On our second trip to Singapore, we decided to do Universal Studios. Upon arriving, we saw masses of people and decided to buy the express ticket as well. In total, S$248 for 2 adults. While the express ticket was good on some rides, we got through all the rides by 1pm. Warning: leave the rapids ride till last because you will get very wet. Alternatively, leave S$3 in your pocket before stowing all your belongings (for S$4) and buy a poncho. You will need it and it will be your best purchase on the day. Food is reasonable priced, however, if travelling with kids, bring snacks. They didn't check our bags coming in and we brought in coke and water so we didn't have to buy it continually. We left early and din't do any of the shows, but the water one at 4.30 is supposedly good. Overall, I wouldn't go back and still feel that Dreamworld or Movieworld (Gold Coast, Australia) is probably better value. However, if you do have kids, it would be worth spending 1 day there, but do check the website and see what they have and if it is worth the cash as it is an expensive day out.

I really enjoyed this. It is so much fun for toddlers and adults alike. Even better for teenagers. I wouldnt recommend it if you have a aby as you will be restricted. I however appreciated the child friendly facilities

Yep... A really great experience. I believe its really worth for the money you pay. And honestly you can manage to go for all the rides in one day with out the express pass. But if you like to attend the concerts and shows, you will have plan your trip really well as you wont have time to attend each and every show with all rides in leisure. Get the map and ask for the times of the shows from the information counter to plan your day. All in all its a wonderful way to spend a day.

This was my second times visited USS which last time here for about one year ago.  We felt that the attraction sight was increased and we love the transformer very much! but my sister like the mummy!  Some of the areas still look the same example, far far away 3D show, water world(FYI, during our show, there are technical fault and didn't watch till end), the harbour site building could have look into more development)  Tips: transformer must go & bring raining coat along to avoid any wet from the water park.

Although there are a comparable number of rides that are made for children and young adults, there are still too little rides in the park which was supposed to be a "world class" theme park.Being a Singaporean myself, I know Singapore is trying to develop in tourism and trying to be the best in Asia but this theme park is not up-to-standard.Even though there are some rides that are extremely worth the time to try out such as Transformers: The Ride and Battlestar Galactica, the theme park needs to be expanded and more rides be built in order to get that "world class" spot and also the satisfaction of the tourists so that their time in Singapore will totally be worth it.As a helping hand, how about getting new ideas from the Universal Studios-themed movies that are recent and making them into rides....and also making it a one-of-a-kind ride.It was still a great time in Universal Studios Singapore and those first-timers have to visit it.
It is a nice place to hang out with friends and family. Not too big but enough to go wander around for a day.

Must-visit attractions include Lights, Camera. Action!, Battlestar Galactica, Transformers, Revenge of the Mummy, Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure, WaterWorld, and Donkey Live. Opt for the Express Pass if time is tight. Queue lines can be crazy on weekends and public holidays.  Your Universal Studios ticket should come with a meal or retail voucher, good for outlets within RWS. Tip: Loui's NY Pizza Parlor serves awesome pizzas.  For photo opportunities, look out for roving TV personalities, but be quick because each character only appears for about 10 minutes at a stretch before heading backstage.

If you've been to universal Orlando or LA don't expect the same park as its much smaller and doesn't have a huge selection of rides but its still a really good day out.  We visited on a week day and there wasn't really any queues so got to do everything. It's pretty reasonably priced which was good.  We also visited on a Saturday night for the after dark party and had an amazing time. If your in the park during the day you can stay for free or you pay I think it was $20 and then add $13 for free flow drinks and can also do all you can eat for another $13.  There is a live band and the one that was on during our night were pretty good.  If you like to have a drink this is a really good night.

I went to Universal Studios Singapore (USS) on 15 December 2012. It was a Saturday so the place was jam-packed. I purchased the tickets online beforehand so I didn't have to join the long queue at the ticket booths. It was my first time at USS and never been to any other Universal Studios before so I was quite enchanted. I need to come again in the future since I didn't get to ride some rides. So here's my tips based on my experience. 1) Try to go on weekdays instead of weekends / school holidays. The crowd will be lesser. 2) Arrive early so that you have ample time. 3) Purchase tickets online 4) Go for the outdoor rides first because they will cease operation if the weather looks cloudy or if there's lightning or thunder. 5) Some rides don't allow you to carry your belongings with you but they provide lockers near the ride's area which are free to use with time limits of 30 mins, 55 mins etc depending on the lockers. 6) Some rides have the Single Rider's line where they use you to fill the empty seat left from incomplete party. I queued for the Transformers using this line and managed to get on the ride faster if I were to queue using the normal line. 7) I recommend you purchase the Express Pass ONLY when there's a really huge crowd and if you don't mind spending extra $50 to cut queues.

Loved the games, the shopping and the whole set up. The action roller-coaster was scary but amazing. I also loved taking pictures with Marilyn Monroe and Frankenstein! My favorite part was Hollywood. The only downside is the occasional rain.

Great theme park. My little daughter simply enjoyed the experience. Shrek (Far far away), Madagascar, The Mummy (Egypt), Lost World, Sci fi and Hollywood - great memories. strongly recommend taking the express pass of S$50 each - well worth it as one can finish all rides and shows in one day without the wait at each queue (some running into 1-2hours). the Parade was nice. highlights are the rides in Sci fi (Transformers, Cyclon and Human), Ancient Egypt, Lost World and some great shows, hollywood style!

We purchased a 2 day pass and are very thankful we did.  Day One: got there at 10.30 - park was already busy and we waited 2 hours for the Jurassic Park ride - only problem was they were quoting 1hr 10 mins. If it's a long wait tell people - that way they can make a decision on whether to move on to something else. We ended up leaving at 4.00 as the crowds by then were out of control. I'm sure they have a capacity limit, however you need sufficient attractions to keep that capacity crowd occupied. We are seasoned Disney visitors and have never experienced wait times like this. Disney know how to move and manage crowds!  Day Two: we didn't want to go back, but we had paid for the 2 day ticket and refused to be ripped off by paying an additional $60 EACH for the express pass (more on that later). I had a sneaking suspicion the park opened earlier than the advertised 10.00 and being experienced Asian travelers, know that they aren't really 'morning' people. Sure enough, got to the park at 9.30 as the gates were opening. We blitzed through the rides with zero wait times (including Transformers, the Mummy and Jurassic Park) and managed to fit in a coffee, some shopping (limited choices) whilst the kids went off on their own. Then the down pour came. We had some lunch and headed off by 1.00 completely satisfied with what we had done. It's very clear that afternoons are not the time to be at the park.  Fast pass: I appreciate that people have paid extra for this advantage, however if you are going to provide them with express entry into the park: give them their own dedicated entrance!!! The rudeness of some of these people is incredible - so desperate to get into the park they will push themselves into the middle of what is clearly a family of 4 so they can get a 10 second advantage.... the staff obviously have to be sooo polite to these people that they are unable to stand up to them and say show some manners, I will be with you in a moment and then are left embarrassed and apologetic to those in the line who have waited patiently. It's a joke the way they manage this system.  Single riders: yep, may seem like a good idea, but we witnessed many families take this option only to be on rides separated from their family members - in some cases it was 20-30 minute wait between each family member - how do you then coordinate the next ride you want to go on?  Food: despite the notices on the tickets about not bringing in your own food, there is NO policing of this. They do not check backpacks which is just absurd given that both in Australia and the US we are routinely checked and at some events, you aren't permitted to take in backpacks at all.  Prayer rooms: I am not particularly religious but am respectful of other religions. I don't think that the park is particularly friendly towards respecting peoples need to pray. On the first day, I was seated behind a 'cart' and then discovered that the area was being used a non-designated prayer area. The number of people that were stepping over or on prayer mats was disgraceful. Please give people some respect and provide a location for them to pray.  Overall: waste of money and time as the rides aren't that fantastic.

We visited as a family of 4 on New Years Eve. We found the park to be very good but small. We were staying for the New Years Countdown and this might have been a problem if we were not slowed by the rain. There just is not really enought to do for the 14 hours we were planning to be there although for a regular day when you didn't need to stay to a midnight deadline it would have been fine. Some advice on managing the waits for attractions...be there when they open the gates (on our day they opened early at 9:45). Go straight to the big attractions and ride them while the lines are low (nothing had a line longer than 10 mintues during our visit until after 11am). After 11am you will need the Express Pass for the bigger rides unless you want to wait in line for more than an hour for a single ride. Definitely worth the cost in my view although, yes, the express pass is expensive. Regarding the attractions, here's our take on what's what in the park. I'll start by noting that my family are not big on roller coasters so we did not ride the BattleStar Galactica Coaster or the Mummy Coaster which are probably the 2 biggest profile rides in the park. From what I saw and heard of them from others they would go in the "Excellent" category if you like big time coaster rides.  Outstanding Rides/Shows: Transformers - Best ride in the Studios hands down. A 3-D effects ride which makes you feel like you are in the movie. We rode this 3 times. Would have loved to do more. Should have started the day with this ride. Rock Monsters (Live Pop/Rock performance by Movie Monster Legends - Mummy, Vampire, Wolfman, etc). Sounds corny but really good show. Shrek 4-D Adventure - A funny short movie with 4-D effects. Lots of laughs. If you like the Shrek movies you will love this. Enchanted Airways - Junior Roller Coaster - Very mild coaster. If my family liked it almost everyone will. Canopy Flyer - Fun mild roller coaster. As noted my family does not generally like coasters. We rode this 4 times. Great fun. A must do in the dark as well if you stay in the park late. Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure - A fun mild "flume" type ride. Follow the warnings about getting wet. You will. An all ages fun ride. Great to cool off on a hot day in the park.  Good: Light's, Action, Camera - An interesting show that demonstrates movie special effects on a mock movie sound stage. Clever but not thrilling. Madagascar Crate Adventure - If you have been to Disney World this is basically the Winnie the Pooh Ride. Nothing scary - a mild tour through the Madagascar Movie. Accelerator - A spinning tea cup amusement ride. My kids love these rides. Water World - Ok, terrible movie but it makes a mildly entertaining live stunt show. Beware...if you are here on a rainy day expect long delays and even cancellation of the show. It rained a great deal on our day in the park and it took us 3 tries to catch the show finally.  Not worth the time: Donkey Live - Boring interactive show with bad jokes. May have just been that our crowd was dull but I think we laughed 2 times the whole show. Mostly just uncomfortable. Dino-Soarin' - The Disney Dumbo ride with a Jurasic Park theme. If you have young kids (10 and under) they will love it. Treasure Hunters - A HUGE let down as we love the Mummy Movie franchise. Nothing fun about these slow moving cars and the very dull "dig site" they drive through. You might as well walk around looking at this instead of going on the actual ride. BORING. Rockafellas - Street hip-hop dance show. Total time of show 5 minutes. They did one dance number and spent 4 minutes asking where everyone was from. Total waste of time. The guys seem like good dancers but they barely dance during the "show".  For the New Years Eve Countdown the resort puts on 2 shows...One in "Hollywood" and one in "New York". The Hollywood show was great and we spent most of our countdown here watching the Lady Gaga, Michael Buble and Adel tribute bands - all very good. The New york side had more traditional Christmas songs performed by various bands. Also very good. Both shows were followed by fireworks over the lagoon pool that is the center of Universal Studios.  A very fun family place to spend a day and a good place to spend New Years Eve.

Universal Studios, located in the Sentosa islands, Singapore...is an awesome attraction. It has many modes of entertainment, that it offers to people of all age groups..ranging from rides, roller-coasters, disney, and other cartoon characters to get clicked with, to the short 3-D movies...We all simply loved the place, and never wanted to come back.....Do visit wenever u get an opportunity to do so.... HAPPPY HOLIDAYING!!!! :-)
The new Transformers ride was well worth the visit alone. Unfortunately, the day we visited there was a lot of rain and electrical activity so the rides ran intermittently. We still had a great day.

Girlfriend and I visited Universal Studio on a Tuesday we went early morning arriving at 9:30am. The gates do open earlier around 9:30 before 10 anyway. My Hot Tip "GO EARLY" we got our maps of the park when we purchased our tickets (which I recommend you don't need a 2day pass) Having our maps before it opened we where able to map out our route we chose to run to what we think would be the main attractions first and leave the site seeing till later. We went to Jurassic park which was really good the water ride they try and tell you that you will get wet I think it's just a move to get you to purchase a poncho. Transformers was fantastic the ride was really good and well thought out. Shrek was good for all ages as well good 4D experience. Steven spilbergs movie scene in the theatre was also really cool to see.  Overall was a good day. But with out question I would go early! When you line up for rides you see what is coming very soon and that's massive lines every ride and attraction has rails zig zagging all around to cater for the huge amount of people. Going late in the day expect huge waits in the line.  Our experience was great by the time it got busy we had done all the rides and enjoyed the park all that was left was site seeing and taking photos.

While this park is undeniably small in comparison to the one in Orlando it is also far cheaper too, Regardless there is still plenty to see and when we visited in Decemeber the ques wern't too bad at all. Because the park is newer than those in Orlando there are also new 'lands' such as shrek and transformers and the rides (although far fewer) seem more innovative- transformers was amazing and far better than the spiderman version in Florida. They also had fake 'snow' for Christmas when we visited and a small show and light switch on which was great. All in all, despite the torrential rain, we had a great day!

Visited Universal Studio in January 2013 with family. My five year old really enjoyed the whole experience. The place is ideal for children and adults. The other place which I can compare this place with is Genting Highland. Though the number of rides are more in Genting, I would say the quality of attractions available and the maintenance and house keeping is far suprior in Universal Studio.  Parents with young children should not miss Madagascar.  There are good choice of reataurants in the theme park and the palce is filled with fun and activities through the day.  One tip for travellers during peak holiday season. The place can get crowded with long Qs for entry to various attractions. Many people suggest you to buy the fast track tickets. However, my reommendation from my experience is to not to buy the fast track tickets in advance and decide whether you need to buy or not at the venue. The ticketing staff themselves will tell you if you really need to buy a fast track or not.  Overall, a visit to Singapore on a hoiday is incomplete without a day spend in Universal Studio.

All rides are good. Don't miss Shrek 4d ,most awesome ride  If possible try to buy express pass otherwise you will spend lot of time standing in queue.

We have visited there on last week of January, 2013. Some advice who are planning to go: 1. There is a free shuttle bus starting from Orchard hotel at 9AM to each half hourly. Be sure to pick the first trip to avoid rush in USS. Must keep your passport with embarkation card. Its totally free. Both in and out. 2. We reached there 9:30AM and have photograph outside. At 10AM the gate opens. I just rushed to Sci fi city and rode to Transformer 3D. Within 10 minutes we finished it with the minimum rush. The show is simply best in USS. Then i went to Battestar gallactica and kept my luggage in a cupboard for 30 minutes. As no rush still there, i finished ride within 15 minutes and didn’t pay any money for locker. 3. Then we went to Shrek 4D film. So many people gathered as it was around 11AM but in one show many was gathered. The show was simply awesome which includes water and air spray to your body to give you 4 D feel. 4. After that we entered the Lost world show. Don’t Sit on the down rows as they will throw water directly to your body. We sat on the top rows and thus survived from getting wet. The show was so so. 5. Don’t waste your time in photo in early time; till 1pm. Try to get to ride within this time. There are many shows on road and characters meet and greet. Catch them later. If you can follow above steps you have already saved 50 SGD for express pass!!!  Thanks Showkat  Hope this was helpful to you. If you have any query sent queries to aurthohin2000@yahoo.com

Traveled with 3 young children. We all had a lot of fun. Plenty of rides for adults and children alike. Speed pass was definitely worth it to be able to see everything in one day. The shows felt like full 4D experiences that were both an adventure and a bit educational.

USS is a bit pricey but students can get good discounts sometimes, so don't forget to check! We went on a weekday during one of the off-peak periods, and it was really nice because there wasn't any queue. We could go on the Battlestar Galactica and Transformer rides five times each without having to queue at all. Be prepared to take a lot of pictures!

My 5th visit to USS in 2012 :-) USD63 for the entrance fee but its really worth it. Open at 10am and quickly queue for 'transformer'.....if not...you have to queue more than 1 hour for the ride. Unless you bought 'express lane' ticket with an additional cost of USD40 per person. U really need this during peak season. Dont miss the opportunity to watch 'Water World' at the theater...it was really amazing with the sound & light effects. Watch during the night show. You wont regret. Food court is just next to the main entrance...and for Malaysian...theres a Malaysian Food Street out there but only 2 stalls with halal food...'Nasi Lemak' and 'Nasi Briyani' stall...price is around USD1-3...the rest is not halal. Wear comfortable walking shoes...bring fan...wear sun block...and a proper wear...when its hot...its really hot :-) but when it rains...they will sell a rain coat at USD1 down there.

Its was great day between different ages different moods ...only most of the playing machines doesn't suites bellow 4 years if u r taking ur family..if u r couple it will be great memory for u two.. Watching how fictions happen ,egyptian monuments ,madgascars,new york,its really great. Must visite
Brilliant! we live on the Gold Coast where we have great theme parks, but were very impressed with USS. Highlight was Sci fi world rides so good.

We travelled with 3 children and despite being told taxi was expensive and slow, we took one from downtown at only SGD 12 and only 30 min ride. The park itself is really nice and not crowded at all. We went on a monday as we have been told weekends can be crowded. Waiting was only an issue at a couple of major rides, so we skipped them as the lines were 45 min. But a hint is to go to the part you most want to see in the morning when crowds are less. We went to Madagascar and Shrek areas and found no queues at all. Restaurants were clean and not price. Only thing I would do differently is to book tickets online, so to avoid the long ticket queue.

Visit to universal studio was so much fun that we cant explain it. So many shows with so much entertainment!!!! My children enjoyed each and every ride and I must say dont miss anything there... Great place to get entertained..Need full 7-8 hours so start early... Costly but I advise you to take 2 days pass for sentosa and USS. Its worth.

Go on weekdays which don't need to queue up for long. We have ride transformers for twice coz not many people. We go out the Universal Studio for lunch coz' u allowed to re-entry during the day. Food outside the park is better than those in.

with our 2 kids we have been there on a friday in april 2013. We got the express pass, even it was not very busy. I am not sure if we really needed that extra pass but it was a nice too pass the cues even they were not too long anyway. For the parents the best experience was the Transformer 4D show. AMAZING!!! For the kids the highlight was the Madagascar water ride and the Shrek 3D film. I enjoyed the Waterworld stunt show...even a bit loud and brutal for young kids.

We were 6 of us entered USS in the weekends which was last weekend ;) .. The place is full of wonders. Its like the Movie scenes come true!!.. Amazing customer service from the staffs. We ate our lunch in KT Grill in USS it self.. Not so pricy. Just love the place looking forward to go again. Special tips: Stay untill 6pm/7pm you dont have to que up for the ride ;)

One of the best theme park I ever visited. There is something for every age group. I personally liked the 4D Transformer and the Mummy ride. The transformer ride is just awesome. The simulation is really great and not at all scary. The hollywood park is also nice. We saw a action skit which left us amazed. I was really looking forward for the Madagascar park but it is disappointing, may be its meant for kids :). The park is not very big but big enough to take up entire day. There are plenty of eating options including Indian food. Overall its promises a fun day.

This place is probably not for little kids aged 5 and below as the rides are quite scary (by their standard). There's not many activities for our little fellas. Overall, worth the visit but I think it will be long before I revisit.
Busy - yes. But get there early and have a ball - top entertainment for the kids. If you only have half a day - go the extra and avoid the que's and pay the extra.
I wouldn't bring young children. A lot of queue jumping and shoving spoiled the experience. Other than that, great rides, great attractions but for an older crowd.

Spent one whole day at the Universal Studios in Singapore with family, ages ranging from 7 to 50. My 2 teenager companions coaxed me to ride the blue roller coater. I thought it would be fun at first, having ridden several roller coasters in the past but the Battlestar Galactica ride in Universal was terrifying and at the same time exhilarating!  The Sesame Street show brought back memories having grown up with Big Bird, Ernie and Bert. it was however, the Far Far Away castle that brought out the kid in me. It was fun seeing Donkey and Prince Charming and some of the other casts. I didnt see Shrek and Princes Fiona though.  For SGD$ 63 each (discounted as we got our tickets online), we had one day of fun and adventure! We were at the gates 30 minutes before it opened at 10:00 am to take wacky pictures with the "universal globe" as background. Using the maps given at the gate, we chose to begin our day with the madagascar park at the left of the entrance to escape the crowds who were heading to the Hollywood studios. Each brought a survival kit containing extra shirt,towelette and fan. Dont forget your raincoats!  .  The

We last visited Universal Studios in Sept 2011 and decided this trip we needed another visit as the kids were much older. Second time around was definitely better than the first as we knew exactly which way to go around and what to see first. I lost track on how many times the kids went on the Battlestar Gallactica ride as they kept getting off and lining up again. This was the highlight for the boys aged 12 & 14. I decided to go on the Mummy ride and enjoyed it very much even if it being in the dark was a little scary at first. Transformers was another hit. We thoroughly enjoyed the day and again I firmly believe that it is value for money. We managed to spend heaps and buy loads again so there was a cost there of course. Overall it is a great day out and everything is very well priced.
A was very impressed with how clean it was. The rides were fantastic, but there was not alot of variety. If you get the chance to do the Transformers ride, I highly recommend you do, it blew my mind!

The park is not too big and not too small, it is just nice and sufficient to have fun and enjoy yourself.  They have variety of rides for guests of different ages and great shows to entertain everyone. Just make sure you get the Express pass as it will change the scenario of your visit to this park.  The restaurants are also very nice and lots of halal choices for Muslim guests.  The only downside of yhe park is that it is not adapted with the weather of the country. The rain could possibly ruin your trip or the hot sunny day could also dry-out your energy to have fun.

This place is a must do!  The park is very well themed, the staff are all great and the park itself is very clean. On a number of the rides, there are lockers available with no charge for an hour or so, so you can enjoy the ride. The transformers ride is amazing!  To do the whole park you need 3/4 of the day.

Brilliant and entertaining, it has something for every adult and kid. Arriving half an hour before opening time gives you a lead over the crowd which lets you not just conserve energy, see the best first and comfortably, but also do a few most popular rides multiple times! There are prams and trolleys available for hire here too. Being the first in queue gave us chat-time with the staff, who told us to do an anti-clockwise route, so that the more activity oriented ones are completed first. That indeed was one great advice. After the Steven Spielberg (amazing) and surrounding sections, we managed to do the super popular Transformer ride twice over, before heading to do both the Blue and Red (Cyclone and Galactica) roller coasters, to get our insides thoroughly churned before heading to the remainder sights and the food zones! We managed to stick to the advice received and completed the entire trip in about 6 hours, despite the rain. The daredevil waterworld show was a superb finale, before heading to the SEA Aquarium just opposite to the Universal Studios gate. Along Hollywood Boulevard, I also managed to take a pic along with Marylin (Monroe for you guys!), but Frankenstein got scared seeing me and deprived me the photo-op! The kiddo had fun with the duck, mouse, fairy and the like, as also every single ride there. The food courts are well laid out and so are the water filling points. It is advisable to carry umbrellas/ caps as well, and when heading for the blue and red roller coasters, remember to take a locker and dump every loose item (including non-secure slippers, goggles and caps) before you launch! Or catch hold of the weak tummied and make them security in-charge! The Dinosaur Park ride is superb, and the poncho is recommended only for one member who can also carry the wallet, camera and bag within the poncho. This way, every other member gets to be drenched and have the full fun quotient of the ride. Drying up in the heat is no worry, all it takes is half an hour. And if it is rainy, either way you'll be wet! A word of caution for the Daredevil Waterworld show - when they mean 'splash zone' they mean soak/drench/pickle, so those on the border of tolerance please stay behind! Even that way there is no guarantee the stunt guys will spare you!!! Must see, with a capital 'M' and 'S' there! And if you visit minus the kids, beware the wrath that awaits!!

We came to the theme in a family of four; two adults, 8 years old and 5 years old kids. We just managed to try Jurassic Park (Adventure wet ride), Water World, Science (Transformer), Madagascar, Cinema, Far Far Away (Shrek4D show). Some rides have height requirement, check it before you enter. So, we could not go for Battlestar Galatica and Revenge of Mumy. Buy ticket early for discount to avoid queue at the box office. When spend declare if you have MasterCard and may be granted 10% off. Stay till 5pm for hollywood parade and 8pm for the fireworks. In between this period you may get ride waiting time as minimum as 5 minutes!

Spent some time here on our last day of our honeymoon as we had some time to kill after checking out of our hotel and waiting for our flight later that evening. I think Universal Studios is more catered to families and teenagers but we still had a pretty good time. Managed to go on most of the rides. The lines thankfully weren't too long for most. Plenty of places to eat though quite expensive.

Please do not go on a weekend, school holidays or public holidays. We went on a Vesak Day holiday, the wait for Transformer was 3 hours! If you really have no other choice, then suggest to buy the express pass.  The human and cyclone was thrilling, if you go on a weekend , the park closes at 8pm . There are fireworks only on weekends.  Bring raincoats,umbrellas and lots of water. Choice of food is plenty average about s$12 per burger set. The park is smaller than the other universal studios in LA or Osaka, but the rides are definitely more thrilling.  Thank you

Naturally, for a family with kids, Universal Studios Singapore is a must.  Good thing that the theme park is easily accessible via many methods because the free shuttle bus from strategic places in the country is always full on weekends. The bus driver was nice enough to radio ahead to the person at the pick-up point that his bus could no longer accommodate additional riders. There went the free shuttle but rather than waste time waiting, we took cabs to Sentosa and got there faster. Tip # 1. Be flexible.  Of course, the best time to go would be a weekday. You will have a lot of the park to yourself. If you do intend to be there on a weekend, make sure you come early. By lunch time on a Saturday, the place is packed. Since we arrived early enough, we were able to get a few rides under our belt with almost no line up time. Tip # 2. Be early.  If you cannot be early, plan strategically. Expect to have longer lines for the roller coasters so lunch time (when many are eating) might be a good time to line up for the thrill rides. By the way, do not eat before riding the roller coasters. I did not ride them myself but my husband and kids said that they were glad they opted for lunch after the coasters. They enjoyed "Revenge of the Mummy" and survived the (literally) gravity-defying Cylon. If you are not a speed freak, you still have Madagascar and Treasure Hunters.  Do not miss the Lost World water ride. I opted not to buy a rain coat and got soaking wet and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I imagine though that not everyone would be happy getting drenched. Also, do not miss "Lights, Camera, Action!" It is an impressive tour of a movie set. Again, this involves water. Tip # 3. Expect to get wet.  Do not plan to do anything but Universal Studios for that day. It is tiring, involving a lot of walking. If you go during the summer, you will have to contend with the energy-zapping heat too. Tip # 4. Wear the most comfortable shoes and cool clothes that you have. Bring a small face towel for the expected sweat.  Bring a camera so that you can save some money on photos. I have to admit that the park photos are very nice but they are pricey. The entrance tickets themselves are not all that cheap. But, is it worth it? Definitely. For the delight that I saw in my kids' eyes, this was worth it.

Stayed in johor baru. Went there by bus. Stopped at the Merlin tower and bought a to and for bus ticket to USS. The 707 counter open by 8.30am. They have buses there daily every hour by first come to book first get it basis. It's only $5 per head. Took 2 hours to reach USS as there will be 2 points kastam check in(vise versa) and traffic jam towards the woodland check in point. You can safe precious time from the USS ticket booth by buying from the 707 bus counter with a same price in ringgit or in sing.money.and don't forget to get the white card from them too to fill in ur custom/passport particulars. The USS activities are fun, suitable only for bigger children to healthy adults as there are a lot of vibrant,loud movement and sounds in most of the rides and also the long 20-60 minutes waiting for the games/rides. There were many long maze of waiting queues. The USS opens from 10-6pm.
