There some nice catchy shows and Disney characters walk around where u can take photos with but I would rather play the games before the crowd enlarges. The transformer, shriek, egypt /mummy rideb is nice..(to name a few.) Bring extra shirt for change as u'l get wet by some rides and also by sweats, cap,umbrella,mineral water to hydrate ur self from the hot sun. And maybe some snacks/bread as the food is quite costly.
Being small, the queues are long, even for those with Express tickets, so, we had to go for the ridiculously expensive VIP option.

This place was beyond amazing! i loved it! Its worth going again! I had soo much fun with my friends and family! You have to go on the Space Galactic Human and the Cylon but i only managed to go on the human one! it was amazing! There are zoo many amazing rides that you cant explain all of them! Well you will just have to find out yourself! YOU CAN ALSO GET AN EXPRESS PASS TO SKIP THE LINES!  HOPE YOU HAVE FUN! I DEFINITELY DID! AND SHARE UR EXPERIENCE! :)

Universal Studios Singapore is a wonderful place. It is quite different and smaller to Universal Studios in California however just as much fun if not more so. The best ride is Transformers, do not miss out on this ride it is a must do.......it is well worth going to this ride first as the waiting times when we were there were as long as 45mins - 1 hour for this ride. Our daughter who was 7 years old was able to go on the Transformers ride and loved it. If you go on the Jurassic Park ride be prepared to get wet to the bone or though that is a nice cool down in the heat of the day. Most of the rides had queues at least 20mins long the day we went, we were there mid week in the hope to miss the weekend rush.....I guess it is just busy all week, I bet the weekends are crazy. A queue jumper pass for this theme park would be well worth investing in. We were there from 10am - 7pm and still didn't manage to go on all the rides as spent a lot of time stuck in queues.  Besides the queues we had a wonderful time and would most definitely go back again. It is a big day especially in the heat and humidity of Singapore so be prepared to pace yourselves if going with young children.  One of the best characters we saw was Puss in Boots from Shrek.....so realistic and quite the character.

We visited this place in december so the climate was perfect experience this outdoor attraction and wow what an experience we had.. Right from the entrance to the first ride of madagascar that we sat to the water world show the jurassic park ride, the battlestart gallactica ride the road shows the 4d theatre just about everything in this place spells MARVELLOUS and AMAZING.. We spend a full day here going through all the rides and shows and just kept on feeling we need more.. Must say a Superb staff always smiling and will to help you through. A must visit place this is in Singapore. Would defineatly be coming here again and again!!!

Its a very fun filled and awesome place . You cant expect it to get better . Try out all the shows and awesome rides as they are very entertaining . Especially kids , teens and young people.  For adults its fun as long as you have good weather or good company or you are willing to take it on.  Please check weather and wear suitable clothes . Weather can get really humid and drain you out.  Please check at every ride about the conditions and suggested Do's and Dont's .  Some rides For Eg The Revenge of the Mummy can be very dangerous for people with heart conditions etc or elderly people. If you just walk in No one might tell you what the rides are all about untill you ask them .  So its better to check at the rides counter .  Take a One Day pass and make it on Time to utilize the full value.  Have a great Time.

I've been to all the Universal Studios now. I think this was quite good. It's a smaller version of what I've seen in US. But definitely manageable to the entire park in a day. Be sure to get the speed lane pass, it really helps!  We loved the Mummy, roller coaster and transformers ride the most...  Food choices are nothing great...

This is somewhere that you must include in your itinerary for Singapore! Went with my parents and partner, and even my parents (70 & 60) were getting in on the rides! Unfortunately it was raining when we were there so some rides were closed and we had a wait a little longer for others but it was worth the wait. Food is expensive as you would expect, and there is lots of expensive merchandise to choose from. Definitely need a whole day here.

I have taken this attraction along with combo day pass offer with Sentosa Day pass for around 125 sing dollar. It has many parts such as madgascar, lost world, Newyork, Hollywood, Ancient egypt, sci-fiction and one more. Each part is based on that theme and have rides, shops and eateries that are based on that theme. Rides are amazing, attractions are wonderful and awesome. Everything seems to be perfect and treat for eyes. A must do attraction in Singapore but only drawback is long ques and waiting time in some attraction it is around two hours. So it is advisable and highly recommended that one must take express pass before hand along with ticket that cost extra 50 sgd otherwise you will end up in seeing only half attractions.
The first trip to Singapore. I have purchased reserve tickets in advance. The Universal singapo pretty as well Universal Usa and big. I love roller coaster it was fun and Excited.

We visited USS and enjoyed the experience.  We got to ride Transformers The Ride (twice!), Battlestar Galactica:Human, Revenge of the Mummy (twice) and the other rides in the park. It is still small in comparison to Hong Kong Disneyland and the kiddie rides in Disney were much better and more detailed.  The Spaghetti Space Chase and Madagascar The Crate Adventure were disappointments as there was too much space in between installations and sections of the rides. Jurassic Park Rapids Adventure was ok but I think the Enchanted Kingdom Rio Grande Rapids (Philippines) is way cooler!  Waterworld was great entertainment and you are bound to get wet! Transformers The Ride, Battlestar Galactica,and Revenge of the Mummy probably are the rides that make you say that it was worth going to USS.  I'm not sure if the kids that you brought to Disneyland would enjoy USS the same way as I think USS caters more to teens and adults in general.  Oh by the way, don't waster your time watching Monsters Rock! It can't compare to Disney's Golden Mickeys or One Man's Dream. Better do a repeat of Transformers than watch this show.
The visit was worthwhile but it would have been more fun if we came earlier to enjoy and repeat many attractions and rides during cool weather months.

This write up may appear slightly different from other reviews on this attraction which is spread over the large area and has many entertainments..Youngster can enjoy rides most dangers but among the best in the world ; where as those on wheel chairs and elders may just stroll around and see tricks being performed ; while walking around get yourself photographed with jokers and performers but have to form Q wait and at some place pay for this ; old model cars are on display.Enjoy 4 D shows and children movies . If one likes'please there are shops for souvenir etc etc ----.The only problem is heat ; hot and humid conditions which makes every body specially elderly exhausted Take plenty of waters . If one want to enjoy Universal Studio comfortably take two days time . There are long Qs for every ride and most of rides are enjoyed by youngsters .The entry fee is on higher side .The whole area is noisy with music and over crowded . However it is one of best place worth visiting during trip to Singapore Universal Studio

We have been to the LA universal, but this one is great. Its nice and small which suits smaller children, but also has the rides for older kids to. The Waterworld show was awesome and the highlight of the day.

Located in the Resorts World Sentosa complex, Universal Studios is a full day attraction. We visited the venue with our 4-year old child and she enjoyed most of the rides and entertainment, specifically the ones in the New York and Madagascar areas. There is enough to keep adults entertained as well.

ti absolute love it here, i bring my 1 and half year old son and 6 months pregnant at the time . and the park is perfect for us not too big nor too small. you will finish the park with in a day easily ( adults ) or a day and half if you want to walk slowly or bring small kids . the food are better at Disney but the attraction are as great as Disney.

We caught a taxi from our hotel to the top of the cable car and then had a fun way to get to Sentosa Island. We arrived at 10am and a short walk downhill, we got to the ticket office for Universal Studios. We didn't have to wait too long to purchase our tickets. I had decided earlier not to purchase the VIP pass as I had heard mixed reports and that you couldn't repeat rides and get to the start of the line. In hindsight as we were on limited time and didn't end up repeating any rides, this option would of suited us perfectly - oh well you live and learn.  The park wasn't too crowded and as per a review in the forum, we headed to Scifi Land first and then worked our way around anti clockwise. The Terminator ride was a lot of fun, as were the two roller coasters. We had finished the park in a few hours and didn't need to view waterworld as we had already seen this twice in LA. All in all the park is fun but isn't a patch on the 'real thing'. We headed back to the cable car and exited at the shopping centre and caught a taxi back to our hotel ( the taxi wait took about 30 minutes)

This is really the longest and tiring queue that I ever did entire of my life. But all the tired and emotional feeling will be paid at once when you ride the car and enjoy the attraction. If the queue is not that long, I will ride it many times.

The "highlight" of Singapore. Truly marvelous. Unparallelled experience for first time visitors. It is not as big as the one in Orlando but the size is perfect for a day trip. The place is very organized and you dont need Express Passes unless you have picked a public holiday maybe. I took my kids there on the birthday of my elder son, they had a blast.  The Transformers, Mummy, Shrek 4D are must, we went to the Transformers twice.  The Character parade wasnt that great, maybe because they dont have many presentable/exciting characters. The fireworks are done too late in the day, we waited for an extra hour for it but then it was called off due to rain.  Take lots of water with you, you will need it on a sunny day.  Just Go, you will love it!

We went to Universal Studios at Singapore because of all the reviews about Sentosa. It is actually interesting how they've built a complete entertainment island, that is What Sentosa means. Still for someone that has been to Universal Studios in the U.S. the one in Singapore is really small, they only have 1 great attraction and when we went it was close for mantainance (if you buy your ticket at Vivo city be careful because they didn't inform us that the attraction was closed! They work as an agency and are not part of the Universal Studios, you can buy your ticket at the main entrance in Sentosa). The rest of the attractions are great for kids but not that interesting for grown-ups. When going there, don't take the railway, the boardwalk is only a 7 minutes walk with nice scenery and it only cost s$1. You can reach it from Vivo's city lobby.
Liked it all,we went in August and it was quiet,but i can imagine it getting really busy on other times of the year.Then it would be Hell

We went on a public holiday and I expected the worst. But, with the universal express it was actually a pleasant experience. Did not regret purchasing the express pass. Our longest wait was at the canopy flyer at the Jurassic Park. Best ride goes to the Transformers 3d ride. It was thrilling! Unfortunately the battlestar gallectica roller coasters were not in service and The Mummy ride had technical issues and they closed temporarily. Was impressed with the layout of the park, availability of ample clean restrooms with drinking water fountains.

Getting there We took MRT to Harbour front station and had lunch at Vivocity (huge mall). We then took the RWS8 bus outside Vivocity into Sentosa. after you get off the bus it is very close to the entrance of Universal  The park After getting pictures with the symbolic spinning globe head inside the park! the park is not gigantic you can definitely finish everything in 1 day. My hubby is a big transformers fan and loved the ride and merchandise. Make sure you ask the staff about the character greetings - humans dressed up as Optimus Prime and Bumble Bee come out for short time and specific times during the day - don't miss it! go line up early.  There are a lot of characters throughout the park to take pictures with, minus the long queues at disneyland! my only dislike was the lack of food selection in the park - only fastfood available.  Apologize that i am writing this review way too long after visiting and the only vivid memory is transformers. Overall loved this park very much and recommend it for all. Leaving the park is also very easy taking the RWS8. For some reason it was free on the way out.

After paying S$74, we found out that the main attraction, Battlestar Galactica, was closed on the day we visited because of the rain. I would think that they should've offered a discount since not all rides were available. If you don't want to line up 30minutes -1 hour for a ride that may just last one minute, then you have to shell out another S$60 to buy express privileges. Place was quite small and the rest of the rides not thrilling enough.

I visited Universal Studios, Singapore in April 2013 with my partner and my parents. We queued for approximately 10 minutes for tickets (10% off with an international passport) and then entered the park. The approach to this venue is an experience in itself, the giant Universal Studios Globe fountain was a highlight, as was the giant candy store (complete with giant candy decorations). The park is very well maintained, clean, bright and modern. Wheelchair/electric ride-ons are available from the front gate as needed. Clearly no expense was spared on creating a fully engaging experience here - the New York City street landscapes were amazing and each "world" area was in perfect theme - right down to the themed cafe/restaurants/merchandise stores in each.  There were a good range of food options in each area and plenty of refreshment stands, also vendors selling chilled water spritzers with fans attached - they were a godsend in the humidity of Singapore,as were the shaded areas. We purchased the VIP line ride add on ($30 SGD) to get to the front of the ride queues, but the lines weren't too bad anyway (except the Transformers 3D ride at 90 minutes wait time). My favorite was the Egypt area where everything was in perfect theme - including giant replica structures of Anubis and Egyptian costumed staff parading around for free photograph opportunities (Cleopatra, Prince of Theives, etc). Even the ride line to the Revenge of the Mummy attraction was perfectly detailed as the interior of an Egyptian Pyramid. The Battlestar Galactica roller coaster had two options - the "Human" or "Cylon" ride - the latter being the more extreme, but both were very fun (I went on the Cylon 4 times). As we were all adults, I did not really check out the children's options - but I saw many a smiling little face around the park.  Overall, it was an immensely enjoyable experience, I was blown away by the intricacy of each world and the swift, efficient service provided. The trip over to Sentosa Island is great too - I recommend the cable car to top off your day.

My family and I spent four days in Singapore recently, one day of which was spent at Universal Studios on Sentosa. It's great fun for all ages. Themed zones including Jurassic Park and Far, Far Away and great rides in each zone. Best of the bunch for us were the Jurassic Park Rapids and Canopy Flyer and the Transformers ride though my 10 year old was a bit scared so definitely not for the faint-hearted or very young.  We went mid-week and the queues for rides weren't bad at all - half an hour maximum but mostly less than 10 minutes. The food outlets are refreshingly good value and not a McDonalds in sight! Chicken and rice platter was delicious. Water and other soft drinks are pricey though so take plenty with you.  All in all - a great fun day out for everyone.
Loved the place though I think there should be more awesome rides especially for the young ones so that they get to enjoy as well.

Wounder full experience remember my child hood days Best rides include Transformers, Jurassic Park and The Mummy Returns and Human . The park is broken down into several zones, including New York, a magical kingdom, ancient Egypt and Jurassic Park. well manage Queues can be long but its fun to be there

Oh My God i just loved this place.full of fun,my favorite cartoon characters all over the place.So colourful,lively. Love the food and candies.The shows were awesome.All of the stuff to do was a surprise in its own way.The transformer ride was paisa vasool.The souvineers were so damn kool.I am 28,but was a 10yr old all over again.i will come back for sure.

Loads to do at the theme park but the queues are long. My advice would be to start from Madagascar rides first and then work your way to New York! We managed to ride the Transformers 3D ride without any queue because everyone was watching the parade :p Sadly the best and main attraction of the place was closed for maintenance AGAIN! sighs.  Note: Foreigners with passports can get 10% off admission tickets

my family went to Universal Studio in Sentosa Singapore... I approached the customer service to check if they give special assistance to person with disability (PWD), YES.... they were very accommodating, they issued 3 special unlimited pass for my visually impaired son, myself and my husband as an addition they give 20 pcs express pass to any attractions/rides for my two other children...recommended rides are transformer which my VI son truly enjoyed, accelerator, the mummy, shrek and alot more.....

A day or two must be kept separate to enjoy universal studios at Singapore....  the rides are worth the entry fee you pay, dont miss the Transformers section and their amazing 4d ride....about 60$ SGD pp....

1 word to describe : Awesome! It's a must go place in Singapore. The prayer room available for muslim (between cyclone & Jurassic park). Wear your rain coat if u wish to ride the boat in Jurassic Park. It will be totally wet.

This was my first ever trip to Universal Studios anywhere! Though by the size of it, Universal Studios Singapore is much smaller than its counterparts elsewhere in the world, it is amazing to see how much the creators have managed to capture into the park. We had spent the entire day at the attraction and still had to leave a few rides/ attractions for our next visit to Singapore! The place in itself is amazing.,..you have rides and attractions for everyone and for all ages and no matter what age you are, you end up finding yourself like kid in a candy store!! It was an awesome experience!!!All hands down one of the most amazing experience in Singapore!!
The rides were fun & staff were polite. Queues got a little long as the day went on - definitely worth it to purchase the express passes.

My tip - if you have primary school-aged kids who won't tolerate long queues, get there early at opening time and get the big rides in first (like The Mummy and Transformers). By midday (when the teenagers have woken up) the crowds are bigger and the waits times up to 90 per ride. The rides are over so quickly compared to the 20-30 minute queue you have just had!You can buy an express pass to 'jump the queue' if you want to. The food was not good - but I expected that. ( I hadn't been to a theme park before, and was a little cynical) I have to admit we had lots of fun and the Transformers ride was so thrilling, I don't think I'll ever forget it!

We visited as a couple to Singapore for the first time and as researched, Universal Studios stood to be a must visit if in Singapore. We went on a saturday. Started our day there around 10.30 and as being foreign nationals at Singapore, got 10% discount on tickets by flashing our passports. Its a big island which is constructed very well and i will suggest picking up the map before starting the journey. As we being indians and used to visit Essel World and Water kingdom, Comparitively, we felt this outing a not so exciting one. For 73$ a person, this might be given a miss. But considering the fact that it has rides like, The Transformers, The Mummy, Shrek the movie and Lost world, it should not be missed. Albeit all these rides are a one time entertainment.Being a weekend, the rush was expected, but the wait time was exorbitant which amounted to over 90 minutes of waiting for popular rides.After waiting for such longer times, the excitement diminishes and it becomes tiring to wait under the grueling sun. The major attractions, both of the Battlestar Galactica roller coasters were closed on saturday, and were replaced by fireworks in the evening, which was a major disappointment. I would suggest checking on the availability of the rides and only then visit this park.All in all, this park is a one time visit if you're expecting much from it. If you havent visited Disney land or Essel world or any other park, this might be a welcome experience for you. In Singapore and you have time with ample money, do visit this one.

Universal studios in Singapore could be considered one of the costliest attractions if you were to Singapore for some amusement. costs around SGD 74 if you buy your tickets there but a bit less if you prefer to buy it from somewhere else that gives discounted prices like your hotel, travel agents, etc.  There are just a handful of rides for adults and kids but my favorite is the 3D Transformers ride. A parade was also there when I went on a Saturday lasting about 15 mins. The fireworks display at 8pm was also so-so. For smokers like me, there are some places to go ahead and light a cigarette.  If you were the type who enjoys rides and amusement, this is for you. For me, a half day (2pm to 8pm) was already enough to take some pics, get on some rides and enjoy the place.
We've been to the Universal Studio in Orlando and California and this one is pretty much the same. Kids will love it, adults will not.

Cable car,Tiger Sky Tower,S.E.A. Aquarium,Cansio,Beach, The Merlion and Universal Studios are all inside Sentosa. Interesting and good experience during few hours inside the island. Everybody should enjoy the update Singapore .
Universal studios singapore is good but very small in comparison to Orlando however overall a good decent park with enough for the kids to enjoy - one day is more than enough though
A must to all themes. A different experience in each theme. Takes a lot of time . Can be a good idea to spend more than a day

This was a fun day out for me and my wife on our honeymoon.We got there pretty much at opening time and we had already brought a ticket from the airport so we didn't have to wait in line to buy the tickets. It is a good idea to buy the ticket before going to the attraction as it saves significant amount of time waiting to buy the tickets  Getting to the park earlier meant that we got on all the rides without any queuing at all. The only ride we had to queue for was the Transformers ride which by the way is the BEST ride I have ever been on. Food here is fairly expensive so if you can pack some snacks with you. The rides on the park are awesomely done and maintained. The staff are very efficient on how the rides are run.  The one downside was that I believe the park is very small for a international theme park. In comparison to the other Universal studios in America. this park is so much smaller with a significant drop on the amount of rides. Altogether a lovely experience which finishes way too early.

Due to the overseas guests, I visited this place for the very first time. The park is not very huge like others and you do not have to burn your full day, maybe 4 hours will be enough to see major attractions. Accessibility from the city is also great. I visited therevon weekdays, but the place was quite crowded. I can imagine weekends and holidays. It is recommended to visit on weekdays. They have good ranges of souvenir shops and restaurants. Very tourist friendly place, although the service is not up to the international level. Some staff there was without smile and hospitality.

There are a lot of attractions, one day wouldn't be enough. If you're interested in water attraction, don't forget to bring your raincoat, else you have to buy one in the entrance. The Transformer is so dimensional and is a must, as well as the rollercoasters. The blue rollercoaster is scary than the red one, and The Mummy is so thrilling!

Okay..hard review to write.  Definitely worth a visit and during the week when it opens....no crowds. Don't try and save a $1 on your tickets online somewhere, your hotel concierge will look after you. Now, after 10 minutes of arriving our child felt sick and started throwing up....we decided to leave immediately and were advised that we couldn't receive tickets for another day. We hadn't been on a ride or anything. Disappointing!!!

Great place and my 7 year old enjoyed the 3D Transformers ride.  The restaurants are a great relief from the scotching sun (air conditioned) and they are scattered throughout the place.  Avoid weekends and school holidays as a majority of visitors were locals and we chose a Saturday of the school holiday (which was the worst). Advise check for school holidays and plan travels accordingly).  The rides had wait times from 40 - 60 minutes. The exceptions were the kids ride like Madagascar, Shreik 4D and a few other kids rides or shows.  Waterworld show is a must see. Don't worry about the crowd being huge and missing out as there was a massive amphitheater arrangement. People were running in the heat to get seats which turned out be more then enough.

We had a great day with two young girls, wasn't too busy but rides still packed out to a 60min wait. Still plenty to do and give the heat in Singapore the size of the park I felt was just right. The park characters were fantastic and the Madagascar boogie is well worth the wait for the little ones, great interaction with all the family. Food was about $10 a person and we received $10 vouchers from our tour organiser for both my wife and I so it cost us $20 all up. By 5:30 we were exhausted but loved the day and some great pics!

We avoided the weekend and found it quite easy to get into most of the attractions without much queueing on a Monday. Initially we thought it looked a bit boring from the gate as you can only see one street but we bought our non-express tickets and found an amazing choice of things to do and see. The fact the ticket covers the rides meant it was great value and there was something there for all ages. Definitely thought the Transformer ride was the best, with Lights, Sound and Action another favourite. I wouldn't take very young children to that because it is realistic and a number of them were crying when they came out. Preschoolers could handle the Madagascar crate adventure which wends its way through the hull of a huge ship and there are friendly looking animal characters and only a few little scary moments. The Shrek 4 D attraction is suitable for young and old but pick the right seats as some really rock! The street scapes were very clever particularly New York and the Hollywood diner. Plenty of eateries but they are quite expensive and the mementoes are very expensive. It gets hot so take plenty of water.

it was too cramped... they tried to fit in everything in a small space...  some of the rides were not available when we went there...  i could be wrong in comparing it to universal in the US, but this Universal really had kids in mind, whereas the one in the US has something for all ages.

Visited USS last month...pretty good day there, except--the long queus there.Hence, I encourage you all to purchase the express card, tomskip the lines like Jurassic Park, and so on and so forth.The ride which has left the greatest impression on is the Blue and Red Coaster!It was SO awesome,and even my cousin, who is in primary 2 went for it.Worth a try!

well, when it is Univ Studios it is not just the rides or the shows, it is the whole ambience, the liveliness of the place. Univ Studios Singapore is also such a holistic package. Much in the lines of its LA counterpart, most of the rides are the same. Rides of the Jurassic Park, Lost world, Transformers are some of the not-to-be-missed ones.Besides, the water stunt,the sound show are very good. Wholesome entertainment which is guaranteed to make you feel lot younger :-)

We got the combo package of SEA World and Universal Studios and I recommend you guys to do the same as its cheaper.  Before it was just all in the movies! Now, it has come to life! It was a great experience to visit Singapore's Universal Studios. The 4d and 3d rides are cool and unique. I would recommend all of you to try all, but my favorites are the Mummy and Transformers <3  Too bad that when we went there, the roller coaster ride was closed :(  Overall it was a great value for money! Just make sure to visit in a clear sunny day plus make sure to arrive early!

well what can I say, took myself, hubby and three children aged 13,11, 7 we had an absolute ball, on arriving by shuttle (bus - free from across the road from our hotel) to Sentosa Island we brought our tickets at the gates, we went during the week so the line wasn't long at all most children where at school, as we enter the gates it's a totally different world, the excitement the children had on there faces was so worthwhile, there are rides for all ages Madagascar, Shrek, Mummy, Transformers etc. the transformer ride was the best ride I have ever been on, anyone that goes there must go on this ride, the only ride my 7 year old missed out was the mummy ride which he was just alittle short but didnt bother him as there was so many things to do and explore, with the ticket admission each adult gets a $10 voucher to use on food and $5 voucher if you purchase merchandise. We arrived at 10.00am and the rides finish at 7.00pm but you can still wander around till as late as 9.30pm. We didnt get the express pass on any rides as most of the rides we only waited 15min or even less, alot of people I spoke to about express pass didnt realise that you can only use it once on the ride, and then you have to line up again like everyone else which they thought was a waste. But overall a great place for everyone to enjoy and have a great time.

My family - wife, 2 sons (4 years and 10 months) and I had a great time at USS. Having been to the one in US, I was skeptical if this is just as good. Overall verdict...Awesome... and I didn't even go on any thrill rides. With our kids we spent most of our time at Madagascar, Far Far Away, Sci-Fi City and New York. The staff were very well trained and enthusiastic and there were plenty of shade. The queues were relatively short (max 10 - 15 mins). Will return again once the boys are older and taller! You need to spend a full day here.

Went there with my family (small kids). Purchased my ticket online, which freed me from queuing for the ticket counter. Going there on a friday might had been one reason its not that full than I expected. The rides were great, also plenty of movie characters to have your picture taken. The Transformers ride is the kids' favorite. Although the food and drinks there is pricey, you can also have your meal outside the park (would recommend Malaysian Street Food) or from several restaurants and fastfood. For me, Universal Studios is one place you should go when in Singapore. Even you might be spending more while youre there, but the smile on your kids' faces is priceless.
very good day .... in a very good place but unfortunately it ended early with a very heavy rain :( but still satisfied and enjoyed it a lot .....

The place was great fun for kids and also adults. The Transformers 3D ride was just out-of-this-world. We even went twice on this ride. The experience was so real. We also liked the Revenge of the Mummy ride. The roller-coaster ride was in total darkness and was quite scary. However, we were disappointed that both the Battlestar Galactica rides were closed for maintenance. I believe that USS should inform us of this via their website. We also recommend the Shrek 4D adventure and the Monster Rock musical as well as the Waterworld show. They are must sees.

This is a must visit attraction, if you are travelling with kids and during weekends or peak days it is convenient that you book your tickets online to avoid long queue, express tickets are really helpful and worth a penny at such times, u can end up getting good deals on combo attractions, if you have enough time before your visit check out various online combo packs. 4D simulations of shrek and transformer are must , try to experience this ride atleast twice... its wonderful, An umbrella, sunscreen, tissues and a extra change (clothes) are helpful. dont forget to keep a watch on the street inside to spot ur favourite characters
it has improved since we visited 2 years ago.But queue is long.Avoid weekends.transformers ride is the best.

Went here with my hubby last weekend without knowing it was public school holiday in Singapore, plus it was a Saturday, so it was super super crowded @@ we asked the ticketing person and they told us the wait time was 50-60 mins per ride, so without hesitation we paid the extra SGD20 for the single Express pass.  Glad that we bought it. apparently people in Singapore are not too keen on paying extra for this express pass, so our wait time at the express lines were 5 mins max. it took us around 4 hours to finish all rides and even watched the parade.  In conclusion, the extra SGD20 each for the express pass was the most well spent money ever in this trip.  tips: in singapore universal studios they allow you to bring food and drinks inside, we bought a large bottle of water inside. but food and drinks inside was not too expensive either, around SGD6 for a drink, SGD4 for churros, and whopping SGD12 for a turkey leg (MUST TRY).

My husband and I did the VIP Universal tour when we were in Singapore on our Honeymoon. The VIP tour is quite different from the one that is in Los Angeles but still worth paying the extra money. It was SO hot when we were there so the only grumble I would have is that maybe it would be a good idea to get some more mist sprays around the place to keep everyone cool.  We had a great time on our tour and our guide was very entertaining. Overall we had a great time and will be back again on our next visit to Singapore.

This is well worth a day trip or two to see when you are in Singapore, whether on your own, with friends or family. There is something for everyone, some of the rides are pure pleasure, other pure fear and exhilaration. For a bit of fun try the Madagascan ride, for the terror try the revenge of the mummy, to get drenched in a fun way, try the Jurassic park lost world ride. The motto when you go is enjoy yourself anything is possible
This is best theme park so far. Sad that it rained hard a bit when we were there. The rides are so cool. You will spend the whole day if you want maximize your stay here.

Universal is great. This was our second visit. If the first one truly was a five star visit this one was 2-3. Reason was the rain. I would suggest that you plan your visit carefully based on the weather forecast. Universal is to the largest extend an open air park and when it rains you can not really experience it to its full extent.

We went as a family of 4. We were staying in Sentosa & bought a 3 day pass plus an express pass for one day. Would recommend the express pass as it makes the experience a lot more pleasant & fun without long waits in the heat. 3 days proved to be a bit excessive, ended up going on the 3rd day solely to take pics & a couple of favourite rides.
Not as crowded as Universal Studios LA - most rides has waits of only 10 minutes. Lots of the rides and activities were inside, so it was good to escape the heat

The staff who guided the Minion photo shooting was rude. She scolded my 9 yo son who tried to hold the minion hand during photo shooting. It made my son shock because she used harsh words with angry face. Actually she could smile and remind with softer words. Children will not do harm to the character because they just love them.

We visited Universal studios on our 4 day trip to singapore. I have been to 6 flags but the whole atmosphere there was just amazing. All the rides are good, i would highly recommend transformer ride. Its incredible.

USS is the top most attraction of Singapore. A full day is needed to explore it completely and an express pass is a must if you wish to do all the rides. Within USS the Transformers ride is not to be missed. So is the Water World stunt show (beware of water sprays there). Food options are plenty but if you are fussy about the type of food, carry some with you.

We spent an afternoon at USS during our three day holiday in Singapore. We have three children- ages 4, 7 and 9 and thought it would be fun for them. I think the park is impressive- great design and everything was massive with regards to attractions and props. There were plenty of characters walking around and people had to cue up to take photos with the more popular ones. My kids only liked those little people from Despicable Me. The rides we went on were fun. We bought express tickets for my two older children. I will say it was definitely worth purchasing to cut ahead of the line. On some popular rides, the express line wait was up to 30 minutes, so we skipped those. We wouldn't wait in line if it was over 40 minutes. This park only takes all day if you were to wait in the regular line for all the rides. Otherwise, with express tickets and skipping a few rides, half a day is more than enough. I think we should have tried the luge and other experiences that would have been different than your average amusement park. You can get a stamp and leave the park and return later. We left to eat in a restaurant out by the ticketing area. There are single and double strollers, as well as wheelchairs and motorized chairs for rent at the entrance. It was helpful for us to push the kids around and give them a place to sit while we waited for rides. Good place to visit if you are in the mood for an amusement park. We wished they would have had more kiddie rides around the park to bide the wait with the little ones, while older members of the group rode rides. That said, our kids were able to ride most rides( we just didn't because of the wait).

I've been to Universal Studios in US, Disneyland, etc but the crowds here are just crazy. We did go on a weekend just after Christmas and unfortunately did not get an express pass. Big mistake - as others have said long queues of over an hour are common. Throw in the hot and humid conditions, it can be an exhausting day. the park is ideal for kids 5 to 10 years. In general it is more expensive and less interesting than the parks in the US. I would probably place this lower on your list of priorities / attractions to visit in Singapore.

Rides for small kids and rides for big kids. Shows were nice--ours especially liked Shrek 4D, even our 3 year old, who I though would be scared beyond belief, loved it.  Sesame Street song and dance was cute, all the little street performances were fun. A bit pricey, but the kids had a good time so it was worth it. Fun to walk through all the different "worlds".

It's definitely worth a visit,great way to spend a day with family,it's fun all the way for adults and kids alike.. The best rides being The Transformers Ride,Revenge of the Mummy ride..very long lines during weekends,so get there early.

SG Tourism has really accelerated having the USS around. One day is insufficient though we got there before 9am. To avoid queuing, on line ticketting is an advantage. Enjoyed the Jurassic Ride, Water world, SHrek 4D and Lights, Camera, Action meeting Steven Spielberg, truly a cinematic genius.Getting to USS would be more fun if you ride the Jewel Cable Car.it may not have taken us too long to enjoy every minute of it but it created a lasting indelible imprint on my mind. If you wish to buy souvenir SG shirts, I think USS shops had the best quality.The price is worthwhile. Would like to take this opportunity to thank the staff at the USS Clinic who were very accommodating to us when my wife was advised to stay in for about 2 hours for not feeling damn well after riding the unstoppable exhilarating Battlestar Galactica.

Enjoy this place and click pics with all beautiful characters you like in movies.Transformers,Madagascar,jurassic park and many more. Dont miss the Transformers 4d experience but yes let me warn you atlest 4 hours you will waste standing in the line (no place to sit)but yes its worth trying because its the best ride i ever i had in my life.

Great place to spend the day with the kids, however i highly recommend paying the extra for the VIP pass so you don't have to wait in line for rides. Whilst we were there it averaged 40 minute wait per ride.

Visited the Californian counterpart a few years ago; so for a pre Christmas holiday, we decided to visit the attraction to see if Singapore's Universal Studio is up to mark.  Thank god I bought my tickets online! (http://www.rwsentosa.com/language/en-US/Homepage/Attractions/UniversalStudiosSingapore). The queue was so loooong! Holiday season equals busloads of tourist plus local school holidays! Children everywhere, adults of all sizes, bursts of colours everywhere! Vibrant, noisy...you get the picture.  Upon entering the park, our first stop was the customer/park services. Very professional staff, very well trained and we noted that these boys are very young, probably in their early twenties.  The main reason we wanted to visit USS was the Transformer 3D Ride. We were told by our relative that he actually came for this particular ride and had to wait 5 hours! We were VERY lucky; first ride = 40 minutes wait, second ride = 30 minutes wait, third ride = 45 minutes wait!  The ride was AWESOME! No spoilers here but you've gotta try it.  The rest of the rides are good but more for younger kids. My children are in their early twenties (back from UK for the holidays); they have been to most parks but they agreed that this ride is fantastic! We tried several others; Madagascar, The Lost World, Ancient Egypt. The rest of the attractions are too crowded.  We had breakfast and tea here; expensive (of course) but not bad. The park is very clean; toilets reasonably clean despite the crowd.  Do stay till the end cause the parade is fantastic!.  A must visit if you're in Singapore!
Not much for little ones - or those who like gentle rides. Food choices poor and expensive. Much prefer Disney

2 kids aged 8 and 11 could have spent a week there. Only down fall was that the Rollercoaster was down for renovations for a few months. Kids devastated and no discount. Would have changed holiday dates if we knew this.

Definitely a must for everyone, best place to run a whole day, my advise is to go on a weekday as everyone in Singapore stays here during the weekends :)  woot woot for the Streetboys Rockafellas!  good rides for all ages, transformers would definitely rank #1 followed by all coaster rides. bring extra cash as every ride has a wonderful set of souvenirs for keeps.  All in all, excellent theme park!

Not really a cheap place to go. The park is so crowded during holiday, the waiting time for the ride is almost unbearable. The heat is also mean too. One suggestion is to install the Mist Machine similar to that at Disneyworld during summer time to ease the crowd.
Don't wait in the queue for the Treasure Hunters ride - not worth it at all. Other rides are good but it's worth buying an express pass for extra $30

Spent a full day from opening (10am) till 6pm at Universal Studios. Lots to see and do for adults and kids. Crowds were quite good in the earlier part of day but in the afternoon some rides took up to 60 mins to get on. Everything was enjoyable. Lots of toilet and eating/drink facilities. A must do while on holidays in Singapore.

This Universal Studios is very well done and enjoyable. We went on a Sunday in November and it wasn't very crowded. We did the big ones first upon entering the park - Transformers, Mummy and Jurassic Park - and managed to catch all the shows. We also came back to ride Transformers and Mummy multiple times. If you're used to the Universal Studios in the US, the quality is upheld.

the main roller coaster is not working , which is very sad the place is clean enough nice toilets , but its very small not many rides there compared to the universal in america , and u have to line up for hours to get a picture with anyone of the characters

This is a good place for kids to enjoy and have fun. Tickets are expensive and every ride and 4D movie has a fee. It is better to buy a days pass at the Singapore Tourism as the ques are very very long. This is a place for children

I was here on a stopover so had a day to spare and thought I'd try out Universal. As expected I loved it. I've only been to the Universal Studios in LA so only have this to compare it too and it did seem bigger. $74 paid on the gate.  As some previous reviews have stated the largest rollercoaster - Accelorator - was closed but I wasn't overly bothered by this. Transformers 4D, by far one of the best rides and is a must! Characters are out and about throughout the day; Shrek & the Minions by far being the most popular. Bare in mind that they are only allowed out for a short period of time due to health & safety with costumes so even though you're in the queue you're not gaurenteed a photo. The map tells you where different characters can be found.  I paid $14 for a Solo meal and got a Silce of Pizza, a Drink & an Ice lolly. Food was good, but I did want more! Corn dogs, Cupcakes & Cookies are available on stands around the park. Gifts & merchandise is reasonably priced.  I used the CitySightseeing bus to get here. I had pre-purchased a ticket which included transport to Sentosa Island. I was dropped in the car park which is right below the park! Quick & easy and recommended.  I love universal and would return again.

Having been to Universal in Florida & LA, I wanted to try out Singapore and I enjoyed every minute of it. There was lots to do and a few different rides. Anyone who likes to movies should pop by and have some fun.

Spent the whole Saturday in USS. Had an enjoyable day with friends and colleague. one must be careful in planning for which attraction to go otherwise one will waste a lot of time waiting to get on board.

As a child, I loved the theme parks & exhilarating rides. Now in my 50's I still love the excitement that theme parks offer. Universal Studios has some very good rides but make sure you go on a week day if possible and not in holiday periods as the line for the rides can be hours long. We went on a Monday and the longest wait we had was 45mins. The Water World stunt show was very good and worth a look. If your from Australia, its similar to Movie World on the Gold Coast, Qld.

Nothing to say about this unique place. We had lots of fun. We danced, we clicked pictures on every step, We enjoyed rides, we enjoyed shows, we enjoyed films. That day was full of enjoyments. See our pictures.
My first visit to universal studio and it was great in singapore... A must visit to all the people travelling to singapore

The title comment is due to the fact , that when we visited Universla studios , two of its best attractions - Battle Galactica and Waterzone were closed, but the park took the same price for the ticket. And without these two attractions park was limited to only 3 good rides - Transformers, Mummy and Jurassik park. With all repeatance of the above 3 attractions we choose to leave the park only 3 hours after enetering, as it was already boring. So for people who had never been to Universal studios , please ignore above comments and once in live you should experence Universal park. For the ones, who had visited Universal studios in Europe and USA, simply skip this park, because you will be greatly dissapointed by the difference.

We had such a great time, so much fun and laughter. The best advise, book online before the time and go early, especially if you have smaller kids. Lunch time onwards it is very busy and it gets hot and humid, so early is much better. Everybody has to visit a theme park, doesn't matter your age. It brings out the child in all of us. Highly recommended.

We took our 4 year old son here and I doubt we'd ever go back. It was not a busy day, but there were significant waits for many attractions. The quality of the food available for purchase was very poor. I understand that you can't expect anything but fast food at these types of venues, but it just wasn't good.  It was raining on and off, so maybe that is why not much was going on. There were very few opportunities to meet characters. We also found it strange that they didn't offer any sort of 'fast pass' for visitors to buy. I see that others have mentioned a fast pass, but we asked at the front gate and they said they didn't have one!  Perhaps our son was too young and the attractions for older kids would have been better. But the ones for his age were packed and not that great.
kids above 5 years would freak out and so would all adults. Make sure you reach before 10am so that family is able to make best use of the time. The studio closes at 6pm.
The park was incredibly clean not very busy which means you don't have to wait very long lines. the rides were amazing but still terrifying. Good for all ages

We had a blast at this park. The only reason we didn't give it five stars was because the more extreme ride(s) was out of action. Everything else was great. The queues were manageable and if you really liked a ride, popping back for a single ride was an excellent option. The staff are friendly and helpful, the place is clean and the entertainment offered is just right.

Fantastic , Transformers 4D is awesome !! We , along with out 10 years Son , took the 4D ride twice. Highly recommended for kids of all ages.  Other events were also enjoyable , Madagascar ride was great !

Everything about universals was amazing, if you have kids definetly take them all the rides were amazing. Some rides you had to wait up to 45min but it is worth the wait, always something to look at in the line and the line is always moving.

Rides Attractions were sufficient, fun and exciting but what make it irritating is the extremely long Queues you have to go through before its your turn, the revenge of the mummy is worth trying for and especially the transformer 3D really awesome effects. worth to go definitely prepare more money cause food in there will be expensive I suggest that theres a KFC at the imbian station where food will be more affordable

We love everything especially the fireworks. It was amazing!!  My children loved it so much.  However, we got on the boat ride queue and was there for about 45mins already when suddenly the operators informed us that the rides are experiencing technical difficulties.

Opens 10am which is a shame as after a couple of rides you are in the midday heat which can be exhausting. It is a great day out but very busy Fridays - Sundays. We visited on a Monday and the queues were almost non-existent. Staff friendly. Rides are great. Something for the younger kids as well as the older ones, but I think teenagers would struggle to be entertained esp now they have closed the Battlestar Galactica ride (being replaced with something new).

Very tiny park, you can do the loop in about 20 minutes without going through any of the rides. The big coaster was down, but Transformers was solid as well as the mummy ride. 2 hour wait for the Jurassic park water ride... so we missed a few things because of long waits... but most of the other rides were about 10-20 minute waits.

I was blown away with the rides and attractions. Went there on public holiday, so it was super busy. Had to go back and buy express tickets. Normal wait times for the regular tickets were between 1 to 2.5 hours, so it was worth buying the express tickets. I would definitely recommend anyone visiting Singapore to check this place out. Trust me you will not be disappointed.

Firstly, never go on a public holiday as the crowds will be overwhelming. We had no choice so headed there on Good Friday. Expected the crowds but not some inconsistent customer service when the revenge of the mummy ride broke down and were told too bad that we queued for 45 mins and did not get to ride, we would have to queue from the back if we wanted to try again. This time for over 90 minutes. This gave a very negative vibe for our group. For the number of people in the park, there was no way near enough rides, thus the queues everywhere. Overall it was a rather average and expensive day in a theme park that is beginning to look rather tired.
not a big theme park but the facilities are in good conditions and there are plenty of fun performances. You can spend a whole day there

On our recent family holiday to Singapore we decided to go visit Universal Studios on Sentosa Island. Lots of rides & things to see for all ages. I particularly liked the Transformer 3D ride. I think its the best ride I have ever been on. We also especially enjoy the Underwater World show. The stunts, actors & before show entertainment was fantastic. A great day out!

had a great time, awesome Transformers ride ( its a must!). Good restaurants, smaller version from the US parks, but still entertaining, we actually enjoy the place more than HK Disneyland, staff are more friendly! Singapore is always had humid weather but Air-con is on every building, hahhhh...love it! queuing is not too bad, great place for families or fun with friends. Love Shrek castle!

A fantastic theme park!! you feel like you are living the movies, with each zone built to make you feel like you are in a different world. So many awesome rides and side shows - my favourites were The Mummy and Transformers.  AND DONT MISS THE WATERWORLD SHOW!!! its at set times throughout the day, and it is amazing.  The only reason I gave this 4 stars and not 5 was because the 2 scariest roller coasters were closed when we went.

2 adults + 5 year old child had a great time. Longest ride wait was 45 mins, but most less than 10 mins - there are boards all around the park that tell you estimated wait times for rides, and these are handy for planning your next activity. Transformers ride - awesome (scared the 5 yo initially, but kept going back for more). Revenge of the Mummy - great, with easy entry using single riders queue (the only ride working that the 5 year old couldn't go on). The shows were surprisingly great too - thought they'd be cheesy. Donkey and Spielberg shows were the faves. The Waterworld show was highly entertaining as well. Food is pretty average, although not overly expensive considering you're in a theme park (about SGD41 for the three of us to eat lunch). Can get a pass out and eat at one of the other eateries in Resort World Sentosa for better quality food. We covered every ride (and most twice or more) as well as every show (except Monster Rock) on a Wednesday with opening hours of 10am - 7pm (including a pass out for about 45 mins to eat dinner elsewhere), even with most rides being closed for about an hour due to thunderstorms/lightning in the area. Never felt too crowded, even though there were still lots of people in the park.

Universal studios is a must visit if you come to Singapore. The must visits are Transformers, Waterworld and Shrek movie. We also really enjoyed the donkey show. There are two small roller-coasters, the Mummy one is scary....another big one was not working that day so we got a good reason to chicken out :)

Not much to say but this park is very interesting and will visit again in near future. The roller coasters are mostly for adult. The most thriller is the one inside the Egypt theme building which housing the high speed roller coaster ride in a completely dark room.

Transformers: The Ride is a MUST! but the queue tends to get really long really quick so i suggest you start with that ride right after you enter the park and sit in the front row so you get the full effect!  Revenge of the Mummy is also really fun and you should go on this ride before the park is about to close or when people start leaving (like after 5pm) and it's possible you don't have to wait at all plus it's really add that creepy factor because it's so dark both inside and outside hah!  The Battlestar Galactica roller coasters was closed (i think it still is) but from the look of it, it could be the most thrilling ride in the park.

The amount to enter the place is kind of hefty. It is about 74 SGD, so to those who are planning to go here, please take note. Also it is wise to come as early as 9 if you want to enjoy every part of the attraction.  To keep things simple, I'd just name out the rides that you guys should definitely try;  1) The Transformers Ride - This is more of a 3D spectacle, it was immersive and there was countless of times where the ride almost felt real. Do not miss this one.  2) Revenge of The Mummy - Another not to be missed right. The ride is really crazy and I swear, you will not leave this ride without screaming once or twice. The amount of turns and drops will leave your legs trembling after the ride.  In my opinion, this are the rides that are not to be missed, there are other rides in here but those two really takes the cake.  Don't forget to catch the shows as well;  The waterworld show has some pyrotechnics and is good for the family - its a typical hero saves the girl show but the stunts and explosions will make it worth it.  There are also other kinds of places to visit in here, so I will not spoil it further for you guys.

We live in Singapore and have an Annual Express pass for the four of us. It allows us yo go for 2-3 hrs , get on all the rides without the bother of queuing for most of the he time. Whenever we have visitors, we always make sure they buy one day express passes. It may seem expensive but once you're in, all becomes clear that it is well and truly worth it! Good day out for a young family.

The universal studio in Singapore is not as good as it was in Osaka, but it was still great fun to hang out on a day with families. The transformer ride was incredible and the mummy ride was unbelievable.  Remember to bring umbrella and sunscreen as the weather in SIngapore is hot and humid.

First time to visit the Universal Studio in Singapore, lots of fun though it rained a little but we just go on exploring what's in. What we enjoyed the best is the "Lights camera action" well who would not know Steven Spielberg made a great epic of holywood movies for all time. Still we enjoyed the fun & other entertainment inside the studio and outside in the Sentosa for taking a good view of pictures...
A visit to Singapore is incomplete without going to Universal Studios. Plenty of rides to indulge, lotsa Halal eating places and fun for the whole family...

Our experience at the Universal studios Singapore was nice. All the rides were quite exciting, Battlestar Galactica was closed though. Revenge of the mummy is the best roller-coaster there. We had taken a fast pass which allowed us to access all the rides without waiting in the long lines. One day there is enough to sit on all the rides. Would recommend the fast pass.

Since i've been to other park that offer more rides & games, i would say USS was just ok, i think kids will enjoy more. The park was rather small & crowded. I enjoy the Transformer ride the most, we had it more than once. The shows were all great. For those who stay in JB, this park is worth a visit.

It was a manageable park to explore within a day. we started at 10am and we completed all rides by 3pm as we had the fast pass. the kids were very dissapointed as the biggest roller coaster ride was closed. However, the transformers made up for it. There were many halal certified restaurants which we appreciated very much. The shows were well timed, so we managed to cover all of it. We have been to better theme parks than this one, so overall it was just OK.

I visited Universal studios in Singapore thinking it to be like one in U.S.A but it was not as I expected.First of all you have to be a patience guy to visit there as for every ride there is a minimum waiting time of 40 minutes which can reach up to 70 minutes for some ride and after waiting for so long a ride for just a few minutes only.There are rides which you will consider worth waiting like the Transformers ride,Shrek in 3D and the revenge of The Mummy and there is a action stunt show in Water world which is worth watching(No waiting for this,just be on time there) and the rest is just one time go.Food is a bit expensive there so take your favorite meal with you.Overall a one time visit but the ticket price is a bit higher comparing the facilities and rides inside.

Felt a little ripped off coz roller coaster was not working come on all the way from India and this Newayz my kids enjoyed a lot.Although this one is the smallest Universal studio in the world......At the end of the day there was a Parade with all the characters..........Must visit in Singapore..

Wasn't bad. Battlestar galactica and transformer rides where only treacly the 2 major draw cards here. Big park but doesn't look like much room for expansion. not a bad day out if online in Singapore for the day or just wanting something different- can do the park in about 4 hours. - just watch the ticket prices

We spent three days on Sentosa island in Singapore. We purchased six month season passes to give us the freedom to go in and out of universal studios as we liked. I highly recommend paying that little extra to get the express passes. This allows you to skip the regular queues and go almost to the front of the line on many of the attractions. This will save you a lot of time, especially if you don't want to queue with the kids!  Having been to Universal Studios in California and Florida we found Singapore was a great park, considering the space they had. They have done a great job and jamming as many attractions and rides in to the space they obviously had to work with. The park itself is far smaller than any of the other Universal's I've been to. So it is literally bulging with things to do. Definitely recommend using your express pass to its full potential, and go on your favorite rides again, and again!

Awesome place with some amazing Rides. Rides are for all age groups and some rides are really amazing. Kindly note if you are going in weekend do take express pass otherwise you will not be able to enjoy all the rides in one day

Don't get me wrong it's worth going and I thought it was quite inexpensive to go and also inside as well. I don't know why I was disappointed I think I was just expecting something fantastic and that's really not what I got. If I came back to Singapore I wouldn't go again. The new battle star Galactica ride was not working and I really would have like to go on it. I liked the rapids ride in the Jurassic park bit and the dance show I think it was called monsters of rock was quite good too.  Food was pretty naff, cold chips and fish dripping with fat.  Lots of things to but and prices pretty reasonable.

Definitely not universal studios LA or Florida, however lots of good rides and still fun. The main ride was disappointing having been to both parks in the US. Not exactly the tram ride through the different movie sets; However,standing up and experiencing a tornado was still fun. The Sesame Street ride was awesome and worth doing. I definitely wouldn't recommend going on a weekend as the queues were still quite long for a Monday. The food was generally very ordinary to not great and expensive. We took the monorail across rather than pay for the cable car, which was a great decision as we still saw a lot and it was a fun and inexpensive ride.
Our 11 year old had a good day here, but it's not nice queuing in the hot weather. The rides he went on were very good but he was disappointed that the giant roller coaster was not working.

I went to USS by myself on a Thursday. I was a bit worried about going alone, but it was well worth the visit and plenty to keep me entertained. While there were loads of people around, it wasn't packed either.  I read a few comments on here about getting the express pass and I'm so glad I did. Someone mentioned that you should think of the extra $30 as just being part of the admission price and I think that's a good way to think about it if you can. The express pass meant that I never waited more than 2-3 minutes to go on a ride. Plus it makes you feel like a bit of a rockstar! I know that part of the thrill of rides is the delayed gratification that comes with queuing, but walking straight past everyone who is waiting in the heat is also pretty gratifying and it means you can pack more in to your day.  It took me 4.5 hours to do a full loop of the park, going on all but the small kiddy rides. Lucky for me, by then it was around 5pm and even though I'd used all of my express entry passes, I was able to get straight in to most rides for a second go as many people had already gone home.  Yes, it was a shame that the Battlestar ride wasn't working, but the Mummy and Transformers rides were excellent. The Waterworld show was also definitely worth a look.  My advice - be prepared that you will get a little wet on many of the rides. But it's hot and you dry out pretty quickly.

This place was out of this world. What I love about Universal Singapore is the diversity of rides on show. There really is something for everybody regardless of age. The 4D Transformers ride is something you cannot afford to miss. The line was about 30 mins but I would happily wait two hours to go again. Without a doubt this was the best ride I have experienced in my entire life. You get the sensation you're racing down busy streets at 300+kmh, that youre falling off buildings and robots are throwing you about. Because its' 4D there'll be wind, smoke and heat that you experience. Its an insane ride and you just cant get enough. DO NOT MISS THIS RIDE!!! Aside from that the Mummy Ride (indoor rollercoaster) is for the thrill seekers. Very scary because you dont know where you're going.  There's plenty of other rides like the Canopy Ride and Rapid Adventure which is water based. And that's just to name a few (there's many more). There really is something for everybody. I went with a friend and the wait times for us ranged from 5-40 mins. The popular rides (like the Transformers ride) will set you back half an hour usually. So there certainly are crowds and so do expect to wait for some rides. Its a good idea The fact that it can get a little full is more a credit to the popularity of the theme park. The tickets arent too cheap (70+SGD) but they're worth every single cent. Food is a little expensive but there's a decent range and a fairish price considering its in a themepark.  Overall our experience was really great and if you're in Singapore for a while you really cant miss. It'd be harsh to not give the place a 10/10 and was the pinnacle of our trip to Singapore. Thank you Universal for a great time!!

We had just visited the one at Osaka and this is the second US in just one month. This one in Singapore is rather small and packed. It will take you less than an hour to go through the whole park. It was drizzling today and many attractions were announced ' cancelled' due to safety reasons??? Not sure what could be so dangerous just because it drizzled? Disappointed that we could not see many shows.  The toys, souvenirs and food in this park is very expensive and to me way overpriced. They should consider reviewing the price.  Some crowd control needs to be done as it is rather busy early in the morning. We arrived the park at 10.30am and it was already quite busy. People were rushing and pushing so need to ensure you hold onto the hands of the little ones.  The major rollercoaster was not working due to technical reasons. For those who are looking for some thrill and excitement, you will be disappointed!  Sentosa has many things to offer so you can give this a miss if you can.

Pity the Battlestar Galactica rollercoaster is still out of action. But be sure to get the same if not more fun from the other attractions. Doubt you'd finish riding on all of them in one day... and that's not because of the size of the park, but because the queues can be quite long. Expect to spend one whole day there, i.e. from 11am to 7pm. If you're heading there on a Saturday or Public Holiday, you may get to see the parade or the fire works display. If you're on a slow and easy trip to the park, then spend some time at the restaurants. Food is nice and service is decent. Take lots of photos. Even though the backdrops are all, fake, the scenery is nice and I'm sure you're camera will be working on overtime. If you're local, put in your savings into the annual pass (or if you rather, the half-year pass). It gets you unlimited entry during the year that you've signed up for. Which is a damn good deal since you can also go in anytime to have a meal at the park, which will make you leave in a happier mood than before entering the fun zone. USS is a great attraction that should win more awards in years to come, especially with the coming of new rides soon. I've been going there every month (twice a month sometimes) since getting my annual pass in Dec 2013.
I went last june after they first open Wing of Time is awesome, Anyone going there its realy worth it. The Laser ligth so creative.

It is better to buy the entrance ticket on internet for 60 dollars compared to entrance for 75 dollars. Also worth buying 30 dollars express ticket over this which allows you to go to rides without any line . The best ride is transformer . Worth going . He main roller coaster ride is closed form some time. A lot of food options but Louis pizza at New York is the best. Even Indian veg food is available in the Egyptian court.

We had a great day of family fun at Universal Studios. I think we got a quiet day (Tuesday after school hols were finished) so although we had some longish queues, we never waited more than 25 minutes for a ride and by the end of the day, we had been on everything we wanted to (plus more opportunistic ones). Our 3 year old was only slightly limited and was very happy to enjoy what was available to her (I think she took the Sesame Street Spaghetti ride 4 times). My husband and our 7 year old seemed to like the Mummy ride best (I'm glad it hasn't given her nightmares, though!) and I loved the Transformers one. The queue was deceptively long for the Jurassic Park Canopy Flyer as it was really quick and just OK. Waterworld was not my favourite, either. We had a fantastic lunch of laksa and fresh fruit and there are water fountains and plenty of bathrooms around the park. The Battlestar Galactica rollercoaster wasn't operating, but I was kind of glad because I would have forced myself to go on it and been terrified if it was.

Would advise that you get a taxi to the main walk bridge and then just enjoy the walk across towards Sentosa Island. Found that going with a taxi the directions when arriving were a little poor and the additional costs you have to pay just to enter are ludicrous. Universal studios was a little expensive in my opinion, they provide a few options, go for the Universal Express Ticket, which gives you access to rides without waiting in queue's for an hour or so, however be aware that you must purchase a normal ticket at about 70 Dollars per person, and then pay an additional 50 Dollars for an upgrade on your ticket.  Kid wise, perfect, adult wise, some decent rides. When in the lost world, buy one of the plastic water macs as the ride involves getting wet, and then walking around with shoes full of water all day. But obviously of your in to getting wet, don't worry about it. Water world was decent, shows start at 3pm and 5pm, blue and green seats mean you will be getting wet, and the red seats mean keeping dry, again a matter of choice on getting wet or not. Worth the watch, a decent show.  Transformers, probably the best ride of them all and there is some odd ride near the Egyptian location that involves getting in a safari vehicle and literally going on it for 5-,minutes and getting off. Avoid it, pointless ride and you queue for about 30 minutes for nothing.  Decent day out, went on a Saturday and was busy, but not that busy.
Definitely the best thing that happened to us on our trip. An experience of a lifetime for the entire family. Would like to go there again sometime.

We came here with our 2 children and another family. I have been to Universal Studios in LA and Florida before (admittedly about 15+ years ago) but I was a little disappointed with the Singapore Universal Studios. The queues were ridiculous, the main rollercoaster out of action indefinitely and it just didn't feel like a Universal Studios (to me). In saying that the kids enjoyed it but not when we said we weren't going to wait 50 minutes in the queue for this ride or 60 minutes for that ride and one queue was 90 minutes (not happening). I personally prefer MovieWorld on the Gold Coast (in Australia) - better rides, more characters around the place and better set up. Not sure if I would go to Universal Singapore again as to get the express pass is about another $50 each onto the ticket price - undecided. If you go here get here when gates open and go straight to Transformers ride and then the rides in Lost World as the queues wait time isn't worth the short ride you get.
Great fun for kids and adults- go early, go on adventure rides first to avoid long queues and DON'T miss Waterworld show!!Highly recommended.

If you've been to Florida and or California this park is not a patch on them, which shouldn't come as a shock or surprise, however that doesn't mean Universal Studios Singapore is not worth a visit! It's easy to get to either by car, taxi, bus, MRT or by foot! Queuing for tickets I found to be a pain....not all the booths were open so had to wait a while. You have the option to buy a two day pass, which I wouldn't advise.....the park isn't that big, but I would recommend buying (if budget allows) the Express tickets as an add-on. What they don't tell you about these Express tickets on the website is that there are 2 types. Express at $40 only let's you go on the express queue once for each ride, but you can purchase the Express Unlimited (unlimited-ride as many times as you like) for $60 extra per ticket.  The Express Unlimited tickets, although expensive we're worth it as I didn't have to queue for more than 2 minutes and that was for only one ride near peak time of midday. I definitely recommend getting there for before opening at 10am.  The huge duelling roller coaster that is/was Battlestar Galactica is supposedly opening again at some point after being closed for well over a year.....has had a new paint job and according to local Singapore newspaper article says the park have had permission to keep the ride after plans to demolish it and replace it with something else...how accurate this is, well time will tell.  The main attraction for me was Tranformers...Wow, Wow, Wow and Wow (went on 4 times!) love the Transformers anyway and so the ride was even more amazing for me. Not heard a bad thing about the ride at all.  The Mummy Returns ride is good, liked the finger print operated lockers to keep your bags in...there is a charge after 45 mins if you haven't returned to collect your belongings.  Once you have done the big rides, take a step back and visit some of the other attractions...plenty to see and do even though it's a small park.  Food is expensive as is the day once you include tickets, but it wasn't going to be a cheap outing, still glad I went, loved it!

This was a great day out but I don't have the patience to wait 70-90 minutes for a 5 minute ride. If I had to stand in long queues with the kids (who are 7 & 10) I don't think I would have enjoyed the day so much. Was a shame the large roller-coasters were not operational which took away 1 of the prime attractions!

Universal Studios was such a fun day out. We took our 3 kids 12, 6 & 2 because of the age gap between our oldest to our youngest we wanted to be able to & being able to do everything. So we purchase the express pass for us all but didn't have to pay for your 2 year old, this way we didn't have to line up for ages & got to go basically straight on the ride. This was really worth it for our family. If you do go the express pass use the normal line first if it's not busy then you can go back later & use the express pass so you don't need to line up for long at all & go back on ride again. The normal rides could take up to 40mins or more wait time. Get there before opening time to & start lining up early at the gates and go straight for the most popular rides like the transformer ride or the mummy ride. These rides were awesome!!! Be warned there are lots of shops in universal after you come off a ride & are quite expensive and our kids wanted everything.lol another tip maybe take some drinks and snacks in your backpack as food is expensive too. Definitely not to be missed we had the best day out & was there till closing time :)

Great little amusement park, some good rides like the mummy, get there early, before 10, to avoid the worst queues. You will get wet on the water ride. 2 new roller coasters are being built which will make the park better. Avoid the worst queues by going in the single person entrance unless you want to sit together.

I attended with a group and had a great day. There were 2 standout rides: Transformers3D and The Mummy indoor roller coaster. We went on both twice and could easily have gone on them both a few more times.  We went on almost all the rides and came away very happy with the experience.  We set at one of the diners which served surprisingly good quality burgers and fries. There is a Starbucks on site that satisfied by caffeine requirement.  The park was extremely clean and very well organised which is what one typically finds at a Universal.  Tip: purchase an Express Pass if you're able to. It doubles the cost but it fasttracks you through each ride. Even though we were there on a non-holiday Tuesday it was very busy.  Tip2: there park us just one of many attractions within the entertainment quarter of the island. Make sure you give yourself time to check out some of the other ones.

Best attraction in Singapore.  The park is awesome Many of the rides & shows like shrek, mummy, monsters rock are good but the transformers ride was not less than great. It is in a league of its own.
